chapters.title: Chapter 401: Obsidian Sanhedrin [VII / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Rising from the bedrock was a colossal octagonal containment sarcophagus forged from solid transparent mana-crystal and reinforced with twenty-four layers of golden suppression runes.
FSSSSH!
Resting horizontally upon a floating anti-gravity dais inside the crystal sarcophagus was a massive breathtaking weapon.
It looked beautiful...
It was a Khopesh... the iconic ancient curved sickle-sword of the desert kings, but scaled up to magnificent terrifying proportions.
It was not a one-handed ceremonial sidearm, instead it was a massive two-handed sovereign greatsword measuring nearly six feet in total length.
The blade was forged from an ancient luminous golden alloy that had never been successfully replicated by modern metallurgy.
The edge was curved in the deadly shape of a diving hawk’s beak, gleaming with a brilliant polished luster that seemed untouched by the passage of centuries.
Intricate carved bind-runes were etched along the flat of the golden steel, pulsing with a slow dormant amber glow.
The long two-handed hilt was wrapped in the pristine calcified white scales of a divine desert serpent meaning it was cool and seamless to the touch.
Set into the heavy solid-gold pommel was a massive, flawless gemstone of Sun-Amber roughly the size of a fist.
Inside the translucent amber, a miniature swirling vortex of compressed golden sand spun in perpetual motion, radiating a soft hypnotic warmth.

Even sealed within twenty-four layers of suppression glass, a harmonic frequency hummed from the blade, causing tiny specks of dust and loose sand on the stage floor to vibrate in synchronized patterns.
The Chief Auctioneer stepped forward, lightly tapping the crystal surface of the sarcophagus with his knuckles.

"Unlike the previous lot," the auctioneer explained with solemnity. "Our staff shall not be channeling mana into this weapon tonight. The ancestral sellers within the surviving Kemetian bloodlines have strictly stipulated that the awakening protocol of this blade may only be initiated by its rightful buyer upon final collection!"
He turned to face the elevated VIP suites, his amplified voice booming through the silent colosseum.

"Behold the ancestral masterpiece of the First Per-aa! Historical lore dictates that during the founding wars of the Dominion, the First Per-aa channeled a fragment of his own transcendent soul directly into the golden alloy during its forging, rendering the blade a living breathing extension of his sovereign will... When the last Per-aa fell centuries later during the fracturing of the empire, this relic was secretly hidden away in vaults, preserved by the royal bloodline until this very night!"
The auctioneer raised his hands, detailing the terrifying capabilities of the ancient sword.

"This sovereign Khopesh grants its wielder command over the elements of sand, earth, and tectonic pressure... capable of manipulating geological faults and summoning blinding sandstorms capable of suffocating entire invading armies! The sun-amber pommel acts as an inexhaustible reservoir, capable of storing and discharging devastating shockwaves! And legends whisper... that to those worthy of its resonance, the blade itself whispers ancient prophecies, warnings, and the forgotten memories of the First Per-aa directly into their soul!"
The entire amphitheater stood in paralyzed breathless awe.
The Chief Auctioneer raised his gold-headed gavel high into the air, his eyes blazing with electric fervor as he prepared to ignite the greatest bidding war in the history of the Obsidian Sanhedrin.
"We commence the final bidding for the First Khopesh of the Khemet Dominion!" the auctioneer roared with his voice shaking the bedrock.
BANG!
"The starting price is Ten Billion Spirit Credits!"
The heavy gilded gavel struck the obsidian sounding block with a bone-rattling report that echoed straight through the amphitheater of the Obsidian Sanhedrin.
BANG!

The sound rolled through the colosseum like distant thunder, but for several long suffocating seconds, not a single sound answered from the thousands of masked spectators packed into the lower stone tiers.
The number that hung suspended in radiant golden glyphs above the circular stage was simply too colossal and too terrifying for the ordinary mind to fully process.
Ten Billion Spirit Credits?!
It was a figure capable of funding the defense grids of three mid-tier metropolitan districts for an entire decade.
For the rogue Lords, independent syndicate captains, and mid-tier merchant guilds seated across the lower stone benches, ten billion credits was not merely an entry bid...
It was an impenetrable adamantine wall that permanently severed them from the proceedings.
Dozens of transponder wands across Floor Tiers One, Two, and Three were slowly, quietly lowered onto velvet armrests as bidders bowed their heads in silent awe-struck submission.
Yet, high above the common floor, within the shadowed balconies of the sovereign suites, the air did not cool.
It ignited.
BZZZZT-CHUNK!
A piercing crystalline chime echoed from the eastern balcony as VIP Suite Four flared with brilliant azure light.
[BID: VIP SUITE FOUR]
CURRENT BID: 15,000,000,000 SPIRIT CREDITS
Before the crowd could even process the five-billion-credit leap, another chime detonated from the southern mezzanine.
BZZZZT-CHUNK!
[BID: VIP SUITE NINE]
CURRENT BID: 22,000,000,000 SPIRIT CREDITS
BZZZZT-CHUNK!
[BID: VIP SUITE THREE]
CURRENT BID: 30,000,000,000 SPIRIT CREDITS
The numbers climbed with vicious dizzying momentum.
It was no longer a standard auction... it was a brutal war of financial attrition fought between continental oligarchs, corporate directorates, and ancient bloodlines.
Every single pulse of the scoreboard erased billions of credits in the blink of an eye, the digital display flashing violently as the stakes reached astronomical heights.
Across the arena in VIP Suite Twelve, Cedric Blackwood stood gripping the mahogany railing with trembling bloodless knuckles.
His eyes were bloodshot, and burning with desperation.
Moments earlier, when his terminal had flashed a system error during the bidding war for the Tier-5 Calamity Core, he had believed his family’s credit lines were permanently frozen.

But as he frantically tapped the interface now, the display cleared... the earlier lockout had merely been a momentary data synchronization lag caused by the systems recalibrating against the massive flux of high-tier bids.

"I can still take it..." Cedric muttered, his voice cracking into a whisper as he wiped a bead of cold sweat from his lip. "The weapon... If I secure the First Per-aa’s blade, my father will forgive everything. The Council will grant me a seat on the directorate..."
He reached out, his hand shaking violently as he hovered his thumb over the terminal.
Yet, as his eyes locked onto the central scoreboard, his breath hitched in his throat.
BZZZZT-CHUNK!
[BID : VIP SUITE NINE]
CURRENT BID: 45,000,000,000 SPIRIT CREDITS
BZZZZT-CHUNK!
[BID : VIP SUITE FOUR]
CURRENT BID: 55,000,000,000 SPIRIT CREDITS
Fifty-five billion credits...
Cedric’s finger hovered over the glass terminal, completely paralyzed.
A cold creeping dread wrapped around his chest like an iron vice.
His earlier arrogant bravado began to curdle into suffocating doubt.
To push past fifty-five billion meant putting the ancestral deed to House Blackwood’s eastern mining territories on the line.
If he bid and won, he would be a hero but if he bid and another monster pushed the price higher, he would be trapped in an irreversible legal forfeiture that would ruin his lineage forever.
The more the bids ticked upward, the more his resolve crumbled into dust.
"Damn it... damn it all..." Cedric whimpered, his teeth chattering against each other as his hand slowly sank back down to his side.
The young master who had bragged about bottomless wealth was completely broken by the sheer, merciless scale of the numbers flashing before his eyes.

Down on the carpet behind him, the brown-haired maid watched his trembling back, a quiet solemn breath escaping her lips as she realized the storm of his pride had finally crashed against an immovable mountain.
BZZZZT-CHUNK!
Then came the chime that froze the blood in every vein in the room.

High above the northern mezzanine, the display of VIP Suite One... the mysterious box that had effortlessly obliterated Cedric with a forty-billion-credit hammer minutes earlier lit up with a blinding icy-silver luminescence.
[BID : VIP SUITE ONE]
CURRENT BID: 80,000,000,000 SPIRIT CREDITS
Eighty Billion Spirit Credits.
A dead tomb-like hush descended upon the entire colosseum.
VIP Suites Three, Four, and Nine instantly went pitch-black, their consoles falling silent as their delegates conceded defeat.
An eighty-billion-credit strike was not simply a bid... it was an execution order designed to clear the entire room in a single breath.
Inside VIP Suite Seven, Harper Whitmore stood rigidly before the one-way panoramic glass.
Her violet eyes were wide, the pupils dilated with an intense burning fire that seemed to crackle with raw lightning.
Her breath came in shallow rapid draws, her slender fingers digging into the brass edge of the mahogany table until the metal groaned beneath her grip.
’Eighty billion...’ Harper thought, her heart hammering against her ribs like a trapped bird.
Behind her confident exterior, a sudden cold tremor of fear rippled through her stomach.

House Whitmore’s executive committee which consisted of only herself and the High Council had authorized a colossal war chest to secure the Khopesh for themselves, but even the wealthiest sovereign conglomerates had limits.
The entity in Suite One was bidding with the casual indifference of someone who viewed tens of billions of credits as loose pocket change.
Beside her, Seraphina sat up straight on Silas’s lap, her crimson eyes narrowing into sharp slits.

"That is the power of Suite One, huh?" Seraphina murmured, her haughty voice carrying a serious edge. "Whoever sits within that chamber commands the liquidity of an entire dynasty. Harper... does your money extend far enough to challenge such a presence or do you want help? I can lend you money you know..."
Harper swallowed the dry knot in her throat. She looked down at Silas, who was watching her with calm blue eyes.
’Help?’
Silas reached out, his large warm hand covering her trembling fingers on the table, giving them a firm squeeze.
"If this is what you came here for, Harper," Silas said. "don’t hold back and take it... Don’t be afraid to ask for help either, but don’t ask from me though, I’m broke."
Harper looked at his face, looked at the confidence in his eyes, and the lingering fear in her chest instantly vanished, replaced by an explosive and reckless surge of pure determination.
A fierce radiant grin broke across her face.
"Hold onto your seats," Harper whispered.
She didn’t just tap an increment as she slammed her palm flat against the custom numerical array, keying in a figure so high that it would be spoken of in the underground markets for decades to come.
’This should keep you from keeping up...’
BZZZZT-CHUNK!
A crimson shockwave of holographic light detonated across the central ring, tearing through the darkness of the amphitheater with an authoritative roar.
’...And there goes Dad’s savings.’
[BID: VIP SUITE SEVEN]
CURRENT BID: 150,000,000,000 SPIRIT CREDITS
One Hundred and Fifty Billion Spirit Credits.
The entire colosseum did not just fall silent... it felt as though the very oxygen in the room had been violently sucked into a dimensional void.
Down on the lower tiers, several masked syndicate bosses stumbled backward out of their seats, clutching their chests in disbelieving horror.
In VIP Suite Twelve, Cedric Blackwood fell completely flat onto his back on the carpet, his eyes rolled back in his head as his mind completely shut down from shock.
And high in the northern mezzanine, inside VIP Suite One... the icy silver light flickered once, twice, and slowly dimmed into darkness.
The mysterious entity had finally conceded.
On the circular stage, the Chief Auctioneer stood trembling from head to toe, his gold-headed gavel shaking violently in his gloved hand.
He looked up at the dark, reflective glass of Suite Seven with reverent terror.
"One... One hundred and fifty billion Spirit Credits from VIP Suite Seven!" the auctioneer screamed, his voice breaking through the crowd in a hysterical crescendo. "Going once!"
"Going twice!"
BANG!
"SOLD! TO THE TITANS OF VIP SUITE SEVEN!"
The entire amphitheater erupted into a deafening chaotic roar of cheers, gasps, and hysterical shouts that shook the very bedrock of the place.
Inside VIP Suite Seven, the moment the gavel struck the podium, Harper let out a high-pitched squeal of victory.
"WE GOT IT!" Harper cheered wildly, throwing her arms into the air.

Without a single second of hesitation, the energized Lightning Lord spun around, threw herself onto Silas’s chest, wrapped both of her arms tightly around his neck, and planted a loud kiss right on his cheek.
SMACK!
Silas’s eyes widened slightly in surprise, his cheek burning with the warm, electric sensation of her lips as a helpless amused smile spread across his face.
’I can’t even say anything... She gave me money.’
Sitting directly beneath them, Seraphina’s delicate eyebrows twitched violently.
A deep, incandescent crimson blush erupted across the noblewoman’s porcelain cheeks, her red eyes narrowing into lethal daggers as she aggressively shoved Harper’s shoulder away.

chapters.title: Chapter 402: Obsidian Sanhedrin [VIII / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: "Cease this vulgar undignified display of public affection at once!" Seraphina snapped sharply, her melodic voice trembling with flustered indignation as she smoothed down her phoenix-silk gown. "You have secured what you wanted, Harper! There is no justification for slobbering over my future Husband like a wild beast!"

"He’s my date tonight, Princess! I can kiss him whenever I want!" Harper laughed unrepentantly, sticking her tongue out before turning to Silas with a radiant breathless smile. "Come on, handsome. Let’s get out of this box and head down to the private retrieval chambers before the crowd starts a riot..."
Seraphina gave a haughty delicate sniff, though she gracefully rose from Silas’s lap and extended her hand to allow him to stand.
"For once, the woman speaks sense. We should collect our acquisitions and vacate this establishment."
Down on the central stage, the colossal crystal sarcophagus containing the glowing Khopesh smoothly sank into the subterranean mechanism with a deep hydraulic hiss.
The Chief Auctioneer bowed so low his porcelain demon mask nearly touched the red obsidian floor with his amplified voice echoing across the roaring arena.

"The midnight session of the Obsidian Sanhedrin is officially concluded! We extend our deepest gratitude to all honored patrons! The master perimeter blast doors are now unlocking... Guests with standard claim tokens may proceed to the Great Lower Retrieval Hall! Patrons occupying private VIP suites are cordially directed to the private high-tier retrieval chambers corresponding to your suite numbers! May the shadows favor your path!"
Outside VIP Suite Twelve, the heavy iron door slammed open with a violent concussive crash.
SLAM!
Cedric stormed out into the plush, emerald-carpeted corridor like a rabid dog.
His tailored gale-silk suit was rumpled, his slicked-back blond hair was sticking out in sweaty tufts, and his handsome face was twisted into a beet-red mask of pure malice.

"Young Master, please! Stop!" his maid pleaded frantically, rushing out behind him with her hands clasped to her chest. "You cannot cause a disturbance here! The Sanhedrin’s sovereign enforcers will—"
"Shut up! Shut your worthless mouth!" Cedric roared, deaf to reason.

The humiliation of losing every single lot, combined with the agonizing memory of that slap in Weaver’s Spire and the crushing realization that he had achieved nothing all evening, had driven him completely insane.
He marched straight down the private hallway, stopping directly before the towering, dark-iron double doors of VIP Suite Seven.
"OPEN THIS DAMN DOOR!" Cedric screamed, raising his fists and hammering violently against the reinforced iron panels.
THUD! THUD! THUD!

"I know who you are! You think you can hide behind a numbered suite and mock House Blackwood?! Come out here and face me, you cowardly vermin! I will have my father execute your entire bloodline! OPEN UP!"
CREAK... CLICK!
The heavy dark-iron latch disengaged with a smooth oiled click as the massive door slowly swung inward.

Cedric’s bloodshot eyes flared with murderous rage. Without even looking to see who stood in the threshold, he coiled his right arm, channeling a violent gust of green wind mana around his knuckles, and threw a full-force bone-shattering punch straight toward the doorway.
"DIE, YOU BAS—"
SWISH!
The strike never landed.

Standing in the doorway was not a frightened bidder, but the senior Floor Butler of the Obsidian Sanhedrin... the tall silver-masked elder in the immaculate black tailcoat who had escorted Silas’s group hours earlier.
With the effortless fluid grace of a retired shadow assassin, the butler simply tilted his head two inches to the left, allowing Cedric’s mana-infused fist to whistle harmlessly through empty air.

Before Cedric could even register the miss, the butler pivoted on his heel, with his posture completely straight, and brought his polished leather dress shoe forward in a compact accurate upward snap directly between the young master’s spread thighs.
CRUNCH-THWACK!
The impact was sickeningly solid.
Cedric’s pale gray eyes instantly bulged out of his skull until they looked ready to pop from their sockets.
His mouth formed a silent gaping ’O’ of incomprehensible agony.
Every single drop of color drained from his face in a microsecond, replaced by a sickly greenish-white hue as his vocal cords completely seized up.
THUD!

Cedric collapsed straight onto his knees, curling into a tight pathetic fetal ball on the emerald carpet while clutching his groin with both hands, letting out a series of high-pitched breathless wheezes.
"Heeek... huuuugk... m-my..." Cedric choked, tears and snot streaming down his contorted face as he writhed in the dust.
The butler smoothly adjusted the cuffs of his white silk gloves, looking down at the groveling noble scion through the eyeholes of his silver crow mask with chilling disdain.

"House Thorne or otherwise," the butler spoke in a calm voice that carried the cold weight of an executioner’s axe, "the laws of the Obsidian Sanhedrin are absolute. Any assault upon our staff or violation of private suite thresholds is met with immediate physical correction... Be grateful I utilized regular force rather than a void-severing strike, Young Master Blackwood. This suite is vacant and the patrons departed through the private lift three minutes ago."
The butler turned on his heel, stepping back into the corridor and vanishing into the shadows without another word.
"Young Master!" the maid gasped, rushing over and dropping to her knees beside him. "Are you alright?!"
"I’ll... kill him..." Cedric wheezed through clenched teeth, trembling uncontrollably as he clutched his crotch. "I’ll kill... every single one of them..."
BRRRRRRR-CHIME!
Suddenly, a loud clear ringtone echoed through the corridor.
Cedric flinched, groaning in agony as he reached into his inner suit pocket with trembling sweaty fingers.
The dampening wards had disengaged as the master blast doors opened, restoring full cellular and network coverage across the whole place once more..
Flashing brightly on the glowing glass screen of his smartphone was the terrifying caller ID.
[LORD BLACKWOOD]
Cedric’s heart skipped three consecutive beats.
A sudden desperate hope flared in his mind.
If he explained that the auction house workers had assaulted him, his father would deploy House Blackwood’s private military to level this entire facility.
Cedric frantically swiped the screen, pressing the phone to his ear with a trembling hand.

"F-Father!" Cedric cried out, his voice cracking into a pathetic tearful whimper. "Father, you have to send the execution legion right now! The staff here in the underground market assaulted me! A butler kicked me, and the delegates in Suite Seven—"
"Silence," a deep frigid voice interrupted from the other end of the line.
The voice was cold and completely lacking any sort of paternal warmth.
That was the voice of a ruthless clan patriarch who cared only for power and territory.

"I did not contact you to listen to the pathetic whimpering of a spoiled child," Lord Blackwood stated flatly. "The High Council has just received the encrypted broadcast of the grand finale lot... Did you secure the First Khopesh of the Khemet Dominion?"
Cedric froze.
The air in his throat turned to solid ice. His hands began to shake so violently that the phone nearly slipped from his fingers.
"I... Father, listen to me, there was a monster in Suite Seven who bid one hundred and fifty billion, and Suite One—"
"Answer the question, Cedric," his father’s voice dropped. "Did you secure the weapon? Yes or no?"
Cedric swallowed the bitter bile rising in his throat, his voice dropping into a tiny humiliated squeak.
BEEP.
The line went dead.
Cedric stared blankly at the dark screen of his phone, his mouth hanging open in utter disbelief.
His father hadn’t even waited for an explanation... He had simply discarded him like a piece of worthless trash.
Down on the floor beside him, the maid slowly lowered her head, looking away to hide the quiet satisfied smile spreading across her lips.
’Thank you whoever was here in Room 7...’
Deep within the secluded fortified VIP part of the facility, Silas, Harper, Seraphina, and Reginald stepped out of the private glass lift and entered Private Retrieval Room Seven.
The room was vast, elegant, and secured behind twelve inches of enchanted adamantine plating.
The walls were lined with glowing runic arrays that hummed with soft azure light, maintaining a completely stable environment.
Standing behind a polished black-quartz counter in the center of the room was a stunning senior receptionist wearing a flawless silver-embroidered velvet dress and white silk gloves.
The moment the group crossed the threshold, she bowed with deep, impeccable grace.

"Welcome, esteemed patrons of VIP Suite Seven," the receptionist greeted them with a melodic voice. "I have the immense privilege of managing the final settlement and item transfer for your acquisitions tonight... Before we disengage the containment arrays, we must formally process the consolidated transaction ledgers."
She tapped her glass console, projecting two glowing holographic balance sheets into the air before them.
The first ledger displayed the items on one side.
[The Twin Phantoms of the Mist: 35,000,000 SC]
[The Tear of the Slumbering World: 45,000,000 SC]
[Astral Void-Titanium Alloy (8-Ton Shipment): 70,000,000 SC]
[The Scepter of the Dune-Sovereign: 65,000,000 SC]
[70-Piece Frost-Drake Battalion Armor & Spear Set: 120,000,000 SC]
[The Tide-Bringer of the Leviathan’s Wake: 1,500,000,000 SC]
[The First Khopesh of the Khemet Dominion: 150,000,000,000 SC]
[TOTAL LEDGER: 151,835,000,000 Spirit Credits]
The second ledger displayed the items claimed on the other side too. It had been reported that they wanted it separated and the Receptionist did just that.
[The Primordial Will of the Blazing Chimera (Tier-3 Beast Will): 100,000,000 SC]
[Ancient Void-Chrysolite Jewelry Set (Spousal Tribute): 50,000,000 SC]
[Phoenix-Ash Alchemical Crucible (Ancient Relic): 75,000,000 SC]
[TOTAL LEDGER: 225,000,000 Spirit Credits]

"Please note," the receptionist added with a polite professional smile, "as per the sovereign charter of the Obsidian Sanhedrin, all bids are legally binding upon the fall of the gavel... Failure to settle the authorized balance results in immediate asset liquidation and permanent bounty placement."
"We are well aware of that," Harper said with a radiant confident smirk.
She stepped straight up to the terminal, pulled her sleek black House Whitmore executive corporate card from her pocket, and pressed it firmly against the glowing transaction scanner.
BEEP-BEEP-CHIME!
A brilliant cascade of golden light erupted from the terminal as the credit balance cleared instantly, verified through the direct reserve vaults of the Lord Association Building’s primary treasury.
Beside her, Reginald stepped forward with silent dignified grace. Seraphina had returned the card because she wanted him to do it.
The veteran butler retrieved the black military executive card of House Bloom from his coat, tapping it against the second scanner.
BEEP-BEEP-CHIME!
The two hundred and twenty-five million credit balance flashed green and cleared in a fraction of a second.
"Both accounts have been settled in full," the receptionist beamed, bowing deeply. "Allow me to present your acquisitions."
She turned, waving her gloved hand toward the back of the room.
HUMMMMM!
With a smooth hum, the reinforced wall behind the counter parted, revealing seven individual velvet-lined anti-gravity pedestals, each bathed in a focused column of soft white light.
Silas, Harper, and Seraphina walked forward, their eyes taking in the breathtaking array of sovereign treasures.
Harper walked straight past the smaller pedestals, her violet eyes locking onto the central octagonal crystal display case resting at the very back.
Inside the case lay the colossal, six-foot golden Khopesh.
The hawk-beaked blade gleamed with an ethereal warm luster and its hieroglyphic bind-runes pulsing with slow amber light.
The sun-amber gem in the solid-gold pommel swirled with miniature golden sandstorms, radiating a gentle hypnotic warmth that brushed against Harper’s skin even through the glass.
Harper reached out, her slender fingers gently touching the smooth, cool surface of the crystal case with a soft smile touching her lips.
"It’s truly magnificent," Harper whispered softly.
The receptionist walked over, stopping respectfully beside the case.

"Indeed," the receptionist smiled. "The internal appraisal cabal has finalized the archival translation... The weapon’s true, ancient sovereign title, etched into the First Era records of the Khemetian royal family, is The Per-aa’s Judgment."
She reached into her coat, producing a delicate gold-inlaid runic key.

"The full soul-bonding and activation sequence is embedded directly within the blade’s core array," the receptionist explained. "The moment you withdraw the weapon from the containment glass and introduce your spiritual mana, the binding trial shall initiate."
Harper tilted her head, her violet eyes gleaming with sharp curiosity.

"Can we verify its authenticity before we leave?" Harper asked, looking at the receptionist. "I don’t doubt your establishment’s appraisal, but like that pirate saber earlier... I want to feel the true weight of its strength."

"Of course," the receptionist nodded with confidence. "The containment glass is equipped with an external conduit... If you place your palm flat against the central amber rune on the glass and channel a single, concentrated drop of your own mana, the sword will respond with a pulse."
Harper took a breath.
She placed her right palm flat against the glowing amber rune etched into the center of the crystal case.
’Haah... It can’t be that bad.’
She focused her internal core, sending a tiny delicate thread of purple lightning mana through her fingertips.
FZZZZT.
The moment the lightning mana made contact with the rune—
BOOOOOOOOOOM!
The golden blade of The Per-aa’s Judgment flared with an incandescent burst of pure solar-gold light.
SHUUUUUUU!
A colossal surge of ancient mana detonated outward through the glass.
In a fraction of a microsecond, an overwhelming spiritual vision of an endless, burning desert beneath three blazing suns flooded straight into Harper’s consciousness.

The deafening primeval roar of a million slaughtered rift beasts echoed directly inside her skull, accompanied by the crushing suffocating weight of a thousand-mile sandstorm pressing against her lungs.
"O-OH...!" Harper gasped with her entire body violently flinching backward.

sentences.text: "Cease this vulgar undignified display of public affection at once!" Seraphina snapped sharply, her melodic voice trembling with flustered indignation as she smoothed down her phoenix-silk gown.
"You have secured what you wanted, Harper!
There is no justification for slobbering over my future Husband like a wild beast!"
"He’s my date tonight, Princess!
I can kiss him whenever I want!" Harper laughed unrepentantly, sticking her tongue out before turning to Silas with a radiant breathless smile.
"Come on, handsome.
Let’s get out of this box and head down to the private retrieval chambers before the crowd starts a riot..."
Seraphina gave a haughty delicate sniff, though she gracefully rose from Silas’s lap and extended her hand to allow him to stand.
"For once, the woman speaks sense.
We should collect our acquisitions and vacate this establishment."
Down on the central stage, the colossal crystal sarcophagus containing the glowing Khopesh smoothly sank into the subterranean mechanism with a deep hydraulic hiss.
The Chief Auctioneer bowed so low his porcelain demon mask nearly touched the red obsidian floor with his amplified voice echoing across the roaring arena.
"The midnight session of the Obsidian Sanhedrin is officially concluded!
We extend our deepest gratitude to all honored patrons!

Guests with standard claim tokens may proceed to the Great Lower Retrieval Hall!
Patrons occupying private VIP suites are cordially directed to the private high-tier retrieval chambers corresponding to your suite numbers!

SWISH!
The strike never landed.

Before Cedric could even register the miss, the butler pivoted on his heel, with his posture completely straight, and brought his polished leather dress shoe forward in a compact accurate upward snap directly between the young master’s spread thighs.
CRUNCH-THWACK!
The impact was sickeningly solid.
Cedric’s pale gray eyes instantly bulged out of his skull until they looked ready to pop from their sockets.
His mouth formed a silent gaping ’O’ of incomprehensible agony.
Every single drop of color drained from his face in a microsecond, replaced by a sickly greenish-white hue as his vocal cords completely seized up.
THUD!

Cedric collapsed straight onto his knees, curling into a tight pathetic fetal ball on the emerald carpet while clutching his groin with both hands, letting out a series of high-pitched breathless wheezes.
"Heeek... huuuugk... m-my..." Cedric choked, tears and snot streaming down his contorted face as he writhed in the dust.
The butler smoothly adjusted the cuffs of his white silk gloves, looking down at the groveling noble scion through the eyeholes of his silver crow mask with chilling disdain.
"House Thorne or otherwise," the butler spoke in a calm voice that carried the cold weight of an executioner’s axe, "the laws of the Obsidian Sanhedrin are absolute.
Any assault upon our staff or violation of private suite thresholds is met with immediate physical correction...
Be grateful I utilized regular force rather than a void-severing strike, Young Master Blackwood.
This suite is vacant and the patrons departed through the private lift three minutes ago."
The butler turned on his heel, stepping back into the corridor and vanishing into the shadows without another word.
"Young Master!" the maid gasped, rushing over and dropping to her knees beside him.
"Are you alright?!"
"I’ll... kill him..." Cedric wheezed through clenched teeth, trembling uncontrollably as he clutched his crotch.
"I’ll kill... every single one of them..."
BRRRRRRR-CHIME!
Suddenly, a loud clear ringtone echoed through the corridor.

The dampening wards had disengaged as the master blast doors opened, restoring full cellular and network coverage across the whole place once more..

chapters.title: Chapter 403: Grounded [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: She stumbled two paces, her boots skidding across the quartz floorboards as her hand ripped away from the glass.
"Haah... Haah... Haah..."
Her chest heaved rapidly, her breath coming in shallow gasps as beads of cold sweat broke out across her forehead.
Silas was at her side in an instant.
His large hand caught her by the shoulder with his grip firm as his golden-ringed blue eyes scanned her face with deep genuine concern. "Harper! Are you alright? What happened?"
Harper rested her trembling hand against Silas’s broad chest, taking several deep breaths of the cool room air.
Slowly, the shock faded from her eyes, replaced by a breathless triumphant grin that stretched from ear to ear.

"I’m fine... I’m more than fine," Harper laughed breathlessly, looking up into his eyes before turning her gaze back to the golden Khopesh with pure awe. "Holy hell... that was just a single pulse. Silas... this weapon is the real deal."
Silas let out a relieved breath, his lips curving into a satisfied smile as he patted her shoulder.
"Good."
With the verification complete, Silas stepped over to the pedestals holding his acquisitions.
He looked at the exquisite emerald pendant of The Tear of the Slumbering World, imagining the gentle radiant smile Eluned would wear when he presented it to her in the house.
He looked at the golden Scepter of the Dune-Sovereign, knowing how much Kadi’s eyes would light up when she held the powerful weapon in her hands.
’Haah...’

He looked at the massive crate holding the eight tons of Astral Void-Titanium Alloy and the long racks containing the seventy matching sets of Frost-Drake Carapace Bucklers and Short-Spears that would go to the others.
’Thora is going to have a field day with this...’
And finally, he looked at The Tide-Bringer of the Leviathan’s Wake which was the massive curved pirate saber Harper had bought for him.
’I know this has a connection with Morwenna.’
Silas smiled.
"Alright, time to go into the Inventory..."
SHING! SHING! SHING!
With a series of soft blue flashes, Silas channeled his Lord Core, smoothly drawing all five massive lots directly into his Lord Inventory.
Beside him, Harper tapped her spatial ring, drawing The Twin Phantoms of the Mist and the massive containment case of The Per-aa’s Judgment into her storage with a happy hum.
Seraphina gracefully stepped up to her pedestals.
With a delicate wave of her manicured hand, she swept the glowing chimera beast will and the ancient phoenix-ash crucible into her family storage ring.
However, Seraphina did not store the velvet case holding the Ancient Void-Chrysolite Jewelry.
The crimson-haired heiress delicately lifted the heavy obsidian necklace from its velvet cushion.
The dark polished void-metal chain gleamed with a deep, mesmerizing luster as the central black gem thrummed with a soothing mana-acceleration current.
Seraphina turned around, taking slow, graceful steps until she stood directly in front of Silas.
Silas looked down at her, raising an eyebrow in mild curiosity.
Seraphina raised both of her slender arms, her fingers holding the dark necklace open.
A vibrant burning crimson blush swept up her porcelain neck, painting her cheeks and the delicate tips of her ears in brilliant red.
She looked down at the collar of his shirt, her long eyelashes fluttering as she carefully draped the heavy obsidian chain around Silas’s neck, fastening the silver clasp behind his dark hair.
The cool void-metal settled comfortably against Silas’s collarbone, immediately sending a pleasant refreshing pulse of mana recovery circulating through his core.
Seraphina reached out with both hands, gently smoothing down the dark fabric over his broad shoulders.
Her melodic voice dropped into a tiny high-pitched squeak that was barely audible in the quiet room.

"It... it suits you," Seraphina mumbled, her face burning as she stubbornly looked at his top shirt button rather than meeting his eyes. "Consider it... an official non-negotiable spousal tribute from House Bloom. It is a tangible symbol of... of how much I have come to like you. You are forbidden from removing it."
Silas looked down at the flustered adorable noblewoman standing before him.
A gentle warm smile spread across his rugged face.
He reached up, lightly resting his fingers over the cool black gemstone, before looking directly into her trembling crimson eyes.
"Thank you, Seraphina," Silas said softly. "I really like it. I won’t take it off."
Seraphina’s breath caught in her throat.
Seeing his warm genuine smile sent her heart doing violent, chaotic somersaults inside her chest.
Her blush intensified to a nuclear level with steam practically rising from her ears as she quickly turned her back to him, coughing into her silk handkerchief to regain her noble composure.
Harper walked over, linking her arm playfully through Silas’s other side with a wide radiant grin.
"Well, squad," Harper beamed, stretching her arms above her head with a contented sigh. "We bought half an underground market... Phase Five is officially complete. Why don’t we finally head home?"
Silas chuckled, feeling the weight of the long unforgettable day finally settling into his bones.
"Home sounds fantastic."
Standing near the exit doors, Reginald quietly lowered his book.
As he looked across the room at his young lady blushing furiously beside the towering young Lord, a rare respectful smirk touched the corner of the old assassin’s lips.

’A common-born who commands strength, possesses unshakable composure, and treats my Lady with genuine warmth...’ Reginald thought, closing the book and bowing smoothly. ’I think Silas Graves is a truly exceptional match for my Lady.’
The purr of the custom midnight-purple sports coupe settled into an idle sound along the quiet curb of the modest residential street in Silverleaf District.
The velvet cloak embroidered with the Whitmore crest and the obsidian crow mask had already been stowed securely away in Harper’s Lord Inventory.
"Haah..."
Silas stood on the pavement in his familiar comfortable clothes feeling the cool crisp late-night breeze against his skin.
"What a night..."
The heavy void-chrysolite necklace Seraphina had gifted him still rested cool against his collarbone beneath his collar.
Around thirty minutes earlier, when they had finally ascended from the depths of the Obsidian Sanhedrin into the upper tiers of Valoria City, Seraphina and Reginald had parted ways with them.

The Bloom family limousine had arrived remotely, and with a flustered glance and a strict reminder that Silas was "mandated" to wear her tribute, Seraphina had glided into her vehicle under Reginald’s watchful escort.
That left just the two of them.
The scissor-door of the sports coupe hissed open, and Harper stepped out onto the sidewalk beside him.
The golden glow of a nearby streetlamp caught the vibrant violet strands of her hair, casting soft shadows across her radiant flushed face.
She walked up to him with hands tucked behind her back, rocking lightly on the heels of her boots with a playful teasing smile that practically sparked with energy.

"You know, Silas..." Harper purred, tilting her head up to meet his blue eyes. "While we were at the restaurant earlier, my little sister texted me complaining that she was bored and practically begged to sleep over at your place with Lia. Which got me thinking... what if I invited myself inside and slept over tonight, too?"
Silas couldn’t help but raise an amused deadpan eyebrow at the purple-haired Lightning Lord.

"Can you really afford to play hooky and crash on my couch right now?" Silas asked dryly with a smirk tugging at his lips. "You literally just dropped one hundred and fifty billion Spirit Credits on an ancient Khopesh... Aren’t your Business partners waiting for you to deliver the weapon or so?"
Even now, just saying the number out loud made Silas flinch internally.
One hundred and fifty billion.
It was a sum so mind-bogglingly astronomical that it felt completely surreal to him.
’I need to make more money...’
Harper let out an exaggerated dramatic sigh, rolling her shoulders and shrugging in defeat.

"Ugh, don’t remind me," Harper groaned, though a proud victorious smirk lingered at the corners of her lips. "You’re right, unfortunately... The moment the blast doors opened, my phone was bombarded with thirty-seven high-priority pings from the board. If I don’t report to the primary research bunker within the hour to oversee the initial calibration, my people are going to have a collective heart attack."
Harper reached out, her slender fingers slipping smoothly into Silas’s large, calloused hand.
She squeezed his fingers firmly, her glowing violet eyes looking directly into his with an open warmth.

"Still... business aside, tonight was incredible," Harper murmured softly, her thumb tracing the rough skin along the back of his hand. "This was genuinely the best date I’ve ever had in my life, Silas. My first real one, too..."

Silas looked down at the fierce energetic Lord who had spent the entire afternoon to evening alternating between tearing down arcade records, threatening high-society snobs, and showering him in unimaginable fortunes just to see him smile.
’Haah...’
His rugged features softened, and he gave her hand a gentle reassuring squeeze in return.
"I’m really glad," Silas said. "I’m honored that I could be the one to give you your first and favorite date, Harper."
Harper’s face lit up, a rosy blush blooming across her cheeks.
She took a half-step closer, closing the distance between them until the sweet scent of her perfume rolled over Silas’s senses.

"You better remember that, handsome," Harper whispered, her eyes dancing with bold mischief. "Because the next time I have a free evening, I’m claiming you all over again. We’re going on another date."
Silas chuckled, rubbing the back of his neck with his free hand.

"Well, you might have to wait in line for that one. Once I wrap things up here, I’m heading back into the Sovereign Realm for quite a while. My territory needs heavy construction work, especially with all the raw titanium and battalion gear we just secured."
Harper immediately puffed out her cheeks, letting out a cute exaggerated pout.
"Hey! Don’t you dare go vanishing into the Sovereign Realm for a month and leave me hanging!" Harper whined.
Before Silas could offer a reply, Harper suddenly leaned forward, rising gracefully onto her tiptoes.
She caught the lapels of his shirt, pulled his broad frame down, and pressed her soft warm lips firmly against his.
SMACK!
Silas’s eyes widened for a fraction of a second before he naturally leaned into the embrace with his large arms wrapping comfortably around her slender waist.
The kiss started eager and electric, her lips moving against his with breathless intensity.
But as Silas parted his lips, Harper boldly deepened the contact, seeking his tongue with hers.
SMACK... SLIDE!

It was hot, passionate, and slightly clumsy... it was instantly obvious that for all of her loud, confident flirting and bold posturing, the formidable Lightning Lord had very little actual kissing experience.
She was enthusiastic and adorably unrefined with her tongue tangling with his as she leaned her entire body weight against his chest.
SMACK!
"Mmmph~"
After several lingering toe-curling seconds, Harper broke the kiss, pulling back with a sharp gasp for air.
Her violet eyes were completely dilated, her face flushed a brilliant burning crimson that reached all the way to the tips of her ears.
She looked up at Silas with wide dazed eyes, her chest heaving as she frantically wiped her swollen lips with the back of her sleeve.
"I—I have to go!" Harper stammered hastily, her voice cracking in flustered panic. "The council is waiting! Goodbye, Silas!"
Without waiting for a response, the elite Lord practically scrambled backward, dove into the driver’s seat of her sports coupe, and slammed the scissor-door shut.
ROOOOAAAR!
The mana engine screamed to life, and with a sudden screeching chirp of tires, the purple vehicle launched forward like a guided missile, vanishing down the boulevard in a blur of neon exhaust.
Silas stood on the empty sidewalk for a long moment, touching his lips with his fingers where the lingering taste of Harper’s mouth still tingled.
A slow amused chuckle rumbled in his chest.
"Crazy girl," Silas muttered affectionately.
Shaking his head, Silas turned around, walked up the short concrete pathway to the front gate of his apartment, and opened it.
He stepped through, latching the gate securely behind him, and walked up the three porch steps to the front door.
He touched the door.
CREAK!
The warm scent of food immediately greeted him from the hallway but before Silas could even take off his boots, he froze dead in his tracks.
Standing dead center in the hallway, blocking the path with her arms crossed tightly over her chest and her weight shifted onto one hip, was Lia.

The young girl tapped her slippered foot against the wooden floorboard and her sharp eyes narrowed into two deadly slits as she glared up at her towering older brother with pure, unadulterated suspicion.
"Well, well, well," Lia began. "Look who finally decided to grace us with his presence. We haven’t seen a single hair on your head since yesterday afternoon, Big Bro."

sentences.text: She stumbled two paces, her boots skidding across the quartz floorboards as her hand ripped away from the glass.
"Haah...
Haah...
Haah..."
Her chest heaved rapidly, her breath coming in shallow gasps as beads of cold sweat broke out across her forehead.
Silas was at her side in an instant.
His large hand caught her by the shoulder with his grip firm as his golden-ringed blue eyes scanned her face with deep genuine concern.
"Harper!
Are you alright?
What happened?"
Harper rested her trembling hand against Silas’s broad chest, taking several deep breaths of the cool room air.
Slowly, the shock faded from her eyes, replaced by a breathless triumphant grin that stretched from ear to ear.
"I’m fine...
I’m more than fine," Harper laughed breathlessly, looking up into his eyes before turning her gaze back to the golden Khopesh with pure awe.
"Holy hell... that was just a single pulse.
Silas... this weapon is the real deal."
Silas let out a relieved breath, his lips curving into a satisfied smile as he patted her shoulder.
"Good."
With the verification complete, Silas stepped over to the pedestals holding his acquisitions.
He looked at the exquisite emerald pendant of The Tear of the Slumbering World, imagining the gentle radiant smile Eluned would wear when he presented it to her in the house.
He looked at the golden Scepter of the Dune-Sovereign, knowing how much Kadi’s eyes would light up when she held the powerful weapon in her hands.
’Haah...’

He looked at the massive crate holding the eight tons of Astral Void-Titanium Alloy and the long racks containing the seventy matching sets of Frost-Drake Carapace Bucklers and Short-Spears that would go to the others.
’Thora is going to have a field day with this...’
And finally, he looked at The Tide-Bringer of the Leviathan’s Wake which was the massive curved pirate saber Harper had bought for him.
’I know this has a connection with Morwenna.’
Silas smiled.
"Alright, time to go into the Inventory..."
SHING!
SHING!
SHING!
With a series of soft blue flashes, Silas channeled his Lord Core, smoothly drawing all five massive lots directly into his Lord Inventory.
Beside him, Harper tapped her spatial ring, drawing The Twin Phantoms of the Mist and the massive containment case of The Per-aa’s Judgment into her storage with a happy hum.
Seraphina gracefully stepped up to her pedestals.
With a delicate wave of her manicured hand, she swept the glowing chimera beast will and the ancient phoenix-ash crucible into her family storage ring.
However, Seraphina did not store the velvet case holding the Ancient Void-Chrysolite Jewelry.
The crimson-haired heiress delicately lifted the heavy obsidian necklace from its velvet cushion.
The dark polished void-metal chain gleamed with a deep, mesmerizing luster as the central black gem thrummed with a soothing mana-acceleration current.
Seraphina turned around, taking slow, graceful steps until she stood directly in front of Silas.
Silas looked down at her, raising an eyebrow in mild curiosity.
Seraphina raised both of her slender arms, her fingers holding the dark necklace open.
A vibrant burning crimson blush swept up her porcelain neck, painting her cheeks and the delicate tips of her ears in brilliant red.
She looked down at the collar of his shirt, her long eyelashes fluttering as she carefully draped the heavy obsidian chain around Silas’s neck, fastening the silver clasp behind his dark hair.
The cool void-metal settled comfortably against Silas’s collarbone, immediately sending a pleasant refreshing pulse of mana recovery circulating through his core.
Seraphina reached out with both hands, gently smoothing down the dark fabric over his broad shoulders.
Her melodic voice dropped into a tiny high-pitched squeak that was barely audible in the quiet room.
"It... it suits you," Seraphina mumbled, her face burning as she stubbornly looked at his top shirt button rather than meeting his eyes.
"Consider it... an official non-negotiable spousal tribute from House Bloom.
It is a tangible symbol of... of how much I have come to like you.
You are forbidden from removing it."
Silas looked down at the flustered adorable noblewoman standing before him.
A gentle warm smile spread across his rugged face.
He reached up, lightly resting his fingers over the cool black gemstone, before looking directly into her trembling crimson eyes.
"Thank you, Seraphina," Silas said softly.
"I really like it.
I won’t take it off."
Seraphina’s breath caught in her throat.
Seeing his warm genuine smile sent her heart doing violent, chaotic somersaults inside her chest.
Her blush intensified to a nuclear level with steam practically rising from her ears as she quickly turned her back to him, coughing into her silk handkerchief to regain her noble composure.
Harper walked over, linking her arm playfully through Silas’s other side with a wide radiant grin.
"Well, squad," Harper beamed, stretching her arms above her head with a contented sigh.
"We bought half an underground market...
Phase Five is officially complete.
Why don’t we finally head home?"
Silas chuckled, feeling the weight of the long unforgettable day finally settling into his bones.
"Home sounds fantastic."
Standing near the exit doors, Reginald quietly lowered his book.
As he looked across the room at his young lady blushing furiously beside the towering young Lord, a rare respectful smirk touched the corner of the old assassin’s lips.

’A common-born who commands strength, possesses unshakable composure, and treats my Lady with genuine warmth...’ Reginald thought, closing the book and bowing smoothly. ’I think Silas Graves is a truly exceptional match for my Lady.’
The purr of the custom midnight-purple sports coupe settled into an idle sound along the quiet curb of the modest residential street in Silverleaf District.
The velvet cloak embroidered with the Whitmore crest and the obsidian crow mask had already been stowed securely away in Harper’s Lord Inventory.
"Haah..."
Silas stood on the pavement in his familiar comfortable clothes feeling the cool crisp late-night breeze against his skin.
"What a night..."
The heavy void-chrysolite necklace Seraphina had gifted him still rested cool against his collarbone beneath his collar.
Around thirty minutes earlier, when they had finally ascended from the depths of the Obsidian Sanhedrin into the upper tiers of Valoria City, Seraphina and Reginald had parted ways with them.

The Bloom family limousine had arrived remotely, and with a flustered glance and a strict reminder that Silas was "mandated" to wear her tribute, Seraphina had glided into her vehicle under Reginald’s watchful escort.
That left just the two of them.

The golden glow of a nearby streetlamp caught the vibrant violet strands of her hair, casting soft shadows across her radiant flushed face.
She walked up to him with hands tucked behind her back, rocking lightly on the heels of her boots with a playful teasing smile that practically sparked with energy.
"You know, Silas..." Harper purred, tilting her head up to meet his blue eyes.
"While we were at the restaurant earlier, my little sister texted me complaining that she was bored and practically begged to sleep over at your place with Lia.
Which got me thinking... what if I invited myself inside and slept over tonight, too?"
Silas couldn’t help but raise an amused deadpan eyebrow at the purple-haired Lightning Lord.
"Can you really afford to play hooky and crash on my couch right now?" Silas asked dryly with a smirk tugging at his lips.
"You literally just dropped one hundred and fifty billion Spirit Credits on an ancient Khopesh...
Aren’t your Business partners waiting for you to deliver the weapon or so?"
Even now, just saying the number out loud made Silas flinch internally.
One hundred and fifty billion.
It was a sum so mind-bogglingly astronomical that it felt completely surreal to him.
’I need to make more money...’
Harper let out an exaggerated dramatic sigh, rolling her shoulders and shrugging in defeat.

The moment the blast doors opened, my phone was bombarded with thirty-seven high-priority pings from the board.
If I don’t report to the primary research bunker within the hour to oversee the initial calibration, my people are going to have a collective heart attack."

My first real one, too..."

chapters.title: Chapter 404: Grounded [II]
paragraphs: She leaned forward, sniffing the air around his collar with an exaggerated scowl before planting her hands aggressively on her hips.

"You smell like expensive perfume, jasmine flowers, and... is that another woman’s perfume?!" Lia demanded, her eyes widening in mock outrage. "Which woman have you been spending your time with all night?!"
Silas raised both hands in a placating gesture, clearing his throat awkwardly as a guilty sweat-drop formed on his brow.
"Lia, listen, it’s not what it looks like. I was just—"
Before he could finish his sentence, Lia grabbed the sleeve of his shirt with surprising force, yanked him over the threshold, and kicked the front door shut behind him with a solid thud.

"Save your excuses, Mister Big-Shot Lord!" Lia huffed, locking the deadbolt with a decisive click and pointing an accusatory finger straight at his chest. "You’ve been out gallivanting across the upper city while your poor little sister has been sitting here worried sick! So here is the new law of the house... you are officially grounded!"
Silas blinked down at her in disbelief.
"Grounded? I’m an Awakened Lord, Lia."

"I don’t care if you’re the Emperor of the Universe!" Lia declared with authority, stomping her foot. "You are going to stay right here in this apartment with us for at least a full day or two! No meetings, no shady business, and absolutely no running off!"
She narrowed her eyes, delivering her final non-negotiable ultimatum.
"And if you try to sneak off into the Sovereign Realm before your sentence is up, Big Bro... I swear to the gods, I will legally disown you!"
The solid front door of the Silverleaf residence clicked shut with a definitive latch that echoed softly through the quiet foyer.
Lia’s slender fingers remained clamped around the fabric of Silas’s sleeve, her small knuckles whitening against the dark cloth as she tugged him forward into the warm illuminated hallway.
Her slippers scuffed lightly against the polished hardwood floor and her messy brown hair bounced with each step she took.
’Haah... What a cute girl...’
Silas allowed himself to be dragged a few paces with his large frame towering over the eleven-year-old girl.
A wry smirk tugged at the corner of his lips as he looked down at the crown of her head, though the territory-focused thoughts in his mind didn’t simply dissolve.

Between the eight tons of Astral Void-Titanium Alloy sitting in his Lord Inventory, the seventy battalion sets of Frost-Drake gear, and the pending construction blueprints for the Umbral Basin’s outer perimeter, his schedule was practically bursting at the seams.
"Lia," Silas began, his deep baritone rumbling in the quiet corridor as he gently checked his momentum. "What about the territory? You know how critical the developmental phase is right now. I—"
Lia abruptly stopped.
Her grip on his sleeve loosened, her small shoulders sagging as she slowly turned around to face him.
The scolding frown that had dominated her expression moments earlier melted away entirely, replaced by an expression that instead looked fragile and painfully earnest.
Her large brown eyes, usually brimming with quick wit softened into an aching gaze.
She looked up at him, her lower lip trembling just a fraction before she pressed it firmly together.
"I was really worried about you, Big Brother..." Lia murmured, her voice dropping into a quiet hesitant whisper that carried none of her earlier bluster.

She reached up with both hands, clutching the front of his shirt tightly, her fingers bunching the fabric over his chest. "You didn’t come back yesterday. You didn’t send a ping. I know you’re strong now, and I know you’re a Lord with big things to do, but... it was quiet here... Too quiet. So please... at least stay tonight and throughout tomorrow for me. Just... be home."
The lingering urgency in Silas’s chest evaporated instantly.
Looking down at his little sister, the memory of her smaller, frail self shivering in the rainy dumpsters of Sector 4 flashed unbidden behind his eyes.
’Haah...’

No matter how many billions of Spirit Credits flowed through his fingers, no matter how many items he got, and no matter how vast his domain grew across the Sovereign Realm, this eleven-year-old girl remained his anchor to the earth.
Silas’s expression softened into a gentle warmth. He reached out, resting his broad, calloused palm over her messy brown hair, ruffling it affectionately until she let out a soft, embarrassed huff.
"Alright," Silas said softly, his lips curving into a genuine smile. "I’ll stay. Tonight and all of tomorrow, I’m completely yours."
A radiant relieved beam broke across Lia’s face, illuminating her features with pure childhood joy.
"Promise kept!" she declared, her energetic spark returning in full force as she grabbed his wrist and yanked him toward the archway. "Now come on, everyone’s in the living room!"
As Silas stepped past the entrance threshold into the expansive open-concept living area of the Silverleaf villa, the atmosphere immediately became one of a cozy household.
The soft glow of enchanted recessed ceiling fixtures washed over the plush cream carpeting and the large L-shaped sectional sofa.

A low glass coffee table in the center was completely covered in thick textbooks, colored runic styluses, diagrams of foundational mana-pathway formations, and several half-eaten plates of miniature pastries.
Standing near the kitchen counter in her immaculate black-and-white uniform, Martha turned around at the sound of their footsteps.
Her middle-aged gentle face framed by graying hair pulled into a neat, disciplined bun lit up with relief.
The silver tray she held in her hands trembled slightly before she set it down and bowed with deep heartfelt devotion.
"Master Silas," Martha breathed, her eyes shining with quiet emotion. "You have returned safely to us... Welcome home."
"Good to see you, Martha. Thank you for holding down the fort," Silas replied with an easy nod.
Sitting cross-legged on the plush floor cushions around the low table were two young girls who immediately looked up from their sprawling schoolwork.
On the left sat Kaede, her glossy dark hair tied neatly in her signature twin side-ribbons that bounced with every movement.
Her bright expressive eyes sparkled with bubbly, outgoing energy the second she spotted Silas.
She immediately dropped her runic highlighter, leaning forward over the coffee table with a broad mischievous grin that showed off her lively personality.
To her right, seated with impeccable posture on a velvet cushion, was Penelope.
Her silky vibrant purple hair was styled into elegant twin pigtails that draped over her delicate shoulders, perfectly matching her striking violet eyes.
While she carried the composed demeanor typical of her new position in this world, the warmth in her gaze revealed how comfortable she had truly become in the Graves household.

"Big Brother Silas!" Kaede chimed enthusiastically, waving both of her hands in the air. "You’re finally back! We were beginning to think Lia was going to build a tracking radar out of spare mana-crystals just to hunt you down!"
Penelope offered a polite, refined nod, closing her leather-bound notebook with a quiet snap.
"Good evening, Silas. Welcome back."
"Hey, girls," Silas chuckled, walking over to the large armchair adjacent to the sectional and sinking into the deep leather cushions.
He stretched his long legs out, letting out a relaxed sigh as the domestic comfort settled into his bones. "Hard at work, I see."

"How was your day, Master Silas?" Martha asked gently, stepping over with a crystal tumbler of chilled spring water, presenting it to him on a silver coaster. "Did your affairs in the upper districts proceed smoothly?"

Silas took the glass with his mind momentarily drifting back through the sheer, chaotic whirlwind of the past hours... The clothing spree, eating at a luxury machine, playing games, tearing through arcade claw machines, watching Harper drop astronomical billions in the Sanhedrin colosseum, the frantic bidding wars, and the kiss against the sports car outside.
’Feels like I’m living in a fantasy.’
Without fully filtering his thoughts, Silas took a sip of water and answered casually.
"It was fine. Pretty eventful, honestly. I just got back from a date."
The entire living room froze.
CLINK!
The porcelain teacup Kaede was holding rattled against its saucer.
Penelope’s violet eyes widened to twice their normal size with her pen slipping from her fingers and rolling across the table.
Martha gasped softly, pressing a hand against her apron with a look of stunned curiosity.
’Oh I knew... but I didn’t know it was going to truly be a date. Did they have sex?’
And standing right beside his chair, Lia’s head snapped toward him with such violent mechanical speed that Silas half-expected to hear a crack.

"A DATE?!" Lia shrieked, her voice pitching up an entire volume as she lunged forward, slamming her hands down on the armrest of his chair. "Big Bro! With who?! Since when do you go on dates?! Who is she?! Is she pretty?! Is she annoying?!"

"Wait, wait, wait!" Kaede squealed, scrambling onto her knees on the floor cushion, her side-ribbons fluttering wildly as her face flushed with gossiping excitement. "A real date?! Like a romantic, fancy-restaurant, holding-hands date?! Big Brother Silas, you have to tell us everything! Was it with a noble lady?! Did you go to the sky-gardens in Sector 1?!"
’There are sky-gardens?’
Penelope leaned forward, her sharp perceptive gaze narrowing as she scrutinized Silas’s face with a slight knowing smirk forming on her lips.
"Given the faint scent lingering on your collar, Silas... I suspect my elder sister might have had something to do with this ’eventful’ evening?"
Silas felt a bead of sweat form on the back of his neck as four pairs of intensely inquisitive female eyes bore into him like high-powered lasers.

"Whoa, whoa, calm down, all of you," Silas said, raising a placating hand with an awkward defensive chuckle. "It wasn’t an interrogation scene... It was just dinner and an event in the central district so it’s nothing scandalous."
"Uh-huh, sure," Lia muttered with extreme skepticism, crossing her arms and leaning in closer.
Her sharp eyes immediately caught the dark metallic shimmer peeking out from beneath the open collar of his shirt.
Her brow furrowed with her finger pointing straight at his throat.
"Then what is that? You never wear jewelry. I’ve never seen you wear one..."
Silas blinked, looking down at the heavy, dark obsidian chain resting against his collarbone.
The deep void-chrysolite gem sat comfortably against his skin, pulsing with a soothing mana-current.

"It’s just a gift," Silas explained, coughing lightly into his fist as he remembered Seraphina’s furiously blushing face and her strict declaration that it was a mandatory spousal tribute. "A token given to me at the end of the evening by an associate. It accelerates core mana recovery."

"An ’associate,’" Penelope echoed dryly, her purple eyebrows arching with amusement. "That is high-tier Abyssal Void-Chrysolite, Silas. There are few crest-artisans on the continent who cut gemstones in that specific geometry. It seems your evening was remarkably diverse."
Lia puffed her cheeks out, glaring at the necklace with deep protective suspicion, though before she could launch into another round of frantic cross-examination, Silas quickly turned the tables.

"More importantly," Silas said smoothly, gesturing toward the sea of charts and diagrams scattered across the coffee table, "how is your academy project coming along? Aren’t you three supposed to be finalizing the territory logistics for the project?"
The deflection worked like a charm.
Lia groaned loudly, throwing her head back against the sofa cushions, while Kaede collapsed dramatically onto her stomach over the carpet.

"Uuuugh, don’t remind us!" Kaede whined into the plush rug. "The resource allocation numbers for sustainable territory expansion are so complicated... We tried to get a source from another country but that place uses a completely different administrative framework, so my brain feels like it’s melting trying to translate everything!"
Penelope, seated cross-legged on the floor with a sleek holographic projection floating before her, looked up with calm composure.

"We are actually in the final phases of the schematic assembly," Penelope clarified, tapping the glowing projection to rotate the complex territorial grid. "The theoretical framework for the supply chain is complete. We were struggling with the defensive perimeter resource allocation earlier, but my elder sister, Harper, reviewed our drafts yesterday like you told her to... She provided an optimized sequence that bypassed the volatile supply conclusion that we came to initially so we don’t require any further assistance."
Silas smiled with a warm sense of satisfaction settling over him as he saw the genuine teamwork between the girls.
"I’m glad to hear that. Harper knows her territory logistics inside and out. You’re in good hands."

"She was really helpful, actually," Lia admitted, her voice softening as she uncrossed her arms and leaned against the arm of Silas’s chair. "She explained the resource conversion ratios in a way that actually made sense, instead of using all that stuffy academic jargon the professors use at Valoria Academy."
Kaede rolled onto her back, staring up at the ceiling with a dramatic sigh.
"At this rate, we might actually finish before the deadline. Penelope’s sister should come teach at our school!"
"Don’t get your hopes up," Penelope replied dryly with a dry smirk tugging at her lips. "Harper has more important matters to attend to than lecturing a bunch of Second Year students."
