"Lia," Silas began, his deep baritone rumbling in the quiet corridor as he gently checked his momentum.
"What about the territory?
You know how critical the developmental phase is right now.
Lia abruptly stopped.
Her grip on his sleeve loosened, her small shoulders sagging as she slowly turned around to face him.
The scolding frown that had dominated her expression moments earlier melted away entirely, replaced by an expression that instead looked fragile and painfully earnest.
Her large brown eyes, usually brimming with quick wit softened into an aching gaze.
She looked up at him, her lower lip trembling just a fraction before she pressed it firmly together.
"I was really worried about you, Big Brother..." Lia murmured, her voice dropping into a quiet hesitant whisper that carried none of her earlier bluster.
She reached up with both hands, clutching the front of his shirt tightly, her fingers bunching the fabric over his chest.
"You didn’t come back yesterday.
You didn’t send a ping.
I know you’re strong now, and I know you’re a Lord with big things to do, but... it was quiet here...
Too quiet.
So please... at least stay tonight and throughout tomorrow for me.
Just... be home."
The lingering urgency in Silas’s chest evaporated instantly.
Looking down at his little sister, the memory of her smaller, frail self shivering in the rainy dumpsters of Sector 4 flashed unbidden behind his eyes.
’Haah...’

No matter how many billions of Spirit Credits flowed through his fingers, no matter how many items he got, and no matter how vast his domain grew across the Sovereign Realm, this eleven-year-old girl remained his anchor to the earth.
Silas’s expression softened into a gentle warmth.
He reached out, resting his broad, calloused palm over her messy brown hair, ruffling it affectionately until she let out a soft, embarrassed huff.
"Alright," Silas said softly, his lips curving into a genuine smile.
"I’ll stay.
Tonight and all of tomorrow, I’m completely yours."
A radiant relieved beam broke across Lia’s face, illuminating her features with pure childhood joy.
"Promise kept!" she declared, her energetic spark returning in full force as she grabbed his wrist and yanked him toward the archway.
"Now come on, everyone’s in the living room!"
As Silas stepped past the entrance threshold into the expansive open-concept living area of the Silverleaf villa, the atmosphere immediately became one of a cozy household.
The soft glow of enchanted recessed ceiling fixtures washed over the plush cream carpeting and the large L-shaped sectional sofa.

A low glass coffee table in the center was completely covered in thick textbooks, colored runic styluses, diagrams of foundational mana-pathway formations, and several half-eaten plates of miniature pastries.
Standing near the kitchen counter in her immaculate black-and-white uniform, Martha turned around at the sound of their footsteps.
Her middle-aged gentle face framed by graying hair pulled into a neat, disciplined bun lit up with relief.
The silver tray she held in her hands trembled slightly before she set it down and bowed with deep heartfelt devotion.
"Master Silas," Martha breathed, her eyes shining with quiet emotion.
"You have returned safely to us...
Welcome home."
"Good to see you, Martha.
Thank you for holding down the fort," Silas replied with an easy nod.
Sitting cross-legged on the plush floor cushions around the low table were two young girls who immediately looked up from their sprawling schoolwork.
On the left sat Kaede, her glossy dark hair tied neatly in her signature twin side-ribbons that bounced with every movement.
Her bright expressive eyes sparkled with bubbly, outgoing energy the second she spotted Silas.
She immediately dropped her runic highlighter, leaning forward over the coffee table with a broad mischievous grin that showed off her lively personality.
To her right, seated with impeccable posture on a velvet cushion, was Penelope.
Her silky vibrant purple hair was styled into elegant twin pigtails that draped over her delicate shoulders, perfectly matching her striking violet eyes.
While she carried the composed demeanor typical of her new position in this world, the warmth in her gaze revealed how comfortable she had truly become in the Graves household.
"Big Brother Silas!" Kaede chimed enthusiastically, waving both of her hands in the air.
"You’re finally back!
We were beginning to think Lia was going to build a tracking radar out of spare mana-crystals just to hunt you down!"
Penelope offered a polite, refined nod, closing her leather-bound notebook with a quiet snap.
"Good evening, Silas.
Welcome back."
"Hey, girls," Silas chuckled, walking over to the large armchair adjacent to the sectional and sinking into the deep leather cushions.
He stretched his long legs out, letting out a relaxed sigh as the domestic comfort settled into his bones.
"Hard at work, I see."
"How was your day, Master Silas?" Martha asked gently, stepping over with a crystal tumbler of chilled spring water, presenting it to him on a silver coaster.
"Did your affairs in the upper districts proceed smoothly?"
Silas took the glass with his mind momentarily drifting back through the sheer, chaotic whirlwind of the past hours...

The clothing spree, eating at a luxury machine, playing games, tearing through arcade claw machines, watching Harper drop astronomical billions in the Sanhedrin colosseum, the frantic bidding wars, and the kiss against the sports car outside.
’Feels like I’m living in a fantasy.’
Without fully filtering his thoughts, Silas took a sip of water and answered casually.
"It was fine.
Pretty eventful, honestly.
I just got back from a date."
The entire living room froze.
CLINK!
The porcelain teacup Kaede was holding rattled against its saucer.
Penelope’s violet eyes widened to twice their normal size with her pen slipping from her fingers and rolling across the table.
Martha gasped softly, pressing a hand against her apron with a look of stunned curiosity.
’Oh I knew... but I didn’t know it was going to truly be a date.
Did they have sex?’
And standing right beside his chair, Lia’s head snapped toward him with such violent mechanical speed that Silas half-expected to hear a crack.
"A DATE?!" Lia shrieked, her voice pitching up an entire volume as she lunged forward, slamming her hands down on the armrest of his chair.
"Big Bro!
With who?!
Since when do you go on dates?!
Who is she?!
Is she pretty?!
Is she annoying?!"
"Wait, wait, wait!" Kaede squealed, scrambling onto her knees on the floor cushion, her side-ribbons fluttering wildly as her face flushed with gossiping excitement.
"A real date?!
Like a romantic, fancy-restaurant, holding-hands date?!
Big Brother Silas, you have to tell us everything!
Was it with a noble lady?!
Did you go to the sky-gardens in Sector 1?!"
’There are sky-gardens?’
Penelope leaned forward, her sharp perceptive gaze narrowing as she scrutinized Silas’s face with a slight knowing smirk forming on her lips.
"Given the faint scent lingering on your collar, Silas...
I suspect my elder sister might have had something to do with this ’eventful’ evening?"
Silas felt a bead of sweat form on the back of his neck as four pairs of intensely inquisitive female eyes bore into him like high-powered lasers.
"Whoa, whoa, calm down, all of you," Silas said, raising a placating hand with an awkward defensive chuckle.
"It wasn’t an interrogation scene...
It was just dinner and an event in the central district so it’s nothing scandalous."
"Uh-huh, sure," Lia muttered with extreme skepticism, crossing her arms and leaning in closer.
Her sharp eyes immediately caught the dark metallic shimmer peeking out from beneath the open collar of his shirt.
Her brow furrowed with her finger pointing straight at his throat.
"Then what is that?
You never wear jewelry.
I’ve never seen you wear one..."
Silas blinked, looking down at the heavy, dark obsidian chain resting against his collarbone.
The deep void-chrysolite gem sat comfortably against his skin, pulsing with a soothing mana-current.
"It’s just a gift," Silas explained, coughing lightly into his fist as he remembered Seraphina’s furiously blushing face and her strict declaration that it was a mandatory spousal tribute.
"A token given to me at the end of the evening by an associate.
It accelerates core mana recovery."
"An ’associate,’" Penelope echoed dryly, her purple eyebrows arching with amusement.
"That is high-tier Abyssal Void-Chrysolite, Silas.
There are few crest-artisans on the continent who cut gemstones in that specific geometry.
It seems your evening was remarkably diverse."
Lia puffed her cheeks out, glaring at the necklace with deep protective suspicion, though before she could launch into another round of frantic cross-examination, Silas quickly turned the tables.
"More importantly," Silas said smoothly, gesturing toward the sea of charts and diagrams scattered across the coffee table, "how is your academy project coming along?
Aren’t you three supposed to be finalizing the territory logistics for the project?"
The deflection worked like a charm.
Lia groaned loudly, throwing her head back against the sofa cushions, while Kaede collapsed dramatically onto her stomach over the carpet.
"Uuuugh, don’t remind us!" Kaede whined into the plush rug.
"The resource allocation numbers for sustainable territory expansion are so complicated...
We tried to get a source from another country but that place uses a completely different administrative framework, so my brain feels like it’s melting trying to translate everything!"
Penelope, seated cross-legged on the floor with a sleek holographic projection floating before her, looked up with calm composure.
"We are actually in the final phases of the schematic assembly," Penelope clarified, tapping the glowing projection to rotate the complex territorial grid.
"The theoretical framework for the supply chain is complete.
We were struggling with the defensive perimeter resource allocation earlier, but my elder sister, Harper, reviewed our drafts yesterday like you told her to...
She provided an optimized sequence that bypassed the volatile supply conclusion that we came to initially so we don’t require any further assistance."
Silas smiled with a warm sense of satisfaction settling over him as he saw the genuine teamwork between the girls.
"I’m glad to hear that.
Harper knows her territory logistics inside and out.
You’re in good hands."
"She was really helpful, actually," Lia admitted, her voice softening as she uncrossed her arms and leaned against the arm of Silas’s chair.
"She explained the resource conversion ratios in a way that actually made sense, instead of using all that stuffy academic jargon the professors use at Valoria Academy."
Kaede rolled onto her back, staring up at the ceiling with a dramatic sigh.
"At this rate, we might actually finish before the deadline.
Penelope’s sister should come teach at our school!"
"Don’t get your hopes up," Penelope replied dryly with a dry smirk tugging at her lips.
"Harper has more important matters to attend to than lecturing a bunch of Second Year students."

chapters.title: Chapter 405: No Promises Broken
paragraphs: "That is because Sister Harper possesses immense practical combat application rather than mere classroom theory," Penelope said with a proud smile.
The grandfather clock in the corner of the great room chimed softly, its mellow tones marking the late hour.
Martha stepped forward from the kitchen archway, her hands folded neatly over her apron as she offered a warm maternal smile to the three young students.

"Young ladies," Martha announced in a gentle yet firm tone, "it is past eleven o’clock... The academy bells ring early tomorrow morning, and your uniforms for the morning classes have already been pressed, inspected, and arranged within Lady Lia’s wardrobe. It is time to conclude your studies and prepare for bed."
"Awwwww!" Kaede groaned instantly, rolling onto her back and flailing her arms. "Just ten more minutes, Martha! We haven’t even finished packing our satchels!"

"Ten minutes will turn into an hour, and then you will complain that your morning tea is too hot because you woke up late," Lia retorted with a sharp bossy huff, though she too looked reluctantly at her open notebook. "Come on, Kaede. Let’s pack up..."
Lia turned back toward Silas, her eyes narrowing as she prepared to make a final stand to stay in the living room longer.
"Big Bro, maybe I can just stay up for a little bit to—"
Silas simply raised a single dark eyebrow, giving her a calm look that held elder-brother authority.
Lia stopped mid-sentence.
She knew that look all too well... it was the exact same quiet, immovable expression he used back in the slums whenever she tried to stay up past midnight to mend clothing.
’Haah... what a troublesome man.’
She instantly knew arguing was a completely wasted effort.
"Fine," Lia grumbled, though a small affectionate smile betrayed her grumpy facade.

She reached out, pointing two fingers at his eyes and then back at her own. "Remember your promise, Big Bro. You are not allowed to step a single foot into the Sovereign Realm tonight or tomorrow. If I wake up and you’re gone, you are in huge trouble!"
"I promised, didn’t I?" Silas chuckled softly, reaching out to pat her head once more. "Go get ready for bed."
Upstairs, down the wide carpeted hallway on the second floor, Lia pushed open the double doors to her bedroom suite.

The room was spacious and bright, featuring soft beige walls, a massive plush bed adorned with oversized cushions, a dedicated study desk beneath a wide panoramic window overlooking the tranquil gardens of Silverleaf, and a large walk-in wardrobe.
While it lacked the gold-leaf ornamentation and antique tapestries found in the noble estates of Sector 1, it was clean, incredibly comfortable, and radiated a cozy welcoming atmosphere.
Penelope stepped inside, setting her satchel down by the desk and looking around the tastefully furnished space.

"You know, Lia," Penelope remarked thoughtfully, a small, genuine smile gracing her refined features, "while your room might be considered standard by high-noble architectural conventions... it is remarkably pleasant. It feels very warm. My quarters at the Whitmore estate are nearly three times this size, yet they feel cold by comparison."
Lia’s cheeks flushed with a light bashful pink as she looked down at the carpet, rubbing her arm shyly.
"Th-Thanks, Penelope. Big Bro was the one that got most of the furniture done and even the bedsheets, as well as everything else."

"It’s super cozy!" Kaede beamed, practically leaping into the center of the room and flopping face-first onto the large bed, burying her face into the mountain of pillows. "The mattress is like a giant, fluffy marshmallow! I could sleep here forever!"

"Hey! Don’t mess up the sheets before we even put our pajamas on!" Lia scolded playfully, grabbing a plush decorative pillow and lightly swatting Kaede’s back. "Bathrooms first! We need to brush our teeth!"
The three girls trooped into the adjoining en-suite bathroom, chatting and giggling as they lined up in front of the wide mirror.

Kaede hummed a cheerful tune from the Shogunate Isles as she vigorously brushed her teeth, her side-ribbons bobbing in the glass, while Penelope meticulously applied a gentle lavender face cream with the disciplined poise of a young noble lady.𝘧𝑟𝑒𝑒𝘸𝘦𝘣𝑛𝑜𝘷𝑒𝓁.𝘤𝘰𝓂
Lia rinsed her mouth, wiping her chin with a fluffy towel, watching her two friends in the mirror with a quiet contented warmth filling her chest.
After years of isolation and scraping by in the slums, having true friends to share a sleepover with felt like a dream she never wanted to wake up from.
Returning to the bedroom, Lia walked over to her tall wardrobe, opening the cedar doors to retrieve her favorite set of soft flannel pajamas patterned with tiny cartoon mana-beasts.
Across the room, Penelope and Kaede unzipped the sleek enchanted travel bags they had brought with them from their respective estates.
"Huuu..."

Penelope changed into an elegant lavender-colored silk sleep set that fell smoothly around her slender frame, while Kaede donned a bright yellow oversized pajama shirt adorned with traditional Shogunate floral prints.
’Kaede sure is obsessed with the Isles...’
Kaede sat down on the edge of the mattress, swinging her legs back and forth as she watched Lia button up her flannel top.
A sudden, wicked glint of mischief flashed across the dark-haired girl’s bright eyes.

"Hey, Lia..." Kaede began, resting her chin in her hands and tilting her head with a sly playful grin. "Hypothetically speaking... if I decided in a few years that I wanted to date your Big Brother... would you give me your official blessing as his little sister?"
Lia froze mid-button, staring at Kaede with wide deadpan eyes for two full seconds before bursting into a loud uncontrollable fit of laughter.

"Pfft... hahaha!" Lia doubled over, clutching her stomach as she leaned against her wardrobe. "You?! Date Silas?! Kaede, are you crazy?! Big Brother doesn’t like younger girls at all! He looks at kids like us and just sees people he needs to feed vegetable soup to!"
Penelope couldn’t contain herself either.
A soft refined giggle escaped her lips, quickly turning into clear melodious laughter as she covered her mouth with her sleeve.
"Lia is correct, Kaede. That is an absurd proposition. Silas’s patience is formidable, but he would likely treat you like an unruly niece rather than a romantic partner."
Kaede puffed out her cheeks in mock indignation, though she quickly dissolved into giggles herself, falling backward onto the pillows.

"Okay, okay, it was a joke!" Kaede laughed, tossing a small cushion into the air and catching it. "I was just teasing! Besides, we’re way too young to be focusing on boys and romance anyway. We have our entire Year-long foundational curriculum to survive first!"

"Indeed," Penelope agreed, walking over to the bed and smoothing down the sheets. "We have to do some more research... While we informed Silas that the remaining phase was simple, "that" is easily the most intricate component of the entire project."
Lia sighed, climbing onto the mattress and pulling the heavy, plush duvet over her legs.
"Don’t remind me. We’ll have to spend all of Sunday afternoon running tests with "that" so we can get full marks but besides that..."
"There is more than enough space on this bed for all three of us," Lia added, patting the wide expanse of the mattress on either side of her. "Let’s just sleep for now."
Penelope slipped under the covers on the right, resting her head against the silk pillow, while Kaede curled up on the left, hugging a plush bolster tightly against her chest.
"Goodnight, Lia. Goodnight, Penelope," Kaede mumbled, her eyelids already drooping with heavy exhaustion.
"Goodnight, Kaede. Goodnight, Lia," Penelope whispered softly, closing her violet eyes.
"Goodnight, guys," Lia replied, reaching over to tap the bedside button, dimming the room’s ambient lighting into a gentle soothing twilight.
Within minutes, the rhythmic peaceful breathing of her two friends filled the quiet bedroom.
Several hours later, in the dead of the night, Lia’s eyes fluttered open.
The room was completely dark, save for faint silvery moonlight filtering through the sheer curtains of the panoramic window.
The house was utterly silent.
Lia lay still for a moment, listening intently. There were no sounds from the lower floor, no hum of magical machinery from the neighbors, and no footsteps in the hallway.
’Ah God...’
A familiar irrational knot of anxiety tightened in her stomach.

Even though they lived in Silverleaf now, and even though Silas was overwhelmingly powerful, the deep-seated fear that he might quietly slip away into the dangerous Sovereign Realm still haunted the edges of her mind.
Moving with the silent stealth of a former slum pickpocket, Lia carefully peeled back the heavy duvet.

She twisted her body with nimble precision, stepping over Penelope who was currently tossing and turning in the midst of an active dream, mumbling fragments of mana-flow equations and slipped past Kaede, who was sprawled diagonally across her pillow, softly snoring and uttering completely incomprehensible gibberish about sweet rice cakes.
Lia navigated the obstacle course of blankets without making a single sound, gently turning the brass door handle and slipping out into the hallway.
"Huuu..."
She let out a soft relieved sigh through her nose, closing the bedroom door with barely a click.
The second-floor corridor was cool and quiet. Lia walked on bare tiptoes along the plush runner rug, glancing down the central staircase toward the ground floor.
The dining room and kitchen were pitch-black and empty, even Martha’s quarters down the hall was completely dark.
Lia turned her steps toward the master bedroom at the far end of the upper hall.
Her heart hammered lightly against her ribs as she approached the heavy oak door.
’Haah... He needs to be here...’
She braced herself for the worst... half-expecting the room to be empty, the bed untouched, and a note left on the nightstand telling her he had emergency business in the Umbral Basin.
She reached out, gently pushing the slightly ajar door open.
CREAK!
The master suite was bathed in the soft glow of a personal smartphone screen.
Lying comfortably on his back atop the massive king-sized bed, propped up against a stack of pillows, was Silas.
He was still wearing a comfortable charcoal shirt and dark shorts with his blue eyes calmly reading through lines of text scrolling across his glowing display.
At the sound of the door moving, Silas’s sharp eyes shifted toward the entrance.

Seeing the small, brown-haired girl standing in the doorway in her flannel pajamas, clutching the frame with wide hesitant eyes, his rugged expression softened immediately into a warm understanding look.
"Couldn’t sleep?" Silas asked, his deep voice turning into a comforting rumble in the quiet room.
Lia didn’t answer with words.
A wave of pure overwhelming relief washed over her.
"Ah!"
She broke into a sprint, crossing the bedroom floor with quick padding steps, and launched herself straight onto the bed.
Silas laughed warmly, setting his phone face-up on the mattress and opening his arms to catch her.

Lia scrambled right on top of his chest, wrapping her arms tightly around his neck and burying her face into the crook of his shoulder, holding onto him with all the strength her small arms could muster.
"I wanted to sleep here," Lia mumbled into his shirt, her voice muffled and thick with sleep. "My bed was too crowded with Kaede kicking around..."
Silas chuckled, wrapping one large protective arm around her back, holding her securely against his chest just like he used to do when she had terrible nightmares in their drafty room years ago.
"You’re always free to sleep here, Lia," Silas said gently, his fingers lightly smoothing down her messy hair. "You don’t need an excuse."
Lia let out a soft contented sigh, relaxing her entire body against his broad frame.
The steady powerful beat of his heart beneath her cheek was the most soothing sound in the world, instantly banishing every lingering trace of anxiety from her mind.
As heavy, irresistible drowsiness began to pull her under, Lia’s eyes lazily drifted toward the glowing smartphone screen resting beside Silas on the sheets.
The display was showing an encrypted database dossier from the Sovereign Realm, and just before her heavy eyelids closed completely, she saw what he was searching.
Names of Ice Empresses that have been betrayed in the History of the Sovereign Realm? =====================================================

Lia’s brow twitched faintly with mild half-conscious curiosity at the majestic title, but before she could formulate a single coherent thought, the overwhelming warmth of her brother’s embrace pulled her down into a deep peaceful sleep.
’Ice Empres—’

The morning sun rose over the Silverleaf District, casting brilliant golden rays of light across the manicured lawns, polished stone driveways, and elegant architectural villas lining the quiet avenue.
The crisp morning air was clean and invigorating, carrying the subtle refreshing aroma of dew-kissed silverleaf pine trees.

Parked in the center of the Graves residence’s wide stone driveway was the sleek luxurious Zenith IVR and standing beside the open rear passenger door in her pristine black-and-white uniform was Martha with her hands folded neatly in front of her as she waited patiently to drive the young ladies to their morning cohort at Valoria Academy.

Several hours later, in the dead of the night, Lia’s eyes fluttered open.
The room was completely dark, save for faint silvery moonlight filtering through the sheer curtains of the panoramic window.
The house was utterly silent.
Lia lay still for a moment, listening intently.
There were no sounds from the lower floor, no hum of magical machinery from the neighbors, and no footsteps in the hallway.
’Ah God...’
A familiar irrational knot of anxiety tightened in her stomach.

Even though they lived in Silverleaf now, and even though Silas was overwhelmingly powerful, the deep-seated fear that he might quietly slip away into the dangerous Sovereign Realm still haunted the edges of her mind.
Moving with the silent stealth of a former slum pickpocket, Lia carefully peeled back the heavy duvet.

She twisted her body with nimble precision, stepping over Penelope who was currently tossing and turning in the midst of an active dream, mumbling fragments of mana-flow equations and slipped past Kaede, who was sprawled diagonally across her pillow, softly snoring and uttering completely incomprehensible gibberish about sweet rice cakes.
Lia navigated the obstacle course of blankets without making a single sound, gently turning the brass door handle and slipping out into the hallway.
"Huuu..."
She let out a soft relieved sigh through her nose, closing the bedroom door with barely a click.
The second-floor corridor was cool and quiet.
Lia walked on bare tiptoes along the plush runner rug, glancing down the central staircase toward the ground floor.
The dining room and kitchen were pitch-black and empty, even Martha’s quarters down the hall was completely dark.
Lia turned her steps toward the master bedroom at the far end of the upper hall.
Her heart hammered lightly against her ribs as she approached the heavy oak door.
’Haah...
He needs to be here...’
She braced herself for the worst... half-expecting the room to be empty, the bed untouched, and a note left on the nightstand telling her he had emergency business in the Umbral Basin.
She reached out, gently pushing the slightly ajar door open.
CREAK!
The master suite was bathed in the soft glow of a personal smartphone screen.
Lying comfortably on his back atop the massive king-sized bed, propped up against a stack of pillows, was Silas.
He was still wearing a comfortable charcoal shirt and dark shorts with his blue eyes calmly reading through lines of text scrolling across his glowing display.
At the sound of the door moving, Silas’s sharp eyes shifted toward the entrance.

Seeing the small, brown-haired girl standing in the doorway in her flannel pajamas, clutching the frame with wide hesitant eyes, his rugged expression softened immediately into a warm understanding look.
"Couldn’t sleep?" Silas asked, his deep voice turning into a comforting rumble in the quiet room.
Lia didn’t answer with words.
A wave of pure overwhelming relief washed over her.
"Ah!"
She broke into a sprint, crossing the bedroom floor with quick padding steps, and launched herself straight onto the bed.
Silas laughed warmly, setting his phone face-up on the mattress and opening his arms to catch her.

Lia scrambled right on top of his chest, wrapping her arms tightly around his neck and burying her face into the crook of his shoulder, holding onto him with all the strength her small arms could muster.
"I wanted to sleep here," Lia mumbled into his shirt, her voice muffled and thick with sleep.
"My bed was too crowded with Kaede kicking around..."
Silas chuckled, wrapping one large protective arm around her back, holding her securely against his chest just like he used to do when she had terrible nightmares in their drafty room years ago.
"You’re always free to sleep here, Lia," Silas said gently, his fingers lightly smoothing down her messy hair.
"You don’t need an excuse."
Lia let out a soft contented sigh, relaxing her entire body against his broad frame.
The steady powerful beat of his heart beneath her cheek was the most soothing sound in the world, instantly banishing every lingering trace of anxiety from her mind.
As heavy, irresistible drowsiness began to pull her under, Lia’s eyes lazily drifted toward the glowing smartphone screen resting beside Silas on the sheets.
The display was showing an encrypted database dossier from the Sovereign Realm, and just before her heavy eyelids closed completely, she saw what he was searching.
Names of Ice Empresses that have been betrayed in the History of the Sovereign Realm? =====================================================

Lia’s brow twitched faintly with mild half-conscious curiosity at the majestic title, but before she could formulate a single coherent thought, the overwhelming warmth of her brother’s embrace pulled her down into a deep peaceful sleep.
’Ice Empres—’

The morning sun rose over the Silverleaf District, casting brilliant golden rays of light across the manicured lawns, polished stone driveways, and elegant architectural villas lining the quiet avenue.
The crisp morning air was clean and invigorating, carrying the subtle refreshing aroma of dew-kissed silverleaf pine trees.

Parked in the center of the Graves residence’s wide stone driveway was the sleek luxurious Zenith IVR and standing beside the open rear passenger door in her pristine black-and-white uniform was Martha with her hands folded neatly in front of her as she waited patiently to drive the young ladies to their morning cohort at Valoria Academy.

chapters.title: Chapter 406: A Strange Khopesh
paragraphs: Standing on the front porch near the open double doors of the villa was Silas, dressed in a simple high-collared dark tunic and trousers, leaning casually against the polished doorframe with his arms crossed.
Gathered on the stone walkway before him were Lia, Penelope, and Kaede, all three dressed in the immaculate, prestigious uniform of Valoria Academy.
’Haah... It brings back memories.’
They were crisp white button-up shirts, navy-blue blazers adorned with silver academy crests, pleated skirts, and polished dark leather shoes.
Lia stood directly in front of Silas, her academy satchel slung securely over her shoulder.
She looked up at him with her hands on her hips, her brown eyes narrowing into her trademark stern commanding glare.

"Remember your promise, Big Bro," Lia instructed bossily, pointing an accusatory finger at his chest. "You are staying right here in the house today. When Martha brings us back from the academy this afternoon, I expect to see you sitting on that couch, ready to eat lunch with us! If you vanish into the Sovereign Realm, I will personally file paperwork to legally change my last name!"
’It’s not like you can afford it...’
Silas couldn’t help but laugh at her dramatic threats, raising his right hand in a mock oath.
"I hear you, boss. I promise. I’ll be right here waiting when you get back."
Lia’s stern expression broke into a bright satisfied smile, though before she could turn toward the car, Kaede stepped forward with a cheerful bounce in her step.
"Here, Big Brother Silas!" Kaede chirped happily, reaching into her blazer pocket and pulling out a delicate neatly folded silk handkerchief.
The fabric was dyed a deep, lustrous indigo and featured an exquisitely embroidered silver cherry blossom pattern in the corner.
She held it out with both hands, offering it to him with a radiant, bubbly grin.
"A gift from me! For letting us have a sleepover and eating all your delicious breakfast pastries!"
Silas blinked in mild surprise, reaching out with his large hand to accept the delicate square of silk.

"Thank you, Kaede," Silas said, looking down at the intricate embroidery with genuine appreciation, though a slight puzzled amusement flickered in his mind. ’What in the world am I supposed to use a delicate silk handkerchief for? Polish my armor?’
Penelope stepped forward, offering a graceful bow of her head. "Thank you for your hospitality, Silas... The accommodations were exceptional."
"Anytime, Penelope. Take care of each other at school," Silas replied warmly.
"We will!" Kaede beamed, turning and skipping toward the waiting vehicle.
Martha stepped forward, bowing respectfully toward Silas.

"I shall escort the young ladies safely to the academy gates and return immediately to attend to the things I told you about, Master Silas. I might be back later this afternoon, are you sure it’s okay if I use your car?"
"Thank you, Martha... Yes I’m sure and drive safely," Silas nodded.
Lia climbed into the spacious leather interior of the Zenith IVR alongside Penelope and Kaede.
As Martha smoothly closed the door and slid into the driver’s seat, Lia rolled down the tinted window, leaning her head out into the morning breeze.
"See you this afternoon, Big Bro! Don’t be lazy!" Lia called out, waving her hand enthusiastically.
"See you later, kiddo." Silas waved back with a warm smile.
HUMMMMM.
The Zenith IVR’s enchanted mana engine engaged with a silent vibrationless purr.

The sleek vehicle glided down the stone driveway, smoothly traversing the opening security gate of the estate before accelerating gracefully down the wide Silverleaf boulevard, disappearing into the morning traffic.
Silas stood on the porch for a moment, watching the road with a quiet peaceful smile.

’I’ll keep my promise...’ Silas thought to himself, feeling the rare calm of a normal day on Earth wash over him. ’Lia deserves to have a normal life, a safe home, and a brother who actually shows up when he says he will.’
BZZZZT!
Suddenly, the security sensors near the perimeter of the front lawn chimed softly.

Silas turned his gaze toward the outer gate. Standing on the public sidewalk just outside the estate’s railings was an official courier wearing the sharp navy-and-gold uniform of the Lord Association Building.
The delivery courier was carrying a reinforced, silver-trimmed lockbox marked with high-priority security seals.
Silas stepped off the porch, walking smoothly down the stone path toward the front entrance.
’It’s finally here, huh?’
The courier immediately stood at attention the moment Silas approached, recognizing the immense passive physical presence of an elite Lord even without his armor.
"Lord Silas Graves?" the courier asked professionally, presenting a digital stylus and confirmation slate.
"That’s me," Silas confirmed.
"Special priority delivery dispatched directly from the central LAB Vaults..." the courier stated, handing over the stylus. "Please provide your mana signature for verification."
Silas pressed his thumb against the scanning pad, letting a microscopic thread of his mana register on the slate.
BEEP-CHIME!
[IDENTITY CONFIRMED: LORD SILAS GRAVES]
The courier unlocked the silver-trimmed lockbox, carefully lifting out a compact steel chest and he presented the chest to Silas with a respectful bow.
"Consignment delivered in full, My Lord. Have a productive day."
"Thank you," Silas nodded, taking the heavy chest into his hands.
The courier bowed once more and departed down the avenue.
With a simple tap of a button, Silas triggered the estate’s security wards, and the heavy front gates glided shut behind him with a smooth click, locking the perimeter down completely.
Silas carried the chest back to the front porch, resting it on the polished outdoor table.
His fingers traced the runic bands along the seam of the lid and with a slight influx of his mana, the locking mechanism disengaged with a crisp chunk and the heavy lid swung open.
Resting upon a bed of deep black velvet inside the chest was a single breathtaking artifact.
It was a smooth metallic silver card, its surface gleaming with a soft, ethereal luminescence.
Intricate golden runes shifted and swirled across the face of the card in a continuous flowing dance of authority.
The edges were trimmed with delicate gold filigree, and the card radiated a very special aura.
A Hero Summoning Card.
Silas looked down at the glowing silver card, his blue eyes narrowing as the golden ring of his Mythic Gold Core flared to life beneath his pupils.
A slow confident smile spread across his face.
*I think it’s time...* Silas thought, his heart beating with a powerful electric rhythm.
The foundation of the Blessed Land was growing stronger by the day.
To truly establish undisputed dominance over the uncharted regions of the Sovereign Realm, his territory required another pillar.
’I did some research though I couldn’t find much... I wouldn’t mind if she was a Winter Specialist or something? Maybe a Saintess too?’
When he returned to the Blessed Land tomorrow night after fulfilling his promise to Lia, he was going to initiate the summoning and bring a new girl into the territory.
’Regardless of who she is... We’ll treat her like family.’
Meanwhile, across Valoria City, deep within the heavily fortified top-floor executive suite of the Lord Association Building...
A brilliant beam of morning sunlight sliced through the floor-to-ceiling panoramic windows, illuminating the sprawling, high-tech office.

Holographic displays flickered along the walls, projecting real-time Leyline stability maps of the sector, financial audit reports from the Obsidian Sanhedrin, and complex containment schematics for the newly acquired ancient Khopesh, The Per-aa’s Judgment.
Lying horizontally across the long, emerald-velvet executive sofa in the center of the office was Harper Whitmore.
Her vibrant purple hair was a wild messy tangle spreading across the cushions, several strands plastered against her forehead.
Her tailored coat was draped haphazardly over the back of an armchair, her boots kicked off onto the rug, and a half-empty mug of cold celestial coffee sat on the glass coffee table beside her.
Harper’s long eyelashes fluttered weakly against the bright sunlight.
"Haah..."
She let out a low, groggy groan, slowly rolling onto her side and shielding her eyes with the back of her forearm.
Slowly, her violet eyes blinked open, staring blankly at the ceiling tiles above her.
"Wha—what happened?!"

Harper sat up abruptly on the plush velvet sofa with her breath catching in her dry throat as the high-pitched squeak of her own mortified voice echoed off the sound-dampened walls of her top-floor executive office.
Her heart was hammering against her ribs like a runaway piston.

She lifted both hands, burying her slender fingers into the wild tangled mess of her vibrant violet hair, groaning softly as the vivid memory of the night before rushed through her mind in full detail.

The cool night air of the Silverleaf District... The reassuring warmth of Silas’s broad chest beneath her hands... The way she had boldly risen onto her tiptoes, gripped his collar, and pressed her lips against his.
And, worse yet... the passionate clumsy enthusiasm with which she had tangled her tongue into the kiss before panicking and speeding off into the dark like a terrified academy novice.
"Uuuugh..." Harper whimpered, pressing the heels of her palms against her burning cheeks.
Her face was hot enough to melt lead. "What in the world came over me? I am a Lord! Why did I run away like an embarrassed schoolgirl?!"
She rubbed her temples, trying to disperse the dizzying haze lingering in her mind.
Slowly swinging her long legs over the edge of the sofa, her bare feet touched the thick wool carpeting.
"Fuu... No matter..."
She stood up, stretching her sore back until the joints in her spine gave a series of satisfying clicks, and padded across the sprawling glass-walled office toward her private adjoining bathroom.
The bathroom was a masterpiece of sleek modern luxury, finished in polished black obsidian tile, gleaming brass fixtures, and soft amber luminescence.
Harper stepped up to the wide vanity counter and turned on the tap.
FSSH!
Cool enchanted spring water gushed into the basin, and she scooped two large handfuls directly onto her face, letting the freezing liquid shock her system awake.
’I needed that...’
She stayed bent over the sink for several long seconds with water dripping steadily from the tip of her nose, her chin, and the stray violet curls framing her cheeks.
When she closed her eyes, the phantom sensation of Silas’s lips lingered... they felt firm and intoxicatingly warm.
A small involuntary shiver ran down her spine, followed immediately by a reluctant helpless smile that curled the corners of her mouth.
’It was a good kiss, though,’ she thought, feeling a flutter in her stomach. ’A really, really good kiss.’
She grabbed a clean white hand towel from the heated rack, patting her face dry and smoothing down her disheveled hair as best she could with her fingers.
Tossing the towel aside, she turned on her heel and pushed open the frosted glass door, stepping back into the open space of her main office.
The morning sunlight was now pouring through the floor-to-ceiling panoramic windows, casting long geometric rays of gold across the modern desk, the holographic terminals, and the leather armchairs.
Harper froze in the middle of the room.
Her violet eyes widened, locking onto the center of her massive executive desk.
Resting atop the dark mahogany wood... completely free of its twenty-four-layer runic containment sarcophagus was the massive, six-foot golden Khopesh.
’Wait... what?’ Harper thought, her instincts instantly snapping into sharp focus.
Her brow furrowed deeply.

She had spent seven straight hours with the World Council’s chief masters in the vault, locking the ancient weapon within multi-layered spatial suppression spells before retiring to her office for a brief rest.
The blade was supposed to remain in the maximum-security containment chamber on Sub-Level Nine until the official activation trial was sanctioned by the board.
"I explicitly remember leaving it in primary containment..." Harper muttered aloud, her voice dropping into a tense cautious tone.

Her boots made not a sound as she slowly advanced across the carpet and her right hand hovered instinctively near her hip with her Lord core humming softly as tiny microscopic sparks of purple lightning crackled across the tips of her fingers.
The ancient weapon lay perfectly flat across the desk.
The hawk-beaked blade of untarnishable golden alloy gleamed with a hypnotic radiant luster that seemed completely untouched by the centuries.

The hieroglyphic bind-runes carved along its surface pulsed with a rhythmic breathing amber light, and the fist-sized sun-amber gem in the pommel swirled with a perpetual vortex of compressed golden sand.
Harper reached her hand out with her fingers trembling slightly as they hovered inches above the hilt wrapped in the calcified white hide of the divine desert serpent.
Before her skin could make contact with the leather...
"Greetings, Daughter of the Storm."

chapters.title: Chapter 407: Nitocris-Hathor
paragraphs: Harper flinched violently, her entire body snapping backward three paces as a jagged arc of purple lightning instinctively detonated from her knuckles with a sharp crackle.
"Who’s there?!" Harper demanded, her violet eyes darting rapidly across the empty corners of the reinforced office.
"Peace, young warrior," the voice resonated again.
It did not originate from the room, nor from the conduits in the ceiling.
It echoed directly inside Harper’s mind, sounding ancient, melodic, and deeply resonant as well carrying the dry whispering weight of shifting desert dunes.
Harper’s gaze snapped down to the golden Khopesh.
The swirling vortex inside the pommel’s sun-amber gem was spinning faster, pulsing in perfect synchronization with the voice.
"You’re... the blade," Harper said, lowering her hand slightly, though her guard remained firmly raised. "You possess an awakened sentience?"

"I am the memory, the will, and the judgment of the First Per-aa," the voice answered, rich with regal dignity. "For millennia, my form has languished in the dark, dormant vaults of my fractured lineage but when your spark of lightning touched my containment seal within the Sanhedrin, my soul stirred from its slumber. You do not carry the sacred bloodline of Khemet, Daughter of the Storm. Your mana flows from a lineage of thunder and iron... yet the resonance of your ambition and the purity of your spirit have chosen you. I have chosen you as my rightful successor."
Harper took a slow measured breath, crossing her arms over her chest, though the skepticism in her analytical eyes did not waver.

"And why would an ancient weapon choose me so readily?" Harper countered with her tone guarded. "The historical archives from the First Era warn that primordial relics carry severe soul-trials... You don’t simply hand over authority to the first Lord who buys you at an auction."

"Wise words from a sharp mind," the ancient presence chuckled softly, a low sound vibrating through the mahogany desk. "Power unearned is an illusion... To finalize the rite of succession and awaken the dormant tectonic authority sealed within my core, a blood pact of mutual resonance must be sealed. Cut the palm of your right hand. Allow your vital essence to touch the sun-amber pommel, and let the trial of the First Per-aa begin."
Harper’s eyes narrowed into slits.
"And if I refuse? If I keep you locked under containment until my research team completes a full runic diagnostic?"
The weapon hummed, the voice softening with a curious contemplative edge.
"You could do so. But tell me, Daughter of the Storm... what has become of the world in my long slumber? What realm does your spirit inhabit?"
Harper hesitated for a brief moment, but feeling no hostility from the blade, she spoke.

She described the modern era of Earth... the development of advanced dimensional suppression arrays, the sprawling industrial metropolises, the rise of the Lord Association, the intricate governance of the World Council, and the endless perilous expeditions into the Sovereign Realm to battle the monstrous incursions that threatened humanity’s survival.
The ancient presence listened in silence as the sand inside the amber gem shifted slowly.

"A world of towering steel and complex cages," the voice remarked, carrying a nostalgic sorrow. "Yet the fundamental law remains unchanged. Strength is the only shield between civilization and extinction. You carry the burden of leadership, young one. You carry the weight of an entire territory on your shoulders. The trials ahead will break ordinary steel. Do you not seek the strength to stand above the calamity? Do you not have those you wish to protect with unyielding might?"
As the words echoed in Harper’s consciousness, the sharp authoritative image of her corporate duties suddenly blurred, replaced instantly by the clear vivid image of Silas as well as her sister.
She saw him standing tall against the night breeze, his blue eyes ringed with gold, his gentle smile warming his features as he accepted her playful antics.

She remembered how his presence made the crushing burdens of her family’s schemes feel light, how safe she felt beside him, and the fierce protective fire that had burned in her chest when she thought of anyone threatening him.
’Sis too... I can’t let anything happen to that cute girl.’
She wanted to stand beside Silas as an equal.
She wanted to be strong enough that no calamity, no high-tier beast, and no ancient house could ever threaten the future they were building.
The lingering hesitation in Harper’s chest dissolved into a sharp resolve.
"Alright," Harper whispered.
She stepped up to the desk.
Channeling a microscopic blade of ionized lightning to the tip of her index finger, she made a swift shallow cut across the palm of her right hand.
A single drop of crimson blood, crackling with faint purple sparks, welled on her skin.
Harper leaned forward and pressed her open palm flat against the glowing Sun-Amber pommel.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The entire executive office vanished in a blinding instantaneous flash of solar-gold radiance.
"Haah!"
Harper gasped as the physical sensation of the floor beneath her boots disappeared entirely.
In a microsecond of spatial distortion, the modern glass walls, the leather furniture, and the city skyline were stripped away.
She found herself standing beneath a colossal, burning sky filled with three blazing suns.

Endless dunes of pure golden sand stretched in every direction as far as the eye could see, rolling and shifting beneath a hot, dry wind that carried the heavy scent of crushed stone and ancient mana.
SHUUUUUUUU.
Suddenly, the sand thirty paces before her began to swirl into a violent, spiraling vortex.

The golden grains rose higher and higher into the air, compressing and weaving together with divine fluid grace until the vortex smoothly dissolved, leaving a breathtaking figure standing upon the crest of the dune.
It was a woman of divine majesty.
Her skin was a flawless warm bronze that seemed to radiate the heat of the desert sun.
She possessed sharp striking golden eyes that carried the terrifying, ancient wisdom of a conqueror.
Draped in flowing white linen secured by intricate bands of solid gold and lapis lazuli, an ornate headdress depicting a rearing golden cobra crowned her long, raven-black hair.
In her right hand, she casually held the massive six-foot golden Khopesh with the hawk-beaked blade resting against the sand without sinking an inch.
The woman took a slow regal step forward, her golden eyes locking onto Harper with an intense, piercing pressure that made Harper’s Lord core thrum.

"I am Nitocris-Hathor, the First Per-aa of the Khemet Dominion," the woman spoke, her voice ringing across the endless desert with primordial authority. "I am the hand that built the great pyramids upon the bedrock of the first rifts... I am the blade that reaped one million nightmares from the Sovereign Realm to carve out an empire for mankind..."
Nitocris stepped closer, stopping only an arm’s length away, her gaze sweeping over Harper’s violet hair, her modern attire, and the fierce unbroken fire burning in her violet eyes.
A slow approving smile curved the First Per-aa’s lips.

"You have the eyes of a true warlord, Daughter of the Storm," Nitocris said softly. "You carry raw power, but it is unrefined. As my successor... I shall temper your lightning with the eternal weight of the tectonic sands. I shall make you vastly stronger than you have ever dreamed."
The ancient empress tilted her head, her golden eyes glowing with a sudden fierce luminescence as she raised her left hand.
SHING!
In the air between them, shimmering projections of golden sand began to coalesce, forming vivid moving illusions.

Harper’s breath hitched as she saw Silas... laughing as he caught Lia in the living room, standing calmly with his hands in his pockets, smiling down at Harper under the streetlights of Silverleaf, his lips parting in their breathless kiss.
Nitocris’s golden eyes burned with an intoxicating intensity.

"You hold a great sovereign within your heart," the First Per-aa whispered, her voice wrapping around Harper’s soul like a warm comforting desert breeze. "You wish to be his shield. You wish to be the unyielding storm that crushes his enemies beneath the earth. To claim this legacy... to master the judgment of the desert kings... you have only to open your core completely. You just have to put all your trust in me... in Nitocris."
Harper looked at the ancient empress, looked at the glowing Khopesh, and felt the immense terrifying power of the desert calling to the lightning in her blood.
A determined fearless smile spread across Harper’s lips.
"Show me what you’ve got, Your Majesty," Harper replied.
Later that afternoon, the quiet tree-lined avenue of the Silverleaf District was bathed in the warm, mellow rays of the descending sun.

The pristine Zenith IVR Supercar turned smoothly off the main boulevard, its enchanted mana engine emitting a soft vibrationless hum as it glided along the polished stone driveway of the Graves residence.
’I finished paying all of my debts...’ Martha thought as she looked forward, she was grateful.
Lord Silas was truly doing a lot for her, now all she had to do was to pay her personal debts to him by being the best maid he could have.

The automated perimeter security gates slid open with a whisper of metal, allowing the luxury vehicle to pull up directly in front of the villa’s grand front porch before smoothly coming to a complete halt.
The driver’s door opened, and Martha stepped out in her crisp black-and-white uniform, smoothing down her apron as she walked around to open the rear passenger door.
Lia stepped out onto the driveway, her heavy academy satchel slung over one shoulder and her uniform blazer slightly rumpled after a full day of foundational theory lectures and practicals.
She stood beside the vehicle, looking up at the quiet curtained front windows of the house as a sudden familiar hesitation flickered in her brown eyes.

"Martha..." Lia murmured, turning her head slightly toward the middle-aged maid. "Do you... do you think Big Brother actually stayed home all day? Or do you think he got called away to his territory?"
Martha offered a gentle reassuring smile, placing a warm hand lightly on Lia’s shoulder.

"Master Silas is a Lord with immense territorial responsibilities, Lady Lia," Martha answered softly, her tone carrying the patient wisdom of a devoted caretaker. "Even if matters in the Sovereign Realm required his immediate attention, you must know that his devotion to your well-being never wavers but your brother is also a man of his word."
Lia gave a small quiet nod.
She understood the weight of Silas’s position... she knew how dangerous and unforgiving the Sovereign Realm was, and how much effort was required to build a safe domain from nothing.
But deep down, in the hidden, vulnerable corners of her heart, she just wanted her big brother to be there when she came home.
Taking a breath, Lia walked up the three stone steps to the front porch, grasped the polished brass handle, and pushed the heavy oak front door open.
CREAK!
The moment the door swung inward, a rich and wonderfully savory aroma washed over the foyer.
It was the warm comforting scent of slow-simmered garlic, sweet roasted root vegetables, aromatic herbs, and rich golden poultry broth sizzling over a low flame.
Lia’s eyes widened.

Her nose twitched as she took in the delicious scent, and without even kicking off her academy shoes, she dashed down the entrance hallway with her shoes skidding across the polished hardwood as she rounded the corner into the large open kitchen.
Standing by the central marble island, wearing a simple navy-blue kitchen apron tied over his dark shirt and trousers, was Silas.
He was holding a large wooden ladle in one hand, carefully tasting a spoonful of rich, golden broth from a massive enameled pot simmering on the induction range.

Beside him on the island rested a large porcelain platter piled high with golden-brown roasted garlic-herb chicken thighs, crispy roasted baby potatoes tossed in rosemary and sea salt, and a vibrant medley of caramelized honey-glazed carrots and tender buttered green beans.
Silas turned his head at the sound of frantic footsteps, a warm relaxed grin breaking across his rugged face.

"Hey," Silas greeted her, wiping a stray drop of sauce from the counter with a clean cloth. "Perfect timing. Food’s almost ready... the garlic-herb chicken is just finishing resting, and the vegetable potage is at the exact right consistency."
Lia didn’t say a single word.
A radiant wave of pure happiness exploded across her face.
THUD!

She dropped her heavy academy satchel straight onto the floor with a loud sound, crossed the kitchen in three rapid strides, threw her arms around Silas’s waist, and buried her face into his apron, hugging him with everything she had.
Silas laughed warmly as he set the wooden ladle down and wrapped his large, muscular arm around her shoulders, giving her an affectionate squeeze.
"What’s this?" Silas teased gently, ruffling her messy brown hair. "Did the academy professors work you so hard that you lost the ability to speak?"
"You stayed," Lia mumbled into his apron, her voice thick and slightly muffled. "You actually stayed the whole day."

"Of course I stayed," Silas said softly, looking down at her with gentle warmth. "I made a promise to my little sister, didn’t I? A Lord who can’t keep a promise to his family isn’t fit to command a single foot of territory."

chapters.title: Chapter 408: Make Your Sister Happy
paragraphs: Standing in the kitchen doorway, Martha clasped her hands together with a look of pleasant surprise washing over her gentle face as she took in the sight of Silas in an apron and the elaborate spread of home-cooked food.

"My word, Master Silas..." Martha breathed, stepping forward with an apologetic bow. "I should have prepared the meal prior to our departure! It is my duty to manage the household cuisine. You should not have labored over the stove!"

"Don’t worry about it, Martha," Silas chuckled, waving his hand dismissively. "I felt like cooking today. It’s actually pretty therapeutic to cook with real high-grade ingredients for once. Though, honestly..."

Silas rubbed the back of his neck with an awkward, self-conscious grin. "I didn’t have a whole lot to work with in the pantry that I knew how to make, so it’s nothing fancy. Just some rustic roasted chicken and herb potage."

"Nothing fancy?!" Lia gasped, pulling back from the hug and staring at the glorious spread with sparkling, hungry eyes. "Big Bro, it smells better than the five-star banquet they served at the Academy Founders’ Day! I’m starving!"
’Better than the food at the Academy Founders’ Day? Is Lia insane?’
"Master Silas, the presentation and aroma are truly exceptional," Martha complimented warmly, her eyes shining with genuine admiration. "Allow me to assist with serving the table immediately."
Within minutes, the trio moved into the adjoining dining room.
The large mahogany dining table was set with pristine porcelain plates, polished silverware, and cloth napkins.

Martha smoothly poured three tall crystal glasses of chilled, freshly squeezed sun-citrus juice before taking her seat alongside Silas and Lia, invited warmly by Silas to sit as equals at the table rather than stand on formal servant decorum.
Lia didn’t wait a single second.
She eagerly sliced into a piece of the roasted chicken with her fork, popped the juicy, herb-crusted meat into her mouth, and let out a dramatic blissful groan of pure culinary ecstasy.
"Mmmmmph!" Lia chewed rapidly, her eyes rolling back in delight. "Big Bro! This is amazing! The skin is super crispy and the meat is so juicy! How did you even make it taste like this?!"

"The seasoning is balanced to perfection, Master Silas," Martha praised, taking an elegant delicate bite of the roasted rosemary potatoes and nodding with deep appreciation. "The subtle infusion of fresh thyme and roasted garlic complements the natural sweetness of the poultry wonderfully. You possess a remarkable talent for culinary arts."
’I was just picking up from Kaelia...’
Silas smiled, feeling a quiet satisfying warmth settle in his chest as he dug into his own plate.
"Glad you guys like it," Silas said, taking a sip of the citrus juice.

He looked across the table at Lia, who was happily devouring her honey-glazed carrots. "So, how was the rest of your day at the academy? Did you, Penelope, and Kaede finish assembling that territory logistics project you were stressing over before?"
Lia swallowed her food, puffing her chest out with childish pride.

"We totally crushed it!" Lia declared, waving her fork in the air. "Penelope handled the primary resource allocation, Kaede calibrated the defensive perimeter optimization runes, and I built the central supply chain stabilization core! Even the Assistant Professor had to admit our schematic was the most efficient in the entire First Year cohort! He said we’re almost certainly looking at an A-plus mark when Professor Vance officially grades it next week!"
"That’s incredible," Silas praised with a genuine proud grin. "I knew you three would pull it off. You’ll have to show me the completed thing sometime."

"I wanted to bring the project home today, but Kaede is taking it home this weekend," Lia explained, a soft smile touching her face. "I’ll bring the project back for you next time you’re home from the realm! You’re going to be super impressed, Big Bro!"
"I’m looking forward to it," Silas chuckled.

The dinner proceeded with lively comfortable conversation. Lia animatedly recounted the hilarious antics of Kaede accidentally turning her practice wand into a miniature water sprinkler during practical combat class, while Martha shared amusing updates about the friendly neighborhood gossip from the Silverleaf merchant market.
For an hour and a half, the realities of the world completely melted away, replaced by the pure irreplaceable joy of a family sharing a warm meal.
Eventually, the plates were cleared, and the lingering crumbs were wiped clean.

"I shall attend to the dishes and the kitchen sanitization, Master Silas," Martha said, rising gracefully from the table and stacking the empty porcelain platters. "Please, rest comfortably in the sitting room."
"Thanks, Martha," Silas nodded, standing up and stretching his arms.
Silas walked into the expansive living room, sinking into the plush leather sofa and letting out a relaxed sigh.
He reached into his pocket, retrieving his sleek holographic smartphone and resting it on his thigh.
PING!
A sharp notification chimed from the screen.
Silas blinked, tapping the glowing display. Flashing on the screen was a newly registered contact he had saved the night before.
[Seraphina]: Send a picture of you right now.
Silas stared at the message with a deadpan amused smirk spreading across his face.
’She really is something else,’ Silas thought, shaking his head. ’She isn’t just bossy and demanding in person or over voice calls... she acts like an imperious empress over text messages, too.’
Silas tapped the keyboard with his thumb, replying dryly.
[Silas]: Why?
The response was practically instantaneous, popping up within three seconds:
[Seraphina]: Because I requested it. Is a prospective consort required to justify a simple visual confirmation of your wellbeing? Do not dally, Silas Graves. Send the image at once...
Silas chuckled quietly.

Shrugging his shoulders, he switched the device to the front-facing camera, casually holding the phone up to snap a quick, unfiltered selfie from the couch, making sure the dark collar of his shirt and his relaxed expression were clearly visible.
He hit send.
A minute of silence passed before the three typing dots pulsed on the screen, followed by a detailed paragraph.

[Seraphina]: Acceptable... You appear sufficiently rested, though your hair is slightly disheveled. If you allowed it to grow two inches longer and utilized proper styling oil, your profile would align far more suitably with the refined aesthetic of the high-noble events.
Silas couldn’t help but grin as he typed back.
[Silas]: Alright, Princess. I’ll make sure to consult your personal hair stylist next time.

[Seraphina]: ...Do not mock me. Furthermore, I have visually confirmed via the image that you have not removed the Abyssal Void-Chrysolite necklace... For this, you receive my official commendation. It is functioning properly? Are you feeling the effects?
Silas touched the cool black gemstone beneath his collar with his thumb.
[Silas]: It works great. Core recovery is noticeably smoother. Thanks again, Seraphina.
Before Silas could send another line, the screen flashed with a rapid flustered follow-up:
[Seraphina]: My mother is entering the parlor. I must terminate this transmission immediately. Do not neglect your training. Farewell!
The status indicator next to her name switched to offline.
Silas chuckled softly, his thumb scrolling through his recent contact logs.
His eyes caught Harper’s name.

He had sent her two casual messages earlier that morning, teasing her about her hasty departure and asking how the LAB board was handling the Khopesh delivery, but there had been no replies, no read receipts, and no activity on her channel for the entire day.

’That’s strange,’ Silas mused, his brow furrowing slightly. ’Harper is usually glued to her phone or at least that’s what I think with the amount of messages she sent me while I was in Shogitown, constantly sending memes or complaining about paperwork... She must be completely buried under debriefs over that weapon.’
Before he could dwell on it any further—
FLOP!
A sudden light weight landed directly in his lap.
Silas looked down to see Lia casually making herself comfortable, curling her legs beneath her and spreading a thick leather-bound mathematics textbook across his knees.
She held a silver runic stylus in her hand, tapping the tip against a complex geometric diagram of spatial flux vectors with a deep pout.

"Big Bro," Lia announced, looking up at him with wide, pleading brown eyes. "I need pointers on this advanced vector calculus... The professor said if we don’t master spatial curvature by next week, we won’t be allowed into the intermediate core-shaping lab."
Silas rested his chin lightly atop the crown of her head, leaning his weight down just enough to make her let out an affectionate squawking grunt.

"Advanced spatial calculus?" Silas teased. "I thought you told me at the dinner table that you three completely crushed the project and got an A-plus? Now you’re claiming you don’t know basic spatial geometry?"

"That was practical application!" Lia retorted, turning her head and playfully nudging his chin with her forehead. "This is raw theoretical mathematics! That’s why you’re here as my Big Brother... to teach me and make sure I don’t fail! Stop being annoying and explain equation four!"
Silas laughed warmly. "Alright, boss. Look at the second variable..."
For the next two hours, the living room fell into a quiet rhythm.
Silas patiently broke down the intricate spatial formulas, using simple practical analogies from his own experiences navigating these questions to make the abstract math crystal clear.
Lia’s sharp brilliant mind absorbed every word like a sponge, her stylus dancing across the paper as she solved problem after problem.
Outside the panoramic windows, the twilight deepened into a rich, starry night.
Lia solved the final equation on the page, letting out a long exhausted yawn that stretched her entire small frame.
She leaned back against Silas’s chest, rubbing her tired eyes with the sleeve of her shirt.
A soft happy smile spread across her face as she looked up at him.
"I’m really happy you were here today, Big Bro," Lia whispered softly, her voice filled with pure peaceful contentment. "I wish... I wish you could be home like this every single day."
Silas looked down at her, feeling a gentle tug at his heartstrings.
Lia’s smile turned slightly bittersweet, though she patted his arm with mature understanding grace.

"I know you can’t, though," Lia continued softly, looking at her slippers. "I know the Sovereign Realm is important, and I know you’re building something huge so we never have to worry about surviving in the cold again. So... I’ll let you go back tonight without crying about it. But when you come back next time, you have to spend a ton of time with me again, okay?"
Silas’s heart swelled with protective warmth.
He wrapped both arms around her, pulling her close into a tight warm hug.
"I’ll keep my promise, Lia," Silas said softly. "And who said our time today is over yet? The night is still young. What do you think about getting out of the house for a bit?"
Lia’s brown eyes instantly snapped wide open, every trace of exhaustion vanishing in a microsecond.
"Really?!" Lia gasped, her face lighting up like a festive lantern. "You mean it?!"
"I mean it," Silas smiled. "Where do you want to go?"

"The Starlight Plaza in Sector 2!" Lia rattled off rapidly, bouncing excitedly on his knees. "There’s that midnight dessert parlor Kaede told me about that serves glowing ice cream parfaits! And the enchanted arcade with the neon hover-racers! And the rooftop observation terrace overlooking the lower city lights!"
Silas chuckled at her boundless energy. "Sounds like a solid plan. Why don’t we go? Run upstairs and change out of your academy uniform first."
"YES!" Lia cheered, practically launching herself off his lap and sprinting toward the stairs like a bolt of lightning with her slippers pounding up the steps.
Standing near the hallway archway, Martha walked into the living room, a deeply touched smile gracing her features as she watched Lia’s retreating figure.
"Master Silas," Martha said softly, her eyes shining with quiet emotion. "Lady Lia has not smiled with such joy in a very long time... You have made her remarkably happy today."
Silas stood up from the sofa, smoothing down the front of his shirt with a confident, relaxed grin.
"It’s time to make her even happier," Silas said warmly.
He looked directly at Martha with his tone leaving no room for argument. "Go grab your coat, Martha. You’re coming along with us."
Martha blinked, her middle-aged face flushing with a sudden flustered pink as she stepped back, clutching her hands to her apron.
"Oh! Master Silas, no, I could not possibly intrude upon your family outing! I am merely the household servant—"

"You’re not intruding," Silas interrupted gently, his voice firm, kind, and deeply sincere. "You take care of Lia every single day while I’m away. You keep this house running, you worry about us, and you protect this home. We’re one big family under this roof, Martha. You’re coming with us to have dessert."
Martha’s throat tightened, a sudden overwhelming warmth flooding her chest as tears of profound gratitude welled at the corners of her eyes.
She bowed deeply with her voice trembling slightly. "Thank you... thank you, Master Silas. I shall retrieve my wrap at once."

"I’ll bring the project back for you next time you’re home from the realm!
You’re going to be super impressed, Big Bro!"
"I’m looking forward to it," Silas chuckled.
The dinner proceeded with lively comfortable conversation.

Lia animatedly recounted the hilarious antics of Kaede accidentally turning her practice wand into a miniature water sprinkler during practical combat class, while Martha shared amusing updates about the friendly neighborhood gossip from the Silverleaf merchant market.
For an hour and a half, the realities of the world completely melted away, replaced by the pure irreplaceable joy of a family sharing a warm meal.
Eventually, the plates were cleared, and the lingering crumbs were wiped clean.
"I shall attend to the dishes and the kitchen sanitization, Master Silas," Martha said, rising gracefully from the table and stacking the empty porcelain platters.
"Please, rest comfortably in the sitting room."
"Thanks, Martha," Silas nodded, standing up and stretching his arms.
Silas walked into the expansive living room, sinking into the plush leather sofa and letting out a relaxed sigh.
He reached into his pocket, retrieving his sleek holographic smartphone and resting it on his thigh.
PING!

Silas blinked, tapping the glowing display.
Flashing on the screen was a newly registered contact he had saved the night before.

Silas stared at the message with a deadpan amused smirk spreading across his face.

The response was practically instantaneous, popping up within three seconds:

Is a prospective consort required to justify a simple visual confirmation of your wellbeing?
Do not dally, Silas Graves.
Send the image at once...
Silas chuckled quietly.

You appear sufficiently rested, though your hair is slightly disheveled.
