chapters.title: Chapter 409: Morwenna’s Past [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: It was well past midnight when the Zenith IVR returned to the quiet driveway of the Silverleaf villa.
The outing had been a triumph.

They had eaten glowing starlight parfaits on the high terrace, raced holographic hover-cars until Lia’s sides ached from laughing, and watched the sprawling glittering lights of Valoria City stretch out into the horizon beneath the twin moons.
Silas walked softly down the second-floor hallway, carrying an utterly exhausted fast-asleep Lia in his arms.
He entered her bedroom, gently laying her down upon the plush mattress beneath the soft duvet.
Lia stirred faintly, her eyes fluttering open just a sliver as she felt the cool pillow against her cheek.
"Big Bro..." Lia mumbled sleepily, reaching her small hand out from beneath the blanket to lightly grasp his wrist. "Thank you for today... it was the best day ever..."
Silas leaned down, his rugged expression softening into pure unreserved tenderness as he pressed a gentle, protective kiss against her forehead.
"You’re welcome..." Silas whispered warmly. "Goodnight, Lia."
"Love you very much, Big Bro..." Lia murmured, her grip on his wrist loosening as she drifted instantly back into a deep sleep.
Silas watched her breathe for a quiet moment, then adjusted the blankets around her shoulders, tapped the nightlight button, and quietly exited the room, pulling the door shut with barely a click.
He walked down the hall and entered the master suite.
’Haah... what a night... It’s good to have money.’
Silas rolled his shoulders, letting out a long invigorating stretch as he looked around the room.
During the quiet morning hours while Lia was at school, Silas had taken the time to thoroughly organize his belongings.

He opened the tall wardrobe, looking at the neatly hung rows of premium tailored clothing, combat tunics, and fine coats that Seraphina and Harper had bought for him during their excursions to the most expensive mall in the city.
Everything in his life on Earth was stable, prosperous, and secure.
Now, it was time to tend to the domain that made it all possible.
Silas walked over to the center of the spacious bedroom.
With a single focused thought, he summoned his internal Lord Interface as a translucent, deep-blue holographic panel materialized in the air before his eyes, pulsing with crisp blue.
[Descend]
Silas raised his hand, his index finger pressing firmly against the glowing icon.
HUMMMMM... FLASH!

Blackness enveloped his vision as the familiar weightless sensation of dimensional teleportation pulled at his consciousness, tearing through the spatial boundary separating Earth from the boundless primordial expanse of the Sovereign Realm.
SHING!
The darkness dissolved in an instant, replaced by the warm amber-lit stone architecture of his private Lord Manor at the heart of the Blessed Land.
Silas materialized in the center of his spacious master quarters, the rich, invigorating aroma of powerful spiritual mana and blooming World-Tree blossoms immediately flooding his lungs.
The moment his boots touched the polished stone floor, Silas blinked, greeted by a completely unexpected and striking sight.
Morwenna was there.
The Pirate Queen was sprawled across his bed like she owned the place because in her mind, she probably did.
Her wild dark hair was fanned out across his pillows with a tattered leather coat tossed carelessly over the footboard.
She was wearing nothing but a loose linen undershirt and her worn leather trousers, one of her heavy boots already kicked off onto the floor.
A half-empty bottle of something strong rested on the nightstand beside her.
She had clearly been waiting for him.

"Took you long enough, Captain," Morwenna drawled, propping herself up on her elbows with a sharp grin that showed her canines. She looked him up and down, her stormy gray eyes gleaming with that familiar glint. "I was starting to think you’d gotten lost in that soft human world of yours. Did you forget how to find your way back to the realm?"
Silas let out a warm laugh, shaking his head as he crossed the room. "Miss me that much, Morwenna?"
She snorted, but the way her eyes softened betrayed her.

"Someone has to keep an eye on you. The weed’s been pacing the Keep all day, Talira’s been burning holes in the training dummies with her dragon fire, and Thora’s been asking when you’re going to upgrade her forge again... You cause chaos just by being gone, Captain."
Silas sat down on the edge of the bed, and Morwenna immediately shifted, swinging her legs over his lap like it was the most natural thing in the world.
She rested her head against his shoulder, letting out a long contented sigh that completely contradicted her earlier gruffness.
"Welcome back," she murmured, her voice dropping its usual bite.
Silas wrapped his arm around her waist, pulling her closer. "Good to be back."
They sat like that for a moment as the comfortable silence settled between them like a well-worn blanket.
The crackling hearth, the distant howl of the Umbral Basin wind, the soft warmth of her body pressed against his side... it was a reminder of why he kept fighting.
Silas took a breath, his expression shifting from domestic warmth into focused curiosity.
He looked down at Morwenna, his voice dropping into a serious inquiring tone.
"Before we start organizing the new supplies and summoning preparations..." Silas began, his blue eyes narrowing slightly, "Morwenna, do you know what The Leviathan’s Wake is?"
For some strange reason...
The entire room became completely silent.
Morwenna’s body went rigid against him.
Her stormy gray eyes, which had been soft and relaxed just a moment ago, sharpened until they became cold and her fingers tightened against his shirt.
"Where did you hear that name, Captain?" Morwenna asked, her voice dropping to a low tone that Silas had never heard from her before.
The tension in the Lord’s master quarters was so dense it felt as though the atmospheric pressure had suddenly plunged to the bottom of the deep ocean.
Morwenna’s fingers remained buried tightly in the fabric of Silas’s shirt.
Her stormy gray eyes... usually so full of feral swagger, sharp mockery, and effortless bravado had changed completely.
They were hollow and swimming with a chilling fathomless cold that mirrored the abyssal depths she had once conquered.
Silas did not flinch, nor did he pull back. He simply held her close, keeping his arm securely around her waist to anchor her against him.

"I was at an auction in the human world yesterday," Silas explained gently, his voice level and steady as he broke the heavy silence. "In the Obsidian Sanhedrin. A lot of rare items were brought up from various sectors and frontlines. Among them, a name was spoken during one of the premier bidding rounds. They said it was the name of a legendary flagship... a pirate vessel that had crashed and vanished into the depths centuries ago or something like that. The Leviathan’s Wake."
Morwenna’s breath hitched.
She looked down, her wild dark hair spilling forward to conceal her face in shadows.
Her shoulders shook with a microscopic tremor, her jaw setting so hard that the muscles along her neck coiled like steel wires.
Her stormy eyes darkened further, swirling with the violent ghosts of five hundred years of buried devastation.
Silas reached out with his free hand, gently covering her trembling knuckles where they gripped his shirt.
"You can trust me, Morwenna," Silas whispered softly, leaning down slightly so his breath brushed against her temple. "You know you can."
A shudder ran through her entire body. The Pirate Queen swallowed hard, a dry ragged breath scraping up her throat before she finally forced herself to speak.
"I..." Her voice cracked, uncharacteristically frail, before she steadied it with a bitter self-mocking scoff. "It... it was my ship, Captain."
Silas’s blue eyes narrowed in genuine surprise. He kept his silence, allowing her the space to let the words bleed out at her own pace.

"Before the void took it... before it was shattered to kindling and dragged to the bottom of the sea, the Leviathan’s Wake wasn’t just a vessel," Morwenna muttered, staring blankly at the dark wood of the bedstead. "It was our home. It was where I gathered my family. A whole crew of misfits, orphans, bastards, and strays... people the upper realms threw away like garbage. People who had no lives, no domains, and no hope until I pulled them out of the mud and gave them the deck of a ship."
She swallowed again with her chest heaving against his ribs.

"We ruled the Abyssal Seas for centuries," she whispered, her fingers digging deeper into his chest. "We took whatever we wanted from the divine fleets, danced on the edges of forbidden rifts, and answered to no god or emperor. We were free. But freedom is a sin in the eyes of the divine hierarchy. The corporate deities... the higher pantheons... they couldn’t stand a mortal-born crew laughing in their faces."
A dark agonizing sorrow flickered across her face as memories she had spent half a millennium trying to drown surged back to the surface.

She remembered how the betrayal had actually happened. Their impenetrable defensive arrays had been bypassed from the inside and the coordinates of their hidden anchorage of the barrier had been hit by... Lyra.
’Lyra...’
Lyra had been just a sixteen-year-old kid when the inquisitors got their claws into her.
The girl had been terrified, weeping, manipulated by promises that they would spare her little brother if she only killed them by dropping the barriers.
Lyra had been an idiot child who thought she was saving family, only to end up leading every single soul on board into a cosmic meat grinder.
The entire crew had been butchered. The deck had run red before the divine fleets dragged the broken wreckage down into the sunless abyss to drown forever.
Morwenna didn’t voice the girl’s name.
Even after five hundred years of burning rage, what was the point of blaming a terrified child manipulated by gods? The pain was hers to carry...
She tugged weakly on Silas’s sleeve, it was a desperate silent plea for grounding.
’I don’t want to talk about them.’
The memories she shared with her crew were amazing and she would do so dozen times over.𝓯𝓻𝒆𝙚𝒘𝓮𝙗𝓷𝒐𝓿𝙚𝒍.𝙘𝓸𝙢
...But they were painful, very painful and even though it was selfish, Morwenna wanted to think about her new family.
Silas understood instantly.

He didn’t press her for details, nor did he lecture her about past mistakes. He firmly squeezed her hand, pulling her body completely flush against his chest, wrapping his arms around her back, and gently patting the back of her dark head.
"There, there..." Silas murmured in a deeply affectionate rhythm, resting his chin lightly atop her hair. "I’ve got you. It’s over now."
Morwenna was an SSS-Rank Mythic Dread Queen... a terrifying entity capable of ripping fleets of ships enhanced by even gods apart with tidal fury.

She was nobody’s fragile princess, and she certainly wasn’t a baby yet, surrounded by the warm, sovereign aura radiating from his Gold Core, feeling the genuine protectiveness bleeding through his touch, the rigid armor around her heart completely crumbled.
Not like it was there whenever Silas touched her.
She let out a shaky, muffled sigh into the crook of his neck.
With a subtle, needy squirm, she pulled herself even higher onto his lap, curling her legs securely around his waist and resting her forehead against his clavicle.
She allowed herself to be held, to be coddled, to be babied by the only man in two universes who held her loyalty.
If it was her Captain doing the coddling, then she didn’t give a damn about her pride.
’It feels good too...’
For several minutes, the room remained entirely peaceful, save for the rhythmic rise and fall of their chests and the comforting crackle of the hearth fire.
Eventually, Morwenna stirred. She tilted her head back, her dark and slightly messy hair swaying across her shoulders as she looked up into his face.
Her stormy gray eyes were still slightly rimmed with red, but the cold had vanished, replaced by a curious gaze.
"So..." she murmured, clearing her throat to regain a shred of her typical pirate rasp. "How in the hells do you know about my ship, Captain? You said an auction?"
Silas smiled warmly, brushing a stray dark lock from her cheek.

"At the Obsidian Sanhedrin," Silas explained, his voice rich with quiet satisfaction. "The auctioneers brought out a relic that had supposedly washed ashore from a deep rift in the outer sectors. They claimed it was recovered from the very wreckage of the Leviathan’s Wake."
Morwenna’s brows furrowed in pure bewilderment.

"Recovered from the wreck?" she scoffed softly, shaking her head. "Captain, I spent five centuries trapped at the bottom of the abyssal trenches, drowning in divine chains before you pulled me through that portal. Anything made of mortal steel or standard enchantments would have been crushed to dust under that water pressure hundreds of years ago. What could have possibly survived down there?"
Silas didn’t answer with words.
Instead, he focused his intent, calling upon his dimensional storage.
A brilliant blue flash of spatial light ignited across the palm of his right hand. The ambient air in the master quarters suddenly grew rich with the distinct scent of an oncoming oceanic tempest.
With a soft hum of displacement, a massive magnificent weapon materialized in his grasp.
"Oof—" Silas let out a low grunt as the weight of the blade dragged his arm downward, the pommel hitting the stone floor with a heavy thud. "Damn... it’s got quite a bit of weight to it."

Lia stirred faintly, her eyes fluttering open just a sliver as she felt the cool pillow against her cheek.
"Big Bro..." Lia mumbled sleepily, reaching her small hand out from beneath the blanket to lightly grasp his wrist.
"Thank you for today... it was the best day ever..."
Silas leaned down, his rugged expression softening into pure unreserved tenderness as he pressed a gentle, protective kiss against her forehead.
"You’re welcome..." Silas whispered warmly.
"Goodnight, Lia."
"Love you very much, Big Bro..." Lia murmured, her grip on his wrist loosening as she drifted instantly back into a deep sleep.
Silas watched her breathe for a quiet moment, then adjusted the blankets around her shoulders, tapped the nightlight button, and quietly exited the room, pulling the door shut with barely a click.
He walked down the hall and entered the master suite.
’Haah... what a night...
It’s good to have money.’
Silas rolled his shoulders, letting out a long invigorating stretch as he looked around the room.
During the quiet morning hours while Lia was at school, Silas had taken the time to thoroughly organize his belongings.

He opened the tall wardrobe, looking at the neatly hung rows of premium tailored clothing, combat tunics, and fine coats that Seraphina and Harper had bought for him during their excursions to the most expensive mall in the city.
Everything in his life on Earth was stable, prosperous, and secure.
Now, it was time to tend to the domain that made it all possible.
Silas walked over to the center of the spacious bedroom.
With a single focused thought, he summoned his internal Lord Interface as a translucent, deep-blue holographic panel materialized in the air before his eyes, pulsing with crisp blue.
[Descend]
Silas raised his hand, his index finger pressing firmly against the glowing icon.
HUMMMMM...
FLASH!

Blackness enveloped his vision as the familiar weightless sensation of dimensional teleportation pulled at his consciousness, tearing through the spatial boundary separating Earth from the boundless primordial expanse of the Sovereign Realm.
SHING!
The darkness dissolved in an instant, replaced by the warm amber-lit stone architecture of his private Lord Manor at the heart of the Blessed Land.
Silas materialized in the center of his spacious master quarters, the rich, invigorating aroma of powerful spiritual mana and blooming World-Tree blossoms immediately flooding his lungs.
The moment his boots touched the polished stone floor, Silas blinked, greeted by a completely unexpected and striking sight.
Morwenna was there.
The Pirate Queen was sprawled across his bed like she owned the place because in her mind, she probably did.
Her wild dark hair was fanned out across his pillows with a tattered leather coat tossed carelessly over the footboard.
She was wearing nothing but a loose linen undershirt and her worn leather trousers, one of her heavy boots already kicked off onto the floor.
A half-empty bottle of something strong rested on the nightstand beside her.
She had clearly been waiting for him.
"Took you long enough, Captain," Morwenna drawled, propping herself up on her elbows with a sharp grin that showed her canines.
She looked him up and down, her stormy gray eyes gleaming with that familiar glint.
"I was starting to think you’d gotten lost in that soft human world of yours.
Did you forget how to find your way back to the realm?"
Silas let out a warm laugh, shaking his head as he crossed the room.
"Miss me that much, Morwenna?"
She snorted, but the way her eyes softened betrayed her.
"Someone has to keep an eye on you.
The weed’s been pacing the Keep all day, Talira’s been burning holes in the training dummies with her dragon fire, and Thora’s been asking when you’re going to upgrade her forge again...
You cause chaos just by being gone, Captain."
Silas sat down on the edge of the bed, and Morwenna immediately shifted, swinging her legs over his lap like it was the most natural thing in the world.
She rested her head against his shoulder, letting out a long contented sigh that completely contradicted her earlier gruffness.
"Welcome back," she murmured, her voice dropping its usual bite.
Silas wrapped his arm around her waist, pulling her closer.
"Good to be back."
They sat like that for a moment as the comfortable silence settled between them like a well-worn blanket.
The crackling hearth, the distant howl of the Umbral Basin wind, the soft warmth of her body pressed against his side... it was a reminder of why he kept fighting.
Silas took a breath, his expression shifting from domestic warmth into focused curiosity.
He looked down at Morwenna, his voice dropping into a serious inquiring tone.
"Before we start organizing the new supplies and summoning preparations..." Silas began, his blue eyes narrowing slightly, "Morwenna, do you know what The Leviathan’s Wake is?"
For some strange reason...
The entire room became completely silent.
Morwenna’s body went rigid against him.
Her stormy gray eyes, which had been soft and relaxed just a moment ago, sharpened until they became cold and her fingers tightened against his shirt.
"Where did you hear that name, Captain?" Morwenna asked, her voice dropping to a low tone that Silas had never heard from her before.
The tension in the Lord’s master quarters was so dense it felt as though the atmospheric pressure had suddenly plunged to the bottom of the deep ocean.
Morwenna’s fingers remained buried tightly in the fabric of Silas’s shirt.
Her stormy gray eyes... usually so full of feral swagger, sharp mockery, and effortless bravado had changed completely.
They were hollow and swimming with a chilling fathomless cold that mirrored the abyssal depths she had once conquered.
Silas did not flinch, nor did he pull back.
He simply held her close, keeping his arm securely around her waist to anchor her against him.
"I was at an auction in the human world yesterday," Silas explained gently, his voice level and steady as he broke the heavy silence.
"In the Obsidian Sanhedrin.
A lot of rare items were brought up from various sectors and frontlines.
Among them, a name was spoken during one of the premier bidding rounds.
They said it was the name of a legendary flagship... a pirate vessel that had crashed and vanished into the depths centuries ago or something like that.
The Leviathan’s Wake."
Morwenna’s breath hitched.
She looked down, her wild dark hair spilling forward to conceal her face in shadows.
Her shoulders shook with a microscopic tremor, her jaw setting so hard that the muscles along her neck coiled like steel wires.
Her stormy eyes darkened further, swirling with the violent ghosts of five hundred years of buried devastation.
Silas reached out with his free hand, gently covering her trembling knuckles where they gripped his shirt.
"You can trust me, Morwenna," Silas whispered softly, leaning down slightly so his breath brushed against her temple.
"You know you can."
A shudder ran through her entire body.
The Pirate Queen swallowed hard, a dry ragged breath scraping up her throat before she finally forced herself to speak.
"I..." Her voice cracked, uncharacteristically frail, before she steadied it with a bitter self-mocking scoff.
"It... it was my ship, Captain."
Silas’s blue eyes narrowed in genuine surprise.
He kept his silence, allowing her the space to let the words bleed out at her own pace.

"Before the void took it... before it was shattered to kindling and dragged to the bottom of the sea, the Leviathan’s Wake wasn’t just a vessel," Morwenna muttered, staring blankly at the dark wood of the bedstead.
"It was our home.
It was where I gathered my family.
A whole crew of misfits, orphans, bastards, and strays... people the upper realms threw away like garbage.
People who had no lives, no domains, and no hope until I pulled them out of the mud and gave them the deck of a ship."
She swallowed again with her chest heaving against his ribs.
"We ruled the Abyssal Seas for centuries," she whispered, her fingers digging deeper into his chest.
"We took whatever we wanted from the divine fleets, danced on the edges of forbidden rifts, and answered to no god or emperor.
We were free.
But freedom is a sin in the eyes of the divine hierarchy.
The corporate deities... the higher pantheons... they couldn’t stand a mortal-born crew laughing in their faces."
A dark agonizing sorrow flickered across her face as memories she had spent half a millennium trying to drown surged back to the surface.
She remembered how the betrayal had actually happened.
Their impenetrable defensive arrays had been bypassed from the inside and the coordinates of their hidden anchorage of the barrier had been hit by...
Lyra.
’Lyra...’
Lyra had been just a sixteen-year-old kid when the inquisitors got their claws into her.
The girl had been terrified, weeping, manipulated by promises that they would spare her little brother if she only killed them by dropping the barriers.
Lyra had been an idiot child who thought she was saving family, only to end up leading every single soul on board into a cosmic meat grinder.
The entire crew had been butchered.
The deck had run red before the divine fleets dragged the broken wreckage down into the sunless abyss to drown forever.
Morwenna didn’t voice the girl’s name.
Even after five hundred years of burning rage, what was the point of blaming a terrified child manipulated by gods?
The pain was hers to carry...
She tugged weakly on Silas’s sleeve, it was a desperate silent plea for grounding.
’I don’t want to talk about them.’
The memories she shared with her crew were amazing and she would do so dozen times over.𝓯𝓻𝒆𝙚𝒘𝓮𝙗𝓷𝒐𝓿𝙚𝒍.𝙘𝓸𝙢
...But they were painful, very painful and even though it was selfish, Morwenna wanted to think about her new family.
Silas understood instantly.
He didn’t press her for details, nor did he lecture her about past mistakes.
He firmly squeezed her hand, pulling her body completely flush against his chest, wrapping his arms around her back, and gently patting the back of her dark head.
"There, there..." Silas murmured in a deeply affectionate rhythm, resting his chin lightly atop her hair.
"I’ve got you.
It’s over now."
Morwenna was an SSS-Rank Mythic Dread Queen... a terrifying entity capable of ripping fleets of ships enhanced by even gods apart with tidal fury.

She was nobody’s fragile princess, and she certainly wasn’t a baby yet, surrounded by the warm, sovereign aura radiating from his Gold Core, feeling the genuine protectiveness bleeding through his touch, the rigid armor around her heart completely crumbled.
Not like it was there whenever Silas touched her.
She let out a shaky, muffled sigh into the crook of his neck.
With a subtle, needy squirm, she pulled herself even higher onto his lap, curling her legs securely around his waist and resting her forehead against his clavicle.
She allowed herself to be held, to be coddled, to be babied by the only man in two universes who held her loyalty.
If it was her Captain doing the coddling, then she didn’t give a damn about her pride.
’It feels good too...’
For several minutes, the room remained entirely peaceful, save for the rhythmic rise and fall of their chests and the comforting crackle of the hearth fire.
Eventually, Morwenna stirred.
She tilted her head back, her dark and slightly messy hair swaying across her shoulders as she looked up into his face.
Her stormy gray eyes were still slightly rimmed with red, but the cold had vanished, replaced by a curious gaze.
"So..." she murmured, clearing her throat to regain a shred of her typical pirate rasp.
"How in the hells do you know about my ship, Captain?
You said an auction?"
Silas smiled warmly, brushing a stray dark lock from her cheek.
"At the Obsidian Sanhedrin," Silas explained, his voice rich with quiet satisfaction.
"The auctioneers brought out a relic that had supposedly washed ashore from a deep rift in the outer sectors.
They claimed it was recovered from the very wreckage of the Leviathan’s Wake."
Morwenna’s brows furrowed in pure bewilderment.
"Recovered from the wreck?" she scoffed softly, shaking her head.
"Captain, I spent five centuries trapped at the bottom of the abyssal trenches, drowning in divine chains before you pulled me through that portal.
Anything made of mortal steel or standard enchantments would have been crushed to dust under that water pressure hundreds of years ago.
What could have possibly survived down there?"
Silas didn’t answer with words.
Instead, he focused his intent, calling upon his dimensional storage.
A brilliant blue flash of spatial light ignited across the palm of his right hand.
The ambient air in the master quarters suddenly grew rich with the distinct scent of an oncoming oceanic tempest.
With a soft hum of displacement, a massive magnificent weapon materialized in his grasp.
"Oof—" Silas let out a low grunt as the weight of the blade dragged his arm downward, the pommel hitting the stone floor with a heavy thud.
"Damn... it’s got quite a bit of weight to it."

paragraphs: The weapon was a masterwork of forgotten artistry.
It was a curved pirate saber, forged from an iridescent light-drinking oceanic alloy that shimmered between deep abyssal blue and seafoam green.
The guard was sculpted like the unhinged jaws of a sea serpent, and intricate runic veins mapped themselves across the fuller of the blade, radiating a rhythmic heartbeat of tidal mana.
"They called it..." Silas began, looking up at her with a knowing grin.
"Tidebringer," Morwenna and Silas said at the exact same moment.
Silas’s smile widened into a beaming expression.
"You really do know it."
Morwenna stared at the blade, completely transfixed.
The laziness, the lingering grief, and the haze instantly evaporated from her demeanor.
She scrambled off his lap in a fluid breathless motion, her bare feet hitting the cold floorboards as she stood before him.
She reached out with trembling hands.

With an instinctive and deeply ingrained gesture of ultimate reverence toward the blade and the man who had returned it to her, she offered a small respectful bow before wrapping her calloused fingers around the leather-bound hilt.
FUU!
The moment her skin made contact with the oceanic metal, her stormy gray eyes flared with terrifying intensity.
A fierce, breathtaking smirk spread across her lips, showing her sharp canines.
"It really is you, Tidebrin—"
WHOOSH!
Before she could finish the name, the physical reality of the master quarters violently dissolved.
The air pressure inverted with catastrophic force. In a fraction of a second, the stone walls, the hearth, and the wooden furniture were completely engulfed by a colossal, roaring phantom ocean.
Silas’s breath was violently ripped from his lungs.
An overwhelming sensation of being plunged miles deep into an icy, pitch-black abyss washed over his senses.

The suffocating weight of billions of gallons of phantom seawater crushed against his ribs, making it impossible to draw oxygen with the roar of deep-sea currents thundering directly inside his skull.
Morwenna stood in the center of the surging illusion.
Her long dark hair billowed upward as if suspended weightlessly in the deep ocean tides, her loose linen shirt rippling violently against the phantom current.
The saber in her hand was howling, drinking in the sudden resonance of its true master.
Instead of panicking, Morwenna simply threw her head back and let out a loud ringing laugh that echoed through the watery void.
"Still as feisty as ever, aren’t you, girl?!" Morwenna barked at the weapon with fierce affection. "Calm yourself! We’re home now!"
She slammed a massive surge of her own SSS-Rank mythic mana down her arm and directly into the hilt.
The saber shuddered, letting out a submissive musical chime.

Instantly, the roaring phantom ocean shattered like fragile glass. The crushing water pressure vanished, the suffocating depths evaporated, and the dry warm air of the Keep flooded back into the room.
"Gah!"
Silas took a deep sudden gasp of air, coughing lightly as his lungs readjusted to the reality of the bedroom.
He looked up at her, thoroughly impressed and slightly exasperated by the absurdity of the relic.
’Does it need to be like that? Or is it me or has it become stronger?’
Morwenna didn’t pause as she fluidly swept the curved blade through the empty air of the room.
SHING! SHING!
The strikes were executed with terrifying master-class elegance.
Even though she wasn’t channeling destructive force into the room, the razor-sharp edge cut the ambient air so cleanly that faint vacuum whistles chirped along the trajectory of her slashes.
She stopped, resting the flat of the glowing blue-green blade against her palm, admiring the pristine metal with an expression of quiet awe.
"It hasn’t aged a single day..." Morwenna murmured softly, her fingers tracing the serpentine crossguard. "Still just like I remember it. So damn beautiful."
She looked over at Silas, her stormy eyes glowing with a personal warmth.

"This blade was the only gift my mother ever gave me before she vanished into the cosmic rifts," Morwenna explained, her voice dropping to a gentle nostalgic murmur. "She forged it from the heart of a fallen deep-sea leviathan. I carried it through every raid, every storm, and every war I ever fought. Both of us... we’ve truly come a long way, Captain."
With a subtle mental command, Morwenna released her grip.
Instead of falling to the floor, the heavy saber liquefied into a stream of iridescent oceanic light.
The light surged into the back of her right hand, searing itself into her flesh with a soft sizzle.
When the glow faded, an intricate deep-blue tattoo of a curved saber wrapped in sea serpents rested cleanly against her skin.
Silas blinked in surprise.
"A spatial imprint?"

"Soul-bound," Morwenna replied with a sharp satisfied smirk, flexing her fingers. "As long as it’s within my dimensional vicinity, only I can draw it to its full potential. To anyone else, it’s just a ridiculously heavy slab of pretty metal with a bit of power."
She slowly turned her gaze back toward him.
The nostalgic reverence in her posture shifted seamlessly into something far more dangerous, Morwenna looked fiercely affectionate like she wanted to eat him whole.

"Now then..." Morwenna purred, stepping across the floorboards toward the edge of the bed. Her hips swayed with lazy, deliberate confidence. "You went all the way to that soft human world, spent a small fortune, and brought me back my soul... A good Captain deserves an appropriate reward, doesn’t he?"
Silas raised an eyebrow, a slight smirk playing on his lips. "Oh? And what kind of reward does a Pirate Queen offer?"
Morwenna didn’t bother answering with words.
She lunged forward like a striking panther, climbing directly back onto the bed and straddling his lap with overwhelming physical force.
Before Silas could even react, she planted her calloused hands firmly against his shoulders, slamming him backward flat against the plush mattress and pinning him down beneath her weight.
She leaned down until her face was mere inches from his, her dark hair curtaining their faces in intimate shadow.
Despite her aggressive dominating posture, a sudden furious bright red blush violently erupted across her cheeks, spreading all the way down to her neck.
Her stormy gray eyes wavered between fierce hunger and flustered shyness.
"For doing this for me..." Morwenna stammered slightly, her voice dropping into a breathless, desperately bold whisper, "...you can put your babies inside me, Captain."
Silas stared at her, genuinely taken aback by her bluntness.
Morwenna’s face burned like a furnace, but she refused to back down. Her mind was entirely consumed by the lingering memories of the past few nights.

She remembered hiding in the closet behind them waiting for Silas to enter so she could ask for sex with the moves Eluned had taught her, only to hear the unmistakable shameful sounds of Silas and Eluned together.
She had peeked through the crack in the closet and seen the breathtaking World-Tree Goddess completely undone, weeping and crying out as Silas took her against the headboard.
Morwenna was a virgin of course, she didn’t even know what Intercourse meant truly... People in her ship did it and had more kids but Morwenna couldn’t, they were like children to her.
Why would she fuck her kids?
Right now, in terms of actual experience with a man she genuinely loved? She was hopelessly behind... That arrogant elven Goddess held all the advantages, and it drove the Pirate Queen insane.

She had even made the catastrophic mistake of venting her frustrated feelings to Aeliana earlier that week over a bottle of rum, confessing how hot and flustered it made her feel just watching the two of them from the shadows.
Aeliana had stared at her with utter deadpan elven judgment and casually muttered. "So you’re a cuckold, then."
A cuck?! Morwenna had nearly drawn steel on the Arcanist right then and there.
What in the seven hells did that mortal word even mean?!
Just because she had touched herself in the dark, getting dripping wet to the intoxicating image of her Captain roughly railing that whiny divine tree-spirit into the mattress?
That didn’t make her a watcher... it made her a starving woman waiting for her turn at the table!
She wanted to be the one crying out under his hands. She wanted her Captain to dominate her, to pin her down, and to breed her until she couldn’t walk.
Most importantly, she wanted to win.

In the Sovereign Realm, it was notoriously difficult for a lower-ranked or lower aged being to impregnate an SSS-Rank, especially one that had lived for centuries due to the massive conceptual gap in life-force power.
It required endless attempts, dedication, and sheer volume of stamina but Morwenna didn’t care about the mathematical odds.

She would ride him until the sun broke if she had to. As long as she claimed the title of bearing his very first child before Eluned, before Aeliana, or before any of the other seventy women in the barracks could even try, she would die a happy conqueror.
"You’re making quite a bold proposition, Morwenna," Silas teased softly, a low chuckle vibrating in his chest as his hands came up to lightly grip her waist. "Are you sure you can handle it?"
"Don’t mock me, Captain!" Morwenna snapped playfully, though her voice trembled with raw desire.
She leaned down and aggressively crushed her mouth against his, grinding her lips against his in a desperate bruising kiss that tasted of rich liquor and sweet untamed fire.
SMACK! SMACK!
She parted from his lips with a wet panting gasp, her gray eyes burning with fierce determination.
"Haah... Haah..."
"I am serious," she growled against his jawline. "I want your children. I want them right now so you better breed me into the mattress, Captain, or I’ll—"
Before she could finish her threat, Silas’s blue eyes flashed with a sudden golden light.
In a terrifyingly swift and effortless burst of motion, Silas shifted his weight.
The physical tables turned in a fraction of a second.
Morwenna gasped as the world spun, finding herself thrown flat onto her back against the furs, her slender wrists pinned firmly above her head against the wooden headboard by Silas’s unyielding grip.
Silas loomed over her, his broad shoulders casting her entirely in his shadow as he looked down at her with a smirk.
"Well, well..." Silas murmured, his voice dropping into a dark baritone that sent a violent jolt of electricity straight down her spine. "I shouldn’t keep my Hero waiting, should I?"
Morwenna’s entire body shuddered.
A desperate burning heat flared between her thighs as the fabric of her trousers instantly grew heavy and damp against her skin.
’Gods... I just completely wet myself,’ Morwenna thought frantically, her mind short-circuiting as a euphoric wave of submission washed over her.

She was a woman who bowed to no god, yet the feeling of being utterly overpowered, pinned down, and thoroughly dominated by Silas was the hottest and most intoxicating sensation she had ever experienced in her entire life.
’I want to have sex... Please no interruptions... Let him rail me hard. My womb is trembling too...’𝚏𝕣𝐞𝗲𝐰𝕖𝐛𝐧𝕠𝕧𝚎𝚕.𝐜𝚘𝗺
Silas leaned down slowly, his eyes locking onto her exposed pale throat.
Just as his lips were about to press against her skin—
CREEEAAAK!
The heavy oak doors of the master quarters swung completely open.
"Ehehehe~" A familiar melodic giggle echoed merrily through the room.
Silas froze, his forehead resting lightly against Morwenna’s collarbone. Morwenna’s eyes snapped wide in disbelief, her head violently turning toward the entrance.
Standing in the doorway, wearing her pristine, flowing emerald silk dress, was Eluned.
The SSS-Rank Goddess leaned comfortably against the doorframe, her silver-green hair tumbling over her shoulders.
She had a massive radiant smile plastered across her face with her cheeks lightly flushed as she casually rubbed her bare thighs together in shameless excitement.
"You two were just about to do it, weren’t you?" Eluned purred happily, her vibrant green eyes practically sparkling with voyeuristic delight.
She waved a delicate hand toward the bed, gesturing for them to continue. "Oh, please, do not stop on my account! Proceed, proceed! I want to watch every single second of it!"
Silas slowly lifted his head, letting out a heavy exhausted sigh. "Eluned..."

"What in the nine hells are you doing in here, you overgrown houseplant?!" Morwenna shrieked, her face turning an incandescent crimson as she desperately tried to pull her pinned wrists free from Silas’s grip.
Eluned didn’t flinch.
Instead, she reached into the folds of her silk robes with a triumphant grin and pulled out a sleek, rectangular device made of polished dwarven brass and runic glass.
It was a camera.

Just two days prior, Thora and the dwarven blacksmiths had reverse-engineered the high-tier digital recording technology brought over by Lord Sky’s integration team, adapting it to run on mana crystals.
Eluned had claimed the very first functional prototype for herself.

"I need proper documentation!" Eluned declared proudly, holding the device up to her eye and adjusting the runic focus. "The Pirate Queen always acts so tough and terrifying on the battlefield... I want to see the exact face she makes when Silas takes her! I want to capture her little ahegao expressions and preserve them in crystal forever!"
After they had sex... Eluned had turned into a very big pervert.

Before Silas could even react, she planted her calloused hands firmly against his shoulders, slamming him backward flat against the plush mattress and pinning him down beneath her weight.
She leaned down until her face was mere inches from his, her dark hair curtaining their faces in intimate shadow.
Despite her aggressive dominating posture, a sudden furious bright red blush violently erupted across her cheeks, spreading all the way down to her neck.
Her stormy gray eyes wavered between fierce hunger and flustered shyness.
"For doing this for me..." Morwenna stammered slightly, her voice dropping into a breathless, desperately bold whisper, "...you can put your babies inside me, Captain."
Silas stared at her, genuinely taken aback by her bluntness.
Morwenna’s face burned like a furnace, but she refused to back down.
Her mind was entirely consumed by the lingering memories of the past few nights.

She remembered hiding in the closet behind them waiting for Silas to enter so she could ask for sex with the moves Eluned had taught her, only to hear the unmistakable shameful sounds of Silas and Eluned together.
She had peeked through the crack in the closet and seen the breathtaking World-Tree Goddess completely undone, weeping and crying out as Silas took her against the headboard.
Morwenna was a virgin of course, she didn’t even know what Intercourse meant truly...
People in her ship did it and had more kids but Morwenna couldn’t, they were like children to her.
Why would she fuck her kids?
Right now, in terms of actual experience with a man she genuinely loved?
She was hopelessly behind...
That arrogant elven Goddess held all the advantages, and it drove the Pirate Queen insane.

She had even made the catastrophic mistake of venting her frustrated feelings to Aeliana earlier that week over a bottle of rum, confessing how hot and flustered it made her feel just watching the two of them from the shadows.
Aeliana had stared at her with utter deadpan elven judgment and casually muttered.
"So you’re a cuckold, then."
A cuck?!
Morwenna had nearly drawn steel on the Arcanist right then and there.
What in the seven hells did that mortal word even mean?!
Just because she had touched herself in the dark, getting dripping wet to the intoxicating image of her Captain roughly railing that whiny divine tree-spirit into the mattress?
That didn’t make her a watcher... it made her a starving woman waiting for her turn at the table!
She wanted to be the one crying out under his hands.
She wanted her Captain to dominate her, to pin her down, and to breed her until she couldn’t walk.
Most importantly, she wanted to win.

In the Sovereign Realm, it was notoriously difficult for a lower-ranked or lower aged being to impregnate an SSS-Rank, especially one that had lived for centuries due to the massive conceptual gap in life-force power.
It required endless attempts, dedication, and sheer volume of stamina but Morwenna didn’t care about the mathematical odds.
She would ride him until the sun broke if she had to.

As long as she claimed the title of bearing his very first child before Eluned, before Aeliana, or before any of the other seventy women in the barracks could even try, she would die a happy conqueror.
"You’re making quite a bold proposition, Morwenna," Silas teased softly, a low chuckle vibrating in his chest as his hands came up to lightly grip her waist.
"Are you sure you can handle it?"
"Don’t mock me, Captain!" Morwenna snapped playfully, though her voice trembled with raw desire.
She leaned down and aggressively crushed her mouth against his, grinding her lips against his in a desperate bruising kiss that tasted of rich liquor and sweet untamed fire.
SMACK!
SMACK!
She parted from his lips with a wet panting gasp, her gray eyes burning with fierce determination.
"Haah...
Haah..."
"I am serious," she growled against his jawline.
"I want your children.
I want them right now so you better breed me into the mattress, Captain, or I’ll—"
Before she could finish her threat, Silas’s blue eyes flashed with a sudden golden light.
In a terrifyingly swift and effortless burst of motion, Silas shifted his weight.
The physical tables turned in a fraction of a second.
Morwenna gasped as the world spun, finding herself thrown flat onto her back against the furs, her slender wrists pinned firmly above her head against the wooden headboard by Silas’s unyielding grip.
Silas loomed over her, his broad shoulders casting her entirely in his shadow as he looked down at her with a smirk.
"Well, well..." Silas murmured, his voice dropping into a dark baritone that sent a violent jolt of electricity straight down her spine.
"I shouldn’t keep my Hero waiting, should I?"
Morwenna’s entire body shuddered.
A desperate burning heat flared between her thighs as the fabric of her trousers instantly grew heavy and damp against her skin.
’Gods...
I just completely wet myself,’ Morwenna thought frantically, her mind short-circuiting as a euphoric wave of submission washed over her.

She was a woman who bowed to no god, yet the feeling of being utterly overpowered, pinned down, and thoroughly dominated by Silas was the hottest and most intoxicating sensation she had ever experienced in her entire life.
’I want to have sex...
Please no interruptions...
Let him rail me hard.
My womb is trembling too...’𝚏𝕣𝐞𝗲𝐰𝕖𝐛𝐧𝕠𝕧𝚎𝚕.𝐜𝚘𝗺
Silas leaned down slowly, his eyes locking onto her exposed pale throat.
Just as his lips were about to press against her skin—
CREEEAAAK!
The heavy oak doors of the master quarters swung completely open.
"Ehehehe~" A familiar melodic giggle echoed merrily through the room.
Silas froze, his forehead resting lightly against Morwenna’s collarbone.
Morwenna’s eyes snapped wide in disbelief, her head violently turning toward the entrance.
Standing in the doorway, wearing her pristine, flowing emerald silk dress, was Eluned.
The SSS-Rank Goddess leaned comfortably against the doorframe, her silver-green hair tumbling over her shoulders.
She had a massive radiant smile plastered across her face with her cheeks lightly flushed as she casually rubbed her bare thighs together in shameless excitement.
"You two were just about to do it, weren’t you?" Eluned purred happily, her vibrant green eyes practically sparkling with voyeuristic delight.
She waved a delicate hand toward the bed, gesturing for them to continue.
"Oh, please, do not stop on my account!
Proceed, proceed!
I want to watch every single second of it!"
Silas slowly lifted his head, letting out a heavy exhausted sigh.
"Eluned..."

"What in the nine hells are you doing in here, you overgrown houseplant?!" Morwenna shrieked, her face turning an incandescent crimson as she desperately tried to pull her pinned wrists free from Silas’s grip.
Eluned didn’t flinch.
Instead, she reached into the folds of her silk robes with a triumphant grin and pulled out a sleek, rectangular device made of polished dwarven brass and runic glass.
It was a camera.

Just two days prior, Thora and the dwarven blacksmiths had reverse-engineered the high-tier digital recording technology brought over by Lord Sky’s integration team, adapting it to run on mana crystals.
Eluned had claimed the very first functional prototype for herself.
"I need proper documentation!" Eluned declared proudly, holding the device up to her eye and adjusting the runic focus.
"The Pirate Queen always acts so tough and terrifying on the battlefield...
I want to see the exact face she makes when Silas takes her!
I want to capture her little ahegao expressions and preserve them in crystal forever!"
After they had sex...
Eluned had turned into a very big pervert.

paragraphs: "I WILL RIP YOUR WORLD-TREE ROOTS OUT OF THE DIRT AND BURN THEM FOR FIREWOOD!" Morwenna roared, thrashing wildly against the mattress with pure embarrassment.
"Stay still, Morwenna," Silas ordered smoothly, his grip on her wrists remaining entirely unbreakable.
Morwenna blinked with her furious rant cutting off. "C-Captain?"
Silas didn’t give her a chance to question him. He leaned down and aggressively sank his teeth deep into the soft vulnerable crook of her neck.
"Ahn—!"
A sharp high-pitched whimper tore from Morwenna’s throat, instantly melting into a long, trembling groan of overwhelming pleasure.
Because her soul was bound to his and recognized him, her body offered zero physical resistance to the bite.
Silas’s sharp canines pierced cleanly through her pale skin, drawing a small brilliant bead of bright crimson blood.
He pulled his teeth back slightly, pressing his lips against the puncture to aggressively suck and lap the blood away with the flat of his warm tongue.
"There," Silas murmured against her heated skin, pulling back with a satisfied grin. "A proper love bite."
Morwenna lay completely paralyzed beneath him, her eyes wide, glassy, and swimming with a helplessly adorable expression of pure shock.
Her mouth was parted in a tiny, stunned gasp and her cheeks were burning so intensely they looked like ripe spirit-fruits.
’I... I got a hicke—’
CLICK! FLASH!
A bright burst of mana-light violently illuminated the entire bedroom.
"Cheese~!" Eluned cheered cheerfully from the doorway.
The Goddess giggled, tapping the runic dial on the back of the camera.
A small perfectly developed rectangular projection of crystal paper slid out from the brass slot.
Eluned held it up, admiring the high-definition image of the terrifying Astral Dread Queen looking thoroughly ravished and hopelessly flustered.
"Oh, this is a masterpiece," Eluned beamed, waving the photo in the air to show them. "I am framing this in the office!"
That was the final straw. The monumental humiliation snapped Morwenna out of her daze.
"GIVE ME THAT DAMN THING!"
With a feral shriek of pure rage, Morwenna forcefully exploded upward with the entirety of her mythic strength.
The violent unexpected thrust was so massive that Silas was literally thrown entirely off the mattress, flipping gracefully through the air before landing on his boots near the center of the room.
Morwenna launched herself off the bed like a guided missile, her claws extended as she dove straight for the Goddess’s throat.
Eluned, however, was an SSS-Rank deity in her own right.

With a breezy musical laugh, the World-Tree Spirit smoothly drifted backward on a cushion of gentle wind currents, easily dodging Morwenna’s frantic lunge as the Pirate Queen crashed headfirst into the Keep’s heavy corridor carpet.

"Hey! Didn’t you want to have sex with him?!" Eluned teased playfully, dodging another swipe of Morwenna’s hands while holding the photograph high out of reach. "You’re ruining your own reward, Morwenna! If you keep fighting me, Silas is just going to give all his energy to me tonight instead!"
"I WILL KILL YOU! I WILL DROWN YOU IN SEAWATER!" Morwenna screamed, scrambling to her feet with her dark hair completely wild.
Silas stood in the center of the master quarters, running a hand down his face as he let out a long groan.
"I leave for a few days..." Silas muttered to himself. "Just some damn days."
Before the two mythic entities could turn the second floor of the Keep into a smoking crater of elemental warfare, a polite throat-clearing echoed from the bottom of the stone staircase.
"Ahem."
The commotion instantly halted.
Stepping gracefully onto the landing was Kadi, the Second Secretary.
The sandy-haired mage looked exceptionally neat, wearing her tailored administrative robes and carrying a leather-bound inventory ledger against her chest.
She casually ran a hand through her hair, looking unfazed by the sight of a half-naked Pirate Queen wrestling a laughing Goddess on the floorboards.
"Welcome back to the territory, Lord Graves," Kadi greeted smoothly, bowing her head with crisp unflappable professionalism.
"Thank you, Kadi," Silas replied, leaning against the doorframe with relief. "Please tell me you have a report that requires my immediate presence elsewhere."
Kadi adjusted her ledger, her lips curling into a dry, highly knowing smirk as her amber eyes flickered between the two disheveled deities.

"Actually, my Lord, I came to deliver a brief update on territory morale," Kadi said, her tone dripping with subtle amusement. "The Keep has been unnervingly quiet while you were away on Earth. Interestingly enough, Lady Eluned and Lady Morwenna have spent the last few days acting remarkably friendly toward one another... right up until the exact moment they realized you were back in your bed."
Both Eluned and Morwenna stiffened, their cheeks flushing identically as they immediately turned to glare at the secretary.
"We were not being friendly!" Morwenna hissed, crossing her arms defensively.
"I was simply tolerating her presence near the gardens!" Eluned pouted.
Kadi didn’t flinch in the slightest.
Over the past few days, as the territory expanded and the hierarchy solidified, Kadi had come to a very simple realization.
At the core of it all, whether they were mortal mages, elves that wrote smut, or ancient SSS-Rank cosmic deities... they were all hopelessly devoted to the exact same man.
Every single woman in this domain ultimately wanted to be dicked down and claimed by their Lord.
So why waste energy fighting over turns when they could simply share the load together?
An empire was built on teamwork, after all.
"Of course, my Ladies," Kadi replied smoothly, entirely ignoring their weak protests.
She turned her full attention back to Silas. "The department heads and the captains have gathered in the Mess Hall, my Lord. They have prepared their reports regarding the new girls."
Silas nodded firmly, immensely grateful for the interruption. He straightened his long black shirt, brushing the wrinkles from his sleeves.

"Understood," Silas said, stepping past the flustered Pirate Queen and the giggling Goddess toward the stairs. "Tell everyone to assemble in my office and make sure Talira and Aeliana are present as well. We have a massive logistics overhaul to handle."
"Right away, Lord Graves," Kadi bowed.
Fifteen minutes later, Silas sat behind the massive obsidian-and-ironwood desk in his primary command office on the ground floor of the Keep.
He took a slow, deep breath, staring at the absolute chaos unfolding across the heavy table in front of him.
’This isn’t what I meant by a tactical meeting...’ Silas thought, his eye twitching slightly.
The office was packed to the brim.
Standing around the desk weren’t just his military commanders; practically every prominent woman in the Blessed Land had crammed themselves into the room.
Aeliana stood near the window, her Royal Elven robes clean and pristine once more, though her eyes carried a newfound disciplined reverence whenever she looked at him.

Beside her, Talira leaned against the wall, her tail flicking with restless draconic heat. Rowenna, Brida, and Tasmin were huddled near the maps, while Eluned and Morwenna stood on either side of his high-backed chair like two possessive royal sentinels.
And dominating the center of the desk was Kaelia.
The Culinary Maestro was in her element.
The dark-haired chef had laid out nearly a dozen steaming, intricately garnished silver platters across Silas’s maps.

"You have to try this one first, Lord Graves!" Kaelia insisted with passion, using a polished silver fork to present a glistening, caramelized cut of spiced meat. "During your absence, another stray migration of Tier 2 Magma-Scaled Drakes attempted to breach the eastern crags! I took the flank cuts, cured them in sweet spirit-nectar, and flash-seared them with wild ember-herbs!"𝙛𝓻𝒆𝓮𝒘𝙚𝙗𝒏𝙤𝙫𝓮𝒍.𝓬𝒐𝙢

"No, Captain, eat the ocean-bass first!" Morwenna interrupted aggressively, shoving a bowl of fragrant broth-poached fish right in front of his face. "I caught it in the deep river trench myself! It restores raw stamina three times faster than drake meat!"

"My Lord, please," Eluned chimed in with a sweet, competitive smile, presenting a crystal bowl filled with glowing, sliced Spirit-Flora. "You must balance your palate with the fruits of the World Tree. It purges all mortal fatigue!"
"Lord Graves, the Shieldmaidens baked these protein flatbreads for you!" Brida boomed from the back, holding up an entire basket.
"Try the glazes, Sovereign," Aeliana murmured politely from the window, her cheeks dusting pink.
Silas sat frozen in his chair, completely surrounded by forks, platters, and eager, shining eyes.
Every single girl in the room was aggressively leaning forward, practically begging him to taste the specific dish they had helped prepare.
He let out a long, helpless sigh, running a hand through his dark hair.
’All that time I spent handling business in the regular world, life kept moving here too...’ Silas reflected warmly.
He had an empire to build, massive upgrades to calculate, and more than a hundred women looking to him for leadership, sustenance, and safety.
He couldn’t afford to ignore their efforts.
"Alright, alright," Silas chuckled, holding his hands up in surrender as he picked up his fork. "I’ll try it. I’ll try everything. Just don’t choke me."

The office erupted into a chorus of delighted giggles and eager chatter as Silas began methodically tasting each dish, praising Kaelia’s incredible culinary mastery and nodding in genuine appreciation at the flavors.

’Once I finish eating, I’ll distribute the Frost-Drake battalion armor to Brida, hand the Scepter to Kadi, give Eluned the Tear relic, and then we can finally move on to summoning the Hero...’ Silas mapped out his priorities in his mind.
He reached for a piece of the roasted drake meat, ready to call the meeting to order—
SLAM!
The heavy double doors of the command office swung open without a single polite knock.
The lively chatter in the room instantly died down.
Stepping through the threshold, dragging a thick cloud of pungent, gray tobacco smoke behind her, was Evelyn.

The former Lord Sky of the Unmovable Wall looked completely relaxed as the petite dark-haired woman was wearing a sleek gray oversized hoodie over cargo pants, her boots crunching arrogantly against the stone floor.
Resting casually between her lips was a thick glowing cigar.
She took a long, slow drag, letting the aromatic smoke billow lazily toward the ceiling, completely unbothered by the twenty pairs of deadly eyes immediately glaring daggers at her.
Silas dropped his fork onto the plate, his brows furrowing as he leaned back in his chair.

"Evelyn," Silas sighed, waving his hand to disperse the cloud of gray smoke drifting across his desk. "Do you have to smoke those damn things inside my Keep? We have a Conservatory full of celestial crops next door."
Evelyn stopped a few paces from his desk. She took the cigar from her lips, flicked the glowing ash carelessly onto the floor, and offered him a dry razor-sharp smirk.

"Don’t be such a delicate little princess, Graves," Evelyn insulted smoothly, her voice carrying that distinct, husky rasp. "If your fancy magic plants can’t survive a little high-grade tobacco, you’re building a pretty pathetic empire... but then again... What did I expect? You complain all the time."
’I missed you... and I did exactly as you asked.’
Eluned’s emerald eyes flared with violent intent, and Morwenna’s hand instinctively drifted toward the tattoo on her right wrist, ready to draw Tidebringer and cut the arrogant woman in half.
Silas raised a single calm hand, silently signaling his Heroes to stand down.
"What do you want, Evelyn?" Silas asked, crossing his arms. "I thought you were busy overseeing the rest of your garrison’s reorganization on the western ridge."
Evelyn reached into the breast pocket of her military coat, pulling out a sleek laminated plastic card.
With a flick of her wrist, she tossed the card across the desk. It slid across the smooth obsidian surface, coming to a halt right next to Silas’s plate.

"I just got back from the human world myself," Evelyn stated, crossing her arms over her chest and taking another slow puff of her cigar. "I figured you’d already made your Descent back to the territory, considering I texted your Spirit Phone not too long ago and your status showed completely offline."
’I actually texted that I saw you and your sister having fun and wanted us to go out or something but...’
Silas looked down, picking up the small card.
It was an official encrypted government identification card issued directly by the High Federal Registry of Earth.
Printed squarely on the front, beneath a digital photograph of a striking, single-armed woman with glowing purple eyes and dark hair, was a full profile though she looked a bit younger.

"That’s your official registered citizen identity in the Human world," Evelyn explained, a faint, mocking grin touching her lips. "The one tied to your ’Vespera’ disguise persona. It’s fully validated in the global database... Nobody from the Guilds or the Lord Association will ever trace it back to a scholarship kid from Valoria Academy."
Silas looked at the bold black lettering printed beneath the photograph.
’Did you have to say scholarship kid?’
He blinked.
His jaw slowly dropped, his face deadpanning as he read the name aloud to the empty room.
"...Kara White?"
Silas looked up from the card, staring at Evelyn in disbelief.
"Did you seriously have to pick the most generic unimaginative name in human history?!"

"Do you have to smoke those damn things inside my Keep?
We have a Conservatory full of celestial crops next door."
Evelyn stopped a few paces from his desk.
She took the cigar from her lips, flicked the glowing ash carelessly onto the floor, and offered him a dry razor-sharp smirk.
"Don’t be such a delicate little princess, Graves," Evelyn insulted smoothly, her voice carrying that distinct, husky rasp.
"If your fancy magic plants can’t survive a little high-grade tobacco, you’re building a pretty pathetic empire... but then again...
What did I expect?
You complain all the time."
’I missed you... and I did exactly as you asked.’
Eluned’s emerald eyes flared with violent intent, and Morwenna’s hand instinctively drifted toward the tattoo on her right wrist, ready to draw Tidebringer and cut the arrogant woman in half.
Silas raised a single calm hand, silently signaling his Heroes to stand down.
"What do you want, Evelyn?" Silas asked, crossing his arms.
"I thought you were busy overseeing the rest of your garrison’s reorganization on the western ridge."
Evelyn reached into the breast pocket of her military coat, pulling out a sleek laminated plastic card.
With a flick of her wrist, she tossed the card across the desk.
It slid across the smooth obsidian surface, coming to a halt right next to Silas’s plate.
"I just got back from the human world myself," Evelyn stated, crossing her arms over her chest and taking another slow puff of her cigar.
"I figured you’d already made your Descent back to the territory, considering I texted your Spirit Phone not too long ago and your status showed completely offline."
’I actually texted that I saw you and your sister having fun and wanted us to go out or something but...’
Silas looked down, picking up the small card.
It was an official encrypted government identification card issued directly by the High Federal Registry of Earth.
Printed squarely on the front, beneath a digital photograph of a striking, single-armed woman with glowing purple eyes and dark hair, was a full profile though she looked a bit younger.
"That’s your official registered citizen identity in the Human world," Evelyn explained, a faint, mocking grin touching her lips.
"The one tied to your ’Vespera’ disguise persona.
It’s fully validated in the global database...
Nobody from the Guilds or the Lord Association will ever trace it back to a scholarship kid from Valoria Academy."
Silas looked at the bold black lettering printed beneath the photograph.
’Did you have to say scholarship kid?’
He blinked.
His jaw slowly dropped, his face deadpanning as he read the name aloud to the empty room.
"...Kara White?"
Silas looked up from the card, staring at Evelyn in disbelief.
"Did you seriously have to pick the most generic unimaginative name in human history?!"

chapters.title: Chapter 412: Social... Media?
paragraphs: Evelyn brought the thin cigarette back to her chapped lips, drawing in a short deliberate pull of bitter smoke before exhaling a thin gray stream straight up toward the vaulted obsidian ceiling of the command office.
’Is it just me or does Evelyn seem more depressed all of a sudden...?’ Silas thought with a raised eyebrow.
That seemed to be the issue, why the hell would she randomly call him Graves then?
She gave a lazy, one-shouldered shrug, completely unbothered by the collective hostile glares radiating from the room’s resident powerhouses.

"Look, Silas, you weren’t on the surface, and I needed something solid that wouldn’t get flagged by the regional census algorithm," Evelyn rasped, tapping her cargo pant pocket. "Besides, ’Evelyn White’ isn’t a bad family name to piggyback off of but the name on the laminated plastic is only half the battle. Right now, what we actually need to do is set up a functional, verified Social Media presence for the persona."
A collective pause settled over the command room.
Eluned blinked her luminous emerald eyes, tilting her head with genuine innocent curiosity.

Beside her, Morwenna crossed her arms over her loose linen tunic, her brow furrowing in confusion, while Talira’s draconic wings rustled against the stone wall as the warrior looked around the room as if searching for a physical object.
Even Aeliana and Kadi paused, their hands hovering over their respective ledgers and platters.

"Social... Media?" Morwenna echoed, rolling the foreign mortal words over her tongue with deep suspicion, her stormy gray eyes narrowing at Evelyn. "What kind of astral ward or communication array is that? Is it a human surveillance spell?"

"It’s not a spell, sea-dog," Evelyn muttered, flicking a microscopic flake of ash toward the base of the desk. "It’s a global network where millions of regular mortals and low-tier awakened post their daily lives, share broadcasts, and validate whether someone actually exists in the modern world... Silas is going to have to interact with real-world guild executives, sector officials, and global media outlets sooner rather than later. If ’Vespera’ just drops out of thin air with zero digital footprint, zero registered communications, and zero past history, every corporate intelligence syndicate on the planet is going to put a tracer on her within forty-eight hours... We have to make her look like an actual living, breathing person who has a normal life on Earth."
Before anyone could ask a follow-up question, the heavy double doors of the office were violently kicked open with a deafening bang.
"LORD GRAVES!"
A loud, boisterous roar echoed through the stone corridor as a short, incredibly sturdy figure bounded into the office like a launched cannonball.
It was Thora.
The dwarven blacksmith was still wearing her heavy soot-stained leather forge apron, her thick braided hair bouncing wildly behind her shoulders.
The second her sharp eyes locked onto Silas sitting behind the massive desk, all concept of military decorum ceased to exist.
She didn’t salute, she didn’t wait for permission, and she certainly didn’t care about the high-ranking meeting.

Thora stomped across the floor, kicked off the edge of the stone masonry, and launched herself directly through the air, landing square in Silas’s lap with enough momentum to rattle the heavy wood of the chair.
"Whoa—Thora, calm down!" Silas laughed, catching her sturdy frame by the waist as his hands braced against her rough leather apron.
Thora didn’t listen in the slightest.

She threw her thick, muscular arms around his neck in a crushing headlock of affection, planting a loud, wet kiss directly onto his cheek before burying his entire face straight into the soft, unyielding swell of her chest.

"You’re back! You’re finally back, my Lord!" Thora bellowed joyfully, rubbing his head aggressively against herself. "The forge was dead without ye! These fancy ladies wouldn’t let me smash open the good mead barrels until ye returned!"
From beside the desk, Talira’s golden reptilian slit-pupils violently contracted.
The towering winged human let out a deep rumbling hiss that vibrated the glassware on Kaelia’s food platters.
A twin jet of scalding white steam shot aggressively from Talira’s nostrils as the air temperature around her spiking instantly.
Talira took two heavy strides forward.
With terrifying precision, her hand reached out, grabbed Thora by the thick knot of her braided hair, and forcefully hoisted the squirming dwarf straight into the air like a sack of scrap iron.
"Off," Talira rumbled, her voice vibrating with draconic irritation. "You are suffocating the Lord, you loud anvil."

"Unchain me, ye overgrown flying lizard!" Thora shrieked, kicking her heavy steel-toed boots wildly at the empty air as she swung from Talira’s grip. "I was welcoming our Lord! At least I have the guts to jump in his lap! You just stand in the corner looking like a scaly gargoyle! You ain’t even sexy enough to warm his sheets!"
Talira’s jaw tightened, the muscles in her scaled forearm bulging as she genuinely considered smashing the screaming dwarf headfirst into the stone tiles.
Only a firm, warning glance from Silas kept the dragon from turning the office into a demolition site.
Amidst the screaming and the kicking, Eluned stepped forward, her elegant emerald dress rustling against the floorboards.
The Goddess looked past the bickering vanguard, her vibrant green eyes locking squarely onto Evelyn with a deeply possessive pout.

"So... in essence," Eluned spoke, her melodious divine voice effortlessly cutting through Thora’s cursing. "My Lord has barely set foot within his own domain, and now he must immediately depart back to the mortal realm with you?"
Every single female in the room went dead silent.
Morwenna, Aeliana, Rowenna, Kadi, Kaelia, Brida, Tasmin, and the squirming Thora all simultaneously turned their heads, fixing Evelyn with intense stares.
The power of protective devotion, latent divine pressure, and territorial possessiveness converging on that single spot was heavy enough to buckle the floorboards.
Evelyn stood in the center of the crosshairs, feeling a prickle of cold sweat at the back of her neck beneath her messy bun.
She had fought these women in a brutal televised war, at least some of them.𝐟𝕣𝗲𝕖𝕨𝗲𝐛𝗻𝗼𝐯𝗲𝚕.𝗰𝚘𝐦
She knew for a fact that every single one of them was a terrifying powerhouse who could tear a standard strike team to pieces.
Being surrounded by the very army that had broken her Unmovable Wall was still undeniably unnerving.
’Christ...’ Evelyn thought, tapping the ash from her cigarette with slightly rigid fingers. ’They look like they’re ready to skin me alive just for breathing his air.’
Before the room’s atmospheric pressure could trigger an actual attack, Silas stood up from his chair.
He smoothed the fabric of his long black shirt, rolling his broad shoulders as the warm, calming golden aura of his Gold Core washed through the room, instantly pacifying the rising tension.

"I’ll go," Silas announced calmly, offering the room an easy reassuring smile. "It’s just setting up some administrative paperwork and sorting out the disguise on the surface. It won’t take long and when I get back, we have a mountain of real work to do like processing the new monster migrations, and going through the next summoning phase."
The change in the room’s atmosphere was instantaneous.
The dark murderous glares instantly softened.
Eluned lowered her hands with an obedient, trusting nod; Morwenna’s jaw relaxed; and even Thora stopped kicking, dangling quietly from Talira’s hand with a wide, bashful grin.
Because Silas had spoken with clear authority, not a single one of them raised an objection.
Their respect for his commands superseded everything else.
Evelyn watched the total effortless compliance with wide stunned eyes.

’He didn’t even raise his voice...’ she noted internally, shaking her head in disbelief. ’One sentence and twenty bloodthirsty killers turn into obedient puppies. The command control on this guy is ridiculous...’
"Let’s go, Evelyn," Silas said, stepping around the obsidian desk. "Lead the way."
They walked out of the command office side by side and the heavy reinforced oak doors clicked shut behind them.
The second the latch locked into place, a muffled wave of synchronized female bickering, whining, and complaining instantly erupted from the room behind them, echoing through the thick stone.
Silas winced slightly, letting out a heavy amused sigh as he rubbed the back of his neck.
Evelyn took another drag of her cigarette, a dry smirk pulling at the corner of her lips as they walked down the wide stone corridor toward the grand staircase.
"They really love you, don’t they?" Evelyn remarked, blowing smoke toward the high archways. "It’s almost creepy how much they worship the ground you walk on, Silas..."

"Isn’t that the whole point of being a Lord?" Silas countered smoothly, his heavy boots clicking rhythmically against the stone steps as they descended toward the ground floor. "You give them a real home, you feed them, you fight on the front lines so they don’t die meaningless deaths... and in return, they trust you enough to follow you into hell. If your people don’t love you enough to want to stand by your side, you’re just a glorified slave driver with a title."
Evelyn glanced at his side profile, remaining quiet for a second.

The memory of how her own troops had suffered under the relentless exhausting grind of running a mobile fortress flashed through her mind, alongside the genuine unprompted mercy Silas had shown Elm after the war.
"Yeah, yeah," she muttered, rolling her dark eyes. "Save the inspirational speech for the live streams, saint."
They pushed through the massive double doors of the Keep, stepping out onto the neatly paved central courtyard of the Blessed Land.
The air was crisp and clean, insulated by the towering Tier 3 Steel-Weave Palisade that hummed with intricate defensive blue runes.
Over on the eastern side of the courtyard, the barracks grounds were bustling with activity as dozens of Shieldmaidens and transferred recruits ran synchronized phalanx drills.
"Halt! Form up on the marker!" a loud, authoritative voice barked across the yard.
Standing at the head of the training line was Gunnhild.
The magic Swordsman was fiercely running the new recruits through rigorous positioning routines.
The moment Gunnhild’s sharp eyes caught sight of Silas descending the Keep’s front steps, her stern drill-instructor facade completely shattered.
"LORD SILAS!"
Without a second thought, Gunnhild activated wind magic.
A sudden gust of green mana coiled around her heavy iron-plated boots as she exploded across the stone tiles in a dead sprint, closing the thirty-yard distance in less than two seconds.
She threw herself directly into his arms, wrapping her muscular limbs tightly around his waist with an overwhelming breathless gasp.
"Welcome home, my Lord!" Gunnhild cried out happily, burying her face into the crook of his shoulder. "We secured the western watch perimeter just as you ordered!"
Silas was pushed back half a step by the sudden tackle, but he laughed warmly, wrapping his arms around her back and gently running a hand through her thick hair.
"Good work, Gunnhild. You’ve been keeping everyone in line, I see."
As his hand moved through her hair, however, Silas caught a sudden overwhelming whiff of something distinctly sour and unwashed.
He paused, blinking as he leaned back slightly, taking another subtle sniff near her shoulder.
"Though... you smell a little weird today," Silas noted honestly, raising an eyebrow with an amused smirk. "Did you take a bath in monster blood, or did you just wrestle a pack of wolves?"
Gunnhild completely froze.
The physical color drained from her face for a microsecond before a violent volcanic crimson blush exploded across her cheeks, burning all the way down to her collarbones.
Her legs began to tremble uncontrollably against the stone tiles as reality crashed into her skull.

’I... I haven’t washed my hair since Tuesday!’ Gunnhild screamed internally with pure panic seizing every nerve in her body. ’I’ve been helping Thora at the forge, hauling scrap, skinning beasts, running drills with the new recruits... I haven’t taken a single bath in three days!’
She slowly realized that she reeked of sweat, sulfur, oxidized iron, and rotting drake bile.
And she had just aggressively tackled the man she adored, shoving her disgusting unwashed scalp directly into his face.
’Why didn’t anyone tell me?!’
Gunnhild’s terrified, wide eyes darted across the courtyard toward the edge of the barracks.
Sitting on an empty supply crate, leisurely polishing the mythril string of her recurve bow, was Fenna.
The archer met Gunnhild’s gaze, bit her lower lip so hard it turned white, and desperately puffed her cheeks out to stifle a roaring fit of hysterical laughter.
’YOU TRAITOROUS BITCH!’ Gunnhild cursed in silent fury.
It was always your closest friends who sat back in silence just to watch you humiliate yourself in front of your crush...

Gunnhild knew with agonizing certainty that from this day forward, in the barracks, in the mess hall, and on the training grounds, she was going to be known as the girl who smelled like rotting meat to the Lord.
Rumors spread fast in Blessed Land after all.
