paragraphs: "Hey, it’s really not a big deal," Silas said softly, noticing the pure horror in her eyes as he reached out to pat her arm. "You’ve been working hard on the defenses, so—"
"I AM SORRY, LORD GRAVES!" Gunnhild shrieked at the top of her lungs, forcefully pushing herself backward off his chest with her boots skidding across the stone.

Tears of world-ending embarrassment spilled from the corners of her eyes as she covered her face with both gauntlets, spun on her heel, and bolted toward the bathhouse at high speeds, leaving a trail of dust in her wake.
Silas stood with his hand still hovering in the air, utterly bewildered.𝘧𝘳𝘦ℯ𝓌𝘦𝒷𝘯𝑜𝑣𝘦𝓁.𝒸𝘰𝓂
Evelyn took another long, slow drag of her cigarette, watching the crying warrior sprint across the courtyard before looking over at Silas with that trademark deadpan exhaustion.
’Yeah I’m guessing she’s depressed...’
"Is she going to survive that mental breakdown, or do you need to reassign her squad?"
Silas gave a helpless shrug. "Beats me. Girls in this territory have some weird priorities."
"Clearly," Evelyn snorted, flicking her head toward the southern quadrant. "Come on. My quarters are this way."

A few minutes later, the two of them entered one of the Tier 2 Multi-Floor Living Quarters that Silas had constructed on the western edge of the Blessed Land to house Evelyn and her remaining inner circle.
Silas stepped through the heavy wooden door into Evelyn’s personal quarters, instinctively bracing himself for a room that smelled like a tavern ashtray.
To his genuine surprise, the room was remarkably clean.
The wide stone window was pushed fully open, letting the crisp mana-rich breeze of the Umbral Basin circulate through the spacious chamber.
The air smelled of clean linen, polished wood, and faint traces of lavender... not a single whiff of stale tobacco smoke lingered in the fabrics.
"Huh," Silas noted, nodding in genuine approval as he walked across the room. "I’m impressed, Evelyn. I figured your room would look like a condemned scrap heap. It’s actually really nice in here..."
"I have basic hygiene standards, Silas," Evelyn deadpanned, locking the door behind them. "I smoke outside to keep the fabrics clean... Don’t act so surprised."
Silas walked over to the neatly made bed and sat down comfortably on the edge of the mattress.
As he leaned back on his hands, his blue eyes naturally drifted toward the low wooden counter beside the washbasin.
Resting prominently on the polished stone surface, catching the natural light from the window, was a smooth and brightly colored egg-shaped silicone device with a sleek metallic base.
Silas blinked. He leaned forward slightly, squinting at the odd shape, his brow furrowing as the realization slowly dawned on his modern mind.
’Wait a minute... isn’t that a—’
Before the thought could even finish forming in his head, a blur of dark gray fabric shot across the room.
Evelyn snatched the vibrating egg off the counter with lightning-fast reflexes, violently shoving it behind her back.
Her permanently tired pale face instantly turned an incandescent shade of crimson.
Her dark eyes flared with raw, frantic embarrassment as she glared daggers at him, her chest heaving beneath her oversized hoodie.

’It’s not what you think, fucker!’ Evelyn screamed internally, her soul practically leaving her body. ’You’re an eighteen-year-old virgin, you don’t know shit about adult stress management! Why the hell did I leave that on the counter?!’
Silas didn’t say a word.
He slowly raised a single unimpressed eyebrow at her, his expression flattening into pure deadpan judgment.
He casually rolled his eyes toward the ceiling, quietly pushed himself up off the mattress, and stood up straight, smoothing his clothes.

’If she’s been using that thing in here... did she do it on this bed?’ Silas thought, a slight shiver running down his spine as he took two deliberate steps away from the sheets. ’Did I just sit down directly on Evelyn’s personal—’

"Shut up!" Evelyn snapped aloud, her voice pitching slightly higher than usual as she aggressively shoved the device into an obscure drawer and slammed it shut with a loud clack. "Don’t you dare say a single word, Graves!"
"I didn’t say anything," Silas replied smoothly, crossing his arms with an amused smirk. "You’re the one yelling at the furniture."
Evelyn took a deep shuddering breath, forcibly pulling her oversized gray hood further down over her burning face to hide the lingering blush.
She cleared her throat roughly, trying desperately to salvage whatever shred of dignity she had left.

"Anyway," Evelyn rasped, aggressively changing the subject as she reached into her inventory. "Here’s the rest of the package. Jax managed to forge the database records perfectly so everything is clean."
She tossed two items onto the wooden table in front of him.
The first was a sleek modern smartphone encased in a vibrant pastel-pink cover patterned with cartoon kittens.
The second was a neatly folded, high-tier black designer dress made of elegant alchemical silk, complete with matching gloves and accessories.
Silas picked up the bright pink kitten phone, staring at the screen with bewilderment.
"Really, Evelyn? Kittens?"

"Kara White is a nineteen-year-old civilian girl who lives in Valoria City," Evelyn explained, leaning against the wall and crossing her arms with a defensive scowl. "She doesn’t carry a military slab. The phone is fully registered under Kara’s civilian ID, loaded with basic applications, and completely air-gapped from your Lord Association profile... When you make your Descent back to Earth, you need to find a private changing stall, put on the dress, activate the disguise ring to shift into Vespera, and carry that phone."
Silas picked up the soft silk dress, inspecting the fine embroidery.
"Is there actually a tangible strategic advantage to setting up this whole social media farce? Or are you just enjoying watching me crossdress?"
Evelyn snorted, rolling her eyes.

"I couldn’t care less about your wardrobe, Slas but yes, there is a massive strategic advantage like I said before... Right now, ’Vespera’ is a ghost. The guilds think you’re an unregistered rogue Lord or a hidden weapon from a foreign alliance. By creating an active, verified Social Media profile and sharing basic, controlled livestreams under the Vespera persona, we establish a public narrative. We prove that Vespera is an independent entity operating in the human world. The public attention will act as a legal shield... the big guilds won’t be able to assassinate or kidnap you in the dark if five hundred million people are actively watching your stream."
Silas nodded slowly, recognizing the sound logic behind the plan. In a world driven by corporate monopolies and public perception, fame was an impenetrable armor.
"Alright," Silas agreed, transferring the pink phone and the black dress directly into his Lord Inventory. "That makes sense. So, where are we meeting on the surface?"

"I already booked a private suite under a shell company at the Skybli Hotel near Silverleaf," Evelyn answered, checking the time on her wrist terminal. "We need a secure high-end location to set up the network broadcasting nodes."
Silas paused, his brows slightly raising. "Skybli Hotel? That’s weird. That’s literally right next to the plaza where I went out for dinner with Lia and Martha just tonight."

"Then you should know the area," Evelyn replied dismissively. "We meet on the street outside the main lobby. And for the record, I’m showing up in my normal, real-world appearance... A thirty-year-old masked Lord like ’Lord Sky’ meeting a nineteen-year-old girl at night looks insane. I’ll just be Evelyn."
Silas considered the narrative they had constructed for Kara White.

The official cover story was that Kara had failed her initial Awakening Ceremony at eighteen, only to unexpectedly trigger a delayed anomalous core manifestation a full year later... coinciding with the exact timeframe of Silas’s current group.

Delayed awakenings were rare, but documented anomalies that occurred every single year across the globe. It was the perfect, airtight explanation for why a high-tier talent had zero corporate sponsorship.

"Won’t it cause trouble for you if you’re seen walking around in public with Kara White?" Silas asked, looking at her with genuine curiosity. "Once we launch the stream, Kara is going to be one of the most famous scrutinized names on the planet."
Evelyn gave a careless lazy shrug, pulling another slim cigarette from her pocket and rolling it between her fingers.

"Nobody pays attention to me in the real world, Silas," Evelyn said softly, a faint, self-deprecating smirk touching her lips. "To the rest of the planet, I’m just a rich business woman who lives in the industrial sector. I’ll be fine."
Silas smiled, stepping toward the center of the room. "Alright. Thanks for sorting all of this out, Evelyn. I appreciate the hustle."
"Yeah, yeah. Just don’t embarrass me out there," Evelyn muttered.
Silas called up his digital interface, his finger hovering over the glowing [Ascend] tab.
With a soft hum of displacement magic, his body dissolved into a pillar of light, vanishing entirely from the Sovereign Realm as he initiated his return to Earth.
Evelyn stood in the quiet room, staring at the empty space where he had just been standing.
She let out a long ragged breath with her shoulders sagging.
’I... I should really punch him in the ribs next time,’ Evelyn thought, running a trembling hand through her messy dark hair.
Ever since their trip to Shogitown... where she had completely ruined his day off by dragging him into her family drama and forcing him to help her stalk her brother.
Evelyn had felt a deep, gnawing sense of guilt. Silas had never complained, had treated her with nothing but patience, and had even saved Elm’s life without asking for a single credit in return.
Setting up this fake identity and sorting out his social media was the bare minimum she could do to pay him back. He was a good guy, even if he was an annoying, smug asshole.
She looked down at the floor, catching sight of the forgotten silicone egg lying by the wastebasket where she had kicked it.
’Fuck... Fuck... Fuck!’ Evelyn groaned in agony, burying her face in her hands. ’He definitely knows what that was. He literally looked at the bed and stood up! He thought I soaked the mattress!’
Just when she was trying so hard to present herself as a competent woman, she had managed to look like a desperate, degenerate pervert in front of a teenager.
And the worst part? The reason she had even bought the damn thing in the first place... wasn’t it because her brain wouldn’t stop replaying the way he—?
’Gods damn it all.’
Evelyn aggressively crushed the unlit cigarette between her fingers, tossed it into the bin, and pulled out a fresh one.
She lit it with a quick snap of mana, taking a massive drag to forcefully smother the rising panic in her chest.
"Whatever, fuck it all..."
She was depressed... She was trying to hide it but had Silas seen through? Evelyn doubted it, he couldn’t read her that much.
She brought up her own interface and slammed her thumb onto the [Ascend] button.
The world dissolved into pitch-black nothingness.
A fraction of a second later, the sensory deprivation of the spatial jump shattered.
Evelyn materialized in the physical world, sitting on a weathered wooden park bench across the street from the towering crystal-paned facade of the Skybli Hotel.
The night air of Valoria City was cool and bustling, filled with the distant hum of mag-trains, hovering delivery drones, and the chatter of citizens navigating the pristine sidewalk.
She had deliberately initiated her Descent from this exact park bench earlier, ensuring she would spawn directly at the meeting point.
Evelyn pulled out her personal smartphone, checking the encrypted network feed.
’Silas came online and offline, huh?’
She slipped the phone back into her oversized hoodie, tapping her foot against the concrete.

’Silas has never worn women’s clothing in his life,’ Evelyn thought with a slight smirk playing on her lips despite her impatience. ’He probably put the corset on backward. Should I have offered to help him get dressed? No, that would have been even weirder...’
She leaned back against the bench, letting her head rest against the wood as she stared up at the sky.
How long had it actually been since they met?
It felt like months, but it had only been a matter of a week or so since their brutal clash during the Lord War.
Evelyn had spent her entire life surrounded by sycophants, ruthless mercenary Lords, and her own demanding Brother.
She had maybe one or two real friends in the regular world, and both of them treated her with cautious fragile distance.
But Silas was different.
He didn’t treat her like a famous streamer, nor did he treat her like a broken woman who had lost an empire and was trying to get it back.
He traded insults with her, called her out on her unhealthy habits, gave her an entire residential place for her troops, and treated her like an equal partner.
Was it because he had beaten her so thoroughly in the Lord War? Was that why she felt so unnervingly comfortable around him?
A sudden strange warmth began to bloom in the dead center of her chest.
It was a tight suffocating sensation that made her breathing grow shallow.
It crept up into her neck, making her brain feel fuzzy and sending a subtle uncontrollable tremor through her fingers.
It was an unfamiliar intense emotional flare that completely bypassed her defenses.
It was...
It was...
’I WANT TO KICK THAT SMUG FUCKER STRAIGHT IN THE JAW!’

chapters.title: Chapter 414: Skybli Hotel [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Evelyn forcefully kicked her boot into the empty air, gritting her teeth in frustration.

He was always making subtle mocking jokes about how she was an ’older woman’! She was twenty-two! Exactly twenty-two years old! She was barely four years older than him! Why did he talk to her like she was a retired grandmother sitting on a porch?!
’So what if I was thirty, huh?!’ she fumed internally, crossing her arms tightly. ’Would that make me obsolete?! I’m in my prime!’
She took a deep steadying breath, forcefully quelling her internal rant.
Ten minutes slowly ticked by... The afternoon sun began to cast long shadows across the pavement.
Evelyn clicked her tongue with her patience rapidly wearing thin.
The Skybli Hotel wasn’t even a fifteen-minute drive from the Silverleaf District where Silas lived, especially if he took a high-speed cab. What could possibly be taking him so long?
"Hey, Ev."
The voice was melodic, and carried a subtle husky undertone that made the air chill as Evelyn blinked, snapping her head upward.
Standing on the sidewalk directly in front of the bench was Kara White.
The disguise was perfection as usual.
Standing at approximately 5’7"... just a hair shorter than Evelyn herself, the woman looking down at her was undeniably breathtaking.
She possessed a striking aristocratically sculpted face, framed by silky raven-black hair that swayed gently in the night breeze.
Resting elegantly atop her head was a wide-brimmed designer black sunhat that cast a soft mysterious shadow over her eyes.
The black alchemical silk dress Evelyn had purchased hugged the woman’s slender frame flawlessly, tapering into a graceful flowing skirt that stopped just above a pair of sleek, matte-black heels.
A matching set of dark silk gloves concealed her hands, and beneath the veil of the hat, a pair of sharp mesmerizing purple eyes gleamed with vibrant intelligence.
Evelyn completely choked on her breath, her jaw parting slightly in shock.
’Holy shit...’ Evelyn thought, completely stunned by the visual transformation. ’He actually looks... gorgeous.’
"It took you forever to get here," Evelyn managed to rasp out, forcing her face into a deadpan scowl to mask the fact that she had just been caught staring.
Kara or rather, Silas operating within the seamless perception-disguise of Thora’s ring let out a soft feminine chuckle that carried a surprisingly natural cadence.

"Well, I had to find a secluded changing stall in the commercial district," Kara explained, adjusting the brim of her hat. "And on the walk over here, I had to dodge three different guys in tailored suits trying to ask for my contact handle. Apparently, I’m quite the catch."
Inside the core of the disguise, Silas was internally grinning from ear to ear.
’Damn... I really am a hot human being,’ Silas thought to himself in shameless satisfaction.
Back on Earth, he had been an exhausted unremarkable corporate wage-slave drowning in bills.
But now? When he was a man, high-ranking noble women threw millions of credits and supercars at his feet.
And when he threw on a dress and shifted his mana into a female persona, wealthy bachelors on the street practically tripped over themselves just to hold the door open for him.
It had to be in his spiritual genetics.

The Gold Core didn’t just multiply his physical combat stats; it clearly maxed out his charisma across every single gender spectrum. Who said a kid born in the Lower Ward slums couldn’t ball out on the world stage...?
Evelyn took one look at the smug radiant expression on Kara’s face and immediately knew exactly what the idiot was thinking.
"Don’t flatter yourself, Graves," Evelyn groaned, standing up from the wooden bench and tossing her dead cigarette butt straight into her Lord Inventory to avoid littering.
She reached out, grabbed Kara firmly by the silk-gloved hand, and forcefully began dragging the striking woman across the street toward the grand glass entrance of the Skybli Hotel.
"Come on, ’Miss White,’" Evelyn muttered dryly, pulling her hood down as they approached the revolving doors. "Let’s go set up your stream before someone tries to propose to you on the sidewalk."

The heavy crystal-paned revolving doors of the Skybli Hotel spun with a silent frictionless glide, admitting Evelyn and her striking companion into the cavernous opulence of the ground-floor grand atrium.
The transition from the cool twilight streets of Valoria City to the interior of the five-star establishment was immediate.
The air here was artificially chilled, lightly scented with distilled white lotus and expensive lavender terpenes, and hummed with the quiet continuous murmur of the elite.

Towering pillars carved from veined Calacatta marble stretched four stories high toward a magnificent glass dome, through which the darkening evening sky was visible, scattered with the first faint pinpricks of stars.
Polished obsidian floor tiles mirrored every step, so immaculately maintained that the reflections of the passing guests looked as sharp as physical twins walking beneath their heels.

Scattered throughout the sprawling lobby were dozens of patrons... corporate guild liaisons dressed in sharply tailored mana-silk suits, high-tier awakened lords lounging on plush velvet sectionals while reviewing live auction feeds on floating holographic tablets, and wealthy scions from the Upper Ward sipping champagne served by pristine alchemical automations.
And almost immediately, heads began to turn.
The visual contrast between the two newcomers was stark enough to command attention.

Evelyn looked like she had just rolled out of a cheap hostel and accidentally wandered into the wrong establishment... completely swallowed in her oversized, faded dark-gray hoodie, baggy cargo pants, and scuffed combat boots with her messy dark hair piled into a loose bun that defied all forms of brushwork.
But beside her stood a woman who looked like an untouchable aristocratic phantom. She was truly beautiful.
Despite her lowered head, there was an anomaly that no amount of designer fabric could entirely conceal.
Her left sleeve hung entirely flat, pinned elegantly against the side of her bodice with an ornate silver brocade.
The complete absence of a left arm was a glaring unmistakable hallmark of a seasoned, battle-scarred combatant or a catastrophic survivor of the Sovereign Realm.
Murmurs rippled across the nearest lounge area.
"Look at her... who is that?"
"Is that a high-ranking mercenary? Look at the gait... she isn’t even looking at the floor, but her balance is perfect."

"That silk is grade-four shadow weave. You can’t buy that in the Lower parts of the city but who walks around with an unregenerated limb these days? A high-tier restructuring elixir costs less than a million credits..."
Kara kept her chin slightly tucked, letting the broad brim of the hat do its job as she kept her gaze fixed on the marble floor.

Beside her, Evelyn’s hand remained firmly anchored around her silk-gloved right wrist, dragging her with aggressive unbothered strides past the staring onlookers straight toward the colossal semicircular reception desk that dominated the center of the atrium.
Behind the polished white-quartz counter stood three receptionists, each wearing immaculate gold-trimmed navy blazers and carrying the pristine, practiced smiles of high-end hospitality staff.
As Evelyn and Kara approached the central terminal, the lead receptionist... a meticulously groomed woman with her blonde hair twisted into a sharp French roll straightened her posture.

Her eyes flickered briefly over Evelyn’s oversized hoodie with a microscopic, professional twitch of her left brow, before landing on Kara’s striking figure, lingering for a fraction of a second on the pinned-up sleeve and the mesmerizing sliver of purple visible beneath the hat.

"Good evening, ladies. Welcome to the Grand Skybli," the receptionist greeted smoothly, her voice pitched in that warm melodic tone reserved for elite establishments. "How may we assist you today? Do you have an existing reservation, or are you inquiring about our overnight suites?"
Before Evelyn could even part her lips, the receptionist tapped a small runic glyph embedded in the quartz counter, bringing up a glowing promotional display that projected softly between them.

"If you are looking to book today, you have arrived at a truly fortuitous time," the woman continued with polished enthusiasm. "This week marks the Skybli’s Centenary Anniversary. In celebration of our founding, management is currently offering an exclusive twenty-five percent rate reduction for all premium penthouses and executive suites located on Floor Sixty and above. These rooms feature dedicated high-power mana-insulation arrays, private balcony drop-zones, and direct encrypted connections to the Upper Ward data-sphere. It is an extraordinary opportunity for discerning awakened guests..."
The receptionist paused, her hands clasped delicately over the counter as she waited for a response.
Evelyn, however, said nothing.

The former Lord of the Unmovable Wall simply stood there in her baggy clothes, her dark eyes half-lidded, looking thoroughly bored and exhausted as if the concept of an anniversary discount was entirely beneath her cognitive bandwidth.
She didn’t reach for her pockets, she didn’t open her mouth, and she didn’t even shift her weight.
Standing beside her, Silas locked within the stunning, feminine frame of Kara White felt a sudden prickle of irritation.

She raised her slender, silk-gloved right hand toward the brim of her black sunhat, her fingers catching the edge of the velvet fabric.

sentences.text: Evelyn forcefully kicked her boot into the empty air, gritting her teeth in frustration.
He was always making subtle mocking jokes about how she was an ’older woman’!
She was twenty-two!
Exactly twenty-two years old!
She was barely four years older than him!
Why did he talk to her like she was a retired grandmother sitting on a porch?!
’So what if I was thirty, huh?!’ she fumed internally, crossing her arms tightly. ’Would that make me obsolete?!
I’m in my prime!’
She took a deep steadying breath, forcefully quelling her internal rant.
Ten minutes slowly ticked by...
The afternoon sun began to cast long shadows across the pavement.
Evelyn clicked her tongue with her patience rapidly wearing thin.
The Skybli Hotel wasn’t even a fifteen-minute drive from the Silverleaf District where Silas lived, especially if he took a high-speed cab.
What could possibly be taking him so long?
"Hey, Ev."
The voice was melodic, and carried a subtle husky undertone that made the air chill as Evelyn blinked, snapping her head upward.
Standing on the sidewalk directly in front of the bench was Kara White.
The disguise was perfection as usual.
Standing at approximately 5’7"... just a hair shorter than Evelyn herself, the woman looking down at her was undeniably breathtaking.
She possessed a striking aristocratically sculpted face, framed by silky raven-black hair that swayed gently in the night breeze.
Resting elegantly atop her head was a wide-brimmed designer black sunhat that cast a soft mysterious shadow over her eyes.
The black alchemical silk dress Evelyn had purchased hugged the woman’s slender frame flawlessly, tapering into a graceful flowing skirt that stopped just above a pair of sleek, matte-black heels.
A matching set of dark silk gloves concealed her hands, and beneath the veil of the hat, a pair of sharp mesmerizing purple eyes gleamed with vibrant intelligence.
Evelyn completely choked on her breath, her jaw parting slightly in shock.
’Holy shit...’ Evelyn thought, completely stunned by the visual transformation. ’He actually looks... gorgeous.’
"It took you forever to get here," Evelyn managed to rasp out, forcing her face into a deadpan scowl to mask the fact that she had just been caught staring.
Kara or rather, Silas operating within the seamless perception-disguise of Thora’s ring let out a soft feminine chuckle that carried a surprisingly natural cadence.
"Well, I had to find a secluded changing stall in the commercial district," Kara explained, adjusting the brim of her hat.
"And on the walk over here, I had to dodge three different guys in tailored suits trying to ask for my contact handle.
Apparently, I’m quite the catch."
Inside the core of the disguise, Silas was internally grinning from ear to ear.
’Damn...
I really am a hot human being,’ Silas thought to himself in shameless satisfaction.
Back on Earth, he had been an exhausted unremarkable corporate wage-slave drowning in bills.
But now?
When he was a man, high-ranking noble women threw millions of credits and supercars at his feet.
And when he threw on a dress and shifted his mana into a female persona, wealthy bachelors on the street practically tripped over themselves just to hold the door open for him.
It had to be in his spiritual genetics.
The Gold Core didn’t just multiply his physical combat stats; it clearly maxed out his charisma across every single gender spectrum.
Who said a kid born in the Lower Ward slums couldn’t ball out on the world stage...?
Evelyn took one look at the smug radiant expression on Kara’s face and immediately knew exactly what the idiot was thinking.
"Don’t flatter yourself, Graves," Evelyn groaned, standing up from the wooden bench and tossing her dead cigarette butt straight into her Lord Inventory to avoid littering.
She reached out, grabbed Kara firmly by the silk-gloved hand, and forcefully began dragging the striking woman across the street toward the grand glass entrance of the Skybli Hotel.
"Come on, ’Miss White,’" Evelyn muttered dryly, pulling her hood down as they approached the revolving doors.
"Let’s go set up your stream before someone tries to propose to you on the sidewalk."

The heavy crystal-paned revolving doors of the Skybli Hotel spun with a silent frictionless glide, admitting Evelyn and her striking companion into the cavernous opulence of the ground-floor grand atrium.
The transition from the cool twilight streets of Valoria City to the interior of the five-star establishment was immediate.
The air here was artificially chilled, lightly scented with distilled white lotus and expensive lavender terpenes, and hummed with the quiet continuous murmur of the elite.

Towering pillars carved from veined Calacatta marble stretched four stories high toward a magnificent glass dome, through which the darkening evening sky was visible, scattered with the first faint pinpricks of stars.
Polished obsidian floor tiles mirrored every step, so immaculately maintained that the reflections of the passing guests looked as sharp as physical twins walking beneath their heels.

Scattered throughout the sprawling lobby were dozens of patrons... corporate guild liaisons dressed in sharply tailored mana-silk suits, high-tier awakened lords lounging on plush velvet sectionals while reviewing live auction feeds on floating holographic tablets, and wealthy scions from the Upper Ward sipping champagne served by pristine alchemical automations.
And almost immediately, heads began to turn.
The visual contrast between the two newcomers was stark enough to command attention.

Evelyn looked like she had just rolled out of a cheap hostel and accidentally wandered into the wrong establishment... completely swallowed in her oversized, faded dark-gray hoodie, baggy cargo pants, and scuffed combat boots with her messy dark hair piled into a loose bun that defied all forms of brushwork.
But beside her stood a woman who looked like an untouchable aristocratic phantom.
She was truly beautiful.
Despite her lowered head, there was an anomaly that no amount of designer fabric could entirely conceal.
Her left sleeve hung entirely flat, pinned elegantly against the side of her bodice with an ornate silver brocade.
The complete absence of a left arm was a glaring unmistakable hallmark of a seasoned, battle-scarred combatant or a catastrophic survivor of the Sovereign Realm.
Murmurs rippled across the nearest lounge area.
"Look at her... who is that?"
"Is that a high-ranking mercenary?
Look at the gait... she isn’t even looking at the floor, but her balance is perfect."
"That silk is grade-four shadow weave.
You can’t buy that in the Lower parts of the city but who walks around with an unregenerated limb these days?
A high-tier restructuring elixir costs less than a million credits..."
Kara kept her chin slightly tucked, letting the broad brim of the hat do its job as she kept her gaze fixed on the marble floor.

Beside her, Evelyn’s hand remained firmly anchored around her silk-gloved right wrist, dragging her with aggressive unbothered strides past the staring onlookers straight toward the colossal semicircular reception desk that dominated the center of the atrium.
Behind the polished white-quartz counter stood three receptionists, each wearing immaculate gold-trimmed navy blazers and carrying the pristine, practiced smiles of high-end hospitality staff.
As Evelyn and Kara approached the central terminal, the lead receptionist... a meticulously groomed woman with her blonde hair twisted into a sharp French roll straightened her posture.

Her eyes flickered briefly over Evelyn’s oversized hoodie with a microscopic, professional twitch of her left brow, before landing on Kara’s striking figure, lingering for a fraction of a second on the pinned-up sleeve and the mesmerizing sliver of purple visible beneath the hat.
"Good evening, ladies.
Welcome to the Grand Skybli," the receptionist greeted smoothly, her voice pitched in that warm melodic tone reserved for elite establishments.
"How may we assist you today?
Do you have an existing reservation, or are you inquiring about our overnight suites?"
Before Evelyn could even part her lips, the receptionist tapped a small runic glyph embedded in the quartz counter, bringing up a glowing promotional display that projected softly between them.
"If you are looking to book today, you have arrived at a truly fortuitous time," the woman continued with polished enthusiasm.
"This week marks the Skybli’s Centenary Anniversary.
In celebration of our founding, management is currently offering an exclusive twenty-five percent rate reduction for all premium penthouses and executive suites located on Floor Sixty and above.
These rooms feature dedicated high-power mana-insulation arrays, private balcony drop-zones, and direct encrypted connections to the Upper Ward data-sphere.
It is an extraordinary opportunity for discerning awakened guests..."
The receptionist paused, her hands clasped delicately over the counter as she waited for a response.
Evelyn, however, said nothing.

The former Lord of the Unmovable Wall simply stood there in her baggy clothes, her dark eyes half-lidded, looking thoroughly bored and exhausted as if the concept of an anniversary discount was entirely beneath her cognitive bandwidth.
She didn’t reach for her pockets, she didn’t open her mouth, and she didn’t even shift her weight.

chapters.title: Chapter 415: LordGram [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: "Why the fuck would you do that?!" Evelyn yelled, throwing her hands up in the air as the elevator passed Floor 30 in total silence. "The entire point of this disguise is to avoid making a scene in the public registry! You’re supposed to be a low-profile anomaly, not a circus act! Why are you trying to act like an arrogant noble heiress?!"
Evelyn was grateful that she had at least set up a small soundproof barrier around them upon entering.
Kara didn’t argue.

Instead, she reached into the small silk pocket of her dress with her single right hand, pulled out the pastel-pink smartphone with the cartoon kittens, unlocked the screen with a flick of her thumb, and turned the display toward Evelyn’s face.
Hovering on the screen was an open forum thread from Threaddit... the largest decentralized discussion board on Earth.
The title of the post was bolded in bright neon blue.
[GUIDE: Top 10 Psychological Tricks to Pass Flawlessly as a High-Society Awakened Woman (UPDATED 2026)].
Kara’s slender index finger tapped directly against the glowing number one entry on the list.
[Rule 1: Radiate untouchable confidence. Never explain yourself to service staff. If someone questions your presence, act as though their entire bloodline owes you money.]
Evelyn stared at the glowing pink screen.
She stared at the cartoon kittens dancing on the phone case.
She stared at the ridiculous forum advice and then she looked up at Silas’s strikingly gorgeous, purple-eyed face looking back at her with unshakeable sincerity.
Her jaw clenched so hard a vein visibly throbbed against her left temple.
Her fingers twitched at her sides, her chest heaving beneath her oversized hoodie as she fought the overwhelming violent urge to jump forward and punch her square in the jaw.
’I am going to kill him,’ Evelyn thought, her soul screaming in agony.
"You..." Evelyn choked out, her face flushing red with a mixture of embarrassment and rage. "You got your behavior... from a Threaddit thread?!"
Kara snickered softly as she reached out with her gloved hand, playfully tapping Evelyn’s burning cheek with her fingertips.
"You have to admit, Ev," Kara murmured, her purple eyes sparkling with mischief. "Your face looks exceptionally cute when you’re about to pop a blood vessel."
"Fuck you, Silas!" Evelyn spat, swatting her hand away with a ferocious scowl.
DING!
The elevator chime chimed softly as the digital display overhead flashed [Floor 86: Imperial Wing].
The heavy gilded doors slid open silently, revealing a private, carpeted foyer that led directly into a breathtaking multi-thousand-square-foot luxury suite.
The Imperial Suite of the Skybli Hotel looked less like a hotel room and more like a private palace floating above the city.
Floor-to-ceiling panoramic windows lined the entire northern and eastern perimeter of the suite, offering an unobstructed, god-tier view of the sprawling Valoria City skyline at night.

Below them, the gleaming spires of the Upper Ward glittered with thousands of lights, the crisscrossing mag-train lines traced glowing pathways across the city, and the mana-arrays of the commercial districts pulsed with light that shone against the deep indigo of the evening sky.

The interior was outfitted with plush cream-colored leather furnishings, a fully stocked bar made of polished dark mahogany, intricate runic light fixtures that hummed with soothing spiritual frequencies, and a colossal king-sized bed elevated on a low marble dais in the master chamber.
Kara stepped out of her black heels the moment they crossed the threshold, leaving the shoes neatly by the entryway.
"Haah... Finally..."
She walked across the thick, cloud-soft white rug, rolling her shoulders as she casually tossed her wide-brimmed black sunhat onto the nearest leather armchair.
Her long raven-black hair spilled freely over her shoulders, framing her pale face in dark striking waves.
She walked over to the massive sectional sofa facing the skyline, sitting down with a comfortable, sprawling sigh and crossing her legs.
"Not bad," Kara commented, glancing around the massive suite with an approving nod. "The City Lord’s people definitely know how to build luxury and you’ve got good taste in rooms, Evelyn."
Evelyn kicked the heavy suite door shut, locking the deadbolts with a sharp flick of her mana before walking over to the bar.
She pulled a fresh slim cigarette from her cargo pocket, stuck it between her lips, and reached for her lighter.

"Don’t get comfortable yet," Evelyn rasped, lighting the tip and exhaling a thin stream of gray smoke toward the high ceiling’s ventilation array. "We’re here on a schedule. We need to get this account set up, validated, and seeded as soon as possible."

"Alright, boss," Kara smiled, leaning back against the leather cushions. "How are we doing this? You mentioned LordTube earlier I think, but I don’t exactly have a highlight reel of combat footage ready to upload."
Evelyn walked over, leaning against the back of the sofa with her arms crossed.

"LordTube is for long-form raid archives, official guild declarations, and battle breakdowns," Evelyn explained, pulling her own sleek black smartphone from her pocket. "That’s where Lords go when they want to broadcast a full-scale siege or monetize their territory wars. For establishing a fresh, mysterious persona who operates primarily on the surface? You use Lordgram."
Kara tilted her head slightly. "Lordgram?"

"It’s the primary image-and-short-text platform for the global awakened community," Evelyn said, tapping her screen to pull up the application interface. "Lords, high-ranking mercenaries, Guild recruiters, and their fanbases use it to track daily status updates, aesthetic snapshots, and territory milestones... It’s significantly faster to build engagement there, and it doesn’t require a dedicated broadcasting crew. We post three photos of Kara White, seed the algorithm with verified tags, and let the internet do the rest of the heavy lifting."
Kara raised an eyebrow, looking very skeptical.

"What if people think it’s fake?" Kara asked, resting her chin on her hand. "The internet on Earth isn’t stupid. What if they assume these are just AI-generated composite renders, or some high-tier marketing firm using deep-fake alchemical filters to launch a new virtual model?"
Evelyn snorted loudly, looking down at Kara like she had just asked if the sun was hot.

"Do you live under a literal boulder, Silas?" Evelyn deadpanned, rolling her eyes. "Ever since the Great Convergence, the World Lord Association implemented the Global Authenticity Protocols... Every single image uploaded to Lordgram is automatically scanned by a watermark in a way. If an image contains even a fraction of a percent of digital alteration, generative synthesis, or illusion magic, the system tags it with a bright red ’Unverified Composite’ warning and buries the post... Everything that goes through a verified profile is legally recognized as pure physical reality."
She tapped her phone against her palm with a sharp smirk playing on her lips.
"And for extra insurance," Evelyn added, "once your account goes live, I’m going to use my official Lord Sky verified profile to follow you and drop a comment on your first post."
Kara’s purple eyes widened slightly. "You’re going to use the Lord Sky handle? Won’t that blow our cover?"

"Lord Sky has over two hundred million followers, but the profile only follows forty-two people worldwide... all of them top-tier solo Lords, guild masters, or legendary recluses," Evelyn explained with a vicious grin. "If Lord Sky suddenly follows a mysterious one-armed purple-eyed nineteen-year-old girl who lives in Valoria City with zero guild affiliation, the algorithm is going to lose its mind and the traffic will explode within seconds."
"I like the way your little brain works," Kara chuckled. "Alright. Set it up."
Evelyn sat down on the leather sofa beside her, pulling out the pastel-pink kitten phone.
With practiced lightning-fast thumb movements, Evelyn navigated through the encrypted registry protocols.
She bypassed the standard civilian verification queues using the Black-Pass credentials Jax had forged in the underworld, rapidly generating the core account.
[Profile Created: @LordVespera_Official]
[Handle: Vespie022_]
[Bio: "Just the Lord of Blessed Land"]

"Hold still," Evelyn instructed, holding the pink phone up in front of Kara’s face. "Let’s get the primary profile picture first... Don’t do that weird squinty model thing you were doing earlier. Just look at the lens naturally."
Kara sat up straight, turning her head slightly toward the soft golden glow of the city lights streaming through the floor-to-ceiling windows.
She didn’t force a stiff smile... she simply relaxed her features, letting a knowing enigmatic curve touch her lips as her luminous purple eyes met the camera’s optical sensor.
CLICK!
The high-definition mana-camera captured the image in stunning crystal-clear detail.

The warm ambient light from the city illuminated the porcelain texture of her pale skin, the delicate angles of her cheekbones, and the vibrant mesmerizing violet depths of her irises, contrasting magnificently against the deep shadows of her raven-black hair.
Evelyn stared at the captured photo on the screen for a long quiet second, her breath catching slightly in her throat before she aggressively cleared her throat and tapped the ’Set as Avatar’ button.
’He’s way too good at this,’ Evelyn cursed internally. ’It’s genuinely irritating how photogenic this asshole is...’
If she had his confidence, she would feel so much better when she took pictures.

"Now, we need three distinct lifestyle shots for the initial posts," Evelyn commanded, standing up and gesturing toward the panoramic window. "Get over there. Lean against the glass. Look out over the skyline like you’re contemplating whether you want to buy the city or burn it down..."
"What a weird thing to say."
"Just do it fucker!"
Kara stood up, walking barefoot across the plush rug to the massive glass pane.

She turned her body in profile, resting her single right hand lightly against the transparent surface, her dark hair cascading over her bare elegant collarbones as she gazed out over the glittering spires of Valoria City at night.
The black silk dress clung perfectly to her back, the pinned left sleeve adding an aura of dangerous tragic mystery to the breathtaking composition.
CLICK!

"Good," Evelyn muttered, checking the framing. "Now, turn around. Sit on the edge of the low marble table near the bar... Cross your legs, rest your chin on your knuckles, and look directly down the barrel of the camera. Give me that arrogant, ’I could cleave you in half with a butter knife’ look you gave me during the war."
Kara laughed, moving to the marble table.

She sat gracefully on the polished stone, crossing her long legs and leaning forward, her purple eyes narrowing into a sharp confident gaze that radiated the undeniable authority of the Lord of Blessed Land.
CLICK!

"Last one," Evelyn said, walking over to the plush velvet armchair where the black designer sunhat was resting. "Put the hat back on, but tilt it up with your thumb so only your right eye is visible. Keep it casual, like you were just interrupted while having tea."
’I think this could fit Evelyn...’ Silas thought, she could honestly be a good photographer.
Kara picked up the wide-brimmed hat, settling it over her dark locks and lifting the brim with her single silk-gloved thumb, offering the camera a lazy charming smirk.
CLICK!
Evelyn sat back down on the sofa, rapidly cropping the images and attaching the appropriate metadata tags.
Based on Kara’s actual demeanor when she wasn’t locked in combat... she was relaxed, slightly sarcastic and confident too...
Evelyn drafted three short and perfectly understated captions.
’Heh, did he think I was going to do it properly? I’ll sabotage him a bit too! Who doesn’t add captions to their pictures.’
"Done," Evelyn declared, hitting the glowing blue [PUBLISH BATCH] button.
A soft chime resonated from the pink phone as the three high-resolution images synced with the global Lordgram servers, officially establishing Kara White’s digital existence in the modern world.

Evelyn immediately switched to her personal black phone, opened her verified Lord Sky account, and tapped the bright blue [FOLLOW] button on Kara’s profile before dropping a single ambiguous comment on the third photo:
[@LordSky_Official: Where are your captions? 🤣🤣🤣]

"There," Evelyn said, tossing the pink phone back onto Kara’s lap as she collapsed back against the sofa cushions, rubbing her tired eyes. "I’ll drop an official announcement link on my LordTube community tab in about an hour once the algorithm indexes the tags but the foundation is set. We can pack up and head back to the Sovereign Realm whenever you’re ready."
Kara caught the pink phone, sliding it onto the low table beside her. She didn’t reach for her disguise ring, nor did she make a move toward the door.
Instead, she remained seated on the plush cushions, her purple eyes gazing out over the glittering city lights stretching across the horizon.
"Let’s stay here for a little bit," Kara said softly, her voice carrying along gently. "There’s no rush. The territory is secure, the girls is running their drills, and it’s peaceful up here."
Evelyn blinked, turning her head to look at her. She didn’t argue, simply letting out a quiet breath as she leaned her head back against the sofa.
"Fine by me. The silence is nice for once."
Kara smiled. She turned her body toward Evelyn, extending her single silk-gloved right hand over the space between them.
A soft brilliant pulse of azure mana illuminated her palm.

When the light faded, Kara was holding a tall, pristine crystal cup filled with three generous scoops of rich, marbled mint-chocolate-chip and dark-cocoa gelato, topped with a delicate silver spoon and a drizzle of sweet alchemical honey.
Cold mist drifted lazily from the frozen dessert, filling the immediate air with the rich refreshing scent of pure peppermint and roasted cacao.
Kara held the cup out toward Evelyn, offering a warm, genuine smile.
"Here," Kara said. "I passed by that high-end creamery on the corner of the commercial plaza on my way over here. I remembered you looked a little down earlier, so I figured I’d pick it up for you."

Instead, she reached into the small silk pocket of her dress with her single right hand, pulled out the pastel-pink smartphone with the cartoon kittens, unlocked the screen with a flick of her thumb, and turned the display toward Evelyn’s face.
Hovering on the screen was an open forum thread from Threaddit... the largest decentralized discussion board on Earth.
The title of the post was bolded in bright neon blue.
[GUIDE: Top 10 Psychological Tricks to Pass Flawlessly as a High-Society Awakened Woman (UPDATED 2026)].
Kara’s slender index finger tapped directly against the glowing number one entry on the list.
[Rule 1: Radiate untouchable confidence.
Never explain yourself to service staff.
If someone questions your presence, act as though their entire bloodline owes you money.]
Evelyn stared at the glowing pink screen.
She stared at the cartoon kittens dancing on the phone case.
She stared at the ridiculous forum advice and then she looked up at Silas’s strikingly gorgeous, purple-eyed face looking back at her with unshakeable sincerity.
Her jaw clenched so hard a vein visibly throbbed against her left temple.
Her fingers twitched at her sides, her chest heaving beneath her oversized hoodie as she fought the overwhelming violent urge to jump forward and punch her square in the jaw.
’I am going to kill him,’ Evelyn thought, her soul screaming in agony.
"You..." Evelyn choked out, her face flushing red with a mixture of embarrassment and rage.
"You got your behavior... from a Threaddit thread?!"
Kara snickered softly as she reached out with her gloved hand, playfully tapping Evelyn’s burning cheek with her fingertips.
"You have to admit, Ev," Kara murmured, her purple eyes sparkling with mischief.
"Your face looks exceptionally cute when you’re about to pop a blood vessel."
"Fuck you, Silas!" Evelyn spat, swatting her hand away with a ferocious scowl.
DING!
The elevator chime chimed softly as the digital display overhead flashed [Floor 86: Imperial Wing].
The heavy gilded doors slid open silently, revealing a private, carpeted foyer that led directly into a breathtaking multi-thousand-square-foot luxury suite.
The Imperial Suite of the Skybli Hotel looked less like a hotel room and more like a private palace floating above the city.
Floor-to-ceiling panoramic windows lined the entire northern and eastern perimeter of the suite, offering an unobstructed, god-tier view of the sprawling Valoria City skyline at night.

Below them, the gleaming spires of the Upper Ward glittered with thousands of lights, the crisscrossing mag-train lines traced glowing pathways across the city, and the mana-arrays of the commercial districts pulsed with light that shone against the deep indigo of the evening sky.

The interior was outfitted with plush cream-colored leather furnishings, a fully stocked bar made of polished dark mahogany, intricate runic light fixtures that hummed with soothing spiritual frequencies, and a colossal king-sized bed elevated on a low marble dais in the master chamber.
Kara stepped out of her black heels the moment they crossed the threshold, leaving the shoes neatly by the entryway.
"Haah...
Finally..."
She walked across the thick, cloud-soft white rug, rolling her shoulders as she casually tossed her wide-brimmed black sunhat onto the nearest leather armchair.
Her long raven-black hair spilled freely over her shoulders, framing her pale face in dark striking waves.
She walked over to the massive sectional sofa facing the skyline, sitting down with a comfortable, sprawling sigh and crossing her legs.
"Not bad," Kara commented, glancing around the massive suite with an approving nod.
"The City Lord’s people definitely know how to build luxury and you’ve got good taste in rooms, Evelyn."
Evelyn kicked the heavy suite door shut, locking the deadbolts with a sharp flick of her mana before walking over to the bar.
She pulled a fresh slim cigarette from her cargo pocket, stuck it between her lips, and reached for her lighter.
"Don’t get comfortable yet," Evelyn rasped, lighting the tip and exhaling a thin stream of gray smoke toward the high ceiling’s ventilation array.
"We’re here on a schedule.
We need to get this account set up, validated, and seeded as soon as possible."
"Alright, boss," Kara smiled, leaning back against the leather cushions.
"How are we doing this?
You mentioned LordTube earlier I think, but I don’t exactly have a highlight reel of combat footage ready to upload."
Evelyn walked over, leaning against the back of the sofa with her arms crossed.
"LordTube is for long-form raid archives, official guild declarations, and battle breakdowns," Evelyn explained, pulling her own sleek black smartphone from her pocket.
"That’s where Lords go when they want to broadcast a full-scale siege or monetize their territory wars.
For establishing a fresh, mysterious persona who operates primarily on the surface?
You use Lordgram."
Kara tilted her head slightly.
"Lordgram?"
"It’s the primary image-and-short-text platform for the global awakened community," Evelyn said, tapping her screen to pull up the application interface.
"Lords, high-ranking mercenaries, Guild recruiters, and their fanbases use it to track daily status updates, aesthetic snapshots, and territory milestones...
It’s significantly faster to build engagement there, and it doesn’t require a dedicated broadcasting crew.
We post three photos of Kara White, seed the algorithm with verified tags, and let the internet do the rest of the heavy lifting."
Kara raised an eyebrow, looking very skeptical.
"What if people think it’s fake?" Kara asked, resting her chin on her hand.
"The internet on Earth isn’t stupid.
What if they assume these are just AI-generated composite renders, or some high-tier marketing firm using deep-fake alchemical filters to launch a new virtual model?"
Evelyn snorted loudly, looking down at Kara like she had just asked if the sun was hot.
"Do you live under a literal boulder, Silas?" Evelyn deadpanned, rolling her eyes.
"Ever since the Great Convergence, the World Lord Association implemented the Global Authenticity Protocols...
Every single image uploaded to Lordgram is automatically scanned by a watermark in a way.

If an image contains even a fraction of a percent of digital alteration, generative synthesis, or illusion magic, the system tags it with a bright red ’Unverified Composite’ warning and buries the post...
Everything that goes through a verified profile is legally recognized as pure physical reality."
She tapped her phone against her palm with a sharp smirk playing on her lips.
"And for extra insurance," Evelyn added, "once your account goes live, I’m going to use my official Lord Sky verified profile to follow you and drop a comment on your first post."
Kara’s purple eyes widened slightly.
"You’re going to use the Lord Sky handle?
Won’t that blow our cover?"

"Lord Sky has over two hundred million followers, but the profile only follows forty-two people worldwide... all of them top-tier solo Lords, guild masters, or legendary recluses," Evelyn explained with a vicious grin.

"If Lord Sky suddenly follows a mysterious one-armed purple-eyed nineteen-year-old girl who lives in Valoria City with zero guild affiliation, the algorithm is going to lose its mind and the traffic will explode within seconds."
"I like the way your little brain works," Kara chuckled.
"Alright.
Set it up."
Evelyn sat down on the leather sofa beside her, pulling out the pastel-pink kitten phone.
With practiced lightning-fast thumb movements, Evelyn navigated through the encrypted registry protocols.
She bypassed the standard civilian verification queues using the Black-Pass credentials Jax had forged in the underworld, rapidly generating the core account.
[Profile Created: @LordVespera_Official]
[Handle: Vespie022_]
[Bio: "Just the Lord of Blessed Land"]
"Hold still," Evelyn instructed, holding the pink phone up in front of Kara’s face.
"Let’s get the primary profile picture first...
Don’t do that weird squinty model thing you were doing earlier.
Just look at the lens naturally."
Kara sat up straight, turning her head slightly toward the soft golden glow of the city lights streaming through the floor-to-ceiling windows.
She didn’t force a stiff smile... she simply relaxed her features, letting a knowing enigmatic curve touch her lips as her luminous purple eyes met the camera’s optical sensor.
CLICK!
The high-definition mana-camera captured the image in stunning crystal-clear detail.

The warm ambient light from the city illuminated the porcelain texture of her pale skin, the delicate angles of her cheekbones, and the vibrant mesmerizing violet depths of her irises, contrasting magnificently against the deep shadows of her raven-black hair.
Evelyn stared at the captured photo on the screen for a long quiet second, her breath catching slightly in her throat before she aggressively cleared her throat and tapped the ’Set as Avatar’ button.
’He’s way too good at this,’ Evelyn cursed internally. ’It’s genuinely irritating how photogenic this asshole is...’
If she had his confidence, she would feel so much better when she took pictures.
"Now, we need three distinct lifestyle shots for the initial posts," Evelyn commanded, standing up and gesturing toward the panoramic window.
"Get over there.
Lean against the glass.
Look out over the skyline like you’re contemplating whether you want to buy the city or burn it down..."
"What a weird thing to say."
"Just do it fucker!"
Kara stood up, walking barefoot across the plush rug to the massive glass pane.

She turned her body in profile, resting her single right hand lightly against the transparent surface, her dark hair cascading over her bare elegant collarbones as she gazed out over the glittering spires of Valoria City at night.
The black silk dress clung perfectly to her back, the pinned left sleeve adding an aura of dangerous tragic mystery to the breathtaking composition.
CLICK!
"Good," Evelyn muttered, checking the framing.
"Now, turn around.
Sit on the edge of the low marble table near the bar...
Cross your legs, rest your chin on your knuckles, and look directly down the barrel of the camera.
Give me that arrogant, ’I could cleave you in half with a butter knife’ look you gave me during the war."
Kara laughed, moving to the marble table.

She sat gracefully on the polished stone, crossing her long legs and leaning forward, her purple eyes narrowing into a sharp confident gaze that radiated the undeniable authority of the Lord of Blessed Land.
CLICK!
"Last one," Evelyn said, walking over to the plush velvet armchair where the black designer sunhat was resting.
"Put the hat back on, but tilt it up with your thumb so only your right eye is visible.
Keep it casual, like you were just interrupted while having tea."
’I think this could fit Evelyn...’ Silas thought, she could honestly be a good photographer.
Kara picked up the wide-brimmed hat, settling it over her dark locks and lifting the brim with her single silk-gloved thumb, offering the camera a lazy charming smirk.
CLICK!
Evelyn sat back down on the sofa, rapidly cropping the images and attaching the appropriate metadata tags.
Based on Kara’s actual demeanor when she wasn’t locked in combat... she was relaxed, slightly sarcastic and confident too...
Evelyn drafted three short and perfectly understated captions.
’Heh, did he think I was going to do it properly?
I’ll sabotage him a bit too!
Who doesn’t add captions to their pictures.’
"Done," Evelyn declared, hitting the glowing blue [PUBLISH BATCH] button.
A soft chime resonated from the pink phone as the three high-resolution images synced with the global Lordgram servers, officially establishing Kara White’s digital existence in the modern world.

Evelyn immediately switched to her personal black phone, opened her verified Lord Sky account, and tapped the bright blue [FOLLOW] button on Kara’s profile before dropping a single ambiguous comment on the third photo:
[@LordSky_Official: Where are your captions? 🤣🤣🤣]
"There," Evelyn said, tossing the pink phone back onto Kara’s lap as she collapsed back against the sofa cushions, rubbing her tired eyes.
"I’ll drop an official announcement link on my LordTube community tab in about an hour once the algorithm indexes the tags but the foundation is set.
We can pack up and head back to the Sovereign Realm whenever you’re ready."
Kara caught the pink phone, sliding it onto the low table beside her.
She didn’t reach for her disguise ring, nor did she make a move toward the door.
Instead, she remained seated on the plush cushions, her purple eyes gazing out over the glittering city lights stretching across the horizon.
"Let’s stay here for a little bit," Kara said softly, her voice carrying along gently.
"There’s no rush.
The territory is secure, the girls is running their drills, and it’s peaceful up here."
Evelyn blinked, turning her head to look at her.
She didn’t argue, simply letting out a quiet breath as she leaned her head back against the sofa.
"Fine by me.
The silence is nice for once."
Kara smiled.
She turned her body toward Evelyn, extending her single silk-gloved right hand over the space between them.
A soft brilliant pulse of azure mana illuminated her palm.

When the light faded, Kara was holding a tall, pristine crystal cup filled with three generous scoops of rich, marbled mint-chocolate-chip and dark-cocoa gelato, topped with a delicate silver spoon and a drizzle of sweet alchemical honey.
Cold mist drifted lazily from the frozen dessert, filling the immediate air with the rich refreshing scent of pure peppermint and roasted cacao.
Kara held the cup out toward Evelyn, offering a warm, genuine smile.
"Here," Kara said.
"I passed by that high-end creamery on the corner of the commercial plaza on my way over here.
I remembered you looked a little down earlier, so I figured I’d pick it up for you."

chapters.title: Chapter 416: An Unexpected Visitor [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Evelyn completely froze.
She stared at the crystal cup.
’Huh?’
She stared at the specific, marbled swirl of mint-chocolate and dark cocoa and then she looked up at Kara’s face, her dark eyes wide with shock.
’Mint chocolate chip... with dark cocoa honey...’ Evelyn thought, her mind completely short-circuiting. ’That’s... that’s my exact comfort order. I haven’t ordered that since before the Lord War.’
A sudden warm prickle hit the back of her eyes.
It was deeply unnerving and touching too... Silas had noticed she was feeling depressed, but the specificity of the ice cream made her brow furrow in sudden suspicion.
"How... how the hell do you know this is my favorite?" Evelyn asked, her voice dropping to a low whisper.
Kara chuckled, leaning back comfortably. "Elm told me."
"I am going to murder that woman," Evelyn cursed immediately, though the ferocious scowl on her face lacked any real venom.
She looked at the ice cream, her fingers tightening slightly against her cargo pants as she looked back up at him.
"Wait... you actually knew I was feeling off? I thought I was acting completely normal today."

"Evelyn, you were acting like a walking storm cloud," Kara laughed softly, shaking her head. "You looked twice as exhausted as usual, you were dropping cigarette ash directly onto my Keep’s clean floorboards, and you spent the entire time calling me ’Graves’ and Silas while speaking with that rigid formal tone. I just assumed..."
Evelyn looked down at her lap, her messy dark bangs falling forward to hide her face. An embarrassed flush dusted her pale cheeks.
"I... I’m sorry," Evelyn muttered quietly, her voice uncharacteristically small. "I didn’t mean to be an asshole about the disguise. I was just... stressed."

"Don’t apologize," Kara replied warmly, nudging the crystal cup closer until Evelyn finally reached out and took it. "Seriously, Ev. Thank you for everything you’ve done for me. The ID, the Black-Pass registration, the accounts, the cover story... none of this would have been possible without your help."
Kara paused, tapping her chin with a playful smirk.
"Well... technically, I probably could have hired an expensive corporate fixer to forge a mediocre identity eventually, but—"
CLINK!
Evelyn aggressively scooped a massive chunk of mint gelato with the silver spoon, jammed it into her mouth, and glared daggers at Kara while chewing furiously.
"You’re a dumbass, Silas," Evelyn muffled through the mouthful of ice cream, her dark eyes blazing with that familiar combative spark.
Kara threw her head back and let out a ringing laugh that echoed through the luxury suite.
Evelyn swallowed the cold sweet dessert, feeling the rich sugar and mint immediately soothe the tight, exhausting knot that had been sitting in her chest.
She took another slow deliberate bite with her shoulders finally dropping their rigid tension.
"Don’t say anything stupid," Evelyn warned quietly, "and I promise I won’t light another cigarette in here."
Without waiting for permission, Evelyn shifted her weight on the sofa.
She leaned sideways, letting her entire body slump comfortably against Kara’s side.
’Hm? Strange...’ Silas thought.
She rested her head heavily against Kara’s silk-clad shoulder, curling her legs up onto the plush leather cushions as she continued to eat her ice cream in slow bites.
Inside the disguise, Silas didn’t move.
’Ah very weird... but it’s good enough for me.’
For several minutes, the only sound in the penthouse was the soft hum of the city below and the gentle scrape of the silver spoon against the crystal cup.

"I cut off my brother’s university stipend yesterday," Evelyn spoke suddenly, her voice muffled against Kara’s shoulder as she stared at the empty base of the cup. "The whole thing. Canceled the trust transfer, locked the secondary credit cards, and blocked his number from my personal line."
Kara kept her eyes on the distant horizon, listening quietly.
"He called me screaming," Evelyn continued, her voice trembling with a mixture of raw grief and bitter anger. "Told me I was a selfish, ungrateful person."
She swallowed hard, scraping the last bit of melted cocoa from the rim.
"Was... was that a bad choice?" Evelyn asked, the question sounding agonizingly fragile. "Did I just act like a piece of shit sister?"
Kara didn’t hesitate for a single second.

"Well coming for me, I think it’s okay... You’ve done a lot to keep your brother afloat, Evelyn," Kara said firmly, her voice leaving zero room for doubt. "You spent years in a freezing mobile fortress, fighting bloody sieges, breathing toxic miasma, and watching your closest friends bleed out in the dirt just so he could sit in an air-conditioned lecture hall and live like a prince and the moment the gravy train slows down, he treats you like an ATM instead of a human being."
Kara gently bumped her shoulder against Evelyn’s head.

"He doesn’t respect the blood you spilled to get here. Cutting him off wasn’t selfish... it was the healthiest choice you’ve made all year. It was your choice to make, and you were completely right. I would have done the same thing too but my Lia isn’t like that."
Evelyn sat motionless against her side. She let out a long shuddering exhale, feeling a suffocating weight lift off her ribs.
"Yeah..." Evelyn whispered softly, a genuinely relieved smile finally touching her lips. "Yeah. You’re right."
She set the empty crystal cup onto the table, pulling her knees tightly against her chest as she nestled deeper into Kara’s silk-clad side.
"Hey, Silas?"
"Yeah?"

"Is it okay if we just... stay like this for a little bit?" Evelyn asked, her eyelids suddenly growing impossibly heavy as the overwhelming exhaustion of the past month finally caught up to her. "I just want to rest my eyes for five minutes... Just five minutes..."
"Take your time, Ev," Kara replied softly. "I’m not going anywhere."
Within less than thirty seconds, the rhythmic rise and fall of Evelyn’s breathing deepened.
Her body went completely slack, her face resting peacefully against Kara’s shoulder as she went fast asleep.
Silas sat perfectly still, looking down at the messy dark bun resting against his arm.

’Haah...’ Silas sighed warmly to himself with a soft smile playing on his lips. ’Even though she’s technically older than me, she really can be pretty damn cute when she isn’t screaming or blowing smoke in my face.’
He let her rest, keeping his posture steady so as not to disturb her sleep.
With his free right hand, Kara picked up the pastel-pink smartphone from the table, intending to check the local time.
The moment the screen illuminated, however, the device violently vibrated in his grip.
BZZZZ-BZZZZ-BZZZZ-BZZZZ!
A continuous blinding cascade of bright neon-blue push notifications began flooding the display at a rate so rapid the screen’s refresh rate was visibly struggling to keep up.
[Lordgram Alert: @LordSky_Official commented on your post!]
[Lordgram Alert: Your profile is currently trending #1 in the World!]
[Lordgram Alert: You have gained 500,000 new followers!]
[Lordgram Alert: You have gained 1,200,000 new followers!]
[Lordgram Alert: Your post has reached Global Explore!]
Kara’s purple eyes widened in absolute shock.
’What the fuck?!’ Silas thought, nearly dropping the pink phone.
She frantically tapped the application icon, bringing up the main profile interface.
In the span of less than twenty minutes... the exact amount of time he had spent eating ice cream and talking with Evelyn, the profile had completely exploded.
[Profile: @LordVespera_Official]
[Followers: 2,418,902]
[Following: 1]
[Total Post Likes: 6,850,000+]
The three photos Evelyn had taken were sitting at the very top of the global trending page.

Because Lord Sky... a legendary Lord had actively followed and commented on the account, the entire internet had descended upon the profile like a swarm of ravenous locusts especially since they had been looking for it.𝒻𝑟𝘦𝘦𝘸ℯ𝒷𝑛𝘰𝓋ℯ𝘭.𝘤𝘰𝘮
Kara rubbed her temples with her single hand, letting out a stunned disbelieving breath.
"It can’t be this easy, can it?" Kara muttered under her breath. "Two million followers in twenty minutes just from three pictures and a comment?"
Curious, she tapped on the comment section of the third photo... the one where she was tilting the wide-brimmed sunhat with a smirk.
The comments were flying past at hundreds of messages per second. Kara scrolled through the top-ranked replies.
[@Aegis_Guild_Official: Lord Vespera! Welcome to Lordgram and thank you for blessing us with your divine beauty]
[@Nightfall_Sniper: That missing arm isn’t a disability, look at the shoulder balance... Lord Vespera is truly beautiful.]
[@LordSky_FanClub_Alpha: SKY FOLLOWED LORD VESPERA?! SKY COMMENTED ON A POST?! LORD VESPERA, YOU LOOK SO BEAUTIFUL!]
[@Valoria_HighSociety_Daily: Lord Vespera, welcome to Lordgram! If you would like to appear on our Interview, please answer your DMs! We’re waiting!
[@SimpLord_99: Step on me, my Queen. I will literally surrender my starter territory to you right now.]
Kara stared at the screen with a satisfied smirk spreading across her face as she locked the phone.
’Well...’ Silas thought cheerfully. ’Social media really isn’t that bad after all. The clout is magnificent.’
KNOCK! KNOCK! KNOCK!
A firm sophisticated three-stroke knock echoed loudly against the heavy reinforced oak door of the Suite.
Kara’s smirk faded instantly into sharp awareness.
She looked down at Evelyn, who was still fast asleep, completely dead to the world against her side.
Moving with agonizing care and precision, Kara gently slid her arm out from under Evelyn’s head.

She reached for one of the plush velvet sofa cushions, carefully sliding it beneath Evelyn’s cheek before lifting the sleeping girl’s legs onto the sofa and draping a warm cashmere throw blanket over her shoulders.
She picked up the empty crystal ice cream cup and set it neatly on the low bar counter.

’Room service already?’ Kara thought, walking silently across the thick rug toward the foyer. ’I didn’t order anything yet, but Evelyn might have requested complimentary champagne when she checked in. Good timing, honestly. I could go for a snack...’
Kara reached the heavy double doors.

She smoothed the front of her black silk dress with her single right hand, cleared her throat to ensure her vocal frequency remained in the cool, feminine register, and pulled the heavy brass handle inward.
"Room service, I—"
The words died instantly in her throat.
Kara’s breath completely caught, her purple eyes locking into a dead paralyzed stare.
Standing in the brightly lit, carpeted hallway directly outside the suite wasn’t a hotel waiter carrying a silver tray.
Standing there, perfectly framed by the gilded archway, was Elora Verinda.
The former Campus Belle of Valoria Academy and the daughter of the City Lord looked utterly breathtaking.
Her cascading, pale-blonde hair fell in pristine shimmering waves over a tailored, royal-blue mana-silk blazer that bore the silver crest of the Verinda High Council.
Her sharp aristocratic features were completely composed, and her piercing, icy-blue eyes met Kara’s gaze with unyielding focus.
Elora blinked once, her gaze sweeping smoothly over Kara’s wide-brimmed sunhat, the pinned-up left sleeve, and the striking, ethereal beauty of the woman standing in front of her.
A small, flawless, highly aristocratic smile bloomed across Elora’s lips.

"Lord Vespera..." Elora spoke, her voice smooth and chillingly confident as she offered a slight formal nod of her head. "...or should I say, Miss Kara White. It is a profound honor to finally meet you in person."
Silas felt every single muscle in his body rigidly lock up.
’How the hell did she find this room so fast?!’
Elora’s icy blue eyes sparkled with deep, calculated ambition as she gestured gracefully toward the private express elevators behind her.

"My father’s security network flagged your registration the moment your Black-Pass cleared the lobby terminal," Elora continued smoothly, her smile widening by a fraction of a millimeter. "I took the liberty of clearing the penthouse restaurant on the top floor. Would you do me the honor of joining me for dinner downstairs, Miss White? We have a great deal of business to discuss regarding your future in Valoria City."
