Her body went completely slack, her face resting peacefully against Kara’s shoulder as she went fast asleep.
Silas sat perfectly still, looking down at the messy dark bun resting against his arm.

’Haah...’ Silas sighed warmly to himself with a soft smile playing on his lips. ’Even though she’s technically older than me, she really can be pretty damn cute when she isn’t screaming or blowing smoke in my face.’
He let her rest, keeping his posture steady so as not to disturb her sleep.
With his free right hand, Kara picked up the pastel-pink smartphone from the table, intending to check the local time.
The moment the screen illuminated, however, the device violently vibrated in his grip.
BZZZZ-BZZZZ-BZZZZ-BZZZZ!
A continuous blinding cascade of bright neon-blue push notifications began flooding the display at a rate so rapid the screen’s refresh rate was visibly struggling to keep up.
[Lordgram Alert: @LordSky_Official commented on your post!]
[Lordgram Alert: Your profile is currently trending #1 in the World!]
[Lordgram Alert: You have gained 500,000 new followers!]
[Lordgram Alert: You have gained 1,200,000 new followers!]
[Lordgram Alert: Your post has reached Global Explore!]
Kara’s purple eyes widened in absolute shock.
’What the fuck?!’ Silas thought, nearly dropping the pink phone.
She frantically tapped the application icon, bringing up the main profile interface.
In the span of less than twenty minutes... the exact amount of time he had spent eating ice cream and talking with Evelyn, the profile had completely exploded.
[Profile: @LordVespera_Official]
[Followers: 2,418,902]
[Following: 1]
[Total Post Likes: 6,850,000+]
The three photos Evelyn had taken were sitting at the very top of the global trending page.

Because Lord Sky... a legendary Lord had actively followed and commented on the account, the entire internet had descended upon the profile like a swarm of ravenous locusts especially since they had been looking for it.𝒻𝑟𝘦𝘦𝘸ℯ𝒷𝑛𝘰𝓋ℯ𝘭.𝘤𝘰𝘮
Kara rubbed her temples with her single hand, letting out a stunned disbelieving breath.
"It can’t be this easy, can it?" Kara muttered under her breath.
"Two million followers in twenty minutes just from three pictures and a comment?"
Curious, she tapped on the comment section of the third photo... the one where she was tilting the wide-brimmed sunhat with a smirk.
The comments were flying past at hundreds of messages per second.
Kara scrolled through the top-ranked replies.
[@Aegis_Guild_Official: Lord Vespera!
Welcome to Lordgram and thank you for blessing us with your divine beauty]
[@Nightfall_Sniper: That missing arm isn’t a disability, look at the shoulder balance...
Lord Vespera is truly beautiful.]
[@LordSky_FanClub_Alpha: SKY FOLLOWED LORD VESPERA?!
SKY COMMENTED ON A POST?!
LORD VESPERA, YOU LOOK SO BEAUTIFUL!]
[@Valoria_HighSociety_Daily: Lord Vespera, welcome to Lordgram!
If you would like to appear on our Interview, please answer your DMs!
We’re waiting!
[@SimpLord_99: Step on me, my Queen.
I will literally surrender my starter territory to you right now.]
Kara stared at the screen with a satisfied smirk spreading across her face as she locked the phone.
’Well...’ Silas thought cheerfully. ’Social media really isn’t that bad after all.
The clout is magnificent.’
KNOCK!
KNOCK!
KNOCK!
A firm sophisticated three-stroke knock echoed loudly against the heavy reinforced oak door of the Suite.
Kara’s smirk faded instantly into sharp awareness.
She looked down at Evelyn, who was still fast asleep, completely dead to the world against her side.
Moving with agonizing care and precision, Kara gently slid her arm out from under Evelyn’s head.

She reached for one of the plush velvet sofa cushions, carefully sliding it beneath Evelyn’s cheek before lifting the sleeping girl’s legs onto the sofa and draping a warm cashmere throw blanket over her shoulders.
She picked up the empty crystal ice cream cup and set it neatly on the low bar counter.

’Room service already?’ Kara thought, walking silently across the thick rug toward the foyer. ’I didn’t order anything yet, but Evelyn might have requested complimentary champagne when she checked in.
Good timing, honestly.
I could go for a snack...’
Kara reached the heavy double doors.

She smoothed the front of her black silk dress with her single right hand, cleared her throat to ensure her vocal frequency remained in the cool, feminine register, and pulled the heavy brass handle inward.
"Room service, I—"
The words died instantly in her throat.
Kara’s breath completely caught, her purple eyes locking into a dead paralyzed stare.
Standing in the brightly lit, carpeted hallway directly outside the suite wasn’t a hotel waiter carrying a silver tray.
Standing there, perfectly framed by the gilded archway, was Elora Verinda.
The former Campus Belle of Valoria Academy and the daughter of the City Lord looked utterly breathtaking.
Her cascading, pale-blonde hair fell in pristine shimmering waves over a tailored, royal-blue mana-silk blazer that bore the silver crest of the Verinda High Council.
Her sharp aristocratic features were completely composed, and her piercing, icy-blue eyes met Kara’s gaze with unyielding focus.
Elora blinked once, her gaze sweeping smoothly over Kara’s wide-brimmed sunhat, the pinned-up left sleeve, and the striking, ethereal beauty of the woman standing in front of her.
A small, flawless, highly aristocratic smile bloomed across Elora’s lips.
"Lord Vespera..." Elora spoke, her voice smooth and chillingly confident as she offered a slight formal nod of her head.
"...or should I say, Miss Kara White.
It is a profound honor to finally meet you in person."
Silas felt every single muscle in his body rigidly lock up.
’How the hell did she find this room so fast?!’
Elora’s icy blue eyes sparkled with deep, calculated ambition as she gestured gracefully toward the private express elevators behind her.
"My father’s security network flagged your registration the moment your Black-Pass cleared the lobby terminal," Elora continued smoothly, her smile widening by a fraction of a millimeter.
"I took the liberty of clearing the penthouse restaurant on the top floor.
Would you do me the honor of joining me for dinner downstairs, Miss White?
We have a great deal of business to discuss regarding your future in Valoria City."

chapters.title: Chapter 417: Revenge
paragraphs: The carpeted hallway of Floor Eighty-Six was entirely silent, save for the low rhythmic hum of the hotel’s mana-stabilizers embedded within the gilded baseboards.
For several suffocating seconds, neither woman spoke.
Kara White stood framed within the entrance of the Presidential Suite, her single, silk-gloved right hand resting casually against the heavy brass doorframe.
The brim of her designer sunhat cast a dark, elegant shadow over her eyes, but beneath that velvet rim, her luminous purple irises were locked in a razor-sharp stare.
Opposite her, Elora Verinda maintained her immaculate posture.

The Campus Belle of Valoria Academy was clad in a sharp, tailored navy blazer bearing the silver sun-crest of House Verinda, her cascading pale-blonde hair catching the warm illumination of the crystal wall sconces.
Her sharp features were arranged in a mask of effortless composure, her icy-blue eyes analyzing every square millimeter of the woman standing before her.
Internally, however, Elora’s brilliant mind was working at frantic speed.
’It’s just as I felt down in the lobby...’ Elora thought, her analytical gaze tracing the graceful unhurried posture of Kara’s silhouette.
When she saw that someone had effortlessly shattered the Newbie Leaderboards, Elora’s instincts had pointed toward the impossible.
For a brief, fleeting moment back in the Academy armory, she had entertained the absurd theory that Silas Grave might have somehow been the Lord of Blessed Land.
But standing here now, mere inches from the person before her, that theory completely dissolved.
The spiritual pressure radiating from Kara White was fundamentally distinct.
It was vast and chillingly powerful, carrying the undeniable weight of an apex entity who moved through the mortal world like a predator indulging a stroll.
Silas possessed a sharp aura but this woman felt like an mountain of authority.

’There is no connection,’ Elora concluded, a flicker of cold certainty settling in her chest. ’Silas Graves is just a talented anomaly who pulled a decent Blue Core in the slums. This woman... this is the true Lord of Blessed Land.’
Elora’s objective was clear.
To secure House Verinda’s supremacy in the upcoming inter-realm territorial redistribution, she needed the undisputed Number One of the Newbie bracket under her family’s banner.
The global consensus had already pinned the Lord of Blessed Land as the bearer of a legendary Gold Core.
In the political hierarchy of Earth, one did not pry too deeply into the origins of a Gold Core sovereign without courting immediate annihilation.
Elora knew her limits.

She had calculated the raw mana power of the woman standing in the doorway; if Kara chose to unleash a full-power offensive spell right here, she wouldn’t just breach the room... she could collapse the entire eighty-six-story superstructure of the Skybli Hotel into rubble before the city’s defense arrays could even activate.
Elora could not hope to match that destructive output.
Worse still, intelligence reports from the registry confirmed that Kara White possessed zero living relatives, zero institutional debts, and zero corporate attachments.
Elora had no leverage, no pressure points, and no familial vulnerabilities to exploit. She was standing at a total diplomatic dead end, relying solely on charm and high-society prestige.
Elora smiled, her tone dripping with polished diplomatic warmth.
"I took the liberty of having the executive chef prepare a private banquet. We could discuss the parameters of a mutual protection treaty over din—"
"I’m not interested."
The refusal was instantaneous and entirely devoid of hesitation.
Elora’s aristocratic smile completely froze. A subtle twitch rippled across her porcelain brow, genuine surprise cracking her practiced facade.

"Miss White... surely you must understand the practical necessity of regional integration," Elora pressed, stepping forward slightly, her icy eyes narrowing. "Valoria City is governed by established treaties... The Verinda family controls seventy percent of the spatial transport nodes in this hemisphere. An independent territory, no matter how powerful its initial deployment, cannot survive long-term supply embargoes from the global trade hubs. An alliance guarantees you immediate access to our refining syndicates, diplomatic immunity from corporate inquiries, and—"
"I only came here to enjoy myself," Kara interrupted.
Kara adjusted the brim of her hat with her single right hand, looking down at the City Lord’s daughter with a bored curve of her lips.

"I have zero time to deal with political theater. I am not allying myself with your family, I have no intention of signing with any guild, and I am certainly not interested in handing over operational control of my territory or negotiating resource quotas. Furthermore, I have no desire to sign a pact that provides me with zero tangible benefits at the end of the day."
Kara didn’t wait for a rebuttal.
She took a half-step back and swung the heavy, solid-oak suite door shut with effortless force.
SLAM!
The sheer concussive pressure of the door snapping shut generated a sudden gust of displaced air that whipped Elora’s pale-blonde hair wildly across her face.
Elora stood frozen in the empty corridor, her eyelashes fluttering as the breeze settled.
’Oh?’
A cold dangerous silence filled the hallway.
Elora took a slow, calculated step backward, smoothing a stray strand of hair behind her ear.
She was not a brute so she was not going to pound on the wood or make an undignified scene in a five-star hotel.
Her icy blue eyes drifted toward the narrow seam beneath the door frame.
Through the brief gap before the door had closed, Elora’s sharp vision had caught a glimpse of the interior.
She had seen the living quarters and more specifically, she had spotted the dark-haired girl in the oversized gray hoodie currently fast asleep on the plush velvet sofa.
Elora had never seen that face in any official high-society register.
The girl looked like a low-tier commoner, yet she was resting comfortably inside the private sanctuary of a Gold Core Lord.

’A close companion...’ Elora reasoned, her jaw clenching tightly as a ruthless scheme formed in her mind. ’She dropped her guard around that girl. If I can catch that commoner off-guard on the surface, I can secure the leverage I need to force a proper audience with the Lord of Blessed Land.’
Elora turned on her designer heels, her blue coat swirling around her legs as her eyes hardened into frost.
’And if that girl proves useless as a bargaining chip...’ Elora thought with chilling finality, ’I will simply eliminate her to clear the board.’
With silent measured strides, the City Lord’s daughter marched toward the express elevators and vanished from the floor.
Inside the Suite, Kara let out a long groan, leaning her back against the solid oak door.

"Unbelievable," Silas muttered within the disguise, Kara’s purple eyes rolling toward the ceiling. "I put on a dress for thirty minutes and the local nobles are already trying to draft me into their political nonsense. Does that girl ever take a day off from being an arrogant pain in the ass?"
He pushed himself off the door and walked across the thick cream-colored rug toward the central lounge area.
Evelyn was still completely out cold on the sofa, her face buried into the soft velvet cushion, breathing in deep steady rhythms.
Kara walked over to the communications terminal embedded in the mahogany bar. He pressed the glowing gold service rune, bringing up the hotel’s internal audio-link.
PING!
"Grand Skybli Guest Concierge, how may we cater to your desires this afternoon, Miss White?" a polite deferential voice chimed through the speaker.

"I need room service," Kara answered smoothly. "Send up a selection of your premier pastries and cakes. In fact, bring up one of every single specialty dessert the patisserie has prepared today. And bring a bottle of your finest vintage red wine... something from the southern valley vineyards."
"An exceptional choice, Miss. Our pastry team will prepare the grand tasting carousel immediately. Is there anything else the suite requires?"
Kara paused, glancing over her shoulder at Evelyn’s defenseless, sleeping face.
A sudden, devious smirk curled across her lips.
"Yes, actually," Kara added, tapping her knuckles against the mahogany counter. "Could you have the delivery staff include a standard black permanent marker on the tray?"
A brief, confused pause echoed from the other end of the line.
"A... permanent marker, Ma’am?"
"Did I stutter?" Kara asked with lighthearted, aristocratic sharpness. "A fine-tip black marker. Put it on the cart."
"Right away, Miss White! The cart will arrive within ten minutes."
The terminal clicked off.
Kara walked back to the sectional sofa, sitting down quietly on the edge of the leather cushion opposite Evelyn.
She rested her elbow on her knee, leaning her chin against her single silk-gloved palm as she watched the former Lord of the Unmovable Wall sleep.
Without the permanent scowl, the sneer, and the constant cloud of gray tobacco smoke obscuring her features, Evelyn looked remarkably young.
’You really need to learn how to relax, Ev,’ Silas thought warmly with a soft smile touching his lips.
Ten minutes later, a discreet knock sounded at the double doors.
Kara stood up, stepped into the foyer, and unlocked the latch.
A team of two immaculate waitstaff pushed a multi-tiered, gold-plated rolling cart into the suite, bowing deeply with utter reverence.
The cart was a masterpiece.

Arranged across polished silver tiers were nearly a dozen distinct, exquisitely decorated cakes and pastries... a towering dark-chocolate mousse cake glazed with edible gold leaf, a delicate white-lotus sponge topped with crystalized berries, a multi-layered matcha opera cake, a plate of warm caramelized alchemical honey tarts, and a chilled crystal decanter filled with deep shimmering crimson wine alongside a pair of cut-glass goblets.
And resting neatly beside the wine goblets on a small silver saucer was a brand-new, fine-tip black permanent marker.
"Your tasting selection, Miss," the lead waiter murmured, bowing with his hand over his heart. "The cellar master selected the Age-320 Crimson Reserve for your vintage. Shall we serve the wine?"
"No, that will be all," Kara replied smoothly, picking up a generous gratuity chit from the console and handing it over. "Leave the cart. You may go."
"Thank you, Miss White. Enjoy your afternoon."
The staff bowed once more and backed out of the room, the heavy double doors locking securely behind them.
Kara walked over to the rolling cart, picking up a small silver fork and a plate holding a slice of the dark-chocolate mousse cake.
She brought a delicate piece to her lips, savoring the rich, velvety cocoa and the light crunch of the gold leaf.

"Damn..." Kara whispered in genuine delight with her purple eyes widening. "The people in the Upper Ward really know how to spend their credits... I might actually have to start coming here more often."
She poured herself a glass of the vintage red wine, taking a slow appreciative sip of the rich, oaky liquid to wash down the chocolate.
’This is all in Ev’s tab... I’m not paying shit.’
Setting the glass down on the cart, Kara picked up the black permanent marker.
She popped the plastic cap off with a soft click.
A wicked grin spread across Kara’s face as she crept silently across the plush rug toward the sofa.
’This,’ Silas thought with immense internal glee, ’is payback for you smoking in my Keep, calling me an idiot, and acting like an old hag.’
Moving with the precision of a swordsman, Kara leaned over the sleeping girl.

With light, practiced strokes of the fine-tip marker, she carefully drew a thick, magnificent, perfectly symmetrical handlebar mustache right across Evelyn’s upper lip, curling the tips upward toward her cheekbones in elaborate loops.
To complete the masterpiece, she added a tiny dashing French goatee right on the center of Evelyn’s chin.
Kara pulled back, admiring the handiwork.
Evelyn, with her messy dark hair, pale skin, and oversized gray hoodie, now looked like a nineteenth-century French duelist who had passed out in an alleyway.
Kara had to bite her own silk-gloved thumb to keep from bursting into a fit of hysterical laughter.
She recapped the marker, tossed it into her Lord Inventory, and sat down comfortably at the rolling cart to systematically demolish the remaining eleven slices of cake.
Nearly an hour passed in blissful sugary tranquility.
On the sofa, Evelyn’s eyelashes fluttered.
She let out a long, groggy groan, her brow furrowing as the bright afternoon light filtering through the panoramic windows stung her retinas.
Her throat felt dry, her limbs felt heavy, and a dull lingering ache pulsed behind her temples.
She slowly pushed herself upright on the leather cushions, rubbing her eyes with the sleeves of her hoodie as a jaw-cracking yawn tore from her throat.
"Ugh... my head..." Evelyn rasped..
She blinked rapidly, her vision clearing as she looked across the room.
Sitting at the empty rolling cart, Kara was just setting down an empty dessert plate.
The silver platters that had once held twelve intricate cakes were completely bare, wiped clean with terrifying efficiency.
"Ahhhh~"
A soft undignified feminine burp escaped Kara’s lips. She patted her flat stomach with her single right hand, letting out a contented sigh as she downed the final sip of her wine goblet.
"Well, well," Kara smiled, turning her head with an amused twinkle in her purple eyes. "Look who finally decided to rejoin the land of the living. It’s about time you woke up, Sleeping Beauty."

The silver platters that had once held twelve intricate cakes were completely bare, wiped clean with terrifying efficiency.
"Ahhhh~"
A soft undignified feminine burp escaped Kara’s lips.
She patted her flat stomach with her single right hand, letting out a contented sigh as she downed the final sip of her wine goblet.
"Well, well," Kara smiled, turning her head with an amused twinkle in her purple eyes.
"Look who finally decided to rejoin the land of the living.
It’s about time you woke up, Sleeping Beauty."

chapters.title: Chapter 418: The Saintess of The Argent Flame
paragraphs: Evelyn’s face instantly burned with a sudden flare of self-conscious embarrassment.

’I actually passed out on him?!’ Evelyn thought in horror, frantically checking the state of her oversized hoodie to make sure she hadn’t drooled everywhere. ’Gods damn it, I told him I was just going to rest for five minutes! Why am I so comfortable around this asshole?!’
Before she could stammer out a defensive insult, Kara tapped the console, summoning the hotel staff to clear the empty cart.
Two waiters quickly arrived, bowed respectfully, cleared the platters, and vanished back into the hallway.
Kara stood up, smoothing down the fabric of her black silk dress and picking up her wide-brimmed sunhat from the armchair.
"Are you ready to head out?" Kara asked, settling the hat over her dark hair. "We’ve got a long checklist waiting for us back in the basin."
Evelyn cleared her throat, shaking off the lingering grogginess as she swung her boots onto the floor.
"Yeah. Let’s get out of here before your ego gets any bigger."
As they stepped toward the private foyer, Kara naturally reached out with her single silk-gloved right hand and took Evelyn’s hand in hers.
Evelyn’s entire body tensed for a second.
Her heart did an erratic uncoordinated flip against her ribs at the sudden, warm contact.
She looked down at their intertwined fingers, feeling another wave of ridiculous adolescent shyness wash over her face.
She pulled her gray hood lower over her head to hide her cheeks.
"Why are you being so clingy...?" She muttered but she notably didn’t pull her hand away.
They took Express Elevator Seven back down to the ground floor.
When the gilded doors slid open into the bustling grand atrium, Evelyn immediately noticed a bizarre shift in the room’s atmosphere and it even remained there when they returned the Key Card.
As they walked across the pristine obsidian floor tiles toward the exit, nearly every single guest and high-society scion in the lobby turned to stare at them.
People lowered their champagne glasses in mid-sip.

Awakened mercenaries stopped their conversations dead in their tracks with their jaws slacking. Several noble heiresses sitting in the velvet lounge covered their mouths with their silk fans, their eyes wide with poorly suppressed shock.
Evelyn frowned deeply, her grip tightening on Kara’s hand.
’Why the hell is everyone looking at me like I have two heads?!’ Evelyn thought, feeling deeply self-conscious. ’I know my hoodie is a little worn out, but this is a Hotel, not a royal coronation!’
"Kara..." Evelyn whispered out of the side of her mouth, feeling the burning heat of fifty pairs of eyes on her back. "Why is everyone staring at us? Is my hood crooked?"
Kara didn’t miss a beat.
She kept her chin high, walking with the majestic untouchable poise of an empress as she guided Evelyn toward the revolving glass doors.

"Don’t mind their gazes, Ev," Kara replied in a calm comforting tone, suppressing the violent urge to cackle. "They’re just intimidated by your undeniable charisma. You look absolutely striking today."
"You’re full of shit," Evelyn grunted, but the compliment still caused a pleased warmth to bloom in her chest.
They stepped through the revolving doors, leaving the crystal-paned luxury of the Skybli Hotel behind and emerging into the crisp night air of Valoria City.𝘧𝑟𝑒𝑒𝘸𝘦𝘣𝑛𝑜𝘷𝑒𝓁.𝘤𝘰𝓂
The streetlights were beginning to flicker to life, casting long golden pools of light across the polished sidewalks.
They walked a block down the bustling sidewalk until they reached a relatively secluded plaza lined with manicured pine trees and stone benches.
Kara stopped, releasing Evelyn’s hand and stepping back with an easy radiant smile.
"Alright, this is where we split up," Kara said, adjusting the brim of her hat. "I need to drop off in a private alley, and you need to head back to your place. I’ll see you next time, Ev."
Evelyn stuffed her hands into the front pocket of her hoodie, nodding with a rare gentle expression on her face.
"Yeah. Don’t take forever."
"See ya, Ev."
With a fluid graceful pivot, Kara turned and jogged lightly down the pedestrian walkway, her black silk dress fluttering in the night breeze before disappearing around a distant corner.
Evelyn stood on the sidewalk, watching the empty corner where he had vanished.
A soft warm sigh escaped her lips.
’He really is... strangely nice,’ Evelyn thought, a tender uncharacteristic softness settling deep within her chest.

Despite all his teasing, his arrogance, and his endless banter, Silas had bought her favorite dessert, listened to her vent about her family without an ounce of judgment, and validated every hard decision she had made.
In a world full of corporate vultures and cutthroat warlords, having someone like him in her corner felt like a miracle.
She reached into her cargo pocket, pulling out a slim cigarette and sticking it between her lips.
She snapped her fingers, igniting a small spark of mana to light the tip.
FWOOSH!
Evelyn took a long, relaxing drag of smoke, feeling entirely at peace with the world.
As she exhaled the thin gray cloud, she happened to glance to her left.
Parked along the curb was a pristine polished black luxury sedan, its dark-tinted passenger window acting as a flawless, high-definition mirror.
Evelyn casually looked at her reflection to fix a stray lock of hair beneath her hood.
She froze.
The cigarette fell completely out of her mouth, tumbling onto the concrete pavement.

Staring back at her from the tinted glass was her own pale face... prominently adorned with a pitch-black impeccably drawn handlebar mustache and a sharp French goatee, framing her lips in cartoonish perfection.
The silence lasted for three full agonizing seconds.
And then, an apocalyptic wave of crimson fury erupted across Evelyn’s entire face, burning so hot it practically threatened to ignite her hair.
The realization hit her like an orbital strike.
The receptionist in the lobby... The elevator mirrors... The guests staring and whispering... Silas holding her hand and telling her she looked ’striking’...
"She drew on my face while I was asleep..." Evelyn whispered in horrified, trembling disbelief.
She clutched her head with both hands, took a massive chest-heaving breath of the night air, and let out a blood-curdling shriek of rage that echoed across the entire commercial district.
"KARAAAAAAAAAAAAAA—!!!"
HUM!
A brilliant column of golden spatial displacement mana flashed within the bedroom of Evelyn’s suite in the Living Quarters of the Blessed Land.
Silas materialized in the center of the room.
He was no longer clad in alchemical silk, designer sunhats, or black heels.

He had completely shed the Kara White persona in a secluded alleyway three blocks from the hotel, returning to his true, tall broad-shouldered form, dressed in his comfortable black combat robes and heavy leather boots.
He rolled his shoulders, taking a deep, satisfying breath of the territory’s crisp, mana-dense air.
’Man...’ Silas thought, stretching his arms over his head until his joints popped. ’It’s really exhausting wearing a dress. My respect for women just increased tenfold.’
He glanced around the bedroom.

Evelyn hadn’t returned to the Sovereign Realm yet... she was probably still in the human world desperately scrubbing her upper lip with alchemical soap and swearing vengeance upon his entire bloodline.
Chuckling to himself, Silas pushed open the heavy wooden door of the suite, descended the polished stone stairs, and walked out into the sunlit courtyard of the Blessed Land.
The evening sky was painted in deep purples and oranges, casting long shadows across the stone tiles.
The territory was thriving.
Over by the main gates, The Shieldmaidens were running phalanx drills against the reinforced walls, their steel shields clashing with thunderous, rhythmic precision.
Silas turned toward the eastern industrial district of his domain, his boots crunching against the stone tiles as he approached a colossal smoke-belching stone structure.
The Warlord Foundry.
He pushed open the heavy reinforced iron-banded doors.
A blistering wave of intense dry heat immediately slammed into his face, carrying the metallic scent of molten steel, crushed coals, and glowing embers.
Inside, the foundry was a whirlwind of violent activity.
Standing in the center of the massive room, surrounded by six glowing blast furnaces, was Thora as usual but the dwarven blacksmith wasn’t working alone anymore.

Scattered across the various anvils and quenching troughs were nearly a dozen female dwarven artisans... all transferred recruits from Evelyn’s old Unmovable Wall garrison who possessed metallurgical traits.
They were swinging heavy iron sledges in perfect synchronization, shaping glowing ingots of tempered steel with astonishing inhuman speed.

"Keep the bellows pumping, you lazy whelps!" Thora roared, her voice booming over the sound of clashing metal as she brought her massive war-hammer down on an anvil. "That mythril alloy needs to reach fifteen hundred degrees before we quench it in drake oil!"
CLANG! CLANG! CLANG!
As Silas stepped into the light of the main forge, Thora paused mid-swing.
She wiped a thick streak of black soot from her brow with the back of her leather gauntlet, her sharp dwarven eyes lighting up with delight the moment she saw him.

"Well, well! Look who finally decided to grace the working class with his presence!" Thora grinned broadly, setting her heavy hammer onto the anvil and rolling her thick, muscular shoulders. "What brings you down to the hot zone, Lord Graves? Did you come down here to finally sweep me off my feet and knock me up, or are you just inspecting the armory?"
The surrounding dwarven smiths paused their hammering, letting out a chorus of boisterous crude chuckles that echoed off the stone rafters.
Silas shook his head with a warm, dry laugh, crossing his arms over his chest.
"Not today, Thora," Silas replied smoothly. "Though I appreciate the offer. I came here because I brought you a little something from the human world."
Thora’s bushy eyebrows shot straight up. "A gift? For me?"
Silas focused his intent, opening his Lord Inventory with a mental command.
He swiped his hand through the air, and a massive glowing blue spatial rift tore open directly above the center of the foundry floor.
BOOM!

A colossal, eight-ton reinforced titanium industrial container dropped heavily from the ether, slamming into the stone floor with a bone-jarring impact that sent a shockwave of dust and sparks rippling across the room.
The solid stone foundation groaned beneath the staggering weight of the delivery.
Thora’s jaw dropped.
She scrambled over the anvils, rushing to the front of the massive container.
PSHHHHHHH!
Thora popped the heavy pneumatic latches with a sharp hiss of venting air and heaved the thick metal lid open.
The moment the interior was exposed, the entire foundry was illuminated by a mesmerizing, deep-purple and silver luminescence.

Resting inside the container were dozens of massive, raw ingots of Astral Void-Titanium Alloy... the eight-ton shipment harvested from a fallen meteor in the Deep Wastes that Silas had secured at the Obsidian Sanhedrin auction for seventy million credits.
Thora leaned deep into the container, her eyes wide as dinner plates.
She reached out with her bare hand, running her calloused fingers along the cold rippling surface of the meteor metal, before leaning in and taking a deep sniff of the raw alloy.
"By the ancient forge-fathers..." Thora breathed out, her voice trembling with genuine sacred reverence. "Kendra! Bring me my primary etching chisels and the diamond-tipped tester! Now!"
One of her dwarven assistants hurriedly ran over, handing Thora a set of runic diagnostic tools.
Thora aggressively struck the diamond chisel against the edge of an ingot, channeling her innate dwarven mana to read the metal’s internal crystal matrix.
PING!
The metal rang with a clear, bell-like resonance that vibrated through the teeth of every person in the room.

"It’s pure..." Thora gasped, looking up at Silas with awe shining in her eyes. "There isn’t a single fracture in the crystalline weave. This is high-density Void-Titanium from a deep-space impact! With this much alloy, I can forge full suits of void-plate for the entire frontline, reinforce the gate ballistae mechanisms, and line the Keep’s inner sanctum with kinetic absorption plating! It’s perfection, my Lord!"
Silas walked over, reaching down and giving the sturdy dwarven blacksmith an affectionate, reassuring pat on the top of her braided head.
"I’m glad you like it," Silas smiled warmly. "Put it to good use. We’re expanding the perimeter soon, and I need our gear to be indestructible."
"Aye, aye, Captain!" Thora beamed, leaning happily into the headpat like a proud hound. "I’ll have the first batch of void-shields forged before the next sunrise!"
Silas nodded, turning on his heel to head back toward the foundry doors. "Keep up the good work, Thora. I’ll let you get back to the forge."
"Wait! Lord Graves, hold on a second!"
Thora dropped her tools, scrambling past the massive container and sprinting toward a heavy wooden bookshelf bolted to the back wall of the foundry office.
She stood on her tiptoes, frantically rummaging through a stack of leather-bound tomes and dusty historical archives she had recovered from the Blessed Land’s library quarters.
With a triumphant shout, she pulled out a massive gold-embossed grimoire bound in weathered dragon-hide.
Thora jogged back over to Silas, cradling the heavy book in her thick arms.
"Before you go," Thora said, her tone suddenly turning remarkably serious and earnest, "you need to look at this."
Silas paused, his blue eyes narrowing slightly in curiosity. "What is it?"
Thora flipped the heavy parchment pages with practiced familiarity until she reached a specific illuminated Chapter near the end of the tome.
She held the book up, pointing her thick calloused index finger directly at a magnificent full-page hand-painted illustration.
Silas leaned forward, his gaze locking onto the artwork.
Depicted on the aged parchment was a breathtaking ethereal woman.

She possessed long shimmering platinum-blonde hair that cascaded around her shoulders like spun silver, and piercing golden-amber eyes but it wasn’t her striking beauty that commanded attention... it was her tragic heart-wrenching expression.
Tears of pure liquid blood were painted streaking down her pale porcelain cheeks.
Her slender hands were tightly clasped together against her chest in a desperate eternal posture of prayer, her body wrapped in heavy, glowing silver chains of radiant divine fire.
Above the illustration, ancient golden calligraphy spelled out her full title:
[Aurelia El Mimonte: The Saintess of the Argent Flame]
Thora tapped the illustration firmly with her knuckle, looking up into Silas’s eyes with conviction.

"I found her record buried in the deep archives," Thora explained, her voice dropping into a reverent whisper. "She was the supreme high-priestess of the Argent Sanctum before she was betrayed. She wields the pure flame of absolute purification... she can cleanse any curse, burn through abyssal miasma, and mend broken cores."
Thora looked at her Lord, a pleading hopeful smile touching her soot-stained lips.
"My Lord... when you step up to the Summoning Portal for your next Hero invocation... why don’t you call upon her? Bring the Saintess home to the Blessed Land."
[Author’s Note:]
These days, we’re maintaining a steady pace.... How about we do a Mass release?
😔 All I need is motivation which could perhaps mean a castle or two.
That aside, Thanks for reading so far and I’m actually surprised we went so long without summoning another person... Morwenna was summoned in Chapter 79 I think, damn. New Hero incoming!

chapters.title: Chapter 419: Time In The Barracks [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The heat radiating from the massive crucibles of the Warlord Foundry pushed against Silas’s face in sweltering waves, but his focus remained anchored on the yellowed parchment held within Thora’s calloused leather-clad hands.
Silas leaned forward, his blue eyes narrowing as he scrutinized the intricate, illuminated artwork.
"Aurelia El Mimonte..." Silas murmured, testing the foreign syllables upon his tongue. "I’ve never heard of that name in any of the Valoria Academy archives or the modern codexes."
He glanced up from the ancient dragon-hide tome, meeting the dwarven blacksmith’s earnest gaze.

"How did the betrayal even happen in the first place, Thora? If she was the supreme high-priestess of an entire celestial sanctum, how did pantheons manage to bypass her wards and drag her into the ether or however?"
Thora let out a dry exasperated breath, shaking her braided head as she tapped the edge of the parchment with a stubby, soot-stained finger.

"The book doesn’t give many details on the exact collapse, Lord Graves," Thora explained in a serious voice. "The records from that era are fragmented but from what little text survived the burning of the Great Archives or whatever the book calls it, it says an inner sect elder poisoned the sacred flame with corruption, breaking the temple’s dimensional barrier from the inside. When the deities breached the sanctum, she chose to seal herself within the Argent Flame rather than let her divine spark be harvested for her core."
Silas nodded slowly, running a hand through his dark hair as he absorbed the historical weight behind the illustration.

"I can try," Silas replied with an easy self-deprecating shrug with a smirk playing on his lips. "Though it’s not like I have a personalized menu when I activate the Archway. Summoning isn’t an exact science, Thora..."
At least, that was what Silas genuinely believed based on his limited experience.

When he had stepped before the Archway to summon Eluned, he hadn’t known her true name or divine lineage... his core had simply burned with the desperate intent to summon an entity with absolute, overwhelming power to stabilize his barren territory.

When he had summoned Morwenna, his thoughts had been locked on finding a master-class frontline blade-wielder capable of carving through abyssal horrors, having zero clue that the spatial currents would drag a foul-mouthed alcohol-drinking Astral Dread Queen through the rift.
In truth, Silas had originally entertained thoughts of calling upon an elemental Ice Goddess to balance out the searing draconic heat and abyssal flames already dominating his ranks.
But looking down at the tragic, tear-stained face of the Saintess captured in the illuminated manuscript, a strange undeniable tug resonated deep within his Gold Core.
"I’ll keep her in mind when I want to summon," Silas assured her, offering Thora a warm, confident smile. "If her soul is adrift in the ether, maybe our domain’s frequency can pull her through."
"That’s all I ask, Lord Silas," Thora beamed, carefully closing the heavy dragon-hide tome and hugging it against her leather apron.
Silas turned his attention toward the rest of the foundry floor, where the dozen female dwarven smiths had paused their hammering, watching him with eager soot-smeared expressions.

"Listen up, everyone!" Silas projected his voice across the cavernous stone hall, his tone commanding yet deeply appreciative. "You’re doing incredible work here... The weapons, the plating, the infrastructure you’re building with this new Void-Titanium is going to be one of the backbones of our entire domain. Keep your rhythm steady, don’t rush the quenching cycles, and make sure every single blade that leaves these anvils is sharp enough to cut through a dragon’s hide. When we expand the perimeter, your craftsmanship will keep our sisters alive!"
The dwarven smiths erupted into a unified, thunderous cheer, pumping their heavy iron sledges into the air with triumphant roars.
"FOR THE LORD!"
"WE’LL FORGE WALLS THAT CAN’T BE BROKEN!"
Thora laughed loudly at the uproar, stepping forward and boldly blowing Silas an exaggerated kiss across the glowing coals.
"You heard the boss!" Thora barked at her crew, turning back to the anvils with renewed vigor. "Back to the bellows, ladies! We’ve got eight tons of meteor metal to shape before the stars shift!"

Silas chuckled warmly, shaking his head as he stepped through the heavy reinforced iron doors of the foundry, leaving the blistering heat behind and emerging back into the crisp courtyard of the Blessed Land.

’It’s good to see Thora finally having competent hands to share the load,’ Silas thought, taking a deep, refreshing breath of the open air. ’Now that the metal is delivered, I’ve got some free time before going to summon..’
His thoughts naturally drifted toward the military sector.

’I should head over to the barracks and see how the integrated recruits are settling in. After everything they went through on the battlefield during the war, I need to make sure their morale isn’t slipping...’
Silas turned his boots toward the southern sector of the compound, strolling leisurely across the paved walkways that separated the industrial zone from the residential fortress.
The Barracks were soon in view and they looked as beautiful as ever, Silas was really proud of himself.
As Silas pushed open the heavy double oak doors of the barracks, the loud clash of ringing steel and high-pitched female cheers instantly washed over his senses.
"Drive her back! Don’t give her the center line!"
"Watch the footwork! She’s baiting your low sweep!"
Inside the central training ring, a furious high-speed sparring match was underway.
Lupina... the silver-haired wolf-kin demi-human was a whirlwind of gray motion.
Her silver wolf ears were pinned flat against her skull in razor-sharp focus, her bushy silver tail flicking aggressively behind her leather-clad hips for balance.

She held a runic training spear with an iron-tight, white-knuckled grip, shifting her weight fluidly between all fours and an upright stance as she aggressively pressed the attack against Hieck, one of the other recruits.
CLANG!

Lupina vaulted forward in a sudden burst of raw, beast-kin agility, crossing spears with Hieck with such ferocious force that a visible shockwave of displaced air rippled across the sand, kicking up a fine dust cloud.
The surrounding crowd of female recruits and seasoned warriors leaned over the wooden railing, screaming encouragement and banging their practice bucklers.
Suddenly, one of the recruits near the entrance caught sight of the tall, dark-robed figure standing in the doorway.
"Lord Graves is here!" the girl shouted in surprise.
The entire sparring ring instantly froze.
The cheering died down in a heartbeat as dozens of heads snapped toward the entrance.
Hieick’s guard faltered slightly with her stance widening as she reflexively prepared to snap to attention.

’If I can impress Lord Graves right now...’ Hieck thought, her heart racing as she adjusted her grip. ’If he sees that my defensive spear-arts can hold off an agile beast-kin Hero, he might assign me to the primary vanguard!’
Lupina, however, did not drop her guard.
The moment the silver-haired wolf-girl saw Silas standing by the doorway, waving casually with a relaxed friendly smile, a violent desperate spark flared within her golden-amber eyes.
Her whole life in the military had been an agonizing cycle of feeling weak, feeling inadequate, and being knocked into the dirt while others carried the glory.
The crushing humiliation of being flattened during the Lord war and even before that... it all burned inside her chest like liquid fire.
She didn’t want Silas’s polite pity. Lupina wanted to prove, beyond a shadow of a doubt, that she wasn’t some terrified useless stray who needed protection.
"HAAAAAH!"
With a savage beast-like roar, Lupina’s speed multiplied tenfold.
A burst of feral wind mana exploded from beneath her leather boots. In the blink of an eye, she closed the distance, her spear blurring into a silver arc of terrifying momentum.
Hieck’s eyes went wide as the veteran desperately tried to bring her buckler up to parry, but the attack was moving at a different conceptual tier.
CRACK!
Lupina’s spear struck the center of Hieck’s defense, cleanly cleaving the reinforced wooden practice shield in half and shattering the outer clasp of her chest armor.
The sheer concussive force lifted Hieck off her feet, sending the warrior flying backward five yards through the air before she landed with a heavy sliding thud in the soft sand.
Lupina stood over the fallen warrior with her chest heaving as the tip of her practice spear pointed steadily at Hieck’s throat.
"You’re weak," Lupina growled out with sharp ferocity. "Your center of gravity dropped the moment your focus split. On a real battlefield, that mistake costs your life."
A tense breathless silence gripped the arena for two full seconds before the surrounding recruits exploded into wild, roaring applause.
"Incredible speed!"
"Did you see that low-angle burst?!"
Lupina lowered her spear, exhaling a hot, panting breath but as the adrenaline faded and the reality of the room set in, her sharp ears suddenly drooped.
She turned her head, looking over at Silas.
Her bushy silver tail, which had been standing tall and aggressive moments ago, completely fell, tucking itself nervously against the back of her thighs.
Her wolf ears folded backward in sudden agonizing anxiety.

’Did I overdo it...?’ Lupina panicked internally, her fingers trembling against the spear shaft. ’Did I look like a bloodthirsty monster in front of the Lord? Is he going to scold me for breaking armor during a friendly drill?!’
Silas didn’t scold her.
He walked across the sand, clapping his hands together with a genuine approving smile.

"That was fantastic, Lupina," Silas commended warmly, his blue eyes meeting hers with sincerity. "Your acceleration from a dead stop is unbelievable, and your target acquisition didn’t waver for a millisecond. That was high-level combat instincts..."
Lupina’s breath hitched.
The moment the words registered in her ears, her folded wolf ears violently popped back upright.
Her tucked silver tail shot straight up, wagging left and right with frantic, joyful, blur-like speed that betrayed every ounce of her tough-warrior persona.
"T-Thank you, my Lord!" Lupina stammered, her pale face flushing a violent shade of red.

Overwhelmed by the praise and utterly terrified of letting her tail-wagging betray how desperately happy she was, she shoved her practice spear into a nearby weapon rack, spun on her heel, and bolted toward the back of the barracks at full sprint.
Silas chuckled softly, watching her run off before turning toward the observation deck near the ring.
Standing together by the weapon racks were Gunnhild and Brida.
The two senior commanders were overseeing the training rotation, but Silas’s attention was immediately drawn to Gunnhild.
The woman was completely soaking wet, droplets of water glistening along her exposed collarbones and damp blonde hair, her skin radiating a fragrant cloud of lavender-infused alchemical soap.
Silas blinked with an amused smirk tugging at his lips.
’Did she really spend the last two hours scrubbing herself raw in the bathhouse just because I made a joke about monster blood...?’ Silas thought, he appreciated the effort though.
Silas stepped up to the railing, addressing the gathered crowd of recruits and veteran soldiers.
"At ease, everyone," Silas called out. "You’ve all been working hard today. How are the new quarters treating you? How are you settling into the Blessed Land?"
A chorus of enthusiastic eager voices echoed back from the ranks.
"It’s incredible, Lord Graves!"
"The food from Lady Kaelia is unbelievable... we actually have mana-rich meat for every single meal!"
"The barracks beds are so soft, and the defensive arrays make us feel completely safe!"
"We love it here, my Lord!"
Silas nodded, feeling a deep sense of satisfaction warm his chest.
"I’m glad to hear that. You’re all part of this territory now. Train hard, eat well, and know that you will always have my full support."
As the crowd dispersed to resume their physical conditioning drills, Silas’s gaze naturally drifted toward the far corner of the sparring hall.
Sitting alone on a wooden bench, away from the loud chatter of the main group, was Morrighan.
The Demonic Caster Hero was a striking imposing presence as usual.
Her tall, slender frame was clad in the mythril-reinforced uniform of the Blessed Land recruits, her long flowing crimson hair contrasting starkly against her pale, ashen skin.

Two polished, obsidian-black horns curved gracefully from her temples, and her long spade-tipped demon tail was wrapped quietly around the legs of the wooden bench as her molten-gold eyes were fixed quietly on her own hands.
Silas’s brow furrowed with a twinge of guilt.

’Damn...’ Silas thought. ’I remember Sky mentioning how much discrimination she faced in their old army because of her demonic aura. I should have made sure she was fully integrated with the others. I shouldn’t have let her isolate herself—’
Before Silas could finish his thought, one of the younger human recruits walked past the bench and playfully bumped Morrighan with her hip.
"Hey, look, Mori!" the girl giggled, pointing toward Silas. "Lord Graves is staring right at you! Go say hi!"

chapters.title: Chapter 420: The Lord That Gives Gifts [End Of - ]
paragraphs: Morrighan’s pale ashen face instantly flushed with a deep vibrant crimson blush.
"I... I have repeatedly told you not to shorten my name, Rebecca," Morrighan murmured in her deep echoing contralto voice, though there was zero hostility in her tone.
She stood up from the bench, smoothing down the leather folds of her cloak, and walked methodically across the sand toward Silas.
"Greetings, Lord Graves," Morrighan spoke with dignified solemn grace, placing a slender, claw-tipped hand over her chest and bowing her head.
"Hey, Morrighan," Silas replied gently, stepping closer so their conversation remained private. "How has your life been here in the Blessed Land? Are you settling in comfortably?"
Morrighan’s golden eyes flickered with a mixture of awe and lingering disbelief.
Her long, spade-tipped tail began to sway in a soft involuntary rhythmic tremor behind her cloak.

"It has been... extraordinary, my Lord," Morrighan whispered. "To be candid, it feels deeply surreal. In my past service, soldiers avoided my quarters and feared the demonic corruption in my bloodline but here... the other women are endlessly friendly. They invite me to share meals, they ask for my stabilization enchantments during drills, and none of them flinch when my aura flares."
Her gaze drifted briefly toward the far courtyard where the World-Tree was visible through the high windows.

"Even Lady Eluned... a divine Goddess of pure unblemished life who by all rights should despise a creature of abyssal birth... she smiled at me in the gardens yesterday and offered me a spiritual blossom. It made my heart feel... remarkably warm. I did not believe such a place could exist."
Silas smiled softly, stepping forward and gently placing his warm hand atop her head, right between the curve of her obsidian horns.

"I gave you my word during the war, didn’t I?" Silas murmured, giving her a reassuring headpat. "In the Blessed Land, your bloodline doesn’t define your worth... your loyalty and your actions do. You belong here, Morrighan. Keep working hard, and never feel like you have to hide yourself."
Morrighan froze under his touch with her breath catching in her throat.
Her molten-gold eyes shimmered with a delicate fragile brilliance, her spade-tipped tail curling tightly in pure devotion.
"I will not fail you, Lord Silas," she whispered fiercely. "My life is yours."
Silas gave her one final nod before turning on his heel and walking over toward Gunnhild and Brida.
"Gunnhild, Brida," Silas addressed them with a commanding smile. "How are the overall tactical drills progressing?"
Gunnhild snapped to attention, her wet blonde hair swaying as she offered a crisp, flawless military salute.

"Reporting, Lord Graves!" Gunnhild spoke with rigid professionalism, trying desperately to sound like a hardened veteran rather than a girl who had just spent two hours crying in a tub. "The baseline phalanx formations are fully integrated... The transferred troops have successfully adapted to our shield-locking rhythms. Within forty-eight hours, the vanguard will be ready to execute a full-scale sweep of the eastern basin crags to harvest UP and secure fresh meat."

"Good," Silas nodded thoughtfully. "The scouts reported unusual beast movements near the outer sides. I want to know what new species are migrating into the basin and where they’re originating from. Keep the scouts sharp."
He paused, stepping closer to Gunnhild with a teasing glint in his blue eyes. He leaned down slightly, taking a deliberate exaggerated sniff of the air around her shoulder.
"And for the record, Gunnhild," Silas murmured with a quiet laugh, "you smell very nice right now. The lavender suits you."
Gunnhild’s entire body went completely rigid.
A volcanic blush exploded across her face, turning her cheeks, her ears, and her exposed collarbones a brilliant radiant red.
Her legs wobbled beneath her armor as she took three frantic uncoordinated steps backward, covering her face with both hands.
"T-THANK YOU, MY LORD!" Gunnhild squeaked in a pitch nobody had ever heard her reach before, bowing so frantically she nearly pitched forward into the ground.
Silas laughed out loud, thoroughly enjoying her flustered reaction before turning his attention toward Brida.
"Now then... Brida, assemble the other girls," Silas instructed, his voice shifting into a rich, generous cadence. "I brought back something from the Obsidian Sanhedrin that belongs in your hands."
Brida stepped forward, her tall, heavily muscled frame radiating disciplined curiosity. "A shipment for the front line, Lord Silas?"
"Something like that," Silas smiled.
With a flick of his mental intent, Silas accessed his Lord Inventory and called upon the high-tier equipment.
THUD!

A colossal frost-covered storage container materialized in the center of the sand ring, venting a cloud of frigid crystalline mist that dropped the temperature of the room by twenty degrees in an instant.
Silas reached out, popping the runic latches and heaving the lid open.
Resting inside, bathed in a brilliant, mesmerizing azure luminescence, was the complete 70-Piece Frost-Drake Battalion Armor & Spear Set.
The armory set gleamed with peerless craftsmanship.
Each buckler was forged from the iridescent, lightweight carapace of a high-tier Frost-Drake, carved with intricate kinetic-deflection glyphs that pulsed with elemental mana.
Beside them were rows of matching Runic Short-Spears, their tips forged from frost-hardened alloy that radiated an aura of pure, piercing chill.
Brida looked down into the container, her breath completely catching in her throat.

"M-my Lord..." Brida whispered, her voice trembling with awe as her calloused hands hovered over the glowing frost-plate. "This... this is masterwork Drake-Carapace armor. The kinetic deflection runes alone cost a fortune... This entire set could outfit our entire primary assault phalanx!"
It was a new addition to what they had now.

"It’s for you and the Shieldmaidens, Brida," Silas said warmly. "Distribute the seventy sets among the veteran girls and let the new recruits know that as they prove themselves in the upcoming eastern hunt, more sets will be commissioned for their ranks."
The surrounding recruits erupted into a deafening roar of sheer excitement, their eyes burning with intense motivation.
"Thank you, Lord Silas!" Brida shouted with loyalty. "We will paint these shields in the blood of your enemies!"
"Take one complete set down to the foundry first," Silas added. "I want Thora to reverse-engineer the whole thing so we can mass-produce similar defensive glyphs for our entire secondary garrison."
"Understood!" Brida saluted crisply.
With effortless physical strength, the towering warrior scooped up a complete armor-and-spear set, hoisting it under her arm.
She took two steps toward the exit, then suddenly paused.
’Huu... I can do that.’
Brida turned back around, took a long stride toward Silas, leaned down, and planted a firm affectionate kiss right on the center of his cheek.
SMACK!
The entire barracks went dead silent.
The female recruits, Gunnhild, and Morrighan all froze, their jaws dropping in shock as they stared at the woman.
’Did Brida just kiss the Lord in broad daylight?!’ the recruits screamed internally. ’Is she going to be executed for insubordination?!’
Silas didn’t strike her down.
Instead, he reached out with a lighthearted exasperated chuckle and playfully poked Brida right in the center of her forehead, pushing her back half a step.
"You’re getting pretty cheeky, Brida," Silas teased, shaking his head with an amused grin.
Brida let out a loud ringing laugh, completely unabashed by the scandalized stares of her subordinates.
"A good commander always claims her rewards, my Lord!" Brida grinned boldly, giving him a cheeky wink before turning on her heel and sprinting out of the barracks toward the foundry.
Silas waved goodbye to the remaining recruits, who bowed with enthusiastic sparkling eyes.
"Keep up the drills, everyone. I’ll be coming down to inspect your combat formations much more frequently."
"GOODNIGHT, LORD GRAVES!" the warriors chorused in unison.
Silas exited the barracks compound, stepping back into the cool evening breeze that swept across the central courtyard.
The sun had completely dipped beneath the horizon, bathing the Blessed Land in a magnificent twilight glow punctuated by the soft luminous blue pulses of the palisade’s warding runes.
He walked past the central plaza toward the base of the grand Keep.
On the manicured, stone-lined secondary training grounds adjacent to the Keep’s western wing, a lone figure was vigorously practicing her spellcasting.
"Ha!"
A sharp, determined feminine shout echoed across the empty courtyard.
Kadi... the sandy-haired Second Secretary of the Blessed Land was standing in the center of the training ring, clad in her tailored dark-brown administrative robes.
She swept her hands forward in a fluid, circular motion, channeling her innate earth-affinity mana.
RUMBLE!
A massive wave of fine golden desert sand surged upward from the soil beneath her boots, coalescing into dozens of razor-sharp crystalline spikes that hovered in the air.
With a sharp thrust of her palms, Kadi launched the spikes forward.
BOOM! BOOM! BOOM!
The sand-spikes slammed into a series of reinforced stone practice dummies, detonating upon impact with concussive force.
Before the dust could even settle, Kadi flexed her fingers, actively pulling the scattered grains back together and reforming them into a swirling protective barrier that orbited her body.
"Whew..." Kadi exhaled, wiping a drop of sweat from her brow with a satisfied grin. "Sand manipulation really is incredible when the density locks in..."
A sudden shift in mana in the air caught her attention.
Kadi turned her head, her amber eyes widening in pleasant surprise as she spotted Silas approaching the ring with his hands tucked casually into his black pockets.
"Lord Silas!" Kadi greeted, immediately dropping her spell and bowing respectfully with a bright radiant smile. "Welcome back to the training grounds."

"That was impressive control, Kadi," Silas smiled, walking up to the edge of the stone perimeter. "The reformation speed on those sand-spikes was practically instantaneous. You’ve made serious progress since the last time."
Kadi rubbed the back of her neck with an embarrassed flattered laugh.

"Thank you, my Lord," Kadi explained eagerly, her eyes shining with academic excitement. "Ever since you gave me that seed, the earth and sand in this basin feel completely responsive. It feels like the ground is an extension of my own circulatory system. It’s effortless to shape."
"That’s great to hear," Silas said, stepping into the ring. "Because I have something that’s going to take that control to a different dimension."
Kadi tilted her head in curiosity. "A new spell scroll?"
Silas smiled, calling upon his Lord Inventory.
A bright golden spatial circle manifested in his grasp, and with a soft hum of displacement magic, he withdrew a magnificent weapon.
The Scepter of the Dune-Sovereign.
The Tier-3 master staff was an awe-inspiring sight.
Carved from a solid branch of petrified desert gold, the shaft was inscribed with swirling shifting hieroglyphs of tectonic runes.
Resting atop the crown of the staff, suspended within a cage of golden claws, was a swirling, crackling orb of concentrated earth mana that radiated a deep vibration through the ground.
Silas held the scepter out toward her.
"For you, Kadi," Silas said warmly. "A gift from the Obsidian Sanhedrin... Take it and see how it feels in your hands."
Kadi stared at the golden artifact, her jaw parting in breathless disbelief.
Her heart hammered wildly against her ribs.
For a wild, fleeting second, the urge to throw decorum out the window, jump forward, and aggressively plant her lips onto Silas’s mouth nearly overpowered her common sense.
But she held herself back, taking a deep, trembling breath and offering a deep formal bow as she accepted the staff with both hands.
"M-my Lord..." Kadi stammered. "This... this is a huge gift! I... I will cherish this with my entire life! I will polish it every single night and carry it into every battle under your banner!"
"Don’t just polish it," Silas laughed softly. "Channel your mana through the core and let’s see what it can do."
Kadi closed her eyes, steadying her breathing. She tightened her grip on the petrified gold shaft, pouring her own earth mana directly into the swirling golden orb.
VUUUUUUM.
The ambient air in the courtyard instantly turned razor-sharp.
A deep tectonic vibration surged up through the soles of their boots. In a fraction of a second, a miniature violent whirlwind of golden sand erupted around the perimeter of the Keep.

The swirling grains moved with terrifying velocity as the friction left fine micro-scratches across the reinforced stone masonry that slowly knitted themselves shut under the territory’s self-repair arrays.
Kadi opened her eyes, gasping in awe as she willed the sandstorm to dissipate with a simple flick of her wrist.
"The mana conductivity is flawless..." Kadi breathed out, looking at Silas with sparkling eyes. "The casting cost is reduced by nearly sixty percent, and the tectonic range is massive!"
She paused, a sudden, ambitious glint flashing across her face.
"Lord Silas, I have an idea," Kadi said, stepping back slightly. "I want to test a long-range terrestrial transmutation spell using the scepter’s amplified power!"
Silas leaned forward, watching with genuine curiosity. "Show me."
Kadi took a wide, grounded stance, driving the base of the golden scepter firmly into the soil of the training ring.
"By the shifting sands of the deep basin," Kadi chanted with focused intensity, channeling a massive wave of earth mana into the earth, "Mudify!"
Meanwhile, on the northern pathway leading forward, Brida was sprinting toward the Warlord Foundry at high speed.
