chapters.title: Chapter 421: Threesome? [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Brida wasn’t running at her maximum combat velocity, but her long powerful strides still carried her across the paved stones with impressive momentum.
Under her arm, she securely held the crate containing the sample set of Frost-Drake armor.
’I need to deliver this to Thora immediately so she can start analyzing the runes before tomorrow’s dawn!’ Brida thought with urgent determination.
Just as she crossed the intersection near the western garden, her right boot came down hard against what should have been solid reinforced stone.
SQUELCH!
The ground beneath her foot instantly liquefied into a deep, churning pool of thick, viscous mud.
"Whoa—!"
Brida’s forward momentum was violently arrested as her leg sank knee-deep into the sludge.
The sudden uncoordinated deceleration caused her upper body to pitch forward, the heavy armor crate slipping from her grasp and shooting through the air like a launched projectile.
Before the precious drake-alloy could shatter against the ground—
SHING!
A brilliant cascade of starlight mana flared in mid-air.
Aeliana... the Archon of the Stars materialized in a graceful blur of midnight-blue silk, catching the heavy crate effortlessly against her chest before landing lightly on the dry grass nearby.
Brida looked down at the bubbling pit of mud, her face twisting into a furious, deadpan grimace.
"That fucking Kadi..." Brida cursed out loud, violently pulling her leg free from the suction with a wet shluck.
She channeled a quick burst of physical mana through her greaves, blasting the clinging mud particles away in a spray of dry dust.
She knew for a fact that Kadi’s sudden surge in casting power was the direct result of whatever gift Silas had just gifted her.
Being the Second Secretary certainly had its perks.
Brida walked over to Aeliana, taking the heavy crate back with an appreciative nod.
"Thanks for the catch, Aeliana."
She looked at the Royal Elven Arcanist, noticing the book tucked into the sash of Aeliana’s robes.
Brida’s lips curled into a wicked, teasing grin.

"Hey, Aeliana," Brida purred quietly, leaning in close. "How about you use your magic to make Kadi’s clothes vanish right now? I’ll let you use me as a full anatomical test subject for that new spellcasting thesis you’re writing for Lord Silas."
Aeliana’s porcelain elven face instantly turned a catastrophic burning shade of pink.
The pristine Archon of the Stars choked on her breath, her pointed ears twitching violently as she stammered in flustered panic.
"I—I... O-Okay..."
Brida laughed heartily, hoisting the crate onto her shoulder and continuing her sprint toward the foundry.
Back in the western training ring, Kadi threw her hands up with a triumphant victorious cackle.
"It worked!" Kadi cheered proudly, looking at the distant patch of ground. "The terrestrial transmutation carried over sixty yards through the stone foundation!"
Silas stood beside her, blinking.
"What worked, Kadi? Did you—"
Before Silas could finish his question, something happened.
POP!
A soft sharp chime of displaced elemental energy flashed around Kadi’s body.
In a fraction of a second, every single piece of fabric, leather, and silk constituting Kadi’s tailored administrative robes completely vanished from her skin.
Silas froze and Kadi froze as well.
A long awkward gust of evening wind swept through the empty courtyard, gently rustling Kadi’s sandy hair.
Kadi stood completely naked in the center of the training grounds.
Her fair skin, her slender waist, the soft curves of her hips, and her perky unblemished breasts were completely exposed to the open air and the twilight sky.
Kadi looked down at her own bare chest, then down at her bare feet, her brain processing the catastrophic wardrobe malfunction at glacial speed.
"AH!"

With a high-pitched squeak of sheer panic, Kadi frantically crossed her arms over her chest, pressing her forearms tightly against her breasts while twisting her thighs together to desperately cover herself with her single free hand.
’Why am I completely naked out here?!’ Kadi screamed internally, her face burning hotter than Thora’s blast furnaces.
She gritted her teeth, glancing up through her bangs to find Silas still standing mere feet away, his blue eyes locked onto her in a state of stunned paralyzed silence.
A sudden inappropriate tempting thought flared in Kadi’s mind.

’Wait...’ Kadi thought, her heart pounding violently against her ribs. ’He’s staring... He’s really staring at me. Should I just... loosen my hands? What if I let him see everything? If he gets enticed enough right now, he could literally pull me into the shadows of the Keep and claim me right here...’
Her fingers began to subtly loosen their grip over her chest—
CREEEAAAK!
The second-story window of Silas’s master quarters swung violently open.
Leaning out over the stone windowsill was Eluned.
The World-Tree Goddess’s flowing emerald hair billowed aggressively around her shoulders, her divine aura flaring with terrifying intensity.
Her vibrant green eyes were narrowed into a chilling, world-ending glare that could have cleaved a mountain range in half if it had been a physical offensive spell.
Kadi caught sight of the murderous divine stare and instantly flinched in pure terror.

Abandoning all thoughts of seducing her Lord on the grass, the naked secretary snatched the golden scepter from the ground, turned on her bare heels, and sprinted toward the residential quarters at supersonic speeds, leaving a trail of dust in her wake.
Silas stood alone in the training ring, letting out a long exhausted sigh as he rubbed the bridge of his nose.
’The girls in my Territory sure are beautiful...’
Up at the window, Eluned’s murderous glare instantly vanished, melting seamlessly into an impossibly sweet affectionate smile.
She leaned her chin onto her delicate hands, resting against the stone sill as her melodic voice drifted down through the courtyard.

"I heard you are giving out wonderful gifts today, Hubby~" Eluned purred sweetly, her emerald eyes practically sparkling with possessive delight. "Tell me... you have something special for me too, right?"
Silas looked up at the open stone window of his master quarters, catching the radiant expectant glimmer in Eluned’s emerald eyes.
"I’m coming up," Silas called out with a warm, resigned chuckle, shaking his head as he turned away from the empty training grounds.
He pushed through the side entrance of the grand Keep, the cool stone interior welcoming him back into the sanctum.
The air within the corridors hummed with mana, carrying the soothing floral fragrance drifting from the conservatory.
As Silas crossed the threshold into the lower galley kitchen, he immediately spotted a commanding silhouette standing near the polished granite counters.
Talira stood with her back partially turned, the dark magnificent span of her draconic wings resting smoothly against her shoulder blades.
Two polished, obsidian dragon horns swept gracefully back from her temples, and her thick scaled tail swayed in a slow, rhythmic arc behind her legs.
In her claw-tipped hand, she held a crystal pitcher, casually tilting it to pour a thick stream of glowing royal-purple spirit juice into a heavy tumbler.
She paused mid-pour, her golden reptilian slit-pupils flicking toward the entrance the exact second Silas’s boots touched the flagstones.
Setting the pitcher down with deliberate care, Talira turned her full frame toward him.
Her posture straightened into that of an elite draconic guardian, though the sharp edge of her expression softened into genuine warmth.
"Oh... Lord Silas," Talira greeted. "Welcome home to the Blessed Land properly this time. Your presence was sorely missed during the morning drills."
’I miss when she was shy...’
Talira couldn’t be shy after all they had spent all that time training with each other, she had gotten used to him.
Silas smiled, stepping closer and giving the dragon warrior an appreciative nod.
"It’s good to see you, Talira. Don’t worry, we’re going to get some proper sparring sessions in very soon. I haven’t forgotten about pushing your combat threshold."
A visible spark of fierce delight flared within Talira’s golden eyes. Her dark wings flared slightly at the promise of battle, her tail giving a sharp satisfied flick against the floor.
"I shall hold you to that, My Lord," she murmured, a breathtaking smile touching her lips before she raised her cup in a respectful toast.
Leaving the kitchen behind, Silas ascended the grand spiraling staircase of the Keep.
Each step brought him closer to the quiet upper sanctum, the soft murmur of familiar voices drifting from beneath the master doorframe.
Silas pushed the heavy reinforced oak door open, stepping inside.
The master quarters were bathed in the soft glow of the setting twilight. Sitting gracefully on the wide stone sill near the open window was Eluned.
The World-Tree Goddess’s emerald silk robes pooled like liquid moss around her bare feet, her silver-green hair tumbling over her delicate shoulders as she offered him a sweet adoring smile.
Across the room, sprawled lazily across the center of the massive fur-lined bed, was Morwenna.
The Pirate Queen had discarded her heavy boots, propping herself up against a mountain of plush pillows.
Her wild dark hair fell in messy waves across her face as she meticulously wiped down the glowing oceanic alloy of Tidebringer with a strip of fine oil-cloth.
The curved saber hummed quietly with her touch, the serpentine runes along the fuller flashing with a gentle blue heartbeat.
"Took you long enough to climb a few stairs, Captain," Morwenna drawled lazily without looking up from her blade, though the fond smirk tugging at her canines betrayed her rough tone.
"I was making sure the territory wasn’t burning down," Silas replied dryly, stepping into the center of the master chamber.
Eluned smoothly rose from the windowsill, gliding across the polished floorboards on a cushion of gentle breeze until she stopped mere inches from his chest.
She tilted her chin up, her luminous green eyes practically vibrating with shameless possessive anticipation.

"Well, Hubby?" Eluned purred softly, clasping her slender hands together against her chest. "From what my roots saw, The blacksmith received a mountain of meteor iron, the secretary received a golden staff, and even the shieldmaidens received entire crates of armor... What did my Lord bring back for his devoted Goddess?"
Silas chuckled, meeting her eager gaze. "I told you I wouldn’t leave you empty-handed."
Silas focused his intent, opening his Lord Inventory with a subtle mental command.
A brilliant, deep-azure flare of spatial light flashed across the palm of his right hand. The moment the rift parted, a staggering wave of primeval life-force violently flooded the master quarters.

The air grew impossibly pure and invigorating, the wood grain of the floorboards faintly sprouted tiny luminescent green moss buds, and the scent of wild untouched celestial forests washed over their senses.
Resting within Silas’s palm was The Tear of the Slumbering World.
The relic was an ethereal masterpiece of ancient nature craftsmanship.
Suspended from an intricate shimmering chain woven from petrified vines was a massive, tear-shaped celestial gemstone that pulsed with a deep ocean of concentrated emerald mana.
Within the core of the crystal microscopic nebulas of living spiritual sap swirled in eternal soothing currents.
It looked much better than before, was it because it was in Eluned’s vicinity

"I found this at the Obsidian Sanhedrin," Silas explained softly, holding the glowing pendant up between his fingers. "The moment I saw it, I knew it would look breathtaking around your neck. Not to mention... it carries an overwhelming reservoir of—"
"Nature magic..." Silas and Eluned spoke the words in unison.
Eluned’s emerald eyes went completely wide, shimmering with pure breathless adoration.
Her divine spark resonated so violently with the ancient relic that glowing floral glyphs manifested across the pale skin of her collarbones.
Silas smiled warmly, stepping behind her.
"Here... Let me help..."
He gently brushed her long silver-green locks over her shoulder, feeling the delicate shiver running through her frame as he fastened the petrified vine clasp securely around her slender neck.
The moment the teardrop crystal rested against the valley of her chest, an emerald shockwave rippled through the room.
Eluned spun around on the balls of her feet, her silk dress billowing as she ran her delicate fingers over the cool, pulsing gem.
"It is... perfection, Silas," Eluned breathed out, her eyes locking onto his with a gaze so hot and heavy it threatened to melt the stone beneath them.

She stepped forward, pressing her entire body flush against his chest, her arms wrapping tightly around his neck. "And now that your Goddess is properly adorned... we should resume where we were interrupted. It is time to start breeding again, Hubby~"
A deep, involuntary flush crept up Silas’s neck.
He looked down at the World-Tree spirit, letting out a half-strangled laugh. "Elu, seriously? Do you have to be completely obsessed with getting dicked down every single hour of the day?"
"It is a sacred duty!" Eluned declared proudly, not a shred of shame in her angelic voice.

She turned her head toward the bed, casting a provocative competitive glance toward the Pirate Queen. "In fact... Morwenna is already in the room. Why don’t we simply have a threesome right now? You can take both of your top Heroes together!"
Morwenna’s hand instantly paused mid-stroke across Tidebringer’s hilt.
The Pirate Queen lifted her head, her stormy gray eyes narrowing into razor-sharp daggers as she scoffed with aggressive disgust.

"Not a chance in the seven hells, plant-bitch," Morwenna snapped with a feral sneer, swinging her legs over the edge of the bed. "If I’m going to have sex with my Captain, I am doing it alone, unrestricted, and on my own terms. I want him focused entirely on me so he can properly break me into the mattress, not splitting his attention because some needy tree-spirit is whining for scraps."
Eluned puffed her cheeks out in an arrogant mocking pout, resting her chin on Silas’s shoulder.
"Oh, please! Silas would get bored within three minutes with you anyway. He’d probably find it far too easy to slip right out, considering how loose an old pirate must be down there~"

sentences.text: Brida wasn’t running at her maximum combat velocity, but her long powerful strides still carried her across the paved stones with impressive momentum.
Under her arm, she securely held the crate containing the sample set of Frost-Drake armor.
’I need to deliver this to Thora immediately so she can start analyzing the runes before tomorrow’s dawn!’ Brida thought with urgent determination.
Just as she crossed the intersection near the western garden, her right boot came down hard against what should have been solid reinforced stone.
SQUELCH!
The ground beneath her foot instantly liquefied into a deep, churning pool of thick, viscous mud.
"Whoa—!"
Brida’s forward momentum was violently arrested as her leg sank knee-deep into the sludge.
The sudden uncoordinated deceleration caused her upper body to pitch forward, the heavy armor crate slipping from her grasp and shooting through the air like a launched projectile.
Before the precious drake-alloy could shatter against the ground—
SHING!
A brilliant cascade of starlight mana flared in mid-air.
Aeliana... the Archon of the Stars materialized in a graceful blur of midnight-blue silk, catching the heavy crate effortlessly against her chest before landing lightly on the dry grass nearby.
Brida looked down at the bubbling pit of mud, her face twisting into a furious, deadpan grimace.
"That fucking Kadi..." Brida cursed out loud, violently pulling her leg free from the suction with a wet shluck.
She channeled a quick burst of physical mana through her greaves, blasting the clinging mud particles away in a spray of dry dust.
She knew for a fact that Kadi’s sudden surge in casting power was the direct result of whatever gift Silas had just gifted her.
Being the Second Secretary certainly had its perks.
Brida walked over to Aeliana, taking the heavy crate back with an appreciative nod.
"Thanks for the catch, Aeliana."
She looked at the Royal Elven Arcanist, noticing the book tucked into the sash of Aeliana’s robes.
Brida’s lips curled into a wicked, teasing grin.
"Hey, Aeliana," Brida purred quietly, leaning in close.
"How about you use your magic to make Kadi’s clothes vanish right now?
I’ll let you use me as a full anatomical test subject for that new spellcasting thesis you’re writing for Lord Silas."
Aeliana’s porcelain elven face instantly turned a catastrophic burning shade of pink.
The pristine Archon of the Stars choked on her breath, her pointed ears twitching violently as she stammered in flustered panic.
O-Okay..."
Brida laughed heartily, hoisting the crate onto her shoulder and continuing her sprint toward the foundry.
Back in the western training ring, Kadi threw her hands up with a triumphant victorious cackle.
"It worked!" Kadi cheered proudly, looking at the distant patch of ground.
"The terrestrial transmutation carried over sixty yards through the stone foundation!"
Silas stood beside her, blinking.
"What worked, Kadi?
Did you—"
Before Silas could finish his question, something happened.
POP!
A soft sharp chime of displaced elemental energy flashed around Kadi’s body.
In a fraction of a second, every single piece of fabric, leather, and silk constituting Kadi’s tailored administrative robes completely vanished from her skin.
Silas froze and Kadi froze as well.
A long awkward gust of evening wind swept through the empty courtyard, gently rustling Kadi’s sandy hair.
Kadi stood completely naked in the center of the training grounds.
Her fair skin, her slender waist, the soft curves of her hips, and her perky unblemished breasts were completely exposed to the open air and the twilight sky.
Kadi looked down at her own bare chest, then down at her bare feet, her brain processing the catastrophic wardrobe malfunction at glacial speed.
"AH!"

With a high-pitched squeak of sheer panic, Kadi frantically crossed her arms over her chest, pressing her forearms tightly against her breasts while twisting her thighs together to desperately cover herself with her single free hand.
’Why am I completely naked out here?!’ Kadi screamed internally, her face burning hotter than Thora’s blast furnaces.
She gritted her teeth, glancing up through her bangs to find Silas still standing mere feet away, his blue eyes locked onto her in a state of stunned paralyzed silence.
A sudden inappropriate tempting thought flared in Kadi’s mind.
’Wait...’ Kadi thought, her heart pounding violently against her ribs. ’He’s staring...
He’s really staring at me.
Should I just... loosen my hands?
What if I let him see everything?
If he gets enticed enough right now, he could literally pull me into the shadows of the Keep and claim me right here...’
Her fingers began to subtly loosen their grip over her chest—
CREEEAAAK!
The second-story window of Silas’s master quarters swung violently open.
Leaning out over the stone windowsill was Eluned.
The World-Tree Goddess’s flowing emerald hair billowed aggressively around her shoulders, her divine aura flaring with terrifying intensity.
Her vibrant green eyes were narrowed into a chilling, world-ending glare that could have cleaved a mountain range in half if it had been a physical offensive spell.
Kadi caught sight of the murderous divine stare and instantly flinched in pure terror.

Abandoning all thoughts of seducing her Lord on the grass, the naked secretary snatched the golden scepter from the ground, turned on her bare heels, and sprinted toward the residential quarters at supersonic speeds, leaving a trail of dust in her wake.
Silas stood alone in the training ring, letting out a long exhausted sigh as he rubbed the bridge of his nose.
’The girls in my Territory sure are beautiful...’
Up at the window, Eluned’s murderous glare instantly vanished, melting seamlessly into an impossibly sweet affectionate smile.
She leaned her chin onto her delicate hands, resting against the stone sill as her melodic voice drifted down through the courtyard.
"I heard you are giving out wonderful gifts today, Hubby~" Eluned purred sweetly, her emerald eyes practically sparkling with possessive delight.
"Tell me... you have something special for me too, right?"
Silas looked up at the open stone window of his master quarters, catching the radiant expectant glimmer in Eluned’s emerald eyes.
"I’m coming up," Silas called out with a warm, resigned chuckle, shaking his head as he turned away from the empty training grounds.
He pushed through the side entrance of the grand Keep, the cool stone interior welcoming him back into the sanctum.
The air within the corridors hummed with mana, carrying the soothing floral fragrance drifting from the conservatory.
As Silas crossed the threshold into the lower galley kitchen, he immediately spotted a commanding silhouette standing near the polished granite counters.
Talira stood with her back partially turned, the dark magnificent span of her draconic wings resting smoothly against her shoulder blades.
Two polished, obsidian dragon horns swept gracefully back from her temples, and her thick scaled tail swayed in a slow, rhythmic arc behind her legs.
In her claw-tipped hand, she held a crystal pitcher, casually tilting it to pour a thick stream of glowing royal-purple spirit juice into a heavy tumbler.
She paused mid-pour, her golden reptilian slit-pupils flicking toward the entrance the exact second Silas’s boots touched the flagstones.
Setting the pitcher down with deliberate care, Talira turned her full frame toward him.
Her posture straightened into that of an elite draconic guardian, though the sharp edge of her expression softened into genuine warmth.
Lord Silas," Talira greeted.
"Welcome home to the Blessed Land properly this time.
Your presence was sorely missed during the morning drills."
’I miss when she was shy...’
Talira couldn’t be shy after all they had spent all that time training with each other, she had gotten used to him.
Silas smiled, stepping closer and giving the dragon warrior an appreciative nod.
"It’s good to see you, Talira.
Don’t worry, we’re going to get some proper sparring sessions in very soon.
I haven’t forgotten about pushing your combat threshold."
A visible spark of fierce delight flared within Talira’s golden eyes.
Her dark wings flared slightly at the promise of battle, her tail giving a sharp satisfied flick against the floor.
"I shall hold you to that, My Lord," she murmured, a breathtaking smile touching her lips before she raised her cup in a respectful toast.
Leaving the kitchen behind, Silas ascended the grand spiraling staircase of the Keep.
Each step brought him closer to the quiet upper sanctum, the soft murmur of familiar voices drifting from beneath the master doorframe.
Silas pushed the heavy reinforced oak door open, stepping inside.
The master quarters were bathed in the soft glow of the setting twilight.
Sitting gracefully on the wide stone sill near the open window was Eluned.
The World-Tree Goddess’s emerald silk robes pooled like liquid moss around her bare feet, her silver-green hair tumbling over her delicate shoulders as she offered him a sweet adoring smile.

The Pirate Queen had discarded her heavy boots, propping herself up against a mountain of plush pillows.
Her wild dark hair fell in messy waves across her face as she meticulously wiped down the glowing oceanic alloy of Tidebringer with a strip of fine oil-cloth.
The curved saber hummed quietly with her touch, the serpentine runes along the fuller flashing with a gentle blue heartbeat.

chapters.title: Chapter 422: To Summon A Hero...
paragraphs: "I WILL CUT YOUR TONGUE OUT AND FEED IT TO THE TIDE-SERPENTS!" Morwenna roared, shooting up from the bed with Tidebringer blazing with phantom water pressure.
"Enough! Both of you, calm down!" Silas commanded firmly, raising his authority to clamp down on the rising elemental storm before the master quarters collapsed into a crater.
Both women stiffened, falling silent under his authoritative gaze, though they continued to glare daggers at each other across his chest.
"There is no sex happening right now," Silas stated, crossing his arms with a firm, resolved expression. "We have something far more critical to handle before the night ends."
Eluned blinked with her pout returning. "More critical than ensuring your bloodline?"

"Yes," Silas answered, looking between the Goddess and the Pirate Queen. "The eastern borders are shifting, new beasts are encroaching on the basin, and we need to expand our frontline command. I am going down to the Archway right now to summon another Her—"
"NO."
The rejection was instantaneous and spoken in perfect unison.
Silas blinked, genuine surprise flickering across his face.
Eluned aggressively tightened her grip around his left arm, burying his elbow deep into the soft unyielding swell of her chest, her emerald eyes blazing with possessive fury.

"No more women, Silas! You already have a Goddess and a Pirate Queen at your beck and call! We are more than enough to conquer the entire Sovereign Realm for you! What could you possibly need another woman for?!"
Morwenna marched across the floorboards, aggressively seizing Silas’s right arm and locking it securely against her ribs, her stormy gray eyes flashing with fierce jealousy.

"For once, I agree with the weed. You’ve already got an army of more than seventy women running around your barracks, an elven arcanist staring at you like a god, and a dragon-hybrid breathing fire in your kitchen. You don’t need another stray, Captain."
Silas looked down at the two terrifying powerhouses currently clinging to his arms like territorial toddlers, letting out a long exhausted sigh.

"You two are being ridiculous," Silas reasoned, an amused smirk tugging at his lips. "It’s not like whoever comes through that portal is going to magically fall in love with me the second her boots touch the grass. It’s not a romantic courtship... it’s a strategic expansion. We need specialized support to stabilize our divine infrastructure. It’s really not that serious."
Eluned and Morwenna exchanged a skeptical unified glance, clearly not believing a single word that came out of his mouth.

"Fine," Morwenna growled softly, her fingers digging firmly into his sleeve as she looked up into his blue eyes with a dangerous warning. "You can summon your new asset, Captain. But you better promise no funny business... because the second this new Hero tries anything weird with you, I am personally taking Tidebringer and cleaving her arms off at the shoulders."
The heavy timber doors of the Keep creaked softly as Silas stepped out into the night air.
The atmosphere of the Umbral Basin had settled into a quiet reverent stillness.

Above the fortified stone walls of the Blessed Land, the sky stretched out like a colossal vault of polished obsidian, pierced by millions of sharp crystalline stars that glittered with cold, diamond-like brilliance.
The surrounding mountain crags were reduced to jagged silhouettes against the dark heavens, their towering peaks acting as natural ramparts that boxed in the basin.
Silas walked down the wide polished stone steps leading away from the Keep’s main entrance, flanked closely on either side by his two powerhouses.
His dark combat robes swayed against his shins with every measured step.
He rolled his broad shoulders, taking in a deep lung-filling breath of the crisp night air, feeling the spiritual energy of the territory circulate smoothly through his Gold Core.
’What a day...’
Inwardly, he was grateful that the erratic spatial tear that connected their sector to Asgard hadn’t opened another atmospheric cold front into the depths of Asgard.

The heavy layer of snow that had buried the courtyard quite a while ago during the initial storms had finally melted and completely dried up under the radiant warmth of the sun and Silas wanted to keep it like this.

’Thank God,’ Silas thought, glancing up at the peaceful heavens with a sense of genuine relief. ’The last thing we need right now is another blizzard dumping three feet of ice on the barracks while the new recruits from the Unmovable Wall are still trying to find their footing. We need clear weather to run perimeter drills...’
FLUTTER!
A microscopic speck of white descended from the dark sky.
It drifted lazily through the still air, tumbling downward in slow erratic spirals until it landed squarely on the bridge of Silas’s nose.
A tiny, icy prickle touched his warm skin, and the flake instantly melted into a single drop of chilled moisture.
Silas stopped dead in his tracks.
He blinked, slowly wiping the droplet from his nose with the back of his thumb, his eyes staring blankly at the sky.
A second white flake pirouetted past his cheek, followed by a third, and then a fourth, dancing through the twilight like teasing sparks of frost.
Within seconds, a thin gentle veil of descending snow began to dust the dark stonework around them.

"Are you serious right now?" Silas muttered aloud, his voice thick with deep exhaustion as he stared upward into the dark canopy. "I literally just finished thinking about how nice it was that the snow had dried up. Does the weather in this basin have a direct psychic wire hooked into my brain specifically just to piss me off?"
"The skies of the Sovereign Realm don’t give a damn about your schedule, Captain," Morwenna drawled lazily from his right side.
The Pirate Queen casually extended a black leather-clad hand, letting several descending snowflakes settle across the palm of her glove.
Her stormy gray eyes narrowed with feral amusement as she turned her head, casting a wicked smirk across Silas’s chest toward the ethereal Goddess walking gracefully on his left.

"Look at it fall," Morwenna said, her deep voice carrying a cruel throaty chuckle. "Once enough of this white shit piles up on the stones, I’m going to pack a solid boulder of ice and throw it with enough force to cave in that smug plant-bitch’s pristine forehead."
Eluned didn’t even turn her head.
The World-Tree Goddess glided across the stone walkway, her emerald silk robes hovering half an inch above the ground on a gentle current of nature mana.

Her newly gifted relic, The Tear of the Slumbering World, rested gracefully against the pale valley of her collarbone, pulsing with a mesmerizing emerald light that cast soft reflections across her porcelain neck.

"You are entirely free to indulge in your childish little fantasies, pirate," Eluned replied, her melodic bell-like voice practically dripping with condescension. "I have zero time to waste playing your pathetic virgin games. Go throw mud at the training dummies where you belong..."
SNAP!
The sound of Morwenna’s jaw clamping shut was so violent and abrupt it was practically audible across the empty courtyard.
The Dread Queen’s stormy gray eyes widened in apoplectic fury.
The relaxed slouching posture she carried instantly hardened into coiled steel, her right hand instinctively snapping down to the leather-wrapped hilt of Tidebringer at her hip.
’Where did she even get a hilt for that sword...?’
The runes along the saber’s scabbard flared with an angry volatile blue glow, but beneath the explosive rage burning across her sun-kissed face, her lips pressed into a tight trembling line.
She gritted her sharp canines so hard a muscle twitched violently along her jaw, but she notably didn’t draw her steel, nor did she manage to find a snappy comeback.
She simply glared daggers through the side of Eluned’s head, utterly paralyzed and rendered speechless by the disrespect of the insult.
Silas walked between them in paralyzed silence, his gaze flicking back and forth between the two terrifying women.
’Wait... does that actually work?’ Silas’s internal voice echoed in genuine stunned disbelief. ’Ah, should I try it too?’
The absurd thought lingered in Silas’s mind for half a second before survival instinct violently took over.

’Hell nah. What am I, suicidal? If I say that to Morwenna, she isn’t going to back down and pout. She’ll literally tackle me into the dirt, rip my combat robes in half, and grab my ass like I owe her fifty million credits just to prove she isn’t one... Hard pass. I like keeping my pelvis intact.’
Pushing the terrifying mental image aside, Silas led them across the wide illuminated stone bridge spanning the central aqueduct.
Standing in the absolute center of the primary courtyard was the Summoning Archway.
The structure was an awe-inspiring marvel of cosmic architecture.

Twin pillars of seamless starlight-white celestial stone curved upward toward the sky like the towering horns of a forgotten deity, meeting at the apex where an eternal dormant vortex of liquid golden mana spun in quiet mesmerizing stasis.
’Did it upgrade since the last time I saw it? Damn...’

At the base of the circular marble dais stood a monolithic rectangular pedestal carved from a solid block of starlight quartz, its surface etched with thousands of micro-fine runic circuits that channeled the territory’s raw core power.
Silas stepped up the low marble steps, his boots tapping softly against the polished surface as his eyes swept over the pedestal.
There was not a single smudge of soot, dust, or moisture marred the glowing stone.
"The pedestal is spotless," Silas noted, nodding in genuine approval.
Eluned stepped up beside him, her chest swelling with proud authority as she smoothed down the emerald silk of her sleeves.

"Of course it is, Hubby," Eluned purred softly, tilting her chin up with a radiant affectionate smile. "Under my direct divine command, the maidens and trainees are ordered to cleanse the dais twice daily using distilled spirit-dew and enchanted silk cloths. The gateway that links your glorious soul to the cosmic ether must remain pure and unblemished at all times..."
Silas smiled warmly.
Looking down at the devoted Goddess, he reached out, gently cupping her delicate cheek in his palm, and leaned down to plant a firm affectionate kiss right on the center of her smooth forehead.
"You’re amazing, Elu," Silas murmured genuinely. "Thank you for keeping everything so well-organized."
Eluned’s breath caught in her throat.
An incandescent blush erupted across her porcelain cheeks, spreading all the way to the tips of her delicate pointed ears.
She melted entirely under his touch, her emerald eyes shimmering with breathless dizzying adoration as she pressed her cheek deeper into his warm hand, practically glowing with pure romantic triumph.
Standing three feet away on the marble dais, Morwenna completely froze.
The Pirate Queen’s stormy gray eyes locked onto Silas’s lips, then darted to Eluned’s blushing glowing face.
Her chest seized with a sudden wave of pure uncoordinated jealousy.

She opened her mouth, her hand twitching at her side as she prepared to aggressively demand a forehead kiss of her own, but the realization of how hopelessly needy it would sound made the words die in her throat.
’I didn’t even think to bribe the guards to clean the damn rock...’ Morwenna cursed internally, feeling a ridiculous, burning frustration well up in her chest.
Silas gently lowered his hand from Eluned’s cheek, turning his focus toward the quartz pedestal.
As he stepped forward, Morwenna let out a disappointed sigh, crossing her arms over her chest only to catch sight of Eluned deliberately peering around Silas’s broad back.
The World-Tree Goddess narrowed her vibrant green eyes, raised her chin, and stuck her pink tongue out directly at Morwenna in a childish mocking taunt.
Morwenna’s stormy eyes flashed with murderous intent.
Her canines bared as she silently mouthed.
’I am going to chop you into kindling and light my cigars with your corpse.’
Eluned simply smiled serenely, silently mouthing back: ’Virgin.’
Morwenna’s fists clenched so tightly her leather gloves creaked under the strain, and the two beings immediately devolved into another round of silent venomous death-glares behind their Lord’s back.
Silas ignored the silent war brewing behind him, letting out a steadying breath as he planted his boots before the central quartz pedestal.
It felt like a lifetime had passed since he had last stood before this ancient altar.
The memory of summoning Morwenna was still burned fresh into his mind.
So much had happened since that day... It was almost funny.
His territory had expanded from only him and the girls into a fortified domain holding over one hundred women which were his and his alone.
And now, the time had come to call upon another soul.
Silas closed his eyes, centering his breathing.
Deep within his chest, his Gold Core hummed with boundless power, circulating pure mana through his body in a golden tide.
He raised his right hand over the pedestal.
SHING!
A brilliant spatial fracture parted the air above his palm. With a crisp metallic rustle, an ornate rectangular card materialized between his fingers.
[Hero Summoning Ticket].

The heavy timber doors of the Keep creaked softly as Silas stepped out into the night air.
The atmosphere of the Umbral Basin had settled into a quiet reverent stillness.

Above the fortified stone walls of the Blessed Land, the sky stretched out like a colossal vault of polished obsidian, pierced by millions of sharp crystalline stars that glittered with cold, diamond-like brilliance.
The surrounding mountain crags were reduced to jagged silhouettes against the dark heavens, their towering peaks acting as natural ramparts that boxed in the basin.
Silas walked down the wide polished stone steps leading away from the Keep’s main entrance, flanked closely on either side by his two powerhouses.
His dark combat robes swayed against his shins with every measured step.
He rolled his broad shoulders, taking in a deep lung-filling breath of the crisp night air, feeling the spiritual energy of the territory circulate smoothly through his Gold Core.
’What a day...’
Inwardly, he was grateful that the erratic spatial tear that connected their sector to Asgard hadn’t opened another atmospheric cold front into the depths of Asgard.

The heavy layer of snow that had buried the courtyard quite a while ago during the initial storms had finally melted and completely dried up under the radiant warmth of the sun and Silas wanted to keep it like this.

’Thank God,’ Silas thought, glancing up at the peaceful heavens with a sense of genuine relief. ’The last thing we need right now is another blizzard dumping three feet of ice on the barracks while the new recruits from the Unmovable Wall are still trying to find their footing.
We need clear weather to run perimeter drills...’
FLUTTER!
A microscopic speck of white descended from the dark sky.
It drifted lazily through the still air, tumbling downward in slow erratic spirals until it landed squarely on the bridge of Silas’s nose.
A tiny, icy prickle touched his warm skin, and the flake instantly melted into a single drop of chilled moisture.
Silas stopped dead in his tracks.
He blinked, slowly wiping the droplet from his nose with the back of his thumb, his eyes staring blankly at the sky.
A second white flake pirouetted past his cheek, followed by a third, and then a fourth, dancing through the twilight like teasing sparks of frost.
Within seconds, a thin gentle veil of descending snow began to dust the dark stonework around them.
"Are you serious right now?" Silas muttered aloud, his voice thick with deep exhaustion as he stared upward into the dark canopy.
"I literally just finished thinking about how nice it was that the snow had dried up.
Does the weather in this basin have a direct psychic wire hooked into my brain specifically just to piss me off?"
"The skies of the Sovereign Realm don’t give a damn about your schedule, Captain," Morwenna drawled lazily from his right side.
The Pirate Queen casually extended a black leather-clad hand, letting several descending snowflakes settle across the palm of her glove.
Her stormy gray eyes narrowed with feral amusement as she turned her head, casting a wicked smirk across Silas’s chest toward the ethereal Goddess walking gracefully on his left.
"Look at it fall," Morwenna said, her deep voice carrying a cruel throaty chuckle.
"Once enough of this white shit piles up on the stones, I’m going to pack a solid boulder of ice and throw it with enough force to cave in that smug plant-bitch’s pristine forehead."
Eluned didn’t even turn her head.
The World-Tree Goddess glided across the stone walkway, her emerald silk robes hovering half an inch above the ground on a gentle current of nature mana.

Her newly gifted relic, The Tear of the Slumbering World, rested gracefully against the pale valley of her collarbone, pulsing with a mesmerizing emerald light that cast soft reflections across her porcelain neck.
"You are entirely free to indulge in your childish little fantasies, pirate," Eluned replied, her melodic bell-like voice practically dripping with condescension.
"I have zero time to waste playing your pathetic virgin games.
Go throw mud at the training dummies where you belong..."
SNAP!
The sound of Morwenna’s jaw clamping shut was so violent and abrupt it was practically audible across the empty courtyard.
The Dread Queen’s stormy gray eyes widened in apoplectic fury.
The relaxed slouching posture she carried instantly hardened into coiled steel, her right hand instinctively snapping down to the leather-wrapped hilt of Tidebringer at her hip.
’Where did she even get a hilt for that sword...?’
The runes along the saber’s scabbard flared with an angry volatile blue glow, but beneath the explosive rage burning across her sun-kissed face, her lips pressed into a tight trembling line.
She gritted her sharp canines so hard a muscle twitched violently along her jaw, but she notably didn’t draw her steel, nor did she manage to find a snappy comeback.
She simply glared daggers through the side of Eluned’s head, utterly paralyzed and rendered speechless by the disrespect of the insult.
Silas walked between them in paralyzed silence, his gaze flicking back and forth between the two terrifying women.
’Wait... does that actually work?’ Silas’s internal voice echoed in genuine stunned disbelief. ’Ah, should I try it too?’
The absurd thought lingered in Silas’s mind for half a second before survival instinct violently took over.
’Hell nah.
What am I, suicidal?
If I say that to Morwenna, she isn’t going to back down and pout.
She’ll literally tackle me into the dirt, rip my combat robes in half, and grab my ass like I owe her fifty million credits just to prove she isn’t one...
Hard pass.
I like keeping my pelvis intact.’
Pushing the terrifying mental image aside, Silas led them across the wide illuminated stone bridge spanning the central aqueduct.
Standing in the absolute center of the primary courtyard was the Summoning Archway.
The structure was an awe-inspiring marvel of cosmic architecture.

Twin pillars of seamless starlight-white celestial stone curved upward toward the sky like the towering horns of a forgotten deity, meeting at the apex where an eternal dormant vortex of liquid golden mana spun in quiet mesmerizing stasis.
’Did it upgrade since the last time I saw it?
Damn...’

At the base of the circular marble dais stood a monolithic rectangular pedestal carved from a solid block of starlight quartz, its surface etched with thousands of micro-fine runic circuits that channeled the territory’s raw core power.
Silas stepped up the low marble steps, his boots tapping softly against the polished surface as his eyes swept over the pedestal.
There was not a single smudge of soot, dust, or moisture marred the glowing stone.
"The pedestal is spotless," Silas noted, nodding in genuine approval.
Eluned stepped up beside him, her chest swelling with proud authority as she smoothed down the emerald silk of her sleeves.
"Of course it is, Hubby," Eluned purred softly, tilting her chin up with a radiant affectionate smile.
"Under my direct divine command, the maidens and trainees are ordered to cleanse the dais twice daily using distilled spirit-dew and enchanted silk cloths.
The gateway that links your glorious soul to the cosmic ether must remain pure and unblemished at all times..."
Silas smiled warmly.
Looking down at the devoted Goddess, he reached out, gently cupping her delicate cheek in his palm, and leaned down to plant a firm affectionate kiss right on the center of her smooth forehead.
"You’re amazing, Elu," Silas murmured genuinely.
"Thank you for keeping everything so well-organized."
Eluned’s breath caught in her throat.
An incandescent blush erupted across her porcelain cheeks, spreading all the way to the tips of her delicate pointed ears.
She melted entirely under his touch, her emerald eyes shimmering with breathless dizzying adoration as she pressed her cheek deeper into his warm hand, practically glowing with pure romantic triumph.
Standing three feet away on the marble dais, Morwenna completely froze.
The Pirate Queen’s stormy gray eyes locked onto Silas’s lips, then darted to Eluned’s blushing glowing face.
Her chest seized with a sudden wave of pure uncoordinated jealousy.

She opened her mouth, her hand twitching at her side as she prepared to aggressively demand a forehead kiss of her own, but the realization of how hopelessly needy it would sound made the words die in her throat.
’I didn’t even think to bribe the guards to clean the damn rock...’ Morwenna cursed internally, feeling a ridiculous, burning frustration well up in her chest.
Silas gently lowered his hand from Eluned’s cheek, turning his focus toward the quartz pedestal.
As he stepped forward, Morwenna let out a disappointed sigh, crossing her arms over her chest only to catch sight of Eluned deliberately peering around Silas’s broad back.
The World-Tree Goddess narrowed her vibrant green eyes, raised her chin, and stuck her pink tongue out directly at Morwenna in a childish mocking taunt.
Morwenna’s stormy eyes flashed with murderous intent.
Her canines bared as she silently mouthed.
’I am going to chop you into kindling and light my cigars with your corpse.’
Eluned simply smiled serenely, silently mouthing back: ’Virgin.’
Morwenna’s fists clenched so tightly her leather gloves creaked under the strain, and the two beings immediately devolved into another round of silent venomous death-glares behind their Lord’s back.
Silas ignored the silent war brewing behind him, letting out a steadying breath as he planted his boots before the central quartz pedestal.
It felt like a lifetime had passed since he had last stood before this ancient altar.
The memory of summoning Morwenna was still burned fresh into his mind.
So much had happened since that day...
It was almost funny.
His territory had expanded from only him and the girls into a fortified domain holding over one hundred women which were his and his alone.
And now, the time had come to call upon another soul.
Silas closed his eyes, centering his breathing.
Deep within his chest, his Gold Core hummed with boundless power, circulating pure mana through his body in a golden tide.
He raised his right hand over the pedestal.
SHING!
A brilliant spatial fracture parted the air above his palm.
With a crisp metallic rustle, an ornate rectangular card materialized between his fingers.
[Hero Summoning Ticket].

chapters.title: Chapter 423: Saintess Of The Argent Flame [I]
paragraphs: Silas stared down at the glowing silver border of the ticket.
’Ah... Damn it became more cost.’
In the modern world, the value of a Hero Summoning Ticket had skyrocketed to an astronomical suffocating sum... easily fetching over two million Spirit Credits apiece.
’I can still remember when it was 500k.’

With his current financial reserves and territory dividends, Silas possessed the raw wealth to purchase dozens of these tickets and simply spam the summoning until he flooded the basin with divine combatants.
Yet, Silas had deliberately chosen not to rush the process.

’Every single high-ranking Hero I pull through this rift comes with their own heavy baggage...’ Silas thought solemnly, his thumb tracing the smooth magical edge of the card. ’Eluned according to what she told me was locked in a dying world-core for centuries, watching her domain rot. I don’t know much about Morwenna but I knew she lost everything precious to her...’
He refused to treat these souls like disposable gacha pulls.

If he was going to summon a living, breathing warrior into his Blessed Land, he needed to ensure his territory possessed the emotional, physical, and logistical capacity to actually heal them, support them, and give them a home where they would never be exploited again.
’Take it step by step,’ Silas resolved firmly. ’Build the foundation first.’
Silas extended his arm and placed the glowing golden ticket flat against the central indentation of the starlight quartz pedestal.
The moment the ticket touched the stone, the runic circuits carved across the dais flared with blinding incandescent golden light.
HUMMMMMMM.

A low tectonic vibration reverberated through the bedrock of the entire territory, sending a gentle shockwave through the soles of their boots as a semi-transparent crystalline system interface materialized directly before his vision.
[Would you like to Summon A Hero?]
[Y / N]
Silas took a deep breath, extended his index finger, and firmly pressed the glowing golden [ Y ].
BOOM!
The summoning ticket instantly disintegrated into a tempest of radiant golden light particles.
WHOOSH!

A colossal pillar of concentrated starlight exploded upward from the quartz pedestal, surging vertically into the heavens with enough raw force to violently whip Silas’s dark combat robes and hair backward.
The golden beam tore through the low twilight clouds, scattering the falling snowflakes into sparkling vapor and illuminating the entire Umbral Basin around the territory in a warm breathtaking dawn.
The twin white pillars of the Archway began to rotate slowly, the spatial vortex between them spinning with terrifying cosmic acceleration.
Silas looked up into the swirling golden void, his blue eyes burning with quiet conviction.
’Whoever you are... wherever you are trapped in the endless dark... come to us.’
"A savior, huh...?"
The words drifted into the empty expanse, it was dry and hollow, carrying the fragile tone of a ghost that had long forgotten the melody of human speech.
In the boundless, suffocating expanse of the Great Void, a lone woman sat curled upon a floating slab of shattered white marble.
Around her, there was no sky, no horizon, and no ground.
There was only the infinite pitch-black sea of raw unrefined ether, punctuated by jagged fragments of floating stone, shattered temple ruins, and ancient drifting debris from forgotten worlds.
But this ether was not the gentle spiritual mana of the mortal realms... It was toxic.𝕗𝐫𝚎𝗲𝘄𝐞𝕓𝐧𝕠𝘃𝕖𝐥.𝐜𝚘𝚖
CRACK!
A few hundred yards away, a floating island the size of a mountain was suddenly engulfed by colossal, writhing tentacles formed of raw void-corruption.
The abyssal fiend squeezed with casual uncaring brutality, crushing the ancient stone pillars into dust.
The sound of stone fracturing echoed like thunder through the silence, but the monstrosity simply drifted away, searching for more soul-essence to devour.
Aurelia El Mimonte did not even turn her head.
Her hair was magnificent, falling past her slender waist in thick tangled waves of pure platinum-blonde that caught the sickly luminescence of the surrounding ether.
Her facial features were sculpted with breathtaking beauty... high cheekbones, a soft delicate jawline, and pale porcelain skin yet her expression was completely dead.
She slowly raised her slender, trembling hand, bringing her fingers to the corners of her eyes.
She wiped away a bead of moisture, half-expecting it to be a tear.
But when she rubbed her fingertips together, she felt only the cold, sticky film of dry sweat.
She had tried to weep so many times over the centuries, yet her tear ducts had long since withered into arid scarred silence.
Aurelia had lost all concept of linear time.

Was it a thousand years? Ten thousand? Five centuries? In this sunless, bottomless dimensional graveyard where abandoned souls and dangerous entities were cast out by the higher pantheons to rot, time held zero meaning.
This place was a prison... a cosmic dumping ground designed to hold beings whose powers were deemed too terrifying or too unstable to allow them to live, yet too resilient to easily kill.
She lowered her hand, her knuckles brushing against the cold jagged surface of the stone mound beside her.
It was a grave.
When Aurelia had first been cast into this dimensional purgatory, she hadn’t been alone.
Resting upon this floating slab of rock was an ancient frail woman... the previous High Saintess of the Argent Sanctum, who had been locked away five hundred years before Aurelia’s own era.

The old woman had spent her final dying decades holding Aurelia’s trembling hands, whispering ancient prophecies of a legendary someone... a true Savior who would one day shatter the cosmic chains, cross the boundary of the void, and pull them back into the light.
Aurelia had buried the old woman with her own bare hands three centuries ago.
’A savior...’ Aurelia thought, a bitter hollow smile touching her chapped lips. ’What a cruel, pathetic lie.’
She had lived long enough to understand the depravity of mortals, heroes, and gods alike.
She had believed in a savior once... She had loved a savior once... She had given her entire flesh, her soul, and her sanity to keep her savior alive...
...And that savior had butchered her.
Aurelia turned her head toward the empty abyss.
Her once-radiant golden-amber eyes were completely milky-white, their retinas permanently burned away and scarred by centuries of processing foreign spiritual corruption.
Aurelia was blind.
Truly, completely blind. She could perceive the void only through the agonizing vibrations of mana radiating through the cold ether.

’If there truly is a savior out there in the infinite void...’ she thought, her fingers tracing the cold dirt of the grave, ’I would fall to my knees and praise whoever it is for the rest of eternity.’
She swallowed but even that was dry.
’...But I know the truth. There are no saviors in this universe. Only executioners.’
Because the last time she had believed in a hero, the rain had been falling over a field of rotting corpses.
CLATTER! CRASH!
The freezing rain poured down from the bruised, purple-black sky, pounding relentlessly against the mud, shattered iron, and severed limbs that covered the ruined plains of the Meolion Kingdom.
The air was thick with the suffocating stench of demonic miasma.
Humanity’s grand expeditionary vanguard was completely annihilated.

Thousands of elite paladins, royal knights, and high mages lay dead in the muddy trenches, their flesh actively decomposing into black bubbling sludge beneath the horrific, incurable contagion known as the Demon Rot.
Standing amidst the slaughter, barely holding her balance against the churning mud, was the young High Saintess, Aurelia.
Her golden ceremonial robes were soaked in mud and crimson blood, her hands trembling violently as she dropped to her knees beside a fallen warrior.
Lying in the mud before her was Cassian.
The Otherworldly Hero... the handsome silver-haired champion summoned from a distant planet to save their world was coughing violently, hacking up thick globs of black, coagulated blood.
A horrific jagged gash tore across the entire expanse of his chest plate, exposing shattered ribs and black pulsing veins of abyssal demon rot that were rapidly creeping toward his heart.

"Cassian! No! Don’t close your eyes!" Aurelia screamed, her golden-amber eyes overflowing with terrified tears as she pressed her bare hands against his shattered chest. "Stay with me! You cannot die here! Please, look at me!"
Cassian looked up at her through half-lidded fading eyes.
A weak bloody smile touched his lips as he reached up with a trembling hand, weakly brushing his fingers against her wet cheek.

"Aurelia..." Cassian rasped, his breath rattling in his throat like broken glass. "I... I don’t want to die... I made a promise to you beneath the stars... I want to stay by your side... I want to take you away from this kingdom when the war is over..."
Aurelia’s heart shattered into a million pieces.

’He is the summoned Hero...’ Aurelia’s mind raced with agonizing panic. ’If Cassian dies here, the Meolion Kingdom will fall. The demons will slaughter every innocent soul across the continent. But more than that... I love him. I cannot let the man I love die in the mud!’
Aurelia gritted her teeth so hard blood seeped from her gums.
She reached down into the deepest wellspring within her soul.
VUUUUUUM!

A blinding radiant corona of golden divine fire ignited around her hand but as she focused her intent on saving his life at any cost, the golden flames violently shifted... transmuting into a searing incandescent Argent Flame.
The silver fire roared to life, latching onto Cassian’s chest.
"AARRRRGGGGHHH!"
Aurelia threw her head back, letting out a blood-curdling shriek of unimaginable soul-tearing agony.
The Argent Flame did not simply burn away the affliction. Under the cruel immutable law of its secondary conceptual activation, it acted as a living bridge of transmutation.
The black necrotic demon rot was forcefully pulled out of Cassian’s circulatory system, surging up through the silver fire and slamming directly into Aurelia’s own spiritual core.
In that exact same second, the physical reality of the wound mirrored itself with violence.
SPLURT!

A massive identical jagged gash violently tore open across Aurelia’s own chest, ripping through her flesh, shattering her ribs, and splattering a fountain of her own bright crimson blood into the muddy rain.
"GAAAH—!"
Aurelia staggered backward, crashing into the mud, her vision swimming with blinding white agony as the protective silver barrier she had cast around them shattered like brittle glass.
Cassian gasped.

He bolted upright, his eyes wide in utter bewilderment. He looked down at his chest... the shattered ribs were fully knitted, the black demon rot was completely purged, and his skin was smooth and pristine.
His strength, his vitality, and his mana had been restored to their peak in an instant.
"Aurelia?!" Cassian shouted, scrambling through the mud toward her trembling bleeding form.

"D-Don’t stop..." Aurelia choked out, clutching her shredded chest with blood-soaked fingers, her pale face completely drained of color as she fought desperately to maintain consciousness. "The... the abyssal fiends are closing in... I am fine... I can slowly purge the rot... Go! Defeat them, Cassian!"
Cassian looked at her bleeding body, a dark, complex flicker passing through his eyes before he firmly nodded.

"I will protect you, Aurelia!" Cassian roared, drawing his holy broadsword with renewed invincible fury as he charged into the encroaching swarm of demon lords, cutting them down in a storm of brilliant steel.
That was the fateful day the Kingdom discovered the true nature of the Saintess’s awakening.
The legend of the Argent Flame of Transmutation had become reality.

The Saintess of Meolion possessed a divine miracle capable of curing the incurable Demon Rot... provided she absorbed the corruption entirely into her own flesh, mirroring the fatal wounds upon her own body to grant the recipient absolute, immaculate restoration.
Because of the vast purifying reservoir of the silver flame, she would not immediately perish from the rot; she would simply endure the agonizing process of burning it away within her own core.
It was meant to be a day of miraculous triumph for the realm.
Yet...
BANG!
The heavy iron-reinforced door of the subterranean dungeon slammed shut with bone-jarring violence, barely an inch from Aurelia’s face.
"Ahn—!"
Aurelia recoiled with a sharp terrified gasp, tumbling backward onto the cold, damp stone floor of the prison cell.
The concussive force of the door slamming had nearly shattered her nose.
Outside the narrow iron bars, an armored royal inquisitor sneered down at her with cold, uncaring eyes.

"You performed adequately today, Saintess," the guard stated in a monotonous dismissive voice. "The Third Battalion suffered twenty-four cases of advanced demon rot during the northern skirmish. You will begin processing their wounds at dawn. Do not slack in your duties."
The guard turned on his heel, his heavy iron boots echoing down the dark stone corridor before vanishing into the upper fortress.
Aurelia sat curled in the dark, damp corner of the subterranean cell, pulling her trembling knees tightly against her chest.
It had been a month.
Exactly four weeks since she had awakened the Argent Flame and saved the Otherworldly Hero from certain death.

And instead of being revered as a living deity, instead of being protected as the kingdom’s sacred treasure... she had been locked in high-grade mana-suppression chains beneath the royal dungeons, treated like a consumable biological filter.
She looked down at her own exposed trembling limbs.
Her pale, once-pristine porcelain skin was completely ruined.

Crisscrossing her arms, her thighs, her collarbones, and her torso were dozens of brutal jagged scars... burn marks from abyssal fire, torn flesh from demonic claws, and black necrotic veins of demon rot pulsing beneath her skin.
Every single wound represented a royal knight she had saved from death, reflected onto her own flesh by the cruel laws of the Argent Flame.

’What did I do wrong...?’ Aurelia wept silently, pressing her forehead against the freezing stone. ’I only wanted to save everyone... I only wanted to protect our people... What did I do to deserve this hell?’
