You cannot die here!
Please, look at me!"
Cassian looked up at her through half-lidded fading eyes.
A weak bloody smile touched his lips as he reached up with a trembling hand, weakly brushing his fingers against her wet cheek.
"Aurelia..." Cassian rasped, his breath rattling in his throat like broken glass.
I don’t want to die...
I made a promise to you beneath the stars...
I want to stay by your side...
I want to take you away from this kingdom when the war is over..."
Aurelia’s heart shattered into a million pieces.
’He is the summoned Hero...’ Aurelia’s mind raced with agonizing panic. ’If Cassian dies here, the Meolion Kingdom will fall.
The demons will slaughter every innocent soul across the continent.
But more than that...
I love him.
I cannot let the man I love die in the mud!’
Aurelia gritted her teeth so hard blood seeped from her gums.
She reached down into the deepest wellspring within her soul.
VUUUUUUM!

A blinding radiant corona of golden divine fire ignited around her hand but as she focused her intent on saving his life at any cost, the golden flames violently shifted... transmuting into a searing incandescent Argent Flame.
The silver fire roared to life, latching onto Cassian’s chest.
"AARRRRGGGGHHH!"
Aurelia threw her head back, letting out a blood-curdling shriek of unimaginable soul-tearing agony.
The Argent Flame did not simply burn away the affliction.
Under the cruel immutable law of its secondary conceptual activation, it acted as a living bridge of transmutation.
The black necrotic demon rot was forcefully pulled out of Cassian’s circulatory system, surging up through the silver fire and slamming directly into Aurelia’s own spiritual core.
In that exact same second, the physical reality of the wound mirrored itself with violence.
SPLURT!

A massive identical jagged gash violently tore open across Aurelia’s own chest, ripping through her flesh, shattering her ribs, and splattering a fountain of her own bright crimson blood into the muddy rain.
"GAAAH—!"
Aurelia staggered backward, crashing into the mud, her vision swimming with blinding white agony as the protective silver barrier she had cast around them shattered like brittle glass.
Cassian gasped.
He bolted upright, his eyes wide in utter bewilderment.
He looked down at his chest... the shattered ribs were fully knitted, the black demon rot was completely purged, and his skin was smooth and pristine.
His strength, his vitality, and his mana had been restored to their peak in an instant.
"Aurelia?!" Cassian shouted, scrambling through the mud toward her trembling bleeding form.
"D-Don’t stop..." Aurelia choked out, clutching her shredded chest with blood-soaked fingers, her pale face completely drained of color as she fought desperately to maintain consciousness.
"The... the abyssal fiends are closing in...
I am fine...
I can slowly purge the rot...
Go!
Defeat them, Cassian!"
Cassian looked at her bleeding body, a dark, complex flicker passing through his eyes before he firmly nodded.

"I will protect you, Aurelia!" Cassian roared, drawing his holy broadsword with renewed invincible fury as he charged into the encroaching swarm of demon lords, cutting them down in a storm of brilliant steel.
That was the fateful day the Kingdom discovered the true nature of the Saintess’s awakening.
The legend of the Argent Flame of Transmutation had become reality.

The Saintess of Meolion possessed a divine miracle capable of curing the incurable Demon Rot... provided she absorbed the corruption entirely into her own flesh, mirroring the fatal wounds upon her own body to grant the recipient absolute, immaculate restoration.
Because of the vast purifying reservoir of the silver flame, she would not immediately perish from the rot; she would simply endure the agonizing process of burning it away within her own core.
It was meant to be a day of miraculous triumph for the realm.
Yet...
BANG!
The heavy iron-reinforced door of the subterranean dungeon slammed shut with bone-jarring violence, barely an inch from Aurelia’s face.
"Ahn—!"
Aurelia recoiled with a sharp terrified gasp, tumbling backward onto the cold, damp stone floor of the prison cell.
The concussive force of the door slamming had nearly shattered her nose.
Outside the narrow iron bars, an armored royal inquisitor sneered down at her with cold, uncaring eyes.
"You performed adequately today, Saintess," the guard stated in a monotonous dismissive voice.
"The Third Battalion suffered twenty-four cases of advanced demon rot during the northern skirmish.
You will begin processing their wounds at dawn.
Do not slack in your duties."
The guard turned on his heel, his heavy iron boots echoing down the dark stone corridor before vanishing into the upper fortress.
Aurelia sat curled in the dark, damp corner of the subterranean cell, pulling her trembling knees tightly against her chest.
It had been a month.
Exactly four weeks since she had awakened the Argent Flame and saved the Otherworldly Hero from certain death.

And instead of being revered as a living deity, instead of being protected as the kingdom’s sacred treasure... she had been locked in high-grade mana-suppression chains beneath the royal dungeons, treated like a consumable biological filter.
She looked down at her own exposed trembling limbs.
Her pale, once-pristine porcelain skin was completely ruined.

Crisscrossing her arms, her thighs, her collarbones, and her torso were dozens of brutal jagged scars... burn marks from abyssal fire, torn flesh from demonic claws, and black necrotic veins of demon rot pulsing beneath her skin.
Every single wound represented a royal knight she had saved from death, reflected onto her own flesh by the cruel laws of the Argent Flame.
’What did I do wrong...?’ Aurelia wept silently, pressing her forehead against the freezing stone. ’I only wanted to save everyone...
I only wanted to protect our people...
What did I do to deserve this hell?’

chapters.title: Chapter 424: Saintess Of The Argent Flame [II]
paragraphs: She had been Cassian’s beloved Saintess but over the last four weeks, Cassian had not visited her cell a single time.
The Hero had become the celebrated Champion of the kingdom.

Whenever he charged into battle, he fought with reckless psychotic disregard for his own safety because he knew that no matter how many times his limbs were shredded or his core was infected with demon rot, the kingdom would simply drag his broken body down to Aurelia’s cell, force her to absorb the agony, and send him back out to glory while she screamed in the dark.
’Was it a mistake...?’ Aurelia’s heart tore in two. ’Was it a mistake to love him? Was it a mistake to save his life?’
The overwhelming agony of the rot eating her core, combined with the suffocating despair of betrayal, completely broke her spirit.
Aurelia raised her trembling hands to her own throat.
She dug her thumbs into her windpipe, using all her physical strength to crush her own airway, desperate to end the perpetual torment.
FWOOSH!
The Argent Flame flared instinctively within her chest.
A searing, blinding blast of silver fire violently rejected her suicide attempt, scorching her hands and sending a violent shockwave of purifying agony through her meridians.
"AAAAAAAHHHHHHH!"

Aurelia threw her head back, screaming at the top of her lungs as tears of starlight burned against her cheeks, the guards in the corridor wincing slightly at the muffled shrieks before ignoring them entirely.
Another month passed in agonizing torture.
Thanks to the perpetual, non-stop sacrifices of the imprisoned Saintess beneath the earth, humanity’s grand army was completely restored to full, terrifying combat readiness.
The rot had been completely purged from thousands of elite soldiers.
At the dawn of the final offensive, the gates of the Meolion Grand Citadel swung wide.
Thousands of pristine silver-armored paladins charged across the plains on armored warhorses, their banners fluttering in the wind as they rode to confront the vanguard of the Demon Lord.
Leading the charge at the apex of the formation was Cassian.
The Otherworldly Hero wore magnificent gold-plated divine plate armor, his holy broadsword crackling with starlight.
A wicked grin was plastered across his face, his eyes blazing with ecstasy as his warhorse leaped over the defensive trenches.
"FOLLOW ME!"
He felt invincible... Cassian felt like a god among mortals.
Riding directly to his right was Sir Robert... a veteran paladin captain whose entire upper torso had been completely reconstructed by Aurelia’s Argent Flame just two days prior.
"CHARGE!" Robert roared, lowering his heavy mythril lance. "FOR THE KINGDOM! FOR THE HERO!"
The paladin slammed his horse directly into the front line of the demonic horde, impaling a towering abyssal berserker through the chest with a ferocious war cry.
Deep beneath the royal citadel, locked in her pitch-black stone cell, Aurelia sat trembling on the floor.
Her long platinum hair was matted with grime, her milky-white eyes hollow and vacant, looking more like an emaciated corpse than a living human being.

’It hurts...’ Aurelia thought, her consciousness drifting in and out of the cold dark. ’My chest burns... my veins feel like molten lead... Please, God... if there is any mercy in the heavens... just let my heart stop beating...’
Suddenly, a strange terrifying sensation gripped the base of her neck.
It was not the slow burning ache of the Demon Rot. It was a cold, sharp, razor-thin line of phantom pressure wrapping around her throat like a garrote wire.
On the distant battlefield, the dying abyssal berserker let out a monstrous roar.
With its final ounce of strength, the demon swung a massive obsidian cleaver in a blinding horizontal arc.
SHING!
Sir Robert’s mythril neck guard was completely sheared through.

The paladin captain’s head was cleanly severed from his shoulders, spinning wildly through the bloody air before crashing into the mud with a fountain of bright arterial blood erupting from his decapitated neck.
And in that exact second...
There was a final terrible rule governing the secondary phase of the Argent Flame that the corrupt High Council and the Otherworldly Hero had deliberately concealed from Aurelia.
The soul-link was not a temporary bridge. As long as the mirrored scars remained etched upon the Saintess’s soul, the resonance between the vessel and the saved soldier remained complete.
Inside the quiet dark dungeon cell, Aurelia’s vacant golden eyes suddenly widened in paralyzed shock.
’Ah...’ Aurelia’s final thought echoed in the freezing darkness. ’...I am dying.’𝙛𝒓𝓮𝙚𝔀𝒆𝒃𝓷𝒐𝓿𝙚𝓵.𝙘𝒐𝒎
SCHLICK!
A clean violent line of bright crimson light flashed around Aurelia’s slender throat.
In a fraction of a millisecond, the physical decapitation mirrored itself with flawless reality.

Aurelia’s head was violently ripped from her shoulders, spinning gracefully through the air of the prison cell in a spray of bright arterial blood, before slamming heavily against the iron bars of the dungeon window as her headless body collapsed limply onto the freezing stone.

The severed head of Aurelia El Mimonte slammed against the heavy iron bars of the high dungeon window with a sickening wet crunch, leaving a thick smear of dark arterial blood against the cold metal before rolling onto the damp stone floor.
Her vocal cords had no lungs to drive them, yet the raw agony tearing through her consciousness forced an impossible blood-curdling shriek from her severed lips.
"AAAAAAAGGGHHH—!"
The sound was a hollow, gargling scream of torment, spraying fine mists of red across the flagstones as her wide golden-amber eyes bulged in horror.
In the torchlit corridor outside, the sudden violent commotion brought the young novice guard running.
His iron-plated boots clattered frantically against the spiral stone steps, his hand clutching the hilt of his broadsword as he reached the cell gate.
"What happened?! Saintess?!"
The guard gripped the iron bars, peering into the gloom and his breath instantly caught in his throat. His face drained of all color with his stomach violently heaving.
Lying in the center of the cell was Aurelia’s limp, headless body, crimson blood pumping from her open neck in dying spurts.
And two yards away, sitting upright against the wall, her severed head was staring directly at him, screaming in agony.
"Gods above..." the guard whispered, his voice trembling with vomit-inducing terror. "Her head... someone breached the dungeon! She’s been murdered—"
VUUUUUM.
Before the guard could fumble for his keys, a brilliant incandescent glow erupted from the hollow stump of her neck.
It was not normal divine mana. It was the Argent Flame.
Wisps of searing pure white-silver fire leaked from her exposed flesh, hissing as they vaporized the pooling blood on the stones.
Like living undulating tendrils of liquid silver, the flames whipped across the damp floor, wrapping tightly around her severed head.
With terrifying precision, the tendrils lifted the dislocated head into the air, dragging it slowly back toward the bleeding torso.
Aurelia’s screams intensified, rising in pitch until her vocal cords shredded.
Every single microscopic nerve ending, every severed tendon, every severed artery and fractured vertebra began to stitch itself back together across the blazing bridge of silver fire.
It was not a painless miracle... it was an excruciating reconstruction where she felt every microscopic fiber of her flesh burning, knitting, and fusing back into place under unimaginable heat.
CRACK-CRACK-SNAP!
Her cervical spine re-aligned with a series of wet hollow pops.
The silver fire sealed the seam across her neck, leaving behind a raised burning crimson scar that pulsed with fresh agony.
Aurelia collapsed onto her hands and knees, gasping and retching as thick strings of saliva and blood dripped from her trembling lips.
"Help me..." she sobbed, clawing at the stone floor, her fingernails splintering against the rock. "Please... please, make it stop... I can’t... I can’t bear this..."
The young guard outside shook violently, his key rattling against the heavy iron lock.
"Hold on! I’m opening the gate! I’ll call the high clerics—"
WHOOSH!

A heavy gauntleted hand clamped down hard on the novice guard’s shoulder as a veteran royal inquisitor stood behind him, his cold shadowed eyes staring through the iron bars at the sobbing Saintess with chilling apathy.
"Step away from the gate, recruit," the veteran commanded in a flat, uncaring monotone.
"B-But sir! Her head was cut off! She’s being torn apart in there!" the young guard cried, desperately pointing a trembling finger. "We have to stop whatever curse is doing this!"

"Silence," the inquisitor snapped, pulling the boy back with brutal force and shoving him against the stone wall. "This is her designated purpose... The First Vanguard has engaged the demonic horde on the northern plains. This is part of the job. She is fulfilling her duty to the Crown."
"Her duty?!"
BANG!
The inquisitor slammed the heavy outer iron grate shut, locking the entire corridor in suffocating darkness and shutting off all access to the inner cell.
Inside the pitch-black dungeon, Aurelia sat alone, shivering violently.
Her ragged blood-soaked breath rattled in her chest as the silence of the underground fortress settled around her.
’Is it over...?’ she thought, her mind swimming in a haze of blinding shock. ’Did the battle end...? Please... please let it be over...’
SCHLICK! SCHLICK!
Two simultaneous razor-thin lines of invisible force sheared through the air. Without warning, both of Aurelia’s arms were violently severed at the wrists.
"GAAAAAH!"

Her hands flew through the air, tumbling end-over-end before slamming against the reinforced glass of the high dungeon window, leaving twin bloody handprints against the pane before dropping into the dirt.
On the distant battlefield, two royal spearmen had just had their hands severed by an abyssal bladed demon and beneath the earth, the Saintess paid their blood-debt in full.
Aurelia fell forward, her bleeding wristless stumps striking the stone floor.
The pain was an all-consuming fire that blinded her senses, making her thrash and writhe in the pooling crimson.
"HELP ME! CASSIAN! CASSIAN, PLEASE!" she screamed into the dark, calling out for the man who had promised to protect her beneath the stars.
No one answered, it was only the sizzle of the Argent Flame roared in response.
The silver fire burst from the open stumps of her forearms, extending outward like blazing white claws to seize her severed hands.
The flames dragged the limbs back, violently fusing the bones, mending the torn flesh, and welding the severed nerves back together in another wave of screaming ungodly agony.
The fire subsided.
Aurelia lay facedown on the freezing stone, her body convulsing in involuntary spasms. Her throat was raw, her tears completely dried into crusty salt tracks across her cheeks.
’Cassian... where are you...?’
Silence returned to the dungeon. For ten agonizing seconds, nothing moved.
Aurelia slowly pushed her trembling upper body off the floor with her newly fused hands. She let out a long shuddering gasp, daring to believe the nightmare had finally passed.
PRICK.
A tiny microscopic sensation touched the exact apex of her skull. It felt like nothing more than the gentle tap of a needle.
Aurelia’s golden eyes widened in instinctual dread as she slowly tilted her chin upward toward the ceiling.
SHIIIIING—!
A colossal vertical cleavage of conceptual force tore straight down through the center of her reality.
In less than a fraction of a second, Aurelia’s body was vertically bisected from the crown of her head, down through her nose, her neck, her sternum, and her pelvis.
SPLAT!
The two symmetrical halves of her body fell in opposite directions, collapsing heavily against the stone floor.
Blood erupted in a massive catastrophic deluge, and her internal organs spilled across the damp flagstones in a steaming tangled mess of gore.
Her consciousness did not fade into the mercy of death.
Even split in two, her dying brain registered the apocalyptic torment as the Argent Flame roared to life once more.

The incandescent silver fire erupted from both halves of her split spine, coiling like radiant blazing serpents around her scattered organs, dragging the two halves of her butchered body back together in an eternal, inescapable loop of forced resurrection.
...Immortality.
That was the true horrific secret hidden within the secondary phase of the Argent Flame of Transmutation.
The soldiers of humanity marching upon the battlefield were effectively immortal.

They could charge recklessly into the jaws of demonic monstrosities, suffer decapitations, lose limbs, and endure fatal strikes... and their wounds would simply vanish, their lifelines defying death itself because the Saintess locked in the dungeon endured their deaths for them.
The Argent Flame would never allow the vessel to perish.
It made the Saintess immortal, chaining her soul to an unending cycle of slaughter, torture, and resurrection so that others could claim the glory of war.
Miles away, across the blood-soaked plains of the Meolion Kingdom, the thunderous clatter of armored hooves shook the earth.
Cassian galloped at the head of the royal cavalry, his white warhorse surging effortlessly over the mounds of demonic corpses.
Standing before him was one of the colossal Demon Kings of the Blight... a towering behemoth of jagged obsidian armor and abyssal horns.
"Die, pathetic mortal!" the Demon King roared, thrusting its massive claw forward.

A monumental blast of concentrated, toxic black rot erupted from the demon’s palm, surging across the air like a tidal wave of pure death, slamming directly into Cassian’s chest with apocalyptic force.
Cassian didn’t even raise his shield. Hell, he didn’t even bother attempting to dodge.
A wide smirk stretched across his handsome face as he let the demonic blight engulf him completely.
"Rot does not affect me!"
The attack tore at his flesh for barely half a second.

A flash of pain sparked across his skin and then, with a soft hiss, the black rot vanished into thin air, replaced by a radiant burst of harmless white fire that cleanly knit his armor and flesh back to perfection.
"For I am the Hero!"
Far beneath the citadel, Aurelia’s lungs burned into ash before regenerating and on the surface, Cassian felt nothing.
"Is that all you have, beast?" Cassian laughed maniacally.
With a blinding triumphant sweep of his holy broadsword, Cassian cleaved straight through the Demon King’s neck, sending the massive obsidian head flying into the mud in a fountain of black blood.
The surrounding human vanguard erupted into a deafening, thunderous roar of worship.
"ALL HAIL THE HERO!"
"THE INVINCIBLE CHAMPION!"
Cassian sat atop his warhorse, bathed in the dying demon’s blood, his eyes glowing with craziness as he looked up at the sky.
’I...’ Cassian thought, a psychotic grin spreading across his face as the cheers of thousands washed over him. ’I truly am the Invincible Hero.’

A colossal vertical cleavage of conceptual force tore straight down through the center of her reality.
In less than a fraction of a second, Aurelia’s body was vertically bisected from the crown of her head, down through her nose, her neck, her sternum, and her pelvis.
SPLAT!
The two symmetrical halves of her body fell in opposite directions, collapsing heavily against the stone floor.
Blood erupted in a massive catastrophic deluge, and her internal organs spilled across the damp flagstones in a steaming tangled mess of gore.
Her consciousness did not fade into the mercy of death.
Even split in two, her dying brain registered the apocalyptic torment as the Argent Flame roared to life once more.

The incandescent silver fire erupted from both halves of her split spine, coiling like radiant blazing serpents around her scattered organs, dragging the two halves of her butchered body back together in an eternal, inescapable loop of forced resurrection.
...Immortality.
That was the true horrific secret hidden within the secondary phase of the Argent Flame of Transmutation.
The soldiers of humanity marching upon the battlefield were effectively immortal.

They could charge recklessly into the jaws of demonic monstrosities, suffer decapitations, lose limbs, and endure fatal strikes... and their wounds would simply vanish, their lifelines defying death itself because the Saintess locked in the dungeon endured their deaths for them.
The Argent Flame would never allow the vessel to perish.
It made the Saintess immortal, chaining her soul to an unending cycle of slaughter, torture, and resurrection so that others could claim the glory of war.
Miles away, across the blood-soaked plains of the Meolion Kingdom, the thunderous clatter of armored hooves shook the earth.
Cassian galloped at the head of the royal cavalry, his white warhorse surging effortlessly over the mounds of demonic corpses.
Standing before him was one of the colossal Demon Kings of the Blight... a towering behemoth of jagged obsidian armor and abyssal horns.
"Die, pathetic mortal!" the Demon King roared, thrusting its massive claw forward.

A monumental blast of concentrated, toxic black rot erupted from the demon’s palm, surging across the air like a tidal wave of pure death, slamming directly into Cassian’s chest with apocalyptic force.
Cassian didn’t even raise his shield.
Hell, he didn’t even bother attempting to dodge.
A wide smirk stretched across his handsome face as he let the demonic blight engulf him completely.
"Rot does not affect me!"
The attack tore at his flesh for barely half a second.

A flash of pain sparked across his skin and then, with a soft hiss, the black rot vanished into thin air, replaced by a radiant burst of harmless white fire that cleanly knit his armor and flesh back to perfection.
"For I am the Hero!"
Far beneath the citadel, Aurelia’s lungs burned into ash before regenerating and on the surface, Cassian felt nothing.
"Is that all you have, beast?" Cassian laughed maniacally.
With a blinding triumphant sweep of his holy broadsword, Cassian cleaved straight through the Demon King’s neck, sending the massive obsidian head flying into the mud in a fountain of black blood.
The surrounding human vanguard erupted into a deafening, thunderous roar of worship.
"ALL HAIL THE HERO!"
"THE INVINCIBLE CHAMPION!"
Cassian sat atop his warhorse, bathed in the dying demon’s blood, his eyes glowing with craziness as he looked up at the sky.
’I...’ Cassian thought, a psychotic grin spreading across his face as the cheers of thousands washed over him. ’I truly am the Invincible Hero.’

chapters.title: Chapter 425: Saintess Of The Argent Flame [III / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: And so that was how the nightmare continued.
For six long unrelenting years, humanity marched across the scorched reaches of the realm, butchering demon hordes in a war of total attrition.
And in the pitch-black subterranean bowels of the Meolion Kingdom, inside the damp stone crypt that had become the Prison of the Saintess, Aurelia was forced to endure death every single day.
Day after day... Month after month... Season after season...
She endured decapitations while sitting in total darkness.
She endured having her chest cleaved open while she was attempting to chew on stale crusts of bread.

She endured having her ribs caved in by siege-class abyssal bludgeons, her limbs torn from her sockets by feral fiends, her throat crushed by demonic fangs, and her lungs liquified by sulfurous necrotic flame.

Over and over again, tens of thousands of times, the Argent Flame coiled through her shattered flesh like living silver serpents, dragging severed tendons back together, welding splintered bone, sealing open arteries, and forcibly re-igniting her consciousness so that she could serve as the living shield for the next strike on the front lines.
Eventually, death stopped being a terrifying concept.
It stopped being an agony to fear. It became nothing more than a dull mechanical afterthought... an irritating interruption of the dark silence she sat in.
’Ah... another spear through the liver,’ She would think as blood filled her mouth in the dark. ’The third vanguard must be pushing through the marshlands.’
’My left leg just shattered into twelve pieces... The cavalry must have hit a trench.’
’My throat just tore open... Someone was ambushed in their sleep.’
The boundary of her torment did not stop at the edge of the battlefield.
During the fourth year of the endless campaign, an abyssal miasma seeped into the kingdom’s central aquifers and riverbeds.
It planted insidious seeds of necrotic soul-rot into the spiritual veins of every living human within the realm’s borders.
It did not kill instantly, but rather ate away at their life-force, threatening to turn the entire populace into decaying husks.

To prevent the collapse of society, the High Council and the Grand Patriarch forced Aurelia to cast a kingdom-wide web of the Argent Flame, tethering her soul directly to the life-force of every single citizen across the provinces.
From that moment on, her hell evolved into an unbearable cacophony of borrowed misery.

She was no longer just paying the blood-debt of the warriors facing demons on the front lines. She became the living receptacle for every scrap of physical violence, sickness, and mundane agony that occurred across the entire empire.
If a drunken blacksmith got into a tavern brawl in the Upper Ward and had his jaw broken, Aurelia’s teeth cracked in the dark, her mouth filling with coppery blood.
If a thief was captured in the slums and flogged with barbed leather, the lacerations mirrored themselves with searing precision across Aurelia’s back, peeling her skin to the bone.

If a laborer in the northern quarries was crushed beneath a falling boulder, Aurelia’s pelvis snapped, pinning her to the damp floor as her bones violently ground together until the silver fire forced them into place.
Even the smallest cruelties... a child being beaten by a cruel master, a merchant cutting his finger on glass, a soldier stubbing his toe against an iron chest reverberated into her flesh.
She lived in a permanent state of being mutilated, burned, crushed, and regenerated without a single second of peace.
And yet, eventually, humanity finished the war. The demonic hordes were wiped from the face of the world.
And today... today was meant to be quite a glorious day.
SCREEECH!
The heavy rusted iron hinges of the outermost dungeon gate groaned loudly in the gloom.

A royal guard pushed his way down the winding stone corridor, his iron-plated boots clattering against the slick steps. But the moment his hand shoved open the thick timber door of the inner cell, what hit him first was the smell.
It was a suffocating wall of stench.

The royal sanitation crews and prison attendants had long since stopped cleaning the deep cells; no one had set foot down here in over two years because the priests declared the room "spiritually toxic."
The air was a humid stagnant swamp of rotting biological waste, old coagulated blood, dried vomit, and the nauseatingly sweet, coppery odor of burnt flesh and constant regenerations.
The stone floor was slick with layers of dried and re-melted crimson fluids that had pooled and dried into black tar-like crusts across the flagstones.
The guard instinctively gagged, coughing violently into his armored gauntlet as his eyes watered from the pure toxicity of the air.
"By the gods..." the guard wheezed, stepping into the gloom with his hand resting on the hilt of his broadsword.
He raised his lantern, letting the yellow light wash over the corner of the cell. Sitting on the filth-encrusted stone, slumped against the damp wall, was Aurelia.
She looked utterly grotesque.
The radiant, golden-haired beauty who had once been the revered High Saintess of the realm was completely gone, replaced by a hollow emaciated husk.
Her skin was a translucent sickly gray, pulled so tightly over her visible ribcage and hip bones that she looked like a skeleton wrapped in paper.
Thick pale-silver scars covered every single square inch of her exposed flesh... a chaotic horrifying mosaic of thousands of healed lacerations, missing patches of skin, and deep burn marks.
Her matted platinum hair was caked with grime and old blood, hanging over her face in greasy tangled knots.
The guard looked down at her with unfiltered disgust, curling his lip in open contempt.
"Look at you," the guard sneered, his voice echoing off the stone walls. "A filthy, wretched creature rotting in her own filth. You look like a demon that crawled out of the bottom of an open sewer."
Aurelia did not answer as she could not see the guard’s face... she could not see the yellow glow of his lantern either.
Aurelia was blind.
Years ago, during one of the great battles against an abyssal demon lord, an invisible blade of demonic energy had cleaved across Cassian’s eyes in a blinding horizontal arc.

When the Argent Flame had violently pulled the fatal wound across the soul-link, the silver fire had attempted to regenerate her shredded retinas while simultaneously burning through a massive influx of abyssal venom.
The chaotic clash of divine fire and demonic corruption had burned her optical nerves into charred ash, leaving her retinas completely milky-white and hollow.
She had lived in pitch-black darkness ever since.
The guard stepped forward, his heavy boots splashing through the dark residue on the floor. He reached down, unhooking the heavy iron chain that bound the rusted collar around her throat.
"Get up, freak," he barked.
Without an ounce of gentleness, he gave the iron chain a savage upward yank, hauling her bodily off the stone floor by her neck.
Aurelia’s bare, scarred feet dragged against the flagstones.

Her joints popped and groaned under her frail weight, but not a single sound of complaint escaped her lips. She simply let herself be dragged forward, moving like a corpse being hauled to a disposal pit.
He pulled her up the long spiraling staircase, through the heavy iron portcullises, and into the torchlit upper garrison.

"Take this garbage," the male guard grunted, shoving the end of her chain into the hands of two female guards who were waiting in the clean tiled anteroom. "Wash the stench off her before she makes the whole palace vomit."
The two female guards took hold of Aurelia’s bony arms, leading her down a bright, polished corridor and into an expansive dressing chamber filled with steaming bronze tubs and clean linens.

"Today is the day all of your suffering finally ends, Saintess," the first female guard said as she unhooked the chain from her collar, her voice surprisingly gentle, carrying a strange hollow tone of pity.

"That’s right," the second female guard chimed in, pouring a bucket of warm, rose-scented water over Aurelia’s trembling shoulders. "The war is over... The demons are extinct and today, you are going to be celebrated by the entire kingdom."
Aurelia said nothing.
She stood motionless in the warm water, listening to the soft splashes and the rustle of coarse linen as the two women began stripping away the rotting rags that clung to her dried wounds.
She felt the sponges scraping against her scarred collarbones, her emaciated thighs, and her sunken ribs.
As they washed her, the two women couldn’t help but whisper to each other, their voices carrying clearly in the quiet room.

"Look at her body..." the first guard murmured, running a cloth over a brutal, jagged scar that ran from Aurelia’s shoulder to her hip. "She’s so thin... It’s horrifying. Remember when she was crowned Saintess? She was the most breathtaking, voluptuous beauty in the entire realm. Noble lords wrote songs about her figure. Now... she looks so ugly and broken it’s not even a joke. There isn’t a single spot on her skin that isn’t ruined by scars."
"She looks like a patchwork doll that was ripped apart and sewn back together a thousand times," the other woman agreed in a low somber whisper.
Aurelia said nothing.
Her physical eyes were dead, but her internal spiritual sense... sharpened into a razor-thin diagnostic tool through six years of enduring soul-trauma mapped out the room with terrifying precision.

She could perceive the subtle mana signatures of the two guards, the warmth of the hearth, the texture of the fine silk robes they draped over her damp frame, and the careful hurried motions of their hands as they combed through her tangled platinum hair.
They were genuinely trying to make her look pretty.
One of the attendants stepped in front of her, opening a small jar of scented white powder.
With a careless jab of a velvet puff, she slammed the cosmetic powder directly onto Aurelia’s hollow cheek, sending a cloud of fragrant chalk into her nose and mouth.
Aurelia let out a sharp cough with her dry throat convulsing.
"Ah! I am so sorry, Saintess!" the woman gasped, frantically patting her chest and waving the air clean. "I didn’t mean to do that!"

They continued their work, their hands smoothing perfumed oils into her skin, lining her lips with red paste, and carefully arranging her long platinum-blonde hair into neat, flowing waves over the shoulders of an immaculate pristine white dress.
Even the heavy iron collar that had bitten into her neck for six years was unlatched and cast aside, leaving her throat bare and unencumbered.
A dark fragile thought flickered through the cold embers of Aurelia’s shattered mind.
’Is this really it...? Is the nightmare truly over...? Will I finally see Cassian again...?’
A wave of pure venomous ice pooled in the bottom of her stomach, burning with an intensity hotter than any fire she had ever absorbed.

’When I meet him...’ Aurelia thought, her fingers subtly curling against the smooth silk of her skirt. ’When I stand before him and hear his voice... I will not thank him. I will not weep with joy. I will curse him to the deepest, most agonizing pits of hell. I will curse him, I will curse the Grand Patriarch, I will curse the King, and I will curse every single citizen who slept peacefully in their beds while I died ten thousand deaths in the dark. I will curse all of them...’
"You are ready," the female guards announced, draping a heavy velvet-lined travel cloak over her shoulders and pulling a deep hood over her face to conceal her milky-white eyes.
They escorted her out of the palace garrison and into the open courtyard.
The crisp morning air hit her skin, carrying the scent of fresh pine and distant woodsmoke... scents she had not smelled in six agonizing years.
She was helped up the wooden steps into a luxurious, enclosed carriage, the velvet curtains pulled shut against the outside world.

"It is going to be a wondrous, unforgettable celebration," the guard captain assured her through the carriage window as the iron-shod wheels began to turn, clattering over the smooth cobblestones of the capital. "The entire city is waiting to greet you..."
Aurelia said nothing.
She sat perfectly still on the cushioned leather seat, feeling the sway of the carriage as it navigated the winding streets.
The distant sound of thousands of voices began to bleed through the wooden carriage walls... a massive roaring ocean of sound that grew louder with every passing second.
Suddenly, a horrific suffocating sensation clamped down upon her throat.
"Gah!"

It was not a physical blade or a reflected wound. It was a potent and colorless alchemical gas that had been secretly funneled into the enclosed carriage through hidden runic vents beneath the seating.
Aurelia’s breath seized in her chest. Her throat closed up, her spiritual sense spun into chaotic static, and her weakened body went completely limp.
The darkness swallowed her whole as she slumped against the carriage cushions, losing consciousness.
CLANG!
The heavy sound of an iron latch locking into place echoed in her ears.

Aurelia gasped, her consciousness violently snapping back into reality as the lingering effects of the paralytic gas were burned away by the natural, defensive reaction of the Argent Flame in her blood.
She tried to move, but her limbs were completely immobilized.
She was kneeling on a raised wooden platform.

Heavy, cold, high-grade suppression chains were wrapped securely around her wrists, her ankles, her waist, and her neck, bolting her frail, kneeling frame directly to the thick oak timbers beneath her knees.
Above her, resting against the nape of her neck, she could feel the cold heavy shadow of an iron bracket which was the guide-rail of a massive executioner’s block.
And surrounding the scaffold was a crowd of unimaginable scale.
Tens of thousands of people filled the grand royal plaza.
The noise was an earth-shaking roar... a deafening cacophony of bloodthirsty screams, violent jeers, and furious stomping that shook the very foundations of the execution platform.
Through her spiritual sense, Aurelia recognized them.

chapters.title: Chapter 426: Saintess Of The Argent Flame [IV / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Aurelia recognized their soul-frequencies and she recognized their spiritual mana. She of course recognized the unique patterns of the wounds she had healed within their flesh.
Directly or indirectly, she had touched every single soul in this crowd.
She had shared her sacred Argent Flame throughout the entire kingdom, absorbing their diseases, their broken bones, their demonic rot, and their fatal wounds for six straight years...
...And now, every single one of them was screaming for her blood.
"DEATH TO THE WITCH!"
"EXECUTE THE MONSTER!"
"CLEANSE THE REALM OF THE DEMONIC PARASITE!"
Aurelia’s lips shrank, pulling tight against her teeth in cold paralyzed silence.
Suddenly, the deafening roar of the mob shifted, turning into a thunderous reverent cheer that parted the crowd like the sea.
Authoritative, heavy footsteps echoed across the wooden scaffold.
Walking onto the platform, bathed in the brilliant light of the midday sun and clad in dazzling, gold-embossed divine plate armor, was Cassian.
The Otherworldly Hero looked magnificent.
His silver hair caught the light like polished steel, his handsome face radiating unshakeable righteousness as he held the delicate silk-clad hand of the Crown Princess.
Cassian stepped to the center of the platform, raising his free hand toward the roaring masses.
A heroic smile graced his lips as he gently let go of the Princess’s hand and addressed the gathered empire.

"People of Meolion! Brave citizens of the Light!" Cassian’s voice boomed across the plaza, amplified by magic until it vibrated in the chest of every man, woman, and child. "Calm yourselves! Today marks the final victory of our grand crusade!"
The crowd’s roar died down to a breathless, worshipful silence as tens of thousands hung on his every word.
Cassian turned slowly, pointing his gleaming gauntleted finger directly down at Aurelia’s kneeling, chained form.

"For six long years, you were led to believe that this woman was a holy Saintess!" Cassian proclaimed, his voice dripping with sorrowful disgust. "You believed she was a blessed maiden sent by the heavens to heal your wounds! But today, the Crown must lay bare the horrific unspeakable truth!"
Aurelia listened, her scarred body perfectly still beneath the iron chains.

"She is no Saintess!" Cassian roared, his eyes blazing with false righteousness. "She is an ancient shape-shifting Demon Noble captured during the early days of the rift! It was her demonic blood that allowed her to manipulate the foul Demon Rot, forcing the abyssal corruption to bow to her dark will! The Crown and the Church kept her chained beneath the earth, forcing the beast to use her foul magic to cure the very poisons her demonic brethren inflicted upon our kingdom!"
Aurelia’s lips shrank into a thin tight line with her brow furrowing slightly.

"She played the martyr to deceive us all!" Cassian shouted, his voice reaching a fever pitch. "She sought to plant her dark corruption deep within our souls so she could devour the kingdom once the war was won! But the sacred power of the Argent Flame is a holy primordial miracle meant exclusively for the true, pure Saintess of the Light! By executing this demonic imposter today, the holy flame will be liberated from her wretched corrupted flesh... reincarnating into a pure righteous maiden of our kingdom who will deliver us into an era of eternal divine prosperity!"
Silence hung heavy over the grand plaza for three long agonizing seconds.
Kneeling on the scaffold, Aurelia almost felt like laughing out loud.

’A demon...?’ she thought, the absurdity of the lie ringing in her ears like shattered glass. ’He called me a demon. The man I bled for... the man whose severed chest I knitted back together while screaming in the mud... is telling the entire world I was a monster all along. Who could possibly be stupid enough to believe such an obvious, pathetic lie—’
"GLORY TO THE HERO!"
A lone voice erupted from the front row of the noble gallery.
"KILL THE DEMON!"
"BEHEAD THE HERETIC!"
"DEATH TO THE WITCH!"
And within the span of a single heartbeat, the entire city of Meolion exploded into a bloodthirsty roar.
Tens of thousands of voices screamed in unified ecstatic approval, throwing stones, rotten food, and curses toward the scaffold.
Aurelia’s lips slowly, unconsciously curved upward into a wide hollow smile.

’Of course...’ she thought, her heart freezing into solid unbreakable obsidian. ’Of course they believe it. They don’t care about the truth. They just want an excuse to wash their hands of the blood they made me bleed.’
She turned her blind, milky-white gaze toward Cassian.
The Otherworldly Hero was standing at the edge of the platform, his arms raised high as he actively led the cheers of the mob, his handsome face twisted into an expression of triumphant ecstasy.
It was deeply painful.

The very man who had promised her under the stars that he would save her, that he would take her away from the corrupt church, that he would marry her and build a peaceful life where she would never have to bleed again... was the one leading the charge to slaughter her like an animal.
And standing next to him on the scaffold, the Crown Princess was holding a newborn infant wrapped in pure silk.
Aurelia’s spiritual perception locked onto the child.
’Ah...’ Aurelia recognized the soul-frequency instantly.

Months ago, during a bitter winter night, the royal physicians had rushed a dead, stillborn infant down into the dark dungeon, weeping and begging the Saintess to channel the Argent Flame to jump-start the child’s heart.
Aurelia had endured the agonizing sensation of having her own heart stopped and restarted three times in the dark to breathe life into the baby’s lungs.
And now, perceiving the subtle familial mana flowing between the child, the Princess, and Cassian, the final crushing truth clicked into place.
The child was Cassian’s daughter.
The Otherworldly Hero had bedded the Princess, fathered a royal heir, and replaced Aurelia entirely while she was rotting in chains beneath his feet.
A soundless chuckle bubbled up from Aurelia’s throat.
"Executioner!" Cassian commanded, turning his back on her with absolute, chilling dismissal. "Proceed! Let her blood water the dawn of our new empire!"
A towering executioner clad in black leather stepped forward, his massive arms hoisting a colossal, two-handed executioner’s greataxe high into the midday air.
"Die, beast," the executioner grunted.
With all his immense physical strength, the executioner brought the heavy steel blade down in a whistling, vertical cleave directly aimed at the back of Aurelia’s exposed neck.
CLANG! SHATTER!
An ear-splitting metallic screech echoed across the entire plaza.

The massive steel blade did not cut her flesh. The moment the hardened edge struck the pale skin of Aurelia’s neck, the metal violently shattered into a thousand jagged iron fragments, exploding outward like shrapnel.
The executioner flinched backward in terror, clutching his bleeding stinging forearms as he stared at the broken wooden haft in his hands.
Aurelia remained kneeling, entirely unharmed.
Her milky-white eyes were closed, and from beneath her pale eyelids, thick streams of liquid starlight and bright crimson blood leaked slowly down her cheeks.
...Yet, she was not crying.
Her thin scarred face was stretched into a wide terrifying grin, showing her pearlescent white teeth to the horrified crowd.

"I expected all of you to do something like this..." Aurelia whispered, her raspy voice cutting through the silence of the scaffold with supernatural clarity. "...Which is why I prepared a gift for you all."
Aurelia opened her eyes.
Her milky-white irises flared with an incandescent silver-white luminescence that washed over the entire plaza.
The executioner... a veteran soldier whose shattered collarbone and severed lung Aurelia had healed during the third year of the war suddenly froze.
His face completely drained of all color as a horrific, burning sensation erupted across his entire torso.
SCHLICK! CRACK!
Without warning, dozens of violent, invisible wounds violently tore open across the executioner’s body.
Slashes appeared out of thin air, ripping his chest plate apart.
His left arm was sheared off at the shoulder.

His right leg was severed at the knee and his head was cleanly sliced from his neck, spinning into the air in a geyser of blood, before his severed torso split down the center, his heart cleaving in two as his shattered soul dissolved into pure spiritual mana and flowed directly into Aurelia’s glowing core.
Aurelia’s manic grin widened.
The divine suppression chains wrapped around her body began to groan, fracturing into spiderweb cracks under the pressure of the ancient magic waking within her veins.
The Argent Flame had always allowed wounds to reflect upon the Saintess’s flesh to grant others life.

But what if she didn’t heal them? What if she simply kept all of those wounds, all of that poison, all of that rot, and all of those deaths contained within a single quarantined corner of her soul... and then, through the indestructible soul-links forged over six years, violently reversed the flow?
Would that work?
The answer was simple.
"Return."
The single quiet word fell from Aurelia’s lips like the decree of a vengeful god.
BOOM!
In a fraction of a second, the concept of mirrored death reversed across the entire kingdom.
A catastrophic slaughter erupted across the city of Meolion and everywhere else at once.
In the royal viewing box, the King’s chest violently caved inward, his ribs shattering through his lungs as an old siege wound returned to crush him.
The Grand Patriarch let out a blood-curdling shriek as his entire circulatory system turned to black boiling sludge, consumed instantly by the demon rot he had once begged Aurelia to purge.
On the execution scaffold, Cassian’s eyes widened in apocalyptic terror.
"A-Aurelia—?!"
SHING! SHING! SPLURT!
Before the Otherworldly Hero could draw his broadsword, hundreds of invisible overlapping lacerations sheared through his divine plate armor.
His arms were severed at the elbows. His chest was torn open from collarbone to pelvis, his organs spilling into the dirt.
A tidal wave of concentrated demon rot erupted from his bone marrow, dissolving his flesh into black slime in less than two seconds.
The Crown Princess and her infant beside him were consumed in the exact same breath, their lifelines severed by the return of their borrowed health.
Across the streets, tens of thousands of citizens and soldiers dropped dead simultaneously.
Some were decapitated by phantom blades, others collapsed as their hearts burst, and thousands more dissolved into pools of sulfurous rot.
Within thirty seconds, the deafening cheers of the capital were replaced by suffocating silence.
Not a single soul remained alive in the entire kingdom...
Only Aurelia sat on the scaffold, surrounded by a boundless sea of corpses.
PIT-PAT! PIT-PAT!
A cold heavy rain began to fall from the darkening sky, washing the blood from the wooden planks.
Aurelia collapsed forward onto her hands and knees in the pooling crimson, her breath rattling in her chest.
’I did it...’ she thought, her fingers digging into the wet wood. ’...I killed all my enemies. Every single one of them.’
Yet, her vengeance brought no warmth, no joy, and no salvation. There was only a cold hollow emptiness echoing in her soul.
VUUUUUUM!
Through the falling rain, the sky above the dead capital shattered like brittle glass, and the space between the clouds violently caved inward.
"What?"

A colossal terrifying entity descended from the fractured heavens. It possessed no definite mortal form... it was an undulating shifting mass of celestial authority, folding endlessly upon itself with interlocking halos of blinding cold light.
The unfathomable pressure radiating from its descent flattened the rain, crushing the marble columns and stone buildings of the city into fine powder under its mere presence.
Kneeling in the sea of blood, Aurelia felt a deep primal terror grip every fiber of her being.

She frantically expanded her spiritual sense, desperately trying to channel her mana outward to estimate the creature’s boundaries, its core, or even its tier but the moment her mana touched the entity, it dissolved into nothingness.
The power looming above her was utterly beyond measurement.
Trembling violently, Aurelia weakly pushed her blood-soaked hands against the scaffold timbers, forcing herself up as she cried out to the sky.

"Why...?" her cracked, raspy voice trembled with raw weeping fury. "Where were you?! For six years, I bled in the dark! For six years, they butchered me, chained me, and tore my limbs apart while you watched in silence! Why do you descend only now?!"
The shifting mass did not care for her tears... It did not listen.𝚏𝗿𝗲𝐞𝐰𝚎𝕓𝐧𝚘𝘃𝗲𝐥.𝐜𝚘𝕞
"AURELIA EL MIMONTE."
The entity’s voice reverberated directly inside her skull... a deafening sound like grinding tectonic plates that made her eardrums bleed.
"YOU ARE FOUND GUILTY OF UNLAWFUL MASS GENOCIDE AND THE TOTAL ANNIHILATION OF AN ENTIRE MORTAL REALM."
’An entire Mortal realm...?’
How was it her fault that these people had not only gone to war with the Demons but other Kingdoms as well and they were the last surviving one?
"They betrayed me!" Aurelia screamed desperately, clutching her throat. "They were going to execute me after I gave them my life! Hear me... listen to my side!"
"JUSTIFICATION IS IRRELEVANT TO THE COSMIC ORDER," the booming law droned, completely deaf to her pleas. "YOUR SOUL IS STRIPPED OF PROVIDENCE. YOU ARE HEREBY SENTENCED TO ETERNAL CONFINEMENT WITHIN—"
The entity spoke the sacred ancient name of the penitentiary realm, but the syllables were far too heavy for mortal ears.
To Aurelia, the pronunciation did not register as words... it tore through her mind as a violent ear-splitting screech of static and deafening white noise.
BZZZZZZT... KZZZZT!
Reality tore open beneath her knees, and before she could draw another breath, a blinding vortex of cosmic compression swallowed her into the eternal dark.
When Aurelia finally opened her eyes, the rain, the blood, and the corpses were gone.
She was lying upon a slab of cold white marble floating in an endless pitch-black sea of raw ether.
Leaning over her, gently dabbing a glowing alchemical salve across the mirrored scars on her throat, was an ancient frail woman with silver hair and withered gentle hands.
Aurelia weakly looked up at her, her voice trembling.
"Who... who are you...? Where is this place...?"
The old woman smiled softly, her eyes filled with boundless tragic compassion as she smoothed back Aurelia’s platinum hair.
"Rest, child," the old woman whispered gently. "You are safe now. Our Savior... our true Savior is coming for us. We must only endure until he arrives..."
’Haah...’
Aurelia gave her head a slow weary shake, forcefully pulling her consciousness out of the suffocating swamp of old memories.

chapters.title: Chapter 427: Welcome To Blessed Land, Aurelia [I / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: She let out a dry ragged breath into the cold ether of the void, her trembling hand resting against the rough dirt of the grave beside her.
Those memories were so exhausting to live through.

Every time she allowed her mind to wander down the corridors of her past, she felt the phantom sting of the guillotine, the cold splatter of the rain, and the deafening cheers of a city that had bayed for her execution.
She lowered her blind milky-white gaze toward the dirt.
The old woman had spent her final centuries burning through her own divine lifeforce just to tend to Aurelia’s spiritual wounds and stabilize her shattered meridians.
The old Saintess had done so because of an unyielding belief...
She insisted that when the prophesied Savior finally pierced through the boundaries of the void, the extraction would only possess enough dimensional anchor to retrieve a single soul.
The old woman had willingly chosen to fade into dust so that Aurelia would be the one rescued.
Aurelia had asked her countless times how she knew of this "Savior."
The old woman had simply smiled, tapping her temple, and said she heard celestial whispers echoing through the cosmic currents whenever the great outer gates shifted.
Given that the old woman had been imprisoned in this dimensional wasteland for over five hundred years before Aurelia’s arrival, Aurelia had simply accepted it without argument.
’And yet... here I sit,’ Aurelia thought, her fingers digging lightly into the soil. ’Sitting on a rock with all these useless skills and an absurd level, completely in vain.’
Over the centuries, Aurelia and the old Saintess had fought tooth and nail to secure this floating marble island... the largest stable landmass in the local sector.

It had taken decades of agonizing bloody skirmishes using the Argent Flame to purge the void fiends, culminating in Aurelia single-handedly slaying an ancient high-tier ether monstrosity that had attempted to devour their sanctuary.
She had fought, she had leveled, and she had survived.
And for what?
Aurelia slowly slinked backward, letting her slender, scarred back rest against the cold stone of the grave mound. She stared up into the infinite starless dark.
"I don’t want to believe..." she whispered aloud to the empty void, her voice barely becoming a breath.
She didn’t want to believe in heroes... She didn’t want to believe in saviors either.
Aurelia didn’t want to open her heart to another golden promise only to be chained in another dark dungeon and butchered for someone else’s glory.
’...But at the same time...’
A small pathetic shudder ran through her chest.
’...I really don’t want to stay here anymore.’
She was so utterly tired.
In her entire mortal life and her centuries in the void, she had never known a single day of genuine peace.
She had never known what it felt like to sleep without fear, to eat without poison, or to be touched without someone trying to extract her power.
Why was her existence defined entirely by suffering? What had she done to the universe to deserve this perpetual damnation?
She closed her eyes, resigning herself to the fragile hope she had spent centuries trying to kill.
If this mysterious Savior truly existed... how much longer would it take for them to find this forgotten corner of the abyss?
If they ever arrived, Aurelia swore she would not be a foolish, naive girl again.
She would not blindly fall in love or offer unconditional devotion like she had with Cassian. She would be sharp, transactional, and calculating.
She would trade her abilities for safety, extracting every ounce of comfort and security she could possibly gain from thi—
PING!
A melodic chime resonated directly against the core of her soul and Aurelia completely froze.
Before her unseeing eyes, a glowing semi-transparent system interface flared to life within the dark void.
Aurelia could not see physical light, but her spiritual perception instantly mapped out the dense mana that formed the radiant golden letters.
[You have been summoned to serve as a Hero for a Lord.]
[ Y / N ]
A breathless silence gripped the floating marble island.
Aurelia sat motionless, her milky-white eyes trembling behind her closed eyelids as her mind struggled to process the reality of the golden glyphs.
’A Hero... for a Lord? Is this Lord... my Savior?’
Her slender, scarred finger trembled as she raised her hand through the cold ether. With a slow, deliberate motion, she tapped the glowing golden [ Y ].
HUMMMMM!
A secondary prompt flashed across her consciousness.
[Your level will be forcefully reset from Level 999 —> Level 1. You will lose some of your Priority Skills; however, you will retain the remaining foundation of your Mythic Skill Tree.]
Aurelia stared at the warning with a hollow smirk.
’Level reset...?’ she thought. ’I would gladly give up every single level and every single skill if it meant being freed from the horrific curse of this Argent Flame.’
Yet, a sharp resolve hardened within her chest.
’No...’ she corrected herself. ’It is precisely because I possess the power of the Argent Flame that I can negotiate a better life with this new Lord. I will use this flame to secure my safety.’
Aurelia raised her chin, her voice ringing out with conviction into the empty void:
"Yes. Please... get me out of here."
CRACK!
The immutable laws of reality shattered around the marble island.
A massive blinding pillar of golden light descended from the heavens, tearing through the fabric of the Great Void.
Space folded, the ether dissolved, and Aurelia’s physical form disintegrated into a brilliant swirl of starlight, vanishing entirely from the dimensional purgatory.
In the center of the Blessed Land’s grand courtyard, the towering pillar of light erupting from the Archway reached its apex.
The ground vibrated with a deep soothing hum of pure mana, sending gentle ripples across the surface of the central aqueduct.
The falling snowflakes were instantly vaporized by the radiant golden warmth radiating from the dais.
Silas took a half-step backward, raising his forearm to shield his eyes from the blinding glare as the spatial vortex between the twin white pillars began to slow its furious spin.
Beside him, Eluned’s emerald eyes narrowed with razor-sharp scrutiny, her hand resting against the pulsing Tear of the Slumbering World at her chest.

On his other side, Morwenna casually leaned her weight onto her back foot, her leather-clad hand resting firmly on Tidebringer’s hilt, her stormy gray eyes scanning the swirling mist with dangerous focus.
WHOOSH!
The golden light gradually subsided, condensing into soft, drifting particles that scattered across the marble steps.
Standing in the center of the invocation circle was a woman.
She was completely naked.
Her long, magnificent hair was a cascade of pure, shimmering platinum-blonde that tumbled over her pale shoulders, barely veiling the soft curves of her breasts and slender waist.
Her facial features were sculpted with breathtaking ethereal perfection which made her look delicate and undeniably gorgeous.
Yet, as Silas’s blue eyes swept over her, a heavy lump formed in his throat.
Her fair, porcelain skin was marred from head to toe.

Thin, pale, silver-white scars crisscrossed her forearms, her collarbones, her ribs, and her thighs... these were etched reminders of thousands of brutal lacerations and fatal wounds that had long since healed.
Her eyes, staring blankly ahead into the night sky, were completely milky-white and hollow.
She was blind.
Before Silas could speak or summon a blanket from his inventory, the platinum-haired woman slowly sank to her knees upon the cold marble of the dais.
She clasped her slender, scarred hands together against her bare chest, bowing her head so low her platinum hair brushed the stone.
"I thank you... for delivering me from the dark, my Lord," Aurelia spoke, her voice carrying a soft tone that trembled with a delicate mixture of fragile hope and deeply guarded calculation.
She slowly tilted her blind face upward, her unseeing milky-white eyes pointing in the general direction of Silas’s aura.

"I possess the power of the Argent Flame," Aurelia continued, her voice steadying into a solemn formal proposal. "I can grant you absolute immortality, my Lord... Even though enduring your deaths will tear my flesh and bring me unimaginable agony, I am willing to bear it all for you."
Aurelia paused, her chapped lips pressing together before she delivered her terms.
"However... if you wish for me to grant you this power... I would like to strike a deal."
The heavy, oppressive silence that followed her words hung over the marble dais like an iron shroud.
Kneeling on the cold stone, her forehead nearly brushing the ground and her trembling hands clasped tightly against her bare chest, Aurelia waited.
Every second that ticked past in suffocating quiet felt like an eternity stretched across the blade of a guillotine.
’Did I say something wrong...?’ she thought, panic coiling tightly within her throat. ’Did I insult him? Was my tone too insolent for a newly summoned servant?’
Her mind raced through the fractured corridors of her memories, desperately trying to calculate what this new master could possibly want from her.
All she possessed in this universe was the Argent Flame of Transmutation.
All she had to offer to any ruler, kingdom, or deity was the terrifying gift of stolen immortality... an eternity of victory purchased through the continuous butcher’s bill carved into her own flesh.
If this Lord did not want her flame, then what else could he possibly desire?
’...Is he after my body?’
A hollow self-deprecating thought flickered through her consciousness.

In the mortal realm of Meolion, she had often overheard the noblewomen and high-born priestesses complaining bitterly in the cathedral gardens, weeping that men were shallow creatures who viewed them as nothing more than decorative flesh and vessels for their desires.
Yet, throughout her entire six years of torture in the dark crypts, not a single man had ever looked upon Aurelia with lust.
No guard had ever laid a hand on her with desire; they had only dragged her by the neck like livestock.

’Perhaps... because I am not beautiful,’ Aurelia mused bitterly, remembering the horrific mosaic of raised jagged scars and missing patches of skin crisscrossing her emaciated ribs, thighs, and collarbones. ’A broken, scarred monster covered in burns and dead tissue could never entice a person. If he wants my flesh to use and discard, I would not mind... I would endure it willingly if it meant I would not be cast back into the void.’
FLUTTER!
A soft cold prickle touched the bare skin of her shoulder. Then another touched her collarbone, melting into tiny beads of moisture.
Aurelia’s unseeing eyes widened behind her closed eyelids. She did not recognize this sensation.
In the dry, sun-baked plains of the Meolion Kingdom, it had never snowed.
In the suffocating pitch-black cells beneath the capital, there had only been damp rot and stagnant humidity.
And in the Great Void, the ambient ether was an arid breathless vacuum. She had never felt frost fall from the heavens.
Before the chill could seep into her meridians—
SWOOSH!
Something thick and immensely warm descended over her shoulders.

It was a broad finely woven mantle lined with soft insulated fur. The garment settled gently over her frame, shielding her bare chest, covering her scarred waist, and wrapping her shivering body in a protective cocoon of dry soothing heat.
"As of right now..." a calm and impossibly gentle male voice echoed from above her. "...you don’t need to give me anything."
Aurelia’s breath seized in her chest. Her throat went completely dry, parched as if she had swallowed desert sand.
’...What?’

She felt the rustle of the heavy fabric as the man reached down, his hands careful and deliberate as he pulled the edges of the cloak together over her trembling collarbones, fastening the clasp beneath her chin without letting his fingers linger or grasp.
Overwhelmed by instinct, Aurelia expanded her internal spiritual sense, channeling a microscopic pulse of mana through the air to map out the physical reality of the man standing before her.
The image that coalesced within her mind stole whatever breath remained in her lungs.
He was tall, broad-shouldered, and carried himself with an effortless presence that felt like an anchored mountain.

His features were sculpted with striking masculine perfection... a strong defined jawline, dark hair that moved gently with the evening wind, and eyes that held the deep crystalline clarity of an endless blue sky.
’He is... breathtaking,’ Aurelia thought, her heart giving a violent, uncoordinated thud against her ribs.

Compared to this man, the memory of Cassian... the silver-haired "Hero" whose handsome face she had once idolized under the stars looked like nothing more than a vulgar hollow riffraff scraped from an alleyway gutter.
There was no arrogance in this Lord’s posture after all... and yet, despite seeing her power, he had rejected the offer of the Argent Flame.

Fear flared up within her chest and she took a frantic half-step backward on her knees, the heavy cloak swirling around her bare legs as the lingering golden light of the Archway dissipated completely into the night.

"I know you want my power..." Aurelia rasped, her voice trembling with defensive desperation as she tilted her blind face upward. "Every Lord, every King, every summoner seeks the Argent Flame. They desire victory without consequence... So why are you saying all this? Why play these games with me?!"
