chapters.title: Chapter 428: Welcome To Blessed Land, Aurelia [II / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Silas did not lash out.
He did not draw a weapon, nor did he order his guards to bind her in chains for daring to raise her voice lie she expected.
Through her mana perception, Aurelia felt the subtle shift in his aura... the soft warm curve of his lips as a genuine reassuring smile formed on his face.
He stepped forward, closing the distance between them, and extended his right hand toward her in an open unthreatening gesture.
"My name is Silas Graves," he introduced himself softly, his voice cutting through the falling snow with crystal clarity. "I am the Lord of this territory. This place is known as the Blessed Land."
Silas paused, letting the words settle into the quiet courtyard before continuing with unwavering candor.

"I won’t lie to you and pretend otherwise... yes, I activated that summoning ticket because my domain needs powerful allies to stand against the dangers of this realm but in the Blessed Land, we don’t treat our people like disposable tools, and we don’t feed off each other’s misery. Here, everyone who stands under my banner is family."
Silas looked down at her frail, trembling form, his blue eyes softening with deep sorrow as he took in the pale scars visible at her neckline.

"And to be completely honest with you... I really can’t bear to see you like this. Look at you. You’re shivering, you’re exhausted, you’re starving, and you’re sitting naked out in the freezing snow. You don’t owe me a single thing. You don’t need to bleed for me, and you don’t need to barter your soul away just to earn the right to breathe."
He lowered his hand slightly, keeping it steady in the air between them and waiting patiently for her.
"Right now, you need a warm meal, a safe bed, and time to heal. If you can find it in yourself to trust me... take my hand. I promise you, I will make it worth your while."
Aurelia froze.
Her mind spun into a chaotic, agonizing tempest of conflicting emotions.
’Trust him...?’
The word echoed in the dark recesses of her mind like a poisonous curse.
The last time she had trusted a man... the last time she had believed a savior’s hollow promises under the night sky.
He had locked her in an iron cage, fed upon her agony for six years, and led the entire kingdom to celebrate her execution on a wooden scaffold.
Trust was a weakness. Trust was the knife that had slit her throat ten thousand times over.
’...And yet...’
She was blind and she was stripped of her levels. She was alone in an unfamiliar world, shivering beneath a fur cloak.
What choice did she truly have?
This man had pierced through the boundaries of the Great Void. He had shattered the cosmic chains that held her soul in purgatory.
He was the one the ancient Saintess had spoken of... the Savior the old woman had blabbed on and on about for centuries before fading into dust.
Aurelia swallowed the lump of raw emotion in her throat. Slowly, with fingers that shook uncontrollably, she reached out from beneath the thick folds of the fur mantle.
Her scarred, delicate fingertips brushed against his palm and then, Silas’s warm calloused fingers closed gently around her hand.
VUUUM!
A radiant wave of pure warmth surged up through her fingers, washing through her frozen meridians and melting the bitter chill that had gripped her soul for hundreds of years.
It was a warmth untainted by greed, malice, or hunger. It was simply the steady heat of a protector.
Tears finally welled up in the corners of Aurelia’s unseeing, milky-white eyes, spilling over her pale cheeks for the first time in centuries.
Silas gave her trembling hand a gentle, reassuring squeeze, his voice ringing with absolute certainty under the falling snow:
"Welcome to the Blessed Land, Aurelia."
The biting chill of the evening draft swept across the elevated marble dais of the Archway, swirling the fine dusting of snow around their boots.
Aurelia tried to rise from her kneeling position, but her emaciated legs, weakened by centuries of stasis and malnutrition, buckled violently beneath her.
Her center of gravity gave out, and a small choked gasp escaped her lips as her slender frame pitched forward toward the hard stone.
Before her knees could strike the marble, a strong calloused hand shot out, catching her securely around her waist and hauling her gently back against a broad chest.
Aurelia’s breath hitched in her throat.
Her bare shoulders pressed into the thick fabric of Silas’s robes, the heavy fur-lined mantle he had draped over her enveloping her in an unbroken cocoon of warmth.
Standing three paces back on the dais, both Eluned and Morwenna stiffened.
The World-Tree Goddess’s luminous emerald eyes narrowed into razor-thin slits, her pristine teeth gritting so tightly that the muscles in her jaw visibly flexed.
Beside her, Morwenna’s stormy gray eyes flared with a volatile spark, her fingers twitching against the leather wrap of Tidebringer’s hilt.
The territorial instinct to rip the new woman away from their Lord flared instantly between them like dry kindling catching a spark.

Yet, as both women took in the horrific, mosaic-like network of raised silver scars along the girl’s collarbones, her hollow cheeks, and the milky-white opacity of her unseeing eyes, the jealous venom died in their throats.
Neither of them moved... They were terrors, but they were not blind fools... They could see that the broken creature in their Lord’s arms was hanging on to reality by a thread.
Silas didn’t release his hold on Aurelia’s waist, keeping his footing solid as he turned his head toward the two women.

"Eluned, Morwenna," Silas spoke, his voice calm and remarkably gentle, lacking even a shred of harsh command. "I need your help right now. Head down to the Haven, find Kaelia, and have her prepare a massive tray of warm, nutrient-dense broth, fresh bread, and whatever restorative meats she has ready. Tell her it’s an emergency for a newly summoned sister."
Eluned blinked, her expression softening into solemn compliance as she gave a crisp nod. "Understood, Hubby."
"Aye, Captain," Morwenna grunted, rolling her shoulders. "We’ll have the cook whip up an entire feast in five minutes flat."
The two mythic powerhouses spun on their heels, practically sprinting down the marble steps side-by-side.
Even in their urgent departure, their mutual disdain couldn’t be entirely suppressed.
"Get your heavy sea-boots out of my side, pirate," Eluned hissed in an undertone, gliding an inch above the flagstones. "You’re kicking up slush like an uncivilized beast."
"Shut your leafy trap, tree-bitch, or I’ll trip you into the aqueduct before we reach the pantry," Morwenna snarled right back, though neither broke their rapid stride toward the Culinary Haven.
Silas let out a soft amused breath through his nose, shaking his head as their bickering faded into the distance.
He adjusted his arm beneath Aurelia’s shoulders, taking the majority of her weight so her bare feet barely had to push against the cold stones.
"Lean on me," Silas murmured into her ear. "I’ve got you."
Aurelia swallowed hard, nodding mutely. She pulled the fur mantle tighter around her front, letting herself be guided down the steps and onto the main paved boulevard of the territory.
As they walked through the quiet central courtyard, the crisp night air hummed with invigorating mana.
Aurelia expanded her internal spiritual perception, letting microscopic ripples of mana map out the surrounding environment.
Her mind spun with overwhelming disbelief.
There was no sulfurous choking stench of demonic miasma hanging in the air and there was no cold toxic vacuum of the Great Void suffocating her lungs either.
The atmosphere of this domain was astonishingly pure, dense with rich earth mana, vibrant life-force currents, and the protective glow of defensive arrays woven into the fortress walls.

’It feels... so peaceful,’ Aurelia thought, her battered heart fluttering with a fragile hesitant warmth. ’How can a territory in this world be this serene? How long has it been since I walked beneath stars that didn’t burn with malice...?’
A patrol of three Shieldmaidens clad in light mythril armor jogged down the intersecting pathway, their spears held at high port.
When the women caught sight of Silas supporting the naked, scarred, platinum-haired woman wrapped in his personal mantle, they immediately halted.
Seeing the grave, protective expression on their Lord’s face, the guards did not shout or raise their weapons in alarm.
They stood at rigid attention, offering crisp respectful salutes with their fists pressed to their chest plates.
"Lord Graves," the lead shieldmaiden acknowledged in a low disciplined murmur.
"At ease, girls," Silas replied with a warm, reassuring smile. "Keep the northern perimeter tight. We’ll have a new rotation up before dawn."
"Yes, my Lord!"
The patrol resumed their march without pressing or prying, their footsteps rhythmic and steady against the flagstones.
Aurelia absorbed the interaction with wide unseeing eyes.

’They didn’t flinch...’ she noted internally, her thoughts running in dizzying circles. ’They didn’t demand to know if I was a demon... They saw my scars, they saw me in his arms, and they simply trusted him and the way he spoke to them... it wasn’t the arrogant bark of a High Inquisitor or the manic shouting of Cassian. He treats them like people.’
A small defensive shudder coiled in her stomach.
’Is he truly this kind? Or is this an elaborate facade? Does he play the gentle ruler under the open sky, only to reveal the monster once the heavy iron gates slam shut behind us...?’
They arrived at the grand double doors of the Keep.
Silas pushed the heavy timber open with his shoulder, guiding her inside into the warm illuminated foyer.
The interior was vast, built from solid reinforced granite and polished dark timber, with crystal mana-lamps casting a warm, golden glow across the corridors.
Waiting near the base of the grand spiraling staircase, holding a wooden clipboard and adjusting her spectacles, was Kadi.
The sandy-haired Second Secretary looked up, her amber eyes widening slightly as she took in the sight of Silas supporting the fragile scarred woman.
"Kadi," Silas greeted, stopping at the landing. "Did you manage to prepare that guest suite on the second floor like I asked before I headed to the Archway?"

"Everything is fully prepared, Lord Silas," Kadi answered crisply, stepping forward with professional efficiency. "I personally aired out the room, laid fresh down-feather mattresses, and reinforced the thermal power on the hearth. Follow me, please."
Kadi turned, leading the way up the broad, carpeted stairs.
As they climbed, Aurelia’s heightened senses caught the distinct scents lingering in the grand Keep.
The air was rich with the exotic fragrance of multiple powerful women and walking ahead of them was this brown-robed secretary, whose earth mana was remarkably powerful.

’Every single woman living in this fortress is immensely powerful for their level,’ Aurelia realized with her breath turning shallow. ’They are all his subordinates... his Heroes. And they live here freely with no chains and no suppression collars. Could a man who surrounds himself with such fierce, unbroken warriors truly be a tyrant in the dark?’
They reached the second-floor landing, where Kadi pushed open a thick oak door, revealing an expansive luxurious bedchamber.
A large stone fireplace crackled with warm, dancing orange flames, casting a comforting glow over a massive four-poster bed piled high with plush silk pillows and heavy fur quilts.
A polished cedar wardrobe stood against one wall, and an adjacent door led into a private bathing chamber.
"Thank you, Kadi," Silas said warmly.
He carefully led Aurelia across the soft woolen rug, gently easing her down onto the edge of the plush mattress.
He knelt slightly before her, making sure the heavy mantle was still wrapped securely around her trembling shoulders.
"This is your room, Aurelia," Silas spoke softly, gesturing around the space. "It’s completely yours. No one enters without your permission. Can you see how it looks?"
Aurelia lowered her head, her platinum hair spilling over her face as she gave a small, self-deprecating shake of her head.
"No, my Lord," she rasped, her voice barely above a whisper. "I am blind. The nerves in my eyes were burned away by the Argent Flame years ago."
Silas blinked, a look of deep empathetic sorrow flashing across his handsome features.
"Oh... I’m sorry. Don’t worry about that right now. When Eluned gets back up here with your food, I’ll have her look at your eyes. Her life-force magic can regenerate almost anything."
Aurelia wanted to laugh.
A bitter, hollow chuckle rose in her chest.

’Regenerate the Argent Flame’s damage? The Argent Flame is an eternal law of transmutation. Nothing is more absolute than the fire that defies death... How could someone possibly heal what the divine flame destroyed?’
Yet, as she felt the gentle warmth of Silas’s hand resting near her knee, she couldn’t bring herself to mock him.
Instead, her lips trembled, and fresh clear tears began to leak uncontrollably from her unseeing milky-white eyes, tracing hot paths down her scarred cheeks.
Silas’s brow furrowed in concern.
"Hey... why are you crying? Is something hurting? Did I touch a wound?"

’Why does he have to be so damn nice...?’ Aurelia wept silently, her fingers gripping the edge of the mattress until her knuckles turned white. ’If someone like him existed in this universe... why wasn’t he the first person I met? Why did I have to spend so many years drowning in blood and centuries rotting in the void before someone spoke to me with kindness?’
Even now, the scarred walls around her heart fought desperately against the warmth, refusing to believe that such pure benevolence was real.
"I am not in pain, my Lord," Aurelia managed to choke out, wiping her face with the rough fur sleeve. "I am just... happy. It has been a very long time since someone offered me a bed."

He stepped forward, closing the distance between them, and extended his right hand toward her in an open unthreatening gesture.
"My name is Silas Graves," he introduced himself softly, his voice cutting through the falling snow with crystal clarity.
"I am the Lord of this territory.
This place is known as the Blessed Land."
Silas paused, letting the words settle into the quiet courtyard before continuing with unwavering candor.

"I won’t lie to you and pretend otherwise... yes, I activated that summoning ticket because my domain needs powerful allies to stand against the dangers of this realm but in the Blessed Land, we don’t treat our people like disposable tools, and we don’t feed off each other’s misery.
Here, everyone who stands under my banner is family."
Silas looked down at her frail, trembling form, his blue eyes softening with deep sorrow as he took in the pale scars visible at her neckline.
"And to be completely honest with you...
I really can’t bear to see you like this.
Look at you.
You’re shivering, you’re exhausted, you’re starving, and you’re sitting naked out in the freezing snow.
You don’t owe me a single thing.
You don’t need to bleed for me, and you don’t need to barter your soul away just to earn the right to breathe."
He lowered his hand slightly, keeping it steady in the air between them and waiting patiently for her.
"Right now, you need a warm meal, a safe bed, and time to heal.
If you can find it in yourself to trust me... take my hand.
I promise you, I will make it worth your while."
Aurelia froze.
Her mind spun into a chaotic, agonizing tempest of conflicting emotions.
’Trust him...?’
The word echoed in the dark recesses of her mind like a poisonous curse.
The last time she had trusted a man... the last time she had believed a savior’s hollow promises under the night sky.
He had locked her in an iron cage, fed upon her agony for six years, and led the entire kingdom to celebrate her execution on a wooden scaffold.
Trust was a weakness.
Trust was the knife that had slit her throat ten thousand times over.
’...And yet...’
She was blind and she was stripped of her levels.
She was alone in an unfamiliar world, shivering beneath a fur cloak.
What choice did she truly have?
This man had pierced through the boundaries of the Great Void.
He had shattered the cosmic chains that held her soul in purgatory.
He was the one the ancient Saintess had spoken of... the Savior the old woman had blabbed on and on about for centuries before fading into dust.
Aurelia swallowed the lump of raw emotion in her throat.
Slowly, with fingers that shook uncontrollably, she reached out from beneath the thick folds of the fur mantle.
Her scarred, delicate fingertips brushed against his palm and then, Silas’s warm calloused fingers closed gently around her hand.
VUUUM!
A radiant wave of pure warmth surged up through her fingers, washing through her frozen meridians and melting the bitter chill that had gripped her soul for hundreds of years.
It was a warmth untainted by greed, malice, or hunger.
It was simply the steady heat of a protector.
Tears finally welled up in the corners of Aurelia’s unseeing, milky-white eyes, spilling over her pale cheeks for the first time in centuries.
Silas gave her trembling hand a gentle, reassuring squeeze, his voice ringing with absolute certainty under the falling snow:
"Welcome to the Blessed Land, Aurelia."
The biting chill of the evening draft swept across the elevated marble dais of the Archway, swirling the fine dusting of snow around their boots.
Aurelia tried to rise from her kneeling position, but her emaciated legs, weakened by centuries of stasis and malnutrition, buckled violently beneath her.
Her center of gravity gave out, and a small choked gasp escaped her lips as her slender frame pitched forward toward the hard stone.
Before her knees could strike the marble, a strong calloused hand shot out, catching her securely around her waist and hauling her gently back against a broad chest.
Aurelia’s breath hitched in her throat.
Her bare shoulders pressed into the thick fabric of Silas’s robes, the heavy fur-lined mantle he had draped over her enveloping her in an unbroken cocoon of warmth.
Standing three paces back on the dais, both Eluned and Morwenna stiffened.
The World-Tree Goddess’s luminous emerald eyes narrowed into razor-thin slits, her pristine teeth gritting so tightly that the muscles in her jaw visibly flexed.
Beside her, Morwenna’s stormy gray eyes flared with a volatile spark, her fingers twitching against the leather wrap of Tidebringer’s hilt.
The territorial instinct to rip the new woman away from their Lord flared instantly between them like dry kindling catching a spark.

Yet, as both women took in the horrific, mosaic-like network of raised silver scars along the girl’s collarbones, her hollow cheeks, and the milky-white opacity of her unseeing eyes, the jealous venom died in their throats.
Neither of them moved...
They were terrors, but they were not blind fools...
They could see that the broken creature in their Lord’s arms was hanging on to reality by a thread.
Silas didn’t release his hold on Aurelia’s waist, keeping his footing solid as he turned his head toward the two women.
"Eluned, Morwenna," Silas spoke, his voice calm and remarkably gentle, lacking even a shred of harsh command.
"I need your help right now.
Head down to the Haven, find Kaelia, and have her prepare a massive tray of warm, nutrient-dense broth, fresh bread, and whatever restorative meats she has ready.
Tell her it’s an emergency for a newly summoned sister."
Eluned blinked, her expression softening into solemn compliance as she gave a crisp nod.
"Understood, Hubby."
"Aye, Captain," Morwenna grunted, rolling her shoulders.
"We’ll have the cook whip up an entire feast in five minutes flat."
The two mythic powerhouses spun on their heels, practically sprinting down the marble steps side-by-side.
Even in their urgent departure, their mutual disdain couldn’t be entirely suppressed.
"Get your heavy sea-boots out of my side, pirate," Eluned hissed in an undertone, gliding an inch above the flagstones.
"You’re kicking up slush like an uncivilized beast."
"Shut your leafy trap, tree-bitch, or I’ll trip you into the aqueduct before we reach the pantry," Morwenna snarled right back, though neither broke their rapid stride toward the Culinary Haven.
Silas let out a soft amused breath through his nose, shaking his head as their bickering faded into the distance.
He adjusted his arm beneath Aurelia’s shoulders, taking the majority of her weight so her bare feet barely had to push against the cold stones.
"Lean on me," Silas murmured into her ear.
"I’ve got you."
Aurelia swallowed hard, nodding mutely.
She pulled the fur mantle tighter around her front, letting herself be guided down the steps and onto the main paved boulevard of the territory.
As they walked through the quiet central courtyard, the crisp night air hummed with invigorating mana.
Aurelia expanded her internal spiritual perception, letting microscopic ripples of mana map out the surrounding environment.
Her mind spun with overwhelming disbelief.
There was no sulfurous choking stench of demonic miasma hanging in the air and there was no cold toxic vacuum of the Great Void suffocating her lungs either.
The atmosphere of this domain was astonishingly pure, dense with rich earth mana, vibrant life-force currents, and the protective glow of defensive arrays woven into the fortress walls.
’It feels... so peaceful,’ Aurelia thought, her battered heart fluttering with a fragile hesitant warmth. ’How can a territory in this world be this serene?
How long has it been since I walked beneath stars that didn’t burn with malice...?’
A patrol of three Shieldmaidens clad in light mythril armor jogged down the intersecting pathway, their spears held at high port.
When the women caught sight of Silas supporting the naked, scarred, platinum-haired woman wrapped in his personal mantle, they immediately halted.
Seeing the grave, protective expression on their Lord’s face, the guards did not shout or raise their weapons in alarm.
They stood at rigid attention, offering crisp respectful salutes with their fists pressed to their chest plates.
"Lord Graves," the lead shieldmaiden acknowledged in a low disciplined murmur.
"At ease, girls," Silas replied with a warm, reassuring smile.
"Keep the northern perimeter tight.
We’ll have a new rotation up before dawn."
"Yes, my Lord!"
The patrol resumed their march without pressing or prying, their footsteps rhythmic and steady against the flagstones.
Aurelia absorbed the interaction with wide unseeing eyes.
’They didn’t flinch...’ she noted internally, her thoughts running in dizzying circles. ’They didn’t demand to know if I was a demon...
They saw my scars, they saw me in his arms, and they simply trusted him and the way he spoke to them... it wasn’t the arrogant bark of a High Inquisitor or the manic shouting of Cassian.
He treats them like people.’
A small defensive shudder coiled in her stomach.
’Is he truly this kind?
Or is this an elaborate facade?
Does he play the gentle ruler under the open sky, only to reveal the monster once the heavy iron gates slam shut behind us...?’
They arrived at the grand double doors of the Keep.
Silas pushed the heavy timber open with his shoulder, guiding her inside into the warm illuminated foyer.
The interior was vast, built from solid reinforced granite and polished dark timber, with crystal mana-lamps casting a warm, golden glow across the corridors.

chapters.title: Chapter 429: A Forbidden Immortality [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Through her mana sense, she felt the handsome man before her relax as a soft and incredibly gentle smile returned to his face.
GRRRRRR!
A loud undisciplined rumble erupted directly from the center of Aurelia’s sunken stomach, echoing loudly across the quiet bedchamber.
Aurelia’s face instantly flushed a brilliant burning shade of crimson as she shrank back into the mantle, ducking her head in pure mortification.
"I... I apologize," she stammered, her voice shrinking to a squeak. "I haven’t eaten solid food in... in a very, very long time."
In truth, Aurelia couldn’t even remember the taste of food. In the Great Void, there had been only dry ether and toxic dust.
The memory of bread was a distant dream from a previous life.
Silas chuckled warmly, the sound rich and utterly devoid of mockery. "Don’t apologize for being hungry. The food is on its way right now."
Kadi stepped toward the adjoining doorway, offering a polite bow.

"I will go draw hot water in the copper tub and infuse it with soothing lavender salts so the Saintess can bathe. Afterward, I’ll run down to the tailoring workshop to fetch a set of enchanted robes."
"Thank you, Kadi," Aurelia whispered, still overwhelmed by the secretary’s polite demeanor.
Kadi slipped into the bathhouse, the sound of rushing steaming water soon echoing softly from the tiles.
Before Silas could ask any further questions about her past, the heavy bedroom door was kicked open with an unsubtle thud.
"Out of the way, plant-bitch!" Morwenna’s voice boomed as she strode into the room, expertly maneuvering a multi-tiered brass serving cart loaded with steaming silver platters.

"Mind your uncouth tongue, sea-rat, you nearly spilled the divine spirit-consommé," Eluned snapped right behind her, gliding gracefully into the chamber with a pitcher of fresh berry nectar floating beside her hand.
The two powerhouses wheeled the cart right up to the side of the bed, presenting a feast.

The air in the room exploded with the rich mouth-watering aromas of slow-roasted drake ribs glazed in honey-wine, steaming bowls of golden root-vegetable stew packed with shredded mana-beast tenderloin, freshly baked loaves of crusty white bread glistening with herb butter, and platters of sliced sweet melons.
Aurelia expanded her spiritual sense to perceive the newcomers and instantly flinched with her breath freezing in her throat.
’G-Gods above...’
The magnitude of the mana radiating from the two women hit her like a physical gale.

The dark-haired woman carrying the saber felt like an endless crushing abyssal ocean trench capable of swallowing continents, while the emerald-haired woman carried the boundless primordial life-force of an ancient realm-core.

’These two... they are mythic entities!’ Aurelia realized in sheer shock. ’They could obliterate entire armies with a flick of their fingers... and they are personally pushing a room-service cart for me?!’
"T-Thank you both..." Aurelia stammered, her voice shaking with instinctual reverence.
Silas looked up at Eluned, gesturing toward Aurelia’s vacant face.
"Elu, she’s completely blind. The optical nerves were severed and burned by a divine fire years ago I assume. Can your magic do anything for her?"
Eluned’s sharp gaze softened as she stepped closer to the edge of the bed.
"Let me see, Hubby."
The World-Tree Goddess reached out, her delicate pale hands cupping both sides of Aurelia’s face.

Aurelia instinctively tensed, her shoulders locking as she prepared to pull away from the foreign touch which was a reflex born from years of having her head seized by executioners and dungeon guards.
"Stay still, little one," Eluned commanded softly, her melodic voice carrying an ancient motherly tone that bypassed Aurelia’s defenses.
Eluned leaned in close, examining the milky-white film covering Aurelia’s eyes. A look of deep understanding crossed the Goddess’s face.

"The optical meridians are entirely fused with chaotic transmutation scars," Eluned diagnosed aloud. "The fire tried to regenerate the tissue while toxic rot was still circulating, welding the nerves into dead calcified stone. A standard healing spell would only shatter the sockets... but to a bit of authority of life itself, it is merely tangled vine."
VUUUUUUM!
Eluned’s hands flared with a radiant emerald-green brilliance.
A cool soothing wave of pure primeval life-force flowed from her palms, sinking directly through Aurelia’s temples and into her skull. It felt like a freezing spring washing over a burning desert.
The calcified scars inside her eye sockets began to unravel, the dead tissue dissolving into harmless light as thousands of microscopic nerve endings sprouted, connected, and flared to life.
Eluned slowly withdrew her hands and Aurelia blinked.
A sharp, blinding prickle of golden light pierced the darkness.
The milky-white film dissolved completely, and for the first time in centuries, the physical world rushed into her retinas in a breathtaking explosion of vibrant color.

Aurelia saw the warm orange glow of the roaring fireplace... She saw the rich crimson grain of the woolen rug... She saw the emerald silk robes and breathtaking ethereal beauty of Eluned standing before her... She saw the rough sun-kissed perfection of Morwenna leaning against the wall with an amused smirk...
And sitting right before her, looking at her with gentle golden ringed blue eyes, was Silas.
"I... I can see..." Aurelia breathed, her hands flying to her face, touching her eyelids in pure disbelieving awe.
Hot tears poured down her cheeks in rivers. Her chest heaved with violent, ragged sobs as the weight of having her sight restored shattered whatever emotional restraint she had left.
Morwenna let out a soft grunt, stepping forward and roughly, yet surprisingly gently, patting Aurelia’s trembling shoulder with a heavy leather gauntlet.
"Alright, alright, don’t drown the room, blondie. You’re in one piece now."
Eluned sat down on the edge of the mattress beside her.

With infinite tenderness, the Goddess wrapped her slender arms around Aurelia’s shoulders, pulling the sobbing Saintess’s face gently against her chest, stroking her platinum hair like a mother comforting a broken child.
"You are safe now, Aurelia," Eluned whispered into her hair, feeling the immense centuries-old agony trapped within the girl’s soul. "No one will ever harm you in this house."
The warmth radiating from Eluned was intoxicating.
Aurelia buried her face into the Goddess’s silk robes, crying until her throat was raw, finally letting centuries of suppressed grief, betrayal, and terror bleed out into the room.
After several minutes, the sobs subsided into quiet hiccups.
Silas pulled the serving cart closer, picking up a bowl of steaming vegetable-and-meat stew along with a wooden spoon, placing it gently into her trembling hands.
"Eat," Silas said with a warm smile. "You need your strength."
Aurelia looked down at the bowl. With trembling fingers, she scooped up a spoonful of the golden broth and brought it to her lips.
The moment the savory liquid touched her tongue, an explosion of rich savory flavor washed over her palate.
The meat was impossibly tender, melting like butter, infused with sweet herbs and pure mana that instantly sent waves of nourishing heat directly into her depleted core.
’It’s... it’s so delicious...’ Aurelia thought, her eyes widening as she took another bite, then another, eating with hurried desperate hunger.
"This is... the most incredible thing I have ever tasted in my life," she mumbled between mouthfuls, tears still glistening on her eyelashes.
Silas watched her eat with quiet satisfaction.
Meanwhile, Kadi emerged from the bathroom, wiping her damp hands on a towel.
Seeing that the Saintess was being fed and tended to, the secretary offered a quiet bow to Silas and slipped out the bedroom door to fetch the tailored clothes from the workshop.
Aurelia swallowed a large piece of roasted meat, took a long gulp of fresh berry nectar from the goblet, and gently set the empty bowl on the cart.
She took a deep steadying breath, wiping her mouth with a linen napkin. The time had come to address the core reason she was here.
Silas leaned back in his chair, his blue eyes meeting hers. "Earlier on the Archway, you mentioned something about being able to grant me immortality... right?"
Aurelia stiffened slightly, but her gaze remained firm. She folded her hands over the fur mantle in her lap, looking directly at her new Lord.

"Yes, my Lord," Aurelia began, her voice steadying as she explained the reality of her abilities. "I possess the Argent Flame of Transmutation. It is a unique conceptual miracle. When its secondary phase is bound to another soul, I become their living anchor. If you suffer a fatal strike, if your limbs are severed, if you are infected with demonic rot or cursed by higher gods... the flame will instantly purge the injury from your flesh and reflect the physical wound entirely onto my own body."
She looked at Silas with her golden-amber eyes turning dead serious.

"Because the Argent Flame ensures my own core cannot truly perish from trauma, you will be, in all practical terms, completely immortal on the battlefield. I am willing to bind this soul-link to you, and to every single warrior in the Blessed Land."
Aurelia’s fingers subtly tightened against the fabric of the mantle as she laid out her terms.

"In exchange for this power... I ask for only two things, Lord Graves. First... I ask that you allow me to walk freely under the sky of this territory, so that I may see the world with my own eyes. You may place me on a strict curfew. You may even bind my wrists in iron chains if you believe I cannot be trusted to roam alone... I will accept it."
She swallowed hard, looking down at the empty plates on the cart.
"And second... I wish to be allowed to eat meals like this every day. That is all I ask."
Silas stared at her in complete stunned silence.
Beside her, Eluned and Morwenna both went dead quiet, their eyes locked onto the frail, platinum-haired woman.

The heartbreaking tragedy of her request hung heavy in the air... she was offering to endure infinite decapitations, dismemberments, and fatal butcheries, and all she wanted in return was the permission to look at the trees and eat a warm meal without being starved in a hole.
Silas slowly leaned forward, resting his forearms on his knees.
He reached out, his warm broad hand coming to rest gently atop Aurelia’s head, his fingers threading softly through her platinum locks in a slow comforting headpat.
"Aurelia, look at me," Silas commanded softly.
Aurelia looked up, meeting his clear blue eyes.

"From this moment forward," Silas spoke with unwavering authority, "you are free to use your Argent Flame to heal our wounded soldiers, to cleanse poisons, to purify curses, or to cast any other divine miracle you desire but the secondary link... the immortality is permanently, completely off the table. I forbid it."
Aurelia’s jaw dropped in pure, staggering disbelief.
"B-But... why?! That is the greatest power I have to offer! With that link, you could conquer entire empires without ever fearing death!"

"I don’t need to conquer empires on the back of your torture," Silas interrupted firmly, his voice ringing with conviction. "You have so much more potential, so much more value as a human being, than simply acting as a trash bin for other people’s pain. You were not summoned here to be butchered in our place, Aurelia. You deserve peace, you deserve safety, and you deserve joy and as the Lord of this domain, I promise you that your days here will be happy."
Aurelia’s breath completely hitched in her chest.
She stared at the earnest protective fire burning in his blue eyes, feeling an overwhelming warmth expand inside her heart that threatened to swallow her whole.
Silas stood up from his chair, brushing down his combat robes with an easy, relaxed smile.
"Now then... finish up whatever food you have left, take a long, warm bath, and get a good night’s sleep. Tomorrow morning, you’ll be receiving a full tour of the territory."
Silas turned toward the door, nodding to the other two women.
Morwenna stepped up to the bed, giving Aurelia a firm encouraging slap on the shoulder that nearly knocked the wind out of her.
"Stay strong, blondie. The Captain’s an idiot sometimes, but he doesn’t lie about his people."
With a wicked smirk, the Pirate Queen turned and swaggered out the door after Silas.
"Wait for meeeee, Hubby!" Eluned squealed, instantly dropping her regal demeanor as she floated off the mattress.
She turned back to Aurelia with a sweet bright smile. "Rest well, sister. Take care of yourself!"
The Goddess zipped out the door, leaving Aurelia sitting alone in the quiet, firelit bedchamber.
Aurelia sat in the silence for a long moment, staring at the closed doorway.
’What kind of man is he...?’ she thought, her heart hammering wildly against her ribs.𝚏𝕣𝐞𝗲𝐰𝕖𝐛𝐧𝕠𝕧𝚎𝚕.𝐜𝚘𝗺

She let out a soft breath, picked up the remaining crust of warm bread, ate it, and let out a soft satisfied burp. Just then, Kadi returned, carrying a neatly folded stack of fine white silk robes trimmed with golden thread.

"These are enchanted garments tailored with auto-sizing threading," Kadi explained, setting them on the dresser and wheeling the empty food cart toward the door. "The bath is hot and ready for you, Lady Aurelia. Please take your time."
"Thank you, Kadi," Aurelia replied softly.
Once the door clicked shut again, Aurelia stood up from the bed, letting the heavy fur mantle fall away. She walked into the private bathing chamber, stepping onto the warm marble tiles.
’So strange...’
Steam rose in thick fragrant clouds from the massive copper tub, carrying the soothing scent of lavender and floral salts.
Aurelia stepped into the water, sinking slowly into the scalding luxurious heat until the water reached her collarbones.
"Haaaa... Amazing~"
She closed her eyes, letting out a long shuddering sigh of pure bliss as the mineral-rich waters soaked into her aching muscles and scarred skin.
She sat in the tub, reminiscing about everything that had transpired over the last hour.
The cold void... The golden light of the Archway... Silas’s warm hands catching her before she fell... The delicious taste of roasted meat... The feeling of sight returning to her dead eyes...
And the unconditional rejection of her sacrificial curse.
THUMP-THUMP!
Her heart beat with a rhythm she had not felt in centuries.

’I will leave it all behind,’ Aurelia resolved, her fingers tracing the surface of the water. ’The Meolion Kingdom... Cassian’s betrayal... The six years in the dark. It is all dead and turned to ash. From this night forward, my life, my flame, and my soul belong entirely to the Blessed Land.’

sentences.text: Through her mana sense, she felt the handsome man before her relax as a soft and incredibly gentle smile returned to his face.
GRRRRRR!
A loud undisciplined rumble erupted directly from the center of Aurelia’s sunken stomach, echoing loudly across the quiet bedchamber.
Aurelia’s face instantly flushed a brilliant burning shade of crimson as she shrank back into the mantle, ducking her head in pure mortification.
I apologize," she stammered, her voice shrinking to a squeak.
"I haven’t eaten solid food in... in a very, very long time."
In truth, Aurelia couldn’t even remember the taste of food.
In the Great Void, there had been only dry ether and toxic dust.
The memory of bread was a distant dream from a previous life.
Silas chuckled warmly, the sound rich and utterly devoid of mockery.
"Don’t apologize for being hungry.
The food is on its way right now."
Kadi stepped toward the adjoining doorway, offering a polite bow.
"I will go draw hot water in the copper tub and infuse it with soothing lavender salts so the Saintess can bathe.
Afterward, I’ll run down to the tailoring workshop to fetch a set of enchanted robes."
"Thank you, Kadi," Aurelia whispered, still overwhelmed by the secretary’s polite demeanor.
Kadi slipped into the bathhouse, the sound of rushing steaming water soon echoing softly from the tiles.
Before Silas could ask any further questions about her past, the heavy bedroom door was kicked open with an unsubtle thud.
"Out of the way, plant-bitch!" Morwenna’s voice boomed as she strode into the room, expertly maneuvering a multi-tiered brass serving cart loaded with steaming silver platters.

"Mind your uncouth tongue, sea-rat, you nearly spilled the divine spirit-consommé," Eluned snapped right behind her, gliding gracefully into the chamber with a pitcher of fresh berry nectar floating beside her hand.
The two powerhouses wheeled the cart right up to the side of the bed, presenting a feast.

The air in the room exploded with the rich mouth-watering aromas of slow-roasted drake ribs glazed in honey-wine, steaming bowls of golden root-vegetable stew packed with shredded mana-beast tenderloin, freshly baked loaves of crusty white bread glistening with herb butter, and platters of sliced sweet melons.
Aurelia expanded her spiritual sense to perceive the newcomers and instantly flinched with her breath freezing in her throat.
’G-Gods above...’
The magnitude of the mana radiating from the two women hit her like a physical gale.

The dark-haired woman carrying the saber felt like an endless crushing abyssal ocean trench capable of swallowing continents, while the emerald-haired woman carried the boundless primordial life-force of an ancient realm-core.

’These two... they are mythic entities!’ Aurelia realized in sheer shock. ’They could obliterate entire armies with a flick of their fingers... and they are personally pushing a room-service cart for me?!’
"T-Thank you both..." Aurelia stammered, her voice shaking with instinctual reverence.
Silas looked up at Eluned, gesturing toward Aurelia’s vacant face.
"Elu, she’s completely blind.
The optical nerves were severed and burned by a divine fire years ago I assume.
Can your magic do anything for her?"
Eluned’s sharp gaze softened as she stepped closer to the edge of the bed.
"Let me see, Hubby."
The World-Tree Goddess reached out, her delicate pale hands cupping both sides of Aurelia’s face.

Aurelia instinctively tensed, her shoulders locking as she prepared to pull away from the foreign touch which was a reflex born from years of having her head seized by executioners and dungeon guards.
"Stay still, little one," Eluned commanded softly, her melodic voice carrying an ancient motherly tone that bypassed Aurelia’s defenses.
Eluned leaned in close, examining the milky-white film covering Aurelia’s eyes.
A look of deep understanding crossed the Goddess’s face.
"The optical meridians are entirely fused with chaotic transmutation scars," Eluned diagnosed aloud.
"The fire tried to regenerate the tissue while toxic rot was still circulating, welding the nerves into dead calcified stone.
A standard healing spell would only shatter the sockets... but to a bit of authority of life itself, it is merely tangled vine."
VUUUUUUM!
Eluned’s hands flared with a radiant emerald-green brilliance.
A cool soothing wave of pure primeval life-force flowed from her palms, sinking directly through Aurelia’s temples and into her skull.
It felt like a freezing spring washing over a burning desert.
The calcified scars inside her eye sockets began to unravel, the dead tissue dissolving into harmless light as thousands of microscopic nerve endings sprouted, connected, and flared to life.
Eluned slowly withdrew her hands and Aurelia blinked.
A sharp, blinding prickle of golden light pierced the darkness.
The milky-white film dissolved completely, and for the first time in centuries, the physical world rushed into her retinas in a breathtaking explosion of vibrant color.
Aurelia saw the warm orange glow of the roaring fireplace...
She saw the rich crimson grain of the woolen rug...
She saw the emerald silk robes and breathtaking ethereal beauty of Eluned standing before her...
She saw the rough sun-kissed perfection of Morwenna leaning against the wall with an amused smirk...
And sitting right before her, looking at her with gentle golden ringed blue eyes, was Silas.
I can see..." Aurelia breathed, her hands flying to her face, touching her eyelids in pure disbelieving awe.
Hot tears poured down her cheeks in rivers.
Her chest heaved with violent, ragged sobs as the weight of having her sight restored shattered whatever emotional restraint she had left.
Morwenna let out a soft grunt, stepping forward and roughly, yet surprisingly gently, patting Aurelia’s trembling shoulder with a heavy leather gauntlet.
"Alright, alright, don’t drown the room, blondie.
You’re in one piece now."
Eluned sat down on the edge of the mattress beside her.

With infinite tenderness, the Goddess wrapped her slender arms around Aurelia’s shoulders, pulling the sobbing Saintess’s face gently against her chest, stroking her platinum hair like a mother comforting a broken child.
"You are safe now, Aurelia," Eluned whispered into her hair, feeling the immense centuries-old agony trapped within the girl’s soul.
"No one will ever harm you in this house."
The warmth radiating from Eluned was intoxicating.
Aurelia buried her face into the Goddess’s silk robes, crying until her throat was raw, finally letting centuries of suppressed grief, betrayal, and terror bleed out into the room.
After several minutes, the sobs subsided into quiet hiccups.
Silas pulled the serving cart closer, picking up a bowl of steaming vegetable-and-meat stew along with a wooden spoon, placing it gently into her trembling hands.
"Eat," Silas said with a warm smile.
"You need your strength."
Aurelia looked down at the bowl.
With trembling fingers, she scooped up a spoonful of the golden broth and brought it to her lips.
The moment the savory liquid touched her tongue, an explosion of rich savory flavor washed over her palate.
The meat was impossibly tender, melting like butter, infused with sweet herbs and pure mana that instantly sent waves of nourishing heat directly into her depleted core.
’It’s... it’s so delicious...’ Aurelia thought, her eyes widening as she took another bite, then another, eating with hurried desperate hunger.
"This is... the most incredible thing I have ever tasted in my life," she mumbled between mouthfuls, tears still glistening on her eyelashes.
Silas watched her eat with quiet satisfaction.
Meanwhile, Kadi emerged from the bathroom, wiping her damp hands on a towel.
Seeing that the Saintess was being fed and tended to, the secretary offered a quiet bow to Silas and slipped out the bedroom door to fetch the tailored clothes from the workshop.
Aurelia swallowed a large piece of roasted meat, took a long gulp of fresh berry nectar from the goblet, and gently set the empty bowl on the cart.
She took a deep steadying breath, wiping her mouth with a linen napkin.
The time had come to address the core reason she was here.
Silas leaned back in his chair, his blue eyes meeting hers.
"Earlier on the Archway, you mentioned something about being able to grant me immortality... right?"
Aurelia stiffened slightly, but her gaze remained firm.
She folded her hands over the fur mantle in her lap, looking directly at her new Lord.
"Yes, my Lord," Aurelia began, her voice steadying as she explained the reality of her abilities.
"I possess the Argent Flame of Transmutation.
It is a unique conceptual miracle.
When its secondary phase is bound to another soul, I become their living anchor.

If you suffer a fatal strike, if your limbs are severed, if you are infected with demonic rot or cursed by higher gods... the flame will instantly purge the injury from your flesh and reflect the physical wound entirely onto my own body."
She looked at Silas with her golden-amber eyes turning dead serious.
"Because the Argent Flame ensures my own core cannot truly perish from trauma, you will be, in all practical terms, completely immortal on the battlefield.
I am willing to bind this soul-link to you, and to every single warrior in the Blessed Land."
Aurelia’s fingers subtly tightened against the fabric of the mantle as she laid out her terms.
"In exchange for this power...
I ask for only two things, Lord Graves.
First...
I ask that you allow me to walk freely under the sky of this territory, so that I may see the world with my own eyes.
You may place me on a strict curfew.
You may even bind my wrists in iron chains if you believe I cannot be trusted to roam alone...
I will accept it."
She swallowed hard, looking down at the empty plates on the cart.
"And second...
I wish to be allowed to eat meals like this every day.
That is all I ask."
Silas stared at her in complete stunned silence.
Beside her, Eluned and Morwenna both went dead quiet, their eyes locked onto the frail, platinum-haired woman.

The heartbreaking tragedy of her request hung heavy in the air... she was offering to endure infinite decapitations, dismemberments, and fatal butcheries, and all she wanted in return was the permission to look at the trees and eat a warm meal without being starved in a hole.
Silas slowly leaned forward, resting his forearms on his knees.
He reached out, his warm broad hand coming to rest gently atop Aurelia’s head, his fingers threading softly through her platinum locks in a slow comforting headpat.
"Aurelia, look at me," Silas commanded softly.
Aurelia looked up, meeting his clear blue eyes.

"From this moment forward," Silas spoke with unwavering authority, "you are free to use your Argent Flame to heal our wounded soldiers, to cleanse poisons, to purify curses, or to cast any other divine miracle you desire but the secondary link... the immortality is permanently, completely off the table.
I forbid it."
Aurelia’s jaw dropped in pure, staggering disbelief.
"B-But... why?!
That is the greatest power I have to offer!
With that link, you could conquer entire empires without ever fearing death!"
"I don’t need to conquer empires on the back of your torture," Silas interrupted firmly, his voice ringing with conviction.
"You have so much more potential, so much more value as a human being, than simply acting as a trash bin for other people’s pain.
You were not summoned here to be butchered in our place, Aurelia.
You deserve peace, you deserve safety, and you deserve joy and as the Lord of this domain, I promise you that your days here will be happy."
Aurelia’s breath completely hitched in her chest.
She stared at the earnest protective fire burning in his blue eyes, feeling an overwhelming warmth expand inside her heart that threatened to swallow her whole.
Silas stood up from his chair, brushing down his combat robes with an easy, relaxed smile.
"Now then... finish up whatever food you have left, take a long, warm bath, and get a good night’s sleep.
Tomorrow morning, you’ll be receiving a full tour of the territory."
Silas turned toward the door, nodding to the other two women.
Morwenna stepped up to the bed, giving Aurelia a firm encouraging slap on the shoulder that nearly knocked the wind out of her.
"Stay strong, blondie.
The Captain’s an idiot sometimes, but he doesn’t lie about his people."
With a wicked smirk, the Pirate Queen turned and swaggered out the door after Silas.
"Wait for meeeee, Hubby!" Eluned squealed, instantly dropping her regal demeanor as she floated off the mattress.
She turned back to Aurelia with a sweet bright smile.
"Rest well, sister.
Take care of yourself!"
The Goddess zipped out the door, leaving Aurelia sitting alone in the quiet, firelit bedchamber.
Aurelia sat in the silence for a long moment, staring at the closed doorway.
’What kind of man is he...?’ she thought, her heart hammering wildly against her ribs.𝚏𝕣𝐞𝗲𝐰𝕖𝐛𝐧𝕠𝕧𝚎𝚕.𝐜𝚘𝗺
She let out a soft breath, picked up the remaining crust of warm bread, ate it, and let out a soft satisfied burp.
Just then, Kadi returned, carrying a neatly folded stack of fine white silk robes trimmed with golden thread.
"These are enchanted garments tailored with auto-sizing threading," Kadi explained, setting them on the dresser and wheeling the empty food cart toward the door.
"The bath is hot and ready for you, Lady Aurelia.
Please take your time."
"Thank you, Kadi," Aurelia replied softly.
Once the door clicked shut again, Aurelia stood up from the bed, letting the heavy fur mantle fall away.
She walked into the private bathing chamber, stepping onto the warm marble tiles.
’So strange...’
Steam rose in thick fragrant clouds from the massive copper tub, carrying the soothing scent of lavender and floral salts.
Aurelia stepped into the water, sinking slowly into the scalding luxurious heat until the water reached her collarbones.
"Haaaa...
Amazing~"
She closed her eyes, letting out a long shuddering sigh of pure bliss as the mineral-rich waters soaked into her aching muscles and scarred skin.
She sat in the tub, reminiscing about everything that had transpired over the last hour.
The cold void...
The golden light of the Archway...
Silas’s warm hands catching her before she fell...
The delicious taste of roasted meat...
The feeling of sight returning to her dead eyes...
And the unconditional rejection of her sacrificial curse.
THUMP-THUMP!
Her heart beat with a rhythm she had not felt in centuries.
’I will leave it all behind,’ Aurelia resolved, her fingers tracing the surface of the water. ’The Meolion Kingdom...
Cassian’s betrayal...
The six years in the dark.
It is all dead and turned to ash.
From this night forward, my life, my flame, and my soul belong entirely to the Blessed Land.’

chapters.title: Chapter 430: Descending From Asgard [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: She finished bathing, stepping out of the tub and wrapping herself in a plush linen towel.
"What a wonderful bath..."
Walking over to the polished silver mirror mounted on the wall, Aurelia wiped away the steam from the glass and looked at her own reflection for the first time in centuries.
She blinked in complete astonishment.
The emaciated sickly frame she remembered had already begun to fill out under the restorative effects of the high-tier food and Eluned’s mana.
Her skin, though still marked with silver scars, was porcelain, smooth, and radiant.
Her facial features were breathtakingly noble, her platinum-blonde hair shimmering like liquid starlight, and her body possessed full voluptuous curves that made her look like a true Saintess.
’I... I’m actually hot...’ Aurelia thought, her cheeks flushing pink as she turned to inspect her own reflection. ’Was I always this beautiful? Or did the reset restore my prime form...?’
She shook her head with an embarrassed laugh, running a comb through her damp platinum hair before slipping into the tailored white silk robes.
The enchanted fabric shifted smoothly against her skin, cinching perfectly around her slender waist.
Aurelia stepped back into the main bedroom, walking over to the wide glass window overlooking the central courtyard.
Outside, the Blessed Land was bathed in peaceful silver moonlight.
The falling snow had ceased, leaving the stone buildings dusted in white.
The territory was completely quiet, but Aurelia could feel the vibrant pulse of life humming beneath the stone which was a promise of the lively bustling domain that would wake with the dawn.
’And I want to see it too... I can’t believe I can use my eyes...’
She walked to the large bed, climbed under the heavy plush quilts, and let her head sink into the soft down pillows.
She closed her eyes, pulling the covers up to her chin.

’Lord Graves is an idiot...’ Aurelia mused fondly, a faint smile touching her lips in the dark. ’What kind of Lord bans immortality? Who turns down invincible soldiers just to spare his healer some pain...?’
She resolved to stay awake for a while, keeping her spiritual senses sharp just in case this was all a dream or an elaborate trap.
Yet, surrounded by the warm, clean sheets and the soothing crackle of the hearth, the exhaustion of a thousand years finally caught up to her.
Within five minutes, the Saintess was sound asleep.
CREEEAK!
The bedroom door opened a crack.
Peeking through the gap was Eluned, her emerald eyes glowing softly in the gloom as she observed the sleeping girl.
Leaning over her shoulders from the hallway were Silas and Morwenna.
Seeing Aurelia resting soundly, Eluned pulled back, giving Silas a silent satisfied thumbs-up before gently clicking the door shut.
The three of them began walking down the quiet corridor toward the master quarters.
Eluned immediately wrapped her arms around Silas’s left arm, pressing her chest flush against his bicep as she tilted her chin up with an eager pleading pout.
"Now that our good deed for the night is officially concluded, Hubby... we should celebrate with intense energetic breeding!"
Silas let out a long, exhausted sigh, rubbing the back of his neck.
"No, Elu. I am completely exhausted. My mana is drained from the summoning ritual, and I have fifty logistics reports to review at dawn... We’re sleeping."
"What?!" Eluned whined loudly, puffing her cheeks out. "That is completely unfair! You promised me romantic attention!"
Morwenna snickered loudly from Silas’s right, crossing her arms. "Look at the needy weed getting rejected. Go water yourself in the garden, plant-bitch."

"Silence, pirate!" Eluned hissed, planting her bare feet firmly on the carpeted floorboards and crossing her arms in absolute defiance. "If you will not mate with me, Silas, then I am simply not sleeping at all tonight! I shall stand right outside your door and cast wind chimes until dawn!"
Silas stopped, looked at the pouting Goddess for half a second, and shook his head.
Without a word, Silas bent down, hooked his arm behind Eluned’s knees, and hoisted the World-Tree Goddess up into a bridal carry.
"E-Eh?!" Eluned squeaked, her face flushing crimson as she instinctively wrapped her arms around his neck.
"You don’t get a choice," Silas said with a smirk, carrying her down the hallway. "Bed. Now."
Morwenna burst into a loud ringing laugh, and the three of them chuckled together as they disappeared into the master quarters for the night.
The morning sun crested the eastern crags of the Umbral Basin, casting long golden rays of light across the Blessed Land.
Aurelia woke up slowly, the soft warm sunlight filtering through the curtains of her bedchamber.
"Wooh... It’s not a dream."

She stretched her arms, feeling an incredible light sensation in her limbs as her vitality was fully replenished, her core was stable, and the phantom aches that had haunted her for centuries were completely gone.
She slipped out of bed, walking over to the window and pulling the velvet drapes aside.
The sight that greeted her stole her breath.

The central courtyard below was packed with lively bustling activity. Dozens of female Shieldmaidens in gleaming armor were running formation drills across the sand pits, their synchronized war cries echoing through the crisp morning air.
Dwarven blacksmiths carrying heavy iron ingots bustled between the Barracks and the foundry, while several people carried ledger scrolls and seemed to be leaving.
’Are they scouts perhaps?’
The territory was vibrant and a small flutter of anxious apprehension tightened in Aurelia’s chest.
’So many people...’
KNOCK-KNOCK!
The bedroom door opened, and Kadi stepped inside carrying a small tray of morning tea.
"Good morning, Lady Aurelia," Kadi greeted with a bright professional smile. "Did you sleep comfortably?"
Aurelia turned from the window, her expression shifting into sharp focused determination.
"Kadi... where is Lord Silas’s office?" Aurelia asked urgently.

Kadi blinked, slightly taken aback by the sudden question. "Lord Silas’s office is located on the top floor of the Keep, at the end of the central hall. But if you wish to speak with him, I can inform—"
Before Kadi could finish her sentence, Aurelia had already darted past her, her white silk robes billowing as she practically sprinted out of the room.
Aurelia rushed up the winding stone stairs, taking two steps at a time as her thoughts raced with urgent calculation.

’We need to negotiate properly,’ Aurelia thought, her fists clenching at her sides as she reached the top-floor landing. ’He was being emotional and soft-hearted last night because of my tears but a ruler cannot afford to be sentimental. In this brutal world, power is everything. If I do not provide him with an overwhelming advantage, my position in this territory will eventually erode... I must convince him to accept the Argent Flame’s link!’𝒇𝒓𝒆𝒆𝙬𝒆𝒃𝓷𝒐𝓿𝙚𝙡.𝒄𝓸𝒎
She reached the massive double mahogany doors at the end of the hall, took a deep breath, and pushed them open.
"Lord Silas, we need to—"
Aurelia froze mid-sentence, the words catching in her throat.
Sitting behind a massive, polished dark-oak desk covered in territorial maps, resource ledgers, and glowing communication crystals was Silas.
He was dressed in a crisp dark-charcoal tunic, his golden ringed blue eyes calm and focused as he reviewed a scroll.
Standing beside his desk was Aeliana.
The Archon of the Stars was gracefully pouring a cold cup of purple drink from a porcelain kettle.
She wore flowing midnight-blue silk robes that shimmered with cosmic starlight and her long blond hair was pinned with a crystal hairpin.
Aeliana paused mid-pour, her sharp elegant eyes turning toward the door as she looked at Aurelia with quiet serene grace.
"Good morning, Lady Aurelia," Aeliana greeted softly with a polite nod.
Aurelia stood frozen in the doorway, suddenly feeling completely out of place before the majestic elf.

Silas looked up from his paperwork with a warm welcoming smile breaking across his face as he reached for a crystal glass filled with royal-purple spirit juice, finishing it off in a single smooth gulp before setting the empty glass on a silver tray.
"Morning, Aurelia," Silas chuckled, noticing her wide-eyed, stiff posture. "Don’t mind Aeliana, she doesn’t bite... Aurelia is just a bit shy this morning, Aeli."
Aeliana offered an elegant smile, picking up the silver tray.
POP!
With a soft whisper of spatial mana, the Archon of the Stars vanished into thin air, leaving the office completely private.
Silas gestured toward the plush leather armchair positioned directly in front of his desk.
"Come on in, Aurelia. Close the door and take a seat."
Aurelia swallowed hard, stepping into the grand office and clicking the heavy mahogany door shut behind her.
She walked over, sitting gracefully on the edge of the leather chair with her posture turning rigid and formal.
She could not allow herself to be swayed a second time.
"How are you feeling this morning?" Silas asked, setting his quill down and leaning back comfortably. "Did you sleep well?"

"I am doing very well, my Lord," Aurelia replied crisply, cutting straight to the point. "The room was magnificent, and my vitality is fully restored which is why... I have come here to properly negotiate the terms of my service."
Silas raised an eyebrow, a slight smirk playing on his lips.
Before she could launch into her prepared speech about the strategic benefits of proxy-immortality, Silas smoothly leaned forward, resting his forearms on the desk.

"Before we get into any heavy negotiations," Silas interrupted smoothly, "the scouts reported some unusual mana-beast migration patterns along the outer perimeter crags. In about an hour, I’m leading a small forward scouting unit outside the territory walls to investigate the terrain. Why don’t you come along? It’ll be a great opportunity for you to get some fresh air, stretch your legs, and get used to the geography of the Umbral Basin..."
Aurelia blinked, nodding instinctively. "I would be honored to accompany you, Lord Silas and if we encounter powerful beasts, I can activate the Argent Flame’s soul-link to ensure your safety—"

"No," Silas cut in instantly, pointing a teasing, yet completely uncompromising finger at her. "I told you last night: the immortality link is permanently banned. You are not absorbing anyone’s damage."
Aurelia’s brow furrowed, a sudden burst of exasperated genuine frustration leaking through her formal facade.

"Why do you care so much?!" Aurelia blurted out, leaning forward in her chair. "Every ruler in existence would kill to have an immortal vanguard... It costs you nothing! Why are you so stubbornly refusing the greatest defensive weapon in this world?!"
Silas didn’t get angry at her outburst.
Instead, he reached across the polished oak desk, gently taking hold of her small delicate hand.
"Hm?"
He slowly threaded his fingers through hers as his warm calloused palm rested snugly against her pale skin.
Aurelia froze, her breath catching as an intense burning blush exploded across her porcelain cheeks.

"I care," Silas said softly, his eyes locking onto hers with unwavering sincerity, "because I care about my people. Every single one of them and that includes you, Aurelia. Your life is not a consumable shield."
Aurelia swallowed hard, her heart pounding wildly against her ribs like a trapped bird as she desperately tried to maintain her composure, looking down at their joined hands.
"I... If I didn’t know any better, my Lord..." Aurelia stammered, her voice trembling slightly, "...I would think you were flirting with me."
Silas chuckled softly, a playful charming glint flashing in his eyes.
"Who knows?" Silas replied with a smooth teasing smirk. "I just might be."
Aurelia’s mind went into overload.

’No... no, no, no,’ Aurelia screamed internally, her face burning hotter than a blast furnace as she fought to pull her gaze away from his devastatingly handsome smile. ’This is a trick! It won’t work on me! I already have experience with charming Heroes! Cassian whispered sweet promises under the stars too, and look where that led—’
THUMP!
Her heart skipped a violent traitorous beat.
A wave of fluster washed over her, making her toes curl inside her slippers.

’Why... why is my heart racing like this?!’ she panicked, biting her lower lip. ’Why am I already coming to like him so much?! Am I really that easy?! I’ve only known this man for less than twelve hours!’
Before Silas could tease the hopelessly blushing Saintess any further—
VUUUUUUUUUM!
A massive ear-splitting cosmic vibration tore through the atmosphere above the Blessed Land.
The ambient mana in the room violently fluctuated, causing the communication crystals on Silas’s desk to flare with unstable light.
Silas’s playful expression instantly vanished, replaced by cold razor-sharp focus.
He released Aurelia’s hand, shooting up from his chair in a single fluid motion and striding swiftly toward the panoramic floor-to-ceiling windows overlooking the territory.
Aurelia bolted to her feet, rushing up beside him.
Outside, the morning sky above the Umbral Basin had completely transformed.
The clear blue heavens had turned a brilliant incandescent shade of liquid gold.
The light was so intense it completely vaporized the morning clouds, clearing away the lingering snow across the entire basin in a matter of seconds.
High above the territory, the golden sky fractured.
A colossal swirling spatial vortex tore open in the upper atmosphere... a majestic blinding rift that radiated an overwhelming suffocating pressure of ancient divine thunder.
Silas leaned forward, his golden ringed eyes narrowing to fine points as he stared into the swirling golden rift.
"Something..." Silas murmured, his voice dead serious as the air in the room crackled with static electricity. "...Something is coming from Asgard."

"What?!" Eluned whined loudly, puffing her cheeks out.
"That is completely unfair!
You promised me romantic attention!"
Morwenna snickered loudly from Silas’s right, crossing her arms.
"Look at the needy weed getting rejected.
Go water yourself in the garden, plant-bitch."
"Silence, pirate!" Eluned hissed, planting her bare feet firmly on the carpeted floorboards and crossing her arms in absolute defiance.
"If you will not mate with me, Silas, then I am simply not sleeping at all tonight!
I shall stand right outside your door and cast wind chimes until dawn!"
Silas stopped, looked at the pouting Goddess for half a second, and shook his head.
Without a word, Silas bent down, hooked his arm behind Eluned’s knees, and hoisted the World-Tree Goddess up into a bridal carry.
"E-Eh?!" Eluned squeaked, her face flushing crimson as she instinctively wrapped her arms around his neck.
"You don’t get a choice," Silas said with a smirk, carrying her down the hallway.
"Bed.
Now."
Morwenna burst into a loud ringing laugh, and the three of them chuckled together as they disappeared into the master quarters for the night.
The morning sun crested the eastern crags of the Umbral Basin, casting long golden rays of light across the Blessed Land.
Aurelia woke up slowly, the soft warm sunlight filtering through the curtains of her bedchamber.
"Wooh...
It’s not a dream."

She stretched her arms, feeling an incredible light sensation in her limbs as her vitality was fully replenished, her core was stable, and the phantom aches that had haunted her for centuries were completely gone.
She slipped out of bed, walking over to the window and pulling the velvet drapes aside.
The sight that greeted her stole her breath.
The central courtyard below was packed with lively bustling activity.
Dozens of female Shieldmaidens in gleaming armor were running formation drills across the sand pits, their synchronized war cries echoing through the crisp morning air.
Dwarven blacksmiths carrying heavy iron ingots bustled between the Barracks and the foundry, while several people carried ledger scrolls and seemed to be leaving.
’Are they scouts perhaps?’
The territory was vibrant and a small flutter of anxious apprehension tightened in Aurelia’s chest.
’So many people...’
KNOCK-KNOCK!
The bedroom door opened, and Kadi stepped inside carrying a small tray of morning tea.
"Good morning, Lady Aurelia," Kadi greeted with a bright professional smile.
"Did you sleep comfortably?"
Aurelia turned from the window, her expression shifting into sharp focused determination.
"Kadi... where is Lord Silas’s office?" Aurelia asked urgently.
Kadi blinked, slightly taken aback by the sudden question.
"Lord Silas’s office is located on the top floor of the Keep, at the end of the central hall.
But if you wish to speak with him, I can inform—"
Before Kadi could finish her sentence, Aurelia had already darted past her, her white silk robes billowing as she practically sprinted out of the room.
Aurelia rushed up the winding stone stairs, taking two steps at a time as her thoughts raced with urgent calculation.

’We need to negotiate properly,’ Aurelia thought, her fists clenching at her sides as she reached the top-floor landing. ’He was being emotional and soft-hearted last night because of my tears but a ruler cannot afford to be sentimental.
In this brutal world, power is everything.
If I do not provide him with an overwhelming advantage, my position in this territory will eventually erode...
I must convince him to accept the Argent Flame’s link!’𝒇𝒓𝒆𝒆𝙬𝒆𝒃𝓷𝒐𝓿𝙚𝙡.𝒄𝓸𝒎
She reached the massive double mahogany doors at the end of the hall, took a deep breath, and pushed them open.
"Lord Silas, we need to—"
Aurelia froze mid-sentence, the words catching in her throat.
Sitting behind a massive, polished dark-oak desk covered in territorial maps, resource ledgers, and glowing communication crystals was Silas.
He was dressed in a crisp dark-charcoal tunic, his golden ringed blue eyes calm and focused as he reviewed a scroll.
Standing beside his desk was Aeliana.
The Archon of the Stars was gracefully pouring a cold cup of purple drink from a porcelain kettle.
She wore flowing midnight-blue silk robes that shimmered with cosmic starlight and her long blond hair was pinned with a crystal hairpin.
Aeliana paused mid-pour, her sharp elegant eyes turning toward the door as she looked at Aurelia with quiet serene grace.
"Good morning, Lady Aurelia," Aeliana greeted softly with a polite nod.
Aurelia stood frozen in the doorway, suddenly feeling completely out of place before the majestic elf.

Silas looked up from his paperwork with a warm welcoming smile breaking across his face as he reached for a crystal glass filled with royal-purple spirit juice, finishing it off in a single smooth gulp before setting the empty glass on a silver tray.
"Morning, Aurelia," Silas chuckled, noticing her wide-eyed, stiff posture.
"Don’t mind Aeliana, she doesn’t bite...
Aurelia is just a bit shy this morning, Aeli."
Aeliana offered an elegant smile, picking up the silver tray.
POP!
With a soft whisper of spatial mana, the Archon of the Stars vanished into thin air, leaving the office completely private.
Silas gestured toward the plush leather armchair positioned directly in front of his desk.
"Come on in, Aurelia.
Close the door and take a seat."
Aurelia swallowed hard, stepping into the grand office and clicking the heavy mahogany door shut behind her.
She walked over, sitting gracefully on the edge of the leather chair with her posture turning rigid and formal.
She could not allow herself to be swayed a second time.
"How are you feeling this morning?" Silas asked, setting his quill down and leaning back comfortably.
"Did you sleep well?"
"I am doing very well, my Lord," Aurelia replied crisply, cutting straight to the point.
"The room was magnificent, and my vitality is fully restored which is why...
I have come here to properly negotiate the terms of my service."
Silas raised an eyebrow, a slight smirk playing on his lips.
Before she could launch into her prepared speech about the strategic benefits of proxy-immortality, Silas smoothly leaned forward, resting his forearms on the desk.
"Before we get into any heavy negotiations," Silas interrupted smoothly, "the scouts reported some unusual mana-beast migration patterns along the outer perimeter crags.
In about an hour, I’m leading a small forward scouting unit outside the territory walls to investigate the terrain.
Why don’t you come along?
It’ll be a great opportunity for you to get some fresh air, stretch your legs, and get used to the geography of the Umbral Basin..."
Aurelia blinked, nodding instinctively.
"I would be honored to accompany you, Lord Silas and if we encounter powerful beasts, I can activate the Argent Flame’s soul-link to ensure your safety—"
"No," Silas cut in instantly, pointing a teasing, yet completely uncompromising finger at her.
"I told you last night: the immortality link is permanently banned.
You are not absorbing anyone’s damage."
Aurelia’s brow furrowed, a sudden burst of exasperated genuine frustration leaking through her formal facade.
"Why do you care so much?!" Aurelia blurted out, leaning forward in her chair.
"Every ruler in existence would kill to have an immortal vanguard...
It costs you nothing!
Why are you so stubbornly refusing the greatest defensive weapon in this world?!"
Silas didn’t get angry at her outburst.
Instead, he reached across the polished oak desk, gently taking hold of her small delicate hand.
"Hm?"
He slowly threaded his fingers through hers as his warm calloused palm rested snugly against her pale skin.
Aurelia froze, her breath catching as an intense burning blush exploded across her porcelain cheeks.
"I care," Silas said softly, his eyes locking onto hers with unwavering sincerity, "because I care about my people.
Every single one of them and that includes you, Aurelia.
Your life is not a consumable shield."
Aurelia swallowed hard, her heart pounding wildly against her ribs like a trapped bird as she desperately tried to maintain her composure, looking down at their joined hands.
If I didn’t know any better, my Lord..." Aurelia stammered, her voice trembling slightly, "...I would think you were flirting with me."
Silas chuckled softly, a playful charming glint flashing in his eyes.
"Who knows?" Silas replied with a smooth teasing smirk.
"I just might be."
Aurelia’s mind went into overload.
’No... no, no, no,’ Aurelia screamed internally, her face burning hotter than a blast furnace as she fought to pull her gaze away from his devastatingly handsome smile. ’This is a trick!
It won’t work on me!
I already have experience with charming Heroes!
Cassian whispered sweet promises under the stars too, and look where that led—’
THUMP!
Her heart skipped a violent traitorous beat.
A wave of fluster washed over her, making her toes curl inside her slippers.
’Why... why is my heart racing like this?!’ she panicked, biting her lower lip. ’Why am I already coming to like him so much?!
Am I really that easy?!
I’ve only known this man for less than twelve hours!’
Before Silas could tease the hopelessly blushing Saintess any further—
VUUUUUUUUUM!
A massive ear-splitting cosmic vibration tore through the atmosphere above the Blessed Land.
The ambient mana in the room violently fluctuated, causing the communication crystals on Silas’s desk to flare with unstable light.
Silas’s playful expression instantly vanished, replaced by cold razor-sharp focus.
He released Aurelia’s hand, shooting up from his chair in a single fluid motion and striding swiftly toward the panoramic floor-to-ceiling windows overlooking the territory.
Aurelia bolted to her feet, rushing up beside him.
Outside, the morning sky above the Umbral Basin had completely transformed.
The clear blue heavens had turned a brilliant incandescent shade of liquid gold.
The light was so intense it completely vaporized the morning clouds, clearing away the lingering snow across the entire basin in a matter of seconds.
High above the territory, the golden sky fractured.
A colossal swirling spatial vortex tore open in the upper atmosphere... a majestic blinding rift that radiated an overwhelming suffocating pressure of ancient divine thunder.
Silas leaned forward, his golden ringed eyes narrowing to fine points as he stared into the swirling golden rift.
"Something..." Silas murmured, his voice dead serious as the air in the room crackled with static electricity.
"...Something is coming from Asgard."
