paragraphs: The penthouse suite in the upper tier of Rhyx City was quiet, save for the steady drumming of rain against the reinforced glass.
Standing before a floor-to-ceiling mirror framed in polished mahogany, the Princess tilted her head slightly, adjusting the silken fall of her royal-blue hair.
Her locks cascaded over her shoulders in immaculate liquid waves, catching the soft, recessed lighting of the vanity.
She hummed a light delicate melody beneath her breath, a courtly tune from the central provinces that felt far removed from the hum of the metropolis below.
Today was not an ordinary day.
Today was the day she was scheduled to journey into the Sovereign Realm... specifically to the contested land of the Umbral Basin where Blessed Land resided.
She smoothed down the front of her attire with deliberate unhurried grace.
It was a modest gown of pale celestial silk, embroidered along the hem with subtle gold crests that denoted imperial lineage without being overly ostentatious.
There were no heavy ceremonial mantles or ostentatious diadems as she had deliberately chosen an ensemble that walked the fine line between aristocratic dignity and understated refinement.
She turned her head, her clear azure eyes meeting the nervous gaze of her personal maid who stood waiting near the dressing screen with a folded stole over her arms.
"Tell me, Mira," the Princess spoke, her voice measured, calm, and smooth as polished jade. "Do you believe Lord Vespera will find this presentable?"
The maid swallowed hard, fidgeting with the hem of the stole before bowing her head in a hurried flustered stammer.

"Y-Yes, Your Imperial Highness! Without a doubt! It... it is refined, elegant, and perfectly balances your stature with modesty. The Lord of Blessed Land would certainly be honored by your appearance if you met her!"
The Princess offered a faint, amused smile, nodding gently. "Good. That will be all, Mira. You may leave me."
"Understood, Highness."
The maid bowed deeply once more and retreated through the heavy double doors, letting them click shut with a soft, pneumatic hiss.
Left alone in the expansive suite, the Princess walked slowly toward the adjoining private quarters.
It was a simple modest dress.
She wasn’t an idiot... she knew she wasn’t embarking on this clandestine journey to seduce the mysterious female Lord who had crushed the forces of the Unmovable Wall.
’My reasons are very personal.’
She reached her bedchamber, stepping across the plush carpet, and gently closed the interior door behind her.
As the latch locked into place, the serene composed mask she wore for the household staff subtly cracked.
Her right hand, adorned with a delicate ring of suppression quartz, began to tremble. She lowered her gaze to her manicured fingers, watching them shake with cold bitter familiarity.

’This is all I will ever be,’ she thought, a suffocating weight settling over her chest like lead. ’A Princess in name... A Princess in budget... A decorative ornament to be displayed at state galas and imperial banquets...’
In the grand hierarchy of the Supreme Royal Family, bloodline was only the baseline.
True power, true standing, and the right to inherit the stars were dictated entirely by the awakening of a Lord Core.
Her older brother, the Crown Prince, had awakened a Purple Lord Core at the age of sixteen, commanding vast legions across the mid-tier battlefields of the Sovereign Realm.

Even the illegitimate halfling child... the girl her Imperial Father had fathered with a commoner from the lower rim sectors had manifested a Purple core too, instantly elevating the bastard into the inner circle of imperial succession with territorial grants and private war fleets.
And then there was her.
She had stood before the Great Awakening Obelisk on her sixteenth birthday, surrounded by thousands of expectant nobles, high patriarchs, and imperial cameras.
And when her hand had touched the cold celestial stone... nothing had happened.
There was not a flicker of mana...
From that single second onward, her fate had been sealed.

She was not an heir... she was an asset. A political pawn to be maintained with lavish allowances, housed in gilded penthouses, and eventually bartered away into a convenient arranged marriage to cement a treaty with some ancient clan or corporate syndicate.
It was a confusing hollow existence... living in the apex of luxury while having zero agency over her own destiny.

Yet, when reports of the Blessed Land had crossed her weeks ago... when she had read about a powerful territory that then crushed the Unmovable Wall as well... a strange unexplainable tug had pulled at her heart.

She didn’t know why, but whenever she read the dispatches regarding that strange fortified territory, she felt an irrational instinctual pull, as if going there might somehow shatter the suffocating invisible walls that surrounded her life.
She walked to the panoramic floor-to-ceiling windows overlooking the rain-slicked towers of Rhyx City.
She unlatched the central pane, pushing the heavy glass outward.
A gust of wet humid wind rushed into the warm room, carrying the cold scent of the storm.
The rain was coming down in thick relentless sheets, drumming against the exterior terrace and blurring the neon skylines of the lower districts into streaks of cyan and magenta.
She looked up into the dark swirling storm clouds, pulling her silk fan from her sash and lightly tapping it against her open palm.
’Will she actually arrive in this downpour?’ the Princess mused silently. ’Even for a deity of Asgard, flying into an urban air-space like this without clearance is—’
KRA-BOOOOOOOOM!
The sky above the penthouse did not simply flash... it tore apart.
A colossal pillar of pure, incandescent golden lightning descended from the upper stratosphere, piercing the storm clouds with apocalyptic speed.

The bolt did not strike the terrace as it detonated directly in mid-air mere inches from the open window, releasing an ear-splitting thunderclap that shattered the surrounding rain into vapor and kicked up a violent concussive shockwave of displaced air that whipped the Princess’s royal-blue hair and silk drapes wildly into the room.
But it did not harm her...
When the blinding golden static dispersed, a towering muscled figure was hovering casually in the open air, completely unbothered by gravity.
Thor stood with wild unkempt blonde hair falling in thick, untamed waves over broad, corded shoulders that possessed the raw power of a battle-hardened god.

Her storm-blue eyes crackled with residual arcs of electricity and clad in her heavy silver battle armor with the ancient short-handled war hammer Mjölnir strapped securely to her hip, she looked like a walking cataclysm.
"GWAHAHAHA!"
Thor’s booming full-chested laughter reverberated through the penthouse, rattling the crystal chandeliers and vibrating right through the floorboards.

"Greetings, little Princess!" Thor bellowed with a grin that showed off her sharp fearless canines. "The weather out here is perfect for a flight! I remember I finished off that six-star roasted drake feast your chefs prepared, so I am a woman of my word! Are you ready to depart for this Blessed Land, or are you still admiring your ribbons?"
The Princess didn’t flinch from the thunder, nor did she cower before the raw divine aura washing over her terrace.
She simply snapped her silk fan shut with a sharp clack, hiding a fond composed smile behind the jade-inlaid ribs.

"I have been ready, Lady Thor," the Princess replied smoothly, stepping up to the edge of the terrace and extending her delicate unblemished hand toward the God of Thunder. "Let us not keep the Sovereign Realm waiting..."
Thor grinned widely, reaching out with her massive calloused hand and taking the Princess’s fingers.
In a single effortless motion, the Daughter of Odin scooped the royal maiden up, cradling her securely in a broad ironclad princess carry against her silver breastplate.
"Highness!"
The interior doors of the suite were suddenly thrown open as three royal security maids rushed onto the terrace, their sidearms drawn in panic.

"Lady Thor, release the Princess at once!" the lead maid cried, though the terror in her eyes betrayed the lack of any real venom in her voice. "Taking an imperial scion without official flight manifests violates seventeen sector treaties!"
"Tell your sector treaties to catch me first! GWAHAHAHA!" Thor roared with delighted mockery, completely ignoring the drawn weapons.
Thor shifted her stance in mid-air, looking down at the blue-haired girl in her arms. "Hold your breath, little one! The air up here gets thin enough to choke a frost giant!"
The Princess immediately closed her lips, drawing in a deep lung-filling breath and pressing her face against the cold silver of Thor’s armor.
VUUUUUUM... BOOM!
A blinding golden corona of pure Asgardian thunder-mana enveloped them like an impenetrable sphere.
With a deafening sonic boom that blew the remaining rain away from the entire penthouse district, Thor shot straight upward into the heavens.

The city of Rhyx shrunk into a microscopic grid of neon specks in less than two seconds as they tore through the cloud layer, ascending with hypersonic acceleration into the upper stratosphere where the blackness of space met the curvature of the planet.
The atmospheric pressure dropped to zero, but inside the golden lightning sphere, the Princess felt neither the crushing G-force nor the freezing void.
Her azure eyes went wide with pure breathless awe as the entire world expanded beneath them... an ocean of clouds painted gold by the rising sun.
"Hold on tight!" Thor’s voice echoed directly into her mind. "We’re breaking the planar seal!"
The golden sphere accelerated, warping the space around them until the physical universe blurred into streaks of liquid starlight.
FLASH!
In less than a heartbeat, their physical presence completely vanished from the mortal planet.
When the Princess opened her eyes, the biting cold of the upper atmosphere was gone, replaced by a warm fragrant breeze that smelled of blooming wildflowers and morning dew.
She blinked, taking in her surroundings.
They were standing in an immense tranquil celestial garden that seemed to stretch infinitely in all directions.
Colossal, luminous trees with silver bark and golden leaves arched overhead, shading lush emerald lawns dotted with crystalline ponds.

Scattered throughout this peaceful realm were dozens of colossal, free-standing archways... towering stone portals carved from pristine white marble and ancient runic slate, each one swirling with a different color of concentrated spatial mana.
Some burned with the crimson fire of the infernal planes, others hummed with the deep azure of oceanic rifts, and many stood dormant, their stone surfaces covered in moss.
Resting near the base of a towering, spear-shaped obelisk in the center of the garden was a solitary guardian.
He was a tall, imposing man with a completely bald head, his dark skin etched with intricate glowing white tribal marks that pulsed every few seconds.
In his right hand, he held a massive obsidian-tipped spear that rested against his shoulder.
The bald guardian lowered his spear slightly, his stoic timeless gaze locking onto the God of Thunder as she set the Princess down onto the soft grass.
"Greetings, Executioner of the Deities," the guardian spoke. "I am the Guardian of the Outer Gates. What brings the Daughter of Odin to the crossroads of the realms?"
Thor rested her hands on her hips, her heavy silver armor clanking as she tossed her wild blonde mane back with an easy grin.

"At ease, Gatekeeper! I’m taking a little detour to the lower sovereign basins. I need an active portal... specifically, the one that’s barely being used these days. I think it’s known as the forgotten one."
The guardian’s brow furrowed beneath his glowing markings. "The forgotten gate? You speak of the rift that connects to the jagged hollows of the Umbral Basin?"
"That’s the one!" Thor nodded boisterously. "Point me in the right direction, spear-man!"
The guardian turned, extending his obsidian spear toward the far eastern edge of the garden, where the tranquil atmosphere began to rapidly deteriorate.

"The eastern perimeter," the guardian warned solemnly. "The spatial currents in that sector have suffered extreme degradation due to anomalous dimensional shifts... The weather phenomena beyond that threshold are violent and completely erratic so proceed with caution."
"Erratic weather is my favorite kind of weather! GWAHAHAHA!" Thor laughed, stepping forward and scooping the Princess back into her arms before the girl could even take two steps.
"Hold on to your fan, Princess!" Thor warned with a wicked grin.
WHOOSH!
Thor took to the air in a low-altitude glide, flying across the vast celestial garden toward the eastern boundary.
As they crossed the threshold, the Princess watched in fascination as the serene, sunny garden instantly gave way to a chaotic fractured expanse.
The sky above them turned into a swirling mosaic of contradictory elemental storms.

In one sector, heavy, crystalline snow fell in thick sheets, dropping the temperature to sub-zero levels; mere yards away, a blazing artificial sun shone with searing desert heat; above that, violent purple lightning danced through rainstorms that fell sideways against localized gravity wells.
"This is fascinating..." the Princess murmured, her voice steady despite the apocalyptic elemental clash occurring around them.
She reached out, but her fingers encountered a solid frictionless barrier of golden lightning that Thor maintained around her, completely neutralizing the extreme temperatures and pressure.
Thor hovered to a halt in front of the eastern gate.
"I knew it..." Thor muttered, her storm-blue eyes narrowing with sharp, analytical interest.𝒇𝒓𝒆𝒆𝙬𝒆𝒃𝓷𝒐𝓿𝙚𝙡.𝒄𝓸𝒎
The portal before them was colossal... easily fifty yards wide, framed by jagged, dark-iron megaliths covered in frost.
But unlike the stable tranquil portals in the garden, this gate was violently awake.
Swirling currents of thick, frigid snow were actively being sucked into the golden spatial vortex at the center, creating a massive swirling blizzard that howled like a caged beast.

The Princess immediately closed her lips, drawing in a deep lung-filling breath and pressing her face against the cold silver of Thor’s armor.
VUUUUUUM...
BOOM!
A blinding golden corona of pure Asgardian thunder-mana enveloped them like an impenetrable sphere.
With a deafening sonic boom that blew the remaining rain away from the entire penthouse district, Thor shot straight upward into the heavens.

The city of Rhyx shrunk into a microscopic grid of neon specks in less than two seconds as they tore through the cloud layer, ascending with hypersonic acceleration into the upper stratosphere where the blackness of space met the curvature of the planet.
The atmospheric pressure dropped to zero, but inside the golden lightning sphere, the Princess felt neither the crushing G-force nor the freezing void.
Her azure eyes went wide with pure breathless awe as the entire world expanded beneath them... an ocean of clouds painted gold by the rising sun.
"Hold on tight!" Thor’s voice echoed directly into her mind.
"We’re breaking the planar seal!"
The golden sphere accelerated, warping the space around them until the physical universe blurred into streaks of liquid starlight.
FLASH!
In less than a heartbeat, their physical presence completely vanished from the mortal planet.
When the Princess opened her eyes, the biting cold of the upper atmosphere was gone, replaced by a warm fragrant breeze that smelled of blooming wildflowers and morning dew.
She blinked, taking in her surroundings.
They were standing in an immense tranquil celestial garden that seemed to stretch infinitely in all directions.
Colossal, luminous trees with silver bark and golden leaves arched overhead, shading lush emerald lawns dotted with crystalline ponds.

Scattered throughout this peaceful realm were dozens of colossal, free-standing archways... towering stone portals carved from pristine white marble and ancient runic slate, each one swirling with a different color of concentrated spatial mana.
Some burned with the crimson fire of the infernal planes, others hummed with the deep azure of oceanic rifts, and many stood dormant, their stone surfaces covered in moss.
Resting near the base of a towering, spear-shaped obelisk in the center of the garden was a solitary guardian.
He was a tall, imposing man with a completely bald head, his dark skin etched with intricate glowing white tribal marks that pulsed every few seconds.
In his right hand, he held a massive obsidian-tipped spear that rested against his shoulder.
The bald guardian lowered his spear slightly, his stoic timeless gaze locking onto the God of Thunder as she set the Princess down onto the soft grass.
"Greetings, Executioner of the Deities," the guardian spoke.
"I am the Guardian of the Outer Gates.
What brings the Daughter of Odin to the crossroads of the realms?"
Thor rested her hands on her hips, her heavy silver armor clanking as she tossed her wild blonde mane back with an easy grin.
"At ease, Gatekeeper!
I’m taking a little detour to the lower sovereign basins.
I need an active portal... specifically, the one that’s barely being used these days.
I think it’s known as the forgotten one."
The guardian’s brow furrowed beneath his glowing markings.
"The forgotten gate?
You speak of the rift that connects to the jagged hollows of the Umbral Basin?"
"That’s the one!" Thor nodded boisterously.
"Point me in the right direction, spear-man!"
The guardian turned, extending his obsidian spear toward the far eastern edge of the garden, where the tranquil atmosphere began to rapidly deteriorate.
"The eastern perimeter," the guardian warned solemnly.
"The spatial currents in that sector have suffered extreme degradation due to anomalous dimensional shifts...
The weather phenomena beyond that threshold are violent and completely erratic so proceed with caution."
"Erratic weather is my favorite kind of weather!
GWAHAHAHA!" Thor laughed, stepping forward and scooping the Princess back into her arms before the girl could even take two steps.
"Hold on to your fan, Princess!" Thor warned with a wicked grin.
WHOOSH!
Thor took to the air in a low-altitude glide, flying across the vast celestial garden toward the eastern boundary.
As they crossed the threshold, the Princess watched in fascination as the serene, sunny garden instantly gave way to a chaotic fractured expanse.
The sky above them turned into a swirling mosaic of contradictory elemental storms.

In one sector, heavy, crystalline snow fell in thick sheets, dropping the temperature to sub-zero levels; mere yards away, a blazing artificial sun shone with searing desert heat; above that, violent purple lightning danced through rainstorms that fell sideways against localized gravity wells.
"This is fascinating..." the Princess murmured, her voice steady despite the apocalyptic elemental clash occurring around them.
She reached out, but her fingers encountered a solid frictionless barrier of golden lightning that Thor maintained around her, completely neutralizing the extreme temperatures and pressure.
Thor hovered to a halt in front of the eastern gate.
"I knew it..." Thor muttered, her storm-blue eyes narrowing with sharp, analytical interest.𝒇𝒓𝒆𝒆𝙬𝒆𝒃𝓷𝒐𝓿𝙚𝙡.𝒄𝓸𝒎
The portal before them was colossal... easily fifty yards wide, framed by jagged, dark-iron megaliths covered in frost.
But unlike the stable tranquil portals in the garden, this gate was violently awake.
Swirling currents of thick, frigid snow were actively being sucked into the golden spatial vortex at the center, creating a massive swirling blizzard that howled like a caged beast.

chapters.title: Chapter 432: Thor In Blessed Land [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: "This gate has been siphoning Asgardian frost-drafts straight into the basin for days," Thor observed with a sharp, toothy grin. "No wonder that little territory down there had so much snow to shovel initially!"
She rolled her broad shoulders, letting out a deep booming laugh that cut straight through the howling wind.
"Let’s go in with a proper bang! GWAHAHAHA!"
Thor’s body erupted into a blinding torrential inferno of golden thunder-mana.
The air around them ionized into ozone, and with a single earth-shattering thrust of her legs, the God of Thunder plunged straight into the center of the swirling chaotic vortex.
CRACK!

Once again, the Princess felt the surreal disorienting sensation of her physical body dissolving into pure conceptual momentum, traveling across the dimensional ether in the fraction of a millisecond.
SHATTER!
Reality violently reformed, and they broke through the upper cloud layer with a deafening sonic crack.
The Princess opened her azure eyes, looking down as the blinding golden light dissipated.
Stretching out beneath them was the colossal expanse of the Umbral Basin.
The basin was a breathtaking savage realm of towering obsidian cliffs, winding river canyons, and ancient forests.

Under normal circumstances, an Unawakened mortal... someone lacking a Lord Core or high-tier cultivation meridians would have had their internal organs instantly crushed by the suffocating environmental pressure of the Sovereign Realm.

However, resting against the Princess’s chest beneath her silk gown was a small, glowing pendant carved from Celestial Anchor Quartz... an ultra-rare multi-million-credit imperial artifact specifically engineered to stabilize the biology of non-awakened within the Sovereign Realm.
Thanks to the relic, she breathed the crisp air without the slightest discomfort.
She looked ahead, her eyes widening as she spotted the massive fortified stone walls of a territory rising proudly from the valley floor.
The Blessed Land.
The fortress was magnificent, enclosed by reinforced ramparts lined with glowing blue defense runes.

"There it is!" Thor called out, her voice booming over the wind as she hovered in the sky above the perimeter. "I can see the main Keep in the center! And more importantly... I can feel the unmistakable signature of the domain’s Lord radiating right from the top floor!"
The Princess tapped Thor’s armored shoulder with her silk fan, leaning in close.
"Lady Thor, approach at maximum speed, but do not release any destructive shockwaves. I wish to catch this Lord completely off-guard..."
Thor glanced down at the blue-haired girl, a mischievous and thoroughly amused smirk spreading across her face.
"Catch her off-guard, you mean?" Thor teased, recalling the reports that Blessed Land was ruled by a woman named Vespera. "Alright, little Princess! Let’s see what this Lord is made of!"
BOOM!
Thor shot forward like a falling meteor.

She blurred into a streak of gold, moving with such absurd low-altitude speed that she bypassed the outer palisades, zipped past the patrolling Shieldmaidens in the training rings, and crossed the central courtyard before anyone could even register the gust of wind.
In less than half a second, Thor decelerated from hypersonic speed to a complete dead stop directly outside the panoramic glass window of the Keep’s top-floor office.

Though Thor had strictly suppressed her destructive kinetic force as the Princess requested, the Daughter of Odin couldn’t resist letting out a tiny, concentrated pulse of raw divine thunder-mana... just enough to test the reflexes and psychological fortitude of the territory’s ruler.
CRASH! SHATTER!
The massive reinforced glass pane of the window exploded inward, shattering into tens of thousands of sparkling diamond-like crystalline shards that rained across the office carpet.
Standing directly on the other side of the shattered window, bathed in the morning sunlight, was Silas.𝒇𝓻𝓮𝓮𝙬𝙚𝒃𝒏𝓸𝙫𝒆𝙡.𝓬𝓸𝒎
Silas did not flinch.
He did not duck, he did not dive behind his heavy oak desk, and his clear blue eyes didn’t even blink as the glass shrapnel exploded around him.
He simply stood tall, his dark robes hanging straight against his frame and his Gold Core humming with calm stability as he looked at the two women floating outside his office.
Silas let out a soft dry breath with his eyebrows raising slightly.
"Ah..." Silas muttered, completely unfazed by the sudden home invasion.
Thor hovered in the open gap, resting her hands on her hips as her wild blonde hair danced in the breeze.
"Greetings, mortal!" Thor’s booming voice filled the entire top floor with deafening cheer. "I am Thor! God of Thunder, Daughter of Odin, and Executioner for the Council of Deities!"
She shifted her arm, gesturing grandly to the composed, blue-haired maiden in her grasp. "And this quiet little beauty beside me is the Princess of the Human World where you hail from!"
Thor paused, her storm-blue eyes narrowing as she peered closely into Silas’s face. A spark of sudden, sharp recognition flashed across her features.
"Hold on a moment..." Thor rumbled, leaning forward in the air. "Haven’t we crossed paths before, lad?"
Silas gave a slow, calm nod, his lips twitching into a slight wry smile. "We have. Back in Ititius’s Secret—"

Before Silas could finish his sentence, Thor leaned all the way through the shattered window frame, reached out with her massive, iron-plated gauntlet, and firmly patted Silas right on top of his head with heavy thuds.
PAT! PAT! PAT!

"GWAHAHAHA!" Thor laughed with booming, unrestrained delight, ruffling his dark hair like an affectionate older sister. "I knew it! You’ve got a fantastic, remarkably pattable head on your shoulders, boy!"
Her eyes widened in sudden realization as she pulled her hand back, pointing a thick finger directly at his chest.
"I remember that aura! You’re that ridiculous Gold Core brat from the Secret Realm! The one who possesses a Gold core just like my old man, Odin!"
Thor threw her head back, laughing so hard the floorboards trembled.
"So it was you all along! You’re the true Lord of Blessed Land, not some female phantom named Vespera! GWAHAHAHA! What a magnificent shameless trick!"
Floating in Thor’s arms, the Princess’s mouth slowly parted into a perfect, silent ’O’ of pure, unadulterated shock.
Her azure eyes darted from Silas’s calm, masculine face to his broad shoulders, then to the signet ring on his finger.

’The Lord of Blessed Land... is a man?’ the Princess’s mind reeled in complete disbelief. ’Every single intelligence dossier from the Central Guild claimed Blessed Land was founded by an elite female Lord. The entire military apparatus was deceived...’
Silas sighed softly, running a hand through his ruffled hair.

The entire sequence of events had unfolded in less than three seconds... one moment he had seen a golden flash in the sky, and the next, an Asgardian deity was patting his head and exposing his deepest identity secret in front of a princess.
It wasn’t looking good.
"Before the window finishes healing," Silas said, stepping back from the ledge and gesturing into the room, "you two should probably step inside."
Thor stepped through the open gap, setting the Princess lightly onto her feet upon the plush woolen rug.
HUMMM!
The moment their boots cleared the threshold, the territory’s self-repair enchantments flared to life.

The shattered glass fragments on the floor dissolved into glowing blue mana particles, rising into the air and reforming into a pristine flawless glass pane that sealed the room back into silent climate-controlled comfort.
Silas calmly walked back to his desk, taking a seat in his high-backed leather chair.
Standing vigilantly to his right was Aurelia.

The platinum-haired Saintess had stepped forward the moment the glass shattered, her pure white robes rustling as her golden-amber eyes locked onto the newcomers with defensive focus and her hands subtly glowing with the dormant silver light of the Argent Flame.

Thor casually pulled up one of the heavy guest armchairs, sprawling into it with her legs kicked wide, while the Princess smoothed her skirts and sat gracefully in the adjacent chair, snapping her silk fan open to fan herself with practiced composure.
BAM!
The heavy mahogany doors of the sovereign office were violently kicked open, slamming hard against the stone walls with a deafening crack.
Standing in the doorway, barefoot and radiating a terrifying suffocating aura of oceanic pressure, was Morwenna.
The Dread Queen held Tidebringer drawn in her right hand, the curved saber blazing with an intense blue heartbeat as her stormy gray eyes swept across the room with murderous fury.
"Captain!" Morwenna barked. "Are you alright?! Who breached the sanctum?!"
Silas raised a calm hand, meeting his Pirate Queen’s frantic gaze with a reassuring nod.
"I’m fine, Morwenna. Stand down... They aren’t enemies."
Morwenna’s tense coiled stance subtly relaxed, though she kept her fingers firmly wrapped around Tidebringer’s hilt.
Sitting in the armchair, Thor’s storm-blue eyes lit up with intense warrior-appreciation as she looked over the scarred wild-haired Dread Queen.

"Oho!" Thor grinned broadly, leaning forward and resting her elbows on her knees. "Now that is a proper warrior! Look at that stance! Look at that terrifying bloodlust! You’ve got fine steel in your soul, woman! How about you and I step down into the dirt right now and have a glorious bone-crushing brawl?!"
Morwenna let out a long dismissive sigh, rolling her eyes as she prepared to scoff.
"I’m not interested in wasting my energy on random brawlers, muscle-brain—"
Morwenna paused mid-sentence.
Her stormy gray eyes narrowed into razor blades as she focused on the divine mana radiating from Thor’s silver breastplate and Mjölnir’s runic head.
"Wait a second..." Morwenna’s voice dropped into a low, terrifying growl, the temperature in the room instantly plummeting as the air grew humid and salty. "Are you... a God?"
Thor grinned, tapping her chest plate with an iron thumb. "God of Thunder, Daughter of Odin! At your service, sailor!"
VUUUUUUUUUM!
In less than a fraction of a millisecond, the entire office felt as though it had been violently plunged ten thousand leagues beneath the surface of a sunless crushing ocean trench.
Morwenna’s eyes darkened into pitch-black voids.

The runes along Tidebringer ignited with blinding luminescence, and the ghostly silhouette of a colossal world-swallowing Leviathan manifested behind her shoulders, bearing its fangs at the Asgardian deity.
Centuries of deep burning hatred for the divine pantheons that had chained her in the dark abyss surged to the surface in a single explosive breath.
Thor’s eyes widened with ecstasy.

"GWAHAHAHA! YES! THIS IS MAGNIFICENT!" Thor roared, her hands reaching toward the leather grip of Mjölnir as crackling golden lightning erupted from her armor. "SHOW ME WHAT AN ABYSSAL CALAMITY CAN DO—"
CLAP!
A single sharp clap echoed through the room.
Instantly, the crushing ocean pressure vanished and the blinding golden lightning snapped out of existence.
Both Morwenna and Thor froze, their momentum violently arrested by Silas’s command.
Silas lowered his hands, looking between the two mythic monsters with a deadpan unimpressed expression.

"You two are not going at it in my office," Silas stated flatly, his voice carrying an unquestionable tone of leadership. "I just had this desk polished, and I am not having my floorboards vaporized because you two want to measure your divine dicks. If you want to spar, you will wait until Aeliana finishes her daily rounds so she can erect a barrier for you two. Am I clear?"
Morwenna clicked her tongue, sheathing Tidebringer with a sharp clack.
"Tch. Fine, Captain. But I’m taking the first swing when the barrier goes up."

"GWAHAHAHA! Deal!" Thor laughed boisterously, releasing her hammer and slumping back into her chair with a satisfied smirk. "I like your style, boy! A Lord who can stop the actions of even high ranking beings with a single clap has my respect!"
Sitting beside Thor, the Princess watched the entire exchange from behind her silk fan, her azure eyes shimmering with deep astonishment.

’He just gave orders to the God of Thunder and his Hero... and both of them obeyed without hesitation,’ the Princess thought, her heart racing beneath her silk gown. ’Even the High Emperors of the Central Alliance speak to Thor with trembling formal diplomacy. This man commands them like an older brother managing unruly children.’
Thor leaned forward once more, reaching across the desk and planting another heavy, affectionate pat on Silas’s dark head...
PAT! PAT!

"I’m here for two reasons, lad!" Thor declared with booming cheer. "First, I heard you brought a magnificent dragon-hybrid into your territory, and I want to see her! And second, I came to personally congratulate you! I watched the crystal feeds of your war against the Unmovable Wall... crushing an entire army with raw strategy and force was peak combat! Odin himself would have raised a horn of mead to your victory!"
Silas smiled, accepting the compliment with a gracious nod, though he quickly reached up and gently swatted Thor’s iron gauntlet away from his hair.
"Thank you, Thor. I appreciate the praise," Silas said with a dry chuckle. "Now please, stop patting my head. I’m a Lord, not a golden retriever."
"GWAHAHAHA! I’ll think about it!" Thor laughed loudly, completely unapologetic.
Silas shook his head with an amused sigh, turning his full attention toward the elegant blue-haired noblewoman sitting quietly in the guest chair.
"Now then..." Silas leaned his forearms on his desk, his blue eyes locking onto the Princess with calm scrutiny. "You’ve been remarkably quiet. Who might you be?"
The Princess lowered her silk fan, resting her hands neatly in her lap as she offered a flawless, courtly bow of her head.
"I am the Princess of the Lord World," she introduced herself softly.

"I’m here for two reasons, lad!" Thor declared with booming cheer.
"First, I heard you brought a magnificent dragon-hybrid into your territory, and I want to see her!
And second, I came to personally congratulate you!
I watched the crystal feeds of your war against the Unmovable Wall... crushing an entire army with raw strategy and force was peak combat!
Odin himself would have raised a horn of mead to your victory!"
Silas smiled, accepting the compliment with a gracious nod, though he quickly reached up and gently swatted Thor’s iron gauntlet away from his hair.
"Thank you, Thor.
I appreciate the praise," Silas said with a dry chuckle.
"Now please, stop patting my head.
I’m a Lord, not a golden retriever."
"GWAHAHAHA!
I’ll think about it!" Thor laughed loudly, completely unapologetic.
Silas shook his head with an amused sigh, turning his full attention toward the elegant blue-haired noblewoman sitting quietly in the guest chair.
"Now then..." Silas leaned his forearms on his desk, his blue eyes locking onto the Princess with calm scrutiny.
"You’ve been remarkably quiet.
Who might you be?"
The Princess lowered her silk fan, resting her hands neatly in her lap as she offered a flawless, courtly bow of her head.
"I am the Princess of the Lord World," she introduced herself softly.

chapters.title: Chapter 433: The Princess Threatens [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Silas blinked while waiting for her to continue. When several seconds of silence passed, he tilted his head in mild confusion.
"And... do you have a name?" Silas asked.
The Princess offered a self-deprecating smile that carried a touch of bittersweet sorrow.
"It appears you do not have a complete understanding of how the Supreme Royal Family operates, Lord..." she paused first as she did not know his name.
"Silas."

"Lord Silas..." The Princess continued in a calm musical voice. "In our lineage, those born under the Royal bloodline are granted the title of Prince or Princess of the World at birth. However... If a scion fails to awaken a Lord Core upon their sixteenth to eighteenth year, the law dictates that they are left permanently nameless by their parents. Furthermore, we are strictly forbidden by law from bestowing a name upon ourselves."
She paused, gesturing lightly to herself.

"I fall under that exact category. While I carry the royal blood in my veins and enjoy the boundless material wealth of a Royal princess... I failed to awaken. In the eyes of the High Empire, I am merely an unawakened pawn. Nameless, and waiting to be traded."
Silas listened quietly, a flicker of deep understanding empathy passing through his blue eyes.
Beside him, Aurelia’s expression softened, the Saintess recognizing the familiar tragic scent of someone discarded by their own realm.
The Princess’s azure eyes suddenly sharpened as an incredibly dangerous glint danced beneath her noble composure.
She leaned forward slightly, resting her chin on her fingers as she looked Silas dead in the eye.

"Now then, Lord of Blessed Land..." the Princess began, her tone shifting into that of a razor-sharp prosecutor. "I hope you are fully aware of the legal magnitude of what has transpired in this room."
Silas raised an eyebrow, gesturing for her to continue.

"According to the Central Governance Accord of the Sovereign Realm," the Princess recited flawlessly, "forging an official sovereign identity... Specifically, making this domain known under the false name of a female warlord named ’Vespera’ while you are, in fact, a man constitutes a Class-A Fraud Violation. Furthermore, fabricating identification documents and deceiving the Central Guild’s regulatory committee carries a mandatory sentence of sixty years in the deep penitentiary mines of the outer rim."
Silas didn’t flinch as an amused smirk played on his lips. "Is that so?"

"Indeed," the Princess smiled, snapping her silk fan open and fluttering it gently against her collarbone. "If I were to dispatch a single encrypted communication to the High Court right now, three grand inquisitor fleets would descend upon the Umbral Basin before nightfall to strip your territorial core..."

’That’s if they managed to find it...’ The Princess thought, she had no way of dispatching anything and that was if they even took her seriously which they would not. ’I’m not the Gold core after all.’
She paused, letting the dramatic silence hang in the air for two seconds before her lips curved into a warm unapologetic grin.

"However..." the Princess continued, her azure eyes sparkling with genuine adventurous delight, "...I am willing to overlook all seventeen counts of fraud, permanently seal the investigation dossiers, and maintain your secret from the world."
Silas tilted his head, thoroughly entertained by the royal negotiation. "And what, exactly, is the price of your silence, Princess?"
The Princess snapped her fan shut with a crisp clack, pointing the gilded tip directly at Silas’s chest.
"I want you to let me stay here," the Princess declared boldly with her smile widening. "Show me what it truly means to be a part of Blessed Land for one full week."
The silence in the office was thick, broken only by the sound of the newly reconstructed runic glass sealing the room against the morning breeze.
Silas sat back in his heavy dark-oak chair, his fingers loosely laced together over the polished mahogany surface.
He studied the blue-haired royal maiden seated across from him, his clear blue eyes unmoved by her noble posture.
"Stay in Blessed Land for an entire week?" Silas repeated then he frowned. "No."
The Princess blinked.
The delicate practiced smile on her porcelain face remained intact, though the slight twitch at the corner of her azure eyes betrayed her sudden disbelief.
She snapped her silk fan open with a soft clack, resting the ribs against her palm.

"I beg your pardon, Lord Silas?" she inquired, keeping her tone light and thoroughly composed though she was nervous. "Did you not hear the terms of the proposal? I am offering you complete unconditional immunity from fraud inquiries. The truth regarding ’Lord Vespera’ will never reach the real world, the inquisitorial division will never cast their gaze toward the Umbral Basin, and you will maintain yourself without Royal interference. In exchange, all I ask is seven days within your domain..."
"I heard you perfectly," Silas answered, leaning forward and resting his forearms against the desk. "And the answer is still no."
"May I ask why?"

"Because you’re an Unawakened," Silas stated bluntly, leaving zero room for interpretation. "You don’t possess a Lord Core... You don’t have refined spiritual meridians, you don’t circulate mana, and your physical constitution is that of an ordinary mortal woman. The Sovereign Realm isn’t a royal resort where pampered nobles go on vacation... The atmospheric pressure in this basin alone is dense enough to crush an ordinary human’s lungs over prolonged exposure. The moment you step outside from Thor’s safety, the spiritual gravity will grind your joints to dust. You wouldn’t last forty-eight hours."
A haughty glint danced in the Princess’s azure eyes.
She didn’t look offended... rather, she looked as though she had anticipated this exact objection from the very moment she stepped through the portal.
With an elegant fluid sweep of her silk-embroidered sleeve, she reached toward the neckline of her gown and the small velvet satchel resting at her hip.
"If environmental pressure is the extent of your concern, Lord Silas, you may put your mind entirely at ease," the Princess said smoothly. "Thor, if you will..."
Thor expended her mana and made sure that she would be able to take them off.
She retrieved a series of shimmering crystalline talismans, setting them one by one upon the dark-oak desk with crisp delicate taps.

First was a pendant of deep oceanic blue... a teardrop-shaped gem carved from pure Celestial Anchor Quartz, glowing with a pulsing rhythm that actively smoothed out the ambient mana around her upper body.
Next, she unfastened a slender bracelet forged from interwoven strands of Void-Weave Mithril, etched with thousands of microscopic stabilization arrays designed to neutralize spatial turbulence.
Finally, she produced a pair of polished rings inlaid with Abyssal Null-Gems, which hummed with nullification fields capable of absorbing environmental shockwaves.

"This pendant is a Tier 4 life-tether," she explained with measured pride, gesturing gracefully to the jewels. "It creates a permanent self-regulating atmospheric envelope around my body, replicating the exact gravity, air density, and oxygen saturation of the mortal plane’s biosphere... The mithril band reinforces my cellular integrity against the Sovereign Realm, and the null-rings dissipate high-tier spiritual radiation before it can touch my skin. I am more than equipped to survive within the Sovereign Realm."
Silas glanced down at the glittering array of multi-million-credit relics, then looked back up at her with a deadpan expression.
"And what am I supposed to care about?" Silas asked, his voice sounding dry and unimpressed.
The Princess’s composure hitched for a fraction of a second. "Excuse me?"

"You’re carrying a walking museum of fragile defensive glass," Silas pointed out, tapping his finger against the desk. "Those artifacts work great as long as you’re sitting in a climate-controlled car or sipping tea in a reinforced parlor but what happens if a stray mana-beast charges the outer perimeter? What happens if a shockwave clips your flank and shatters that little quartz pendant into dust? You’ll be crushed into paste by the basin’s gravity before I can even reach out my hand... I am running a territory, not a day-care for fragile royalty."
The Princess’s lips thinned into a sharp rigid line.
The courtly warmth in her expression evaporated, replaced by a cold look.
’No... I won’t go back now...’
She slowly leaned forward across the desk, her azure eyes narrowing to needle points as her voice dropped into a chilling tone.

"You speak as though you hold the luxury of choice, Lord Silas," she said softly, her words carrying the venomous weight of tyranny. "Let us be exceedingly clear about the reality of your situation. If Lady Thor turns around and takes me back to Rhyx City this very morning, I will walk straight into the Grand Inquisitor’s office. I will file an official, unredacted report documenting your true gender, your forged identity, and the deception of the world."
She tilted her chin up.

"When that report is stamped with my seal, no amount of combat prowess or power will save you. Three retribution fleets will descend upon the Umbral Basin before the week is out. Your territory will be incinerated... Your core will be extracted and ground into fuel and before they execute you, the World Court will track down every single member of your bloodline across the mortal world, dragging your family from their homes to be imprisoned."

’Eh?’ Silas thought, now he was even more certain the Princess didn’t know what she was talking about... They would kill him? They would want him more instead, including that Lohan Sterling and nothing would change. ’Why is she so desperate though?’
SCHING!
The temperature dropped.
Standing by the doorway, Morwenna’s stormy gray eyes flared with pure madness.
Her right hand gripped the leather-wrapped hilt of Tidebringer, drawing the curved abyssal steel three inches from its scabbard.

A suffocating pitch-black aura of crushing oceanic pressure erupted from her frame, the ghostly silhouette of a massive, world-devouring Leviathan flashing in her eyes as her canines bared in a feral snarl.

"You arrogant little royal whore," Morwenna hissed, her voice vibrating with murderous intent that made the stone walls crack. "Say one more word about the Captain’s family, and I will sever your head from your shoulders so fast your brain won’t even realize you’re dead until your skull hits the floor."
Beside Silas’s desk, Aurelia had already stepped forward, her pale porcelain face completely devoid of its earlier warmth.
Her golden-amber eyes burned with incandescent fury, and a torrent of pure, blazing white Argent Flame coiled violently around her slender hands.
The air around her ignited with sacred heat, the wood of the floorboards beginning to smoke beneath the soles of her slippers.
After six years of enduring torture at the hands of arrogant royals who viewed human life as disposable currency, the Princess’s threats struck a deep nerve within the Saintess’s soul.
She genuinely wanted to incinerate this blue-haired girl where she sat.
The Princess felt the two killing intents locking onto her neck like physical guillotines. They were enough to kill her but thanks to Thor’s aura, they didn’t.
Her skin prickled, her breath seized, and her heart hammered wildly against her ribs, but before the situation could devolve into an immediate bloodbath...
SLAP!
A massive iron-plated gauntlet struck the Princess across the upper back with the force of a falling oak tree.
"GWAHAHAHA! Knock it off, little Princess!" Thor’s booming voice shattered the murderous tension like a thunderclap.
The God of Thunder leaned forward in her armchair, shaking her head with an amused toothy grin as she wagged a heavy finger in the girl’s face.

"I told you already... I like this boy! He’s got a Gold Core just like my old man, and he runs this fortress like a proper Lord! You don’t come into a strong man’s hall and threaten to murder his kin while I’m sitting in the room! Stop puffing your chest out with threats you don’t even have the stomach to carry out!"
The concussive slap knocked the wind completely out of the Princess’s lungs.
She stumbled forward in her chair, clutching her chest and coughing sharply as the haughty mask shattered completely into pieces.
She lowered her head, looking down at her trembling hands in her lap.
The silence returned to the office, but this time, the venom was gone, replaced by a raw vulnerability.

"I... I apologize," the Princess whispered, her voice cracking as she pressed her forehead down against the polished wood of the desk, bowing before Silas in genuine supplication. "I am sorry, Lord Silas. I spoke out of turn... I was grasping at straws."
Silas didn’t move. He simply watched her with his expression becoming even more unreadable as the blue-haired girl poured her heart onto the wood.

"Please..." she begged, her shoulders trembling beneath her fine silk gown. "I just... I just wanted to see what the world truly looks like on the outside. For my entire life, I have been locked away in gilded towers, surrounded by marble walls, bodyguards, and protocols. I wanted to know what I was missing... what life actually feels like for those who possess the power to forge their own destiny."
Aurelia’s white flames subtly flickered, her golden eyes softening as she watched the girl bow.

"In the eyes of the Supreme Royal Family, I am nothing more than a failure," the Princess continued, her voice muffled against the desk and thick with unshed tears. "I failed to awaken a Lord Core. I have no authority, no military command, and no political weight. If I were to vanish from the face of the mortal world this very second, my Father and my brother would not shed a single tear. They would simply strike my title from the registry and replace me with another asset. I have no power. I have no future... and I have nothing left to lose."

Silas sat in silence for several long seconds, letting her words breathe in the room.
He reached up, running a hand through his dark hair and rubbing the back of his neck with a long resigned sigh.
"Raise your head, Princess," Silas said gently.
The Princess slowly lifted her face from the desk, her azure eyes red-rimmed and wide with uncertain hesitation.
Silas looked at her with a wry smile tugging at the corners of his lips.

"I’ll make an exception for you," Silas said, shaking his head. "You can stay in the Blessed Land for one week but make no mistake... this isn’t a free vacation. You are going to pay for your lodging, your food, and the security detail required to keep you from getting yourself killed."𝑓𝓇𝘦ℯ𝘸𝘦𝑏𝓃𝑜𝘷ℯ𝑙.𝑐𝑜𝓂
The Princess’s eyes lit up with an overwhelming burst of relief.
Before Silas could even blink, the blue-haired royal shot up from her chair, lunging across the desk and grabbing both of his hands with ecstatic gratitude.

"Thank you! Thank you, Lord Silas!" she cried, her porcelain face beaming with radiant joy. "I will pay whatever fee you name! I have access to private vaults worth hundreds of millions of credits! I will transfer the funds immediately! In fact... if credits are insufficient, I will gladly offer you my body as collateral! I will serve you however you wish—"

"Whoa, whoa, hold on! Stop right there!" Silas frantically yanked his hands back, his face flushing with sudden flustered embarrassment as he held his palms up defensively. "Nobody is buying or selling bodies here! Dial it back about ten notches, Princess! A standard credit transfer for room and board is more than enough!"
Standing to his right, Aurelia crossed her arms over her chest, letting out a long sigh as she rolled her golden eyes toward the ceiling.

’Unbelievable,’ Aurelia thought with a frown touching her lips. ’He was sweet-talking me and holding my fingers a few minutes ago, and now he has a princess throwing herself across his desk offering her flesh... Does this man flirt with every single woman who crosses his threshold, or is it simply an involuntary reflex?’
At the doorway, Morwenna let out a loud derisive click of her tongue, sheathing Tidebringer with a heavy clatter.
"Tch. Look at the Captain collecting another stray. You’re lucky you have a big fortress, Silas, or we’d be sleeping on the roof."

The Princess flushed a deep embarrassed pink, realizing how undignified she had sounded, and quickly sat back down in her chair, smoothing her rumpled skirts and clearing her throat behind her silk fan.
Silas cleared his own throat, adjusting his sovereign tunic to regain his composure.
"Right. Now that we’ve sorted out the royal hostage situation..." Silas muttered, turning his gaze toward the open hallway behind Morwenna, "...why don’t I call in our resident eavesdropper?"
Silas raised his voice, calling out toward the corridor with an amused smirk. "Talira! You can stop pretending to inspect the outside. Get in here."
Morwenna smirked, stepping aside and pulling the mahogany door completely open.
Standing sheepishly in the hallway, caught red-handed with her ear barely an inch from the doorframe, was Talira.
The Ancient Crimson Dragon was currently in her humanoid form.
Her skin was flawlessly pale, contrasting sharply with the vibrant fiery crimson locks that cascaded in wild, silky waves down to her waist.

Her sharp, reptilian eyes glowed like molten rubies beneath delicate brows, and resting against the small of her lower back were a pair of sleek, scaled crimson wings that fluttered with subtle nervous agitation.
Realizing she had been discovered, Talira cleared her throat, stood tall, and stepped gracefully into the office.
She offered a crisp formal bow to Silas, her crimson hair spilling over her shoulders.
"Good morning, my Lord," Talira greeted. "I was merely... ensuring the security of the upper landing."
"Sure you were," Silas chuckled.
Sitting in her armchair, Thor’s storm-blue eyes instantly locked onto the crimson-haired dragon woman.
The God of Thunder sat up straight, a ferocious grin stretching across her face as she inhaled deeply, catching the unmistakable scent of primordial dragon-fire.

"Oho!" Thor’s booming voice filled the room, her eyes sparkling with pure, unbridled excitement. "Look at what we have here! The blood of the ancient flame itself! Tell me, girl... are you interested in stepping into the ring for a proper spar with the God of Thunder?"
Talira blinked, her glowing red eyes narrowing with instinctual draconic pride.

"Naturally, I’ll hold back my divine output so I don’t turn you into cinder," Thor added with a boisterous wink. "But I haven’t crossed fists with a pure-blooded Crimson Dragon since the great crusades! Let’s see what the last daughter of the red brood is made of!"
Talira’s brow furrowed. She crossed her slender arms beneath her chest, her wings flaring slightly as she clicked her tongue with haughty annoyance.

"I accept your challenge, deity," Talira answered, her dual-harmonic voice rich with draconic arrogance. "After all... my own Lord is apparently far too busy managing ledgers and entertaining royalty to spar with his own Dragon."
She cast a sharp, side-eyed pout directly toward Silas.
Silas let out a nervous chuckle, a large sweat drop forming on the back of his neck as he raised his hands in surrender.
"I apologize, Talira. I was just checking out the reports just now... I promise I’ll make time for combat drills this weekend."
Talira gave a small satisfied huff, her crimson wings fluttering with pleased amusement.
"GWAHAHAHA! I love the spirit!" Thor roared, slapping her armored thigh. "A dragon with fire in her belly! That’s what I like to see!"

Morwenna stepped forward from the doorway, her stormy gray eyes flashing with dangerous battle-hunger. "If we’re opening up the sparring ring, count me in too. I’ve been itching to test my saber against her for a while now..."
Silas nodded, clapping his hands together with a decisive nod. "Alright, that works out perfectly. We can begin immediately."
Silas raised his right hand, snapping his fingers once. "Aeli!"
POP!
A swirl of radiant starlight mana parted the air beside the desk.
Aeliana materialized instantly.
The elven Archon of the Stars stood with pristine grace as her violet-gold eyes looked upon Silas with boundless devotion.
"I am here, my Lord," Aeliana purred softly, offering a graceful curtsy. "How may this humble servant assist you?"

Silas smiled warmly. "Thor, Morwenna, and Talira want to hold a full-contact sparring session. I need you to escort them down to the subterranean training vault beneath the Keep and deploy your isolated sub-space barrier so they don’t bring down the foundation of the fortress."
Aeliana tilted her head, a playful sweet smile curving her delicate lips.
"Of course, Lord Silas. I would be more than happy to deploy my spatial dome for a fight... however, such an advanced spatial expenditure requires proper motivation."
She leaned forward over the edge of the desk, pointing a slender, manicured finger to her porcelain forehead. "A kiss of encouragement from my Lord, if you please."
Silas let out an amused laugh, shaking his head. "Come here, you."
Aeliana stepped closer, leaning down with her eyes closed and a breathless expectant smile.
Silas reached out, gently cupping her chin, and planted a firm affectionate kiss right in the center of her smooth forehead.
Sitting in the guest chair, Thor let out a loud teasing scoff, resting her chin in her hand with a wide grin.
"GWAHAHAHA! Look at that! Kisses on the forehead are reserved for proper couples, lad! You’re running a sovereign domain, not a romance novel!"
Aeliana’s porcelain cheeks instantly flushed a brilliant shade of crimson.
She pulled back with a flustered squeak, smoothing down her robes in a frantic attempt to regain her dignified archon composure.
"I-I shall transport them immediately!" Aeliana declared in a high hurried pitch.
With a sweeping flick of her hand...
VUUUUUUM... FLASH!

A blinding sphere of starlight mana enveloped Aeliana, Thor, Morwenna, and Talira simultaneously. In the fraction of a millisecond, all four women vanished into thin air, leaving the office in peaceful quiet.
Left behind in the office, Silas turned his attention back to the blue-haired royal maiden seated before him.
He looked over her attire, then gestured to the various crystalline relics resting on his desk.

"Now then, Princess," Silas began, leaning back in his chair. "Since you’re going to be staying here for a week, we need to assess your defensive capabilities properly. What other armaments and protective gear are you carrying under those silk robes?"
The Princess sat up straight, eager to prove her preparedness.
"I possess several high-tier defensive items woven directly into my undergarments," she explained, reaching down to the hem of her pale silk tunic.

Without an ounce of hesitation, the Princess gripped the edge of her embroidered shirt, lifting the fabric all the way up past her ribs to expose her smooth porcelain midriff, revealing an intricate, leather-and-mithril harness strapped tightly around her slender waist and right hip.
Mounted directly upon the hip-plate was a pulsing barrier generator etched with defense runes.

"This generator can deploy an omnidirectional forcefield capable of absorbing up to three direct strikes from a Tier-4 siege beast." she noted proudly, turning slightly to display the runic wiring along her hip.
Standing to Silas’s right, Aurelia’s jaw slowly dropped.

The Saintess’s golden-amber eyes darted from the Princess’s exposed milky-white stomach to Silas, who was leaning forward, squinting with deep concentration as he inspected the runic engravings on the metal plate near her hip bone.
’Perverts...’ Aurelia thought, her cheeks burning as she glared daggers at the side of Silas’s head.
Silas, completely oblivious to Aurelia’s silent mental prosecution, nodded in genuine appreciation.

"The runic power on that hip-plate is solid," Silas commended, leaning back. "It’s a well-engineered piece of tech but silk robes and a light waist-harness aren’t going to cut it if you’re walking the perimeter walls. The wind alone will freeze your ribs, and a stray shard of shrapnel could bypass that field."
Silas stood up from his desk, smoothing down his charcoal tunic.
"We’re going down to the foundry to have Thora forge you a proper set of lightweight, enchanted traveling armor and we’ll get a set for Aurelia while we’re at it."
The Princess lowered her shirt, smoothing down the silk with a satisfied nod.
Silas looked at her, his eyebrows raising with sudden curiosity.
"By the way... do you actually know any form of personal self-defense? Any martial arts, blade forms, or unarmed combat styles?"
The Princess froze.
A flicker of panic flashed across her azure eyes.
As an unawakened royal, she had spent her life attending diplomatic lectures, tea ceremonies, and finance seminars... She had never held a sword in her life.
But desperate not to disgrace her lineage in front of the Lord of Blessed Land, she quickly stood up, setting her feet in what she believed to be a fierce imposing stance.
"Of course I possess martial knowledge!" the Princess declared boldly. "I have studied the grand physical arts of the elite Knights!"
With a sharp dramatic shout, the Princess threw her right leg outward in a high sweeping roundhouse kick aimed at the empty air.
"HAAAH!"
Unfortunately, lacking mana to stabilize her center of gravity, and wearing smooth silk slippers on a polished wooden floor, her left foot immediately lost all traction.
WHOOSH...THUD!

Her support leg slipped completely out from under her, and the Princess went crashing down onto her rear with an undignified squeak, her limbs sprawling across the plush woolen rug like an overturned turtle.
Aurelia covered her mouth with her hand, her shoulders shaking with silent laughter and Silas stared down at the sprawled royal maiden for two long seconds.
"Did you..." Silas began, his lips trembling as he fought back a massive grin, "...did you literally just try to perform a spinning kick you watched on television?"
The Princess sat on the floor, her entire face, neck, and ears turning a brilliant shade of scarlet.
"Pfffft—" Silas couldn’t hold it in.
A loud wheezing chuckle escaped his chest, quickly turning into a full, hearty laugh as he shook his head in amusement.
"Oh man... that was magnificent. Come on, Your Highness. Let’s go get you some armor before you injure yourself on the carpet."
HUMMMMM!
Deep the Keep, inside the training vault, the air suddenly tore open with a brilliant flash of starlight mana.
Aeliana, Thor, Morwenna, and Talira materialized simultaneously upon the cold, dark-granite floor.

The underground vault was vast... easily two hundred yards wide and vaulted with massive rune-inlaid stone pillars capable of withstanding a lot but Aeliana did not waste a single second allowing them to admire the masonry.
The elven Archon of the Stars planted the base of her hand firmly against the center of the chamber, her violet-gold eyes glowing with cosmic authority.
"Dome!" Aeliana chanted, her melodic voice echoing through the vault.
VUUUUUUUUUM!
In less than a fraction of a millisecond, the physical walls, the stone floor, and the granite pillars dissolved into an infinite blinding expanse of pure white sub-space.

chapters.title: Chapter 435: Thor Vs. Talira [I]
paragraphs: The dimension expanded infinitely in all directions... there was no ceiling, no floor, and no horizon, yet their boots rested securely upon a solid frictionless plane of spatial force.
The mana of the outside world vanished completely, severed by a dimensional barrier that insulated their space from reality itself.
Thor looked around the infinite white void, her storm-blue eyes widening with deep genuine appreciation.
She stomped her heavy armored boot against the invisible floor, feeling the nigh-unbreakable power of the spatial fabric beneath her soles.

"GWAHAHAHA!" Thor laughed with booming approval, tossing her wild blonde hair back. "Now this is impressive! An isolated sub-space completely disconnected from the cosmic flow of the Sovereign Realm! You’ve got fine talent with spatial weaving, elf!"
Aeliana offered a serene curtsy, walking over to the perimeter and sitting gracefully upon a manifested chair of starlight mana.

"I thank you for the compliment, Lady Thor. I have spent many long evenings refining this construct under Lord Silas’s instruction. You may unleash your physical output without fear as this dome will not fracture... Just not all of it."
Standing in the center of the white expanse, Morwenna and Talira turned to face each other.
The Dread Queen and the Ancient Crimson Dragon locked eyes, both of their expressions sharp with intense lust for battle.
"I’m taking the first dance with the Thunder God," Morwenna declared, her hand resting firmly on Tidebringer’s hilt. "I’ve got centuries of divine grudges to settle."

"In your dreams, Miss Morwenna," Talira countered, her voice rumbling as her crimson wings flared behind her back. "The God of Thunder specifically challenged the blood of the Crimson Dragon. Step aside."
"Let fate decide it, then," Morwenna smirked, raising her right hand. "Rock, paper, scissors. One throw."
"Done."
The two mythic warriors squared off, their hands pumping in synchronized rhythm.
"Rock... Paper... Scissors... SHOOT!"
...Morwenna threw Scissors.
...Talira threw Rock.
Talira’s ruby eyes lit up with triumphant, draconic satisfaction. "Victory is mine."
Morwenna clicked her tongue in sharp annoyance, sheathing her hand and turning on her heel to walk toward Aeliana’s side of the void.
"Tch. Don’t embarrass our Lord, lizard. If you get knocked out in five seconds, I’m never letting you live it down."
"Worry about your own sword, Miss Morwenna," Talira replied smoothly, turning her full focus toward the God of Thunder.
Morwenna didn’t know why but Talira trying to be nice and also trying to insult her just made it more insulting.
Talira and Thor walked in opposite directions, putting fifty yards of open white space between them before turning to face each other.
Thor stood tall, rolling her broad corded shoulders with a ferocious toothy grin.
She raised her left arm, flexing her massive chiseled bicep until the iron-hard muscle strained against her silver battle armor.

"Listen well, little dragon!" Thor’s booming voice echoed across the sub-space. "To keep this exchange entertaining and properly balanced, I am bringing my physical output down to match your own! We fight with pure grit!"
With a casual flick of her wrist, Thor unhooked her legendary war hammer from her belt.
SWOOSH.
She tossed Mjölnir casually to the side.

The short-handled ancient hammer spun lazily through the air before coming to a dead stop in mid-space, hovering silently twenty feet above the ground, its runic engravings glowing with dormant power.
Next, Thor reached for her wrists, unlatching the ancient, rune-etched iron gauntlets... Járngreipr.
She tossed them down, the divine metal striking the invisible floor with a heavy concussive clang that sent ripples through the spatial fabric.
Finally, she unbuckled Megingjörð which was the legendary Belt of Power that doubled her god-tier physical strength.
She tossed the heavy leather-and-gold relic aside, letting it land beside her gauntlets.
Stripped of her divine armaments, clad only in her heavy silver breastplate, dark trousers, and bare corded fists, Thor dropped into a low brawler’s stance.
Her storm-blue eyes blazed with pure electric hunger for combat.
"No weapons... No divine armor buffs... Just raw fists!" Thor bellowed with a wide, feral grin. "Come at me, daughter of the flame!"
Across the void, Talira lowered her center of gravity.
Her pale skin began to radiate waves of shimmering superheated pressure with her ruby eyes glowing like burning embers as her crimson wings spread wide.

"I accept your terms, God of Thunder," Talira’s dual-harmonic voice resonated with chilling, draconic pride. "And I promise you... before this spar is over, I will force you to pick up at least one of those weapons."
BOOM!
The white floor beneath Talira’s boots did not merely crack as Thor expected... it detonated instead.
Talira blurred into a streak of pure crimson momentum, crossing the fifty-yard distance in less than a fraction of a millisecond.
At the exact same instant, Thor surged forward like a golden lightning bolt.
KRA-BOOOOOOOOM!
Their fists collided dead-center in the void.
The apocalyptic force of the impact generated a massive, omnidirectional shockwave of compressed air that tore across the sub-space, expanding outward like a nuclear pressure wave.
The violent gust whipped Aeliana’s robes and Morwenna’s dark coat wildly, but neither of the spectators blinked as the two titans clashed.
Neither fist yielded.
Talira’s molten-red mana screamed against Thor’s golden lightning, their knuckles locked in an contest of pure physical pressure.
SWOOSH!
Without breaking the lock, Talira rotated her hips, driving a lightning-fast left hook directly toward Thor’s jaw.
Thor anticipated the strike instantly, tilting her head back by a fraction of an inch as the razor-sharp wind from Talira’s knuckles sliced through the air.
Thor countered with a ferocious rising right uppercut, aiming to cave in Talira’s sternum.
Talira snapped her crimson wings forward, crossing them over her chest like an iron shield.
BANG!
Thor’s fist struck the draconic wings with the force of a siege ram, sending a concussive boom echoing through the dome but Talira didn’t slide back.
’My Lord does this too...’
She absorbed the energy, uncurling her wings with explosive force to deflect Thor’s arm while launching into a blinding high-speed combination of martial strikes.
RATTLE-BOOM!
The two women vanished into a high-speed blur of fighting.
Talira dominated the initial exchange with ruthless power.

Her strikes flowed with ancient draconic martial forms that her mother taught her... palm thrusts infused with thermal shockwaves, sweeping elbow strikes aimed at vital nerve clusters, and spinning heel kicks that created razor-sharp air blades.
Every single blow landed with thunderous shockwaves that distorted the surrounding space.
POW! CRACK! BANG!

Talira drove a palm strike into Thor’s shoulder, followed by a sweeping low kick that forced the deity to shift her footing, capping the assault with a savage double-fisted hammer blow straight down onto Thor’s guard.
The continuous barrage pushed Thor back three paces, the God of Thunder grinning through the storm of blows as her arms deflected the onslaught with ease.
"Good! Faster, dragon! Hit me harder!" Thor roared in the midst of the exchange. In the microsecond between Talira’s recovery and her next strike, Thor’s posture shifted.
Her storm-blue eyes flared with blinding gold.
Slipping beneath Talira’s extended left jab with terrifying fluid speed, Thor closed the pocket in a single explosive step.
Her right fist cocked back, loaded with concentrated mass, and drove forward in a brutal straight body blow.
KRA-THUMP!
Thor’s fist buried itself dead-center into Talira’s solar plexus.
The bone-shattering force of the clean hit punched a vacuum through the air behind Talira’s back.
The dragon woman’s eyes bulged with the air violently expelling from her lungs in a choked gasp as the shockwave rippled through her internal organs.
Thor dominated the tempo instantly.

Without giving Talira a fraction of a second to breathe, Thor pivoted on her heel, driving a heavy left hook into Talira’s ribs, followed by a savage forearm smash across her collarbone that sent the dragon woman tumbling across the white floor.
ROLL-CRASH!
Talira slammed into the spatial floor, skidding ten yards, but she did not stay down.
’Strong...’
Deep within her body, Talira’s draconic core roared to life.

She instantly flooded her internal organs, her ribcage, and her muscle fibers with thick, concentrated layers of primordial fire mana, completely reinforcing her internal anatomy against the blunt-force trauma and matching Thor’s crushing physical output.
Thor lunged forward, closing the distance to deliver a descending axe-kick stomp aimed at crushing Talira into the floor.
BOOM!
Before Thor’s boot could land, Talira’s hands slammed against the ground.
Using her incredible core strength, Talira flipped her body horizontally across the floor, narrowly evading the stomp as Thor’s boot cratered the invisible space.
In the exact same breath, Talira swung her right leg upward in a vicious rising sweep, driving the heel of her boot directly beneath Thor’s gut.
THWACK!
The upward blow landed cleanly, lifting Thor’s heavy armored frame two feet off the ground and breaking the deity’s forward momentum.
Talira vaulted to her feet in a fraction of a second. Her jaw unhinged slightly and her throat began glowing with a white-hot heat.
"Die!"
FWOOOOOOSH!
A colossal concentrated torrent of pure crimson-gold dragon fire erupted from Talira’s mouth at point-blank range, engulfing Thor in a thousand-degree inferno of incinerating heat.
...Thor didn’t even flinch.
Standing inside the roaring vortex of dragon fire, Thor threw her left arm outward, delivering a massive open-handed slap straight through the flames.
SLAP!

The concussive air pressure from Thor’s bare hand physically cleaved the dragon fire in half, deflecting the roaring stream of flame to the side like water from a hose, splashing harmlessly against the distant white void.
"GWAHAHAHAHA!"
Through the parting flames, Thor surged forward to seize Talira’s throat but Talira anticipated the counter.

Using the blazing recoil and the thermal updraft from her own dragon fire, Talira kicked off the air, twisting her slender body in a breathtaking mid-air corkscrew that allowed her to narrowly slip past Thor’s reaching gauntlet.
Spinning gracefully at the apex of her leap, Talira reached deep into her core, unlocking her newly awakened secondary elemental authority.
VUUUUUUUM!
A violent pressurized vortex of emerald-green wind erupted around Talira’s limbs.
Channeling the hurricane-force currents into her right heel, she brought her leg down in a high-velocity axe kick aimed directly at the crown of Thor’s head.
KRA-BOOOOOOM!

The wind-infused strike struck Thor squarely across the top of her skull with enough force to at least make her move as the shockwave exploded outward in a deafening sonic boom, warping the white space around their heads.
Yet... Thor did not fall.
The God of Thunder simply stood tall, her neck muscles corded like steel cables, tanking the full concentrated force of the awakened wind strike with raw durability.
Her boots didn’t even budge an inch either.
Thor looked up through her wild blonde bangs, her storm-blue eyes blazing with ecstatic battle-joy.
"GWAHAHAHA! A secondary wind element! That was magnificent, girl!" Thor bellowed, a wicked grin splitting her face. "NOW MY TURN!"
Thor coiled her arm back, preparing to unleash a counter-punch that would shatter the sound barrier.
Realizing that her humanoid form lacked the mass and physical power required to trade blows with the durability of an Asgardian deity, Talira did not hesitate.
She kicked off Thor’s shoulder, launching her body sixty feet straight up into the boundless white sky.
Hovering in the air, Talira closed her eyes.
She reached deep into the absolute center of her primordial bloodline, deliberately unlocking the ancient slumbering majesty of the Crimson Dragon.
CRACK! SNAP! KRA-THOOM!

The white sub-space fell silent for a single heartbeat and then, all hell broke loose as a colossal suffocating wave of volcanic crimson pressure erupted outward from Talira’s pale skin, instantly superheating the entire sub-space into a blazing furnace.
Her spine violently elongated with a terrifying wet snap, tearing through her humanoid silhouette as her physical mass ballooned outward with explosive acceleration.
Her pale skin hardened and calcified into thick, overlapping layers of volcanic-red scales that glowed like molten iron.
Her jaw unhinged, extending forward into a massive terrifying reptilian snout lined with rows of serrated sword-sized fangs beneath twin swept-back obsidian horns.
FWHUUUUUUM!

Two colossal leathery crimson wings burst from her back, unfurling to their full magnificent fifty-foot wingspan with a concussive shockwave of displaced air that shook the very foundations of Aeliana’s dome.
The transformation completed in four seconds flat.
Hovering in the center of the void was an ancient Crimson Dragon.
"RAHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHH!"
Talira threw her massive horned head back, releasing an earth-shattering Dragon’s Roar.
The physical concussive soundwave tore through the sub-space like a hurricane, the air pressure so immense that even Aeliana had to plant her boots to maintain her balance.
Her reptilian eyes blazed with apocalyptic crimson fire, looking down upon the God of Thunder like a calamity woken from the primeval dawn.
Standing on the floor below, Thor threw her head back, her storm-blue eyes drinking in the magnificent terrifying sight of the fifty-foot dragon.

"GWAHAHAHA!" Thor roared with booming, unrestrained applause, her laughter echoing over the dragon’s snarls. "LOOK AT YOU! You’re definitely a bit smaller than those ancient elder-dragons my father used to hunt across the fiery realms... but your scale thickness, your mana output, and your fighting spirit are FAR above average!"
Thor rolled her shoulders, dropping back into her bare-fisted brawler’s stance as golden lightning danced violently across her knuckles.𝐟𝐫𝕖𝗲𝘄𝚎𝗯𝕟𝐨𝕧𝐞𝚕.𝕔𝕠𝐦

sentences.text: The dimension expanded infinitely in all directions... there was no ceiling, no floor, and no horizon, yet their boots rested securely upon a solid frictionless plane of spatial force.
The mana of the outside world vanished completely, severed by a dimensional barrier that insulated their space from reality itself.
Thor looked around the infinite white void, her storm-blue eyes widening with deep genuine appreciation.
She stomped her heavy armored boot against the invisible floor, feeling the nigh-unbreakable power of the spatial fabric beneath her soles.
"GWAHAHAHA!" Thor laughed with booming approval, tossing her wild blonde hair back.
"Now this is impressive!
An isolated sub-space completely disconnected from the cosmic flow of the Sovereign Realm!
You’ve got fine talent with spatial weaving, elf!"
Aeliana offered a serene curtsy, walking over to the perimeter and sitting gracefully upon a manifested chair of starlight mana.
"I thank you for the compliment, Lady Thor.
I have spent many long evenings refining this construct under Lord Silas’s instruction.
You may unleash your physical output without fear as this dome will not fracture...
Just not all of it."
Standing in the center of the white expanse, Morwenna and Talira turned to face each other.
The Dread Queen and the Ancient Crimson Dragon locked eyes, both of their expressions sharp with intense lust for battle.
"I’m taking the first dance with the Thunder God," Morwenna declared, her hand resting firmly on Tidebringer’s hilt.
"I’ve got centuries of divine grudges to settle."

"The God of Thunder specifically challenged the blood of the Crimson Dragon.
Step aside."
"Let fate decide it, then," Morwenna smirked, raising her right hand.

One throw."

The two mythic warriors squared off, their hands pumping in synchronized rhythm.

Scissors...

Talira’s ruby eyes lit up with triumphant, draconic satisfaction.
"Victory is mine."
Morwenna clicked her tongue in sharp annoyance, sheathing her hand and turning on her heel to walk toward Aeliana’s side of the void.
"Tch.
Don’t embarrass our Lord, lizard.
If you get knocked out in five seconds, I’m never letting you live it down."
"Worry about your own sword, Miss Morwenna," Talira replied smoothly, turning her full focus toward the God of Thunder.
Morwenna didn’t know why but Talira trying to be nice and also trying to insult her just made it more insulting.
Talira and Thor walked in opposite directions, putting fifty yards of open white space between them before turning to face each other.
Thor stood tall, rolling her broad corded shoulders with a ferocious toothy grin.
