"Listen well, little dragon!" Thor’s booming voice echoed across the sub-space.
"To keep this exchange entertaining and properly balanced, I am bringing my physical output down to match your own!
We fight with pure grit!"
With a casual flick of her wrist, Thor unhooked her legendary war hammer from her belt.
SWOOSH.
She tossed Mjölnir casually to the side.

The short-handled ancient hammer spun lazily through the air before coming to a dead stop in mid-space, hovering silently twenty feet above the ground, its runic engravings glowing with dormant power.
Next, Thor reached for her wrists, unlatching the ancient, rune-etched iron gauntlets...
Járngreipr.
She tossed them down, the divine metal striking the invisible floor with a heavy concussive clang that sent ripples through the spatial fabric.
Finally, she unbuckled Megingjörð which was the legendary Belt of Power that doubled her god-tier physical strength.
She tossed the heavy leather-and-gold relic aside, letting it land beside her gauntlets.
Stripped of her divine armaments, clad only in her heavy silver breastplate, dark trousers, and bare corded fists, Thor dropped into a low brawler’s stance.
Her storm-blue eyes blazed with pure electric hunger for combat.
"No weapons...
No divine armor buffs...
Just raw fists!" Thor bellowed with a wide, feral grin.
"Come at me, daughter of the flame!"

Her pale skin began to radiate waves of shimmering superheated pressure with her ruby eyes glowing like burning embers as her crimson wings spread wide.
"I accept your terms, God of Thunder," Talira’s dual-harmonic voice resonated with chilling, draconic pride.
"And I promise you... before this spar is over, I will force you to pick up at least one of those weapons."
BOOM!
The white floor beneath Talira’s boots did not merely crack as Thor expected... it detonated instead.
Talira blurred into a streak of pure crimson momentum, crossing the fifty-yard distance in less than a fraction of a millisecond.
At the exact same instant, Thor surged forward like a golden lightning bolt.
KRA-BOOOOOOOOM!
Their fists collided dead-center in the void.
The apocalyptic force of the impact generated a massive, omnidirectional shockwave of compressed air that tore across the sub-space, expanding outward like a nuclear pressure wave.
The violent gust whipped Aeliana’s robes and Morwenna’s dark coat wildly, but neither of the spectators blinked as the two titans clashed.
Neither fist yielded.
Talira’s molten-red mana screamed against Thor’s golden lightning, their knuckles locked in an contest of pure physical pressure.
SWOOSH!
Without breaking the lock, Talira rotated her hips, driving a lightning-fast left hook directly toward Thor’s jaw.
Thor anticipated the strike instantly, tilting her head back by a fraction of an inch as the razor-sharp wind from Talira’s knuckles sliced through the air.
Thor countered with a ferocious rising right uppercut, aiming to cave in Talira’s sternum.
Talira snapped her crimson wings forward, crossing them over her chest like an iron shield.
BANG!
Thor’s fist struck the draconic wings with the force of a siege ram, sending a concussive boom echoing through the dome but Talira didn’t slide back.
’My Lord does this too...’
She absorbed the energy, uncurling her wings with explosive force to deflect Thor’s arm while launching into a blinding high-speed combination of martial strikes.
RATTLE-BOOM!
The two women vanished into a high-speed blur of fighting.
Talira dominated the initial exchange with ruthless power.

Her strikes flowed with ancient draconic martial forms that her mother taught her... palm thrusts infused with thermal shockwaves, sweeping elbow strikes aimed at vital nerve clusters, and spinning heel kicks that created razor-sharp air blades.
Every single blow landed with thunderous shockwaves that distorted the surrounding space.
POW!
CRACK!
BANG!

Talira drove a palm strike into Thor’s shoulder, followed by a sweeping low kick that forced the deity to shift her footing, capping the assault with a savage double-fisted hammer blow straight down onto Thor’s guard.
The continuous barrage pushed Thor back three paces, the God of Thunder grinning through the storm of blows as her arms deflected the onslaught with ease.
"Good!
Faster, dragon!
Hit me harder!" Thor roared in the midst of the exchange.
In the microsecond between Talira’s recovery and her next strike, Thor’s posture shifted.
Her storm-blue eyes flared with blinding gold.
Slipping beneath Talira’s extended left jab with terrifying fluid speed, Thor closed the pocket in a single explosive step.
Her right fist cocked back, loaded with concentrated mass, and drove forward in a brutal straight body blow.
KRA-THUMP!
Thor’s fist buried itself dead-center into Talira’s solar plexus.
The bone-shattering force of the clean hit punched a vacuum through the air behind Talira’s back.
The dragon woman’s eyes bulged with the air violently expelling from her lungs in a choked gasp as the shockwave rippled through her internal organs.

ROLL-CRASH!

chapters.title: Chapter 436: Thor Vs Talira [II / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The boundless isolated sub-space of Aeliana’s dimensional dome shuddered violently down to its very conceptual seams.
High above the frictionless pristine white floor, the colossal fifty-foot silhouette of Talira hung suspended on massive, leathery crimson wings.
Her volcanic-red scales glowed with blinding molten heat, hissing and popping as they radiated waves of pressurized distortion that warped the surrounding void into watery mirages.
Below her, standing firmly on the invisible floor with her bare fists cocked and her wild blonde mane dancing in the gale, Thor grinned like a maniac.
KRA-BOOOOOOOOM!
The two titans collided in mid-air.

The initial impact did not simply push the air... it displaced thousands of cubic meters of atmosphere in an instantaneous omnidirectional shockwave that detonated across the dome like an artillery battery.
"Agh!"
Talira’s massive razor-sharp claws slammed directly against Thor’s bare unyielding forearms.
Neither combatant gave an inch.
The pure mass of a fifty-foot primordial dragon crashed relentlessly against the immovable god-tier power of the Asgardian Executioner.
Golden sparks of atmospheric thunder shrieked against roaring crimson fire, carving bright arcing scars across the infinite white expanse.
Using the monumental recoil of the clash, Talira snapped her colossal wings backward, launching herself fifty yards into the sky.
WHOOOOOSH!
’I need to attack another way!’
As she vaulted through the air, her thick spiked tail whipped through the void in a blinding horizontal cleave.

The tail moved with the supersonic velocity of a falling meteor, its razor-edged bone spikes tearing through the air with a deafening screech aimed straight at Thor’s skull but Thor didn’t even blink.
Her storm-blue eyes flared with incandescent gold as she coated her right hand in a thick crackling sheath of thunder-mana.
Instead of dodging, the Daughter of Odin threw her palm outward, intercepting the massive multi-ton tail dead-center.
BANG!
The concussive collision sounded like a battering ram striking an adamantine fortress wall.
The physical momentum of Talira’s tail strike propelled Thor’s body violently to the left, sending her hurtling across the spatial void like a silver cannonball.
Yet, even as she flew sideways through the air, Thor’s wild grin never wavered.
With veteran battlefield-honed instinct, Thor dug her boots into the invisible spatial friction of the dome, arresting her lateral spin in less than a microsecond.
She twisted her muscular core, planting her feet against the empty air, and forcefully absorbed every ounce of the displacement.
VUUUUUUM... CRACK!

Transferring the diverted momentum into pure explosive forward thrust, Thor detonated the air beneath her boots, converting herself into a golden streak of blinding speed that shot straight back at the descending dragon.
"GWAHAHAHA! NICE WEIGHT BEHIND THAT TAIL, LIZARD!" Thor bellowed,her voice echoing over the roar of the gale as she closed the distance in the blink of an eye.
Thor reached the dragon’s chest in a fraction of a heartbeat.
Her right fist cocked back, loaded with concentrated mass and a crackling corona of golden lightning, and drove straight upward into the dense plate of scales covering Talira’s breastbone.
KRA-THUMP!
The blunt-force trauma was catastrophic.
A web of golden lightning surged through the volcanic scales, rippling violently across Talira’s entire fifty-foot frame.
"AGHHHH!"
The dragon let out a sharp choked roar of pain as the air was blasted from her colossal lungs.
But Talira was not a mindless beast... she was an ancient predator whose bloodline had ruled the skies before mortals built their first stone walls.
Tolerating the searing electrical shock coursing through her meridians, Talira unhinged her massive fanged jaw.
"RAHHHHHHHHH!"
At point-blank range, a concentrated beam of blinding white-hot Dragon’s Flame erupted from her gullet.
The torrent of primordial fire washed over Thor, enveloping the deity in a blinding inferno that reached thousands of degrees in seconds.
"GWAHAHAHAHAHA!"
Thor’s laughter cut straight through the roaring fire.
The God of Thunder threw both arms outward, delivering a double-handed,open-palm cleave that physically parted the dragon fire like curtains of red silk.
WHOOSH!
But as the flames split, Thor found nothing behind them.
...Talira was already gone.
Using the blinding light and the intense thermal updraft of her own breath attack as an evasive smokescreen, the Crimson Dragon had used her Wing-Strike Launch.
FWHUUUUUUM!
A hurricane-force gust of pressurized air detonated beneath her wings, propelling her multi-ton body straight up into the upper atmosphere of the sub-space.
Hovering at the ceiling of the white void, Talira’s glowing ruby eyes burned with fierce light.
’This situation is a bit good...’
She tapped into her awakened True Wind Magic, weaving razor-sharp gale currents around her wings and tail until her aerial velocity multiplied tenfold.
She folded her fifty-foot wings against her flanks, pointing her horned snout downward, and entered a vertical terminal-velocity dive.
"DIEEEEEEEEEE!"
Talira plummeted toward the floor like a falling star, shrouded in a violently spinning drill of emerald wind and molten fire.
Down below, Thor looked up, her broad shoulders coiling like iron springs as golden lightning arced across her teeth.
"NOW WE’RE TALKING! BRING IT DOWN, DRAGON!"
Thor planted her boots, threw her hands up, and prepared to catch the falling calamity with her bare strength.
KRA-BOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The impact between the diving dragon and the God of Thunder was so immense that the white sub-space momentarily inverted its colors, flashing pure negative black before returning to blinding white.
Thor caught Talira’s descending snout with both hands, her boots sliding backward across the invisible floor as she ground her teeth against the staggering force.
But even as Thor held her ground, she did not notice the subtle microscopic shift occurring within the dragon’s biology.
Throughout their entire brutal exchange... from the first fist collision to the point-blank body blows, Thor’s golden lightning had been continuously discharging into Talira’s thick hide.
Normally, foreign elemental mana would tear an opponent’s meridians to shreds.
But Talira’s primordial draconic core was an ancient evolutionary furnace designed to process, adapt, and withstand cataclysms... As dragons did...
Deep within the dragon’s volcanic blood vessels, the residual electrical charges that Thor had poured into her flesh were not dissipating.
They were being absorbed, compressed, and metabolized by her bone marrow.
Thor grinned fiercely, her biceps bulging as she prepared to hoist the fifty-foot dragon by her snout and slam her into the floor.
"TIME’S UP, GIRL! THIS ONE’S GOING TO LEAVE A BRUISE!" Thor roared, drawing back her left fist, enveloped in an apocalyptic sphere of golden thunder to deliver the finishing blow.
In that exact second... Just as Thor’s fist began its forward trajectory, Talira’s glowing ruby eyes violently changed.
The deep crimson of her irises turned into a blinding blue-white.
ZZZZZZZZZT... KRA-KRA-KRA-KRA!
Thor’s eyes widened in sudden astonishment.
"What the—?!"
Talira’s entire fifty-foot body erupted into a violent tempest of True Lightning.

Having accumulated and metabolized Thor’s divine electrical output throughout the entire battle, the primordial bloodline within Talira had forcefully unlocked a brand-new elemental affinity under the crushing pressure of combat.
’Plot armor, huh?’ Aeli thought as she looked at it, was Talira perhaps a chosen daughter of Heaven?

Violent bolts of blue-white lightning tore through Talira’s scales, coiling down her elongated neck and gathering directly inside her unhinged maw, supercharging her breath with terrifying dual-elemental destruction.
"DIIIIIIIIIEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEE!"
It was point-blank as there was zero distance between them...
A colossal beam of fused Primordial Dragon-Fire and True Lightning erupted directly into Thor’s face.
KRA-BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The blinding explosion engulfed the entire central sector of the sub-space in a swirling, deafening vortex of blue lightning and red fire.
The shockwave ripped across the floor, tearing at Aeliana’s robes and forcing the elven Archon to channel fresh mana into the air to keep the dome stabilized.
For two breathless seconds, the roaring elemental tempest obscured everything then, from the center of the incinerating blast...
STEP!
A heavy silver-plated boot stomped down onto the floor.
Emerging from the smoke and flames, her skin smoking and her silver breastplate slightly scorched, was Thor.
The God of Thunder had borne the full concentrated brunt of the point-blank lightning-fire breath.

Her wild blonde hair was wilder than ever with small static arcs dancing across her eyelashes, and a thin trickle of blood dripped from the corner of her lip yet her stance remained completely unbroken.

"GWAHAHAHA!" Thor laughed, spitting a bead of blood onto the floor with a terrifying ecstatic grin. "AWAKENING LIGHTNING MID-FIGHT JUST TO HIT ME WITH MY OWN MEDICINE?! YOU MAGNIFICENT BASTARD OF A REPTILE!"
She was only hurt like this because she allowed herself to be... Thor thought of it like a reward for the woman to feel more motivated.
Before Talira could even recover from the massive mana drain of her ultimate breath attack, Thor stepped into the pocket.
Her bare fist drove forward with the speed of an inescapable comet.
BANG!
The blow struck Talira squarely beneath the lower jaw, right at the focal point of her draconic equilibrium.

The concussive force scrambled the dragon’s nervous system instantly as Talira’s glowing blue-white eyes rolled back into her head, the blinding lightning fading from her scales and her massive fifty-foot frame collapsed forward into the floor.
FWHUUUUUUSH!
As her consciousness slipped into darkness, the extreme magical exhaustion and blunt-force trauma forcefully collapsed her draconic form.

The massive wings, the thick scales, the sweeping tail, and the horned snout rapidly shrunk, dissolving into wisps of red vapor until only the small humanoid body of Talira lay resting on the white floor, her chest rising and falling in shallow unconscious breaths.
Sitting near the boundary, Morwenna’s stormy gray eyes narrowed in disgust.

"Bullshit," Morwenna spat, crossing her arms with a loud click of her tongue. "Taking a point-blank dragon breath infused with her own awakened lightning and she doesn’t even drop to a knee? Total divine plot armor bullshit..."
Thor wiped the blood from her lip with the back of her forearm, looking down at the unconscious crimson-haired girl with deep unreserved respect.

"GWAHAHAHA! She’s got incredible guts," Thor rumbled warmly. "Awakening Lightning in the middle of a brawl... Odin’s ravens would have sung of that strike for a month. We are definitely fighting again once she wakes up."
Thor bent down, casually scooping the unconscious dragon girl up by the back of her shirt with one hand, and tossed her gently through the air toward the sideline.
"Catch, elf!"
Aeliana raised her slender hands, catching Talira’s limp body with a gentle cushion of mana, cradling the sleeping dragon against her lap as she stroked her fiery hair.
Thor turned slowly on her heel, her storm-blue eyes locking dead-center onto Morwenna.𝒻𝘳ℯℯ𝑤ℯ𝒷𝘯ℴ𝓋ℯ𝘭.𝑐ℴ𝑚

"Now then, sailor..." Thor grinned ferociously, pointing a thick thumb over her shoulder. "You’ve been talking all that hot shit about divine grudges. Are you stepping up, or are you going to keep scowling from the peanut gallery?"
Morwenna’s lips slowly parted into a sharp smile.
"I thought you’d never ask, muscle-brain," Morwenna drawled, her raspy voice dripping with cold delight.
She rose from the spatial floor, stepping forward into the center of the void.
Her black leather coat swayed around her shins and her bare feet tapping softly against the invisible surface as her right hand rested comfortably on the hilt of Tidebringer.
Thor’s eyes narrowed slightly as she observed the Dread Queen’s posture.
Despite Morwenna currently operating under the restricted levels of the Sovereign Realm, Thor’s god-tier instincts could perceive the dormant world-crushing abyss resting beneath the mortal seal.
This was not a standard warrior... this was a being who had once commanded the terrors of the deepest sunless ocean trenches.

"You’re a dangerous one," Thor noted, her boisterous voice adopting a rare serious edge. "You’ve lost an immense amount of your original power... but the steel in your soul is ancient. It is only basic battlefield courtesy to face a true weapon-master with proper steel."
Thor extended her right hand into the open air.
SHING!
Hovering twenty feet away in mid-space, the short-handled ancient war hammer Mjölnir flared with blinding cosmic starlight.

The hammer crossed the distance in a fraction of a millisecond, snapping cleanly into Thor’s open palm with an ear-splitting sound that sent a ripple of absolute divine authority through the entire dome.
VUUUUUUUUUM!
The moment Thor gripped the hammer, the atmosphere shifted once more.

The air around Morwenna grew impossibly heavy as a phantom ocean manifested around the Dread Queen’s silhouette... dark abyssal waters that swallowed the white light of the sub-space, creating an eerie sunless pressure that made the void tremble.
Morwenna drew Tidebringer.
The curved abyssal saber slid from its scabbard with a crisp singing hiss.
The runic engravings along the dark blade ignited with a deep pulsing blue luminescence, resembling the terrifying heartbeat of a slumbering Leviathan.
Thor took to the air, hovering thirty feet above the ground as she began spinning Mjölnir in a rapid mesmerizing circle.
The hammer blurred into a golden disc of pure energy, generating a high-pitched hum that ionized the air into ozone.
Even suspended in mid-air, the crushing pressure of Morwenna’s phantom ocean did not cause the God of Thunder to waver in the slightest.
Morwenna tilted her head back, looking up at the flying deity with cold half-lidded eyes.
"Tell me, God of Thunder..." Morwenna whispered, her voice cutting through the hum of the spinning hammer with chilling clarity. "...Do you know what it’s like to fall?"
Thor chuckled, continuing to spin Mjölnir with casual ease.
"GWAHAHAHA! To fall?! Little sailor, I’ve fallen through burning stars and plummeted into the frozen pits of Niflheim! Falling is just another way of traveling fast!"
Morwenna’s stormy gray eyes flashed with a sudden blinding burst of pure crimson light.
"That’s not falling," Morwenna murmured softly. "This is."
VUUUUUUM... SNAP!
In less than a second, the entire fifty-yard patch of space surrounding Thor turned into an ominous suffocating shade of deep blood-red mana.
The gravity within that red pocket did not merely increase... it multiplied by ten thousand times.

’Thankfully I have replicas of my skills saved in Tidebringer that only I can use and a lot of my mana is here too.’ Morwenna thought with a smile, Tidebringer was simply another half of her that made her complete.

As for this attack, it was not standard gravity everyone was aware of... It was the crushing hydrostatic pressure of the Mariana Trench, the weight of an entire conceptual ocean collapsing inward upon a single point in space.
Thor’s flying stance was violently arrested.
Her spinning hammer seized mid-rotation, and despite her immense godly physical strength straining to resist, the crushing mass of the red abyss dragged her out of the sky.
KRA-BOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!

sentences.text: The boundless isolated sub-space of Aeliana’s dimensional dome shuddered violently down to its very conceptual seams.
High above the frictionless pristine white floor, the colossal fifty-foot silhouette of Talira hung suspended on massive, leathery crimson wings.
Her volcanic-red scales glowed with blinding molten heat, hissing and popping as they radiated waves of pressurized distortion that warped the surrounding void into watery mirages.
Below her, standing firmly on the invisible floor with her bare fists cocked and her wild blonde mane dancing in the gale, Thor grinned like a maniac.
KRA-BOOOOOOOOM!
The two titans collided in mid-air.

The initial impact did not simply push the air... it displaced thousands of cubic meters of atmosphere in an instantaneous omnidirectional shockwave that detonated across the dome like an artillery battery.
"Agh!"
Talira’s massive razor-sharp claws slammed directly against Thor’s bare unyielding forearms.
Neither combatant gave an inch.
The pure mass of a fifty-foot primordial dragon crashed relentlessly against the immovable god-tier power of the Asgardian Executioner.
Golden sparks of atmospheric thunder shrieked against roaring crimson fire, carving bright arcing scars across the infinite white expanse.
Using the monumental recoil of the clash, Talira snapped her colossal wings backward, launching herself fifty yards into the sky.
WHOOOOOSH!
’I need to attack another way!’
As she vaulted through the air, her thick spiked tail whipped through the void in a blinding horizontal cleave.

The tail moved with the supersonic velocity of a falling meteor, its razor-edged bone spikes tearing through the air with a deafening screech aimed straight at Thor’s skull but Thor didn’t even blink.
Her storm-blue eyes flared with incandescent gold as she coated her right hand in a thick crackling sheath of thunder-mana.
Instead of dodging, the Daughter of Odin threw her palm outward, intercepting the massive multi-ton tail dead-center.
BANG!
The concussive collision sounded like a battering ram striking an adamantine fortress wall.
The physical momentum of Talira’s tail strike propelled Thor’s body violently to the left, sending her hurtling across the spatial void like a silver cannonball.
Yet, even as she flew sideways through the air, Thor’s wild grin never wavered.
With veteran battlefield-honed instinct, Thor dug her boots into the invisible spatial friction of the dome, arresting her lateral spin in less than a microsecond.
She twisted her muscular core, planting her feet against the empty air, and forcefully absorbed every ounce of the displacement.
VUUUUUUM...
CRACK!

Transferring the diverted momentum into pure explosive forward thrust, Thor detonated the air beneath her boots, converting herself into a golden streak of blinding speed that shot straight back at the descending dragon.
"GWAHAHAHA!
NICE WEIGHT BEHIND THAT TAIL, LIZARD!" Thor bellowed,her voice echoing over the roar of the gale as she closed the distance in the blink of an eye.
Thor reached the dragon’s chest in a fraction of a heartbeat.
Her right fist cocked back, loaded with concentrated mass and a crackling corona of golden lightning, and drove straight upward into the dense plate of scales covering Talira’s breastbone.
KRA-THUMP!
The blunt-force trauma was catastrophic.
A web of golden lightning surged through the volcanic scales, rippling violently across Talira’s entire fifty-foot frame.
"AGHHHH!"
The dragon let out a sharp choked roar of pain as the air was blasted from her colossal lungs.
But Talira was not a mindless beast... she was an ancient predator whose bloodline had ruled the skies before mortals built their first stone walls.
Tolerating the searing electrical shock coursing through her meridians, Talira unhinged her massive fanged jaw.
"RAHHHHHHHHH!"
At point-blank range, a concentrated beam of blinding white-hot Dragon’s Flame erupted from her gullet.
The torrent of primordial fire washed over Thor, enveloping the deity in a blinding inferno that reached thousands of degrees in seconds.
"GWAHAHAHAHAHA!"
Thor’s laughter cut straight through the roaring fire.
The God of Thunder threw both arms outward, delivering a double-handed,open-palm cleave that physically parted the dragon fire like curtains of red silk.
WHOOSH!
But as the flames split, Thor found nothing behind them.
...Talira was already gone.
Using the blinding light and the intense thermal updraft of her own breath attack as an evasive smokescreen, the Crimson Dragon had used her Wing-Strike Launch.
FWHUUUUUUM!
A hurricane-force gust of pressurized air detonated beneath her wings, propelling her multi-ton body straight up into the upper atmosphere of the sub-space.
Hovering at the ceiling of the white void, Talira’s glowing ruby eyes burned with fierce light.
’This situation is a bit good...’
She tapped into her awakened True Wind Magic, weaving razor-sharp gale currents around her wings and tail until her aerial velocity multiplied tenfold.
She folded her fifty-foot wings against her flanks, pointing her horned snout downward, and entered a vertical terminal-velocity dive.
"DIEEEEEEEEEE!"
Talira plummeted toward the floor like a falling star, shrouded in a violently spinning drill of emerald wind and molten fire.
Down below, Thor looked up, her broad shoulders coiling like iron springs as golden lightning arced across her teeth.
"NOW WE’RE TALKING!
BRING IT DOWN, DRAGON!"
Thor planted her boots, threw her hands up, and prepared to catch the falling calamity with her bare strength.
KRA-BOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The impact between the diving dragon and the God of Thunder was so immense that the white sub-space momentarily inverted its colors, flashing pure negative black before returning to blinding white.
Thor caught Talira’s descending snout with both hands, her boots sliding backward across the invisible floor as she ground her teeth against the staggering force.
But even as Thor held her ground, she did not notice the subtle microscopic shift occurring within the dragon’s biology.
Throughout their entire brutal exchange... from the first fist collision to the point-blank body blows, Thor’s golden lightning had been continuously discharging into Talira’s thick hide.
Normally, foreign elemental mana would tear an opponent’s meridians to shreds.
But Talira’s primordial draconic core was an ancient evolutionary furnace designed to process, adapt, and withstand cataclysms...
As dragons did...
Deep within the dragon’s volcanic blood vessels, the residual electrical charges that Thor had poured into her flesh were not dissipating.
They were being absorbed, compressed, and metabolized by her bone marrow.
Thor grinned fiercely, her biceps bulging as she prepared to hoist the fifty-foot dragon by her snout and slam her into the floor.
"TIME’S UP, GIRL!
THIS ONE’S GOING TO LEAVE A BRUISE!" Thor roared, drawing back her left fist, enveloped in an apocalyptic sphere of golden thunder to deliver the finishing blow.
In that exact second...
Just as Thor’s fist began its forward trajectory, Talira’s glowing ruby eyes violently changed.
The deep crimson of her irises turned into a blinding blue-white.
ZZZZZZZZZT...
KRA-KRA-KRA-KRA!
Thor’s eyes widened in sudden astonishment.
"What the—?!"
Talira’s entire fifty-foot body erupted into a violent tempest of True Lightning.

Having accumulated and metabolized Thor’s divine electrical output throughout the entire battle, the primordial bloodline within Talira had forcefully unlocked a brand-new elemental affinity under the crushing pressure of combat.
’Plot armor, huh?’ Aeli thought as she looked at it, was Talira perhaps a chosen daughter of Heaven?

Violent bolts of blue-white lightning tore through Talira’s scales, coiling down her elongated neck and gathering directly inside her unhinged maw, supercharging her breath with terrifying dual-elemental destruction.
"DIIIIIIIIIEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEE!"
It was point-blank as there was zero distance between them...
A colossal beam of fused Primordial Dragon-Fire and True Lightning erupted directly into Thor’s face.
KRA-BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The blinding explosion engulfed the entire central sector of the sub-space in a swirling, deafening vortex of blue lightning and red fire.
The shockwave ripped across the floor, tearing at Aeliana’s robes and forcing the elven Archon to channel fresh mana into the air to keep the dome stabilized.
For two breathless seconds, the roaring elemental tempest obscured everything then, from the center of the incinerating blast...
STEP!
A heavy silver-plated boot stomped down onto the floor.
Emerging from the smoke and flames, her skin smoking and her silver breastplate slightly scorched, was Thor.
The God of Thunder had borne the full concentrated brunt of the point-blank lightning-fire breath.

Her wild blonde hair was wilder than ever with small static arcs dancing across her eyelashes, and a thin trickle of blood dripped from the corner of her lip yet her stance remained completely unbroken.
"GWAHAHAHA!" Thor laughed, spitting a bead of blood onto the floor with a terrifying ecstatic grin.
"AWAKENING LIGHTNING MID-FIGHT JUST TO HIT ME WITH MY OWN MEDICINE?!
YOU MAGNIFICENT BASTARD OF A REPTILE!"
She was only hurt like this because she allowed herself to be...
Thor thought of it like a reward for the woman to feel more motivated.
Before Talira could even recover from the massive mana drain of her ultimate breath attack, Thor stepped into the pocket.
Her bare fist drove forward with the speed of an inescapable comet.
BANG!
The blow struck Talira squarely beneath the lower jaw, right at the focal point of her draconic equilibrium.

The concussive force scrambled the dragon’s nervous system instantly as Talira’s glowing blue-white eyes rolled back into her head, the blinding lightning fading from her scales and her massive fifty-foot frame collapsed forward into the floor.
FWHUUUUUUSH!
As her consciousness slipped into darkness, the extreme magical exhaustion and blunt-force trauma forcefully collapsed her draconic form.

The massive wings, the thick scales, the sweeping tail, and the horned snout rapidly shrunk, dissolving into wisps of red vapor until only the small humanoid body of Talira lay resting on the white floor, her chest rising and falling in shallow unconscious breaths.
Sitting near the boundary, Morwenna’s stormy gray eyes narrowed in disgust.
"Bullshit," Morwenna spat, crossing her arms with a loud click of her tongue.
"Taking a point-blank dragon breath infused with her own awakened lightning and she doesn’t even drop to a knee?
Total divine plot armor bullshit..."
Thor wiped the blood from her lip with the back of her forearm, looking down at the unconscious crimson-haired girl with deep unreserved respect.
"GWAHAHAHA!
She’s got incredible guts," Thor rumbled warmly.
"Awakening Lightning in the middle of a brawl...
Odin’s ravens would have sung of that strike for a month.
We are definitely fighting again once she wakes up."
Thor bent down, casually scooping the unconscious dragon girl up by the back of her shirt with one hand, and tossed her gently through the air toward the sideline.
"Catch, elf!"
Aeliana raised her slender hands, catching Talira’s limp body with a gentle cushion of mana, cradling the sleeping dragon against her lap as she stroked her fiery hair.
Thor turned slowly on her heel, her storm-blue eyes locking dead-center onto Morwenna.𝒻𝘳ℯℯ𝑤ℯ𝒷𝘯ℴ𝓋ℯ𝘭.𝑐ℴ𝑚

chapters.title: Chapter 437: The Book That Brought The Saintess [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Thor’s body slammed violently into the invisible floor of the sub-space with apocalyptic force.
The impact cratered the spatial fabric, sending shockwaves rippling across the dome as a massive cloud of pressurized vapor exploded outward.
Morwenna stepped forward with Tidebringer held loosely at her side as her dark coat fluttered in the shockwave.
"Don’t go down yet, thunder-bitch," Morwenna purred, her canines showing in a cruel smirk. "We haven’t even started."
CRACK!
From the center of the crushed floor, a golden lightning bolt blasted through the dust.
Thor rose to her feet, her teeth bared in a wild grin of pure battle-ecstasy.
Her silver armor clanked, her wild blonde hair crackling with static electricity as she hoisted Mjölnir high above her shoulder.
"GWAHAHAHA! NOW THAT IS A PROPER DROP!" Thor roared, her muscles coiling as she launched herself forward like an unstoppable artillery shell, closing the gap in a microsecond.
Morwenna didn’t flinch.
She simply lowered her center of gravity, drawing Tidebringer back in a fluid circular arc. Morwenna leaned in, her lips barely moving as she whispered.
"Tide Blade Arts..."
Thor arrived directly in front of her face, Mjölnir descending in a skull-cracking downward cleave enveloped in world-ending golden thunder.
Moments before the hammer made contact, Morwenna’s smile widened into something beautiful and terrifyingly cold.
She spoke the final words.
"Universal... Water."
FWHUUUUUUM!
Sitting at the edge of the void holding Talira, Aeliana’s eyes snapped wide in alarm.

The elven Archon instantly placed both hands together, channeling every single ounce of her mana into the perimeter barriers because the explosion that detonated dead-center between Morwenna and Thor was so incomprehensibly massive that it tore through the sound barrier entirely.
’What the hell...’
It was an explosion so loud... it produced zero sound...
There was only an apocalyptic flash of deep blue and incandescent golden starlight that swallowed reality whole.
Far above the subterranean training vault, on the western perimeter of the territory’s inner district, the heavy iron-reinforced doors of a massive stone complex stood tall against the morning light.

Silas walked down the paved stone walkway, flanked on his left by the quiet observant Aurelia, and on his right by the blue-haired Princess, who was still subtly rubbing the fabric of her skirt to wipe away the phantom dust from her earlier embarrassing fall in the office.
Silas gestured toward the colossal stone archway ahead, above which a massive, glowing runic sign was chiseled into the rock.
’That’s new but it’s the name... The Warlord Foundry.’

"This is our main manufacturing complex," Silas introduced, looking between the two women. "Everything from our light infantry gear to high-tier mythril defenses and heavy siege armaments is forged right here..."
Silas reached out, placing his palm against the heavy iron doors and pushing them inward.
CREEEAK... FWOOSH!

The moment the heavy barriers parted, an intense, suffocating wave of dry, radiant heat washed directly over their faces, carrying the sharp metallic tang of molten iron, crushed spirit-ore, and sulfurous forge-fire.

The interior of the Warlord Foundry was vast, bustling with dozens of muscular soot-stained dwarven artisans and apprentice blacksmiths hammering glowing ingots over anvils, pouring liquid steel into ceramic molds.
Standing at the central master anvil, her muscular sun-kissed arms bare and glistening with sweat beneath her heavy leather apron, was Thora.
The master dwarven smith brought her heavy runic hammer down on a glowing chunk of dark obsidian steel with a concussive clang, sending a shower of bright orange sparks cascading across the workshop.
Hearing the door open, Thora wiped her brow with the back of her forearm, turning her amber eyes toward the entrance.
When her gaze landed on Silas, a wide unhinged grin spread across her soot-streaked face.
"Well, well, well! If it isn’t my handsome Lord Graves!" Thora’s booming cheerful voice rang out over the clatter of hammers.

She set her tongs aside, tossing her hammer onto the anvil with a heavy thud. "What brings you down to my fiery domain, Captain? Did you finally come down here to let me give that fine butt of yours a proper squeeze?"
Silas sighed softly, running a hand down his face with a dry tired smirk.
"Good to see you too, Thora and no, my butt remains strictly off-limits."
Thora let out a hearty booming laugh, resting her thick calloused hands on her hips as her sharp eyes finally swept past Silas, taking in the two women standing at his sides.
The Princess stepped forward, clearing her throat delicately.
She smoothed down her gold-embroidered silk gown, raising her chin to offer a practiced introduction. "Greetings, Master Blacksmith. I am the Princess of the—"
Thora didn’t even let the Princess finish her sentence.
The dwarf completely bypassed the blue-haired royal maiden as if she were a piece of decorative furniture, stepping right past her and stopping directly in front of Aurelia.
Thora’s amber eyes widened in genuine, deep amazement as she looked up at the tall, platinum-haired Saintess.

"By the ancestral forge!" Thora gasped, reaching out and grabbing Aurelia’s slender, scarred hands in her own rough calloused palms, pumping them up and down in an enthusiastic bone-rattling handshake. "Welcome! Welcome to the Blessed Land, lass! It is an honor to have the Saintess of the Argent Sanctum standing in my foundry!"
Aurelia blinked, completely caught off-guard by the dwarf’s overwhelming affectionate warmth.
"I... thank you, Master Smith," Aurelia stammered softly, a flustered blush touching her porcelain cheeks. "I am honored to be here."

Thora beamed with immense pride, tapping her heavy leather apron with a soot-covered thumb. "You know, lass... if we’re being completely honest, it was actually because of me that Lord Graves was able to summon you here in the first place!"
Aurelia’s golden-amber eyes widened slightly in confusion. "Because of you...?"
"Aye! Hold on a second, don’t move!"
Thora spun on her heel, bustling across the stone floor toward a row of reinforced iron bookshelves lining the master office wall.
She rummaged through a stack of leather-bound tomes before pulling out a thick one bound in dark dragon-hide with gold-leaf trim.
She jogged back, blowing a layer of dust off the heavy cover, and proudly flipped open the pages before thrusting the book into Aurelia’s hands.

"Look right here!" Thora pointed with a thick blackened finger. "This is the book I found in the Library! Though... the text in this book explicitly stated that you were completely blind and withered away to nothing, but I guess you can never truly trust what these old scribes write down, eh?"
Aurelia looked down at the open page.
Her breath caught in her throat.
Etched across the parchment was a detailed, beautifully rendered illustration of herself from her last day... where she had killed everyone.
Beside the image was a comprehensive historical profile detailing her divine awakening, her role as the High Saintess of the Meolion Kingdom, and the tragedy of her service.
Aurelia’s slender trembling fingers slowly turned the page backward.
On the preceding leaf, a large colored portrait of a silver-haired man dominated the last one.
[Cassian — The Otherworldly Hero.]
Aurelia’s golden eyes narrowed, her jaw tightening as she read the historical text inscribed beneath his name.

[...Following his miraculous resurrection from the fatal Demon Rot by the grace of Saintess Aurelia, the summoned hero Cassian underwent severe psychological deterioration. Consumed by unchecked megalomania, he declared himself the ’Invincible Champion’ believing all mortal lives beneath his absolute authority. Records confirm that prior to the final purge, Cassian forcefully coerced the Crown Princess into concubinage, fathering an imperial heir to secure his political bloodline while condemning his savior to the crypts...]
A sharp bitter grimace crossed Aurelia’s face.
The cold black ink laid bare the ugly unvarnished truth of the man she had once loved.
Seeing it documented so coldly in the historical records of a foreign realm made the lingering ashes of her past feel completely dead.
She turned the page back to her own profile, looking down at the text with quiet realization.

’This book...’ Aurelia thought, her chest swelling with overwhelming, fragile emotion. ’This ancient chronicle was the anchor... It was through this text that Silas learned of my existence, searched the Great Void, and pulled me from the dark...’
Aurelia closed the heavy tome with a soft reverent thud.
She looked down at the soot-stained dwarven master smith before her. Without a word of hesitation, Aurelia leaned down, wrapping her slender arms around Thora in a tight, heartfelt embrace.
She gently pressed her lips against the dwarf’s forehead in a sacred, celestial blessing, before whispering softly.
"May I... kiss the book as well?"
Thora stood completely dazed, her amber eyes wide and her face flushing bright red beneath the soot as she patted Aurelia’s back awkwardly.
"Y-yes... go right ahead! It’s all yours!"
Aurelia smiled gently, bringing the leather cover to her lips and planting a soft reverent kiss upon the book that had saved her life.
"Boss Thora! The cooling tanks on the primary crucible are boiling over!" a dwarven apprentice shouted frantically from the back of the foundry.
"Hold your horses, you hammer-headed idiot, I’m coming!" Thora barked over her shoulder.
She turned back to Silas, giving him a quick wink. "Make yourselves at home, Captain! I’ll be right back!"
Thora rushed back toward the master anvil, shouting orders at her smiths as the foundry resumed its chaotic symphony of clanging steel.
Silas, Aurelia, and the Princess walked further into the expansive workshop, stepping away from the central traffic of apprentices.
A minute later, Thora returned, wiping her hands on an oily rag as she approached them with a proud, toothy grin.
"Alright, Captain! What are we outfitting today?" Thora asked, looking between the two newcomers.

"I need two complete sets of lightweight high-durability traveling armor," Silas explained, gesturing to the girls. "One for Aurelia, and one for our royal guest here. Along with appropriate sidearm armaments that suit their mobility..."
Thora nodded decisively, turning to two nearby dwarven workers. "Gari, Borde! Wheel out the master racks from Vault Three! Let the ladies browse our finest light-enchanted stock!"
"Right away, Boss!"

The two dwarves jogged toward the back storage, quickly returning with two towering rolling iron racks laden with dozens of exquisitely crafted breastplates, pauldrons, vambraces, and enchanted leather armor sets.
Thora stepped up beside Silas, lowering her voice slightly as she gave her daily operational report.
"By the way, Captain... we officially processed that armor that Brida hauled in yesterday."
Silas raised an eyebrow in interest. "How’s the quality?"

"Incredible," Thora grinned, rubbing her chin. "I’m already drawing up blue-prints to weave the material or construct something similar to it directly into our Blessed Land armor plates... it’ll boost physical damage reduction by at least forty percent across the board but for today, these sets on the racks will serve the ladies more than adequately."
"Excellent work, Thora. Thank you," Silas nodded with genuine appreciation.
He turned toward Aurelia and the Princess, gesturing to the rolling racks. "Go ahead, girls. Choose what fits your frame best."
The Princess stepped up to the nearest armor rack, her azure eyes sweeping over the dark polished steel breastplates.
Etched prominently into the center of every single chest piece was a striking, majestic territorial crest...
A cracked dark obsidian shield, pierced straight down the middle by a glowing golden sword, with a heavy dwarven pickaxe crossed behind the hilt.
The Princess tilted her head, admiring the craftsmanship. "The insignia... it is remarkably striking. It balances martial conquest with industrious foundation."
Silas walked up beside her, pointing toward a rack of lightweight, mithril-mesh tunics.

"Make sure you pick something light, Princess. You’re already carrying twenty pounds of imperial jewelry and barrier generators on your hips. If you pick a heavy plate, the weight will crush your artifacts and pin you to the floor."

The Princess puffed her cheeks out into a haughty pout, crossing her arms beneath her chest. "I will have you know, Lord Silas, that my physical conditioning is far superior to what you assume! A Princess such as myself does not get crushed by simple steel!"𝘧𝘳𝘦ℯ𝓌𝘦𝒷𝘯𝑜𝑣𝘦𝓁.𝒸𝘰𝓂
"Right, sure," Silas smirked. "Just pick the light mesh."
Meanwhile, Aurelia stepped gracefully toward the second rack.
Her fingers brushed against a set of pristine white-enameled steel armor reinforced with flexible leather undergarments.
A female dwarven assistant stepped forward, handing Aurelia a pair of dark expandable leather leggings designed to be worn beneath armored greaves, along with a fitted breastplate trimmed in silver.
"The fitting room is right through that curtain, Saintess," the assistant offered politely, pointing to a clean, partitioned alcove near the office. "It is fully private."
"Thank you," Aurelia nodded.
Taking the armor set and holding the book securely beneath her arm, Aurelia stepped through the heavy canvas curtain into the private dressing room.
The room was surprisingly spotless, free of the soot and iron shavings that filled the main workshop as a large, full-length bronze mirror stood in the corner beside a cedar bench.
Aurelia set the heavy chronicle carefully on the bench. She began sliding the dark, expandable leggings up her legs, feeling the enchanted fabric contour smoothly against her thighs and calves.
She stepped in front of the mirror, adjusting the fit as she moved her legs, testing the flexibility of the material.
Her gaze drifted down to the leather-bound book on the bench.
Aurelia reached out, picking up the heavy volume and flipping it open once more to the Chapter documenting the Meolion Kingdom.
’Is there anything else written here...?’ she thought, her fingers slowly turning the parchment leaves.
She looked at her own profile again.
Seeing the text summarize six years of soul-tearing torture, endless decapitations, and horrific dungeon rot into four brief paragraphs of dry historical summary felt almost insulting.
How could simple ink ever capture the suffocating horror of drowning in other people’s blood for six straight years?
’...And yet,’ Aurelia smiled softly, tracing the golden lettering of her name, ’it was this very insult of a book that allowed Silas to find me. It saved my life.’

sentences.text: Thor’s body slammed violently into the invisible floor of the sub-space with apocalyptic force.
The impact cratered the spatial fabric, sending shockwaves rippling across the dome as a massive cloud of pressurized vapor exploded outward.
Morwenna stepped forward with Tidebringer held loosely at her side as her dark coat fluttered in the shockwave.
"Don’t go down yet, thunder-bitch," Morwenna purred, her canines showing in a cruel smirk.
"We haven’t even started."
CRACK!
From the center of the crushed floor, a golden lightning bolt blasted through the dust.
Thor rose to her feet, her teeth bared in a wild grin of pure battle-ecstasy.
Her silver armor clanked, her wild blonde hair crackling with static electricity as she hoisted Mjölnir high above her shoulder.
"GWAHAHAHA!
NOW THAT IS A PROPER DROP!" Thor roared, her muscles coiling as she launched herself forward like an unstoppable artillery shell, closing the gap in a microsecond.
Morwenna didn’t flinch.
She simply lowered her center of gravity, drawing Tidebringer back in a fluid circular arc.
Morwenna leaned in, her lips barely moving as she whispered.
"Tide Blade Arts..."
Thor arrived directly in front of her face, Mjölnir descending in a skull-cracking downward cleave enveloped in world-ending golden thunder.
Moments before the hammer made contact, Morwenna’s smile widened into something beautiful and terrifyingly cold.
She spoke the final words.
"Universal...
Water."
FWHUUUUUUM!
Sitting at the edge of the void holding Talira, Aeliana’s eyes snapped wide in alarm.

The elven Archon instantly placed both hands together, channeling every single ounce of her mana into the perimeter barriers because the explosion that detonated dead-center between Morwenna and Thor was so incomprehensibly massive that it tore through the sound barrier entirely.
’What the hell...’
It was an explosion so loud... it produced zero sound...
There was only an apocalyptic flash of deep blue and incandescent golden starlight that swallowed reality whole.
Far above the subterranean training vault, on the western perimeter of the territory’s inner district, the heavy iron-reinforced doors of a massive stone complex stood tall against the morning light.

Silas walked down the paved stone walkway, flanked on his left by the quiet observant Aurelia, and on his right by the blue-haired Princess, who was still subtly rubbing the fabric of her skirt to wipe away the phantom dust from her earlier embarrassing fall in the office.
Silas gestured toward the colossal stone archway ahead, above which a massive, glowing runic sign was chiseled into the rock.
’That’s new but it’s the name...
The Warlord Foundry.’
"This is our main manufacturing complex," Silas introduced, looking between the two women.
"Everything from our light infantry gear to high-tier mythril defenses and heavy siege armaments is forged right here..."
Silas reached out, placing his palm against the heavy iron doors and pushing them inward.
CREEEAK...
FWOOSH!

The moment the heavy barriers parted, an intense, suffocating wave of dry, radiant heat washed directly over their faces, carrying the sharp metallic tang of molten iron, crushed spirit-ore, and sulfurous forge-fire.

The interior of the Warlord Foundry was vast, bustling with dozens of muscular soot-stained dwarven artisans and apprentice blacksmiths hammering glowing ingots over anvils, pouring liquid steel into ceramic molds.
Standing at the central master anvil, her muscular sun-kissed arms bare and glistening with sweat beneath her heavy leather apron, was Thora.
The master dwarven smith brought her heavy runic hammer down on a glowing chunk of dark obsidian steel with a concussive clang, sending a shower of bright orange sparks cascading across the workshop.
Hearing the door open, Thora wiped her brow with the back of her forearm, turning her amber eyes toward the entrance.
When her gaze landed on Silas, a wide unhinged grin spread across her soot-streaked face.
"Well, well, well!
If it isn’t my handsome Lord Graves!" Thora’s booming cheerful voice rang out over the clatter of hammers.
She set her tongs aside, tossing her hammer onto the anvil with a heavy thud.
"What brings you down to my fiery domain, Captain?
Did you finally come down here to let me give that fine butt of yours a proper squeeze?"
Silas sighed softly, running a hand down his face with a dry tired smirk.
"Good to see you too, Thora and no, my butt remains strictly off-limits."
Thora let out a hearty booming laugh, resting her thick calloused hands on her hips as her sharp eyes finally swept past Silas, taking in the two women standing at his sides.
The Princess stepped forward, clearing her throat delicately.
She smoothed down her gold-embroidered silk gown, raising her chin to offer a practiced introduction.
"Greetings, Master Blacksmith.
I am the Princess of the—"
Thora didn’t even let the Princess finish her sentence.
The dwarf completely bypassed the blue-haired royal maiden as if she were a piece of decorative furniture, stepping right past her and stopping directly in front of Aurelia.
Thora’s amber eyes widened in genuine, deep amazement as she looked up at the tall, platinum-haired Saintess.

"By the ancestral forge!" Thora gasped, reaching out and grabbing Aurelia’s slender, scarred hands in her own rough calloused palms, pumping them up and down in an enthusiastic bone-rattling handshake.
"Welcome!
Welcome to the Blessed Land, lass!
It is an honor to have the Saintess of the Argent Sanctum standing in my foundry!"
Aurelia blinked, completely caught off-guard by the dwarf’s overwhelming affectionate warmth.
"I... thank you, Master Smith," Aurelia stammered softly, a flustered blush touching her porcelain cheeks.
"I am honored to be here."
Thora beamed with immense pride, tapping her heavy leather apron with a soot-covered thumb.
"You know, lass... if we’re being completely honest, it was actually because of me that Lord Graves was able to summon you here in the first place!"
Aurelia’s golden-amber eyes widened slightly in confusion.
"Because of you...?"
"Aye!
Hold on a second, don’t move!"
Thora spun on her heel, bustling across the stone floor toward a row of reinforced iron bookshelves lining the master office wall.
She rummaged through a stack of leather-bound tomes before pulling out a thick one bound in dark dragon-hide with gold-leaf trim.
She jogged back, blowing a layer of dust off the heavy cover, and proudly flipped open the pages before thrusting the book into Aurelia’s hands.
"Look right here!" Thora pointed with a thick blackened finger.
"This is the book I found in the Library!
Though... the text in this book explicitly stated that you were completely blind and withered away to nothing, but I guess you can never truly trust what these old scribes write down, eh?"
Aurelia looked down at the open page.
Her breath caught in her throat.
Etched across the parchment was a detailed, beautifully rendered illustration of herself from her last day... where she had killed everyone.
Beside the image was a comprehensive historical profile detailing her divine awakening, her role as the High Saintess of the Meolion Kingdom, and the tragedy of her service.
Aurelia’s slender trembling fingers slowly turned the page backward.
On the preceding leaf, a large colored portrait of a silver-haired man dominated the last one.
[Cassian — The Otherworldly Hero.]
Aurelia’s golden eyes narrowed, her jaw tightening as she read the historical text inscribed beneath his name.
[...Following his miraculous resurrection from the fatal Demon Rot by the grace of Saintess Aurelia, the summoned hero Cassian underwent severe psychological deterioration.
Consumed by unchecked megalomania, he declared himself the ’Invincible Champion’ believing all mortal lives beneath his absolute authority.

Records confirm that prior to the final purge, Cassian forcefully coerced the Crown Princess into concubinage, fathering an imperial heir to secure his political bloodline while condemning his savior to the crypts...]
A sharp bitter grimace crossed Aurelia’s face.
The cold black ink laid bare the ugly unvarnished truth of the man she had once loved.
Seeing it documented so coldly in the historical records of a foreign realm made the lingering ashes of her past feel completely dead.
She turned the page back to her own profile, looking down at the text with quiet realization.
’This book...’ Aurelia thought, her chest swelling with overwhelming, fragile emotion. ’This ancient chronicle was the anchor...
It was through this text that Silas learned of my existence, searched the Great Void, and pulled me from the dark...’
Aurelia closed the heavy tome with a soft reverent thud.
She looked down at the soot-stained dwarven master smith before her.
Without a word of hesitation, Aurelia leaned down, wrapping her slender arms around Thora in a tight, heartfelt embrace.
She gently pressed her lips against the dwarf’s forehead in a sacred, celestial blessing, before whispering softly.
"May I... kiss the book as well?"
Thora stood completely dazed, her amber eyes wide and her face flushing bright red beneath the soot as she patted Aurelia’s back awkwardly.
"Y-yes... go right ahead!
It’s all yours!"
Aurelia smiled gently, bringing the leather cover to her lips and planting a soft reverent kiss upon the book that had saved her life.
"Boss Thora!
The cooling tanks on the primary crucible are boiling over!" a dwarven apprentice shouted frantically from the back of the foundry.
"Hold your horses, you hammer-headed idiot, I’m coming!" Thora barked over her shoulder.
She turned back to Silas, giving him a quick wink.
"Make yourselves at home, Captain!
I’ll be right back!"
Thora rushed back toward the master anvil, shouting orders at her smiths as the foundry resumed its chaotic symphony of clanging steel.
Silas, Aurelia, and the Princess walked further into the expansive workshop, stepping away from the central traffic of apprentices.
A minute later, Thora returned, wiping her hands on an oily rag as she approached them with a proud, toothy grin.
"Alright, Captain!
What are we outfitting today?" Thora asked, looking between the two newcomers.
"I need two complete sets of lightweight high-durability traveling armor," Silas explained, gesturing to the girls.
"One for Aurelia, and one for our royal guest here.
Along with appropriate sidearm armaments that suit their mobility..."
Thora nodded decisively, turning to two nearby dwarven workers.
"Gari, Borde!
Wheel out the master racks from Vault Three!
Let the ladies browse our finest light-enchanted stock!"
"Right away, Boss!"

The two dwarves jogged toward the back storage, quickly returning with two towering rolling iron racks laden with dozens of exquisitely crafted breastplates, pauldrons, vambraces, and enchanted leather armor sets.
Thora stepped up beside Silas, lowering her voice slightly as she gave her daily operational report.
"By the way, Captain... we officially processed that armor that Brida hauled in yesterday."
Silas raised an eyebrow in interest.
"How’s the quality?"
"Incredible," Thora grinned, rubbing her chin.

chapters.title: Chapter 438: Child-Bearing Hips [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: She flipped the page forward, scanning through the lesser figures of the fallen kingdom.
Her eyes landed on a small grainy sketch of a sneering armored man:
Senior Inquisitor Enin.
Aurelia’s breath hitched. She recognized him instantly... he was the sadistic prison guard who had dragged her by the neck chain every single morning, spitting in her food and cursing her as a demon.
She read the brief, concluding sentence beneath his record.

[...During the cataclysmic event known as the ’Great Karmic Purge’ Senior Inquisitor Enin suffered instantaneous, catastrophic physical rupture. His skull, spine, and chest cavity exploded simultaneously from the return of thirty-two unpurged battlefield wounds, killing him instantly within the garrison corridor...]
A wide and thoroughly satisfied smile blossomed across Aurelia’s face.
"Good," she whispered quietly to herself. "Useless trash."
Feeling lighter and more liberated than she had in centuries, Aurelia closed the book, tucked it securely into her arm, and pushed the canvas curtain aside to step back into the main foundry floor.
The moment she walked out, the sight before her made her pause mid-stride.
Lying flat on her stomach in the center of the stone aisle, kicking her legs in desperate frustration, was the Princess.
The blue-haired royal had stubbornly insisted on trying on a heavy dwarven vanguard breastplate forged from dense adamantine plate.

The crushing weight of the massive armor, combined with her heavy waist-harness and the lack of mana to support the load, had instantly collapsed her center of gravity, pinning her flat against the flagstones like an overturned beetle.

"It’s... it’s too heavy!" the Princess whined loudly, her face pressed against the stone floor as she kicked her silk-clad heels. "The center of mass on this plate is defective... It’s pulling me downward!"
Standing above her, Silas had his hands on his hips, his shoulders shaking with silent laughter.
Beside him, Thora was practically doubled over, slapping her leather apron in howling amusement.
"I told you to pick the light mesh, Princess!" Silas teased, shaking his head with a wide grin. "You’re way too young and frail to be playing dress-up with heavy plates."
The Princess abruptly stopped kicking.
She pushed her chin up from the floor, her azure eyes flashing with indignant, aristocratic fury as her face turned a brilliant, burning shade of scarlet.

"I will have you know, Lord Silas," the Princess snapped in a sharp, defensive huff, "that I am twenty-six years old! Well... twenty-five, but I am turning twenty-six in three months, which practically counts as twenty-six! I am a fully grown, mature woman!"
Silas paused.
His teasing smile froze on his face, his blue eyes blinking in sudden, stunned realization.

’Wait... she’s twenty-five going on twenty-six?’ Silas’s internal voice echoed in genuine surprise. ’With that height, those pouts, and that complete lack of spatial awareness, I legitimately thought she was an eighteen-year-old high school graduate throwing a royal tantrum...’
Far across the inner district of Blessed Land, inside the quiet luxurious residential complex overlooking the western gardens...
Evelyn sat comfortably on the edge of her balcony railing, the crisp morning breeze rustling the edges of her dark robes.
She held a slender leather-bound ledger in her lap, reviewing her territory’s internal logistical distributions.
Suddenly, without warning...
SHIVER!
An intense freezing chill ran straight up her spine, raising the fine hairs on the back of her neck.
Evelyn blinked, slowly lowering the ledger.
She reached into the pocket of her coat, retrieved a slender silver case, and popped a cigarette between her lips.
With a snap of her fingers, a tiny spark of blue mana ignited the tip.
"Haah..."
She drew in a long, slow breath of cool smoke, exhaling a thin white stream into the morning air as her eyes narrowed toward the distant Keep.
"Eh?" Evelyn murmured softly, a dry amused smirk touching her lips. "It’s been a while since I felt a chill run up my spine like that... That usually means it’s going to be a good smoke day."

The dry radiant heat inside the grand chamber of the Warlord Foundry kept hitting on everyone in it as standing in the center of the stone-paved aisle, the Princess slowly pushed herself up from the floorboards, her cheeks burning with an intense scarlet.
"Huuu..."
Silas reached down with a calm, amused smirk, his strong hands catching her beneath her slender arms and easily hoisting her back onto her feet.

The blue-haired royal maiden wobbled for a second before stabilizing her balance, quickly smoothing down her gold-embroidered silk tunic while deliberately avoiding eye contact with the female dwarven artisans who were openly snickering into their leather aprons.
"Alright," Silas chuckled softly, reaching for the next set of defensive plating that Thora had pulled from the reserve storage racks. "Let’s try this again without giving you a concussion."
Several more minutes passed...
After the embarrassing disaster of the heavy adamantine plate and the subsequent realization that even the standard infantry armor was entirely too dense for an Unawakened constitution...
Thora had dug deep into an older velvet-lined chest in the back corner of the workshop.
"Got it! I won it from Brenna by beating her at drinking!"
She produced an antique ultra-lightweight scout carapace forged from layered shadow-silk, lightweight silver-thread mesh, and thin scales of polished sky-iron.
Silas stepped behind the Princess, lifting the fitted chestpiece and resting it gently over her shoulders.
CLICK! CLACK!
His fingers moved with efficiency, threading the supple leather straps through the side buckles and snapping the enchanted copper clasps into their corresponding runic grooves along her ribs.
The Princess wiggled her torso from side to side, testing the give of the material.
A bright genuine smile returned to her porcelain face as she tilted her chin down to inspect the immaculate fit.

"Oh!" she breathed, her azure eyes lighting up with delight. "This one is remarkably different! The weight distribution does not actively drag my posture toward the flagstones! It breathes quite nicely, Lord Silas!"
She gave another exaggerated wiggle, rolling her hips slightly to test the flexibility of the lower waist-guards.

"Stop wiggling, Princess," Silas commanded with a dry laugh, reaching around her flank to catch the final lower latch. "If you keep twisting like an eel, I’m going to pinch your skin in the copper hinge. Hold still..."
SNAP!
The last clasp locked securely into place as Silas patted the side of the armor, smoothing down the leather straps.
’This is a lot of trouble...’

Originally, Silas’s operational plan for the morning had been straightforward... Gather the newly recruited maidens of Blessed Land, march them out into the perimeter crags of the Umbral Basin, and conduct a controlled combat sweep to harvest vital UP while acclimating the recruits to the brutal realities of the Sovereign Realm and also getting more meat.
That core objective hadn’t changed.
However, with the sudden arrival of an unawakened imperial princess whose presence was currently acting as a shield in keeping his identity safe, the parameters had changed.

Silas needed to personally oversee this outing, ensuring that the blue-haired royal received the full experience of what it meant to fight and survive in Blessed Land without accidentally getting herself trampled by a rogue mana-beast or crushed by the basin’s atmospheric currents.

’Regardless of her tantrums and lack of common sense,’ Silas mused internally, adjusting his own cuffs, ’she’s still a Princess. If she dies on my watch, Thor won’t be able to laugh off the fleets. Plus... it’s about time I see what the rest of the girls can do in the open field like Lupina and Morrighan.’
He had high hopes for those two... Once Evelyn left, Silas would properly swear them all into Blessed Land.
Silas turned his head, his gaze sweeping toward the place where Aurelia stood.

The Saintess had finished fastening her white-enameled cuirass over her dark tunic as the silver-trimmed armor contoured flawlessly against her tall voluptuous silhouette and the pristine metal gleaming under the orange forge-fire like polished pearl.
Her long platinum hair was tied back in a neat flowing ponytail, and her golden-amber eyes carried a tranquil dignity that looked breathtakingly regal.
"You look great, Aurelia," Silas complimented with a warm, genuine smile. "The silver trim suits you."
Aurelia paused.

A subtle sudden prickle of heat dusted her porcelain cheekbones, but instead of offering a sweet reply, she gave a stiff formal nod, deliberately turning her head sharply to the right and staring intently at a stack of raw iron ingots as if they were the most fascinating artifacts in the cosmos.
Silas blinked in mild confusion, scratching his cheek.
’Did something happen while she was in the fitting room?’ Silas wondered, utterly clueless. ’She was all tears and warm hugs last night... why is she giving me the cold shoulder now?’

Before Silas could ponder the mysteries of the Saintess’s sudden mood shift, a short muscular dwarven maiden with soot-covered cheeks and braided auburn hair bustled over, carrying a neatly folded pair of dark expandable leather leggings.

"Here you are, Your Royal Highness," the dwarven girl offered with a crisp polite bow, holding out the garment. "These are tailored with elastic threading... They’ll protect your legs from thorn-bushes and stray shrapnel."
The Princess accepted the folded leggings with an elegant, practiced nod. "Thank you, master artisan. I shall equip them post-haste."
The dwarven girl pointed toward the changing room behind the door. "Right through there, miss!"
The Princess turned, stepping gracefully into the private dressing room and letting the thick door shut behind her.
Left alone in the clean quiet changing room, the Princess leaned her back against the wooden partition, letting out a long shuddering breath of pure relief.
She looked down at her simple trousers as a wide radiant smile bloomed across her face.

The memory of the last thirty minutes... the high-speed flight through the storm with Thor, the comical confrontation in the office, the shattered window, and Silas’s teasing laughter as she tumbled onto the rug echoed in her mind with vivid clarity.

’I cannot remember the last time I laughed like that,’ she thought, her azure eyes shimmering with warmth. ’In the Palace, every single word is weighed by a lot of things, every smile is cataloged by political rivals, and every failure is carved into stone but here... Lord Silas laughs with me. He scolds me when I am foolish, yet he fixes my armor with his own hands. It is... wonderful.’
She shook her head, banishing the sentimental thoughts, and prepared to put on the leggings.
The Princess unfastened her lower garments, stepping into the dark elastic leather.
’Not bad...’
She grabbed the waistband with both hands, planting her feet and pulling the material upward over her shins and calves.
The leggings slid smoothly over her lower legs until they reached her thighs.
The Princess paused, her eyes widening as the elastic fabric came to a sudden dead stop directly beneath her prominent voluptuous hips.
"Nngh...!"
She grunted softly, biting her lower lip as she gave the leather waistband a sharp, upward yank.

"Come on... by the Throne, why is this fabric so stubborn?!" she muttered in an exasperated whisper, shifting her weight from one foot to the other as she hopped awkwardly on the cedar floorboards. "I was told it was an elastic weave! Is this dwarven sizing standard intentionally designed to suffocate the pelvis?!"
She planted her heels firmly, puffed her cheeks out, and channeled every single ounce of her physical strength into a desperate coordinated heave.
"Hnnnngh... HAAAH!"
SCHWIP!
With a sudden snapping sound, the expanding leather gave way, contouring tightly over her generous hips and snapping snugly around her slender waist.
The Princess stumbled forward, catching herself against the wooden bench with a relieved pant.
"Phew... by the stars," she muttered, wiping a bead of sweat from her forehead while smoothing down the dark leather across her thighs. "That was more exhausting than negotiating with him"
She checked her reflection in the bronze mirror.
The dark leggings hugged her lower body like a second skin, accentuating the dramatic curvaceous flair of her hips and long legs while matching the lightweight sky-iron chestpiece above.

Satisfied that she looked every bit the part of a battle-ready pioneer, the Princess took a deep, composed breath, pushed the heavy canvas curtain aside, and strode proudly back out onto the main foundry floor.
The moment she stepped into the warm glow of the forge, several dwarven craftswomen paused their work, their amber eyes scanning the blue-haired maiden from head to toe.
Thora leaned against her master anvil, crossing muscular arms over her leather apron with a wide appreciative grin.

"Well, look at that!" Thora’s booming voice rang out across the workshop, accompanied by hearty nods from the surrounding dwarven women. "Now that is a proper set of child-bearing hips! Built wide and sturdy! You’ll pop out half a dozen healthy babies without breaking a sweat, lass!"
The Princess froze mid-stride.
Her azure eyes blinked once then twice. A look of confusion washed over her face as she tilted her head.
"Is... is that considered an official compliment within this domain?" the Princess asked in complete innocent earnestness.
THUD!
Thora lost all traction on her boots, collapsing sideways against a wooden scrap bin in a fit of howling wheezing laughter.
The surrounding dwarven maidens burst into loud chuckles, slapping their thighs at the royal maiden’s utter lack of common banter.
"I-I apologize if I misconstrued the term!" the Princess squeaked, frantically waving her hands in flustered embarrassment. "Thank you for the praise, Master Smith!"
