The blue-haired royal had stubbornly insisted on trying on a heavy dwarven vanguard breastplate forged from dense adamantine plate.

The crushing weight of the massive armor, combined with her heavy waist-harness and the lack of mana to support the load, had instantly collapsed her center of gravity, pinning her flat against the flagstones like an overturned beetle.
"It’s... it’s too heavy!" the Princess whined loudly, her face pressed against the stone floor as she kicked her silk-clad heels.
"The center of mass on this plate is defective...
It’s pulling me downward!"
Standing above her, Silas had his hands on his hips, his shoulders shaking with silent laughter.
Beside him, Thora was practically doubled over, slapping her leather apron in howling amusement.
"I told you to pick the light mesh, Princess!" Silas teased, shaking his head with a wide grin.
"You’re way too young and frail to be playing dress-up with heavy plates."
The Princess abruptly stopped kicking.
She pushed her chin up from the floor, her azure eyes flashing with indignant, aristocratic fury as her face turned a brilliant, burning shade of scarlet.
"I will have you know, Lord Silas," the Princess snapped in a sharp, defensive huff, "that I am twenty-six years old!
Well... twenty-five, but I am turning twenty-six in three months, which practically counts as twenty-six!
I am a fully grown, mature woman!"
Silas paused.
His teasing smile froze on his face, his blue eyes blinking in sudden, stunned realization.

’Wait... she’s twenty-five going on twenty-six?’ Silas’s internal voice echoed in genuine surprise. ’With that height, those pouts, and that complete lack of spatial awareness, I legitimately thought she was an eighteen-year-old high school graduate throwing a royal tantrum...’
Far across the inner district of Blessed Land, inside the quiet luxurious residential complex overlooking the western gardens...
Evelyn sat comfortably on the edge of her balcony railing, the crisp morning breeze rustling the edges of her dark robes.
She held a slender leather-bound ledger in her lap, reviewing her territory’s internal logistical distributions.
Suddenly, without warning...
SHIVER!
An intense freezing chill ran straight up her spine, raising the fine hairs on the back of her neck.
Evelyn blinked, slowly lowering the ledger.
She reached into the pocket of her coat, retrieved a slender silver case, and popped a cigarette between her lips.
With a snap of her fingers, a tiny spark of blue mana ignited the tip.
"Haah..."
She drew in a long, slow breath of cool smoke, exhaling a thin white stream into the morning air as her eyes narrowed toward the distant Keep.
"Eh?" Evelyn murmured softly, a dry amused smirk touching her lips.
"It’s been a while since I felt a chill run up my spine like that...
That usually means it’s going to be a good smoke day."

The dry radiant heat inside the grand chamber of the Warlord Foundry kept hitting on everyone in it as standing in the center of the stone-paved aisle, the Princess slowly pushed herself up from the floorboards, her cheeks burning with an intense scarlet.
"Huuu..."
Silas reached down with a calm, amused smirk, his strong hands catching her beneath her slender arms and easily hoisting her back onto her feet.

The blue-haired royal maiden wobbled for a second before stabilizing her balance, quickly smoothing down her gold-embroidered silk tunic while deliberately avoiding eye contact with the female dwarven artisans who were openly snickering into their leather aprons.
"Alright," Silas chuckled softly, reaching for the next set of defensive plating that Thora had pulled from the reserve storage racks.
"Let’s try this again without giving you a concussion."
Several more minutes passed...
After the embarrassing disaster of the heavy adamantine plate and the subsequent realization that even the standard infantry armor was entirely too dense for an Unawakened constitution...
Thora had dug deep into an older velvet-lined chest in the back corner of the workshop.
"Got it!
I won it from Brenna by beating her at drinking!"
She produced an antique ultra-lightweight scout carapace forged from layered shadow-silk, lightweight silver-thread mesh, and thin scales of polished sky-iron.
Silas stepped behind the Princess, lifting the fitted chestpiece and resting it gently over her shoulders.
CLICK!
CLACK!
His fingers moved with efficiency, threading the supple leather straps through the side buckles and snapping the enchanted copper clasps into their corresponding runic grooves along her ribs.
The Princess wiggled her torso from side to side, testing the give of the material.
A bright genuine smile returned to her porcelain face as she tilted her chin down to inspect the immaculate fit.
"Oh!" she breathed, her azure eyes lighting up with delight.
"This one is remarkably different!
The weight distribution does not actively drag my posture toward the flagstones!
It breathes quite nicely, Lord Silas!"
She gave another exaggerated wiggle, rolling her hips slightly to test the flexibility of the lower waist-guards.
"Stop wiggling, Princess," Silas commanded with a dry laugh, reaching around her flank to catch the final lower latch.
"If you keep twisting like an eel, I’m going to pinch your skin in the copper hinge.
Hold still..."
SNAP!
The last clasp locked securely into place as Silas patted the side of the armor, smoothing down the leather straps.
’This is a lot of trouble...’
Originally, Silas’s operational plan for the morning had been straightforward...

Gather the newly recruited maidens of Blessed Land, march them out into the perimeter crags of the Umbral Basin, and conduct a controlled combat sweep to harvest vital UP while acclimating the recruits to the brutal realities of the Sovereign Realm and also getting more meat.
That core objective hadn’t changed.
However, with the sudden arrival of an unawakened imperial princess whose presence was currently acting as a shield in keeping his identity safe, the parameters had changed.

Silas needed to personally oversee this outing, ensuring that the blue-haired royal received the full experience of what it meant to fight and survive in Blessed Land without accidentally getting herself trampled by a rogue mana-beast or crushed by the basin’s atmospheric currents.
’Regardless of her tantrums and lack of common sense,’ Silas mused internally, adjusting his own cuffs, ’she’s still a Princess.
If she dies on my watch, Thor won’t be able to laugh off the fleets.
Plus... it’s about time I see what the rest of the girls can do in the open field like Lupina and Morrighan.’
He had high hopes for those two...
Once Evelyn left, Silas would properly swear them all into Blessed Land.
Silas turned his head, his gaze sweeping toward the place where Aurelia stood.

The Saintess had finished fastening her white-enameled cuirass over her dark tunic as the silver-trimmed armor contoured flawlessly against her tall voluptuous silhouette and the pristine metal gleaming under the orange forge-fire like polished pearl.
Her long platinum hair was tied back in a neat flowing ponytail, and her golden-amber eyes carried a tranquil dignity that looked breathtakingly regal.
"You look great, Aurelia," Silas complimented with a warm, genuine smile.
"The silver trim suits you."
Aurelia paused.

A subtle sudden prickle of heat dusted her porcelain cheekbones, but instead of offering a sweet reply, she gave a stiff formal nod, deliberately turning her head sharply to the right and staring intently at a stack of raw iron ingots as if they were the most fascinating artifacts in the cosmos.
Silas blinked in mild confusion, scratching his cheek.
’Did something happen while she was in the fitting room?’ Silas wondered, utterly clueless. ’She was all tears and warm hugs last night... why is she giving me the cold shoulder now?’

Before Silas could ponder the mysteries of the Saintess’s sudden mood shift, a short muscular dwarven maiden with soot-covered cheeks and braided auburn hair bustled over, carrying a neatly folded pair of dark expandable leather leggings.
"Here you are, Your Royal Highness," the dwarven girl offered with a crisp polite bow, holding out the garment.
"These are tailored with elastic threading...
They’ll protect your legs from thorn-bushes and stray shrapnel."
The Princess accepted the folded leggings with an elegant, practiced nod.
"Thank you, master artisan.
I shall equip them post-haste."
The dwarven girl pointed toward the changing room behind the door.
"Right through there, miss!"
The Princess turned, stepping gracefully into the private dressing room and letting the thick door shut behind her.
Left alone in the clean quiet changing room, the Princess leaned her back against the wooden partition, letting out a long shuddering breath of pure relief.
She looked down at her simple trousers as a wide radiant smile bloomed across her face.

The memory of the last thirty minutes... the high-speed flight through the storm with Thor, the comical confrontation in the office, the shattered window, and Silas’s teasing laughter as she tumbled onto the rug echoed in her mind with vivid clarity.

’I cannot remember the last time I laughed like that,’ she thought, her azure eyes shimmering with warmth. ’In the Palace, every single word is weighed by a lot of things, every smile is cataloged by political rivals, and every failure is carved into stone but here...
Lord Silas laughs with me.
He scolds me when I am foolish, yet he fixes my armor with his own hands.
It is... wonderful.’
She shook her head, banishing the sentimental thoughts, and prepared to put on the leggings.
The Princess unfastened her lower garments, stepping into the dark elastic leather.
’Not bad...’
She grabbed the waistband with both hands, planting her feet and pulling the material upward over her shins and calves.
The leggings slid smoothly over her lower legs until they reached her thighs.
The Princess paused, her eyes widening as the elastic fabric came to a sudden dead stop directly beneath her prominent voluptuous hips.
"Nngh...!"
She grunted softly, biting her lower lip as she gave the leather waistband a sharp, upward yank.
"Come on... by the Throne, why is this fabric so stubborn?!" she muttered in an exasperated whisper, shifting her weight from one foot to the other as she hopped awkwardly on the cedar floorboards.
"I was told it was an elastic weave!
Is this dwarven sizing standard intentionally designed to suffocate the pelvis?!"
She planted her heels firmly, puffed her cheeks out, and channeled every single ounce of her physical strength into a desperate coordinated heave.
"Hnnnngh...
HAAAH!"
SCHWIP!
With a sudden snapping sound, the expanding leather gave way, contouring tightly over her generous hips and snapping snugly around her slender waist.
The Princess stumbled forward, catching herself against the wooden bench with a relieved pant.
"Phew... by the stars," she muttered, wiping a bead of sweat from her forehead while smoothing down the dark leather across her thighs.
"That was more exhausting than negotiating with him"
She checked her reflection in the bronze mirror.
The dark leggings hugged her lower body like a second skin, accentuating the dramatic curvaceous flair of her hips and long legs while matching the lightweight sky-iron chestpiece above.

Satisfied that she looked every bit the part of a battle-ready pioneer, the Princess took a deep, composed breath, pushed the heavy canvas curtain aside, and strode proudly back out onto the main foundry floor.
The moment she stepped into the warm glow of the forge, several dwarven craftswomen paused their work, their amber eyes scanning the blue-haired maiden from head to toe.
Thora leaned against her master anvil, crossing muscular arms over her leather apron with a wide appreciative grin.
"Well, look at that!" Thora’s booming voice rang out across the workshop, accompanied by hearty nods from the surrounding dwarven women.
"Now that is a proper set of child-bearing hips!
Built wide and sturdy!
You’ll pop out half a dozen healthy babies without breaking a sweat, lass!"
The Princess froze mid-stride.
Her azure eyes blinked once then twice.
A look of confusion washed over her face as she tilted her head.
"Is... is that considered an official compliment within this domain?" the Princess asked in complete innocent earnestness.
THUD!
Thora lost all traction on her boots, collapsing sideways against a wooden scrap bin in a fit of howling wheezing laughter.
The surrounding dwarven maidens burst into loud chuckles, slapping their thighs at the royal maiden’s utter lack of common banter.
"I-I apologize if I misconstrued the term!" the Princess squeaked, frantically waving her hands in flustered embarrassment.
"Thank you for the praise, Master Smith!"

chapters.title: Chapter 439: Squad Leader Eluned [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: She hurried over to Silas’s side, her face glowing bright pink as she smoothed down her sky-iron breastplate.
The Princess looked up at him with wide hopeful eyes, seeking validation.
"Lord Silas... do I look presentable?"
Silas looked down at her, taking in the fitted shadow-silk, the gleaming sky-iron plates, and the dark leggings that highlighted her athletic curvaceous frame.
"You really do look good, Princess," Silas said with a gentle, approving nod. "The armor fits you perfectly so know, you look like a proper scout of Blessed Land."
The Princess beamed, a radiant, sunny smile lighting up her entire expression. "Thank you, Lord Silas!"
Standing nearby, Aurelia stepped forward, her white-enameled armor clinking softly.
"Master Thora, if it is not too much trouble... I would like to request a sidearm."
"Right away, Saintess!" Thora shouted, dusting off her apron as she stood back up. "Brina! Bring out the light sidearm rack from Vault Two!"
A dwarven apprentice quickly wheeled over an iron rack lined with various daggers, shortswords, rapiers, and curved hunting blades.
Aurelia stepped up to the rack.
Her fingers hovered over the weapons before she reached out, grasping the leather-wrapped grip of a slender exquisitely balanced rapier forged from silver-tempered mithril.
She drew the blade from its scabbard with a crisp singing hiss, testing the point with a single, fluid thrust into the empty air.
The holy mana naturally circulating within her core resonated effortlessly with the silver alloy.
"This will serve me well," Aurelia nodded with quiet satisfaction, sheathing the rapier and securing it to her left hip.
Seeing Aurelia select a weapon, the Princess puffed her chest out, determined not to be left out.
"I, too, shall select a weapon of conquest!" the Princess declared boldly, stepping up to the rolling rack.
Her azure eyes scanned the gleaming blades before settling on a massive double-edged broadsword forged from heavy iron, its blade nearly four feet long with a thick spiked crossguard.
Standing a few paces back, both Silas and Aurelia let out simultaneous snickers.
The Princess’s cheeks flushed a bright indignant pink.
"What are you two laughing at?! A weapon of sovereign stature commands respect on the battlefield!"
"Princess, don’t touch that—" Silas began.
Ignoring his warning, the Princess grabbed the broadsword’s two-handed hilt with all her might and gave a triumphant violent yank to pull it from the iron rack.
CLANG... WHOOSH!
The seventy-pound solid iron slab ripped free from the wooden pegs.
The sheer, unyielding momentum of the heavy steel instantly overpowered the Princess’s unawakened center of gravity.

The heavy blade dragged her arms straight down toward the floor, and with an undignified shriek, the blue-haired royal maiden flipped forward, crashing face-first into the flagstones with her legs splayed and her backside sticking straight up into the air, pinned beneath the massive crossguard.
"Pwahahaha!" Thora howled, pounding the anvil with her fist.
The entire foundry erupted into roaring good-natured laughter from the female smiths.
Silas sighed, stepping forward and easily plucking the massive broadsword off her back with one hand, tossing it back onto the rack before extending his other hand down to the sprawled Princess.
"I told you," Silas said with a helpless grin, hoisting her back to her feet. "You don’t have the mana meridians to swing a greatsword, Princess..."

He reached over to the lower tier of the rack, picking up a slender six-inch utility dagger forged from lightweight Sil-Graves alloy, encased in a polished leather sheath. He placed it gently into her trembling hands.
"Take this," Silas instructed. "It’s light and easy to draw if something gets too close to your flank. Keep it strapped to your right thigh."
The Princess looked down at the small dagger with her fingers curling around the leather hilt as she looked up at Silas, her azure eyes wide with quiet confusion.

’Why is he being so kind to me...?’ she wondered, her heart beating with an unfamiliar gentle rhythm. ’I barged into his office, threatened his life, and tried to extort his sovereignty... Yet he laughs with me, catches me when I fall, and personally ensures I am safe. Is this truly what a benevolent Lord is like?’
She tightened her grip on the sheath, offering a soft and incredibly sincere bow.
"Thank you, Lord Silas. I shall treasure it."
Silas nodded, turning back toward the master anvil. "We’re heading out to the perimeter crags, Thora. Keep the forge hot..."

Thora snapped a crisp, soot-stained salute against her leather apron. "Good hunting out there, Captain! Bring back plenty of beast bodies and pile up those UP! We need more high-tier ore for the next expansion phase!"
Silas nodded in agreement.
Thora tilted her head, glancing at Silas’s bare waist.
"You need me to pull down a set of armor for you, Captain? You’re heading into the basin crags in plain robes."
Silas raised his right hand.
SHING!
A brilliant blinding flash of blue mana erupted from his palm.
In a fraction of a second, a magnificent golden-runed longsword materialized in his grasp.
Silas gave the blade a smooth effortless flourish before letting the light dissipate into his Inventory.
"This is the only armor I need," Silas smiled with quiet confidence. "Let’s move out, girls."
Silas turned, leading Aurelia and the Princess toward the heavy exit doors.
Watching his broad retreating shoulders as the iron doors closed behind him, Thora let out a long appreciative whistle, shaking her head with a wide smirk.
"Tch... what a sexy bastard," Thora muttered under her breath.
She glanced over her shoulder, noticing that nearly every single female dwarven apprentice in the foundry was staring at the closed doorway with dreamy flushed faces and paused hammers.

"Hey! What are you slackers gawking at?!" Thora barked, slamming her hammer onto the anvil with a concussive bang. "The Captain’s handsome face isn’t going to smelt those ingots for you! Get back to hammering before I dock your spirit-ale rations!"
"Yes, Boss Thora!" the dwarven maidens squeaked in unison, the foundry instantly returning to its thunderous rhythm.
Silas, Aurelia, and the Princess stepped out into the cool morning air of the inner district.
Standing right outside the foundry entrance, leaning against a stone pillar with her arms crossed over her chest, was Eluned.
The Goddess was waiting with a bright expectant smile.
She had not come to the office earlier that morning because she had been busy inspecting the nascent spirit-herb crops she was nurturing in the southern greenhouse gardens.

However, because her roots were woven directly into the foundation of the Keep including the floorboards of Silas’s office... she had been fully aware of every single breath, whisper, and broken window that had occurred within the sanctum.
If Silas had truly been in danger, the entire office would have erupted into an iron-piercing forest of emerald execution vines in less than a second.
Seeing Silas emerge, Eluned snapped a playful salute as her emerald eyes began glowing with excitement.
"Squad Leader Eluned, reporting for duty, Hubby!" she declared, her cheeks dusting with a happy pink. "I am fully prepared and excited to lead my own squad into the basin!"
Silas let out a soft defeated sigh, rubbing the back of his neck with an amused smirk.

Last night, after he had bridal-carried her to bed, the Goddess had relentlessly pinched his ribs, pouted, and begged for two straight hours until he finally capitulated and promised to let her command her own independent hunting squad during the morning sweep.
’Well,’ Silas reasoned internally, ’it makes sense anyway.’
Following the conclusion of the Lord War, the Blessed Land had welcomed a total of seventy-two new female recruits.
Twelve of them were dwarven artisans who were permanently assigned to Thora’s foundry and engineering teams, leaving exactly sixty active combat-ready maidens.

Silas planned to divide these sixty recruits into four balanced squads of fifteen, each led by a high-tier captain, while Fenna remained stationed atop the central watchtower with her longbow to maintain overwatch across the entire basin.
Silas looked over Eluned’s attire, raising an eyebrow.
"Elu, where is your armo—"
Before he could finish his sentence, the emerald mana around Eluned’s body flared.
RATTLE-SNAP!
Sprouting directly from the life-force around her, a breathtaking set of living wooden armor formed over her silk robes.

The dark polished iron-wood contoured seamlessly to her body, adorned with blooming golden spirit-flowers, and a sleek closed-face wooden helm snapped over her head, completely obscuring her ethereal beauty.
Silas smiled, stepping forward and gently reaching out with both hands.
He unlatched the wooden helm, pulling it off her head and letting her long shimmering emerald locks spill out into the morning breeze.
"You look far prettier without the bucket on your head," Silas murmured softly, looking into her luminous green eyes.
Eluned’s face flushed an intense radiant crimson. Her heart fluttered wildly, and she instantly leaned forward, puckering her soft lips in eager anticipation of a romantic kiss.
Silas chuckled, leaning down and planting a firm affectionate kiss right in the center of her smooth forehead.
Standing a few paces back, Aurelia crossed her arms, letting out a soft exasperated huff beneath her breath.

’He really is an incorrigible womanizer...’ Aurelia thought, her golden-amber eyes narrowing with a mix of amusement and defensiveness. ’First the Elf, then the Princess, and now this woman too... Does this man distribute forehead kisses like standard rations?’
Beside her, the Princess blinked her azure eyes, watching the exchange with innocent wonder.
’Ah... Lord Silas is remarkably affectionate with his people. The bond between them is truly profound.’
Eluned willed the wooden helm to dissolve back into harmless life-mana, stepping back with a proud beaming grin.
"I shall run ahead to the mobilization grounds and assemble all the recruits and squad commanders immediately!" Eluned chirped happily.
With a graceful leap, she glided across the paved boulevard like a leaf on the wind, shouting back over her shoulder.
"Don’t be late, Hubby!"
Silas watched her go with a warm smile, then turned to Aurelia and the Princess. "Alright. It’s time we head to the gathering point as well."

They walked along the main paved avenue, passing the sprawling residential barracks and heading toward the wide staging grounds located just before the dense forest of ancient Spirit Trees near the western fortress gates.
As they reached the edge of the tree line, a magnificent awe-inspiring sight greeted them.
Gathered in a disciplined semi-circular formation upon the grass were the Blessed Wolves... the majestic Umbral wolf pack that served as the primary cavalry mounts of Blessed Land.
The beasts were seated quietly upon their haunches.
The moment Silas stepped into the clearing, all six adult wolves raised their massive snouts in unison, letting out a synchronized deep-throated howl that sounded through the morning air.
’I love the sound of loyalty in the morning...’
Their three young pups remained safely nestled within the climate-controlled pens of the Beast Pavilion deeper inside the territory.
Standing beside the younger male wolf, Scout, was Reina.
The territory’s Beast Tamer wore a practical leather tunic, her ash-blonde braided hair whipping in the morning breeze as she affectionately scratched Scout behind his large pointed ears.
The energetic wolf thumped his heavy tail against the grass in happy thuds, practically vibrating with food-motivated excitement.
Standing beside Reina was Vala.
The Magic Swordsman was clad in dark leather armor, her hand resting calmly on the hilt of her elemental blade.
Silas walked up to them, nodding respectfully. "Reina, Vala. Are you two ready for the deployment?"
Reina looked up, offering a confident nod.

"Everything is prepared, Lord Silas. Our operational objective is to conduct a wide sweep along the southern crags where the primary hunting squads are not active. Using my newly awakened [Beast Arrest], Vala and I will track, pacify, and subdue wild Umbral Wolves to expand our cavalry stock."
Silas smiled, looking over the vast expanse of the nearby hills.

’There’s plenty of room in the Beast Pavilion to house an entire wolf cavalry corps,’ Silas calculated internally. ’And if we exceed capacity, we can easily construct a second and third wing with me... Maintaining a full battalion of mount-tamed wolves will multiply our mobility across the basin tenfold.’
"Understood," Silas said. "Vala, your mission is to eliminate any rogue beasts or threats that might interrupt Reina’s taming rituals... Keep each other safe."
Vala gave a sharp disciplined nod with her dark eyes looking steady. "By your command, my Lord. None shall touch Reina while I draw breath."
"We love you, Lord Silas! We’ll bring back a whole pack!" Reina chirped cheerfully.
With practiced athleticism, both Reina and Vala vaulted onto the broad back of Luna, the sleek female wolf who let out a sharp eager bark.
With a single powerful bound, Luna surged forward, carrying the two women in a blur toward the southern gate to begin their taming mission.
Silas watched them depart, then turned back toward the remaining wolves.
Stepping forward from the pack was Valkyrie.

However, because her roots were woven directly into the foundation of the Keep including the floorboards of Silas’s office... she had been fully aware of every single breath, whisper, and broken window that had occurred within the sanctum.
If Silas had truly been in danger, the entire office would have erupted into an iron-piercing forest of emerald execution vines in less than a second.
Seeing Silas emerge, Eluned snapped a playful salute as her emerald eyes began glowing with excitement.
"Squad Leader Eluned, reporting for duty, Hubby!" she declared, her cheeks dusting with a happy pink.
"I am fully prepared and excited to lead my own squad into the basin!"
Silas let out a soft defeated sigh, rubbing the back of his neck with an amused smirk.

Last night, after he had bridal-carried her to bed, the Goddess had relentlessly pinched his ribs, pouted, and begged for two straight hours until he finally capitulated and promised to let her command her own independent hunting squad during the morning sweep.
’Well,’ Silas reasoned internally, ’it makes sense anyway.’
Following the conclusion of the Lord War, the Blessed Land had welcomed a total of seventy-two new female recruits.
Twelve of them were dwarven artisans who were permanently assigned to Thora’s foundry and engineering teams, leaving exactly sixty active combat-ready maidens.

Silas planned to divide these sixty recruits into four balanced squads of fifteen, each led by a high-tier captain, while Fenna remained stationed atop the central watchtower with her longbow to maintain overwatch across the entire basin.
Silas looked over Eluned’s attire, raising an eyebrow.
"Elu, where is your armo—"
Before he could finish his sentence, the emerald mana around Eluned’s body flared.
RATTLE-SNAP!
Sprouting directly from the life-force around her, a breathtaking set of living wooden armor formed over her silk robes.

The dark polished iron-wood contoured seamlessly to her body, adorned with blooming golden spirit-flowers, and a sleek closed-face wooden helm snapped over her head, completely obscuring her ethereal beauty.
Silas smiled, stepping forward and gently reaching out with both hands.
He unlatched the wooden helm, pulling it off her head and letting her long shimmering emerald locks spill out into the morning breeze.
"You look far prettier without the bucket on your head," Silas murmured softly, looking into her luminous green eyes.
Eluned’s face flushed an intense radiant crimson.
Her heart fluttered wildly, and she instantly leaned forward, puckering her soft lips in eager anticipation of a romantic kiss.
Silas chuckled, leaning down and planting a firm affectionate kiss right in the center of her smooth forehead.
Standing a few paces back, Aurelia crossed her arms, letting out a soft exasperated huff beneath her breath.
’He really is an incorrigible womanizer...’ Aurelia thought, her golden-amber eyes narrowing with a mix of amusement and defensiveness. ’First the Elf, then the Princess, and now this woman too...
Does this man distribute forehead kisses like standard rations?’
Beside her, the Princess blinked her azure eyes, watching the exchange with innocent wonder.
Lord Silas is remarkably affectionate with his people.
The bond between them is truly profound.’
Eluned willed the wooden helm to dissolve back into harmless life-mana, stepping back with a proud beaming grin.
"I shall run ahead to the mobilization grounds and assemble all the recruits and squad commanders immediately!" Eluned chirped happily.
With a graceful leap, she glided across the paved boulevard like a leaf on the wind, shouting back over her shoulder.
"Don’t be late, Hubby!"
Silas watched her go with a warm smile, then turned to Aurelia and the Princess.
"Alright.
It’s time we head to the gathering point as well."

They walked along the main paved avenue, passing the sprawling residential barracks and heading toward the wide staging grounds located just before the dense forest of ancient Spirit Trees near the western fortress gates.
As they reached the edge of the tree line, a magnificent awe-inspiring sight greeted them.
Gathered in a disciplined semi-circular formation upon the grass were the Blessed Wolves... the majestic Umbral wolf pack that served as the primary cavalry mounts of Blessed Land.
The beasts were seated quietly upon their haunches.
The moment Silas stepped into the clearing, all six adult wolves raised their massive snouts in unison, letting out a synchronized deep-throated howl that sounded through the morning air.
’I love the sound of loyalty in the morning...’
Their three young pups remained safely nestled within the climate-controlled pens of the Beast Pavilion deeper inside the territory.
Standing beside the younger male wolf, Scout, was Reina.
The territory’s Beast Tamer wore a practical leather tunic, her ash-blonde braided hair whipping in the morning breeze as she affectionately scratched Scout behind his large pointed ears.
The energetic wolf thumped his heavy tail against the grass in happy thuds, practically vibrating with food-motivated excitement.
Standing beside Reina was Vala.
The Magic Swordsman was clad in dark leather armor, her hand resting calmly on the hilt of her elemental blade.
Silas walked up to them, nodding respectfully.
"Reina, Vala.
Are you two ready for the deployment?"
Reina looked up, offering a confident nod.
"Everything is prepared, Lord Silas.
Our operational objective is to conduct a wide sweep along the southern crags where the primary hunting squads are not active.
Using my newly awakened [Beast Arrest], Vala and I will track, pacify, and subdue wild Umbral Wolves to expand our cavalry stock."
Silas smiled, looking over the vast expanse of the nearby hills.

’There’s plenty of room in the Beast Pavilion to house an entire wolf cavalry corps,’ Silas calculated internally. ’And if we exceed capacity, we can easily construct a second and third wing with me...
Maintaining a full battalion of mount-tamed wolves will multiply our mobility across the basin tenfold.’
"Understood," Silas said.
"Vala, your mission is to eliminate any rogue beasts or threats that might interrupt Reina’s taming rituals...
Keep each other safe."
Vala gave a sharp disciplined nod with her dark eyes looking steady.
"By your command, my Lord.
None shall touch Reina while I draw breath."
"We love you, Lord Silas!
We’ll bring back a whole pack!" Reina chirped cheerfully.
With practiced athleticism, both Reina and Vala vaulted onto the broad back of Luna, the sleek female wolf who let out a sharp eager bark.
With a single powerful bound, Luna surged forward, carrying the two women in a blur toward the southern gate to begin their taming mission.
Silas watched them depart, then turned back toward the remaining wolves.
Stepping forward from the pack was Valkyrie.

chapters.title: Chapter 440: A Break From Sparring [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The female Umbral wolf walked directly up to Silas. She lowered her massive head, gently nuzzling her snout against Silas’s chest with a deep vibrating purr of affection.
Silas smiled warmly, reaching out with both hands to scratch the thick fur along her neck and jaw. "Good girl, Valkyrie. Ready for a run?"
Valkyrie let out a soft joyful chuff, leaning her massive weight against him.
Just then, the synchronized stomping of dozens of armored boots echoed across the staging grounds as the sixty newly recruited maidens arrived in formation.
Silas stepped back, his posture shifting into that of a commanding sovereign as he surveyed his troops.
The sixty women were lined up in four crisp disciplined ranks of fifteen.
Every single recruit was outfitted in standard Blessed Land scout-infantry armor, their breastplates bearing the cracked obsidian shield and golden sword insignia.
Half the maidens held polished steel arming swords and bucklers, while the other half gripped eight-foot ash-wood spears tipped with refined void-iron.
Stepping forward to stand before the ranks were the three appointed Squad Captains.
First was Brida, looking as imposing and terrifying as ever.
The towering Commander carried her tower shield and axe as her fierce gaze swept over the recruits like an eagle assessing fledglings.
Beside her stood Tasmin.
Silas’s blue eyes narrowed slightly as he looked at Tasmin.
’Is she doing something...?’
He noticed the dark circles beneath her amber eyes and the subtle stiffness in her shoulders... she looked noticeably exhausted.
’Alright then...’
Silas made a quiet mental note to order her to get a good resting period, what kind of example was she showing to the other girls?
And standing on the far right was Eluned, practically bouncing on the balls of her feet with her living wooden armor humming with cheerful life-mana.
Silas stepped forward, his deep clear voice cutting through the morning breeze with absolute authority.

"Recruits of Blessed Land!" Silas addressed the sixty women, his gaze meeting each of their focused eyes. "Today marks your very first official combat deployment into the Umbral Basin! As you well know, the Sovereign Realm is not a gentle training ground... Beyond those stone gates lies an unforgiving wilderness filled with predatory mana-beasts, rogue elemental anomalies, and treacherous terrain."
The sixty maidens stood at rigid attention, their knuckles whitening around their weapons as they listened with rapt intensity.

"I do not expect perfection today," Silas continued, his tone steady and encouraging. "But I expect focus, flawless coordination, and courage. Give your squad captains your complete obedience... Those among you who display exceptional awareness, valor, and teamwork will be formally noted in the territorial registry and granted priority access to advanced skill scrolls and elixirs."
A ripple of determined hungry ambition flashed through the eyes of the recruits.
"We are dividing into four squads of fifteen!" Silas commanded, raising his hand. "Squad Captains, claim your units!"
The staging ground moved with efficiency.
Brida stepped up to Group Two, her booming voice organizing the heavy spear-infantry with military precision.
Tasmin took command of Group Three, aligning the light scouts and archers into a loose agile skirmish formation.
Eluned happily claimed Group Four, her emerald mana weaving a light protective blessing over the weapons of her fifteen maidens.
Silas walked over to Group One, flanked by Aurelia and the Princess.
"Group One will be under my direct command," Silas announced to the fifteen maidens standing before him.
The recruits of Group One instantly beamed with overwhelming pride, their chests swelling at the immense honor of being led personally by their Lord.
Silas turned toward the Blessed Wolves.
The remaining adult wolves... Titan, Ember, and Nova trotted over to the other three squad captains, acting as the vanguard cavalry mounts for Brida, Tasmin, and Eluned.
Silas walked up to the side of Valkyrie.
With an effortless athletic vault, Silas swung his leg over the massive dire wolf’s back, settling securely onto the enchanted leather saddle.
He leaned down, extending his strong right hand toward the blue-haired royal maiden standing on the grass.
"Come on, Princess," Silas said. "Up you go."
The Princess blinked, her face flushing with sudden, flustered panic. "E-Eh?! I am to ride with you?!"
"You’re an unawakened mortal in a high-gravity basin," Silas pointed out with a dry smirk. "If I make you run on foot, your lungs will collapse before we cross the first ridge. Get up here."
The Princess swallowed hard, reaching out her delicate hand. Silas grabbed her wrist, effortlessly hoisting her up into the saddle before him.
She settled into the space between his arms, her back pressing lightly against his chest as Silas’s hands reached around her waist to grip the leather reins.
The proximity sent a wild burning blush straight to the tips of her royal-blue ears.
’Wha... what is this...’
Silas turned his head toward Aurelia, who stood calmly beside Valkyrie’s flank with her rapier at her side.
"Aurelia, you’re on foot with the squad," Silas instructed. "Can your legs keep pace?"
Aurelia’s golden-amber eyes flashed with quiet confident pride.
Her vitality was fully restored, her Argent Core was burning bright, and her physical stats were those of an SSS-Rank mythic entity.
"I will not fall behind, my Lord," Aurelia answered with a sharp respectful nod.
Silas smiled, drawing in a deep breath of the crisp basin air then he raised his hand high into the morning sky.
"Group One... CHARGE!"
HOWL!
Valkyrie threw her head back, releasing a thunderous howl before leaping forward in a colossal ground-shaking bound.

Behind them, the fifteen maidens of Group One surged forward in tight formation, their boots pounding rhythmically against the stone road as Aurelia glided effortlessly alongside them like a silver shadow.
The massive iron gates of Blessed Land swung wide, and the hunting expedition plunged into the untamed, rugged expanse of the Umbral Basin.
KRA-BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
Deep beneath the fortress bedrock, inside the boundless, isolated white expanse of the training vault, an apocalyptic explosion detonated for the umpteenth time.

Aeliana sat upon her floating starlight chair near the perimeter of the sub-space, her delicate porcelain hands trembling as she channeled continuous massive streams of celestial mana into her spell to keep maintaining the integrity of the [Dome].
Her sharp, elegant brows were furrowed in pure exasperation, and her teeth were gritted so tightly her jaw ached.
GRRRRRR!
A loud hollow rumble erupted from the elven Archon’s stomach, echoing pitifully in the quiet zone around her chair.

’By the celestial stars above...’ Aeliana groaned internally, her violet-gold eyes twitching with profound fatigue. ’How long have these two battle-maniacs been going at it?! It has been nearly three continuous hours! My mana reserves are stable, but I haven’t had my morning tea, my Lord is already out on the hunt, and my stomach is actively devouring itself!’
In the center of the void, the blinding tempest of abyssal water and divine golden lightning reached its deafening climax.
CLASH!
The dark curved steel of Tidebringer locked violently against the ancient head of Mjölnir.
Morwenna and Thor stood deadlocked in the center of a cratered, swirling vortex of pressurized mist.
Both women were breathing in synchronized pants as their muscles began straining against the mutual immovable force of their weapons.
Morwenna’s stormy gray eyes were bloodshot, and burning with satisfaction, while Thor’s storm-blue eyes crackled with battle-ecstasy.
Neither woman pushed forward and for three long breathless seconds, the Dread Queen and the God of Thunder stared dead into each other’s eyes.
Then, slowly, Thor’s lips split into a wide exhausted grin.
"GWAHAHAHA!" Thor chuckled, her booming voice hoarse from hours of roaring. "I have to admit, sailor... you swing that curved tooth of yours with magnificent terrifying weight!"
Morwenna’s lips twitched into a sharp tired smirk, her canines showing as she let out a low chuckle. "You don’t hit too soft yourself, thunder-bitch. My forearms are numb down to the bone."
"A mutual recess?" Thor proposed, loosening her grip on Mjölnir by a fraction of an inch. "I think we’ve pulverized enough dimensional fabric for one morning."
"Agreed," Morwenna nodded, sliding Tidebringer back in a smooth fluid motion.
FWHUUUUUSH.
The moment both weapons parted, Aeliana didn’t wait a single microsecond.
"Release!" the elven Archon practically shouted in relief.
POP!
The infinite white sub-space dissolved instantly.
The boundless void vanished, and reality snapped back into place, returning them to the solid,dark-granite training vault beneath the Keep.
Aeliana slumped back against her floating staff, letting out a massive soul-cleansing sigh of pure relief as her feet touched the real floorboards.
Beside her, resting peacefully on a plush woolen bench,
Talira was still sound asleep, her small humanoid chest rising and falling in deep restorative slumber following her intense bloodline awakening.
Morwenna sheathed Tidebringer with a crisp clack, rolling her stiff shoulders as she began walking toward the heavy iron vault doors.
She glanced back over her shoulder, tossing a casual knowing grin toward the God of Thunder.

"Hey, Thor," Morwenna called out in her raspy drawl. "Since we’re calling a truce for the morning... I know a place in the Territory where a fiery cook named Kaelia whips up the most incredible soul-melting roasted feasts you’ll ever taste in your entire immortal life."
Thor’s storm-blue eyes widened to the size of saucers. Her ears practically perked up like a hound catching the scent of fresh meat.

"GWAHAHAHA! NOW THAT IS THE KIND OF PROPOSAL I LIKE TO HEAR!" Thor roared with booming delight, stomping her boots toward the exit. "LEAD THE WAY, SAILOR! IF THE MEAT IS AS GOOD AS YOUR SWORDPLAY, I’LL DRINK A BARREL OF MEAD IN YOUR HONOR!"
The two towering warriors reached for the heavy iron door handle—
"STOP RIGHT THERE!"
A scandalized screech echoed across the subterranean vault.
Morwenna and Thor paused, blinking in confusion as they turned around.
Standing twenty paces back, Aeliana’s face was burning a violent shade of incandescent crimson.
The elven Archon of the Stars was pointing her staff at the two warriors with wide horrified eyes.
"GO PUT ON SOME CLOTHES FIRST!" Aeliana shrieked, covering her eyes with her free hand. "BOTH OF YOU ARE COMPLETELY NAKED!"
Morwenna looked down at herself.

Her black leather coat, her tunic, and her trousers had been incinerated hours ago by Thor’s point-blank lightning discharges, leaving her standing in the cold stone vault in nothing but a few tattered smoking leather scraps that barely covered her navel.
Beside her, Thor looked down at her own broad muscled frame.

Her heavy silver breastplate had been sheared in half by Morwenna’s Universal Water slash, and her dark trousers had been reduced to a pair of shredded singed ribbons, exposing her corded sun-kissed warrior physique to the open air.
Thor looked at Morwenna and Morwenna looked at Thor.
"GWAHAHAHA!" Thor threw her head back, bursting into an unbothered laughter that shook the vault walls. "A minor wardrobe malfunction! The kitchen staff won’t mind a little extra muscle on display!"
"Tch," Morwenna smirked, crossing her scarred arms over her bare chest without an ounce of shame. "Don’t be a prude, elf. It’s just skin..."
"CLOTHES! NOW!" Aeliana screamed, her face glowing brighter than a dying star.
The suffocating ceiling of the Black Forest stretched endlessly in every direction, its dense canopy of gnarled obsidian-barked branches locking out the pale morning sky of the Umbral Basin.
Down below, the forest floor was swallowed by shadows and thick layers of damp moss and snow that swallowed the rhythmic crunch of marching boots.
Squad One advanced in a disciplined attacking formation.

The fifteen newly outfitted recruit maidens held their positions tightly, their hands gripping the polished ash-wood shafts of their void-iron-tipped spears and the leather-wrapped hilts of their arming swords.
Riding tall at the center of the column, Silas held the reins of Valkyrie with a relaxed grace.
The Umbral Wolf stepped silently across the treacherous terrain, her thick blond fur rippling with raw power.
Wedged snugly between Silas’s arms on the saddle, the blue-haired Princess shifted uncomfortably for the third time in as many minutes.
Her lightweight sky-iron cuirass clinked softly against her weave harness, and her fingers drummed a rhythm against the pommel.

"Lord Silas," the Princess spoke up, her musical voice tinged with a disappointed pout as she turned her head back to look at him. "Are we entirely certain that this dreary expanse of dead timber is an active combat sector?... We have been traversing these woods for nearly half an hour, and yet I have not laid eyes on a single terrifying beast. At this rate, my newly tailored scout armor will gather nothing more than dust and damp air rather than glorious combat honors."
Walking effortlessly alongside the dire wolf’s left flank, Aurelia did not break her stride.
The former Saintess had her slender rapier sheathed securely at her hip.
Her white-enameled cuirass gleamed with pure luster, and her golden-amber eyes scanned the dark thickets with a vigilance born of a warrior.
To the right flank, creeping low through the brambles with feral athleticism, Lupina sniffed the damp air, her silver pointed wolf ears twitching toward the upper canopy.
A few paces behind her, Morrighan walked on the moss with her dark tail shifting like living shadows in the gloom.
Silas chuckled softly, glancing down at the blue-haired royal maiden before projecting his voice so every recruit in the ranks could hear him clearly.

"Do not let the quiet fool you, Princess," Silas instructed. "The Umbral Basin may appear silent on the surface, but creatures of all shapes, sizes, and appetites lurk just beneath the shadows. Some of them are prime game... rich in clean mana and thick with tender marbled meat that Kaelia can slow-roast over the fire with sweet honey glaze but others..."
WHOOSH! WHOOSH! WHOOSH!

Thor looked at Morwenna and Morwenna looked at Thor.
"GWAHAHAHA!" Thor threw her head back, bursting into an unbothered laughter that shook the vault walls.
"A minor wardrobe malfunction!
The kitchen staff won’t mind a little extra muscle on display!"
"Tch," Morwenna smirked, crossing her scarred arms over her bare chest without an ounce of shame.
"Don’t be a prude, elf.
It’s just skin..."
"CLOTHES!
NOW!" Aeliana screamed, her face glowing brighter than a dying star.
The suffocating ceiling of the Black Forest stretched endlessly in every direction, its dense canopy of gnarled obsidian-barked branches locking out the pale morning sky of the Umbral Basin.
Down below, the forest floor was swallowed by shadows and thick layers of damp moss and snow that swallowed the rhythmic crunch of marching boots.
Squad One advanced in a disciplined attacking formation.

The fifteen newly outfitted recruit maidens held their positions tightly, their hands gripping the polished ash-wood shafts of their void-iron-tipped spears and the leather-wrapped hilts of their arming swords.
Riding tall at the center of the column, Silas held the reins of Valkyrie with a relaxed grace.
The Umbral Wolf stepped silently across the treacherous terrain, her thick blond fur rippling with raw power.
Wedged snugly between Silas’s arms on the saddle, the blue-haired Princess shifted uncomfortably for the third time in as many minutes.
Her lightweight sky-iron cuirass clinked softly against her weave harness, and her fingers drummed a rhythm against the pommel.
"Lord Silas," the Princess spoke up, her musical voice tinged with a disappointed pout as she turned her head back to look at him.
"Are we entirely certain that this dreary expanse of dead timber is an active combat sector?...
We have been traversing these woods for nearly half an hour, and yet I have not laid eyes on a single terrifying beast.
At this rate, my newly tailored scout armor will gather nothing more than dust and damp air rather than glorious combat honors."
Walking effortlessly alongside the dire wolf’s left flank, Aurelia did not break her stride.
The former Saintess had her slender rapier sheathed securely at her hip.
Her white-enameled cuirass gleamed with pure luster, and her golden-amber eyes scanned the dark thickets with a vigilance born of a warrior.
To the right flank, creeping low through the brambles with feral athleticism, Lupina sniffed the damp air, her silver pointed wolf ears twitching toward the upper canopy.
A few paces behind her, Morrighan walked on the moss with her dark tail shifting like living shadows in the gloom.
Silas chuckled softly, glancing down at the blue-haired royal maiden before projecting his voice so every recruit in the ranks could hear him clearly.
"Do not let the quiet fool you, Princess," Silas instructed.
"The Umbral Basin may appear silent on the surface, but creatures of all shapes, sizes, and appetites lurk just beneath the shadows.
Some of them are prime game... rich in clean mana and thick with tender marbled meat that Kaelia can slow-roast over the fire with sweet honey glaze but others..."
WHOOSH!
WHOOSH!
WHOOSH!

chapters.title: Chapter 441: The Princess’s First Battle
paragraphs: The stagnant air in the upper canopy violently ruptured.
A series of whipping sounds tore down from the high branches, echoing through the dense timber like cracking leather.

Massive boughs groaned and violently rattled under sudden shifting weight, dislodging thick showers of black pine needles, decaying bark, and heavy clumps of rotting moss that rained onto the forest floor below.
The fifteen recruit maidens reacted in a single fluid heartbeat.

Without waiting for a direct command, their rigorous drills took over... boots snapped into the wet loam, shoulder to shoulder, locking their iron-rimmed bucklers edge-to-edge into an unbroken outward-facing defensive perimeter while angling their void-iron spear tips skyward into the shuddering gloom.

"...Others, on the other hand," Silas continued smoothly, his composure remained unshaken as he held Valkyrie’s reins with a relaxed hand. "are inedible, repulsive, and exponentially more dangerous when they coordinate in swarms... That is why individual bravado gets you slaughtered out here. True strength lies in unison!"
THUD! SPLAT! SQUELCH!
Dozens of mucus-slicked bodies dropped from the fifty-foot boughs, crashing violently against the mossy earth in an encircling perimeter.
Silas narrowed his eyes, his gaze coolly sweeping over the writhing ring of monstrosities that had surrounded his girls.
They were grotesque aberrations.

From the neck up, each beast bore the broad armored head of an apex Komodo dragon... lined with thick calcified cranial plates, glowing yellow slit-pupils, rows of serrated fangs dripping emerald venom, and a thick bifurcated black tongue that hissed with corrosive steaming bile.
But from the base of their throats down, all reptilian limbs vanished.
Their forms extended into thirty-foot-long, bloated worm trunks covered in rubbery, slime-coated hide that writhed, squirmed, and churned the damp forest soil into a foul morass.
’Oh? A new species...’ Silas thought, raising an eyebrow in analytical assessment. ’Are these abominations migrating from the deeper trenches of the basin?’
A golden interface chime chimed softly in his peripheral vision.
[Target Analyzed: Komado Wryworms (Tier 2)]
Silas let out a dry resigned sigh.
’Right... Komodo dragon heads grafted onto bloated mucus-dripping worm bodies... Truly the most repulsive combination possible.’
"Squad One!" Silas barked, his voice sounding sharp and commanding. "Engage!"
"Front rank, lock shields!" shouted Helen, the tall freckle-faced recruit anchoring the forward line. "Spears at forty-five degrees! Don’t let them close the pocket!"
"Brace! Dig your heels into the roots!" Sarah called out from the right flank, slamming the bottom rim of her iron buckler into the damp earth to secure her footing.
Three massive wryworms lunged simultaneously, their scaly jaws unhinging wide as pressurized streams of greenish acidic venom sprayed through the air.
"Shields up! Deflect the bile!" Helen yelled.
The front rank angled their bucklers in unison, letting the corrosive spray hiss and splash harmlessly off the reinforced metal faces onto the damp moss.
"Now! Thrust in three... two... ONE!"
Four ash-wood spears punched forward in synchronized harmony.
The void-iron points pierced through the softer fleshy underbellies right beneath the leading wryworm’s scaly throat with a wet bone-crunching crunch.

The thrashing, thirty-foot beast shrieked, green bile spraying from its maw as the four maidens leaned their full body weight into their shafts, pinning the monster’s thrashing mass firmly to the loam.
"Step in and sever the neck!" another maiden shouted, drawing her arming sword.
Stepping smoothly past the braced spear line, she brought her blade down in a heavy two-handed overhead arc.
The sharpened steel cleaved cleanly through the rubbery vertebrae, severing the horned reptilian head from its segmented worm trunk in a single stroke.
Black sulfurous ichor erupted from the stump, splashing across the ferns.
"Watch the right flank! Two more sliding through the brush!"
"I have the flank! Sarah, hold your brace!"
The recruit maidens moved with fluid vocal coordination, calling out enemy movements, covering exposed angles, and dismantling the Tier-2 swarm with disciplined teamwork.
Seeing the recruits holding the line so cleanly, Lupina’s anxious need to prove herself flared to a boiling point.
Her silver wolf ears pinned flat against her silver hair, and her bushy tail bristled with fierce restless agitation.
"I’m not standing behind the fledglings! I’ll prove my worth on this field!" Lupina growled fiercely, her three-inch retractable steel claw gauntlets snapping outward with a metallic shik.
Dropping low onto all fours, the silver-haired demi-human surged forward in a blinding burst of gray speed.

She tore directly into a cluster of five charging wryworms, her steel claws blurring into a whirlwind of silver arcs that ripped through scaly hide, muscle fibers, and thick mucus with frantic, high-velocity savagery.
"DIE! SQUISH! BLEED! AHAHAHA... GACK! CHOKE!"
Mid-cackle, a severed arterial segment of a wryworm ruptured beneath her right claw gauntlet, blasting a pressurized geyser of black, sulfurous monster blood straight into Lupina’s wide-open mouth.
Her manic laughter choked off into violent frantic coughing.
"BLAAARGH! PTOOEY! ACK! COUGH! IT TASTES LIKE RANCID MUD AND ROTTEN WATER!" Lupina shrieked in tearful revulsion, stumbling back onto two feet and clutching her throat with clawed gauntlets.
Her tongue stuck out as she gagged violently. "WATER! SOMEBODY GET ME WATER! I’VE BEEN POISONED! MY TONGUE IS DYING!"
Standing a few paces back with quiet, imposing poise, Morrighan watched the display.
The tall demonic caster stood unbothered, her pale ashen skin contrasting against the long crimson hair cascading down her back.
Her twin obsidian-black horns curved gracefully from her temples, and her deep molten gold eyes glowed with dignified authority.
Her scale-armored spade-tipped tail swayed in a slow arc behind her dark mythril coat.
Morrighan’s lips curved into a reserved smirk, her deep contralto voice cutting smoothly through the din.
"You brought that indignity upon yourself, Lupina," Morrighan murmured. "Perhaps next time you might maintain the discipline to keep your jaws shut while tearing through rancid viscera."
"IT’S NOT FUNNY, YOU HORNED WITCH! COUGH! HACK! WATEEEER!" Lupina wheezed, frantically wiping her tongue against the clean forearm of her tunic.
HISS!
Three more thirty-foot wryworms burst through the dense ferns, lunging with gaping venomous maws at the distracted, gagging wolf-girl.
Lupina’s frantic coughing ceased for a split second as her feral combat reflexes kicked in.
Dropping low, she kicked off the earth in a fluid backward somersault, letting the snapping jaws slam together in the empty air where she had stood a microsecond prior.
Landing lightly on her boots, Lupina’s amber eyes flared with wounded pride and irritation.
"You slimy bastards ruined my momentum!" she snarled, snapping her claws forward.
Morrighan stepped forward, her obsidian horns glowing with dark abyssal light as she calmly took control of the engagement.
"[Demon’s Resolve]." Morrighan incanted.
A dark crimson aura surged across her frame, instantly doubling her physical output.

With a sharp flick of her palm, four shadow-forged abyssal chains erupted from the damp loam, wrapping tightly around the segmented bodies of the three lunging wryworms and pinning them firmly to the earth.
Morrighan closed the distance in a single heavy stride. Her right fist ignited with a swirling superheated vortex of dark demonic fire.
"[Brimstone Punch]!"
KRA-BOOM!
Morrighan drove her fist into the armored skull of the central monster.

The shockwave blasted dirt, roots, and dead pine needles forty feet into the surrounding air as the cranium of the beast caved inward under the dark flames, its segmented body incinerating from within.
Before the remaining two chained wryworms could thrash, Morrighan pivoted smoothly, whipping her heavy spade-tipped tail in a thunderous horizontal cleave.

The armored tail struck with the force of an iron mace, shattering the neck vertebrae of the second beast before she released a point-blank [Brimstone Bolt] from her palm, detonating the third into smoldering ash.
As the dark smoke cleared, Lupina turned her gaze toward the center of the clearing where Aurelia was moving.
The former Saintess advanced with an ethereal musical grace.

Aurelia did not bother drawing the mithril rapier at her hip. Instead, she raised her slender pale hands, extending her fingers toward a cluster of six charging wryworms that were slithering aggressively toward Silas’s mount.
VUUUUUUM!
Thin brilliant threads of incandescent, sacred holy light shot forth from the tips of Aurelia’s fingers.
The beams did not fire as blunt destructive blasts... rather, they wove through the humid air with microscopic precision.
The glowing threads crisscrossed between the obsidian tree trunks, forming an intricate glowing web of pure holy energy that hung suspended across the clearing.
The moment the six wryworms surged into the radius of the sanctified web, the microscopic threads tightened.
SHING! SHING! SHING!
With effortless ease, the holy light sliced through thick scale plates, bone marrow, and segmented worm hides simultaneously.
The six beasts were cleanly carved into dozens of neat, cauterized cubes, collapsing to the mossy earth without a single drop of vile black ichor staining the Saintess’s pristine white cuirass.
Lupina crossed her arms, still wiping phantom tastes of monster blood from her lips.
"Show-off..." she muttered under her breath, her tail twitching in mild annoyance.
Across the clearing, the battle was practically over.
The recruit maidens had wiped out their assigned targets, leaning on their spears as they caught their breath and surveyed the carnage with proud smiles.
Only one solitary wounded wryworm remained.
Its scaly snout was fractured, its segmented tail oozed black fluids, and it dragged its broken body weakly across the moss, coming to a halt directly in front of Valkyrie’s forelegs.
The Princess’s azure eyes widened with sudden electrifying realization.
’A wounded beast... right before my feet!’ she thought, her heart hammering wildly against her ribs with pure adrenaline. ’This is my chance to secure my first sovereign combat kill!’
Without waiting for Silas to stop her, the Princess scrambled down from the saddle, landing on her leather-clad boots with a soft thud.
She drew the small utility dagger from her thigh sheath, gripping the hilt with both hands and setting her feet in a fierce dramatic stance.
"Yield before the might of the High Throne, foul aberration!" the Princess proclaimed with sweeping courtly flair.
She charged forward two determined steps, raising the dagger high and driving it downward with all her mortal strength directly into the center of the beast’s scaly forehead.
CLANG!
The sharp void-iron tip struck the thick calcified bone plate of the Komodo snout.
Lacking mana or enhanced physical strength, the strike did zero damage.
Instead, the monumental kinetic recoil traveled straight back up the blade, violently jarring the Princess’s wrists and elbows.
Her center of gravity was thrown entirely out of alignment.
WHOOSH...THUD!
Her slick boots lost all traction on the wet moss, and for the second time that morning, the Princess went crashing down onto her rear.
She sprawled flat on the damp ground, her skirts bunched and her legs kicking the air as her dagger tumbled harmlessly into the ferns.
"Ow..." the Princess groaned softly, rubbing her aching tailbone with a flustered pout.
The wounded wryworm hissed weakly, its yellow slit-pupils focusing on the fallen royal maiden as it opened its fanged maw.
SCHLICK!
Before the monster could even hiss a second time, Helen lunged from the left flank.
Her arming sword descended in a clean, diagonal cleave, cleanly severing the monster’s head and ending its life instantly.𝚏𝗿𝗲𝐞𝚠𝕖𝐛𝗻𝗼𝐯𝕖𝚕.𝚌𝗼𝗺
Helen stepped over the carcass, wiping the black gore from her blade before extending a strong calloused hand down to the Princess. "You alright there, miss?"
The Princess blinked, staring at the severed monster head, then down at her scuffed leather leggings and trembling hands.
Instead of feeling humiliated, an overwhelming rush of intoxicating exhilaration flooded her chest.
Her porcelain cheeks flushed a brilliant radiant pink, and her azure eyes sparkled with genuine adventurous delight as she grasped Helen’s hand and pulled herself up.
"That was... completely terrifying!" the Princess laughed out loud. "The impact! The deafening hiss! Is this truly what combat feels like?!"
Sitting atop Valkyrie, Silas watched the entire display with a wide approving grin.

"Outstanding work, Squad One!" Silas announced, his sovereign voice ringing out over the clearing. "Your defensive formation held firm, your callouts were sharp, and your coordination in neutralizing Tier-2 swarms was executed with commendable unison."
The fifteen recruits stood at attention, their chests swelling with immense pride. Silas raised his golden-runed sword, pointing the shining blade toward the deeper path of the forest.
"Catch your breath and keep your perimeter tight... There are countless more monsters waiting in these woods for us to clear out. Let’s move!"
"YEAH! FOR BLESSED LAND!" the recruit maidens cheered in thunderous, synchronized unison with their morale soaring as the expedition resumed its march through the Black Forest.
Roughly an hour later, nearly five miles to the southeast in an entirely separate sector of the Umbral Basin...
Squad Three was making its way through a narrow canyon flanked by towering cliffs of obsidian stone.

The rocky floor of the ravine was already littered with the slain corpses of dozens of jagged-horned cliff-stalkers and armored basalt-beetles, all cleanly dispatched by the fifteen scout maidens under Tasmin’s command.
Tasmin walked at the head of the formation, her twin curved scouting daggers twirling smoothly around her fingers.
Despite having scouted and mapped this exact rocky ravine three times over the past week, a prickling unnatural tension hung heavy in the atmosphere.
The usual sounds of the basin... the whistling wind through the jagged crags and the distant scuttling of rock-lizards were completely absent.
The silence was eerie.
"Commander Tasmin," a scout recruit whispered from behind, pointing a trembling finger ahead. "Look... at the canyon mouth."
Tasmin halted, raising her clenched fist to bring the entire squad to an immediate stop.
"I see it," Tasmin muttered, her eyes narrowing into razor slits.
Rolling through the mouth of the ravine was a thick milky-white fog.
It did not drift like ordinary morning mist... it crept along the cold stone floor like a living, sentient entity.
"Weapons ready and tighten the wedge," Tasmin commanded in a low hiss.
The fifteen maidens instantly shifted into a tight interlocking defensive wedge with their spear tips glinting coldly in the pale light.
Through the swirling white mist, the frantic uneven sound of running footsteps echoed against the canyon walls.
"H-Help! Please! Somebody help me!"
