The fifteen recruits stood at attention, their chests swelling with immense pride.
Silas raised his golden-runed sword, pointing the shining blade toward the deeper path of the forest.
"Catch your breath and keep your perimeter tight...
There are countless more monsters waiting in these woods for us to clear out.
Let’s move!"
"YEAH!
FOR BLESSED LAND!" the recruit maidens cheered in thunderous, synchronized unison with their morale soaring as the expedition resumed its march through the Black Forest.
Roughly an hour later, nearly five miles to the southeast in an entirely separate sector of the Umbral Basin...
Squad Three was making its way through a narrow canyon flanked by towering cliffs of obsidian stone.

The rocky floor of the ravine was already littered with the slain corpses of dozens of jagged-horned cliff-stalkers and armored basalt-beetles, all cleanly dispatched by the fifteen scout maidens under Tasmin’s command.
Tasmin walked at the head of the formation, her twin curved scouting daggers twirling smoothly around her fingers.
Despite having scouted and mapped this exact rocky ravine three times over the past week, a prickling unnatural tension hung heavy in the atmosphere.
The usual sounds of the basin... the whistling wind through the jagged crags and the distant scuttling of rock-lizards were completely absent.
The silence was eerie.
"Commander Tasmin," a scout recruit whispered from behind, pointing a trembling finger ahead.
"Look... at the canyon mouth."
Tasmin halted, raising her clenched fist to bring the entire squad to an immediate stop.
"I see it," Tasmin muttered, her eyes narrowing into razor slits.
Rolling through the mouth of the ravine was a thick milky-white fog.
It did not drift like ordinary morning mist... it crept along the cold stone floor like a living, sentient entity.
"Weapons ready and tighten the wedge," Tasmin commanded in a low hiss.
The fifteen maidens instantly shifted into a tight interlocking defensive wedge with their spear tips glinting coldly in the pale light.
Through the swirling white mist, the frantic uneven sound of running footsteps echoed against the canyon walls.
"H-Help!
Please!
Somebody help me!"

chapters.title: Chapter 442: Shapeshifters In The Umbral Basin
paragraphs: A woman stumbled out from the depths of the fog, clutching her left shoulder.
She was clad in the standard scout-infantry armor of Blessed Land, her face smeared with soot and dirt, her eyes wide with breathless panic.

"Thank the gods... Commander Tasmin!" the woman cried, running toward the squad with outstretched arms. "I... I was assigned to Commander Brida’s squad... we were ambushed by an alpha pack near the southern ridge... I got separated from the group and—"
THWIP!
Tasmin’s right arm blurred into a silver streak.
A heavy throwing dagger whistled through the air with terrifying velocity, burying itself dead-center between the running woman’s eyebrows with a sickening hollow thwack.
"Aah!"
Several of the recruit maidens behind Tasmin gasped in sheer, horrified shock, their hands flying to their mouths as the woman’s body froze mid-stride.
"Commander! What did you just do?!" a recruit cried in panic.
Before the panic could spread, the body of the woman did not collapse.
SZZZZT... BUBBLE... SQUELCH!
The woman’s skull and chest began to boil violently, her pale flesh liquefying into gray bubbling slime.
The human silhouette stretched, twisted, and distorted with the wet, agonizing sounds of snapping cartilage and expanding bone, rapidly ballooning into a massive eight-foot-tall bipedal monstrosity.
The creature was a grotesque standing wolf-aberration covered in patchy, matted fur of pitch-black and dull silver.
Its torso was unnaturally long and gaunt, its arms ended in four-foot sickle-claws of jagged bone, and its deformed asymmetrical jaws dripped with foul acidic saliva that hissed against the stone.
Tasmin calmly drew a second throwing dagger from her hip, stepping forward with cold disdain.

"You got the territorial emblem wrong, you ugly parasite," Tasmin drawled coldly, gesturing with the tip of her blade. "The Blessed Land crest has the golden sword piercing the cracked shield straight down the vertical center... On your forged breastplate, you carved the crossguard tilted to the left. If you’re going to shapeshift into one of our sisters, at least pay attention to basic uniform standards."
The grotesque wolf-beast let out a wet gurgling snarl, reaching up with a sickle-claw to wrench Tasmin’s throwing dagger from its forehead.
The wound sizzled and bubbled, regenerating at a sluggish, strained pace.

Tasmin’s sharp amber eyes swept over the monster’s torso, immediately noting the deep cauterized cleave marks and shattered ribs that already riddled its frame... injuries that were clearly inflicted by a massive blunt-force bladed weapon.

’It claimed it was running from Brida’s squad...’ Tasmin thought with a dry sarcastic smirk touching her lips. ’Don’t tell me that muscle-headed brute Brida ran into this shape-shifting trash and half-assed finishing the job?’
Tasmin wouldn’t put it past the towering woman to get bored mid-fight and let an injured straggler run off.
"GRAAAAAAAH!"
Enraged that its ambush had failed, the grotesque wolf-aberration lunged forward with savage speed, its sickle-claws sweeping horizontally to cleave Tasmin in half.
Tasmin smiled calmly, dropping her center of gravity into an agile skirmish stance.
"Alright, girls. Watch closely... this is how you properly dissect a—"
BOOOOOOOOOOM!
The air inside the narrow canyon violently imploded.
An armored blur tore out from the depths of the thick fog at Mach-speed, moving with such absurd velocity that the displaced air formed a visible shockwave cone around its frame.
SPLAT-CRUNCH!
The blur collided dead-center with the leaping wolf-aberration.

The impact was so cataclysmic that the eight-foot monster didn’t even have time to shriek... its entire body was instantaneously pulverized into a fine, crimson mist of crushed bone, shredded fur, and liquified organs that splattered across the canyon walls.
FWHUUUUUSH.
The concussive shockwave blew the surrounding white fog away completely, clearing the entire canyon in a single violent draft.
Standing in the center of the fresh blood splatter looking completely unscathed, was Brida.
The Commander had her tower shield strapped securely to her back, while her heavy war-cleaver rested casually across her broad shoulder.
She was drenched from head to toe in black monster blood, her fierce battle-hardened face sporting a wide and thoroughly satisfied grin.
Brida casually clapped her thick armored gauntlets together, dusting off a chunk of pulverized wolf gristle.
"Fuuu..." Brida exhaled with a relaxed toothy smirk, looking up at Tasmin. "Finally caught up to that slippery little cockroach."
The lingering stench of sulfurous pulverized wolf marrow hung thick in the narrow canyon, settling like a layer of hot grease over the cold obsidian crags.
A dead quiet blanketed Squad Three.
The fifteen recruit maidens stood frozen in their tight defensive wedge, their knuckles turning white against the polished ash-wood shafts of their spears.

Their breaths caught hard in their chests as they stared at the center of the ravine where, barely a second prior, an eight-foot-tall bipedal wolf abomination had been lunging forward with sickle-claws bared to tear their commander in two.
Now, there was only a colossal, pulverized crater of liquid gore, bone splinters, and black slime painting the stone walls.
And standing right in the epicenter of the carnage, completely unbothered, was Brida.
The towering woman stood like an immovable monolith of bloodstained iron.
’She’s scary...’
Her massive tower shield remained locked securely to the harness on her back, while her heavy war-cleaver rested lazily across her broad shoulder.
Black viscous monster blood dripped steadily from the spiked rims of her iron gauntlets, pattering softly onto the rock.
Drip...! Drip...! Drip...!

"Is... is she truly mortal?" a young recruit maiden in the back rank whispered, her voice trembling with awe and sheer terror as she swallowed hard. "She moved so fast the air in the gorge literally imploded..."

"Quiet!" another recruit hissed beneath her breath, her eyes wide as she stared at Brida’s back. "Did you forget what she did during the Lord War against the Unmovable Wall which we were a part of? She held off entire phalanxes of infantry by herself! One would think that after days of war, her muscles would be completely torn, cramped, and sore... but look at her! She’s still a monster!"

"She’s terrifying," a third recruit muttered, a cold bead of sweat rolling down her temple. "I don’t think fatigue even exists in that woman’s vocabulary. If she swung that cleaver at a mountain, the mountain would apologize and split in half..."
Standing ten paces away, Tasmin didn’t share the recruits’ wide-eyed terror.
The agile scout commander twirled her slender void-iron dagger around her fingers with effortless ease, sliding it into her hip sheath with a crisp click.
She crossed her arms over her chest, letting out a long exasperated sigh as she narrowed her amber eyes at the towering Commander.

"Care to explain why you let that parasite escape your sector in the first place, Brida?" Tasmin asked, her melodic voice dripping with deadpan annoyance. "You’re a Commander of Blessed Land. Since when do you let a half-dead straggler sprint three miles across the basin just so it can try to ambush my squad?"
Brida stopped wiping her gauntlets.
She waved a thick iron-plated hand dismissively through the air, rolling her broad shoulders with a loud popping crack of her cervical vertebrae.

"Ah, don’t bust my chops, Tasmin," Brida grumbled, letting out a rough sniffle as she rubbed the bridge of her nose with the back of a bloody glove. "You have no idea what my squad ran into back at the eastern ridge... We were sweeping through the deadwood when suddenly, out of nowhere, we got jumped by an entire pack of those disgusting freaks and do you know what face they were wearing?"
Tasmin raised an eyebrow, entirely unimpressed. "What face?"

"Lord Silas’s face," Brida said, her fierce expression twisting into a dramatic grimace of lingering trauma. "Dozens of them. All running on all fours through the mud, hissing and snapping their jaws, wearing the Captain’s handsome, smiling face! Do you have any idea how psychologically damaging that is?! I had to swing my cleaver and crush twelve of my own Lord’s faces into red paste just to clear a path! My soul was weeping the entire time!"
She threw her hands up in exasperation, the heavy iron plates of her armor rattling loudly against her breastplate.

"By the time I finished smashing the twelfth fake Silas, this last slippery bastard took advantage of my emotional turmoil and bolted into the fog! Truly, shapeshifters are the most vile unholy vermin in existence!"
A massive deadpan sweatdrop practically formed on the side of Tasmin’s temple.
She stared at Brida with an expression that conveyed soul-deep exhaustion.
"You crushed twelve fake copies of our Lord without blinking, and you’re calling that ’emotional turmoil’?" Tasmin deadpanned, shaking her head.
Then, her eyes narrowed with sudden, sharp realization. "Wait a minute... where the hell is your squad, Brida?"
Brida paused. She blinked her large amber eyes, tilting her head to the side like a giant confused hound.
"My squad?" Brida repeated casually. "Oh, I left them behind on the other side of the ridge... In that wide clearing just past the fog bank. It’s barely a five-minute jog from here."
SLAP!
Tasmin brought her palm up, planting it squarely against her own face with a loud stinging crack that echoed through the canyon.
She dragged her fingers slowly down her skin, her teeth grinding together so hard her jaw muscles visibly twitched.

"You... you left fifteen recruits completely unattended..." Tasmin muttered, her voice trembling with rising disbelief. "...in the middle of an uncharted basin sector, immediately after discovering an active nest of bipedal shapeshifting parasites that mimic human appearance?"
Brida opened her mouth to offer a defense—
"Well, they were holding their spears nicely and—"
She froze.
Brida’s eyes snapped wide. The color drained from her fierce face as the catastrophic logistical oversight finally registered inside her battle-hardened brain.
"OH SHIT!" Brida roared.

Without waiting another microsecond, the Titan spun on her armored heels, detonating the stone floor beneath her boots with a violent boom as she sprinted back toward the foggy ridge like a runaway locomotive.
"Squad Three, on me! Double time!" Tasmin barked sharply, gesturing with her blades. "Don’t lose formation!"
"Move, move, move!" the fifteen recruit maidens shouted, hoisting their spears and breaking into a dead sprint behind their commander.
The dense unnatural fog whipped violently past their faces as Squad Three tore through the rocky pass.
Less than two minutes later, the mist abruptly thinned, giving way to a wide, bowl-shaped clearing surrounded by jagged obsidian pillars.
But the moment Brida and Tasmin burst into the clearing, both commanders skidded to an immediate halt, their boots tearing deep furrows into the mossy dirt.
The clearing was in chaotic turmoil.

Thirty recruit maidens... all wearing the identical dark leather-and-sky-iron scout armor of Blessed Land, all bearing the cracked obsidian shield and golden sword insignia were locked in a screaming brawl.
Spears were clashing against bucklers, arming swords were locked at the hilt, and fists were flying wildly across the clearing.
The moment Brida’s armored silhouette breached the perimeter, the fighting instantly halted.
Every single maiden in the clearing turned toward the entrance, pointing their trembling fingers across the divide and screaming in hysterical panic.
"COMMANDER BRIDA! THEY’RE SHAPESHIFTERS! KILL THEM!"
"DON’T LISTEN TO THEM, COMMANDER! THEY’RE THE FAKES! WE WERE WAITING FOR YOU AND THEY SURGED OUT OF THE MIST!"
"LOOK AT HER NOSE! SARAH DOESN’T HAVE A FRECKLE ON HER LEFT NOSTRIL! SHE’S A MONSTER!"
"I’VE HAD THIS FRECKLE SINCE BIRTH, YOU SLIMY PARASITE! DIE!"

"EVERYBODY SHUT THE HELL UP!" Brida’s booming thunderous voice reverberated across the canyon like an artillery strike, physically rattling the teeth in the girls’ jaws and silencing the chaotic screaming instantly.
Brida stepped into the center of the clearing, her heavy boots crunching on the gravel.
She looked back and forth between the two identical groups of fifteen maidens, her broad brow furrowing deeply as she scratched her scarred cheek in utter helpless bewilderment.
"Alright... which one of you is the real Sarah who asked me for extra dried beef rations this morning?" Brida asked, pointing a thick gauntlet.
Both Sarahs raised their hands simultaneously. "Me! I asked for the extra salt-cured strip!"
’How does she even know that...?’
Brida’s eye twitched.
She looked over her shoulder toward Tasmin, completely at a loss for words.
"Tasmin... I’m a brawler. I solve problems by crushing them with heavy steel. My brain isn’t built for psychological detective work. How do we tell which fifteen to slaughter?"
Tasmin let out a soft low chuckle.
She walked past Brida, moving with an eerie grace as she stepped up to the saddle of her Blessed Wolf, swinging her leg over the mount’s back with fluid athleticism.
She reined the silver wolf in, letting the beast pad slowly toward the center of the divided maidens.
"I believe you," Tasmin said softly, her amber eyes scanning the thirty faces with razor-sharp coldness.
"Which ones?!" Brida asked, gripping her cleaver. "Point at them and I’ll turn them into soup!"
"The ones on the left," Tasmin answered smoothly.
The fifteen maidens on the left flank immediately took a step forward, their eyes widening in panic.
"Commander Tasmin, no! We’re the real Squad Two! We swear on our Lord’s name—"
VUUUUUUM.
Before the words could fully leave their mouths, the pitch-black shadow cast beneath Tasmin’s Blessed Wolf violently surged.
The dark puddle did not remain on the ground... it extended outward like a living web of liquid obsidian, shooting across the stone floor in fifteen distinct needle-thin tendrils.
In less than a fraction of a microsecond, the tendrils erupted beneath the boots of the fifteen maidens on the left, coiling around their ankles, calves, and hips like solid iron vices.
"[Shadow Anchorage]."

You don’t cast a single sliver of a shadow... Your bodies are hollow constructs of condensed biological slime and illusion mana. You cannot mimic what you do not truly possess."
The faces of the fifteen frozen maidens instantly lost all human warmth.
Their eyes turned pure milky white, their jaws unhinging with sickening snaps as they let out synchronized ear-splitting shrieks of pure rage.
"SKREEEEEEEEEEEEEEE-CHAAAAAA!"
Their flesh began to boil, dark gray slime bubbling through the seams of their forged armor as their spines buckled outward, trying desperately to break free from the shadow binds.
"Die in silence." Tasmin whispered.
She raised her right hand, curling her slender fingers into a tight crushing fist.
SNAP! KRA-BOOOOOOOOM!
The shadow tendrils violently imploded inward.
Fourteen of the fifteen frozen monstrosities detonated simultaneously under the catastrophic gravitational pressure.
A colossal wet explosion of dark slime, shattered bone fragments, and black ichor sprayed across the clearing, the sheer kinetic shockwave evaporating their fake armor into dust.
Tasmin left exactly one alive.
In the blink of an eye... faster than the recruits could even perceive, Tasmin vanished from the saddle of her mount.
SHING!

She materialized instantly behind the sole surviving shapeshifter, her right arm wrapping tightly around its throat while the cold edge of her dagger pressed deep into the jugular of its bubbling, half-transformed neck.

"Talk," Tasmin whispered into its ear, her raspy voice vibrating with merciless intent. "Who sent your brood into this sector of the basin? Where is your queen nesting? Speak in human tongue, or I will peel your nervous system out through your ribs one millimeter at a time."
The shapeshifter thrashed wildly against her grip.
Its human jaw dissolved completely, replaced by a grotesque dripping wolf snout that snapped its yellow fangs in frantic defiance.
"Grol’kash... vur... kraaa! Zulgath... mor... SKREEE!" the beast gurgled, spraying foul acidic bile from its throat as it hissed in its native guttural dialect.
Tasmin’s expression didn’t change in the slightest.
SCHLICK!
With a single, effortless flick of her wrist, Tasmin drew the dagger horizontally across the monster’s throat, cleanly severing its windpipe, arteries, and spinal cord in one fluid stroke.
THUD!
The decapitated monstrosity collapsed to the dirt, dissolving into a puddle of inert smoking gray ooze.
Tasmin wiped the black blood from her blade against the side of her leather trousers, sliding the weapon back into its sheath with a crisp clack.
She turned slowly on her heel, looking back toward Brida with a dry unimpressed smirk.
"What?" Tasmin shrugged, her raspy drawl echoing over the silent clearing. "Do I look like a translator who speaks fluent swamp-parasite?"
She drew a clean rag from her pouch, wiping her hands as she looked down at the puddle of dissolving slime.

’These creatures are definitely an invasive anomaly,’ Tasmin analyzed internally, her sharp mind piecing together the threat. ’Standard beasts rely on raw brute force, but these things use psychological infiltration, vocal mimicry, and coordinated decoys and more importantly... I certainly don’t feel like explaining to Kaelia why we’re hauling back meat that can transform into the Lord’s face... These things are strictly vermin to be eradicated.’
She looked up at the thirty recruit maidens... fifteen from Squad Two and fifteen from Squad Three who were all staring at her with wide reverent eyes.
"We need to distribute this intel across all sectors immediately," Tasmin announced, stepping back toward her Blessed Wolf. "Fortunately, our Lord ensured we weren’t operating like blind barbarians."
Tasmin reached into her tactical belt, turning toward one of her senior scouts. "Hand me the communication crystal."
"Here, Commander!" the scout maiden responded instantly, unhooking a glowing multifaceted azure crystal from her chest harness and handing it over.
Tasmin accepted the crystal, turning back toward Brida, who was currently standing in front of her genuine Squad Two recruits, rubbing the back of her neck with an awkward sheepish grin.

"Look, girls... I apologize for running off," Brida muttered, coughing into her gauntlet as the real Sarah and the other recruits looked up at her with crossed arms and pouts. "I got a little carried away smashing fake Captains. Next time, I promise I won’t leave you unattended..."
"You owe us double roasted pork rations tonight, Commander Brida!" Sarah declared boldly with her hands on her hips.
"Deal! Double rations for everyone!" Brida laughed heartily, visibly relieved.
Tasmin rolled her eyes at the display, shaking her head.

"Brida, quit bribing your squad with food. Given the nature of these shapeshifters, splitting into isolated fifteen-maiden squads is an unnecessary operational risk for the recruits. Our squads are combining formations right now to sweep the eastern crags together. Understood?"
Brida vaulted onto the back of her own Blessed Wolf, strapping her tower shield tightly to her forearm with a fierce, eager nod.
"Understood, scout master! Let’s hunt as a thirty-maiden phalanx!"
Tasmin raised the azure communication crystal to her lips.
She channeled a steady pulse of mana into the core, causing the facets to flash with bright blue light.
CHIME!
A crisp magical connection established across the planar frequency.
From the other side of the crystal, the ethereal and perfectly cheerful voice of Eluned resonated through the air.
"Squad Four Leader Eluned here! Hubby isn’t on this frequency, is he? If he is, I love you, Hubby!"
Tasmin sighed softly with a small smirk touching her lips. "Lady Eluned... this is Tasmin. We have an operational situation."
"Got it. Thanks for the heads-up, Tasmin!"
CLICK!
The azure glow of the communication crystal faded into dormant translucence as Eluned lowered her slender hand, tossing the small relic into the velvet pouch at her waist with a bright humming tune.
The Goddess walked with light, bouncy steps along the sunlit path, her living wooden armor humming with vibrant emerald life-mana.
She tilted her head, tapping her chin with a slender manicured finger as she pondered the report.

’Monsters that can shapeshift into anyone?’ Eluned thought, a bright and completely unfazed smile curving her delicate lips. ’Isn’t that totally fine? A monster is just fertilizer with extra steps... No matter what face it wears, it all turns into nutritious compost for my greenhouse crops anyway!’
Trailing five paces behind her, the fifteen recruit maidens of Squad Four were marching in a tight nervous formation.

Seeing their divine commander casually pocket the communication crystal after receiving an urgent report, the lead scout... a petite dark-haired maiden named Catelyn stepped forward, her voice trembling slightly.
"L-Lady Eluned..." Catelyn asked hesitantly, clutching her ash-wood spear. "Was that an emergency transmission from Commander Tasmin? Is the situation dire?"
Eluned paused, spinning around on the balls of her armored boots with a radiant sunny smile that practically lit up the dark woods.

"Oh, not at all, little fledglings!" Eluned chirped happily, waving her hand through the air as if brushing away a stray fly. "Tasmin merely informed me that there are naughty little shapeshifting parasites crawling through the basin, mimicking our sisters’ faces to eat our flesh! But you don’t need to worry your pretty little heads about that. As long as you are with me, your big sister Eluned will ensure not a single hair on your heads is harmed!"
The fifteen maidens exchanged wide-eyed nervous glances.
’She said that with such a bright smile...’ Catelyn thought with a bead of cold sweat running down her cheek. ’Why does she sound more terrifying than the monsters?!’
"Now then! Look forward, girls!" Eluned announced, clapping her wooden-armored hands together with a crisp clap. "We have arrived at our designated training sector!"
The fifteen recruits turned their eyes forward, and several of them let out audible synchronized gasps of pure, breathless wonder.
They had stepped out of the gloomy, obsidian-barked deadwood and entered a breathtaking vibrant clearing that looked entirely out of place within the rugged barren expanse of the Umbral Basin.

The clearing was carpeted in lush vibrant emerald moss, surrounded by blooming fragrant black bushes that were heavy with clusters of plump succulent purple berries that shimmered like polished amethyst under the pale morning light.
The sweet intoxicating aroma of ripe mountain fruit and fresh spring honey hung thick in the air, making the recruits’ mouths instantly water after hours of grueling marching.
The maidens stood in disciplined ranks, their eyes wide and hungry, but they remained rigid at attention, waiting for their commander’s orders.

"Look at those bushes, Commander..." a recruit whispered in awe, pointing a spear tip toward the shimmering fruit. "The berries are completely ripe! Could this be a natural spirit-orchard hidden within the basin?"
Eluned looked at the maiden, tilting her head with a look of pitying amusement.
"You poor little things..." Eluned sighed, shaking her head with a gentle, mocking tut-tut. "You really will be tricked by anything with a pretty face and a sweet smell, won’t you?"
Eluned raised her right hand, casually extending her index finger into the open air.
TAP!
She tapped the empty atmosphere as if striking a glass pane.
KRRRR-SHATTER!
A brilliant emerald shockwave rippled outward from her fingertip.

In less than a second, the vibrant green clearing, the fragrant air, and the succulent purple fruits violently fractured like brittle porcelain, shattering into thousands of dissolving translucent shards of illusion mana.
The horrifying grotesque reality of the clearing was laid bare.
The lush green moss vanished, revealing a barren corpse-strewn wasteland of dried mud, cracked shale, and rotting vegetation.

The blooming berry bushes were revealed to be tangled, barbed briars dripping with black caustic venom, covered in hundreds of bloated, pulsating black maggot-worms that writhed through rotting, putrid fruit carcasses.

Piled high against the jagged rocks were dozens of sun-bleached skulls, shattered ribcages, and the picked-clean skeletons of territorial beasts, creating a horrific charnel-ground amphitheater that reeked of stagnant decay.
The recruit maidens recoiled in gagging horror, clutching their throats as the sweet honey scent was violently replaced by the suffocating stench of rotting entrails.
"A-A graveyard...!" Catelyn choked, her face turning pale as she raised her buckler.
And sitting fifty feet ahead, perched high upon the gnarled, dead boughs of an ancient weeping willow tree in the center of the charnel pit, was the master of the illusion.
CREEEAK!
The branches groaned as the creature slowly shifted its massive terrifying weight.
It was a nightmare.
The beast stood over twelve feet tall, possessing the gaunt elongated chitin-plated torso of a predatory praying mantis, fused seamlessly with the savage, horned head of a giant demonic ape.
Its four massive, scythe-like forearms were forged from jagged, serrated bone that gleamed with dripping corrosive purple neurotoxin.𝑓𝑟ℯ𝘦𝓌𝘦𝘣𝑛𝑜𝓋𝑒𝓁.𝑐ℴ𝓂
Hanging from its bloated, insectoid abdomen was a vibrating translucent organ that actively pulsed with residual illusion mana... the biological projector that had cast the false paradise.
Its four glowing crimson eyes locked onto the fifteen women below, its ape-like maw parting to reveal rows of needle-thin rotating fangs that clicked together with a horrifying metallic sound.
CLACK! CLACK! CLACK!
Elu was not sure of the name but she did know it was Tier 3.
A wave of suffocating pressure washed over the clearing, freezing the recruit maidens in their tracks.
Their knees trembled, their breath caught in their throats, and several girls instinctively took a half-step backward, their survival instincts screaming at them to run.
"Stay your ground, fledglings!" Eluned’s voice rang out, no longer playful, but resonating with the authority of a deity.
THUD!
Eluned stepped forward, planting her wooden-armored boot firmly onto the dead earth.
VUUUUUUUUUUUM!
An overwhelming ocean of emerald Life-Mana erupted from Eluned’s frame, spreading outward across the entire clearing in a blinding, radiant shockwave.
The moment the divine green light washed over the fifteen women, an extraordinary transformation took place.
The cold, paralyzing terror gripping their hearts evaporated instantly, replaced by a roaring boundless torrent of pure vitality that surged through their spiritual meridians.
Their fatigue vanished, their heart rates stabilized, and their muscles brimmed with an almost intoxicating sensation of limitless physical stamina.

"Listen well, recruits of Blessed Land!" Eluned commanded, her emerald eyes blazing with sacred power. "While my beloved Hubby is busy managing ledgers and hunting with the others, the true training of our territory begins here! You will not grow into invincible warriors by cowering behind shields! You will forge your spirits in the fires of life-and-death combat!"
She pointed her slender wooden-clad finger straight at the twelve-foot apex mantis.
"RUSH IT! TEAR IT APART! PROVE TO YOUR LORD THAT YOU ARE WORTHY OF HIS SANCTUM!"
The fifteen maidens felt the roaring divine energy burning within their chests.
The fear was gone, replaced by a wild battle-hungry fury that set their blood ablaze.
"CHARGE! FOR THE LORD! FOR BLESSED LAND!" Catelyn roared, raising her spear.
"KILL IT!" the fourteen maidens screamed in blood-curdling defiance, breaking into a full-speed reckless charge straight toward the weeping willow tree.
Seeing the recruits surge forward, Eluned casually walked over to a clean obsidian boulder near the tree line.

chapters.title: Chapter 444: The Lord Of Blessed Land Loves Spider Eggs?
paragraphs: Eluned brushed off the dust with her armored hand, gracefully sitting down and crossing her long elegant legs.

With a bright cheerful hum, she reached into her satchel, pulling out a small, beautifully wrapped wooden bento box containing fresh honeyed biscuits, dried fruit slices, and sweet tea that she had packed herself that morning.
"Hehehe... Looking sweet Elu..."
She popped a golden biscuit into her mouth, chewing happily with puffed cheeks as she watched the fifteen women charge into the jaws of death.
"Let the show begin," Eluned giggled softly, kicking her heels against the stone.

’This truly is the finest method to train new recruits,’ Eluned mused internally with complete, affectionate ruthlessness. ’Hubby is far too gentle with these girls, worried that they might get bruised but Blessed Land’s doctrine is absolute... to serve the Lord, you must be forged in the abyss of mortality. And as long as my Authority blankets this field... they cannot die, even if their bodies are torn to shreds!’
KRA-BOOOOOOOOM!
Perched upon the high branch, the Phantom-Mantis Stalker shrieked with ear-splitting fury.
"AHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHH!"
FWHIP!
The twelve-foot beast blurred into a streak of purple momentum, dropping from the tree like a falling guillotine.
Its right bone-scythe cleaved through the air with Mach-speed, striking the forward line of recruits.
CLANG-CRACK!
Catelyn raised her iron buckler to intercept the blow, but the monumental mass of a Tier-3 beast shattered the reinforced metal face instantly.
The jagged bone-scythe tore straight through Catelyn’s left shoulder, severing muscle, tendon, and clavicle in a horrific bloody spray that sent her flying twenty feet across the dirt.
"CATELYN!" a spear maiden screamed in absolute terror.
"DON’T LOOK AWAY! IT’S SWINGING AGAIN!" Helen yelled, lunging forward with her spear.
The mantis spun its torso with terrifying insectoid flexibility. Its lower left scythe swept horizontally, catching two recruit maidens across their abdomens.
SCHLICK-SPLAT!
The razor-sharp bone sliced clean through their sky-iron cuirasses, opening massive, gushing lacerations across their torsos that spilled crimson blood onto the shale.
Both maidens collapsed to their knees, gasping for air as their vision blurred with shock.
In any standard battlefield, this would have been an instantaneous, catastrophic wipeout.
Three soldiers were critically wounded in the first three seconds of engagement.
...However this was not a standard battlefield.
VUUUUUUUUUM!
The moment their blood touched the emerald-glowing soil, Eluned’s authority ignited with miraculous intensity.
SZZZZZT... SNAP!
A radiant cocoon of emerald life-force enveloped Catelyn’s shattered shoulder.

In less than a fraction of a millisecond, severed nerves reconnected, bone fragments fused with a loud crack, and torn flesh knitted together at high speed, completely restoring her arm to peak condition before her body even finished sliding across the dirt.

Across the clearing, the two gut-cleaved maidens gasped as blinding green light sealed their abdominal wounds instantly, repairing their muscle walls, skin, and armor integrity without leaving so much as a single scar.
Catelyn sat up, her eyes wide as she looked at her fully functional unblemished shoulder.
"I’m... I’m completely healed?!" Catelyn gasped, a wild grin breaking across her face. "IT DOESN’T HURT AT ALL!"
She grabbed her fallen spear, vaulting back to her feet.
"GIRLS! WE CAN’T DIE! SISTER ELUNED IS BACKING US!" Catelyn roared at the top of her lungs, her voice echoing across the canyon. "WE CAN’T DIE! SWARM THE BASTARD! TEAR IT TO PIECES!"
The dam broke completely.
Knowing that death was rendered impossible by the will of the Goddess, all fifteen recruit maidens abandoned every shred of mortal self-preservation.
They transformed into a pack of relentless immortal berserkers, throwing their entire physical existence into an overwhelming swarm.
"PIN ITS LEGS! DON’T LET IT JUMP!"
"I’VE GOT THE LEFT SCYTHE! BRACE!"
Four maidens threw themselves directly into the mantis’s descending bone-scythes.
CRUNCH!

The bone blades impaled two of the girls through their chests, lifting them into the air but instead of screaming in agony, the two impaled maidens bared their teeth, grabbing the serrated scythes with their bare bleeding hands and locking their fingers around the bone to trap the beast’s limbs.
"NOW! STAB IT! WE HAVE ITS ARMS!" the impaled girls screamed, emerald light already healing the puncture wounds around their ribs in real-time!
"DIE! YOU UGLY ROACH!"
Six spear maidens closed the pocket from all sides.
THWACK! CRUNCH! SQUELCH!
Six spearheads punched straight through the mantis’s chitin-plated abdomen, driving deep into its internal organs.
The beast shrieked in deafening, agonizing torment, thrashing violently as black acidic ichor gushed from its punctured thorax.
"DON’T STOP! KEEP STABBING! PUNCH THROUGH THE CRANIUM!"
"STEP IN WITH THE SWORDS! CHOP ITS HEAD OFF!"
Five sword maidens lunged onto the beast’s back, using the embedded spears as footrests.
They raised their arming swords high with both hands, driving the sharpened steel down in a relentless storm of synchronized chops and thrusts.
STAB! HACK! CHOP! SPLAT!
"TAKE THIS!"
"AND THIS!"
"FOR BLESSED LAND!"
"FOR LORD SILAS!"
The fifteen maidens stabbed the twelve-foot apex mantis over two hundred consecutive times in less than thirty seconds.

The beast’s chitin armor was pulverized into fine black powder, its four bone-scythes were snapped into splinters, its illusion organ was shredded to ribbons, and its demonic ape head was reduced to an unidentifiable minced puddle of black brain matter and shattered fangs.
THUD!
The colossal corpse of the Phantom-Mantis Stalker collapsed limp against the stained shale, it had been brutally executed.
PANT... PANT... PANT.
The fifteen recruit maidens stood atop and around the pulverized carcass, their bodies completely drenched from head to toe in black monster blood, their chests heaving in synchronized breaths.
They looked at their trembling bloodstained hands, then turned toward each other, their faces breaking into wild victorious smiles as they threw their arms into the air.
"WE DID IT! WE KILLED A TIER-3 MONSTER! I’M SURE THAT WAS TIER 3!"
"YEAAAAAAAH!"
Sitting on her boulder, Eluned swallowed the last bite of her honeyed biscuit, brushing the crumbs from her lap with a proud beaming smile.
She stood up, clapping her wooden-clad hands together with genuine radiant admiration.

"Magnificent performance, my lovely fledglings!" Eluned cheered warmly, her emerald eyes sparkling. "A truly glorious slaughter! You held your ground, embraced the pain, and dismantled a predator with flawless unison! Hubby will be exceptionally proud of you all!"
The fifteen blood-soaked women cheered even louder, standing tall with unyielding pride in the heart of the conquered charnel pit.
Meanwhile, roughly three miles away in a deep cavern carved into the northern crags of the Umbral Basin...
The air inside the dark vaulted cavern was damp and heavy with the thick pungent smell of burnt silk and roasted arachnid flesh.
Standing near the cavern entrance, Aurelia held her mithril rapier loosely at her side as her white-enameled armor was completely spotless.

Beside her, the blue-haired Princess leaned her back against the damp stone wall, her arms crossed over her sky-iron breastplate as she stared into the center of the chamber with an expression of pure bewilderment.

’I knew Lord Silas was remarkably powerful... and undeniably eccentric...’ the Princess thought, her azure eyes blinking repeatedly as a bead of sweat rolled down her temple. ’...But this? This is beyond the scope of rational comprehension.’
Lying across the center of the cavern floor was the colossal, charred carcass of a Broodmother Spider.

The monstrosity had been brutally eradicated... its eight hairy legs were sheared off cleanly, its chitinous skull had been split in half by a single terrifying strike of Silas’s Gold sword, and its silk glands were smoking from point-blank fire.
And kneeling right in the middle of the spider’s pulverized nest, surrounded by thousands of glowing translucent silk threads, was Silas.
The Lord of Blessed Land had both knees planted firmly in the dirt, completely unbothered by the sticky monster slime coating his boots.
In his hands, he held a big crystalline spider egg that pulsed with rich concentrated mana.
Silas lifted the glowing spider egg high above his head, staring at the translucent shell with eyes that burned with glorious greed.
"I finally have you..." Silas whispered, his voice trembling with overwhelming ecstasy.
A wide grin spread across his handsome face, stretching from ear to ear as he threw his head back, letting out a booming, echoing laugh that shook the cavern stalactites.
"THE SPIDER EGGS! HEHEHEHE... AHAHAHAHAHAHA!"
Silas clutched the massive egg tightly against his chest, rocking back and forth in the dirt like a lunatic who had just struck the mother lode of the cosmos.
"I’M RICH! DO YOU HAVE ANY IDEA HOW MUCH HIGH-TIER ALCHEMICAL SILK AND REINFORCED CHITIN WE CAN HARVEST FROM THIS BROOD?! THE UPGRADE POINTS! THE UPGRADES! HEHEHEHEHAHAHAHAHA!"
Standing by the wall, the Princess leaned over slightly, whispering to Aurelia in a quiet concerned tone.
"Saintess Aurelia... is your Lord experiencing a severe spiritual breakdown from mana toxicity?"
Aurelia sighed softly, a gentle smile touching her lips as she shook her head.
"No, Princess," Aurelia murmured warmly, watching the dark-haired young man laugh like a madman in the dirt. "That is simply our Lord being himself... I think..."

About thirty minutes ago, well before the narrow tunnels had been coated in the sticky acidic sheen of fresh arachnid hemolymph, the vanguard of Squad One was still carving its measured path through the dense shadowed undergrowth of the Black Forest.
The air beneath the towering timber hung thick as usual, saturated with the rich, earthy scent of damp loam, crushed ferns, and the lingering tang of dried wryworm blood.
Silas sat tall and relaxed in Valkyrie’s enchanted leather saddle.
The Blessed wolf stepped across the treacherous root-tangled terrain without making a sound, her corded muscles shifting in slow movements beneath her shimmering coat.
Wedged securely in the space between Silas’s arms, the blue-haired Princess shifted her weight back and forth against the saddle pommel.
Her lightweight sky-iron cuirass clinked softly against the reinforced straps of her weave harness.
Every few seconds, her head darted left and right, her azure eyes searching the gloomy thickets for signs of an ambush.
From the left flank of the marching column, a soft crystalline chime broke the quiet rhythm of the march.

Suspended from the sturdy leather tactical belt around Morrighan’s waist, a polished multifaceted azure communication orb flared to life, casting deep-blue pulses of light across the damp forest floor.
’The orb...’
The tall demonic caster reacted with immediate poise.
Her long, crimson hair swayed gently over the clothes she wore as she stepped out of formation, closing the distance to the front with silent purposeful strides.
Morrighan came to a halt beside the towering flank of Valkyrie, dipping her head in a formal respectful bow.

"My Lord," Morrighan said, her voice a deep contralto that naturally commanded attention without being raised. "The communication orb entrusted to our unit is signaling an active transmission from the perimeter squads."
She reached down to her hip, unclipped the glowing crystal relic, and held it upward with both hands, offering it directly to Silas.
"Thank you, Morrighan," Silas said, offering her an easy appreciative smile.
He reached down to take the orb with his left hand, while naturally extending his right palm outward.
Without a second thought, he lightly patted the crown of her head, his fingers brushing gently against the smooth polished base of her curved horns.
Morrighan’s entire frame locked rigid.
Her heavy spade-tipped tail which had been swaying in a steady arc froze dead in mid-air.
Her molten-gold eyes widened by a fraction of a millimeter as a sudden unfamiliar warmth prickled beneath her pale skin.
In her former service, ordinary soldiers had recoiled from her very presence, terrified of her lineage, refusing even to set up their bedrolls within twenty paces of her tent.
Yet here, her new Lord reached down and touched her head with the casual familiarity of a commander greeting a trusted friend.
’I got a headpat?’
The gesture felt alien, almost destabilizing to her guarded nature.
Yet, as the quiet seconds passed, she realized that deep within her chest, she did not dislike the sensation in the slightest.
Silas tapped the multifaceted surface of the azure orb with the tip of his finger.
BZZZZT... CHIME.
A crisp ripple of mana resonated through the crystal core, and Tasmin’s dry voice projected into the open air.

"Lord Silas, this is Tasmin reporting from the southeastern sector," the scout commander’s voice came through. "Squad Three and Squad Two have engaged an invasive anomaly... Bipedal wolf-like shapeshifters capable of mimicking human physical form, vocal cadences, and territorial armor. Their mimicry is imperfect... They lack shadows and show structural defects sometimes. Brida and I have already eradicated the local nest."
Silas listened attentively, letting the reins rest loosely in his grip.

"Understood, Tasmin. Squad One cleared a cluster of Tier-2 wryworms along the central path. Thus far, the basin’s resistance has been relatively predictable... Keep your formation tight and ensure the recruits remain in pairs. Have you relayed this warning across the other squad channels?"

chapters.title: Chapter 445: Spider’s Lair [I]
paragraphs: "I’ve already informed Lady Elu—"
THUD! CLANG!
A loud metallic scuffle echoed through the transmission, followed by the heavy clatter of iron plates grinding together.

"Move your scrawny elbows, Tasmin! Let me talk to my Lord!" Brida’s booming thunderous voice crashed through the crystal, the volume practically vibrating the magical facets. "Lord! Handsome! Don’t you lose a single wink of sleep over us out here! My cleaver already pulverized twelve fake copies of your handsome face which shattered my heart into pieces, I’ll have you know and I’m currently dragging Tasmin along to sweep the crags! We already tossed the warning crystal over to Lady Eluned’s frequency! She’s handling her recruits just fine!"
Silas let out a soft laugh, shaking his head at the familiar chaos.
"Good work, Brida. Keep each other covered. We are pushing forward toward the northern crags."
"Understood, my Lord!"
CLICK.
The azure luminescence subsided, the crystal returning to its dormant translucence.
Silas handed the orb back down to Morrighan, who accepted it with a quiet nod before falling back into her position alongside the vanguard.
Silas turned his attention back to the path ahead, his gaze drifting over the thinning tree line where the jagged stone roots of the northern mountains began to pierce the loam.

"Oh, right," Silas remarked, glancing down at the Princess. "Once we wrap up this initial perimeter sweep and get the recruits thoroughly acclimated to combat maneuvers, we’ll be organizing our first major territorial mining expedition..."
The Princess blinked in surprise, craning her neck to look up at him.
"A mining expedition, Lord Silas? In the middle of an untamed wilderness?"

"Of course," Silas answered with a confident grin. "The Umbral Basin is far more than just a hunting ground for wandering mana-beasts... Beneath these jagged crags sits an extensive network of untapped mineral veins. The foundry requires a steady influx of high-grade ore if we want to reinforce our territorial walls and forge higher-tier items..."
He leaned forward slightly in the saddle, raising his voice so the fifteen recruit maidens marching behind them could hear him clearly over the rustle of leaves.
"How about the rest of you? Have any of you ever swung a pickaxe or worked a spirit-ore vein before coming to Blessed Land?"
The recruit maidens exchanged glances among themselves.
Helen, holding her ash-wood spear near the front of the rank, raised her free hand with an energetic smile.
"Not personally, Lord Silas! Most of us were garrison guards, farmhands, or city laborers before joining... but we’re definitely eager to learn! We’ll dig up whatever you need!"

"That’s what I like to hear," Silas replied warmly, his blue eyes crinkling with effortless charm. "We’ll set up the first rotation later this week. I’ll head down into the tunnels and mine alongside you..."
A collective murmur of flustered excitement rippled through the ranks, several women ducking their heads and exchanging quiet, blushing smiles at the prospect of working alongside their Lord.
Walking along the left flank, Aurelia let out a barely audible breath as she adjusted the scabbard of her mithril rapier.
’Mining...’ the former Saintess mused, a cold unpleasant memory flickering across her thoughts. ’Underground caverns have never brought me good fortune...’
Her thoughts drifted back to her past in the Meolion Kingdom.
During the earlier stages of the Holy War, one of the Demon Kings had retreated into the depths of an abandoned dwarven mithril mine, barricading himself beneath hundreds of tons of unstable bedrock.
When she and Cassian had led the assault into the dark tunnels to eliminate the threat, the demon had triggered a suicidal collapse of the main support pillars.
The entire mountain had caved in atop their heads.

She had been forced to expend three-quarters of her divine vitality simply to sustain an unbroken barrier of holy light over Cassian’s body for four grueling days in suffocating darkness while the weight of the mountain crushed down upon them.
Aurelia shook her head lightly, dismissing the memory, and refocused on the terrain ahead.
The forest path ended abruptly against the vertical face of an obsidian cliffside.
Carved directly into the base of the rock was a yawning cavern entrance, easily thirty feet wide and twenty feet tall.

Opaque curtains of pale-gray spider silk veiled the mouth of the cave as thick fibrous strands of webbing crisscrossed between the sharp rocks, glistening with a toxic sheen that seemed to swallow the ambient daylight.
Silas pulled gently on Valkyrie’s reins, bringing the massive dire wolf to a halt.
"Spiders, huh?" Silas murmured, his eyes narrowing as he evaluated the web density.
Beside the mount, both Aurelia and the Princess visibly stiffened.
The Princess’s grip on the saddle pommel tightened until her knuckles turned pale, her azure eyes wide with genuine distress.
"S-Spiders...? Multi-legged, venomous monstrosities that skitter in the dark...?"
Even Aurelia, whose combat capability stood among the highest in this group, felt a subtle instinctive prickle of aversion.
Holy mana was pure and immaculate while giant, mucus-covered arachnids with dozens of jointed legs and dripping fangs were an unpleasant contrast to her nature...
SNAP!
Before anyone could suggest adjusting their approach, Valkyrie’s front-left paw came down on a tension-loaded silk tripwire concealed beneath the loose gravel.
VUUUUUUM... FWIP!
The ground directly beneath the vanguard violently erupted.
A massive spring-loaded net of thick, adhesive silk tore upward from the dirt fissures, snapping inward like a colossal cage designed to trap Valkyrie, Silas, and the Princess in a suffocating bind.
"KYAAA!" the Princess shrieked, instinctively ducking her head against Silas’s chest.
Silas didn’t even shift his footing.
With a single effortless flick of his right wrist, a brilliant crescent of Gold Core mana sliced horizontally through the air.
SHING!
The razor-sharp mana wave sheared through the multi-ton web construct, severing it into dozens of disintegrating ribbons before a single strand could touch their armor.
Silas let out a dry sigh, rolling his wrist.
"...A rather rudimentary trap."
He straightened his posture, his voice cutting through the damp air with undeniable authority.
"Squad One! Form your battle lines! Prepare to engage!"
"Move, move, move!" Helen shouted, leading the fifteen recruits as they deployed forward, splitting into two ranks with shields locked and spears leveled directly at the cavern opening.
Inside the dark tunnel, the thick silk curtains shuddered violently.
SKRRRRR... SKLICK... SKLICK... SKLICK!
The rapid, clicking clatter of dozens of hard chitinous legs against bare rock echoed from the darkness.
The web barrier was shredded from within, and a swarming tide of arachnid beasts poured out into the open clearing.

Leading the charge were dozens of scouting spiders... each the size of an armored hound, their dark-brown carapaces dripping with caustic green fluid as their multi-faceted red eyes locked onto the squad.
Following directly behind them marched a far heavier frontline.

Emerging from the gloom were massive ten-foot-wide arachnids whose carapaces were not made of standard chitin, but interlocking plates of slate-gray stone armor that clanked loudly like walking siege engines.
Silas raised an eyebrow in analytical assessment.
’Armored carapaces on arachnid frames? I haven’t seen this particular adaptation in the outer basin.’
A golden interface notification flashed across his vision.
[Target Analyzed: Armorpider (Tier 2)]
"Squad One, advance!" Silas commanded. "Mages, soften their plating from the rear! Vanguards, drive the wedges!"
"Spells loaded! Fire on my mark!" shouted Vila, a recruit mage anchoring the rear rank.
FWOOSH! CRACKLE!
Concentrated bursts of fire-mana and jagged bolts of lightning erupted from the recruits’ staves, slamming directly into the forward ranks of the smaller scouting spiders.
BOOM! KRA-KRA!

The concussive elemental strikes shattered the scout spiders into burning piles of chitin, while scorching lines and hairline fractures spiderwebbed across the dense stone carapaces of the advancing Armorpiders.
"Spears, thrust!" Helen yelled, stepping into the pocket.
THWACK! CLANG!
Four ash-wood spears struck the fractured armor plates of the leading Armorpider.
The tips punched through the weakened stone shell with a heavy crunch, driving deep into its vital blue hemolymph.
"Step in! Don’t let it spray the silk!" Sarah shouted, lunging forward with her arming sword and severing the beast’s left cluster of eyes with a diagonal slash.
To the right flank, Lupina was a blur of silver and steel.
"GET OFF MY FIELD!" Lupina snarled, her retractable three-inch claw gauntlets blurring into a relentless sequence of horizontal and vertical cleaves.
CLANG! SCHLICK! CRUNCH!
Her reinforced steel claws struck the stone plating of an Armorpider, throwing bright sparks into the air before digging beneath the seams of its armor.
"HAAH!"
With a fierce feral pull, the silver-haired demi-human wrenched the top shell clean off the monster’s back before driving her boot straight into its exposed core with a concussive splat.
Across the center, Morrighan stepped forward. Her pale skin glowed faintly as her twin obsidian horns flared with abyssal mana.
"[Demon’s Resolve]," Morrighan incanted, her deep voice cutting across the stone.
Her physical parameters surged instantly.
She closed the distance to a charging ten-foot Armorpider in a single heavy stride, cocking her right fist enveloped in a swirling vortex of black demonic flame.
"[Brimstone Punch]!"
KRA-BOOOOOOOOOM!
Morrighan’s fist collided dead-center with the armored snout of the beast.
The shockwave was deafening.
The dense stone plating caved inward like brittle pottery as the demonic fire incinerated the monster’s internal organs before blasting the corpse thirty feet backward into the cave entrance.
Without breaking her rhythm, Morrighan pivoted on her heel, her heavy, scale-armored spade-tipped tail whipping through the air like an iron wrecking ball.
BANG-CRACK!

The tail strike shattered the legs of a second Armorpider, sending it crashing to the dirt before she raised her palm and released a point-blank [Brimstone Bolt], reducing its head to smoldering cinders.
Sitting atop Valkyrie, Silas watched the engagement with a calm eye.

’Good,’ Silas thought, tracking the unit’s spacing and momentum. ’The recruits are holding their formation, Lupina is channeling her aggression effectively, and Morrighan is locking down the choke points. All we need to do is carve through this forward line, clear the stragglers in the upper tunnels, and reach the Queen’s chamber.’
Silas had little interest in the Spider Queen herself... she was merely another obstacle to be cleared.
His focus was entirely directed toward what lay behind her: the Queen’s eggs.
’Hiro ruined my plan last time,’ Silas recalled, his focus sharpening with clear intent. ’...But this time, there will be no interruptions. The spider eggs! The eggs are the real prize...’
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
A deafening ground-shaking roar tore through the cavern depths.
The rock walls vibrated as a massive heavy silhouette burst through the dark tunnel at terrifying speed, barreling straight toward the sunlight like an enraged battering ram.
Silas blinked in genuine surprise.
Emerging from the spider-infested cavern was not an arachnid... It was a nine-foot-tall Mountain Orc.

The creature possessed thick moss-green skin covered in crude tribal markings, tusks jutting four inches from its lower jaw, and a massive tree-trunk-sized spiked wooden baton gripped firmly in its calloused fists.
Its bloodshot eyes burned with berserk frenzy as it charged blindly toward the open air, trampling over the dead spiders beneath its heavy boots.

’Where did an Orc come from inside an arachnid nest?!’ Silas thought, his mind rapidly assessing the battlefield. ’Is there an active tribal camp deeper in the crags? Was it trapped within the web tunnels and fighting its way out?!’
Before Silas could fully process the arrival, the Princess lost all composure.
She grabbed Silas’s tunic with both hands, shaking him frantically as she buried her face against his chest in panic.
"LORD SILAS! AN ORC! A PRIMITIVE BEAST!" the Princess cried out, her voice cracking. "WE ARE GOING TO DIE! I DO NOT WISH TO BE GROUND INTO MINCE BY A CLUB!"
Silas looked down at her with a flat unimpressed expression.
"Die?" Silas repeated calmly. "Princess, look at the field."
SHING!
Before the charging Orc could close the distance toward Valkyrie, a blinding flash of white light illuminated the clearing.
Aurelia moved.

Her golden-amber eyes flared with tranquil focus. In a matter of seconds, the former Saintess vanished from her position, her movement tearing through the air in a silent frictionless streak of pure platinum mana.
She materialized instantly at the Orc’s blind spot, right behind its massive charging legs.
SCHLICK-SCHLICK!
Aurelia’s slender mithril rapier flickered twice like lightning as the blade effortlessly severed the thick Achilles tendons of both the Orc’s legs.
"GRAAAAAAAGH!"
The nine-foot brute let out a deafening roar of agony as its momentum collapsed instantly.
Its legs buckled, and its massive frame pitched forward, tumbling helplessly through the air in mid-fall.
VUUUUUUUUUM!
As the Orc fell, brilliant incandescent Argent Flames ignited along the severed tendon wounds, surging up its legs and across its torso like living ribbons of holy fire.
The creature screamed as the sacred flames seared through its corrupted flesh.
Aurelia however did not wait for the brute to strike the ground.
Suspended gracefully in mid-air alongside the falling giant, Aurelia drew her rapier back in a fluid circular arc.
Her golden eyes narrowed.
SLASH!
A single immaculate vertical cleave of pure holy light sliced cleanly through the center of the Orc’s massive frame.
SPLAT-CRUNCH!
The colossal green brute was cleaved perfectly in two from crown to groin while still suspended in mid-air.
A shower of cauterized organs, black blood, and pulverized bone rained down across the gravel as the two halves of the carcass slammed into the dirt with a heavy thud.
"Haah..."
Aurelia landed softly on the tips of her boots, her white-enameled cuirass completely spotless, without a single drop of gore touching her silver trim.
She raised the slender rapier to her eyes, admiring the immaculate balance of the dwarven steel.
"A truly fine weapon," Aurelia murmured softly, flicking an invisible speck of dust from the tip before sheathing the blade with a crisp sound.
She turned smoothly on her heel, stepping gracefully back toward the dire wolf mount.
Aurelia looked up at Silas with calm devoted golden-amber eyes, placing a hand over her chest as she offered a soft respectful bow.
"My Lord Silas... are you unharmed?"
Silas sat in the saddle, looking from the split Orc carcass back to the Saintess with a wide impressed grin.
"Never better, Aurelia," Silas smiled. "Never better."

sentences.text: "I’ve already informed Lady Elu—"

CLANG!
A loud metallic scuffle echoed through the transmission, followed by the heavy clatter of iron plates grinding together.
"Move your scrawny elbows, Tasmin!

"Lord!
Handsome!
Don’t you lose a single wink of sleep over us out here!
My cleaver already pulverized twelve fake copies of your handsome face which shattered my heart into pieces, I’ll have you know and I’m currently dragging Tasmin along to sweep the crags!
We already tossed the warning crystal over to Lady Eluned’s frequency!
She’s handling her recruits just fine!"
Silas let out a soft laugh, shaking his head at the familiar chaos.
"Good work, Brida.
Keep each other covered.
We are pushing forward toward the northern crags."
"Understood, my Lord!"
CLICK.
The azure luminescence subsided, the crystal returning to its dormant translucence.
Silas handed the orb back down to Morrighan, who accepted it with a quiet nod before falling back into her position alongside the vanguard.

"Oh, right," Silas remarked, glancing down at the Princess.
"Once we wrap up this initial perimeter sweep and get the recruits thoroughly acclimated to combat maneuvers, we’ll be organizing our first major territorial mining expedition..."
The Princess blinked in surprise, craning her neck to look up at him.
"A mining expedition, Lord Silas?
In the middle of an untamed wilderness?"
"Of course," Silas answered with a confident grin.
"The Umbral Basin is far more than just a hunting ground for wandering mana-beasts...
Beneath these jagged crags sits an extensive network of untapped mineral veins.
The foundry requires a steady influx of high-grade ore if we want to reinforce our territorial walls and forge higher-tier items..."
He leaned forward slightly in the saddle, raising his voice so the fifteen recruit maidens marching behind them could hear him clearly over the rustle of leaves.
"How about the rest of you?
Have any of you ever swung a pickaxe or worked a spirit-ore vein before coming to Blessed Land?"
The recruit maidens exchanged glances among themselves.
Helen, holding her ash-wood spear near the front of the rank, raised her free hand with an energetic smile.
"Not personally, Lord Silas!
Most of us were garrison guards, farmhands, or city laborers before joining... but we’re definitely eager to learn!
We’ll dig up whatever you need!"
"That’s what I like to hear," Silas replied warmly, his blue eyes crinkling with effortless charm.
"We’ll set up the first rotation later this week.
I’ll head down into the tunnels and mine alongside you..."
A collective murmur of flustered excitement rippled through the ranks, several women ducking their heads and exchanging quiet, blushing smiles at the prospect of working alongside their Lord.
Walking along the left flank, Aurelia let out a barely audible breath as she adjusted the scabbard of her mithril rapier.
’Mining...’ the former Saintess mused, a cold unpleasant memory flickering across her thoughts. ’Underground caverns have never brought me good fortune...’
Her thoughts drifted back to her past in the Meolion Kingdom.
During the earlier stages of the Holy War, one of the Demon Kings had retreated into the depths of an abandoned dwarven mithril mine, barricading himself beneath hundreds of tons of unstable bedrock.
When she and Cassian had led the assault into the dark tunnels to eliminate the threat, the demon had triggered a suicidal collapse of the main support pillars.
The entire mountain had caved in atop their heads.

She had been forced to expend three-quarters of her divine vitality simply to sustain an unbroken barrier of holy light over Cassian’s body for four grueling days in suffocating darkness while the weight of the mountain crushed down upon them.
Aurelia shook her head lightly, dismissing the memory, and refocused on the terrain ahead.
The forest path ended abruptly against the vertical face of an obsidian cliffside.
Carved directly into the base of the rock was a yawning cavern entrance, easily thirty feet wide and twenty feet tall.

Opaque curtains of pale-gray spider silk veiled the mouth of the cave as thick fibrous strands of webbing crisscrossed between the sharp rocks, glistening with a toxic sheen that seemed to swallow the ambient daylight.
Silas pulled gently on Valkyrie’s reins, bringing the massive dire wolf to a halt.
"Spiders, huh?" Silas murmured, his eyes narrowing as he evaluated the web density.
Beside the mount, both Aurelia and the Princess visibly stiffened.
The Princess’s grip on the saddle pommel tightened until her knuckles turned pale, her azure eyes wide with genuine distress.
"S-Spiders...?
Multi-legged, venomous monstrosities that skitter in the dark...?"
Even Aurelia, whose combat capability stood among the highest in this group, felt a subtle instinctive prickle of aversion.
Holy mana was pure and immaculate while giant, mucus-covered arachnids with dozens of jointed legs and dripping fangs were an unpleasant contrast to her nature...
SNAP!
Before anyone could suggest adjusting their approach, Valkyrie’s front-left paw came down on a tension-loaded silk tripwire concealed beneath the loose gravel.
VUUUUUUM...
FWIP!
The ground directly beneath the vanguard violently erupted.
A massive spring-loaded net of thick, adhesive silk tore upward from the dirt fissures, snapping inward like a colossal cage designed to trap Valkyrie, Silas, and the Princess in a suffocating bind.
"KYAAA!" the Princess shrieked, instinctively ducking her head against Silas’s chest.
Silas didn’t even shift his footing.
With a single effortless flick of his right wrist, a brilliant crescent of Gold Core mana sliced horizontally through the air.
SHING!
The razor-sharp mana wave sheared through the multi-ton web construct, severing it into dozens of disintegrating ribbons before a single strand could touch their armor.
Silas let out a dry sigh, rolling his wrist.
"...A rather rudimentary trap."
He straightened his posture, his voice cutting through the damp air with undeniable authority.
"Squad One!
Form your battle lines!
Prepare to engage!"
"Move, move, move!" Helen shouted, leading the fifteen recruits as they deployed forward, splitting into two ranks with shields locked and spears leveled directly at the cavern opening.
Inside the dark tunnel, the thick silk curtains shuddered violently.
SKRRRRR...
SKLICK...
SKLICK...
SKLICK!
The rapid, clicking clatter of dozens of hard chitinous legs against bare rock echoed from the darkness.
The web barrier was shredded from within, and a swarming tide of arachnid beasts poured out into the open clearing.

Leading the charge were dozens of scouting spiders... each the size of an armored hound, their dark-brown carapaces dripping with caustic green fluid as their multi-faceted red eyes locked onto the squad.
Following directly behind them marched a far heavier frontline.

Emerging from the gloom were massive ten-foot-wide arachnids whose carapaces were not made of standard chitin, but interlocking plates of slate-gray stone armor that clanked loudly like walking siege engines.
Silas raised an eyebrow in analytical assessment.
’Armored carapaces on arachnid frames?
I haven’t seen this particular adaptation in the outer basin.’
A golden interface notification flashed across his vision.
[Target Analyzed: Armorpider (Tier 2)]
