chapters.title: Chapter 446: Spider’s Lair [II]
paragraphs: The last dying shudders of the cleaved Orc carcass finally stilled against the gravel clearing, its scorched halves hissing softly as the cauterized blood pooled into the dirt.
A few yards away, the remaining scouting spiders and Armorpiders lay completely butchered across the perimeter.
Their stone-like shells were smashed into jagged gravel, their multi-faceted eyes crushed, and their segmented legs scattered across the moss like discarded kindling.
Silas remained mounted atop Valkyrie, his hands resting easily on the leather reins as he watched the fifteen recruits finish clearing the field.

The squad worked with sharp natural coordination... two girls held their spears braced against the cavern mouth to maintain perimeter watch, while others moved from corpse to corpse, driving their arming swords into the skulls of twitching beasts and harvesting the glowing Tier-2 beast cores.
Silas’s gaze drifted toward Aurelia, who was calmly stepping past the fallen Orc.
’She really is something else,’ Silas thought, admiring the effortless grace with which she had severed the nine-foot brute’s tendons and split it from crown to groin in a fraction of a second.
His mind wandered back to the scene in Thora’s foundry earlier that morning.

When Thora had brought out that ancient, leather-bound chronicle documenting the Meolion Kingdom, Aurelia had looked at those yellowed parchment pages with an expression so heavy and so weighed down by unspoken grief, that she had kissed the very leather binding out of fragile gratitude.

’I really want to know what kind of life she lived before I summoned her to Blessed Land,’ Silas mused silently, his fingers idly tapping against Valkyrie’s saddle pommel. ’The book mentioned she was a Saintess who suffered unspeakable torture for six straight years... Should I ask her about it directly? Or would bringing up that past just tear open old wounds?’
He decided it was better to wait.

Once this morning expedition concluded and they were back within the tranquil walls of the Keep, he would find a quiet moment to sit down with her over tea and ask her about her history on her own terms.
Silas glanced down toward Helen, who was securing a beast heart into her leather pouch.
Around Helen’s wrist was a small brass-rimmed mechanical timer and the brass hands were ticking steadily, rapidly approaching the noon mark.

’It’s almost time for all the squads to rendezvous at the central clearing for the scheduled break,’ Silas noted, his mind calculating the operational window. ’We don’t have much time to waste... If we’re going to clear out this cavern and harvest whatever lies in the lower depths, we need to pick up the pace.’

"Lord Silas!" Sarah called out from the front line, wiping her arming sword clean on a patch of ferns before sheathing it with a crisp click. "Perimeter sweep is complete! All forward sentries and beasts are neutralized!"
"Good work, Sarah," Silas responded with a confident nod.
He urged Valkyrie forward with a gentle squeeze of his calves.
The Blessed wolf stepped smoothly through the clearing, the massive beast’s paws crushing broken chitin fragments into powder.
As Silas rode past the ranks, he observed his unit with sharp pride.
Several of the recruit maidens had sustained nasty lacerations, bruised ribs, and minor venom burns along their forearms from the Armorpiders’ acidic spray.

Aurelia was already moving among them, her slender hands glowing with gentle radiant white light as she touched their shoulders and foreheads, closing the shallow wounds and purifying the residual toxins in soothing waves of holy mana.
Silas watched the girls wince slightly as their skin knitted together, their breath coming in exhausted gasps from the physical exertion of the raid.
’They’ve fought hard, but their stamina is dipping,’ Silas thought. He wasn’t too surprised...
Most of the girls that had joined Blessed Land were part of the average women of the Unmovable Wall that felt like their strength were lacking.
’Fortunately that can’t be fixed...’
This was part of why he was doing all of this in the first place, these women needed confidence in themselves.
Silas raised his right hand.
Engraved across the back of his knuckles, the glowing emerald Genesis Rune that Eluned had intimately placed upon him this morning flared with brilliance.
VUUUUUUUUUM!
A boundless gentle wave of emerald life-force erupted from Silas’s hand, expanding across the entire clearing in a blinding, warm ripple of divine mana.
The moment the green light washed over the fifteen maidens, a collective gasp of pure ecstatic relief tore from their lips.
SZZZZT... SNAP!
The remaining scratches, micro-tears in their muscle fibers, and bruised bones completely vanished at light-speed.

Even more remarkably, their lungs filled with an invigorating surge of pure vitality that washed away every ounce of lactic acid and mental fatigue, filling their spiritual meridians with an overwhelming sensation of boundless energy and drive.
"Whoa...!" Helen gasped, flexing her fingers and rolling her shoulders in pure astonishment. "The heaviness in my arms... it’s completely gone!"
"It feels like I just slept for twelve straight hours after a hot bath!" another recruit exclaimed, her cheeks flushing with bright happy color.
Aurelia paused mid-cast, her golden-amber eyes snapping wide as she looked up at Silas with genuine breathless amazement.

’He can heal too...?’ Aurelia thought, her heart skipping a beat as she felt the overwhelming life-force lingering in the air. ’Not only does he possess combat strength and a huge reserve of mana mana... but his authority extends to primordial restoration as well? How many divine blessings does this man hold within his soul?’
Silas brought Valkyrie to a halt just five paces away from the yawning, web-veiled cavern entrance.
Sitting between his arms, the blue-haired Princess blinked, looking around at the dark cavern opening before looking up at Silas with a puzzled expression.
"Lord Silas? Why have we stopped here? If we are to purge this subterranean nest, shouldn’t we ride in and trample them from the saddle?"
Silas’s eyes darkened with a dry deadpan smirk as he looked down at the wolf beneath them.

"As much as I’d love to do that, Princess..." Silas chuckled softly, shaking his head. "Valkyrie can’t fit into those narrow cavern tunnels with both of us sitting on her back. Look at the ceiling clearance... it drops to barely a few feet inside the first choke point."
He leaned forward, reaching down to pat the thick, silver fur along the dire wolf’s neck, letting out an affectionate tease.
"Besides... you’ve been eating far too many roasted meat ribs from the territory kitchens lately, girl. You’re definitely getting a little fatter around the middle."
Valkyrie let out a loud indignant snort, her ears pinning backward against her head.
The Princess blinked her azure eyes in stunned wonder.
’Wait... was that an actual visible pout on the wolf’s face?! Can mana-beasts truly express feminine offense?!’
Silas laughed warmly, steering Valkyrie over to a flat, shaded patch of moss beside the cavern entrance.
"Alright, girl. Settle down and guard the perimeter while we clear the interior."
He swung his leg over the saddle, dismounting effortlessly before reaching up with both hands to catch the Princess by her waist, lifting her gently down onto the gravel.
Once on her feet, Valkyrie lowered her massive eight-foot frame onto the moss, curling her paws beneath her chest with a grumble.
Silas reached into his inventory, pulling out a succulent golden-brown roasted chicken wing... still steaming hot and dripping with sweet sauce.
"Here," Silas smiled, holding the massive meat piece right before her snout. "Why don’t you have some of this while you wait?"
Valkyrie’s golden eyes instantly lit up like two suns.
The pout vanished completely as she gently, greedily took the roasted meat from his hand, crunching through the tender meat and bone with joyful tail-thumping crunches.
Silas patted her massive head, rubbing the soft fur behind her ears before turning back toward the squad.
Standing a few paces back, the Princess watched the interaction with quiet admiration softening her expression.

’In my brother’s territory,’ the Princess thought, her fingers tracing the leather hilt of the void-iron dagger at her thigh, ’war beasts are treated as disposable weapons of state, whipped and starved to cultivate artificial ferocity... Yet Lord Silas treats every single being under his banner... from Heroes to mortal recruits, and even his personal mounts with genuine warmth and dignity. It is impossible not to feel safe beside him.’
She tightened her small fist, looking toward the dark cavern maw with a sudden burning resolve.

’I am a princess of the realm. I cannot spend this entire morning tumbling onto my rear like a helpless ornament! I swear... before we leave this cavern, I will claim my very first monster kill with my own hands!’
Aurelia stepped gracefully up to Silas’s side, her hand resting calmly on the pommel of her mithril rapier.

"Lord Silas," Aurelia spoke softly, her golden-amber eyes fixed on the dense silk curtains swaying within the dark tunnel. "Should the vanguard prepare standard defensive formations before we cross the threshold?"
Silas looked toward the dark opening, his sharp senses extending outward.

"There are bound to be countless traps inside," Silas noted, his tone turning serious and analytical. "Given that they set up a tension-loaded web net right at the entrance, the interior tunnels will be filled with tripwires, false floors, and ceiling ambush pockets... Let me check the mana signatures."
Silas closed his eyes for a brief moment, channeling his perception through the damp air.
His consciousness rippled into the subterranean fissures, picking up dozens of faint scuttling mana signatures clinging along the high granite walls and hidden crevasses.
"There are still quite a few arachnid signatures lurking along the upper cavern walls," Silas murmured. "If we advance blindly on foot, they’ll drop down on the recruits’ rear line."
Aurelia stepped forward, placing herself between Silas and the dark cavern entrance.
"Please do not worry yourself with such vermin, my Lord," Aurelia said calmly, her voice carrying a serene confidence that made Silas blink in mild surprise.
Aurelia stepped to the absolute threshold of the cave, looking deep into the yawning blackness.
Deep within her soul, a quiet resolute thought took root.
’The primary value I can offer to this world... is Immortality,’ Aurelia reflected, the weight of her past washing over her like a distant tide.
While she was in the prison of that world, she had staked everything on that singular promise.
If she had simply been able to grant absolute immortality to the people of her savior, perhaps none of the horrors that happened before would have unfolded.
All that pain... All that death...
’...And yet,’ Aurelia thought, her heart swelling with an emotion so pure and bright it made her chest ache. ’I do not harbor a single shred of regret for that suffering. Because it brought me here.’

She had spent barely a single day within the Blessed Land, yet this brief handful of hours was infinitely more precious, warm, and fulfilling than all the hollow centuries she had endured in her former life.
From the moment she was born, sold as an orphan slave to the High Church, she had known only suffering.
When she was crowned Saintess, the burden of suffering had merely grown heavier beneath golden silk.
And when she had awakened the sacred Argent Flame, her agony had reached its suffocating zenith as she became a living battery for other people’s ambitions.

’In the Meolion Kingdom, every knight, every noble, and every hero sought only to ride upon the coattails of another’s glory,’ Aurelia observed, glancing back at the fifteen recruits who were eagerly tightening their armor straps and checking their spears. ’They were parasites who demanded salvation without paying the price in blood. But here... in Blessed Land... everything is different.’
Every woman in this territory wanted to stand on her own two feet.

They trained until their muscles bled, they threw themselves into battle with fearless laughter, and they fought with everything they possessed not to leech off their Lord, but to become strong enough to stand proudly beside him.
They wanted to create their own glory, to forge their own legends, and to earn Silas’s approving smile through their own sweat and steel.

’I, too, wish to do the same,’ Aurelia resolved, her jaw setting with fierce devoted determination. ’I do not wish to merely be a fragile Saintess protected from the shadows. I want to be a blade worthy of my Lord’s command...’
VUUUUUUUUUUUM.
A brilliant flash of pure celestial white flame ignited within the depths of Aurelia’s golden-amber eyes.

’Argent Flame...’ Aurelia called out into the deepest sanctum of her spiritual core. ’If you hold even the slightest affection for me after all these centuries of shared agony... then hear my plea. Lend me your immaculate fury. Help me impress my Master!’
During her years alongside the older former Saintess who had wanted to be saved, Aurelia had cultivated her holy mana affinity to absurd heights.
Though she had relied primarily on healing and restorative arts, the true destructive nature of the Argent Flame had remained dormant, sealed beneath her gentle nature.
Now, she released the floodgates.
Aurelia thrust her right palm straight into the dark cavern maw.
"[Argent Inferno]!"
FWOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOSH!

sentences.text: The last dying shudders of the cleaved Orc carcass finally stilled against the gravel clearing, its scorched halves hissing softly as the cauterized blood pooled into the dirt.
A few yards away, the remaining scouting spiders and Armorpiders lay completely butchered across the perimeter.
Their stone-like shells were smashed into jagged gravel, their multi-faceted eyes crushed, and their segmented legs scattered across the moss like discarded kindling.
Silas remained mounted atop Valkyrie, his hands resting easily on the leather reins as he watched the fifteen recruits finish clearing the field.

The squad worked with sharp natural coordination... two girls held their spears braced against the cavern mouth to maintain perimeter watch, while others moved from corpse to corpse, driving their arming swords into the skulls of twitching beasts and harvesting the glowing Tier-2 beast cores.
Silas’s gaze drifted toward Aurelia, who was calmly stepping past the fallen Orc.
’She really is something else,’ Silas thought, admiring the effortless grace with which she had severed the nine-foot brute’s tendons and split it from crown to groin in a fraction of a second.
His mind wandered back to the scene in Thora’s foundry earlier that morning.

When Thora had brought out that ancient, leather-bound chronicle documenting the Meolion Kingdom, Aurelia had looked at those yellowed parchment pages with an expression so heavy and so weighed down by unspoken grief, that she had kissed the very leather binding out of fragile gratitude.

’I really want to know what kind of life she lived before I summoned her to Blessed Land,’ Silas mused silently, his fingers idly tapping against Valkyrie’s saddle pommel. ’The book mentioned she was a Saintess who suffered unspeakable torture for six straight years...
Should I ask her about it directly?
Or would bringing up that past just tear open old wounds?’
He decided it was better to wait.

Once this morning expedition concluded and they were back within the tranquil walls of the Keep, he would find a quiet moment to sit down with her over tea and ask her about her history on her own terms.
Silas glanced down toward Helen, who was securing a beast heart into her leather pouch.
Around Helen’s wrist was a small brass-rimmed mechanical timer and the brass hands were ticking steadily, rapidly approaching the noon mark.
’It’s almost time for all the squads to rendezvous at the central clearing for the scheduled break,’ Silas noted, his mind calculating the operational window. ’We don’t have much time to waste...
If we’re going to clear out this cavern and harvest whatever lies in the lower depths, we need to pick up the pace.’
"Lord Silas!" Sarah called out from the front line, wiping her arming sword clean on a patch of ferns before sheathing it with a crisp click.
"Perimeter sweep is complete!
All forward sentries and beasts are neutralized!"
"Good work, Sarah," Silas responded with a confident nod.
He urged Valkyrie forward with a gentle squeeze of his calves.
The Blessed wolf stepped smoothly through the clearing, the massive beast’s paws crushing broken chitin fragments into powder.
As Silas rode past the ranks, he observed his unit with sharp pride.
Several of the recruit maidens had sustained nasty lacerations, bruised ribs, and minor venom burns along their forearms from the Armorpiders’ acidic spray.

Aurelia was already moving among them, her slender hands glowing with gentle radiant white light as she touched their shoulders and foreheads, closing the shallow wounds and purifying the residual toxins in soothing waves of holy mana.
Silas watched the girls wince slightly as their skin knitted together, their breath coming in exhausted gasps from the physical exertion of the raid.
’They’ve fought hard, but their stamina is dipping,’ Silas thought.
He wasn’t too surprised...
Most of the girls that had joined Blessed Land were part of the average women of the Unmovable Wall that felt like their strength were lacking.
’Fortunately that can’t be fixed...’
This was part of why he was doing all of this in the first place, these women needed confidence in themselves.
Silas raised his right hand.
Engraved across the back of his knuckles, the glowing emerald Genesis Rune that Eluned had intimately placed upon him this morning flared with brilliance.
VUUUUUUUUUM!
A boundless gentle wave of emerald life-force erupted from Silas’s hand, expanding across the entire clearing in a blinding, warm ripple of divine mana.
The moment the green light washed over the fifteen maidens, a collective gasp of pure ecstatic relief tore from their lips.
SZZZZT...
SNAP!
The remaining scratches, micro-tears in their muscle fibers, and bruised bones completely vanished at light-speed.

Even more remarkably, their lungs filled with an invigorating surge of pure vitality that washed away every ounce of lactic acid and mental fatigue, filling their spiritual meridians with an overwhelming sensation of boundless energy and drive.
"Whoa...!" Helen gasped, flexing her fingers and rolling her shoulders in pure astonishment.
"The heaviness in my arms... it’s completely gone!"
"It feels like I just slept for twelve straight hours after a hot bath!" another recruit exclaimed, her cheeks flushing with bright happy color.
Aurelia paused mid-cast, her golden-amber eyes snapping wide as she looked up at Silas with genuine breathless amazement.

’He can heal too...?’ Aurelia thought, her heart skipping a beat as she felt the overwhelming life-force lingering in the air. ’Not only does he possess combat strength and a huge reserve of mana mana... but his authority extends to primordial restoration as well?
How many divine blessings does this man hold within his soul?’
Silas brought Valkyrie to a halt just five paces away from the yawning, web-veiled cavern entrance.
Sitting between his arms, the blue-haired Princess blinked, looking around at the dark cavern opening before looking up at Silas with a puzzled expression.
"Lord Silas?
Why have we stopped here?
If we are to purge this subterranean nest, shouldn’t we ride in and trample them from the saddle?"
Silas’s eyes darkened with a dry deadpan smirk as he looked down at the wolf beneath them.
"As much as I’d love to do that, Princess..." Silas chuckled softly, shaking his head.
"Valkyrie can’t fit into those narrow cavern tunnels with both of us sitting on her back.
Look at the ceiling clearance... it drops to barely a few feet inside the first choke point."
He leaned forward, reaching down to pat the thick, silver fur along the dire wolf’s neck, letting out an affectionate tease.
"Besides... you’ve been eating far too many roasted meat ribs from the territory kitchens lately, girl.
You’re definitely getting a little fatter around the middle."
Valkyrie let out a loud indignant snort, her ears pinning backward against her head.
The Princess blinked her azure eyes in stunned wonder.
’Wait... was that an actual visible pout on the wolf’s face?!
Can mana-beasts truly express feminine offense?!’
Silas laughed warmly, steering Valkyrie over to a flat, shaded patch of moss beside the cavern entrance.
"Alright, girl.
Settle down and guard the perimeter while we clear the interior."
He swung his leg over the saddle, dismounting effortlessly before reaching up with both hands to catch the Princess by her waist, lifting her gently down onto the gravel.
Once on her feet, Valkyrie lowered her massive eight-foot frame onto the moss, curling her paws beneath her chest with a grumble.
Silas reached into his inventory, pulling out a succulent golden-brown roasted chicken wing... still steaming hot and dripping with sweet sauce.
"Here," Silas smiled, holding the massive meat piece right before her snout.
"Why don’t you have some of this while you wait?"
Valkyrie’s golden eyes instantly lit up like two suns.
The pout vanished completely as she gently, greedily took the roasted meat from his hand, crunching through the tender meat and bone with joyful tail-thumping crunches.

Yet Lord Silas treats every single being under his banner... from Heroes to mortal recruits, and even his personal mounts with genuine warmth and dignity.

chapters.title: Chapter 447: Spider’s Lair [III]
paragraphs: An apocalyptic torrent of pure blinding white holy fire erupted from Aurelia’s hand, roaring into the tunnels like a sentient living dragon of incandescent light!
The white flames did not spread like ordinary fire.

They possessed a unique intelligence of their own, violently splitting into dozens of surging serpentine branches that swept through every side tunnel, crawled up the twenty-foot cavern walls, and poured into every single hidden ceiling fissure with terrifying speed.
SKREEEEEEEEEEEEE! HISS! SQUELCH! CRACKLE!
Deafening agonizing shrieks of burning arachnids echoed through the subterranean rock.
WHOOSH!

The superheated holy fire incinerated sticky web traps into vapor in a fraction of a millisecond, melting stone-plated Armorpiders and scouting spiders alike into smoldering ash before the beasts could even unhinge their fangs.
The white flames carved an unbroken path of utter purification through the labyrinthine tunnels, illuminating the dark stone in a blinding daytime glow.
Silas stood at the cavern entrance, his perception tracking the sweeping purge.
One by one, the dozens of scuttling arachnid mana signatures clinging to the tunnel walls violently blinked out of existence.
Within ten seconds, the entire upper and middle sectors of the cavern were rendered completely devoid of life.
Except for one massive pressurized mana signature resting at the bottom of the lowest subterranean cavern.
The Spider Queen...
The white flames gently subsided, retreating back into Aurelia’s palm and dissolving into harmless, glowing embers that danced upon the cool breeze.
Aurelia lowered her hand, turning back toward Silas with a slight breathless flush dusting her porcelain cheekbones.
"The path is cleared, my Lord," Aurelia reported softly, her head bowed in quiet reverence.
Silas stared at her, his blue eyes wide with unreserved admiration.
He let out a low, appreciative whistle, stepping forward and clapping a hand gently on her shoulder armor.

"That was incredible, Aurelia," Silas praised warmly, a wide, radiant smile lighting up his face. "A single spell wiped out the entire upper labyrinth without leaving a single trap intact... You’re a powerhouse on your own huh?"
Aurelia’s breath caught in her throat.
The praise hit her straight in the chest, and a deep brilliant crimson blush rushed across her cheeks.
She quickly looked down at her boots as a small thoroughly flustered smile touching her lips. "I... I merely did what was necessary to serve you, Lord Silas."
"Alright, Squad One!" Silas announced, drawing his golden-runed sword with a smooth metallic ring. "Formation alpha! We’re heading down to finish the job!"
"Move out!" Helen commanded, leading the fifteen recruits as they stepped into the cavern.
Silas walked at the front of the column, his golden sword glowing with a soft steady radiance that illuminated the dark stone.
Valkyrie padded silently at his right flank, her golden eyes sharp and alert, while the Princess walked closely on his left, her hands hovering nervously over her void-iron dagger.
As the squad advanced through the wide tunnels, the recruit maidens looked around in open-mouthed awe.
The cavern walls were scorched clean, free of the suffocating, sticky webbing that had covered them moments prior.
The leather soles of their Blessed Land scout boots effortlessly absorbed the residual heat radiating from the polished granite floorboards, keeping their footing completely cool and steady.
Piles of calcified smoldering gray ash were all that remained of the dozens of Armorpiders that had attempted to set up ceiling ambushes.
As they rounded a wide descending bend in the stone corridor, a wet rustling sound reached Silas’s ears.
SKLICK... SKLICK!
Lying near the base of a jagged stalagmite was a single, lone Armorpider.
The beast was heavily scorched, its stone-like carapace cracked and smoking, with four of its eight legs incinerated by the holy flames.
It dragged its broken, twitching body weakly across the gravel, hissing weakly with its remaining fangs as it tried to crawl toward a dark crevice.
Silas paused, glancing down at the Princess.
He noticed the way the blue-haired royal woman’s azure eyes were locked onto the struggling beast.
Her fingers were trembling slightly against her weapon hilt, but beneath the fear, that same fierce hungry spark of combat ambition was burning bright in her gaze.
Silas leaned down slightly, whispering with a gentle encouraging smirk.
"Hey, Princess. Look right there."
The Princess blinked, looking up at him. "L-Lord Silas?"

"You’ve been wanting your first official kill all morning, haven’t you?" Silas gestured toward the crippled spider with the tip of his blade. "That one’s barely clinging to life. Its armor is completely shattered, and it can’t jump. Go on... Finish it..."
The Princess’s heart hammered against her ribs like a war drum.
She looked at the twitching monster, then looked back at Silas’s calm supportive smile.
"I... I can do this," she whispered to herself, setting her jaw with fierce determination.
She reached down, firmly gripping the leather hilt of her six-inch void-iron utility dagger, and drew the blade from her thigh sheath with a crisp shik.
Setting her boots firmly against the gravel, the Princess stepped forward.
"Yield before the judgment of Blessed Land, foul arachnid!" she proclaimed, her voice wavering slightly with adrenaline before steadying.
The crippled Armorpider turned its remaining two multi-faceted red eyes toward her, opening its venomous mandibles to release a weak, sputtering hiss.
"Chaaa!"
The Princess flinched slightly as a droplet of green bile splashed onto the stone near her boot, but she did not fall backward this time.
She lowered her center of gravity, planting her left foot firmly on the gravel just as Silas had instructed earlier.
’I WANT...’

She lunged forward with both hands on the dagger hilt, driving the void-iron point straight into the deep, glowing fracture that Aurelia’s holy fire had blasted across the center of the beast’s carapace.
’MY FIRST KILL DAMMIT!’
CRUNCH!
The blade pierced through the cracked stone plate, sinking deep into the monster’s vital core!
The Armorpider shrieked, thrashing its remaining legs violently against the ground with the impact jarring the Princess’s wrists.
"DIE!" the Princess grunted, gritting her teeth and putting her entire body weight into the hilt, twisting the blade forty-five degrees to shred the internal hemolymph vessels.
SPLAT-SQUELCH!
With a final shuddering gasp, the Armorpider’s remaining legs went completely limp, collapsing flat against the gravel as its red eyes dimmed into lifeless black.
PANT... PANT... PANT!
The Princess stood over the slain beast, her hands still clutching the embedded dagger as her chest heaved in rapid shallow breaths.
She slowly pulled the blade free, wiping a speck of black monster fluid from the metal before looking down at her hands in pure, disbelieving shock.
"I... I did it..." the Princess breathed, a wide ecstatic smile breaking across her face. "I killed it! Lord Silas! I secured my first official monster kill!"
"Outstanding work, Princess," Silas laughed warmly, giving her an approving thumbs-up. "Clean strike, great balance, and you didn’t tumble onto your rear. You’re officially a warrior now."
The Princess beamed, standing tall with her chest puffed out in immense royal pride as she sheathed her dagger with a triumphant flourish.
"Let’s keep moving," Silas commanded, leading the squad further down the descending corridor.
A few minutes later, the tunnel opened up into a massive cavernous drop-off.
Directly in the center of the rock floor was a wide circular chasm stretching nearly forty feet across, descending twenty feet into a brightly illuminated lower subterranean chamber.
The walls of the chasm were smooth, completely stripped of webs... and right at the lip of the drop-off, the scorched marks of Aurelia’s Argent Flames came to a clean sudden halt.
Silas stopped at the edge of the pit, looking down, then turned his gaze toward Aurelia.
Aurelia noticed his gaze and immediately stiffened, her golden-amber eyes flickering with sudden nervous apprehension.

’Did I overstep...?’ Aurelia worried internally, her fingers tightening slightly against her scabbard. ’Did I halt the flames too early? Is he displeased that I did not scorch the entire cavern down to bedrock...?’
On the contrary, Silas’s face broke into a wide delighted grin.

’She stopped the inferno right at the threshold of the lower nesting chamber,’ Silas thought with glowing satisfaction. ’Which means the concentrated heat didn’t reach the nursery! The eggs are completely intact!’
"Brilliant restraint, Aurelia," Silas praised, turning to the squad. "Everyone down into the lower chamber! Mind your landing!"
Without waiting for a rope or ladder, Silas took a single step forward and leaped straight down into the twenty-foot pit!
"Lord Silas?!" Helen and several recruits gasped in shock, rushing to the edge.
THUD!
Silas landed effortlessly on his boots, his Gold Core mana cushioning the impact into a harmless puff of dust.
Aurelia didn’t hesitate.
With a graceful, athletic vault, she leaped onto the back of Valkyrie’s saddle, reaching down and easily scooping the Princess up by her waist to sit before her.
"Hold tightly, Princess," Aurelia instructed calmly.
Valkyrie let out a fierce eager bark, leaping over the edge of the chasm with power.
The Blessed wolf descended through the air like a silver comet, landing firmly on all four paws beside Silas with a low rumbling thud that barely shook the saddle.
Moments later, the fifteen recruit maidens used their spear shafts and ledge grips to drop down into the chamber in crisp rapid succession, immediately fanning out into a wide defensive semi-circle.
The sight that greeted them in the lower cavern took their breath away.
The subterranean chamber was vast and vaulted, stretching nearly a hundred yards in every direction.
The walls were formed from glowing, translucent amethyst crystals that cast a soft ethereal purple light across the cavern floor.

Resting right in the center of the chamber was a colossal and intricately woven nest constructed from thousands of shimmering silver alchemical silk threads that pulsed with rich concentrated cosmic mana.
And inside that nest rested six massive, two-foot-wide, crystalline royal spider eggs that glowed with a mesmerizing, iridescent rainbow luminescence.
SKREEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEE!
A deafening ground-shaking screech tore through the chamber, shattering several protruding crystal clusters from the ceiling!
Standing directly in front of the silk nest, shielding her royal clutch with her colossal frame, was the mother.
[Target Analyzed: Broodmother Spider Queen (Tier 3 - Boss)]
The Spider Queen was a towering, nightmarish leviathan of war.
Her colossal obsidian-plated carapace stood over eighteen feet tall and forty feet wide, covered in thick, razor-sharp bone spikes that jutted from every joint.
Her eight massive, trunk-like legs ended in jagged scythe-like claws of solid abyssal iron that gouged deep furrows into the granite floor with every twitch.
Her eight multi-faceted crimson eyes blazed with berserk fury, and her massive dripping mandibles snapped together with the deafening sound of a hydraulic industrial guillotine.
CLACK! CLACK! CLACK!
A suffocating bone-crushing aura of Tier-3 Boss pressure washed over the room, violently blowing the recruit maidens’ hair back and forcing them to brace their boots against the stone.
"B-Boss monster...!" Helen stammered, raising her spear with trembling arms. "It’s massive!"
Silas stepped forward, entirely alone, stopping twenty paces before the eighteen-foot arachnid titan.
A slow satisfied smile spread across his handsome face.
"A chance for retribution," Silas whispered, his blue eyes igniting with incandescent gold.
"SKREEEEE-CHAAAAAA!"
Enraged by the man’s insolence, the Broodmother Spider Queen launched herself forward with apocalyptic speed.
Her multi-ton frame blurred into a terrifying streak of black and crimson, all eight scythe-legs driving downward like a falling forest of iron spears aimed straight at Silas’s head.
"LORD SILAS! MOVE!" several recruit maidens screamed in desperate terror, lunging forward to try and reach him.
Silas did not move a single millimeter.
He simply stood his ground, holding his golden-runed longsword loosely in his right hand.
VUUUUUUM... BOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
In less than a fraction of a second, a catastrophic burst of superheated red-gold flame erupted from Silas’s core.

The overwhelming thermal radiation detonated outward in a violent blinding gale that blew the recruits’ hair wildly across their faces, forcing every single woman... including the Princess to shield their eyes with their forearms as the entire chamber turned into a blinding scorching whiteout of heat.
For one breathless heartbeat, the world was consumed by fire then, the gale abruptly ceased.
FWHUUUUUSH.
The superheated air cleared, and the recruit maidens slowly lowered their arms, blinking away the bright spots in their vision.
Every single maiden in the room let out a loud and completely stunned gasp.
Lying flat across the scorched cavern floor, barely three inches before Silas’s motionless boots, was the Broodmother Spider Queen.
The eighteen-foot Boss monster was completely dead.
Its eight massive, iron-scythe legs had been sheared off at the joints with precision, lying scattered across the stone like severed timber.
Its colossal bone-plated cranium had been split cleanly in two from the center of its mandibles straight through its cerebral core, black hemolymph sizzling against the scorched rock.
Silas stood tall above the carcass with his sword already resting casually at his side and his breath completely even and calm.
The recruit maidens stood frozen, their jaws hanging slack in pure disbelief.
"W-What just happened...?" Helen whispered, clutching her spear with trembling fingers. "Did... did anyone see him swing?!"
"I didn’t see anything..." Sarah muttered in dazed awe. "There was just a flash of red fire... and then the Boss was dead on the ground!"
Standing beside Valkyrie, Aurelia’s golden-amber eyes trembled with overwhelming shock.
’I saw it...’ Aurelia thought, her breath catching in her throat as a shiver of reverence ran down her spine.

The white flames gently subsided, retreating back into Aurelia’s palm and dissolving into harmless, glowing embers that danced upon the cool breeze.
Aurelia lowered her hand, turning back toward Silas with a slight breathless flush dusting her porcelain cheekbones.
"The path is cleared, my Lord," Aurelia reported softly, her head bowed in quiet reverence.
Silas stared at her, his blue eyes wide with unreserved admiration.
He let out a low, appreciative whistle, stepping forward and clapping a hand gently on her shoulder armor.
"That was incredible, Aurelia," Silas praised warmly, a wide, radiant smile lighting up his face.
"A single spell wiped out the entire upper labyrinth without leaving a single trap intact...
You’re a powerhouse on your own huh?"
Aurelia’s breath caught in her throat.
The praise hit her straight in the chest, and a deep brilliant crimson blush rushed across her cheeks.
She quickly looked down at her boots as a small thoroughly flustered smile touching her lips.
I merely did what was necessary to serve you, Lord Silas."
"Alright, Squad One!" Silas announced, drawing his golden-runed sword with a smooth metallic ring.
"Formation alpha!
We’re heading down to finish the job!"
"Move out!" Helen commanded, leading the fifteen recruits as they stepped into the cavern.
Silas walked at the front of the column, his golden sword glowing with a soft steady radiance that illuminated the dark stone.
Valkyrie padded silently at his right flank, her golden eyes sharp and alert, while the Princess walked closely on his left, her hands hovering nervously over her void-iron dagger.
As the squad advanced through the wide tunnels, the recruit maidens looked around in open-mouthed awe.
The cavern walls were scorched clean, free of the suffocating, sticky webbing that had covered them moments prior.
The leather soles of their Blessed Land scout boots effortlessly absorbed the residual heat radiating from the polished granite floorboards, keeping their footing completely cool and steady.
Piles of calcified smoldering gray ash were all that remained of the dozens of Armorpiders that had attempted to set up ceiling ambushes.
As they rounded a wide descending bend in the stone corridor, a wet rustling sound reached Silas’s ears.
SKLICK...
SKLICK!
Lying near the base of a jagged stalagmite was a single, lone Armorpider.
The beast was heavily scorched, its stone-like carapace cracked and smoking, with four of its eight legs incinerated by the holy flames.
It dragged its broken, twitching body weakly across the gravel, hissing weakly with its remaining fangs as it tried to crawl toward a dark crevice.
Silas paused, glancing down at the Princess.
He noticed the way the blue-haired royal woman’s azure eyes were locked onto the struggling beast.
Her fingers were trembling slightly against her weapon hilt, but beneath the fear, that same fierce hungry spark of combat ambition was burning bright in her gaze.
Silas leaned down slightly, whispering with a gentle encouraging smirk.
"Hey, Princess.
Look right there."
The Princess blinked, looking up at him.
"L-Lord Silas?"
"You’ve been wanting your first official kill all morning, haven’t you?" Silas gestured toward the crippled spider with the tip of his blade.
"That one’s barely clinging to life.
Its armor is completely shattered, and it can’t jump.
Go on...
Finish it..."
The Princess’s heart hammered against her ribs like a war drum.
She looked at the twitching monster, then looked back at Silas’s calm supportive smile.
I can do this," she whispered to herself, setting her jaw with fierce determination.
She reached down, firmly gripping the leather hilt of her six-inch void-iron utility dagger, and drew the blade from her thigh sheath with a crisp shik.
Setting her boots firmly against the gravel, the Princess stepped forward.
"Yield before the judgment of Blessed Land, foul arachnid!" she proclaimed, her voice wavering slightly with adrenaline before steadying.
The crippled Armorpider turned its remaining two multi-faceted red eyes toward her, opening its venomous mandibles to release a weak, sputtering hiss.
"Chaaa!"
The Princess flinched slightly as a droplet of green bile splashed onto the stone near her boot, but she did not fall backward this time.
She lowered her center of gravity, planting her left foot firmly on the gravel just as Silas had instructed earlier.
’I WANT...’

She lunged forward with both hands on the dagger hilt, driving the void-iron point straight into the deep, glowing fracture that Aurelia’s holy fire had blasted across the center of the beast’s carapace.
’MY FIRST KILL DAMMIT!’
CRUNCH!
The blade pierced through the cracked stone plate, sinking deep into the monster’s vital core!
The Armorpider shrieked, thrashing its remaining legs violently against the ground with the impact jarring the Princess’s wrists.
"DIE!" the Princess grunted, gritting her teeth and putting her entire body weight into the hilt, twisting the blade forty-five degrees to shred the internal hemolymph vessels.
SPLAT-SQUELCH!
With a final shuddering gasp, the Armorpider’s remaining legs went completely limp, collapsing flat against the gravel as its red eyes dimmed into lifeless black.
PANT...
PANT...
PANT!
The Princess stood over the slain beast, her hands still clutching the embedded dagger as her chest heaved in rapid shallow breaths.
She slowly pulled the blade free, wiping a speck of black monster fluid from the metal before looking down at her hands in pure, disbelieving shock.
I did it..." the Princess breathed, a wide ecstatic smile breaking across her face.
"I killed it!
Lord Silas!
I secured my first official monster kill!"
"Outstanding work, Princess," Silas laughed warmly, giving her an approving thumbs-up.
"Clean strike, great balance, and you didn’t tumble onto your rear.
You’re officially a warrior now."
The Princess beamed, standing tall with her chest puffed out in immense royal pride as she sheathed her dagger with a triumphant flourish.
"Let’s keep moving," Silas commanded, leading the squad further down the descending corridor.
A few minutes later, the tunnel opened up into a massive cavernous drop-off.
Directly in the center of the rock floor was a wide circular chasm stretching nearly forty feet across, descending twenty feet into a brightly illuminated lower subterranean chamber.
The walls of the chasm were smooth, completely stripped of webs... and right at the lip of the drop-off, the scorched marks of Aurelia’s Argent Flames came to a clean sudden halt.
Silas stopped at the edge of the pit, looking down, then turned his gaze toward Aurelia.
Aurelia noticed his gaze and immediately stiffened, her golden-amber eyes flickering with sudden nervous apprehension.
’Did I overstep...?’ Aurelia worried internally, her fingers tightening slightly against her scabbard. ’Did I halt the flames too early?
Is he displeased that I did not scorch the entire cavern down to bedrock...?’
On the contrary, Silas’s face broke into a wide delighted grin.
’She stopped the inferno right at the threshold of the lower nesting chamber,’ Silas thought with glowing satisfaction. ’Which means the concentrated heat didn’t reach the nursery!
The eggs are completely intact!’
"Brilliant restraint, Aurelia," Silas praised, turning to the squad.
"Everyone down into the lower chamber!
Mind your landing!"
Without waiting for a rope or ladder, Silas took a single step forward and leaped straight down into the twenty-foot pit!
"Lord Silas?!" Helen and several recruits gasped in shock, rushing to the edge.
THUD!
Silas landed effortlessly on his boots, his Gold Core mana cushioning the impact into a harmless puff of dust.
Aurelia didn’t hesitate.
With a graceful, athletic vault, she leaped onto the back of Valkyrie’s saddle, reaching down and easily scooping the Princess up by her waist to sit before her.
"Hold tightly, Princess," Aurelia instructed calmly.
Valkyrie let out a fierce eager bark, leaping over the edge of the chasm with power.
The Blessed wolf descended through the air like a silver comet, landing firmly on all four paws beside Silas with a low rumbling thud that barely shook the saddle.
Moments later, the fifteen recruit maidens used their spear shafts and ledge grips to drop down into the chamber in crisp rapid succession, immediately fanning out into a wide defensive semi-circle.
The sight that greeted them in the lower cavern took their breath away.
The subterranean chamber was vast and vaulted, stretching nearly a hundred yards in every direction.
The walls were formed from glowing, translucent amethyst crystals that cast a soft ethereal purple light across the cavern floor.

Resting right in the center of the chamber was a colossal and intricately woven nest constructed from thousands of shimmering silver alchemical silk threads that pulsed with rich concentrated cosmic mana.
And inside that nest rested six massive, two-foot-wide, crystalline royal spider eggs that glowed with a mesmerizing, iridescent rainbow luminescence.
SKREEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEE!
A deafening ground-shaking screech tore through the chamber, shattering several protruding crystal clusters from the ceiling!
Standing directly in front of the silk nest, shielding her royal clutch with her colossal frame, was the mother.
[Target Analyzed: Broodmother Spider Queen (Tier 3 - Boss)]
The Spider Queen was a towering, nightmarish leviathan of war.
Her colossal obsidian-plated carapace stood over eighteen feet tall and forty feet wide, covered in thick, razor-sharp bone spikes that jutted from every joint.
Her eight massive, trunk-like legs ended in jagged scythe-like claws of solid abyssal iron that gouged deep furrows into the granite floor with every twitch.
Her eight multi-faceted crimson eyes blazed with berserk fury, and her massive dripping mandibles snapped together with the deafening sound of a hydraulic industrial guillotine.
CLACK!
CLACK!
CLACK!
A suffocating bone-crushing aura of Tier-3 Boss pressure washed over the room, violently blowing the recruit maidens’ hair back and forcing them to brace their boots against the stone.
"B-Boss monster...!" Helen stammered, raising her spear with trembling arms.
"It’s massive!"
Silas stepped forward, entirely alone, stopping twenty paces before the eighteen-foot arachnid titan.
A slow satisfied smile spread across his handsome face.
"A chance for retribution," Silas whispered, his blue eyes igniting with incandescent gold.
"SKREEEEE-CHAAAAAA!"
Enraged by the man’s insolence, the Broodmother Spider Queen launched herself forward with apocalyptic speed.
Her multi-ton frame blurred into a terrifying streak of black and crimson, all eight scythe-legs driving downward like a falling forest of iron spears aimed straight at Silas’s head.
"LORD SILAS!
MOVE!" several recruit maidens screamed in desperate terror, lunging forward to try and reach him.
Silas did not move a single millimeter.
He simply stood his ground, holding his golden-runed longsword loosely in his right hand.
VUUUUUUM...
BOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
In less than a fraction of a second, a catastrophic burst of superheated red-gold flame erupted from Silas’s core.

The overwhelming thermal radiation detonated outward in a violent blinding gale that blew the recruits’ hair wildly across their faces, forcing every single woman... including the Princess to shield their eyes with their forearms as the entire chamber turned into a blinding scorching whiteout of heat.
For one breathless heartbeat, the world was consumed by fire then, the gale abruptly ceased.
FWHUUUUUSH.
The superheated air cleared, and the recruit maidens slowly lowered their arms, blinking away the bright spots in their vision.
Every single maiden in the room let out a loud and completely stunned gasp.
Lying flat across the scorched cavern floor, barely three inches before Silas’s motionless boots, was the Broodmother Spider Queen.
The eighteen-foot Boss monster was completely dead.
Its eight massive, iron-scythe legs had been sheared off at the joints with precision, lying scattered across the stone like severed timber.
Its colossal bone-plated cranium had been split cleanly in two from the center of its mandibles straight through its cerebral core, black hemolymph sizzling against the scorched rock.
Silas stood tall above the carcass with his sword already resting casually at his side and his breath completely even and calm.
The recruit maidens stood frozen, their jaws hanging slack in pure disbelief.
"W-What just happened...?" Helen whispered, clutching her spear with trembling fingers.
"Did... did anyone see him swing?!"
"I didn’t see anything..." Sarah muttered in dazed awe.
"There was just a flash of red fire... and then the Boss was dead on the ground!"
Standing beside Valkyrie, Aurelia’s golden-amber eyes trembled with overwhelming shock.
’I saw it...’ Aurelia thought, her breath catching in her throat as a shiver of reverence ran down her spine.

chapters.title: Chapter 448: Mind-Controlling Worms?!
paragraphs: ’Right before the monster’s scythes could make contact, Lord Silas released a point-blank burst of mana so intensely superheated that if I had received it at zero distance, even with my barriers, I would have been incinerated alive in an instant...’
Aurelia gulped.

’...And in that exact second of blindness, he executed a singular, flawless horizontal slash infused with high-frequency wind mana, cleanly severing all eight of the beast’s legs simultaneously, before pivoting smoothly to bring his blade down in a vertical cleave that split the Queen’s armored skull in one go!’
She gulped once more.
’All of it... the flame burst, the eight-fold leg amputation, and the skull execution... took place in less than a tenth of a single second!’
Aurelia looked at Silas’s broad composed back, her chest heaving with awe.

’How strong is my Lord truly...?’ she thought with her golden eyes becoming wide. ’A Demon King? No... a standard Demon King would have been cleaved in two just like that Orc. He is far beyond that. In my old realm, a being of this stature would be revered as a Demon Lord... or a Sovereign of War.’
Silas didn’t pay any attention to the dead spider carcass.

With an excited energetic jog that looked completely out of place for a terrifying Lord who had just split a Tier-3 Boss in two, Silas trotted around the severed legs and rushed straight toward the alchemical silk nest.
The nest had been slightly displaced by the concussive force of the execution, but the six royal spider eggs resting in the center were completely unblemished, shimmering with radiant mana.
Silas dropped to his knees right in the middle of the silk nest, completely unbothered by the sticky monster slime coating the dirt.
He reached out with both hands, lifting one of the massive glowing royal spider eggs high into the air.
His handsome face twisted into an expression of pure glorious greed that would have made the most corrupt goblin merchant in the cosmos weep with envy.
"I finally have you..." Silas whispered, his voice trembling with overwhelming ecstasy.
A wide grin spread across his handsome face, stretching from ear to ear as he threw his head back, letting out a booming, echoing laugh that shook the cavern stalactites.
"THE SPIDER EGGS! HEHEHEHE... AHAHAHAHAHAHA!"
Silas clutched the massive egg tightly against his chest, rocking back and forth in the dirt like a lunatic who had just struck the mother lode of the cosmos.
"I’M RICH! DO YOU HAVE ANY IDEA HOW MUCH HIGH-TIER ALCHEMICAL SILK AND REINFORCED CHITIN WE CAN HARVEST FROM THIS BROOD?! THE UPGRADE POINTS! THE UPGRADES! HEHEHEHEHAHAHAHAHA!"
Silas hugged the crystalline egg close to his ribs, his mind already spinning through endless territorial blueprints.

’Once these royal beauties hatch, we can establish a permanent alchemical silk refinery right beside Thora’s foundry... We’ll weave ballistic shadow-silk into every uniform, extract high-grade paralysis venom for our scout arrows, and sell them out too to the Lord Association! But since their mother is dead, I’ll need to construct a special incubator in the Beast Pavilion to keep the clutch warm until they hatch...’
BEEP-BEEP-BEEP!
A sharp chiming sound echoed from the brass timer strapped to Helen’s wrist.
The mechanical hands had struck the exact noon mark.
Silas paused his manic rocking.
He carefully placed the glowing royal egg back into the safe center of the silk nest, standing up and brushing a bit of dust from his trousers with a calm charming smile.
He turned toward the fifteen dazed recruit maidens, Aurelia, and the wide-eyed Princess, his blue eyes crinkling warmly.

"Well, girls," Silas announced in a perfectly normal, cheerful voice as if he hadn’t just been cackling like a madman in the dirt five seconds ago. "The timer just rang... Why don’t we head back to the surface and go have lunch?"
Meanwhile, roughly four miles to the southwest, in a desolate sunless basin canyon flanked by jagged obsidian ridges...
CLOP! CLOP! CLOP! CLOP!
The heavy pounding of dozens of feral paws against hard stone echoed through the narrow ravine, kicking up thick clouds of black dust.

Surrounding the perimeter of a wide, sunken rock clearing was an entire army of wild Umbral Wolves... easily more than fifty black-furred beasts, each standing seven feet tall at the shoulder with glowing bloodshot crimson eyes.
Standing back-to-back in the absolute center of the encircling pack were Reina and Vala.
Reina had her hands outstretched, her ash-blonde braided hair whipping wildly in the mountain wind as she tried to channel her [Beast Arrest] to pacify the beasts.
But despite her higher affinity, the fifty wolves did not respond to the calming mana.
Their lips were pulled back in violent unnatural snarls, their muscles twitching with jagged spasmodic convulsions.
Beside her, Vala stood in a low combat stance, her dark elemental blade drawn and crackling with volatile mana.𝚏𝗿𝗲𝐞𝐰𝚎𝕓𝐧𝚘𝘃𝗲𝐥.𝐜𝚘𝕞
Vala’s sharp dark eyes narrowed with sudden, intense alarm as she looked closely at the foreheads of the surrounding wolves.
SQUELCH... WRITHE!

Tearing directly through the bone and flesh between the ears of all fifty Umbral Wolves, a grotesque three-foot-long segmented purple worm monstrosity burst outward, waving its pulsating lamprey-like maw in the open air like a grotesque antenna.
Vala’s grip on her sword tightened until her knuckles turned white, her voice dropping into a cold dangerous whisper.
"Mind-controlling worms...?"
Vala shifted her weight, the dark leather of her armor creaking softly against the jagged obsidian stone beneath her boots.
Her right hand held the hilt of her elemental blade in a loose lethal grip as the tip angled toward the ground at a thirty-degree slant.
"Vile," Vala whispered, her dark eyes narrowing with unvarnished revulsion. "Truly... completely disgusting."
"You took the words right out of my mouth," Reina agreed, her nose scrunching up in distaste.
CLINK!
With a practiced, fluid motion, the ash-blonde beast tamer reached behind her back, drawing her twin-pointed ash-wood spear from its harness.
She spun the shaft across her knuckles, letting the butt of the spear rest firmly against her palm as she dropped into a balanced low-center combat stance.
Despite the fact that fifty Tier-2 dire beasts were glaring at them with bloodshot manic eyes, neither woman felt a single drop of genuine panic.
Branded deeply across the back of their right knuckles, the glowing emerald Genesis Runes gifted to them by Lady Eluned pulsed with a warm steady heartbeat of life-force.
They knew the reality of their condition... As long as the Goddess held domain over the basin, death was impossible.
Shattered ribs would fuse in milliseconds and severed arteries would knit before a single drop of blood could hit the gravel.

’Dying isn’t the problem,’ Reina thought, her brow furrowing as she gripped the polished spear shaft tighter. ’The problem is our mission. Lord Graves sent us out here to tame and expand our cavalry corps... How on earth are we supposed to pacify beasts when their skulls are being puppeteered by oversized parasites? Do I have to personally dig into each of their cranial cavities and pull the squirming freaks out one by one?’
"Vala," Reina called out in a low, tight voice, her eyes sweeping across the twitching circle. "Cover my blind spots for five seconds. I’m going to force a wide-band mental override."
"Understood," Vala replied with her voice sounding deadpan. "Do what you must."
Reina closed her eyes, drawing a deep focused breath of the dry sulfurous air.
VUUUUUUUM!
A radian, golden-blue halo of spiritual mana ignited around Reina’s braided ash-blonde hair.
"Beast... Arrest."
A translucent ripple of tranquil pacifying soul-force expanded outward in a thirty-yard ring, washing over the fifty snarling wolves like a soothing spring breeze.
In normal circumstances, this resonance bypassed a beast’s primal aggression, harmonizing their spiritual core with Reina’s will to establish a bond of pack loyalty.
PING!
The moment her soul-force touched the wolves, an unnatural discordant screech reverberated through Reina’s mind.
It was not a beast resisting with wild stubbornness.
It felt like her consciousness had slammed headfirst into an iron wall coated in slick repulsive grease.
Her golden-blue mana shattered on contact, violently rebounding straight back into her core.
"Nngh...!" Reina grunted, stumbling back half a step as a dull ache throbbed behind her temples.
She opened her eyes, watching as the fifty purple worms vibrated violently in synchronized unison as their translucent skin flushed a toxic glowing magenta.

’It didn’t just fail... it completely deflected,’ Reina analyzed, a drop of cold sweat rolling down her cheek. ’Worms are primitive invertebrates with barely a cluster of nerve nodes. There is no way a parasitic worm has the cognitive architecture or spiritual capacity to deliberately counter an awakened beast-taming skill. That means...’
"The Umbral Basin is looking scarier by the minute," Reina muttered under her breath, adjusting her grip on her spear. "These things aren’t acting on instinct..."
KRA-CRACK!
The obsidian shale beneath the lead alpha wolf violently shattered.

Driven by a sudden, jagged spasm of the parasite embedded in its skull, a colossal, eight-foot-tall Umbral Wolf launched itself across the gap at blinding speed. Its jaws snapped open, dripping strings of thick saliva, while its front paws unleashed razor-sharp pitch-black claws aimed directly at Reina’s exposed throat.
"Reina, stay still," Vala’s voice sounded right beside her ear.
SWOOSH.
Vala didn’t just step forward... her entire silhouette dissolved into a dark frictionless blur of compressed mana.
SHING!
A clean, crescent arc of midnight-black elemental mana traced through the air.
Vala’s blade moved with such instantaneous velocity that the displaced air formed a visible vacuum slice.
WHOOSH!
The edge of her sword caught the lunging wolf mid-air, slicing cleanly through the thick fur, jugular, and spinal cord in seconds.
CLANG!

Without even glancing at the decapitated beast, Vala brought the flat of her blade up in a horizontal block, effortlessly intercepting the ferocious bone-shattering downward swipe of a second wolf that had leaped immediately behind the first.
Bright orange sparks erupted as the beast’s blackened claws scraped violently across the tempered steel.
Vala’s boots didn’t slide an inch against the stone.
With a sharp contemptuous twist of her wrists, she redirected the beast’s downward momentum, slamming the hilt of her sword squarely into the center of its snout with a sickening crack.
SPLAT-THUD!
The first wolf’s bisected body crashed heavily onto the gravel, rolling to a dead halt as dark viscous blood pooled beneath its neck.
Yet, even with its head completely severed from its shoulders, the purple worm embedded between its ears continued to writhe and pulse for three whole seconds before finally withering into gray ash.

"They’re completely dead inside," Vala remarked calmly, stepping back to flank Reina with her sword held steady. "There is no mind left to tame in the physical host... The parasite has already hijacked the nervous system entirely."
Reina’s golden eyes narrowed sharply. Her sharp brain rapidly pieced the puzzle together.

"It’s not the worms," Reina said, her voice dropping into a determined tone. "These parasites aren’t acting independently. They’re biological relays. There’s an outside entity... a master puppeteer projecting a hive-frequency into this entire pack from the shadows!"
"Can you trace the frequency?" Vala asked, parrying a lunging snap from a third wolf with a casual flick of her forearm.
"Watch my back and find out!" Reina shouted.
Reina planted her boots into the fissures of the obsidian ground.

Instead of casting a wide-area pacification wave, she condensed her entire soul-force into a single, needle-thin beam of pure golden mana, aiming it directly at the pulsating worm atop the nearest snarling wolf.
"Beast... Arrest."
BZZZZZZZZT!
The golden beam struck the purple parasite dead-center.
The worm shrieked... a high-pitched squeal that vibrated the very air.
The golden mana didn’t pierce the worm’s flesh at all, instead, the foreign command frequency pushed into the beast violently repelled Reina’s intrusion.
PING... FWIP!

The repulsive psychic force bounced off the parasite’s hide, deflecting outward at a sharp forty-five-degree angle and shooting a shimmering purple tether of mana straight toward the jagged, shadowy cliffs rising barely three hundred yards to the northwest.
Reina’s eyes tracked the psychic ricochet in an instant.

"FOUND YOU!" Reina grinned fiercely, pointing the gleaming void-iron tip of her ash-wood spear straight toward the rocky crags. "The puppet master is hiding in that ridge! It’s barely three hundred yards out!"
"Then we stop wasting time on the pawns." Vala nodded, her blade humming with elemental power.
"Vala, on me! MOVE!" Reina yelled.
THUD!
Reina kicked off the stone, breaking into a full-speed sprint straight through the narrowest gap in the surrounding wolf pack.
Vala followed a half-step behind, her sword blurring in fluid defensive arcs that deflected snapping jaws and sweeping claws with metallic clangs as they blasted their way through the perimeter.
"AWOOOOOOOOOOOOO!"

Behind them, the remaining forty-eight Umbral Wolves threw their heads back in synchronized unnatural howls, their purple head-parasites glowing with furious magenta light as the entire army surged across the canyon floor, giving wild relentless chase.
[Author’s Note]

Bonus Chapters won’t be done this month, they’ll be added to next month’s Mass release to make it quite bulkier. Thank you for all the support and gifts, I’m glad you all are enjoying the book. Happy new month in advance btw

SQUELCH...
WRITHE!

Tearing directly through the bone and flesh between the ears of all fifty Umbral Wolves, a grotesque three-foot-long segmented purple worm monstrosity burst outward, waving its pulsating lamprey-like maw in the open air like a grotesque antenna.
Vala’s grip on her sword tightened until her knuckles turned white, her voice dropping into a cold dangerous whisper.
"Mind-controlling worms...?"
Vala shifted her weight, the dark leather of her armor creaking softly against the jagged obsidian stone beneath her boots.
Her right hand held the hilt of her elemental blade in a loose lethal grip as the tip angled toward the ground at a thirty-degree slant.
"Vile," Vala whispered, her dark eyes narrowing with unvarnished revulsion.
"Truly... completely disgusting."
"You took the words right out of my mouth," Reina agreed, her nose scrunching up in distaste.
CLINK!
With a practiced, fluid motion, the ash-blonde beast tamer reached behind her back, drawing her twin-pointed ash-wood spear from its harness.
She spun the shaft across her knuckles, letting the butt of the spear rest firmly against her palm as she dropped into a balanced low-center combat stance.
Despite the fact that fifty Tier-2 dire beasts were glaring at them with bloodshot manic eyes, neither woman felt a single drop of genuine panic.
Branded deeply across the back of their right knuckles, the glowing emerald Genesis Runes gifted to them by Lady Eluned pulsed with a warm steady heartbeat of life-force.
They knew the reality of their condition...
As long as the Goddess held domain over the basin, death was impossible.
Shattered ribs would fuse in milliseconds and severed arteries would knit before a single drop of blood could hit the gravel.
’Dying isn’t the problem,’ Reina thought, her brow furrowing as she gripped the polished spear shaft tighter. ’The problem is our mission.
Lord Graves sent us out here to tame and expand our cavalry corps...
How on earth are we supposed to pacify beasts when their skulls are being puppeteered by oversized parasites?
Do I have to personally dig into each of their cranial cavities and pull the squirming freaks out one by one?’
"Vala," Reina called out in a low, tight voice, her eyes sweeping across the twitching circle.
"Cover my blind spots for five seconds.
I’m going to force a wide-band mental override."
"Understood," Vala replied with her voice sounding deadpan.
"Do what you must."
Reina closed her eyes, drawing a deep focused breath of the dry sulfurous air.
VUUUUUUUM!
A radian, golden-blue halo of spiritual mana ignited around Reina’s braided ash-blonde hair.
"Beast...
Arrest."
A translucent ripple of tranquil pacifying soul-force expanded outward in a thirty-yard ring, washing over the fifty snarling wolves like a soothing spring breeze.
In normal circumstances, this resonance bypassed a beast’s primal aggression, harmonizing their spiritual core with Reina’s will to establish a bond of pack loyalty.
PING!
The moment her soul-force touched the wolves, an unnatural discordant screech reverberated through Reina’s mind.
It was not a beast resisting with wild stubbornness.
It felt like her consciousness had slammed headfirst into an iron wall coated in slick repulsive grease.
Her golden-blue mana shattered on contact, violently rebounding straight back into her core.
"Nngh...!" Reina grunted, stumbling back half a step as a dull ache throbbed behind her temples.
She opened her eyes, watching as the fifty purple worms vibrated violently in synchronized unison as their translucent skin flushed a toxic glowing magenta.
’It didn’t just fail... it completely deflected,’ Reina analyzed, a drop of cold sweat rolling down her cheek. ’Worms are primitive invertebrates with barely a cluster of nerve nodes.
There is no way a parasitic worm has the cognitive architecture or spiritual capacity to deliberately counter an awakened beast-taming skill.
That means...’
"The Umbral Basin is looking scarier by the minute," Reina muttered under her breath, adjusting her grip on her spear.
"These things aren’t acting on instinct..."
KRA-CRACK!
The obsidian shale beneath the lead alpha wolf violently shattered.
Driven by a sudden, jagged spasm of the parasite embedded in its skull, a colossal, eight-foot-tall Umbral Wolf launched itself across the gap at blinding speed.
Its jaws snapped open, dripping strings of thick saliva, while its front paws unleashed razor-sharp pitch-black claws aimed directly at Reina’s exposed throat.
"Reina, stay still," Vala’s voice sounded right beside her ear.
SWOOSH.
Vala didn’t just step forward... her entire silhouette dissolved into a dark frictionless blur of compressed mana.
SHING!
A clean, crescent arc of midnight-black elemental mana traced through the air.
Vala’s blade moved with such instantaneous velocity that the displaced air formed a visible vacuum slice.
WHOOSH!
The edge of her sword caught the lunging wolf mid-air, slicing cleanly through the thick fur, jugular, and spinal cord in seconds.
CLANG!

Without even glancing at the decapitated beast, Vala brought the flat of her blade up in a horizontal block, effortlessly intercepting the ferocious bone-shattering downward swipe of a second wolf that had leaped immediately behind the first.
Bright orange sparks erupted as the beast’s blackened claws scraped violently across the tempered steel.
Vala’s boots didn’t slide an inch against the stone.
With a sharp contemptuous twist of her wrists, she redirected the beast’s downward momentum, slamming the hilt of her sword squarely into the center of its snout with a sickening crack.
SPLAT-THUD!
The first wolf’s bisected body crashed heavily onto the gravel, rolling to a dead halt as dark viscous blood pooled beneath its neck.
Yet, even with its head completely severed from its shoulders, the purple worm embedded between its ears continued to writhe and pulse for three whole seconds before finally withering into gray ash.
"They’re completely dead inside," Vala remarked calmly, stepping back to flank Reina with her sword held steady.
"There is no mind left to tame in the physical host...
The parasite has already hijacked the nervous system entirely."
Reina’s golden eyes narrowed sharply.
Her sharp brain rapidly pieced the puzzle together.
"It’s not the worms," Reina said, her voice dropping into a determined tone.
"These parasites aren’t acting independently.
They’re biological relays.
There’s an outside entity... a master puppeteer projecting a hive-frequency into this entire pack from the shadows!"
"Can you trace the frequency?" Vala asked, parrying a lunging snap from a third wolf with a casual flick of her forearm.
"Watch my back and find out!" Reina shouted.
Reina planted her boots into the fissures of the obsidian ground.

Instead of casting a wide-area pacification wave, she condensed her entire soul-force into a single, needle-thin beam of pure golden mana, aiming it directly at the pulsating worm atop the nearest snarling wolf.
"Beast...
Arrest."
BZZZZZZZZT!
The golden beam struck the purple parasite dead-center.
The worm shrieked... a high-pitched squeal that vibrated the very air.
The golden mana didn’t pierce the worm’s flesh at all, instead, the foreign command frequency pushed into the beast violently repelled Reina’s intrusion.
PING...
FWIP!

The repulsive psychic force bounced off the parasite’s hide, deflecting outward at a sharp forty-five-degree angle and shooting a shimmering purple tether of mana straight toward the jagged, shadowy cliffs rising barely three hundred yards to the northwest.
Reina’s eyes tracked the psychic ricochet in an instant.
"FOUND YOU!" Reina grinned fiercely, pointing the gleaming void-iron tip of her ash-wood spear straight toward the rocky crags.
"The puppet master is hiding in that ridge!
It’s barely three hundred yards out!"
"Then we stop wasting time on the pawns." Vala nodded, her blade humming with elemental power.
"Vala, on me!
MOVE!" Reina yelled.
THUD!
Reina kicked off the stone, breaking into a full-speed sprint straight through the narrowest gap in the surrounding wolf pack.
Vala followed a half-step behind, her sword blurring in fluid defensive arcs that deflected snapping jaws and sweeping claws with metallic clangs as they blasted their way through the perimeter.
"AWOOOOOOOOOOOOO!"

Behind them, the remaining forty-eight Umbral Wolves threw their heads back in synchronized unnatural howls, their purple head-parasites glowing with furious magenta light as the entire army surged across the canyon floor, giving wild relentless chase.
