chapters.title: Chapter 449: I’m Different
paragraphs: The obsidian walls of the sunless gorge groaned beneath the violent concussive thunder of dozens of galloping paws.
Basalt scree and jagged shale showered down the crags, clattering against the cold stone floor like hail as the frenzied swarm pushed through the narrow trench.
CLOP! CLOP! CLOP! CLOP!𝒇𝓻𝓮𝓮𝙬𝙚𝒃𝒏𝓸𝙫𝒆𝙡.𝓬𝓸𝒎
Behind the retreating pair, the pack of infected Umbral Wolves moved in horrifying synchronization.
Their joints buckled and snapped with unnatural extended spasms as yellow froth flew from their bared jaws.

Protruding between their ears, three-foot-long segmented purple worms writhed into the dry mountain air, their translucent mucus-coated skin pulsing with a toxic magenta that hummed at an ear-splitting frequency.
Roughly two hundred yards ahead, perched atop a massive, moss-draped boulder at the mouth of the ravine, Luna sat with her bushy silver tail curled over her front paws.
The Blessed Wolf tilted her broad head, her golden eyes blinking with slow curious detachment.

Luna’s memory was notoriously simple compared to the rest of the pack... her daily priorities revolved around warm sunlit patches, sweet roasted meat ribs, and the gentle scratch of Silas’s as well as the other women’s hands behind her ears.
Yet, as the wind carried the foul sulfurous reek of the oncoming swarm toward her nostrils, a dormant memory flickered in her canine mind.
Worms...
Luna’s silver ears flattened against her skull, her black nose wrinkling in distaste.
They were squirmy purple things and she had smelled them once in the deep trenches. The worms tasted like rotten copper and spoiled grease and made the mouth itch.
It also made her wonder why they were in the skulls of her former brethren... not that she cared at all, after all, all that mattered was family.
Before her simple train of thought could drift, a commanding voice cut straight through the roar of the canyon.
"LUNA! ON US! INTERCEPT!"
Reina’s shout struck Luna’s instincts like an electric spark.
BOOM!
The granite boulder beneath her rear paws fractured into jagged shards as Luna launched herself forward like a silver artillery shell.
Covering the two-hundred-yard gap in the space of several heartbeats, the dire wolf tore a blinding silver wake through the gloom.
Her corded muscles bunched and released with terrifying power, closing the distance before the lead infected wolves could even register the shift in momentum.
CRUNCH! SQUELCH!
Luna slammed dead-center into the forward rank.
Her massive jaws clamped shut around the neck of the lead alpha wolf, the crushing pressure pulverizing bone, fur, and spinal marrow in a single bite.
With a violent snap of her neck, Luna hurled the carcass thirty feet through the air, smashing it flat against the canyon wall with a concussive splat.
Without slowing down, she lowered her broad muscular shoulder, plowing into two more infected wolves like an iron battering ram.
’I never thought about it but Luna is quite strong... isn’t she?’
BANG! THUD! CRACK!
The two beasts were sent cartwheeling across the shale, their ribcages caving inward from the impact.
"Good girl!" Reina shouted, a relieved grin flashing across her face as she sprinted toward her mount.
"Clear the lane!" Vala echoed, her blade humming beside her.
However, the fleeting satisfaction vanished in a single horrifying heartbeat.
SQUELCH... POP!
From the skull of the wolf Luna had just crushed against the stone wall, the three-foot purple parasite did not die with its host.
With a wet, violent tear of cartilage and burst veins, the segmented worm forcefully wrenched its lower body free from the pulverized cranial cavity.
A geyser of dark viscous black ichor sprayed into the air as the wolf’s host body instantly withered into a dry shriveled husk.

’So that’s what happens when the host falls slowly...’ Vala’s dark eyes narrowed sharply, her combat instincts flaring into high gear. ’The parasite abandons the empty shell before the feedback loop can destroy it!’
FWHIP!
Like a coiled spring coated in translucent caustic slime, the detached purple parasite launched itself through the air, hurtling across the gap straight toward Luna’s exposed ear.
"Luna, dodge! Left side!" Reina screamed in frantic panic, lunging forward with her spear outstretched.
"Too late... it’s airborne!" Vala barked.

The worm moved with terrifying velocity as it landed with a wet splat right behind Luna’s left ear, its lamprey-like maw unhinging wide to reveal concentric rings of spinning razor-sharp chitin teeth designed to bore through skull bone.
SKREEEEE!
The parasite drove its fangs downward to breach the Blessed Wolf’s skull—
VUUUUUUUUUM... FWOOSH!
Before the creature’s teeth could pierce even a single millimeter of Luna’s fur, a blinding halo of radiant golden flame violently ignited across the wolf’s entire frame.
KRA-CRACKLE!
It was not a spell cast by Reina or Vala.
It was the passive protection of the contract with Blessed Land... the imprint left behind by Silas Graves upon every beast blessed by his authority.
The moment the parasitic entity attempted to corrupt a vessel bound to Silas’s soul, the flames detonated with purifying wrath.
The purple worm let out a deafening psychic screech of utter torment.

In less than a fraction of a second, its translucent slime boiled away, its segmented hide turned to brittle charcoal, and the entire parasite was completely vaporized into a puff of harmless sparkling white ash that scattered into the wind.
Luna didn’t even flinch. She simply shook her head once, letting out a confused chuff as she trotted up to Reina’s side.
"Lord Silas’s blessing..." Reina breathed, her heart hammering wildly against her ribs with relief. "Even miles away from the main camp, his authority protects his pack."
"Don’t lose focus... mount up!" Vala ordered, her voice sounding sharp and urgent.
With practiced agility, Reina planted her boot into Luna’s stirrup-leather and vaulted into the primary saddle, gathering the reins in a tight grip.
Vala followed in a single, fluid leap, landing lightly on the rear cantle behind Reina with supernatural balance.
"Go, Luna! Full sprint! Northwest ridge!" Reina commanded, leaning low over the neck.
HOWL!
Luna dug her claws deep into the granite, accelerating with explosive torque that kicked up a rooster-tail of shattered stone behind them.
Yet, despite Luna’s superior physical tier, the pursuing pack was closing the distance with unnatural horrifying speed.
Vala stood upright on the rear of the saddle behind Reina, balancing on the balls of her feet with supernatural equilibrium as the wind whipped her dark hair wildly across her face.
She looked over her shoulder, her dark eyes scanning the approaching horde.
What she saw made her stomach turn...
The forty-five remaining Umbral Wolves were no longer running like living creatures.
Driven by the frantic manic signals pulsating from their purple head-parasites, the wolves were entirely overriding their biological pain receptors and skeletal limitations.

Their thigh bones and shoulder joints were literally cracking and splintering under the impossible self-destructive muscle contractions, their paws shredding down to bare bone against the sharp shale.
CRACK... SNAP... THUD!
They didn’t care about torn ligaments, internal hemorrhaging, or shattered ribs.
The hive mind puppeteering them viewed their bodies as disposable meat engines, forcing them to sprint far beyond the threshold of mortal biological failure simply to catch the silver wolf.
"The entity controlling them doesn’t care if the vessels survive the chase," Vala said in a cold voice with the wind tearing at her words. "It’s burning their life-force down to the marrow."
The lead trio of mutated wolves was barely ten feet away, their gaping jaws snapping inches from Luna’s tail.
CLACK! CLACK!
"Reina, hold tight!" Vala shouted over the deafening roar of the chase. "Keep Luna straight and do not deviate!"
"Holding! Do whatever you have to do!" Reina yelled back, leaning her full weight over Luna’s shoulders as the dire wolf pushed her speed to its absolute limit.
Vala drew a slow deliberate breath, drawing the sulfurous mountain air deep into the bottom of her lungs.
She closed her eyes for a single tranquil second.

Her mind briefly drifted back to that quiet moonlit evening inside the keep’s inner courtyard, when Silas had placed his glowing hand upon her chest and channeled the mysterious reality-bending power of the Absolute Upgrade System to force her class evolution.
Like several other senior combatants in Blessed Land, she had awakened the rare prestigious Magic Swordsman class.
But while standard Magic Swordsmen typically bonded with a single elemental affinity... fire, water, or earth... Vala’s awakening had shattered all established logic.
’I am different,’ Vala thought, a calm razor-sharp focus settling over her consciousness as she exhaled slowly through her teeth.
VUUUUUUUUUM!
The air around her slender frame violently distorted.

Coiling tightly around the length of her dark void-iron blade, howling spirals of emerald Wind Mana erupted in a violent vortex, instantly accompanied by crackling jagged branches of cerulean Lightning Mana that hissed and arced across the crossguard with blinding intensity.
Vala’s eyes snapped open, blazing with an intense glowing emerald hue.

’Wind, Lightning, Fire, Water, Earth... Five distinct elemental affinities have awakened within my soul core.’ Vala reflected with icy ambition. ’And I can still feel the dormant tremors of even more elements sleeping beneath the surface.’
She didn’t let pride cloud her judgment though.

’Was I chosen for this reconnaissance mission because Lord Silas recognized my unique potential? Perhaps but potential is worthless if it remains unrefined. In this territory, every woman is striving to carve her own legend. If I wish to stand proudly beside him... if I wish to be more than just his "Hidden Blade"... if I truly desire to warm his bed as his cherished wife, I cannot settle for mediocrity. I must deliver overwhelming results!’
KRA-BOOOOOOOOM!
The lead wolf leaped into the air, its fangs wide open, aiming straight for Vala’s ankles.
Vala didn’t flinch.
She pivoted on the saddle cantle, swinging her electrified wind-wreathed blade in a massive sweeping radial arc.
"Just... Die."
FWHUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUSH!
A miniature hurricane of razor-sharp wind blades and branching lightning bolts detonated backward from the tip of her sword.

The concussive elemental blast tore across the narrow canyon floor like a roaring tidal wave as the three leaping wolves were instantly shredded into hundreds of cauterized, smoking chunks of meat mid-air, while the surrounding wind blades cleaved through the front two ranks of the pursuing pack with horrifying precision.
SKREEEEE! CRACKLE! SPLAT!
Over a dozen wolves were lifted off their feet, their bodies mangled and incinerated as lightning arced through their wet fur, popping the purple head-parasites like overripe grapes.
"Haah... Haah..."
Vala stumbled slightly as the immense spell finished its course, a sharp pang of exhaustion throbbing in her mana core.
The dual-element release had burned through nearly forty percent of her active reserves in a single stroke.
’It’s heavy on the core... but worth it.’ Vala thought, gritting her teeth.
VUUUUUUM... CHIME!
Suddenly, a warm electrifying rush of pure cosmic energy erupted from the void, cascading down through her crown and flooding every single meridian in her body.
Her depleted mana pool refilled to overflowing in an instant, her muscle fibers tightened with newfound density, and her perception expanded by several meters.
A small triumphant smirk touched Vala’s lips as she caught her balance and sat back down onto the saddle cantle.
’A level up...’ Vala smiled inwardly, rolling her shoulders.
"Reina! Trace the tether again!" Vala called out, resting her blade across her lap. "We took out the front rank, but the rest are still coming!"
"On it!" Reina shouted.
Reina raised her left hand, condensing her spiritual mana into a needle-thin golden spike.
"Beast... Arrest."
PING!
The golden pulse struck one of the remaining pursuing wolves.

As expected, the foreign command frequency violently deflected the intrusion, but the resulting psychic ricochet sent a glowing magenta beam shooting straight over the crest of the upcoming rocky ridge.
"Left fork! Up the incline!" Reina barked, pulling hard on Luna’s left rein.
Luna dug her front paws into the dirt, executing a breathtaking high-speed drift around an obsidian boulder, and charged up a steep narrow ravine flanked by twisted, deadwood pine trees.
Less than ten seconds later, they burst out of the ravine into a wide, sunken amphitheater surrounded by jagged rock walls.
Both women and Luna skidded to an immediate halt, their eyes widening in collective revulsion.
"By the gods..." Reina muttered, her face turning pale. "What in the world is that horrific thing...?"
"Vile..." Vala hissed, her brow furrowing deeply.
Wedged tightly between the massive gnarled trunks of two ancient, dead weeping willow trees was a colossal biological monstrosity.
It was a gargantuan twenty-foot-tall cocoon forged from thick translucent mucus-slicked membrane that beat with a sickening rhythm.
THUMP-DUB..! THUMP-DUB...!

Flowing through the translucent skin were thousands of glowing purple veins, feeding a thick bubbling green fluid that continuously dripped from the base of the cocoon into a rancid steaming pool of digestive acids below.
Embedded across the surface of the membrane were dozens of grotesque, writhing purple worm heads, hissing and projecting visible waves of psychic distortion into the surrounding air.
RUSTLE! RUSTLE!

Five distinct elemental affinities have awakened within my soul core.’ Vala reflected with icy ambition. ’And I can still feel the dormant tremors of even more elements sleeping beneath the surface.’
She didn’t let pride cloud her judgment though.
’Was I chosen for this reconnaissance mission because Lord Silas recognized my unique potential?
Perhaps but potential is worthless if it remains unrefined.
In this territory, every woman is striving to carve her own legend.
If I wish to stand proudly beside him... if I wish to be more than just his "Hidden Blade"... if I truly desire to warm his bed as his cherished wife, I cannot settle for mediocrity.
I must deliver overwhelming results!’
KRA-BOOOOOOOOM!
The lead wolf leaped into the air, its fangs wide open, aiming straight for Vala’s ankles.
Vala didn’t flinch.
She pivoted on the saddle cantle, swinging her electrified wind-wreathed blade in a massive sweeping radial arc.
"Just...
Die."
FWHUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUSH!
A miniature hurricane of razor-sharp wind blades and branching lightning bolts detonated backward from the tip of her sword.

The concussive elemental blast tore across the narrow canyon floor like a roaring tidal wave as the three leaping wolves were instantly shredded into hundreds of cauterized, smoking chunks of meat mid-air, while the surrounding wind blades cleaved through the front two ranks of the pursuing pack with horrifying precision.
SKREEEEE!
CRACKLE!
SPLAT!
Over a dozen wolves were lifted off their feet, their bodies mangled and incinerated as lightning arced through their wet fur, popping the purple head-parasites like overripe grapes.
"Haah...
Haah..."
Vala stumbled slightly as the immense spell finished its course, a sharp pang of exhaustion throbbing in her mana core.
The dual-element release had burned through nearly forty percent of her active reserves in a single stroke.
’It’s heavy on the core... but worth it.’ Vala thought, gritting her teeth.
VUUUUUUM...
CHIME!
Suddenly, a warm electrifying rush of pure cosmic energy erupted from the void, cascading down through her crown and flooding every single meridian in her body.
Her depleted mana pool refilled to overflowing in an instant, her muscle fibers tightened with newfound density, and her perception expanded by several meters.
A small triumphant smirk touched Vala’s lips as she caught her balance and sat back down onto the saddle cantle.
’A level up...’ Vala smiled inwardly, rolling her shoulders.
"Reina!
Trace the tether again!" Vala called out, resting her blade across her lap.
"We took out the front rank, but the rest are still coming!"
"On it!" Reina shouted.
Reina raised her left hand, condensing her spiritual mana into a needle-thin golden spike.
"Beast...
Arrest."
PING!
The golden pulse struck one of the remaining pursuing wolves.

As expected, the foreign command frequency violently deflected the intrusion, but the resulting psychic ricochet sent a glowing magenta beam shooting straight over the crest of the upcoming rocky ridge.
"Left fork!
Up the incline!" Reina barked, pulling hard on Luna’s left rein.
Luna dug her front paws into the dirt, executing a breathtaking high-speed drift around an obsidian boulder, and charged up a steep narrow ravine flanked by twisted, deadwood pine trees.
Less than ten seconds later, they burst out of the ravine into a wide, sunken amphitheater surrounded by jagged rock walls.
Both women and Luna skidded to an immediate halt, their eyes widening in collective revulsion.
"By the gods..." Reina muttered, her face turning pale.
"What in the world is that horrific thing...?"
"Vile..." Vala hissed, her brow furrowing deeply.
Wedged tightly between the massive gnarled trunks of two ancient, dead weeping willow trees was a colossal biological monstrosity.
It was a gargantuan twenty-foot-tall cocoon forged from thick translucent mucus-slicked membrane that beat with a sickening rhythm.
THUMP-DUB..!
THUMP-DUB...!

Flowing through the translucent skin were thousands of glowing purple veins, feeding a thick bubbling green fluid that continuously dripped from the base of the cocoon into a rancid steaming pool of digestive acids below.
Embedded across the surface of the membrane were dozens of grotesque, writhing purple worm heads, hissing and projecting visible waves of psychic distortion into the surrounding air.
RUSTLE!
RUSTLE!

chapters.title: Chapter 450: Is It Enough...?
paragraphs: Before they could analyze the monstrosity any further, the sounds of snapping branches and guttural snarls erupted from all sides.

Surging out from the deadwood trees ahead of the cocoon came a fresh horrific amount of monsters... dozens of mutated forest goblins, razor-beaked swamp raptors, and venomous rock lizards, all bearing the same three-foot purple parasites bursting from their skulls!
And behind them, charging up the ravine path, the remaining thirty infected Umbral Wolves arrived, sealing their escape route entirely.
"We’re surrounded," Reina said, her voice dropping into a disciplined tone as she leveled her twin-pointed spear.
Vala didn’t waste breath on words. She raised her blade, channeling a massive sphere of concentrated fire mana to the tip.
"Ignis Lance!"
BOOOOOOM!
A roaring spear of crimson flame shot from her blade, striking the center of the giant pulsating cocoon dead-center.
KRA-SHAAAA!
The fiery explosion blasted green mucus and superheated steam thirty feet into the air.
But as the smoke cleared, both women gasped.
The thick rubbery membrane of the cocoon had barely suffered a surface scorch.
The thousands of glowing purple veins had instantly rerouted psychic mana to absorb and disperse the shockwave, leaving the structure completely intact.
Vala clicked her tongue in frustration, leaning forward over Reina’s shoulder.
"The outer shell has an adaptive mana-dispersion barrier! Reina, do you have a way to crack this overgrown boil?!"
Reina’s eyes narrowed sharply as she analyzed the rhythmic pulsing of the membrane.

"I don’t have enough raw physical output to pierce that barrier with my spear," Reina admitted quickly, her voice steady under pressure. "However... that cocoon isn’t the creature’s true body! It’s a gestation shell protecting the core entity nested inside! If I channel the full unbridled power of Beast Arrest, I might be able to overload its psychic frequency and force the shell to fracture from within!"
"How long do you need?" Vala asked.
"Ten seconds of completely uninterrupted focus!" Reina answered. "If I get interrupted by a single stray beast, the psychic backlash will scramble my brain!"
Vala’s lips curved into a sharp fearless smirk.
"Ten seconds?" Vala whispered.
SWOOSH!
With a graceful, effortless vault, Vala leaped down from Luna’s back, landing lightly on the mossy gravel between Reina and the advancing swarm.
"I’ll give you twenty," Vala declared, her voice ringing with confidence. "Begin your skill. Not a single drop of monster blood will touch your saddle..."
Reina nodded firmly, closing her eyes and pulling Luna five paces back to begin gathering her spiritual reserves.
Vala stood alone in the center of the amphitheater, surrounded on all sides by over fifty mutated beasts.
She rolled her shoulders, letting the cold mountain wind whip through her dark hair.
Vala raised her void-iron blade, looking directly into the bloodshot, worm-infested eyes of the oncoming monsters with a battle-hungry smile.
"Come at me, you ugly vermin," Vala whispered, her voice dripping with provocation. "Give me a good match. Carve away my weaknesses and make me strong enough to stand proudly as my Lord’s wife!"
"GRAAAAAAH!"
A massive eight-foot swamp raptor lunged first, its sickle-claws tearing through the air toward Vala’s neck.
VUUUUUM!
Vala didn’t retreat. She channeled pure emerald Wind Mana through the soles of her boots.𝘧𝓇ℯℯ𝑤ℯ𝘣𝓃ℴ𝓋𝑒𝑙.𝑐𝘰𝑚
BOOM!
With a concussive blast of compressed air, Vala shot vertically into the sky like an arrow, soaring twenty feet into the air as the raptor’s claws slammed harmlessly into empty dirt.
"Zephyr Edge!" Vala called out from above.
SHING-SHING-SHING!
Descending through the air with fluid acrobatic grace, Vala unleashed a flurry of crescent wind blades.
The razor-sharp aerial strikes cleaved through the raptor’s neck, spine, and legs simultaneously, reducing the charging beast into four neat cauterized segments before she even touched the ground.
SPLAT-THUD.
To her left, three mutated goblins brandishing rusted bone daggers shrieked, lunging toward Luna’s flank to disrupt Reina’s concentration.
"Not on my watch!" Reina’s eyes snapped open for a fraction of a second.
THWACK!
Reina’s twin-pointed spear blurred forward like a striking viper, skewering the central goblin through its chest and lifting it three feet off the ground before slamming it into the dirt.
Simultaneously, Luna’s massive hind legs kicked backward with devastating equine force.
CRUNCH!
The second goblin’s skull caved inward like a hollow gourd, its crushed body skipping across the gravel like a thrown pebble.
FWHIP!

Before the third goblin could scramble away, a concentrated blade of wind sliced down from above, severing its head cleanly from its shoulders. Vala landed lightly on her boots, spinning her sword in a tight, defensive arc.
SCREEEEEECH!
A deafening high-pitched screech tore through the sky above.

Dropping from the high obsidian cliffs at terrifying dive-bomb speed was a winged monstrosity... a Gargoyle-Bat Aberration spanning fifteen feet wide, its grotesque jaws dripping with caustic purple bile as its hooked talons reached out to crush Vala’s skull.
Vala didn’t even look up until the beast was barely ten feet above her head.
’Too slow,’ Vala thought calmly. She thrust her left palm straight toward the descending shadow.
CRACKLE... BOOOOOOM!
A blinding spear of concentrated Lightning Mana erupted from her hand, striking the flying beast dead-center in its chest.

The high-voltage electrical discharge instantly vaporized the winged monster’s internal organs, frying the purple parasite in its skull into smoking cinders before the charred carcass crashed into the dirt with a heavy sizzling thud.
VUUUUUUM... CHIME!
Once again, that intoxicating warm surge of feedback flooded through Vala’s spiritual meridians.
’Another surge...’ Vala grinned fiercely, feeling her physical strength, speed, and mana recovery rate elevate yet again. ’I’m leveling up in real-time!’
She gripped her sword with both hands, stepping into the absolute center of the remaining wolf pack.
"Let’s raise the heat!"
FWOOOOOOOOOOSH!
This time, she unleashed her third awakened element... Crimson Fire as her blade transformed into a pillar of roaring superheated flame.

Vala moved like a dancing executioner, her fiery sword cleaving through wolves, raptors, and rock lizards in a relentless breathtaking sequence of spinning slashes, thrusts, and point-blank flame bursts.
SLASH! HACK! BOOM! SPLAT!
"DIE!"
"BURN!"
Every swing left a trail of smoldering cauterized monster corpses in its wake.
In less than eight seconds, Vala had slaughtered over thirty mutated monstrosities on her own, forming an impenetrable wall of fire and steel around Reina.
As the last infected wolf collapsed into a burning heap, Vala looked over her shoulder toward the massive pulsating cocoon.
The purple veins on the membrane were glowing with blinding intensity, preparing to release a massive psychic shockwave.
"REINA! HURRY! BREAK THE DAMN SHELL!" Vala roared at the top of her lungs.
"ALREADY ON IT!" Reina screamed back.
Reina stood tall in Luna’s stirrups, her braided ash-blonde hair floating wildly as an overwhelming ocean of golden spiritual mana erupted from her soul core.
She pointed both palms directly at the giant pulsating cocoon.
"Beast..."
Reina took a deep breath.
"...Arrest."
VUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUM!
A visible beam of solid golden soul-force shot from Reina’s hands, slamming violently into the center of the giant cocoon!
SKREEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEE!

Inside the translucent membrane, a deafening psychic screech reverberated directly into the fabric of the atmosphere as a brutal invisible battle of wills erupted between Reina’s awakened soul-force and the alien consciousness nesting within the cocoon.
The creature possessed an astonishing degree of mental resilience... it fought back frantically, projecting violent psychic needles into Reina’s mind that made blood trickle from her left nostril.
’Fuck... Fuck... Fuck...’
Even while locked in mental combat, the entity desperately commanded three remaining wounded wolves to drag themselves toward Reina’s mount.
SHING!
Vala blurred past, her blade flashing once in a clean horizontal cleave that decapitated all three wolves before they could take another step.
"I’ve got your back, Reina!" Vala yelled, her boots planted firmly in the bloodstained loam. "SHATTER IT!"
"BREAK FOR ME, YOU DISGUSTING FREAK!" Reina roared, pouring every single drop of her spiritual mana and her devotion to Silas into the golden beam.
KRRRR-SHATTER!
The mental barrier snapped.
With the deafening sound of fracturing crystal, the giant twenty-foot cocoon violently ruptured down the center.
The thick, rubbery membrane tore open like peeling fruit, spewing gallons of steaming green mucus and bile across the ground, exposing the grotesque, vulnerable core entity curled inside.
The creature was a bloated six-foot-tall pale-white maggot-queen covered in dozens of pulsating crimson eyes and writhing tentacles.
"VALA! NOW! THE CORE IS EXPOSED!" Reina gasped as she fell back into the saddle, breathless and exhausted.
Vala didn’t need to be told twice.
BOOM!
Vala detonated the earth beneath her boots, shooting across the clearing like a blazing meteor.
She channeled the entirety of her remaining fire mana into her blade, the steel glowing with blinding fury that illuminated the entire amphitheater.
"Just die already!"
SLASH!
Vala brought her blazing blade down in a flawless two-handed vertical execution cleave straight through the maggot-queen’s exposed cranial core.
KRA-BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The white-hot flame sheared through flesh, organs, and nerve clusters, detonating the core entity from within in a colossal geyser of superheated fire and boiling ash.
SKREEEEEEEE—
The queen’s death screech choked off into silence and the moment the master entity perished, the resonance linking the hive mind violently ruptured.
SPLAT! POP! SQUELCH!
Across the entire amphitheater and the surrounding ravine, every single purple worm embedded in the remaining monster corpses violently detonated like overpressurized blood-sacks.
SHOWER!
A colossal, torrential rain of black blood, sticky mucus, and shredded parasite gristle showered down from the sky, covering everything in the clearing.
Reina, Vala, and Luna were instantly drenched from head to toe in foul-smelling lukewarm black monster gore.
"Uuuuugh..." Reina groaned, wiping a thick clump of black slime from her forehead with a look of soul-deep misery. "I smell like a clogged sewer drain in the middle of summer."
She looked around at the dead Umbral Wolves scattered across the ravine floor, letting out a disappointed sigh.

"Great... now we have to trek into another sector and locate a new wolf pack for the cavalry corps," Reina complained, shaking her head. "I swear, if there’s another hive-mind worm nesting in these mountains, I’m going to set the entire forest on fire."
Vala sheathed her sword with a crisp clack, stepping up beside Luna.
She raised her right hand, her eyes shifting to a tranquil, azure hue as she channeled her fourth awakened element... Water Mana.
"Water, be my guide..." Vala murmured softly.
SPLASH!
A gentle swirling vortex of crystal-clear mountain water erupted from her palm, washing over Reina, Luna, and herself in a soothing, thorough torrent.
In less than three seconds, the foul black gore, mucus, and stench were completely washed away, leaving their skin, hair, and armor immaculately clean and dry.
"Thanks, Vala," Reina smiled, shaking out her wet braids. "Water magic really is the most convenient utility in the world..."
"It has its uses," Vala replied calmly, though her mind was already drifting far away from the bloodstained clearing.
She closed her eyes, letting the cool mountain breeze caress her skin.

’Two level ups in a single skirmish... multiple successful multi-element releases... and the complete eradication of an invasive hive core,’ Vala calculated internally, her heart beating with quiet nervous anticipation. ’This should give me enough feats to stand out...’
Her thoughts drifted back to the sacred memory that she held closest to her heart.

The day Silas had awakened her potential, declaring her to be his personal Hidden Blade... He had pinned her against the cold stone wall of the office, his strong hands holding her shoulders, his gaze burning into hers with unshakeable trust... before leaning down and pressing a warm unforgettable kiss upon her forehead.
Vala’s dark eyelashes fluttered, a deep, burning crimson blush rising from the base of her throat all the way to the tips of her ears.
’Does this warrant a kiss on the lips now?’
[The Camp]

Nearly an hour later, in a vast sun-drenched clearing of soft, velvety black grass situated near the center of the Umbral Basin, the entire expeditionary force of Blessed Land had converged for the scheduled midday respite.
Woven linen mats had been neatly laid out across the lush black turf, creating a wide comfortable encampment surrounded by the secure perimeter of resting Blessed wolves and vigilant scout sentries.

The air was rich and intoxicating, filled with the mouth-watering aromas of freshly roasted wild boar ribs, golden-brown herb-crusted poultry, steaming bowls of buttered tuber stew, and platters of chilled mountain berries that had been prepared by the territory’s Chef.
The recruit maidens from all four squads sat together in lively clusters, laughing, chatting, and happily devouring their generous rations as they eagerly recounted their morning battles.
Yet, despite the abundance of delicious food, a palpable simmering tension hung over the encampment.

Every few seconds, dozens of pairs of eyes... including those of Helen, Sarah, Catelyn, Morrighan, and Lupina would subtly dart toward the largest and most luxurious woven mat resting beneath the shade of a weeping willow tree.
And sitting on a mat, Brida was practically gnawing on the bone of her roasted pork rib in jealous frustration.
"Look at that..." Brida grumbled beneath her breath, her large amber eyes narrowing into intense laser-focused slits. "Just look at her... Shameless. She’s absolutely shameless..."

’Does this warrant a kiss on the lips now?’
[The Camp]

Nearly an hour later, in a vast sun-drenched clearing of soft, velvety black grass situated near the center of the Umbral Basin, the entire expeditionary force of Blessed Land had converged for the scheduled midday respite.
Woven linen mats had been neatly laid out across the lush black turf, creating a wide comfortable encampment surrounded by the secure perimeter of resting Blessed wolves and vigilant scout sentries.

The air was rich and intoxicating, filled with the mouth-watering aromas of freshly roasted wild boar ribs, golden-brown herb-crusted poultry, steaming bowls of buttered tuber stew, and platters of chilled mountain berries that had been prepared by the territory’s Chef.
The recruit maidens from all four squads sat together in lively clusters, laughing, chatting, and happily devouring their generous rations as they eagerly recounted their morning battles.
Yet, despite the abundance of delicious food, a palpable simmering tension hung over the encampment.

Every few seconds, dozens of pairs of eyes... including those of Helen, Sarah, Catelyn, Morrighan, and Lupina would subtly dart toward the largest and most luxurious woven mat resting beneath the shade of a weeping willow tree.
And sitting on a mat, Brida was practically gnawing on the bone of her roasted pork rib in jealous frustration.
"Look at that..." Brida grumbled beneath her breath, her large amber eyes narrowing into intense laser-focused slits.
"Just look at her...
Shameless.
She’s absolutely shameless..."
